desc: use_ok AnnotationSource: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource base-class module compiles and loads
rationale: A module-load probe: use_ok asserts that Perl found and compiled Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/AnnotationSource.pm at run time, and nothing about what the class does. Rust settles the same question at compile time — an absent item behind a `use` stops the test crate building — so a run-time assertion would only restate the compiler. docs/ledger-contract.md admits exactly this case for can_ok/isa_ok existence probes; same reading as ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=1, the same idiom on the parent class.

desc: use_ok Config: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config module compiles and loads, so the fixture config can be built
rationale: The second of this file's four module-load probes (rows 1, 2, 6, 8), and pure test scaffolding: Config is loaded only so line 37 can build the config every later object is handed. Same compile-time argument as row 1. What Config actually resolves is the subject of t/Config.t and is classified in ledger/Config.ledger.toml, so nothing is lost by keeping the load probe out of the denominator.

desc: get new config object: Config->new(base_testing_cfg) returns a defined, true config object
rationale: ok($cfg) pins the Perl idiom for `new did not die and did not return undef`, and nothing else — the option set it is handed (VEPTestingConfig::base_testing_cfg) is never inspected on this line. Rust has no undef: a constructor yields a value of its type or the call does not compile, so there is no run-time definedness left to observe. Identical assertion and identical reading at ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=7.

desc: new is defined: AnnotationSource->new({config, cache_region_size => 1000000, up_down_size => 0, info => {foo => 'bar'}}) returns a blessed object
rationale: AnnotationSource::new (AnnotationSource.pm:77 @ release/116.0) delegates to SUPER::new and then copies every key of the hashref onto the blessed hash (:85). ok($as) reads back only that the bless succeeded and the reference is true — Perl object plumbing, not annotation behaviour. None of the three values passed in is checked here: info is checked by row 5, and cache_region_size and up_down_size only take effect in rows 11 and 13. Same reading as ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=2.

desc: info: the info accessor hands back the arbitrary hashref {foo => 'bar'} the constructor was given, unchanged
rationale: A getter pass-through: new copied the key onto the blessed hash (AnnotationSource.pm:85) and info() returns it or an empty hash (:426). The payload is deliberately meaningless — {foo => 'bar'} — so what the assertion pins is that Perl accessor generation works, not any cache metadata. In Rust a struct field holds what was written to it; there is no accessor to generate and no run-time round-trip to observe. docs/ledger-contract.md keeps Perl object plumbing out of the denominator, and ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=19/n=20 read add_shortcuts — the same copy-a-key-onto-the-object idiom — the same way. Note this is not the cache info.txt map: that is filled by the Cache subclass, and its content is asserted in other .t files, not by this line.

desc: use_ok Parser::VCF: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF module compiles and loads
rationale: Third module-load probe, loaded only so lines 56-60 can build an InputBuffer to feed rows 11 and 12. Same compile-time argument as row 1. VCF parsing behaviour itself belongs to t/Parser_VCF.t and ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml; this line asserts none of it.

desc: get parser object: Parser::VCF->new({config, file => the test VCF, valid_chromosomes => [21, 1]}) returns a defined parser
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. The type that stands in is `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`: vepyr never hands a caller a parser object, so the nearest thing an external crate can construct is the provider `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` registers internally (`vcf_sink.rs:1074` and `:1079` @ dfbf 391f94bd, both `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` — the five arguments the named test passes), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The probe is load-bearing rather than plumbing because that constructor is genuinely fallible: it `block_on`s `determine_schema_from_header` and propagates with `?` (`table_provider.rs:869-879` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8), i.e. it reads and parses the VCF header before it can return — exactly the ruling's defined/undef -> `Ok`/`Err` case. The named test asserts both limbs: `Ok` over a one-row VCF written to a tempdir, and over a missing path a typed error that is classified `NotFound` and names the path — because an `is_ok()` on its own would also pass against a constructor that never fails. Dual-claimed with the fourteen sibling rows the sweep moved together; all fifteen are the same statement at the same boundary, and the roster is kept in one place, the table at the top of tests/port_parser_vcf_construct.rs. The `valid_chromosomes` argument this call adds is not a boundary difference: `ok($p)` inspects no argument, so the assertion holds for any defined return and would still hold if the file were empty. What that argument does is ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml's subject.

desc: use_ok InputBuffer: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer module compiles and loads
rationale: Fourth and last module-load probe. Same compile-time argument as row 1. The buffer it loads is the fixture for rows 9-12; what the buffer does with variants is asserted in t/InputBuffer.t.

desc: check class: ref($ib) is exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer, not a subclass and not a plain hashref
rationale: A blessing probe — ref() reads back the package a hashref was blessed into. docs/ledger-contract.md lists assertions about blessing and Perl object identity as the legitimate not-applicable case: a Rust value's type is fixed by its declaration and checked by the compiler, and there is no ref() to call at run time. Same assertion, same reading, at ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=3.

desc: check buffer next: InputBuffer::next returns an arrayref — a list-shaped batch rather than a scalar, hashref or object
rationale: A reftype probe on a method's return value, and only that: an empty arrayref satisfies it, so the line says nothing about how many variants were read or which. What it pins is the shape of the return, which in Rust is a compile-time fact carried by the signature — vepyr's counterpart hands back arrow RecordBatch values whose type no run-time check could contradict. ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=9 reads ref() on an accessor return the same way. The content of this same buffer is not dropped: row 12 asserts it, and row 12 is deferred, not not-applicable.

desc: get_all_regions_by_InputBuffer: the buffer filled from the test VCF resolves to exactly one 1 Mb cache region, [[21, 25]] — chromosome 21, block 25, i.e. positions 25000001-26000000
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay; the blocked-api reading was correct at the base pin and is closed rather than refuted. Perl reduces the buffer in AnnotationSource::get_all_regions_by_InputBuffer (AnnotationSource.pm:235-262) over get_regions_from_coords (:168); dfbf 391f94bd does the identical reduction over the input RecordBatches in collect_buffer_cache_regions (annotate_provider.rs:11465) via cache_regions_for_coords (:11429) and cache_region_index (:11410). All three are private at the base: re-measured in this checkout by a throwaway tests/zz_probe_w2_neg.rs naming the pre-overlay paths, which emitted error[E0603]: function `cache_region_index` is private and four more E0603 while annotate_provider::cache_lookup_column_names resolved in the same file as the positive control — so the errors are visibility, not a broken build. PINS.toml dfbf_test_overlay (aa2be930) re-exports each as a single-expression delegation under annotate_provider::test_internals, and the test calls those. analog-port and not unit-port for the reason #98 asked the porter to settle: Perl compares a one-element LIST, vepyr returns a HashSet<TranscriptCacheRegion>, so the test asserts len()==1 plus membership of (21, 25) — the whole content of a singleton — and additionally that neither neighbouring block is present, so a reduction answering only some region on 21 could not pass. The buffer is built from the committed tests/data/vep116_runner_input/test.vcf.gz (VEPs own t/testdata/input/test.vcf) with coordinates normalised by the public vep_norm_start/vep_norm_end, not by a re-typed literal. The <DEL> ORDER half of #98 is answered on n=13, which goes through cache_regions_for_coords (a Vec) instead. Mutation-checked: membership asserted on BUFFER_REGION_INDEX + 1 fails with the buffer's only region must be (21, 25); transcript in the test file header.

desc: InputBuffer min_max: the same buffer records chromosome 21 spanning 25585733-25982445 — the per-chromosome min start and max end accumulated while row 11's regions were computed
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay. min_max is a side effect of row 11 loop: get_regions_from_coords tracks (min, max) per source chromosome (AnnotationSource.pm:185-187) and get_all_regions_by_InputBuffer writes the map back onto the buffer (:260). dfbf 391f94bd carries the identical reduction as a private free fn, buffer_variant_bounds(batches) -> Option<(String, i64, i64)> at annotate_provider.rs:11362, min over start.min(end) and max over start.max(end). Private at the base and re-measured here: error[E0603]: function `buffer_variant_bounds` is private, against a resolving control in the same probe file; reachable through annotate_provider::test_internals::buffer_variant_bounds at PINS.toml dfbf_test_overlay aa2be930. analog-port rather than unit-port because Perl indexes a per-chromosome hash ($ib->min_max->{21}) while vepyr returns the chromosome inside the tuple, so the hash key and the pair are asserted together as ("21", 25585733, 25982445). The 132 records are read from the committed test.vcf.gz and normalised through the public vep_norm_start/vep_norm_end, so the pair is derived from VEPs own input file rather than transcribed. Mutation-checked: expecting BUFFER_MAX_END - 1 fails with left: ("21", 25585733, 25982445) / right: ("21", 25585733, 25982444).

desc: get_regions_from_input: the region tuples for each of the 7 $inputs cases (t/AnnotationSource.t:78-96) — 999999 and 1000000 give [[1,0]], 1000001 gives [[1,1]], the AC>GT MNV and the C>CT insertion at 1000000 each give [[1,0],[1,1]], the END=3000001 <DEL> gives [[1,0],[1,1],[1,2],[1,3]], and two single-base variants either side of the boundary give [[1,0],[1,1]] deduplicated
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay, and the order question #98 flagged is answered rather than papered over. The counterpart is cache_regions_for_coords (dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:11429-11459), which reproduces AnnotationSource.pm term for term and links #L190 at :11444; it returns a Vec in the ascending order of the inclusive walk at :194, so it — unlike the HashSet reduction n=11 uses — CAN witness the order this is_deeply asserts for the 4-region <DEL> case, and the test compares the full ordered list for all six single-record cases. The seventh case is two VCF records and its Perl expectation is the DEDUPLICATED union, so that one alone runs through collect_buffer_cache_regions, which is where dedup lives. Private at the base (error[E0603]: function `cache_regions_for_coords` is private, with a resolving control in the same probe file); reachable via annotate_provider::test_internals. Coordinates come from the public vep_norm_start/vep_norm_end for the five allele-bearing cases, and the insertion inversion (1000000 C>CT gives start 1000001, end 1000000) is pinned separately so the table cannot degrade into six copies of the SNV case. analog-port, not unit-port: the <DEL> row takes its end from INFO END=3000001, and extracting END from INFO is a different boundary that this test supplies directly rather than claims. Mutation-checked: cutting the across boundary expectation to [(1,0)] fails with left: [("1", 0), ("1", 1)] / right: [("1", 0)].

desc: use_ok AnnotationSourceAdaptor: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSourceAdaptor module compiles and loads
rationale: A module-load probe: use_ok asserts that Perl found and compiled modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm at run time. Rust settles the same question when the test crate is built — a `use` naming a missing item is E0432/E0433 and there is no binary to run — so a run-time assertion could only restate the compiler. docs/ledger-contract.md admits use_ok / can_ok / isa_ok existence probes as the legitimate not-applicable case; ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml row 1 is the same assertion on the base class.

desc: new is defined: AnnotationSourceAdaptor->new() with no arguments returns a defined blessed object
rationale: ok($asa) pins one thing: the zero-argument constructor returned a defined, true value, i.e. the `bless` inherited from BaseVEP::new (BaseVEP.pm:93 @ release/116.0) succeeded. Rust has no undef and no bless — a constructor either yields a value of its declared type or the call site does not compile — so there is no run-time definedness to assert. That vepyr has no AnnotationSourceAdaptor type at all is a separate fact, and it is recorded where it is load-bearing (rows 7-9), not smuggled in here.

desc: check class: ref($asa) is exactly the string Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSourceAdaptor
rationale: A blessing probe — ref($obj) reads back the package name a hashref was blessed into. docs/ledger-contract.md lists assertions about blessing and Perl object identity as the legitimate not-applicable case: a Rust value's type is static, nothing corresponds to calling ref() at run time, and a type-identity assertion would be a tautology the compiler already enforced.

desc: use_ok Config: Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config compiles and loads, so the remaining subtests can hand the adaptor a config object
rationale: Second module-load probe in the file, this time for the config class every later subtest needs. Same reason as row 1: in Rust the question is answered at link time, not by an assertion. Note the division of labour — what Config *does* with its options is ledger/Config.ledger.toml's business (M2 issue #28, 5 analog-port rows against tests/port_config.rs); this row only pins that the module loads.

desc: get new config object: Config->new($test_cfg->base_testing_cfg) returns a defined object
rationale: Definedness of the blessed hashref returned by Config::new (Config.pm:667 @ release/116.0) — Perl object construction, not annotation behaviour. The pinned counterpart is a plain struct: AnnotateVcfConfig (dfbf vcf_sink.rs:381-456 @ 391f94bd) with a Default impl at :458; building one cannot fail and cannot produce undef, so the failure mode this assertion guards against does not exist. Config option *resolution* is covered in ledger/Config.ledger.toml, not here.

desc: new with config: AnnotationSourceAdaptor->new({config => $cfg}) returns a defined object that carries the config in its _config slot
rationale: Row 2 with the config slot filled: BaseVEP::new (BaseVEP.pm:93 @ release/116.0) stores $config under `_config` and returns the blessed ref, and ok() asserts only that the result is defined. vepyr keeps no factory object to hold a config — AnnotateVcfConfig is passed by value into annotate_to_vcf (dfbf vcf_sink.rs:1018 @ 391f94bd) — so there is neither a `_config` slot to inspect nor a constructor that could return undef.

desc: get_all_from_cache: with the default offline test config the adaptor returns exactly one source — a Cache::Transcript whose full attribute hash matches, including dir, cache_region_size, the cache's info.txt metadata (assembly GRCh38.p5, GENCODE 24, dbSNP 149, …) and valid_chromosomes [21, 22, LRG_485]
rationale: The fixture #99 tracked is now in the repository, so this row is a port rather than a plan: tests/data/vep115_native_slice/ is a four-file, 18434-byte slice of a native (Storable) Ensembl VEP 115 cache — info.txt verbatim plus one transcript region file under each of 21/, 22/ and LRG_485/ — cut so that the crate's own contig discovery reproduces the Perl expected value literally rather than by re-derivation. get_all_from_cache (AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:111-123 @ release/116.0) delegates to CacheDir::get_all_AnnotationSources, and the assertion pins both which source was built and what the cache told it about itself; EnsemblCacheTableProvider::for_entity(EnsemblEntityKind::Transcript, EnsemblCacheOptions) at datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache table_provider.rs:470, tag v1.10.0#0d9730c83f3ac936efa1595335caee0b0e538fa1, is the vepyr side of it. analog-port and not unit-port because both halves of the contract's test move: the inputs are a different cache (115 against VEP's own t/testdata cache at GRCh38.p5 / GENCODE 24 / dbSNP 149) and the observation point is an Arrow schema plus a scanned row rather than a blessed Perl hash. The expected hash carries 17 top-level keys (:54-84) and this port asserts six of them — valid_chromosomes [21, 22, LRG_485] is TranscriptTableProvider::chromosomes() and the schema's bio.vep.chromosomes; the info hash is the source_<name> provenance columns CacheInfo derives from each info.txt source_ line (12 of Perl's 13 keys survive into 115; ESP does not); dir is the source_cache_path column; source_type 'ensembl' is the schema's bio.vep.cache_source_type; serializer_type undef, Perl's spelling of 'plain Storable', is the serializer_type column at 'storable', where CacheInfo::from_root resolves the same absent info.txt line; and cache_region_size is the exported constant VEP_CACHE_REGION_SIZE_BP at 1_000_000, which docs/ledger-contract.md admits as a witness where it settles a pair on FeatureType::rank. The other eleven — _config, gencode_basic, gencode_primary, all_refseq, sift, polyphen, everything, filter, bam, use_transcript_ref, nearest — are NOT carried, and that is the part of this row to attack: every one of them is a config-default echo (nine literally undef, filter [], _config the config back-reference), so what the is_deeply pins through them is that Config->new defaulted them off, not anything the cache produced. Measured rather than asserted, because it is a claim about vepyr's vocabulary: `grep -oh 'parse("[a-z_0-9]*")' src/*.rs` in datafusion-bio-function-vep at the pin prints 31 names, four of the eleven among them (all_refseq, everything, gencode_basic, gencode_primary) and seven absent, with check_existing as the positive control that the grep finds an option when there is one. What those four DO is a future row's claim; row 7 pins that they were not asked for. The test does not SKIP on a missing fixture: the data is checked in, so absence panics — which is exactly the defect audit/ports-compile-status.md recorded in the gathered port this replaces, where both tests returned on a SKIP line and reported ok.

desc: get_all: the aggregator returns the same single Cache::Transcript as get_all_from_cache, because with the default offline config the database and custom arms both contribute nothing
rationale: Re-examined when #99's native fixture landed and row 7 became a port, which the review ruling on that issue required. What this row adds to row 7 is the aggregator: get_all (AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:86-97 @ release/116.0) concatenates get_all_from_cache, get_all_from_database and get_all_custom and sorts the result by can_filter_vfs, and under the default test config the last two return empty lists (get_all_from_database returns [] when param('offline') is set, :140), so the list collapses to row 7's. blocked-data no longer describes anything here — the cache is committed and row 7's analogue runs against it — and what is left is the aggregator itself, which vepyr does not have: each call site constructs one typed provider per entity kind (EnsemblCacheTableProvider::for_entity, table_provider.rs:470 @ v1.10.0#0d9730c8), there is no list of annotation sources to concatenate, no can_filter_vfs rank to sort by, and neither non-cache arm exists to contribute an empty list in the first place — the closed 31-key options_json vocabulary at the pin names no custom, database, offline or no_remote, measured with its control in AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=10 (no-feature). Per docs/ledger-contract.md an operation vepyr does not perform is no-feature however easy it would be to add, and the work this row names is building the aggregator, not exporting something. Still not merged into row 7: the sort and the two empty arms are a distinct claim, and a future multi-source vepyr must reproduce it.

desc: get_all - var comes first: with check_existing=1 the first element of get_all() is a Cache::Variation, i.e. the variation source outranks the transcript source in the returned list
rationale: The ordering is mechanical, not incidental: `get_all` sorts the concatenated sources by `can_filter_vfs` descending (AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:90 @ release/116.0) and only the variation source sets that flag, so Perl's first-source-wins iteration meets variation first. vepyr keeps no ordered Vec of sources to index into, so the analogue reads the ordering off what the pipeline does with it -- which is what makes it analog and not unit. Two observations, and the second is the sharp one -- it is the one the classification rests on. With `check_existing` on, every transcript group at 21:25585733 carries the same `rs142513484`, so the variation answer is uniform across features: a property of the ROW rather than of the feature, and therefore not derived from the transcript source. That is all it licenses; an earlier draft of this rationale read it as `the lookup happened once for the row`, which review refused and rightly, because a per-feature lookup keyed on the variant's own coordinates returns the same record on every call and would produce the same output. The discriminating observation is the second: at 21:8987004, sixteen megabases from the nearest transcript in the committed cache, `Consequence` is `intergenic_variant` with an empty `Feature` and `Existing_variation` is still `rs1319575564` -- a pipeline that consulted variation AFTER the transcript source, per feature, would have nothing to hang it on and would report nothing. The control is the same input with no options: both columns empty while the transcript source's own consequences are unchanged, so the empty column is an observation rather than an empty run. `check_existing` is a real option at the pin (`VepFlags::from_options_json`, dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_provider.rs:1181-1182`, gating the `Existing_variation` field at `:356`), reachable only through the `annotate_vep` UDTF's `options_json` because `AnnotateVcfConfig` carries no such field. Was `deferred`/`blocked-data` under issue 99 -- fixture, not API, exactly as that issue said -- until `tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/` and `tests/data/vep115_reference_slice/` landed (issue 96). Distinct from Config.ledger.toml n=20, which drives `af` and asserts the option SET; this row drives `check_existing` itself and asserts where its answer shows up, so the `af` implication could regress without this test noticing.

desc: get_all_custom - invalid file: a --custom spec carrying format/short_name/type but no file= dies with 'No file was added for custom annotation source.'
rationale: The missing feature is custom annotation sources themselves: vepyr annotates from an Ensembl cache and from plugin caches, and consumes no user-supplied annotation file. The Perl guard is AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:250 @ release/116.0, one of three run before get_all_custom (:201) hands the spec to AnnotationSource::File. At the pin there is no spec to validate: AnnotateVcfConfig exposes 35 public fields (dfbf vcf_sink.rs:381-456 @ 391f94bd) and none names a custom source, and the DataFusion options_json path recognises a closed key set — `grep -oh 'parse("[a-z_0-9]*")' src/*.rs | sort -u` run in datafusion/bio-function-vep prints 31 lines, none of them custom, database, offline or no_remote. Negative claim with its control: `grep -rq 'no_remote\|get_all_custom\|custom_multi_allelic' src/` exits 1, `grep -rq 'plugin_cache_root' src/` exits 0. The only custom-anything in that crate is plugin_cache_root's custom-plugin cache (vcf_sink.rs:452-455), an unrelated mechanism.

desc: get_all_custom - invalid format: a --custom spec with file= and short_name= but no format= dies with 'No format specified for custom annotation source.'
rationale: Second of the three guards, AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:251 @ release/116.0. It pins that format is mandatory even when the file exists — VEP will not guess a parser from the extension. vepyr has no format-dispatch decision to make because it has no custom-file reader at all (see row 10 for the measured absence and its positive control); the format its cache is in is fixed by the cache, not chosen per annotation source.

desc: get_all_custom - invalid format value: format=foo dies with 'Unknown or unsupported format foo', i.e. the format string is checked against a closed map, not merely required
rationale: Unlike rows 10, 11 and 13 this throw does not live in AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm at all: get_all_custom passes the spec on and the rejection happens in AnnotationSource/File.pm:181 @ release/116.0, where %FORMAT_MAP is the closed set of readers VEP can construct (vcf, bed, gff, gtf, bigwig, …). The feature that is missing from vepyr is that whole reader family — no AnnotationSource::File::VCF / BED / GFF / GTF / BigWig equivalent exists at the pin — so there is no map to miss and no unsupported-format error to raise. Same measurement and positive control as row 10.

desc: get_all_custom - invalid options: an unrecognised key (random=2) dies naming it, 'The following options are not supported for custom annotations: random'
rationale: An allow-list check, not a parse failure: @VALID_OPTIONS (AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:206-220 @ release/116.0) enumerates the thirteen keys a --custom spec may carry, and :245 throws listing every key that is not in it — so a typo is reported rather than silently ignored. vepyr has no --custom spec, hence no key vocabulary to police (row 10 measures the absence). Note the difference from vepyr's own option discipline, which does exist and is asserted elsewhere: reject_options_json_source_selectors refuses merged/refseq in options_json (ledger/vepyr-only.ledger.toml, parquet-cache-01).

desc: get_all_custom - no_remote: with no_remote=1 a custom file= naming an http:// URL dies with 'Access to remote data files disabled', i.e. the switch is enforced at source-construction time
rationale: Two features are absent at once, and the row names both: remote annotation files (the guard at AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:252 @ release/116.0 matches file= against ^(ht|f)tp://) and the --no_remote switch that disables them. vepyr reads a local cache directory and a local plugin cache; there is no URL fetch path to gate, so the switch would have nothing to switch off. Measured with row 10's probe: `grep -rq 'no_remote' src/` in datafusion/bio-function-vep exits 1, against the positive control `grep -rq 'plugin_cache_root' src/` exit 0.

desc: use_ok AnnotationSource::File: the custom-file source base class loads — which is also what makes its $CAN_USE_TABIX_PM package variable readable by the SKIP guard on line 120
rationale: A module-load probe, the case docs/ledger-contract.md admits as not-applicable, and here it does double duty: line 120 skips the following five assertions unless $Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::File::CAN_USE_TABIX_PM is true, which presupposes the package was compiled. Both halves — that Perl found the file, and that a package variable is now visible — are Perl run-time plumbing with no Rust counterpart. The *feature* this module implements is absent from vepyr, but classifying this row not-applicable hides nothing: every row that asserts what the module does (10-14, 16-20) is no-feature and stays in the denominator.

desc: get_all_custom: a well-formed spec (file=<vcf>,short_name=test,format=vcf,type=exact) builds exactly one AnnotationSource::File::VCF, compared key-for-key over its whole attribute hash — type exact, report_coords 0, num_records 50, overlap_cutoff 0, reciprocal 0, the overlap_def sentence, gff_type transcript, custom_multi_allelic and custom_suppress_filter undef — plus the echoed copy of those under info->custom_info
rationale: The first of five rows that assert the *constructed* custom source rather than a rejection, and the strongest statement of the missing feature: it fixes the complete default attribute set of AnnotationSource::File::VCF, the class vepyr has no equivalent of. The class is chosen by %FORMAT_MAP in AnnotationSource/File.pm (:181 is the rejection arm; row 12), and the defaults it fills in come from the $opts hash at AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:254-267. Nothing at the pin constructs a per-file annotation source (row 10 measures it), so there is no attribute set to compare. vep116_delta is changed for the bookkeeping reason audit/vep-116/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.md sets out: 116.0 added 'custom_suppress_filter' => undef at line 133 of the 116.0 file, and is_deeply over a hash is exact, so the expected value differs from 115.2's even though the adaptor's behaviour does not.

desc: get_all_custom - default overlap type: the same spec with type= omitted yields type 'overlap' rather than dying or leaving it undef — the one option in the spec with a non-trivial default
rationale: Pins a default, not a rejection: AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:259 @ release/116.0 sets type => $hash{'type'} || 'overlap', so an unspecified match mode means overlap and the constructed File::VCF's info->custom_info echoes it. vepyr has no custom sources and therefore no match-mode vocabulary — exact, overlap, and the overlap_cutoff / reciprocal / distance / same_type family that goes with them exist nowhere at the pin (row 10's probe). vep116_delta changed for the same reason as row 16: 'custom_suppress_filter' => undef inserted at line 175 (audit/vep-116/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.md).

desc: get_all_custom - report_coords: coords=1 in the spec sets report_coords to 1 on the constructed source and on its info->custom_info copy, where the default (rows 16, 17) is 0
rationale: The spec key is coords but the attribute is report_coords (AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:260 @ release/116.0: report_coords => $hash{'coords'} || 0), so the row pins a rename as well as a value — a custom source can be asked to report the matched record's coordinates instead of a field value. vepyr emits CSQ fields from its cache and has no per-source reporting mode to toggle, because it has no per-source anything (row 10). vep116_delta changed: 'custom_suppress_filter' => undef inserted at line 216 (audit/vep-116/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.md).

desc: get_all_custom - fields: fields=FOO%BAR is split on % into the arrayref ['FOO','BAR'] on the constructed source, so % and not comma is the sub-delimiter inside a comma-separated --custom spec
rationale: A parsing detail with a reason: the spec itself is comma-separated (AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:228 splits on /,/), so the field list needs a different separator and % is it. What it pins is that a custom source can project named INFO fields out of its file. vepyr's nearest concept is the plugin cache, whose fields come from a manifest rather than a command-line list (plugin_cache_root, dfbf vcf_sink.rs:452-455 @ 391f94bd) — a different mechanism, not a different spelling of this one, and not reached by any assertion in this file. vep116_delta changed: 'custom_suppress_filter' => undef inserted at line 258 (audit/vep-116/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.md).

desc: get_all_custom - automated ###CHR###: one spec whose file= contains the ###CHR### token expands into TWO File::VCF sources, one per chromosome file found (test_vcf21 and test_vcf_MT), each carrying its own resolved path
rationale: The only row in the custom block where one spec does not mean one source: the ###CHR### token turns a path template into a per-chromosome fan-out, and the assertion pins both the count and each expanded path. vepyr does discover per-chromosome files, but inside the cache (discover_*_files in datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache) where the layout is the cache's own and not user-templated; there is no user-facing path template because there is no user-supplied annotation file (row 10). Classified no-feature rather than analog-port for exactly that reason: the observation point is not different, the product is. vep116_delta changed, and this is the row the audit calls out as taking TWO added lines (319 and 354) for one assertion, because its expected value is a list of two sources (audit/vep-116/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.md).

desc: get_all_from_database: in database mode (database=1, offline=0) against the homo_vepiens MultiTestDB the adaptor returns exactly one source, a Database::Transcript whose attribute hash is compared in full — core_type core, cache_region_size 50000, _species homo_vepiens, and the info hash read from the core DB (genebuild 2014-07, GENCODE 24, GRCh38.p5)
rationale: The missing feature is database mode: vepyr annotates from an on-disk Ensembl cache and has no Ensembl-core MySQL client, so the whole Database::* source hierarchy this and rows 22-29 exercise has no counterpart. get_all_from_database (AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:137 @ release/116.0) returns [] the moment param('offline') is set, which is the mode vepyr is permanently in. Measured at the pin: `grep -rqi 'mysql\|dbi:\|db_adaptor' src/` in datafusion/bio-function-vep exits 1, against the positive control `grep -rqi 'parquet' src/` exit 0. Classified no-feature and not not-applicable although the fixture is a mock DB: docs/ledger-contract.md admits mock database *handles* as not-applicable, but the value asserted here is what database mode returns — a product statement — and no-feature keeps the row in the denominator where it belongs.

desc: get_all - DB: with database=1 the aggregator returns the same single Database::Transcript as get_all_from_database — the DB arm of get_all, mirroring row 8's cache arm
rationale: Row 8 and this row are the two halves of the same dispatcher: get_all (AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:86-97 @ release/116.0) concatenates the cache, database and custom lists, and which arm is non-empty is decided by param('offline') / param('cache'). This is the database half, so it is blocked by the same absent product as row 21 rather than by row 8's missing fixture — and that is why the two rows are classified differently. Both _adaptors keys are deleted before comparison (t/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.t:433, :438), so what is asserted is the source's own attribute hash, not the live DB handles hanging off it.

desc: get_all_from_database - variation: with check_existing=1 the second element is a Database::Variation carrying failed 0 and the undef no_check_alleles / exclude_null_alleles switches — the DB counterpart of row 9's cache-side variation source
rationale: Pins that database mode adds a variation source on demand and what its defaults are: failed => 0 (do not return variants flagged failed), no_check_alleles and exclude_null_alleles unset. vepyr has no database variation source (row 21's probe). Note that vepyr does have a colocated-variant path with a failed threshold — AnnotateVcfConfig::failed (dfbf vcf_sink.rs:434 @ 391f94bd) — but it reads the cache, not a variation database, so it is the analogue of the *cache* Variation source that ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.ledger.toml owns, not of this row. Claiming it here would double-count one Rust behaviour across two ledgers.

desc: get_all_from_database - regfeat: with regulatory=1 the second element is a Database::RegFeat whose only non-inherited attribute is cell_type (undef here)
rationale: Same absent product as row 21, one source class along: no Ensembl funcgen database client exists at the pin. The row also pins cell_type as a per-source attribute of the DB regulatory source — a funcgen concept (restrict regulatory features to one cell line) with no vepyr counterpart at all. vepyr's regulatory annotation is cache-backed and is asserted in ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml (issue #12); that ledger's rows, not this one, are where the regulatory feature's presence is accounted for.

desc: get_all_from_database - SV: with check_svs=1 the second element is a Database::StructuralVariation carrying nothing but the config and cache_region_size 50000
rationale: Two absences stack here, and the row is no-feature on either: database mode (row 21's probe) and structural-variant annotation. The second is the harder one — vepyr's CSQ path has no --check_svs analogue and no structural-variant overlap source, so even the cache-mode equivalent of this row could not be written today. Recording it as no-feature rather than deferred is the honest call: nothing is blocking a port that would otherwise be written, the product does not exist.

desc: get_all_from_database - no var/reg 1: on the homo_vepiens_coreonly MultiTestDB (core DB only, no variation or funcgen DB) database mode returns exactly 1 source instead of failing
rationale: The first of four rows that pin graceful degradation rather than construction: when a species has only a core database, get_all_from_database (AnnotationSourceAdaptor.pm:137 @ release/116.0) silently omits the sources it cannot build instead of dying, and the count 1 is the whole assertion. The behaviour presupposes a per-species database inventory to be incomplete about, which vepyr has no equivalent of (row 21's probe: no MySQL client at the pin). Rows 26-29 are one property under four flag settings; each needs its own row because each turns on a different source, and this one is the baseline with no flag set.

desc: get_all_from_database - no var/reg 2: same core-only species with check_existing=1 still returns 1 source — the variation source is skipped, not faked and not fatal
rationale: The check_existing arm of the degradation property (row 26). It is the sharpest of the four because check_existing is the flag that would otherwise add the Database::Variation of row 23: asking for it on a species with no variation DB must be a no-op, not an error. No vepyr counterpart, for the reason row 21 measures — there is no database inventory that can be partial.

desc: get_all_from_database - no var/reg 3: same species with regulatory=1 (on top of check_existing) still returns 1 source — the funcgen source is skipped too
rationale: The regulatory arm of row 26's property, and note that the flags accumulate: line 494 set check_existing and it is never reset inside this block, so this row asserts 1 source with both check_existing and regulatory on. It pins that missing databases are skipped independently rather than short-circuiting after the first. Absent in vepyr for the reason row 21 measures; the cache-mode regulatory behaviour it superficially resembles belongs to ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml.

desc: get_all_from_database - no var/reg 4: same species with check_svs=1 as well still returns 1 source — with all three optional sources requested and none available, the core transcript source is still the only one built
rationale: The last arm of row 26's property and the strongest statement of it: check_existing, regulatory and check_svs are all on by this line (each set and not reset, t/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.t:494, :497, :500) and the count is still 1. The structural-variation source that check_svs would add lives on the variation database, so a species without one loses it too — which is why this row is not simply row 26 repeated. No vepyr counterpart on either count: no database mode (row 21) and no structural-variant source (row 25).

desc: BASIC TESTS: the AnnotationSource::Cache base-class module loads under `use`
rationale: A module-load probe: `use_ok` asserts only that Perl found and compiled `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::Cache` at run time. Rust answers the same question at link time — tests/port_annotation_source_cache.rs cannot build unless `datafusion_bio_function_vep::parquet_cache::detect::PartitionedParquetCache` exists at the pin (dfbf 391f94bd, parquet_cache/detect.rs:27; audit/vepyr-master/api-delta.md §4 locates it there) — so a run-time assertion here would restate the linker. Same family as the `can_ok`/`isa_ok` existence probes docs/ledger-contract.md lists as legitimately not-applicable, and the identical treatment the merged AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml gives its own n=1.

desc: BASIC TESTS: Cache->new({dir => t/testdata/cache/homo_sapiens/84_GRCh38}) returns a defined object
rationale: A constructor-truthiness probe, and the Perl makes it unfalsifiable: AnnotationSource/Cache.pm defines no `new` at all, so the call reaches `AnnotationSource::new` (AnnotationSource.pm:77-93), which copies the hashref's keys onto `$self` and returns it, over `BaseVEP::new` (BaseVEP.pm:93-118) whose body is `bless {}, $class`. A blessed hashref is always true and no branch can yield undef; the directory is not stat-ed, opened or validated anywhere on that path, so what the line pins down is Perl blessing — one of the cases docs/ledger-contract.md names as legitimately not-applicable, and how the merged AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=3/n=4 classify the same probe. Note the contrast with vepyr, whose constructor for the same concept is deliberately fallible: `PartitionedParquetCache::detect` returns `None` unless `variation/chrom_manifest.json` is readable (detect.rs:36-43). That is a stronger contract than this line asserts, and n=3's test exercises it.

desc: METHODS: `dir` get — the cache source hands back, verbatim, the directory it was constructed with
rationale: Same property, different observation point. Perl reads the value off the blessed hash through Cache.pm:72-76's `sub dir`, an accessor on a mid-tier AnnotationSource base class vepyr has no counterpart for; vepyr holds the cache directory in `PartitionedParquetCache`'s private `base_dir: PathBuf` (detect.rs:29) and exposes it through `pub fn base_dir(&self) -> &Path` (detect.rs:46). Not unit-port, because the inputs had to change: Perl's `new` accepts any string and never touches the filesystem, while `detect` (detect.rs:36-43) returns `None` unless the directory carries a readable `variation/chrom_manifest.json`, so the Rust fixture must be a cache root rather than an arbitrary path, and what comes back is a `&Path` rather than the string Perl stored. The test asserts the verbatim half of the property — `detect` does `PathBuf::from(cache_source)` and never canonicalises — and detects two independent tempdir roots, asserting each reports itself and that the two differ, so it cannot pass on a constant. The fixture's `chr21.parquet` is a placeholder byte string: this row is about which directory is retained, never about the cache being readable. In-src disclosure, per the contract's in-src convention: dfbf's own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` in `parquet_cache/detect.rs:72-137` carries three tests and **none** asserts `base_dir()` — `grep -n base_dir` over that module's lines exits 1, positive control being 8 hits in the file as a whole (:28, :37, :38, :41, :46, :47, :58, :63), every one of them outside the test module. This row's assertion therefore has no in-src twin, and the external test earns the row by pinning the *public* contract from outside the crate, which an in-src test cannot do. The fixture helper `write_variation_manifest` is adapted from that module's `write_entity` (detect.rs:76-84, same `parquet-shard-placeholder` bytes) — the same lineage as tests/port_cache_layout.rs's helper. Two further nails in detailed_plans/AnnotationSource_Cache.md's premise that CacheDir.md would carry this property: the analogue it proposes, `CacheInfo::from_root(&path).cache_root == path`, is unreachable from any external crate — `mod info;` is private in datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache v1.10.0 (lib.rs:15) and `CacheInfo` is `pub(crate)` (info.rs:48), so a compiled probe importing it fails with E0603 ("module `info` is private") — and CacheDir.ledger.toml is still 44/44 skeleton.

desc: METHODS: `dir` set — dir('/tmp') re-points the cache source at a new directory and echoes the new value back
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay; the blocked-api reading was correct at the base pin and is closed rather than refuted. Perl's sub dir is the classic get/set form (Cache.pm:72-76, $self->{dir} = shift if @_; return $self->{dir};), so one call both re-points the annotation source and returns the new value -- run-time re-pointing, the property n=3 does not cover. The MUTATION half was already public: LookupProvider::set_cache_root(&mut self, root: impl Into<PathBuf>) at lookup_provider.rs:199-201, under the default parquet-cache feature. The READ-BACK half was the blocker: cache_root is a private Option<PathBuf> at :87 with no accessor, and PartitionedParquetCache's base_dir is read-only (detect.rs:36-67). PINS.toml dfbf_test_overlay (aa2be930) adds LookupProvider::cache_root(&self) -> Option<&Path> at :344, one field read behind cfg(all(feature = "test-internals", feature = "parquet-cache")). analog-port and not unit-port because vepyr SPLITS what Perl fuses: set_cache_root returns () and cache_root() reads back, so the single Perl call becomes two. What the row is about -- that the mutation takes effect and is observable -- survives intact, and the test asserts it twice over (None before, then two different roots in sequence) so a setter that stored only its first argument, or ignored the argument, would fail. Note the two halves of Perl's one accessor land on two different vepyr objects, which is deliberate rather than sloppy: the value a run is DETECTED from lives on PartitionedParquetCache (n=3, base_dir), and the value a lookup can be RE-POINTED to at run time lives on LookupProvider; only the second can be set. The provider is built from the minimum LookupProvider::new validates -- a variation schema carrying schema_contract::REQUIRED_VARIATION_COLUMNS (schema_contract.rs:10-16) -- and no cache is read, which matches Perl handing its own accessor /tmp. Mutation-checked: expecting the FIRST root after the second set fails with left: Some("/tmp/second-root") / right: Some("/tmp/first-root").

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Cache::RegFeat annotation-source module loads under `use`
rationale: A module-load probe: `use_ok` asserts only that Perl found and compiled the class at runtime. Rust answers the same question at link time — `tests/port_cache_layout.rs` cannot build unless `datafusion_bio_function_vep::parquet_cache::detect::PartitionedParquetCache` exists at the pin — so a runtime assertion here would restate the linker. Same family as the `can_ok`/`isa_ok` existence probes docs/ledger-contract.md names as legitimately not-applicable.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config module loads under `use` before a config object is built
rationale: The second module-load probe, for `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config`. vepyr's configuration is the `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` struct, whose existence the test crate proves by compiling against it; there is no runtime load step that could fail and therefore nothing to assert. See n=1.

desc: BASIC TESTS: Config->new returns a defined object for the base testing config
rationale: A constructor-truthiness probe — it asserts `Config->new` returned something other than `undef`. vepyr's analogue `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` is a plain struct built by literal initialisation, which is infallible and cannot yield a null; the Rust type system carries at compile time the guarantee this line checks at runtime. Perl-runtime plumbing, per docs/ledger-contract.md's not-applicable list.

desc: BASIC TESTS: Cache::RegFeat->new returns a defined annotation source for dir + cache_region_size
rationale: Reclassified by the #120 sweep (Ruling 2 from the tier-2 batch review, recorded on that issue): this is the constructor-probe ruling's THIRD line, not its first. What `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::Cache::RegFeat` denotes is the regulatory annotation source over a cache directory, and vepyr HAS that source, under a different type — `RegulatoryFeatureTableProvider`. The named test is a live test for exactly that property: it constructs the provider over the v84-shaped fixture cache and `.expect`s success (tests/port_cache_dir.rs:392-393), then — as the control that makes the positive arm mean anything — constructs it over a transcript-only cache built from the same info.txt and asserts the refusal names `No source files discovered for RegulatoryFeature` (`discovery.rs:103-105` and `table_provider.rs:208-214` in `bio-format-ensembl-cache` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8). Dual-claimed with ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=33, which asserts the same property at the same boundary — the regulatory source is constructible exactly when the cache carries regulatory files — as docs/ledger-contract.md §"dual-claim across ledgers" requires. What does not survive is the `cache_region_size => 1000000` argument, whose absence is n=8's and n=10's subject; `ok($c)` does not inspect it, so it is not a boundary difference here. The previous not-applicable put a real coverage claim outside the denominator, which is the direction the contract says to be strictest about.

desc: METHODS: the RegFeat cache reports `storable` as its on-disk serializer
rationale: Same property — which serialization format the regulatory cache is stored in — read through a different channel. Perl exposes it as a `serializer_type` accessor returning `storable`; vepyr has no such accessor because the format is not pluggable, so the format is observable only in the artefact the resolver hands back: `PartitionedParquetCache::context_path("regulatory", chrom)` yields a path whose extension is `parquet`, which the named test asserts. The expected value necessarily differs (`storable` vs `parquet`), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The fixture is deliberately hollow — `write_entity` writes the literal bytes `parquet-shard-placeholder` — so this row and n=6/7/9/16 assert path and manifest *resolution* only, never that a real parquet is readable. This row is also the weakest of the three suffix/path claims: n=7's `assert_eq!` against a fully constructed path subsumes both it and n=6, which assert only the extension. They are kept as separate rows because Perl asserts them separately, not because the Rust adds three independent checks.

desc: METHODS: the RegFeat cache's per-region dump files carry the `gz` suffix
rationale: The Perl pins the file extension the cache writes and reads (`gz`, from the gzip-wrapped Storable dumps). vepyr's per-chrom files end in `.parquet`, and the same claim is made where vepyr exposes it — on the string the resolver returns. Distinct from n=5 in the Perl (suffix and serializer are separate accessors) and distinct in the Rust (`ends_with(".parquet")` on the whole path vs `Path::extension`), so the two rows are not one assertion counted twice — but both are subsumed by n=7's full-path `assert_eq!`, and like it they observe a placeholder fixture, so what is asserted is resolution, not readability.

desc: METHODS: get_dump_file_name(chr, region) builds <dir>/1/1-100_reg.gz — the per-chrom, per-1-Mb-block path scheme
rationale: Reclassified by the #120 sweep, against the sibling `AnnotationSource_Cache_Transcript.t` n=8, which was corrected to no-feature in-chain on the identical assertion; this row is the merged half of that pair, and the sweep is where the two are made to agree. The discriminator is the one docs/ledger-contract.md's dual-claim ruling states in its `Variation.t:186` worked case, and which the recorded `AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.t` n=5 ruling applies: does the expected file name contain the REGION? Here it does — `1-100_reg.gz` — so the assertion's whole content is that changing the region changes which file is opened. `PartitionedParquetCache::context_path(context_type, chrom)` (parquet_cache/detect.rs:62-68 @ dfbf 391f94bd) has no region parameter, so nothing it returns can vary with one, and the test that named this row could not fail if only this behaviour regressed — which is precisely the hollow claim the contract refuses. Only the region-DISCARDING form (`all_vars.gz`, VariationTabix n=5, where the region argument is accepted and thrown away) is a legitimate analogue. The absent feature is per-(chrom, 1-Mb-region) dump-file addressing: `ChromDatasetEntry` maps a chromosome to exactly one dataset, so the region dimension does not exist to be resolved, and supplying it means re-partitioning the parquet cache rather than writing a test. What survives — that a locus resolves to one named file rather than a directory scan, and that the name is per-chromosome — is n=5 and n=6. `tests/port_cache_layout.rs::regfeat_context_path_for_regulatory_returns_per_chrom_parquet_path` is deliberately left in place and unnamed, as resolution-only evidence of exactly that boundary; the gate stays green because the orphan rule is per file and other rows name port_cache_layout.rs. Same disposition as the transcript sibling, whose n=8 keeps `transcript_context_path_returns_per_chrom_parquet_path` the same way. CORRECTION (executed re-audit 2026-08-31): the sentence this rationale used to carry — that vepyr has no block dimension — was false, and is replaced by the measurement. vepyr's NATIVE-cache reader does carry the per-(chrom, 1-Mb-region) dimension: `datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache` v1.10.0 discovers a cache by parsing `<start>-<end>.gz` and `<chr>_<start>-<end>_var.gz` region-file names (`discovery.rs::looks_like_region_file_name`, `:198-208`), and the names are load-bearing — renaming the committed slice's `21/12000001-13000000.gz` to `21/all.gz` makes the cache undiscoverable (`No source files discovered for Transcript under …`). What is absent is COMPOSITION, which is what `get_dump_file_name` is: `discovery.rs` only ever parses names it finds on disk (`grep -n 'format!(' discovery.rs` → 2 hits, both error strings; positive control, `grep -c storable discovery.rs` → 18). The category is unchanged for that reason.

desc: METHODS: get_dump_file_name's 3-arg arity (chr, start, end) normalises to the same path as the 2-arg (chr, 'start-end') form
rationale: What this row adds over n=7 is arity-normalisation: two spellings of the same 1-Mb block must resolve to one file. vepyr has no block dimension to spell — `ChromDatasetEntry` maps a chromosome to a single file and `context_path` takes exactly `(entity, chrom)` with no coordinates — so there is no second arity and no normalisation rule to exhibit. The absent feature is per-(chrom, 1-Mb-region) dump-file addressing; supplying it would mean re-partitioning the parquet cache, not writing a test. The category is unchanged for that reason.

desc: METHODS: get_dump_file_name with no chromosome dies with 'No chromosome' instead of building a path
rationale: Same property — an unusable chromosome argument must be refused, not silently turned into a path that fails later — through Rust's error channel instead of Perl's. `context_path("regulatory", "")` returns `None`, and the named test also covers the neighbouring case of an existing entity with an absent chromosome (`chr99`). Resolution only: the fixture's shards are placeholder bytes, so a `Some` here proves a file was found, not that it could be read.

desc: METHODS: get_dump_file_name with a chromosome but no region dies with 'No region'
rationale: This row is specifically about the *region* argument being mandatory. vepyr's resolver has no region parameter, so there is no argument that can be omitted and no error condition to raise; the `chr99` half of `regfeat_context_path_with_empty_chrom_returns_none` covers a missing *chromosome*, which is n=9, not this. The absent feature is the same one as n=8: 1-Mb-block addressing.
