desc: annotate_InputBuffer - display_consequence: the annotated variant's most severe consequence over its transcript set is missense_variant
rationale: `display_consequence` is a reduction: the most severe SO term across every TranscriptVariation the variant collected. vepyr has no VariationFeature to hang an accessor on, but it has both halves of the reduction in public API at dfbf 391f94bd — `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::evaluate_variant_with_context` (transcript_consequence.rs:1154) returns one `TranscriptConsequence` per overlapping transcript, and `so_terms::most_severe_term` (so_terms.rs:294-300) reduces by `SoTerm::rank`, VEP's own severity order. **The composition of the two is the test's, not the product's**: no shipped item named `display_consequence` exists, so what this row claims is that the two public pieces compose to VEP's accessor, and a reviewer who thinks the composition is wrong should reject the row rather than the test. The named test annotates one substitution against two overlapping transcripts, one of which it makes missense and the other 3'-UTR, so the reduction has something to choose between, and asserts `missense_variant` plus the `D/A` / `gAt/gCt` amino-acid and codon evidence behind it. The inputs are synthetic rather than the chr21 v115 block, which is why this is `analog-port` and not `unit-port`; the fixture-bound half of the same Perl block, how many transcripts the first VF collected, is n=69.

desc: with filter - filtered transcript absent: `filter => 'stable_id ne ENST00000352957'` removes that transcript from the variant's annotations
rationale: This is VEP's `--transcript_filter`: a per-transcript predicate written as a small expression language over transcript attributes (`stable_id ne …`), applied while the annotation source hands features to the buffer. vepyr has no such thing. Measured over the pinned crate, `grep -rniI 'transcript_filter'` returns **0** hits against **32** for `gencode_basic` as the positive control that the search reaches the tree, and the transcript-selection predicate it does have (`passes_transcript_selection`, annotate_provider.rs:7517-7550) reads fixed flags only — there is no place to put a user expression. The missing feature is an expression-driven transcript filter; the *consequence* of filtering, which is what the next line asserts, is n=72 and does have an analogue.

desc: with filter - display_consequence: with the missense transcript filtered out, the same variant falls back to 3_prime_UTR_variant
rationale: Separable from n=71, and the separation is the point: n=71 is the filter *expression*, which vepyr does not have, while this row is the *recomputation* — with the transcript that carried the missense gone, the most-severe reduction must fall back to the next term rather than going empty or holding a stale value. The named test reaches the reduced set by building it instead of filtering by expression, then asserts `3_prime_UTR_variant` through the same `evaluate_variant_with_context` + `most_severe_term` composition n=70 uses — a composition the test performs, not one the product ships, so the same caveat applies as at n=70. Same property, different observation point, and the half that is not observed here is recorded as absent rather than quietly claimed.

desc: TREE: _tree_coords_filename resolves to <dir>/transcript_gene_tss.txt, the auxiliary file the nearest-tree is built from
rationale: VEP materialises its nearest-feature tree as a flat text side-car in the cache directory — one line per transcript with its TSS, gene and symbol — and this row pins the file's name and location. vepyr builds no such artefact: its interval structure is `PreparedContext::tx_trees`, a `HashMap<String, COITree>` assembled in memory from the transcript rows for the buffer being annotated (transcript_consequence.rs:1029-1041). Measured over `datafusion/bio-function-vep/src`: `grep -rniI 'transcript_gene_tss\|tss'` returns **0** hits, against **44** for `mane_select` as the positive control that the search reaches the tree. The missing feature is a persisted transcript-coordinate side-car; n=74 through n=77 are the four assertions about its lifecycle and contents.

desc: TREE: tree_file generates the side-car on first call when it is absent from the cache directory
rationale: The row after n=73 asserts the *side effect*: the Perl unlinks the file, calls `tree_file`, and checks it now exists. That is lazy materialisation of a cache artefact by the annotation source — a write into `dir_cache`. vepyr never writes into the cache directory at all during annotation; the tree is rebuilt per buffer in memory, so there is no first call that creates anything and nothing on disk whose existence could be tested. See n=73 for the missing feature and the measurement.

desc: TREE: the generated side-car has a readable mtime, recorded before the regeneration check
rationale: A `stat()` on the file VEP just wrote, capturing the baseline that n=76 compares against. It is Perl-runtime filesystem plumbing in form, but its subject is the same absent artefact rather than the Perl runtime, so docs/ledger-contract.md's SKIP-block corollary — a probe *of* the absent thing stays `no-feature` — applies rather than `not-applicable`. Without a side-car there is no mtime.

desc: TREE: a second tree_file call reuses the existing side-car instead of rewriting it — the mtime is unchanged
rationale: The substance of the n=74/n=75/n=76 sequence: materialisation is idempotent, so an annotation run pays the tree-building cost once per cache rather than once per invocation. vepyr's economics are different by construction — the COITree is built per input buffer from rows it has already read for the annotation itself, so there is no cross-run artefact to reuse and no invalidation rule to exhibit. Building one is the missing feature; until then this row has no observable.

desc: TREE: md5_hex of the whole side-car equals 271bab11eab4624937c69817abc6588d — its bytes are pinned exactly
rationale: The strongest form the previous four rows could take: not just that the file exists and is reused, but that its bytes are exactly these. It is doubly unreachable — there is no side-car (n=73), and even the in-memory structure that replaces it has no serialised form to hash, since `PreparedContext::tx_trees` holds `coitrees` nodes rather than text. Byte-exact digests of a serialisation vepyr does not perform are also the one thing the porting recipe lists as an explicit anti-goal (`detailed_plans/AnnotationSource_Cache_Transcript.md`, mapping row #44).

desc: TREE: transcript_tree() really hands back a Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::TranscriptTree
rationale: RULING R1, second bullet: a class readback where the class denotes a capability vepyr has. It does — a per-chromosome interval structure over the source transcripts, as `PreparedContext::tx_trees`, which `ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml` already ports through `tests/port_transcript_tree.rs` — so the readback restates a compile-time fact, a Rust constructor's return type being its class. Note this is a different call from n=73's: `transcript_tree()` returns the object, `tree_file` returns the side-car it was built from, and only the side-car is absent.

desc: TREE: the tree reports the chromosome set of the annotation source that built it — [21, 22], both of the source's valid_chromosomes
rationale: vepyr keeps no chromosome list to read back: the set exists only as the key set of `PreparedContext::tx_trees`, built by `normalize_chrom(&tx.chrom)` over the source transcripts (transcript_consequence.rs:1029-1041), and the named test asserts exactly that key set on a multi-chromosome source. The claim is shared with `ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml` n=9 under the dual-claim ruling in docs/ledger-contract.md, which permits it only when property *and* boundary are identical — they are, and the Perl says so itself: `TranscriptTree.pm:108` populates the tree's list with `$self->valid_chromosomes($as->valid_chromosomes)`, so `TranscriptTree.t` n=9 and this row read the same propagation off the same accessor, once from the tree's own constructor and once through `$c->transcript_tree()`. Applying the ruling's test — could that Rust test fail if only this row's behaviour regressed? — yes: a tree that lost a source chromosome fails it either way.

desc: TREE: get_nearest with no type argument dies with 'No type'
rationale: Argument validation on `get_nearest`, VEP's `--nearest` implementation. vepyr's VEP annotator has no nearest-feature lookup to validate arguments for: measured over `datafusion/bio-function-vep/src`, `grep -rniI 'nearest'` returns **0** hits against **44** for `mane_select` as the positive control, and there is no `NEAREST` CSQ column in its output vocabulary. Being precise about the near-miss, because it looks closer than it is: a nearest-interval primitive does exist one crate over — `datafusion-bio-function-ranges` carries 94 `nearest` hits, 15 of them naming its `NearestIntervalIndex` — but `bio-function-vep` declares that crate under **`[dev-dependencies]`** (Cargo.toml:45), so it is not linked into the shipped annotator at all and no production path could call it even if one wanted to. docs/ledger-contract.md is explicit that an operation vepyr does not perform is `no-feature` "however easy it would be to add", so cheapness of the fix does not move the row. n=80 through n=90 are the eleven assertions this absence covers.

desc: TREE: get_nearest with an unrecognised type ('foo') dies with 'Invalid type'
rationale: The second validation row: the type argument is not merely required, it is closed — only `transcript`, `gene` and `symbol` are accepted, which is what makes n=82 through n=84 a complete enumeration rather than samples. vepyr has no such vocabulary because it has no `--nearest`. See n=80 for the measurement.

desc: TREE: get_nearest(chr21:1, 'transcript') returns [ENST00000419219] — the nearest transcript to a position far outside any feature
rationale: The first of the three type modes, and the one that defines the semantics: from a position with no overlap at all, the tree walks outward and returns the single closest transcript by TSS distance. vepyr emits nothing comparable — there is no NEAREST CSQ field and no distance-ranked fallback when a variant overlaps no transcript; it reports the variant as intergenic and stops. See n=80.

desc: TREE: get_nearest(chr21:1, 'gene') returns [ENSG00000154719] — the same lookup projected to the gene of the nearest transcript
rationale: The second type mode. It is not a restatement of n=82: the projection from transcript to gene is where two transcripts of one gene must collapse to a single answer, which is a distinct behaviour from picking the nearest transcript. Absent for the same reason (n=80), and absent as a whole rather than as a projection, since there is no nearest transcript to project from.

desc: TREE: get_nearest(chr21:1, 'symbol') returns [MRPL39] — the same lookup projected to the gene symbol
rationale: The third and last type mode, and the one the end-to-end row n=90 exercises. It differs from n=83 in what it must do when a gene has no symbol, a case the `symbol` projection has to decide and the `gene` projection never meets. See n=80.

desc: TREE: get_nearest on chr20 — a chromosome the tree does not carry — returns an empty list rather than dying
rationale: The out-of-range case: an unknown chromosome is answered with no result, not an error and not a nearest feature from some other contig. That is a real design decision about a lookup vepyr does not have. Distinct from n=82 in the same way an empty tree is distinct from a distant query — see `tests/port_transcript_tree.rs::fetch_on_an_unpopulated_tree_returns_nothing`, which covers the *overlap* query's empty case for `TranscriptTree.t` and cannot stand in here, because `nearest` and `fetch` are different operations and only `fetch` exists. See n=80.

desc: TREE: get_nearest at chr21:25607517 returns [ENST00000352957] — a position inside a transcript reports that transcript
rationale: The overlap case, which `nearest` must handle as distance zero rather than by walking outward past the containing feature. vepyr's interval query does have an overlap notion — that is exactly what `PreparedContext::tx_trees` is queried for — but overlap is where `nearest` and `fetch` coincide, and the row's content is `nearest`'s treatment of it. Claiming the tree-fetch test for this row would claim the one case in which the two agree and say nothing about the eleven-row block. See n=80.

desc: TREE: get_nearest over chr21:25607514-25607519, a range straddling the same transcript's edge, still returns [ENST00000352957]
rationale: The partial-overlap case: a query wider than a single base must not be split into per-base lookups or return the feature twice. Absent with the rest of `nearest` (n=80).

desc: TREE: get_nearest with an insertion's inverted coordinates (start 25607517 > end 25607516) returns [ENST00000352957]
rationale: VEP represents an insertion as `start = end + 1`, so every coordinate consumer has to accept a range whose end precedes its start. This row pins that `get_nearest` does. The convention itself is alive in vepyr — `VariantInput::from_vcf` normalises VCF anchor bases into VEP-style coordinates (transcript_consequence.rs:34) — but the consumer this row is about does not exist. See n=80.

desc: TREE: the other insertion orientation (start 25607518 > end 25607517) also returns [ENST00000352957]
rationale: The second insertion offset, one base along, so the pair pins that the inversion is handled by normalising the range rather than by a special case that happens to work at one coordinate. Absent with the rest of `nearest` (n=80).

desc: TREE: with --nearest symbol, annotate_InputBuffer stamps every one of the 20 buffered variants with its nearest gene symbol (MRPL39 / JAM2 / GABPA)
rationale: The end-to-end row of the block, and the one that would matter most to a user: twenty positions, each mapped to the symbol VEP would print in the `NEAREST` column. It stands for all twenty cases in the one `is_deeply`. vepyr's CSQ vocabulary has no `NEAREST` column to carry any of them, which is the same absence as n=80 seen from the output side rather than the API side — and the reason no amount of cache would help, so this is `no-feature` rather than `blocked-data` even though it is an annotation-run assertion like n=69.

desc: SEREAL: a source built with serializer_type => 'sereal' reports sereal, not the storable default
rationale: RECLASSIFIED 2026-08-31 by executed measurement, from `no-feature`. The rationale that stood here — 'vepyr has one on-disk format: `PartitionedParquetCache` resolves `.parquet` and nothing else, and there is no serializer-selection parameter anywhere' — reasoned about the wrong layer. It is true of the ANNOTATION cache and false of the NATIVE-cache reader, which is the layer this Perl line is about, and which `ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml` n=7 already ports as `analog-port` for the `storable` arm of this very accessor — so the corpus was asserting both halves of a contradiction. Resolved in favour of the measurement. `datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache` v1.10.0 carries a text-payload decode module for each (`src/decode/storable.rs`, 58 lines behind a `JSON:` prefix, and `src/decode/sereal.rs`, 57 behind `SRL1`) — twin stubs, neither of them a reader of a Perl serialisation — reads the declaration from `info.txt` (`info.rs:105-107`, four accepted spellings, defaulting to `storable` at `:164`) and admits exactly VEP's two-value vocabulary (`table_provider.rs:445`). The port asserts the selection behaviourally rather than by reading the field, because a cache declaring `sereal` over Storable bytes cannot be scanned — which is the proof: the identical committed bytes decode under the default declaration and stop decoding under `sereal`, the refusal naming Storable's own `pst0` magic, and `msgpack` is refused by name. `analog-port` and not `unit-port`: Perl builds a real Sereal cache and reads a field back; here one Storable slice is re-declared three ways and the decoder selection is observed. CORRECTED 2026-09-02 on review: an earlier draft of this line called that pair "BOTH decoders". What actually reads a native cache is `src/decode/storable_binary.rs` (1471 lines, naming Storable's `pst0` seven times), which `physical_exec.rs:707` enters only when `serializer_type == Some("storable")` — so Storable has a binary path and Sereal has none. That is why `AnnotationSource_Cache_Transcript.ledger.toml` n=93-96 are `no-feature` while this row stays `analog-port`: what this row asserts is the selection, and the named test observes it.

desc: SEREAL: the sereal source's file_suffix is `sereal`, so dump names follow the serializer
rationale: The counterpart of n=6 inside the sereal block, and the row that shows the two accessors move together: choosing a serializer changes the file names, not only the codec. With one format there is nothing that could disagree. See n=91.

desc: SEREAL: deserializing a sereal dump yields the same top-level hash shape as the storable path
rationale: RE-CLASSIFIED 2026-09-02 back to `no-feature`, by probing the decoder the previous rationale leaned on. That rationale said the second serializer was already there and only a Sereal-encoded artefact was missing; the measurement says the opposite. At the pinned formats revision `ae7f5669` `datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache`'s `src/decode/sereal.rs` is 57 lines whose entire body is `payload.strip_prefix("SRL1")` followed by `serde_json::from_str` — an ASCII marker over JSON, which is not the Sereal format; the file beside it, `src/decode/storable_binary.rs`, is 1471 lines and recognises Storable's own `pst0`, which is what a decoder of a Perl serialisation looks like in this crate. The corpus's own Sereal fixture at the pinned VEP ref `57ea5c52` (`t/testdata/cache/sereal/homo_sapiens/84_GRCh38/21/25000001-26000000.sereal`) opens `3d f3 72 6c 23` — binary Sereal v3 — and is not valid UTF-8, so it never reaches `decode_payload`, whose payload parameter is `&str`; and `physical_exec.rs:707` enters the real streaming parser only when `serializer_type == Some("storable")`. No crate named `sereal` occurs in any `Cargo.toml` or in `Cargo.lock`, with `flate2` as the positive control for that same probe. Handing vepyr the fixture #491 asked for therefore changes nothing: reading a Sereal dump is an operation vepyr does not perform, and the contract makes an absent operation `no-feature` however easy it would be to add ("Absent operation vs present-but-private state"). n=91 ports the SELECTION of a serializer; nothing ports the decoding of one. This row's subject is the top-level shape `deserialize_from_file` restores from a Sereal dump — vepyr restores nothing from one, so there is no shape to compare. The corpus already reads this way elsewhere in the same suite: `AnnotationSource_Cache_Transcript.ledger.toml` n=20-25 are the same `deserialize_from_file` re-run under the two alternative gunzip backends and have carried this category throughout — the 2026-08-31 pass moved the Sereal siblings and left those, which is the inconsistency this restores.

desc: SEREAL: the per-chromosome array survives the sereal round trip
rationale: RE-CLASSIFIED 2026-09-02 back to `no-feature`: the missing part is the decoder, not the artefact. `src/decode/sereal.rs` at the pinned formats revision `ae7f5669` is a 57-line `SRL1`-prefix-plus-JSON stub, and the corpus's own Sereal dump opens `3d f3 72 6c 23` and is not valid UTF-8, so no supplier of a fixture can make this assertion runnable; the full measurement is on n=93. This row's subject is the per-chromosome ARRAY inside that restored hash, which does not exist because the hash does not.

desc: BASIC TESTS: use_ok loads Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::Cache::Variation, the class the whole file exercises
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2: a `use_ok` row is not-applicable unconditionally. The reason is not the usual one, that the compiler already carries the fact -- it is that no Rust design contains a runtime module-load assertion at all. `use_ok` tests Perl's own loader: that `require` found the file, compiled it, and ran its `import`. Rust performs no module load at run time that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. The class's absence-or-presence is not lost by this: what `Cache::Variation` does is counted by the rows that exercise it (n=4 through n=32, n=38 through n=54), and counting the load line as well would count the same fact twice.

desc: new is defined: Cache::Variation->new({config, dir, cache_region_size => 1000000, cols => var_cols}) constructs VEP's DEFAULT offline variation source over a cache directory
rationale: The `ok($obj)` constructor ruling in docs/ledger-contract.md decides by what the class denotes. `Cache::Variation` denotes VEP's DEFAULT offline variation-cache source -- the one `Cache::VariationTabix` is the alternative to -- and that is a capability vepyr has under a different type, so this row takes the ruling's third branch, not the `no-feature` its tabix sibling takes at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=4 (whose rationale states the split: `vepyr has one shape, per-chrom parquet resolved by PartitionedParquetCache::context_path, and no tabix-backed cache reader at all`). The vepyr constructor is `PartitionedParquetCache::detect(dir)`, which is fallible and resolves a cache root into a per-entity resolver; the named test's fixture helper `tmp_variation_layout` (tests/port_cache_layout.rs:198-206) calls it over a tempdir holding only a `variation` entity and `.expect(...)`s the `Ok`, then asserts the constructed object resolves variation/chr21 to a path ending in `.parquet` -- i.e. that what was constructed is in fact a parquet variation cache, which is the closest vepyr comes to the Perl's blessed-and-defined. Two arguments of the Perl constructor have no counterpart and are accounted for elsewhere rather than smuggled in here: `cache_region_size => 1000000` is the 1-Mb block dimension (n=19, n=20, n=22, all no-feature) and `cols` is the delimited-text column list (n=23, no-feature).

desc: filter_variation pass: a cache record carrying failed => 0 survives the default filter and is kept as an existing variant
rationale: Channel, and why analog-port rather than unit-port: Perl calls `filter_variation({...})` DIRECTLY on the annotation source and reads its truthiness. vepyr has no per-record predicate an external crate can call -- the same rule is `if failed > allowed_failed { continue; }` inside the lookup (dfbf 391f94bd cache/lookup_exec.rs:1219, co-located arm at :1160), fed by `AnnotateVcfConfig::failed` (vcf_sink.rs:434) serialised at :587-590 and read back as `allowed_failed` with `unwrap_or(0)` (annotate_provider.rs:5221-5225) -- so `kept` and `dropped` are observed as a non-empty or empty `Existing_variation` CSQ cell after an `annotate_to_vcf` run. UNBLOCKED BY A FIXTURE REBUILD, not by re-reading the old one. The previous rationale for this row named the blocker precisely -- 0 of the committed shard's 16666 records carried `failed = true` -- and kept it executable in tests/port_cache_variation_dump_records.rs::the_committed_shard_carries_no_failed_record so it would go red the day such a record landed. It has: tools/build_micro_cache.sh gained a ninth window, `21:25491000-25492000`, 330 rows, and the shard is now 16996 rows carrying EXACTLY ONE QC-failed record -- rs11399548 at 21:25491565-25491564, `-/C/NC/TCACAATTCTTGACCTCCTGGAAACTGTAGC/TCC`. Finding it was not free: chr21 holds 170 failed rows out of 14571914 and almost all are failed BECAUSE their alleles are unusable (25 of shape `L/LNL`, 10 `dbSNP_novariation`, 9 `-/N`), so no legal VCF input can match them; rs11399548 is the only one both inside the 25-26 Mb transcript block and carrying an N-free ALT. The probe test is renamed `the_committed_shard_carries_exactly_one_failed_record` and now pins the count AND the identity, because a second failed record would put a second name in the very cell these rows read. Positive controls that the Boolean read is sound and the window changed nothing else: 178 `somatic` and 252 `phenotype_or_disease` rows, both unchanged. See tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/PROVENANCE.md, section `The ninth window is cut for a PROPERTY, not a coordinate`. THE DIFFICULTY OF THIS ROW, stated because it is what a reviewer should check: a filter that did NOTHING AT ALL would also keep a `failed = 0` record, so asserting `rs142513484 comes back` proves nothing on its own -- which is exactly why the previous rationale refused to port it even though every committed record was `failed = false` and every one of them did come back. What separates the two readings is the OTHER row of the same annotation: 21:25491564 is dropped in the very same `annotate_to_vcf` call, so the named test asserts both cells from ONE run and the pair is the assertion. The record's `failed = 0` is read off the shard rather than assumed (the CSQ output does not carry it), because the Perl's subject is a record whose `failed` field is 0. Mutation-checked: expecting `rs11399548` in the dropped cell turns it red, and so does flipping the `failed = false` assertion on rs142513484.

desc: NOVEL TESTS: use_ok loads Bio::EnsEMBL::Variation::VariationFeature, the ensembl-variation class the compare_existing inputs are built from
rationale: A module-load probe on a class from ensembl-variation rather than ensembl-vep, loaded so :65-70 can build the `$input` object the compare_existing rows use. R2 is unconditional and does not turn on which distribution the class comes from: Rust has no run-time module load, so the assertion has no counterpart in any Rust design. The behaviour that matters here -- what the matcher does with that input's allele string, position and strand -- is n=9 through n=18, which are classified on their own merits and are where the coverage claim lives.

desc: compare_existing exact match: input A/G at 10/+1 against an existing A/G record at 10/+1 matches on the single shared ALT, reported as a_index 0 / a_allele G / b_index 0 / b_allele G
rationale: Same inputs, same expected value. Perl's `compare_existing` (modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/AnnotationType/Variation.pm:146-206 @ release/116.0) is, once its three special-case branches are past -- unknown alleles, no_check_alleles, exclude_null_alleles, none of which this row reaches -- a single delegation to `get_matched_variant_alleles({allele_string, pos, strand}, {allele_string, pos, strand})` at :168-180. dfbf 391f94bd carries a PUBLIC, same-named, source-equivalent port of that delegate: `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles` (src/allele.rs:203), taking `VariantAlleleInput { allele_string, pos, strand }` (:20) per side and returning `MatchedVariantAllele { a_allele, a_index, b_allele, b_index }` (:12) -- the same three fields in and the same four out. Its own doc comment names `compare_existing()` and links the Ensembl Variation source it was ported from. The named test passes the Perl's own literals (A/G at pos 10 strand +1 on both sides, from t/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.t:65-77) and asserts the whole result with `assert_eq!` against the Perl's whole expected list, not by containment. What the Rust does not re-observe, stated rather than hidden: `compare_existing`'s shallow copy of the existing record -- the `%$existing` half of Perl's `is_deeply` expectation is the literal input hash built four lines earlier, and vepyr writes matched alleles into an Arrow column rather than into a copied hash. Measured: `cargo test --test port_compare_existing` -> `test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed`, with no cache and no fixture.

desc: compare_existing exact match from multiple: with the input widened to A/G/T against the same A/G record, exactly one match is reported -- the shared G at input index 0 -- and the unmatched second input ALT neither suppresses it nor appears in it
rationale: The multi-ALT half of n=9's claim, and the reason it is a separate row: a matcher that returned the first ALT regardless, or that gave up on an input carrying an unmatched ALT, would pass n=9 and fail here. Same public delegate and the same reasoning as n=9 -- `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles` (src/allele.rs:203 @ dfbf 391f94bd) -- with the input allele string set to A/G/T at t/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.t:93 and the existing record left at A/G; the named test asserts the Perl's whole expected list with `assert_eq!`. Not redundant with the dependency's own multiallelic test: `src/allele.rs:947 test_get_matched_variant_alleles_multiallelic` exercises a different case (A/G/T against A/C/T, matching at index 1 on BOTH sides), and in any event an in-`src` test cannot be indexed from this crate.

desc: compare_existing alleles dont match with check: with the existing record's alleles changed to A/T, allele checking on, the A/G input matches nothing and the call yields undef
rationale: Same inputs, same expected value, through the same public delegate as n=9. The existing record becomes A/T at t/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.t:109 against the unchanged A/G input, and Perl asserts `undef`. That `undef` is not a second channel: AnnotationType/Variation.pm:199-206 is `if(@$matched_alleles) { ... } return undef;`, so the wrapper returns it precisely when the delegate's list is empty. The asserted fact -- no ALT of the input matches any ALT of the existing record -- is therefore identical, and Rust encodes it as an empty `Vec` only because it has no `undef`. The named test asserts `Vec::<MatchedVariantAllele>::new()`, i.e. exact emptiness, not a weaker `!contains`.

desc: compare_existing alleles dont match no check: with --no_check_alleles on, an existing A/T record at the same start/end is returned in full despite sharing no ALT with the A/G input
rationale: This row's subject is the `--no_check_alleles` option, not the matcher: AnnotationType/Variation.pm:158-166 @ release/116.0 is an `elsif($self->{no_check_alleles})` branch that skips allele comparison entirely and returns the existing record on a bare start/end equality. vepyr has no such option and no such branch. Measured at the pin (dfbf 391f94bd, over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src): `grep -rniIE 'no_check_alleles|check_alleles'` returns 0 lines, against positive controls `existing_variation` 31 and `allele_matches` 43 -- so this is absence of the option, not a search that found nothing. The missing feature is a coordinate-only colocation mode: a switch that keeps a colocated ID whose alleles do not match the input at all. Note this is NOT the same as vepyr's `allele_matches_relaxed` (src/allele.rs:479), which relaxes indel representation but still requires an allele match.

desc: compare_existing rev strand exact match: an existing T/C record on the MINUS strand at the same position matches the plus-strand A/G input, and each side is reported in its own spelling -- a_allele G un-complemented, b_allele C as stored
rationale: Same inputs, same expected value, same public delegate as n=9. The existing record is reassigned at t/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.t:124-129 to T/C on strand -1 at start/end 10, and Perl expects `a_allele => 'G'` with `b_allele => 'C'`. The content of the row is that the matcher reverse-complements across a strand disagreement and STILL reports each side in its own spelling. `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles` does exactly that: it complements the a-side only when `a.strand != b.strand` (src/allele.rs:219-235 @ dfbf 391f94bd) and then reports `a_allele: orig_a_alt.clone()` (:261), the pre-complement allele -- so the asserted G is the input's own G, not a round trip. The named test asserts the whole expected list with `assert_eq!`.

desc: compare_existing rev strand alleles dont match with check: an existing T/G record on the minus strand shares the literal G with the A/G input and must still NOT match, because the input's G complements to C
rationale: The negative control that makes n=13's strand handling load-bearing, and the reason it is a separate row: the existing record becomes T/G at t/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.t:145, so a matcher that skipped the complement step would find a false match on the shared literal G. Perl asserts `undef`; the public delegate returns an empty `Vec` for the reason set out at n=11 (AnnotationType/Variation.pm:199-206). Same function and same pin as n=9: `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles`, src/allele.rs:203 @ dfbf 391f94bd, complementing the a-side at :219-235 only when the strands disagree. The named test asserts exact emptiness.

desc: compare_existing rev strand alleles dont match no check: --no_check_alleles also overrides the reverse-strand mismatch of n=14, returning the T/G minus-strand record unchanged
rationale: The reverse-strand instance of n=12's claim, and a separate row because it pins that the option short-circuits BEFORE strand handling: AnnotationType/Variation.pm:158-166 returns on start/end equality alone, so the strand disagreement n=14 turns into a rejection never gets evaluated. The same measurement disposes of it -- 0 occurrences of `no_check_alleles` over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at dfbf 391f94bd, positive controls as at n=12 -- and the same feature is missing: a coordinate-only colocation mode. Until the option exists there is no order of evaluation to assert.

desc: compare_existing missing alleles: an existing record whose allele_string carries no '/' at all (NULL, HGMD_MUTATION, COSMIC_MUTATION) cannot be allele-matched, so VEP falls back to start/end equality and returns it unchanged, with no matched_alleles key
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay, and this is the one row in its file that the public sibling genuinely cannot express -- the reason it was blocked-api rather than merely unported. A real annotation behaviour, not plumbing: it is why HGMD and COSMIC identifiers reach the Existing_variation column at all, and AnnotationType/Variation.pm:149-157 @ release/116.0 is the branch (if($existing_var->{allele_string} !~ /\//). vepyr implements it exactly as the first statement of colocated::compare_existing_variant_alleles (dfbf 391f94bd src/colocated.rs:237-250): if !existing_allele_string.contains('/') { return (existing_start == compare_start && existing_end == compare_end).then_some(Vec::new()) } -- Some(vec![]), a match carrying no matched alleles, which its doc comment at :234-236 states verbatim, with in-src tests at :350 and :368 an external crate cannot index. colocated is a pub(crate) mod (lib.rs:53) and the item is pub(crate), so it was doubly unreachable; re-measured in this checkout as error[E0603]: module `colocated` is private pointing at lib.rs:53, against a resolving positive control in the same probe file. A bare pub use of a pub(crate) fn is E0364, so PINS.toml dfbf_test_overlay (aa2be930) reaches it by delegation instead. WHY THE PUBLIC SIBLING COULD NOT STAND IN, now asserted rather than argued: handed "NULL" as the b-side, allele::get_matched_variant_alleles finds no '/' in parse_variant_allele_string (allele.rs:170) and returns an empty Vec -- textually identical to a genuine mismatch such as A/G vs A/T -- and the test pins both of those returning the same value, so the distinction the Perl asserts is visibly beyond the public API. analog-port and not unit-port: Perl returns the $existing hash itself while vepyr returns Some(vec![]), the same fact in a different shape. All three no-slash spellings the row names are covered (NULL, HGMD_MUTATION, COSMIC_MUTATION) and each is also run one base off, returning None, so the fallback is shown to be start/end equality rather than an unconditional match. Mutation-checked: expecting None at equal coordinates fails with left: Some([]) / right: None. Tracked in issue 174.

desc: compare_existing missing alleles no check: switching --no_check_alleles on does NOT change the NULL-allele outcome -- the unknown-allele branch wins the if/elsif and the record is still returned
rationale: The subject is branch precedence, and the branch that must lose is `--no_check_alleles`: AnnotationType/Variation.pm:149-166 is one `if ... elsif` chain, so the unknown-allele arm is evaluated first and the option never gets a say. Both halves of that claim need the option to exist, and it does not: 0 occurrences of `no_check_alleles` over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at dfbf 391f94bd, positive controls `existing_variation` 31 and `allele_matches` 43. This row is therefore not a duplicate of n=16 even though the two expect the same value -- n=16 is blocked on visibility of a branch vepyr HAS (see #174), while this one names a second branch vepyr does not have and an ordering between them that consequently cannot be observed. Missing feature: as n=12, a coordinate-only colocation mode.

desc: compare_existing missing alleles exclude_null_alleles: with --exclude_null_alleles on, the same NULL-allele record is dropped instead of kept -- the opposite disposition to n=16
rationale: The mirror image of n=16 under a second option, and the first arm of the same chain: AnnotationType/Variation.pm:150-152 returns `undef` outright when `$self->{exclude_null_alleles}` is set, so HGMD/COSMIC-style records with no parsable alleles are suppressed entirely. vepyr has no such option -- `grep -rniIE 'exclude_null_alleles' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` at dfbf 391f94bd returns 0 lines, positive controls `existing_variation` 31 and `parquet` 913 -- and `colocated::compare_existing_variant_alleles` (src/colocated.rs:237) offers only the keep disposition, with no switch to invert it. The missing feature is a user-facing suppression of unknown-allele colocated records; adding it is an option plus a branch, not a test.

desc: get_dump_file_name: (chr 1, region '1-100') resolves to <dir>/1/1-100_var.gz -- the 1-Mb block is part of the file NAME, so the cache is addressed per (chrom, region) rather than per chrom
rationale: Already adjudicated, and recorded so this issue would not re-litigate it: see ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=5, whose rationale awards `tests/port_cache_layout.rs::variation_context_path_returns_per_chrom_parquet_path` to the tabix side and names this row as the refused second claimant. What this row pins is region-DEPENDENCE: AnnotationSource/Cache/Variation.pm:162-179 @ release/116.0 formats `%s/%s/%s_var.gz` from `$self->dir`, `$chr` and `$region`, so the 1-Mb block appears in the filename. vepyr's resolver is `PartitionedParquetCache::context_path(context_type, chrom)` -- the region parameter is absent from the signature, so no call of it can witness a region-dependent name; the tabix row's claim is the opposite property, region-INDEPENDENCE (VariationTabix.pm:315-322 accepts a region and discards it), which is exactly what that signature does witness. Why this differs from ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=7, which reads the structurally identical RegFeat.t:54 as analog-port: there the path test had no competing claimant. Here it is claimed, `analog-port` requires a `rust_test`, and none remains -- so the question is no-feature versus deferred, and `context_path` structurally cannot express a region, which is a missing feature and not unfinished work. Missing feature: per-(chrom, 1-Mb-region) cache addressing; supplying it means re-partitioning the parquet cache, not writing a test. CORRECTION (executed re-audit 2026-08-31): the sentence this rationale used to carry — that vepyr has no block dimension — was false, and is replaced by the measurement. vepyr's NATIVE-cache reader does carry the per-(chrom, 1-Mb-region) dimension: `datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache` v1.10.0 discovers a cache by parsing `<start>-<end>.gz` and `<chr>_<start>-<end>_var.gz` region-file names (`discovery.rs::looks_like_region_file_name`, `:198-208`), and the names are load-bearing — renaming the committed slice's `21/12000001-13000000.gz` to `21/all.gz` makes the cache undiscoverable (`No source files discovered for Transcript under …`). desc: get_dump_file_name with end: the 3-arg arity (chr, start, end) normalises to the same path as the 2-arg (chr, 'start-end') form -- two spellings of one 1-Mb block resolve to one file

The category is unchanged for that reason.

desc: get_dump_file_name no chromosome: calling the resolver with no chromosome dies with /No chromosome/ instead of building a path
rationale: Same property -- a dump-file resolver must refuse a request that names no chromosome rather than silently building a path that fails later -- observed through a different channel. Perl throws: AnnotationSource/Cache/Variation.pm:167 @ release/116.0 is `throw("No chromosome given") unless $chr;`. vepyr returns `Option::None`; `context_path` has no fallible-result variant on this path, so `None` is the whole of the refusal, and that difference in channel (exception versus Option) is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The named test asserts `cache.context_path("variation", "").is_none()` and, as a second case, that a chromosome absent from the manifest (chr99) also yields `None`. This test IS dual-claimed, with ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=6, and that ledger's rationale records the ruling permitting it: VariationTabix.pm:319 and AnnotationSource/Cache/Variation.pm:167 assert the identical property at the identical boundary, so the shared-`rust_test` norm is satisfied exactly. Contrast n=19, where the same review refused the dual claim because the two Perl lines assert opposite properties.

rationale: This row is specifically about the REGION argument being mandatory: AnnotationSource/Cache/Variation.pm:168 @ release/116.0 is `throw("No region given") unless $region;`, one line below the chromosome guard n=21 ports. vepyr's resolver has no region parameter, so there is no argument that can be omitted and no error condition to raise. The category is unchanged for that reason.

desc: delimiter: the default variation cache parses its dump rows as SPACE-delimited text (qr/ /), the field that switches parse_variation()'s line splitter between VEP's two variation-cache backends
rationale: A text-shape accessor, and the one place VEP's two variation-cache backends differ at the parser level: AnnotationSource/Cache/BaseCacheVariation.pm:485-487 @ release/116.0 is `sub delimiter { return qr/ /; }` while VariationTabix.pm:298-300 overrides it to `return "\t";`, and `delimiter` is what `parse_variation()` splits on. vepyr never parses variation-cache text at all: the cache is parquet read through DataFusion, so columns are binary-typed and there is no separator to configure. ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=7 makes the same call for the tab side with a compiled probe -- `error[E0599]: no method named `delimiter` found for reference `&PartitionedParquetCache``, against `context_path("variation", "chr21")` compiling in the same probe file as the positive control. Measured at the pin: `grep -rniI delimiter datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 14 lines, 13 of them under `plugin_cache/` (`source_manifest.rs:51 pub delimiter: String`, consumed at `provider.rs:82`) for user-supplied TSV plugin sources and the 14th a comment about AF value separators at `cache/af_bundle.rs:73`; none is a variation-cache line parser. Missing feature: a delimited-text variation-cache reader.

desc: read_variations_from_file ref: deserialising a per-region _var.gz dump yields an array of variant records rather than a scalar or a hash
rationale: A reference-type probe on the deserialiser's return value, and only that: `ref($features) eq 'ARRAY'` is satisfied by an empty arrayref, so the line does not even assert the file was read. In vepyr the deserialised unit is a typed Arrow `RecordBatch` stream, so the container's shape is a compile-time fact carried by the signature and a run-time check would restate the compiler. What the read actually produced is n=25, which is deferred rather than not-applicable, so the substance stays in the denominator. Same reading as ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=19 and n=24 for the regulatory deserialiser.

desc: read_variations_from_file first el: the first record of the chr21 25-26 Mb variation dump is rs574523538 at 25000001 with allele_string C/T, and is asserted field by field -- 17 keys including the five 1000-Genomes population frequencies, minor_allele_freq 0.0002, clin_sig, pubmed, somatic and phenotype_or_disease
rationale: Ported against tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache (#96), which is the artefact this row's previous rationale named. Channel: the shard IS the dump, and the pin's own variation-record reader, `SinglePathParquetVariationLookup` (parquet_cache/variation_lookup.rs @ dfbf 391f94bd), is its deserialiser -- it reconstructs the `allele:freq` spelling VEP's cache text uses and coalesces `variation_name` over `dbsnp_ids`, so 14 of the Perl's 17 keys come back under the SAME NAMES: AFR, AMR, EAS, EUR, SAS, clin_sig, pubmed, somatic, phenotype_or_disease, failed, allele_string, start, end, variation_name. 14 + the 3 recorded below = the 17 the Perl asserts; `AF` is NOT one of them -- it is the vepyr column that carries two of the three misses, and an earlier draft miscounted it into the total. The three that do not map are recorded rather than dropped: `minor_allele` 'T' and `minor_allele_freq` '0.0002' have columns that are NULL in the v115 shard -- both values are the two halves of the `AF` column, `T:0.0001997`, whose freq VEP rounds to 0.0002 in output -- and `strand` has no column at all, the parquet variation rows being +1 by construction. `First record` needed an argument, and here it is. Perl reads ONE 1-Mb region dump, `<dir>/21/25000001-26000000_var.gz` (t/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.t:196-201), and takes its element [0]. vepyr has no block dimension -- `chrom_manifest.json` maps a chromosome to a single dataset file -- so the block must be re-imposed by coordinate, and the test does that explicitly rather than assuming it. Two wrong answers are asserted away, both measured over the whole 16666-row scan: the shard's overall lowest `start` is 8986608, which is in block 8 (the outlying 8985000-8990000 window), so reading `first row of the file` literally gives the wrong record; and the shard carries 349 records in 24999000..25000001 -- block 24, from the window the builder cut at 24999000 -- which are lower still, so an off-by-one block bound lands in them. Inside 25000001..=26000000 the lowest start is 25000001, and that is rs574523538. Mutation-checked: widening the block bound to 24999000 turns the row red. The record's values are v115 and agree with the Perl's v84 literals throughout: allele_string C/T, start = end = 25000001, failed/somatic/phenotype_or_disease all false, clin_sig and pubmed null, AFR/AMR/EAS/SAS `T:0` and EUR `T:0.001`. One half of `is_deeply` that a column read usually loses is partly recovered: `is_deeply` also fails on an EXTRA key, and the Perl's 17-key record carries no `gnomADe*` key at all, so the test asserts all ten gnomADe columns are empty -- a fixture whose gnomAD-exome data grew would be noticed. `gnomADg` is a v115 addition v84 did not have (`T:1.97e-05` here) and is recorded, not asserted away. Mutation-checked on the variation name and on EUR.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached ref 1: the disk read for region (21, 25) returns an array of variant records
rationale: The disk-read path's reference-type probe, the counterpart of n=24 one method up. `ref(...) eq 'ARRAY'` is true of an empty arrayref, so the line asserts a container shape and nothing about the read; in Rust that shape is the function's static return type. Its substance -- that the read found records, and which -- is n=27 and n=28, and n=28 is deferred, so nothing leaves the denominator that should stay in it. Identical call at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=24 for RegFeat.t:108.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached ref 2: the first element is a plain HASH -- the variation cache hands back unblessed records, unlike the transcript and regulatory caches which return blessed Ensembl objects
rationale: A reference-type probe again, and specifically a NEGATIVE claim about blessing: `HASH` says the record was not blessed into a class. docs/ledger-contract.md lists assertions about blessing and Perl object identity as the not-applicable case, and Rust has no blessing to withhold -- every cache row is a typed value. This is where this row differs from its regulatory counterpart, ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=25, which is deferred: there the probe names a FEATURE TYPE (`Bio::EnsEMBL::Funcgen::RegulatoryFeature`) and so carries content about what came back, while `HASH` names no content at all. The one thing this line does carry beyond blessing -- that element [0] exists -- is subsumed by n=28, which asserts that element's identity and is deferred.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached variation_name: the first record of the uncached region read is rs574523538 -- the region query returns the same first variant the raw file read did
rationale: A different boundary from n=25, which is why it is a different test and not a second claim on the same one: n=25 could be satisfied by a hardcoded path, this row cannot. Perl's `get_features_by_regions_uncached([[21, 25]])` reaches the dump through `get_dump_file_name`; vepyr reaches the shard through `PartitionedParquetCache::variation_path`, which parses `chrom_manifest.json` and applies the bare-contig alias fallback (`21` -> `chr21`). The named test drives that resolution and then asserts the resolved shard's record at 25000001 is rs574523538 with allele_string C/T -- and, closing the Perl's actual claim, that it is the same record the whole-file scan of n=25 says is first in block 25. So the row's content, that the region accessor and the raw file reader AGREE, is asserted as an agreement rather than as two independent identities. Positive control that the resolution does work rather than answering unconditionally: the same cache returns `None` for chr7, and reports exactly one available contig. What does NOT carry across is the region ARGUMENT itself -- `context_path`/`variation_path` take no region, which is the absence already adjudicated at n=19 and n=22 (no-feature); this row's `[[21, 25]]` is therefore reproduced as its chromosome half plus the coordinate block n=25 re-imposes. Blocker closed: tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache (#96).

desc: get_features_by_regions_cached ref 1: the second read of the same region, served from the in-memory region cache rather than from disk, also returns an array
rationale: The memory-cache path's reference-type probe, the third instance of the same idiom in this file (n=24, n=26, n=29) and satisfied by an empty arrayref. In Rust the shape is static. That the second read is served from memory at all is a claim about the region cache, and vepyr's region cache is n=32's subject, classified there as no-feature; that the memory read agrees with the disk read is n=31, which is deferred. This row alone adds neither. Identical call at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=27 for RegFeat.t:115.

desc: get_features_by_regions_cached ref 2: the first element of the memory-served read is a plain HASH, as on the disk path
rationale: The memory-path twin of n=27: a reference-type probe whose content is the absence of blessing, which Rust has no way to have or to withhold. The claim that would matter -- that the memory-served record is the SAME record the disk read produced -- is n=31, and n=31 is deferred, not not-applicable.

desc: get_features_by_regions_cached variation_name: the memory-served read returns the same rs574523538 the disk read did -- the region cache is a faithful memo, not a second, different query
rationale: Ported against tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache (#96). The memo asserted is the pin's OWN, not a stand-in: `ParquetVariationLookupCell` is a `pub type` in `cache::lookup_exec` (dfbf 391f94bd cache/lookup_exec.rs:144), a `tokio::sync::OnceCell<(String, Arc<SinglePathParquetVariationLookup>)>`, and it is the cell `KvLookupExec` threads through lookup_provider.rs:104 and :185 so that -- its own comment at :130 -- `simultaneous fan-out probes build it exactly once`. Driving that cell directly is the closest an external crate gets to Perl's `get_features_by_regions_cached`, and it is closer than re-using an already-open handle would be, because the cell is precisely what decides whether a READER is rebuilt. Analog-port rather than unit-port because the memo is per-plan and keyed on a contig where Perl's is a caller-visible hash keyed on (chrom, 1-Mb region) -- the difference in shape this row's previous rationale flagged. The named test reads 21:25000001 twice through one cell and asserts (a) the two records are identical and are rs574523538, and (b) an `AtomicUsize` counter in the initialiser reads 1, not 2. The counter is the whole point: without it the test would pass against a cell that re-opened the shard every time, which is the exact failure `a memo that returned something different from what it memoised` names. Mutation-checked on the counter.

desc: clean_cache: emptying the region cache leaves the annotation source's cache hash empty -- the caller can see, and drive, region eviction
rationale: VEP bounds memory by evicting whole 1-Mb regions from an in-memory feature cache, and exposes BOTH the store (`$c->cache`) and the eviction call (`$c->clean_cache`) to the caller; `is_deeply($c->cache, {})` asserts the store is caller-visible and observably empty afterwards. vepyr has no variation-scoped equivalent to empty. Measured at dfbf 391f94bd: `grep -rniI clean_cache datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 2 lines, both doc comments on `prune_persisted_buffer_transcripts` (annotate_provider.rs:11515-11523) -- which is transcript-scoped and is declared `fn`, not `pub fn`. The variation-side memo, `ParquetVariationLookupCell`, has no caller-facing clear and no accessor that would report emptiness. Missing feature: caller-visible region-cache eviction for the variation source; until it exists there is no state whose emptiness could be asserted. Same call, for the regulatory source, at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=30.

desc: TESTS WITH AN INPUT BUFFER: use_ok loads Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF, so the file can build a real VCF-backed input buffer
rationale: The fourth module-load probe of five, and scaffolding for the buffer section: `Parser::VCF` is loaded so :244 can construct the parser n=34 checks. R2 is unconditional. What the VCF parser does with a file is the subject of t/Parser_VCF.t and is classified in ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml.

desc: get parser object: Parser::VCF->new({config, file => test_vcf, valid_chromosomes => [21]}) returns a defined object
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. The type that stands in is `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`: vepyr never hands a caller a parser object, so the nearest thing an external crate can construct is the provider `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` registers internally (`vcf_sink.rs:1074` and `:1079` @ dfbf 391f94bd, both `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` — the five arguments the named test passes), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The probe is load-bearing rather than plumbing because that constructor is genuinely fallible: it `block_on`s `determine_schema_from_header` and propagates with `?` (`table_provider.rs:869-879` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8), i.e. it reads and parses the VCF header before it can return — exactly the ruling's defined/undef -> `Ok`/`Err` case. The named test asserts both limbs: `Ok` over a one-row VCF written to a tempdir, and over a missing path a typed error that is classified `NotFound` and names the path — because an `is_ok()` on its own would also pass against a constructor that never fails. Dual-claimed with the fourteen sibling rows the sweep moved together; all fifteen are the same statement at the same boundary, and the roster is kept in one place, the table at the top of tests/port_parser_vcf_construct.rs. The `valid_chromosomes` argument this call adds is not a boundary difference: `ok($p)` inspects no argument, so the assertion holds for any defined return and would still hold if the file were empty. What that argument does is ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml's subject.

desc: TESTS WITH AN INPUT BUFFER: use_ok loads Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer, the batching layer the annotation source is driven through
rationale: The last of this file's five module-load probes. R2 is unconditional and does not turn on whether vepyr has an InputBuffer type -- it turns on Rust having no run-time module load to assert. The buffering behaviour itself is the subject of t/InputBuffer.t and ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml, where the pin's private `InputBufferAccumulator` is worked out row by row.

desc: check class: ref($ib) is exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer, not a subclass and not a plain hashref
rationale: A blessing readback, decided by docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R1's second limb: the class denotes a capability vepyr has, under a different type, so the readback restates a compile-time fact -- a Rust constructor's return TYPE is its class and cannot disagree with itself at run time. vepyr's counterpart is `InputBufferAccumulator` (dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:9521), private but present, and whether the buffer's private-ness is a gap is ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml's subject, not this file's. R1's first limb does not apply -- this file carries no `ok($ib = …->new)` -- but the second is sufficient on its own. Identical call at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=9, ledger/AnnotationSource_Database_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=22 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Database_StructuralVariation.ledger.toml n=9.

desc: check buffer next: InputBuffer::next returns an arrayref -- a list-shaped batch rather than a scalar, hashref or object
rationale: A reference-type probe on `next()`'s return value: `ref(...) eq 'ARRAY'` is true of an empty arrayref too, so the line does not even assert the buffer filled. In vepyr the unit handed to the annotator is a typed Arrow `RecordBatch`, so the container's shape is static and no run-time check could contradict it. Whether the buffer holds the expected variants is what n=38 onward assert, and those are classified on their own merits. Identical call at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=10, ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=35 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=12.

desc: get_all_regions_by_InputBuffer: a buffer of chr21:25-26 Mb variants reduces to exactly one cache region, [[21, 25]] -- chromosome 21, and 1-Mb block 25 alone
rationale: Same property — the set of cache files a buffer needs is derived from the buffer's coordinates — observed through the path resolver rather than through a region tuple. Perl computes (chrom, 1-Mb-block) pairs (AnnotationSource.pm:219 `sub get_all_regions_by_InputBuffer` @ release/116.0), and `[[21, 25]]` says two things: chr21 is selected, and nothing else is. vepyr's per-chrom layout has no block dimension, so the tuple reduces to a chromosome selector; the named test asserts `context_path("variation", "chr21").is_some()` and, for chr22, chrX and chrMT, `.is_none()`. SOFTENED in the #120 sweep, per the closing review of #14: that second half is FIXTURE-SCOPED selectivity, not a demonstration that the resolver narrows a wider cache. `tmp_variation_layout` writes chr21 alone, so chr22/chrX/chrMT return `None` because the manifest never carried them — the test shows that a chromosome outside the cache does not resolve, which is the portable half of "and nothing else", and it does NOT show a resolver choosing chr21 out of several present chromosomes. Read the row as the chromosome-selector claim plus that negative control, not as the full set-valued claim Perl's `[[21, 25]]` makes. The block half (`25`) is not reproduced and is not smuggled in either: it is the same absent 1-Mb-block addressing n=19, n=20 and n=22 name. The 1-Mb machinery that does exist at the pin is for transcripts and is private — `const VEP_TRANSCRIPT_CACHE_REGION_SIZE_BP: i64 = 1_000_000` at annotate_provider.rs:8826, with no `pub` — and is tracked as old-repo issue #98. Resolution only: `tmp_variation_layout` writes the literal bytes `parquet-shard-placeholder`, so a `Some` here proves a file was found, not that it could be read.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 1: the buffer-wide pull across every region the buffer touches returns an array of variant records
rationale: The buffer-wide instance of the same reference-type idiom as n=24, n=26 and n=29, and satisfied by an empty arrayref -- which n=45 makes explicit by asserting exactly that for an exhausted buffer. In Rust the shape is the signature. What the pull actually returned is n=40 through n=43, three of which are deferred. Identical call at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=37 for RegFeat.t:142.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 2: the first element of the buffer-wide pull is a plain HASH, as on the per-region paths
rationale: The buffer-wide twin of n=27 and n=30: a probe whose content is the absence of blessing, which Rust neither has nor can withhold. The identity of that first element is n=41, which is deferred, so the substance stays counted.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer variation_name 1: the buffer-wide pull over the chr21:25-26 Mb test VCF opens with rs142513484
rationale: The blocker this row carried was two-part and its first part was FALSE at the pin: it said `$test_cfg->{test_vcf}` is not vendored here. It is -- `tests/data/vep116_runner_input/test.vcf.gz`, which decompresses byte-identically to upstream's t/testdata/input/test.vcf (sha256 of the plaintext a7ecda18970e4546e0e3850648f55682c96f884a89f2c1e2ec153d76dc2d4bf3, 132 records, all chr21). The search behind the claim was `find -name '*.vcf'`, which cannot match a `.vcf.gz`; `-name '*.vcf*'` finds it. NO new artefact was needed for the RECORD this row names: rs142513484 @25585733 was already in the committed shard and is already the minimum of the pull window, so unlike n=42 and n=47 this row was never actually blocked on data -- measured, not asserted: reverting the shard to its pre-rebuild bytes leaves n=44's memo test green while moving the population guard, and n=44 names the same record. The test's own population guard (9534 rows in the pull window) is derived from the rebuilt shard, which is why the row still lands after the fixture in this chain. Channel, named: Perl's `get_all_features_by_InputBuffer` (AnnotationSource.pm:109-145) does not return the region dump -- it returns `merge_features(filter_features_by_min_max(\@features, $buffer->min_max))`, and `filter_features_by_min_max` (:331-341) widens the buffer's min_max by `up_down_size`, which for a variation source is ONE base (AnnotationType/Variation.pm:243-245, `sub up_down_size { return 1; }`, against RegFeat's 0). The vendored buffer spans 25585733..25982445, so the pull window is 25585732..25982446. vepyr's counterpart is the committed variation shard read through `parquet_cache::scan::read_context_parquet` and filtered by the same overlap rule `_check_overlap` (:288-312) applies. The first record of that window is rs142513484 at 25585733, and it is the only record at that coordinate, so `the first element` is unambiguous here. Control that the filter is load-bearing rather than a no-op: the shard's own lowest start is 8986608, 16.6 Mb below the buffer, and n=25 (ported) asserts the region dump's first record is rs574523538 at 25000001 -- 585 kb earlier -- so `first row of the shard` and `first row of the block` are both wrong answers this test excludes.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer variation_name 2: the same pull CLOSES with COSM5057537 -- a COSMIC somatic identifier, so the pull spans both the dbSNP and the COSMIC halves of the cache
rationale: The blocker this row carried was two-part and its first part was FALSE at the pin: it said `$test_cfg->{test_vcf}` is not vendored here. It is -- `tests/data/vep116_runner_input/test.vcf.gz`, which decompresses byte-identically to upstream's t/testdata/input/test.vcf (sha256 of the plaintext a7ecda18970e4546e0e3850648f55682c96f884a89f2c1e2ec153d76dc2d4bf3, 132 records, all chr21). The search behind the claim was `find -name '*.vcf'`, which cannot match a `.vcf.gz`; `-name '*.vcf*'` finds it. Unblocked by recipe R1 in the fixture's PROVENANCE.md, which extends the variation windows by +-100 bp around each of the 132 vendored input positions. Channel, named: Perl's `get_all_features_by_InputBuffer` (AnnotationSource.pm:109-145) does not return the region dump -- it returns `merge_features(filter_features_by_min_max(\@features, $buffer->min_max))`, and `filter_features_by_min_max` (:331-341) widens the buffer's min_max by `up_down_size`, which for a variation source is ONE base (AnnotationType/Variation.pm:243-245, `sub up_down_size { return 1; }`, against RegFeat's 0). The vendored buffer spans 25585733..25982445, so the pull window is 25585732..25982446. vepyr's counterpart is the committed variation shard read through `parquet_cache::scan::read_context_parquet` and filtered by the same overlap rule `_check_overlap` (:288-312) applies. What makes this row worth its place is that ONE base of slack: the record Perl names sits at 25982446, exactly `buffer max + up_down_size`. All three candidate windows are distinguishable in the committed shard and all three are asserted -- whole shard 21164 rows topping out at 25982544 (rs1205568710); slack 0 giving 9532 rows topping out at 25982445; VEP's slack 1 giving 9534 rows topping out at 25982446 -- so neither an unbounded filter nor a missing slack can pass. v115 RENAMED the record and the rename is recorded rather than hidden: `variation_name` is COSV61004410 and Perl's COSM5057537 survives as a COSMIC synonym, `cosmic_ids = COSV61004410,COSM5057537`; it is the only record of the pull carrying that identifier and it is `somatic`. One half does NOT cross and is not claimed: two records share start 25982446 (the other is rs780257087), so `the last array element` is a property of VEP's v84 dump ORDER, which a coordinate-sorted Parquet shard cannot reproduce; the test asserts the record is at the pull's upper bound, not that it is the final element. The row's own wording -- that the pull spans both halves of the cache -- is asserted directly: the pull opens on a dbSNP record and closes on a COSMIC one.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer count: exactly 50848 cache variants overlap the regions the chr21:25-26 Mb test buffer touches
rationale: STILL BLOCKED, and the blocker is now named exactly rather than as `the absent v115 cache` -- that one is closed (tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache, #96) and ten rows of this ledger are ported against it in the same PR chain. TWO artefacts are missing, and both are about the BUFFER rather than the cache. (1) `$test_cfg->{test_vcf}` is ensembl-vep's t/testdata/input/test.vcf, which this repository does not vendor: `perl/` holds 49 `.t` and 49 `.provenance` files and nothing else, and the only `*.vcf` anywhere in the checkout are five hand-built inputs under tests/_quarantine/data/port/, four stamped `##source=vepyr-port-test-<name>-v115` and the fifth `##source=vepyr-port-test-smoke`. desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer again: calling the buffer-wide pull a second time returns the same first record, rs142513484 -- the second call is served from the region memo and agrees with the first

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer on empty buffer: once the buffer is advanced past the end of the input, the pull returns an EMPTY list rather than the previous batch's features or an error
rationale: Ported against tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache (#96). This row's content is that EMPTY is distinguished from STALE -- the shape probe at n=39 is satisfied by an empty arrayref, so only this row separates `nothing left` from `the previous batch again`. The named test reproduces that ordering rather than just the emptiness: it does the HIT first on the same reader (21:25585733 -> rs142513484) and only then the miss, so a reader that returned its last take would pass a fresh-handle version of this test and fail this one. The miss is 21:25585701, chosen INSIDE the committed 25583000-25588000 window: it carries no variant, so a hit there would mean rounding to a neighbouring page rather than resolving an exact `start`. Asserted: `requested_positions = 1`, `matched_positions = 0`, and `batch.num_rows() = 0`. Analog-port because Perl's boundary is `get_all_features_by_InputBuffer` over an exhausted InputBuffer and vepyr has no InputBuffer an external crate can exhaust (`InputBufferAccumulator` is private -- see ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml); the feature-pull layer beneath it is the observation point that exists, and it is where the empty-not-stale property lives. Mutation-checked on the row count.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer: after annotation the first buffered variant carries a single existing record for rs142513484, asserted exhaustively -- 31 keys covering the five 1000-Genomes populations, ten gnomADe sub-populations including gnomADe_REMAINING and gnomADe_MID, ESP AA/EA, minor_allele_freq 0.0010, clin_sig, pubmed, somatic, phenotype_or_disease, and matched_alleles [T -> T]
rationale: The integration keystone of this file, ported against tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache and tests/data/vep115_reference_slice (#96). Channel: Perl observes `$vf->{existing}`, an array of cache-record hashes hung off the annotated VariationFeature; vepyr never materialises one, so the same values are read out of the CSQ subfields the emitted VCF carries -- `Existing_variation`, the six 1000-Genomes `*_AF` columns, the ten `gnomADe_*_AF` columns, `CLIN_SIG`, `SOMATIC`, `PHENO`, `PUBMED`. Dual-claimed with ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml, which docs/ledger-contract.md's RULING (dual-claim across ledgers) permits only when the property AND the boundary are identical. Reclassifying the tabix twins turns two precedent citations in ledger/AnnotationSource_Database_Variation.ledger.toml (n=24, n=27) into category-word advisories -- they cite VariationTabix n=16 and n=18 beside the word `deferred`, and those rows are now analog-port. The specific twin is ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=16, whose Perl line (:172) is the same statement against the same `$exp` modulo the tabix file's extra `chr` key. Values: the six 1000-Genomes numbers come back from the v115 fixture IDENTICAL to the Perl's v84 literals (AF 0.0010, AFR 0.003, AMR 0.0014, EAS/EUR/SAS 0); all ten gnomADe values moved and are re-derived. The two caveats this row's previous rationale asked to be recorded are recorded: the CSQ channel cannot reproduce `is_deeply`'s no-extra-keys half at all here (n=25 keeps a fragment of it, this row does not), and `matched_alleles` has no CSQ column -- for THIS record it is the trivial `[T -> T]`, and the non-trivial cases are n=50 and n=51, ported through the public matcher.
