desc: nastiness 1: for VCF row 21 8987005 A -> AGCG, an insertion written with one base of left context, the matched allele is reported as GCG on BOTH sides -- input index 0 against cache index 0
rationale: Ported, and #173's own prediction is what made it possible: `Read the cache record once and rows 50-53 become fixture-free unit ports`. Half of that is right -- the observation point is the PUBLIC `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles` (src/allele.rs:203 @ dfbf 391f94bd), which this ledger's n=9 through n=14 already unit-port with no fixture at all, and `matched_alleles` has no CSQ column so nothing else could reach it. It is analog-port rather than unit-port for two reasons the issue could not have known: the b-side comes out of a v115 cache where the Perl's came out of a v84 one, and the a-side has to be derived from the VCF row rather than read off it. The derivation is not an invention: `allele::vcf_to_vep_input_allele` (src/allele.rs:353) is dfbf's public source-equivalent port of `Parser::VCF::create_VariationFeatures()`, and the only thing added is the multi-ALT rule its biallelic signature cannot carry (the anchor base is chopped only when the FIRST alt shares it with REF, and that verdict then applies to every alt). It is checkable against the Perl without running Perl, because the Perl's own expected a_allele spells the VF out: `-/GCG` at 8987006 gives `GCG` at `a_index 0`, which is what the Perl asserts and what the test asserts verbatim. The b-side is re-derived: the v84 record's alleles were `GCG`/`GTG`, the committed v115 record is rs372061766, `GCGGCGGCGG/GCGG/GCGGCGG/GCGGCGGCGGCGG/GCGGCGGCGGCGGCGG` at 21:8987006-8987015. The test is exhaustive rather than locus-picked -- it runs the matcher over all 16666 committed records and asserts the complete match set -- and carries two positive controls: four records spelling `GCG` literally do not match, and the neighbouring insertion at the same start (rs1555836472, `G/GTGG`) does not either. Dual-claimed with ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml, which docs/ledger-contract.md's RULING (dual-claim across ledgers) permits only when the property AND the boundary are identical. They are: the two `.t` files drive VEP's two variation-cache backends, `Cache::Variation` and `Cache::VariationTabix`, over the same locus with the same input, and vepyr has ONE code path -- no tabix reader at all -- so the axis the two files differ on is exactly the axis vepyr collapses. Ask the ruling's test, `could this test fail if only the other row's behaviour regressed?`: there is no other behaviour, because there is no second backend. The specific twins are ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=36 and n=49. Mutation-checked on a_index and on the match count.

desc: nastiness 2: for 21 8987004 TA -> C,TAGCG, only the SECOND ALT matches -- a_index 1, a_allele TAGCG against cache b_allele GCG at index 0 -- so the report carries the untrimmed input spelling and the trimmed cache spelling side by side
rationale: The multi-ALT indel case, and the one that pins index bookkeeping under trimming: an off-by-one in the a-side enumeration passes n=50 and fails here. BOTH halves of its a-side survive v115 intact and are asserted as the Perl's own literals: `a_index 1` and the UNTRIMMED `a_allele TAGCG`. Untrimmed because the first alt `C` does not share `T` with the REF, so VEP's parser chops nothing and the VF stays `TA/C/TAGCG` at 8987004 -- a fact the Perl records only implicitly, in the spelling of its expected value, and which the derivation described at n=50 reproduces. Positive control on the index: the same input reduced to its first ALT alone (`21 8987004 TA C`) matches nothing over the whole shard, so `a_index 1` is a selection rather than the only allele on offer. The b-side is re-derived exactly as at n=50. Dual-claimed with ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml, which docs/ledger-contract.md's RULING (dual-claim across ledgers) permits only when the property AND the boundary are identical. They are: the two `.t` files drive VEP's two variation-cache backends, `Cache::Variation` and `Cache::VariationTabix`, over the same locus with the same input, and vepyr has ONE code path -- no tabix reader at all -- so the axis the two files differ on is exactly the axis vepyr collapses. Ask the ruling's test, `could this test fail if only the other row's behaviour regressed?`: there is no other behaviour, because there is no second backend. The specific twins are ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=37 and n=50. One measured reason the channel is the matcher and not the emitted VCF, recorded because it is a live divergence: `annotate_to_vcf` over this very row (`21 8987004 . TA C,TAGCG`) emits a CSQ group whose fields are shifted by one (`Allele=C`, then `TAGCG` in the Consequence slot, `intergenic_variant` in IMPACT, `indel` landing in SYMBOL_SOURCE rather than VARIANT_CLASS), while every single-ALT row of the same run is well-formed. Mutation-checked on a_index and on a_allele.

desc: nastiness 3: for 21 8987004 TAT -> TAGCGT, an insertion with shared prefix AND shared suffix, both sides trim to GCG -- a_allele GCG at index 0 against b_allele GCG at index 0
rationale: STILL BLOCKED, and now measured. The cache is no longer the blocker (#96); its siblings n=50 and n=51 are ported against it through the public `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles`. What is missing is narrower: a cache record at 21:8987004-8987006 carrying the v84 INSERTION ALLELES the Perl's expected value spells. Measured with the a-side derived from the public `allele::vcf_to_vep_input_allele` plus VEP's first-alt anchor rule: the VF is `AT/AGCGT` at 8987005, and over ALL 16666 committed records the single match is rs372061766 with `a_allele AGCGT`, `a_index 0`, `b_allele GCGGCGGCGGCGG`, `b_index 2`. The Perl expects `a_allele GCG` -- the TRIMMED spelling -- and that difference IS this row's whole content over n=50, which already ports `a_index 0` with `a_allele GCG`. Positive control that the search for the v84 alleles was real: four OTHER records in the shard carry an allele token that is literally `GCG` (rs1601202819, rs1988347167, rs1419902987, rs1168016116), none of them at this locus. RECORDED FOR WHOEVER OBTAINS THE RECORD: the `a_allele` difference may be a real divergence in reporting rather than a fixture artefact -- VEP reports the pass-current allele of whichever trim direction matched, dfbf always reports the pre-trim input allele (`orig_a_alt`, src/allele.rs:261 @ 391f94bd) -- and it is not adjudicable with a different b-side, because the two implementations are then not being asked the same question. Same finding as ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=38.

desc: nastiness 4: for 21 8987004 TAT -> TAGCGT,TAGTGT, TWO cache records match, one per input ALT, and the report pairs them in order -- AGCGT/GCG at indices 0/0 and AGTGT/GTG at indices 1/1
rationale: STILL BLOCKED, for a sharper reason than n=52's and one no re-derivation closes. This row's content is that ONE cache record accumulates TWO matches with paired a/b indices. Measured over all 16666 committed records with the a-side derived as at n=50: the VF `AT/AGCGT/AGTGT` at 8987005 matches TWO DIFFERENT records, one per ALT -- rs372061766 gives `(a_index 0, AGCGT, b_allele GCGGCGGCGGCGG, b_index 2)` and rs1555836472 (`G/GTGG`) gives `(a_index 1, AGTGT, b_allele GTGG, b_index 0)`. Perl's per-record array therefore holds one entry per record here, and the accumulate-rather-than-short-circuit property has no input at all. Measured: 0 of the 16666 records carry both a `GCG` and a `GTG` alt token (positive control: 4 carry a literal `GCG`, 2 a literal `GCGG`). What is missing is a single cache record whose allele_string offers two alts each matching a different input ALT. vepyr's half of the property is present -- `get_matched_variant_alleles` accumulates into a Vec with a HashSet guard against exact duplicates (src/allele.rs:250, :266-269) -- it is the second input that is absent. A RE-SITED analogue is available if the owner wants one (rs1402623917 at 21:8987004, `C/CCGC/CGGC`; rs1555836714 at 21:8987929, `-/A/GC/GGC/T`) but it would change the Perl's input, so it is flagged rather than taken. Same finding as ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=39.

desc: old_maf: with --old_maf on, the AMR frequency is reported as the bare number 0.0014 instead of the allele-qualified string T:0.0014 -- a pre-v81 output-format compatibility switch
rationale: The subject is the `--old_maf` option, a backward-compatibility switch that strips the allele qualifier from per-population frequency values so output written for pre-v81 VEP keeps parsing. vepyr does not have it: `grep -rniIE 'old_maf' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` at dfbf 391f94bd returns 0 lines, against positive controls `minor_allele_freq` 21 (the column itself is present, at cache_common.rs:320 among others) and `parquet` 913 -- so what is absent is the reformatting switch, not the frequency data. The missing feature is a legacy MAF output format; supplying it means adding an option and a formatter, not writing a test, and it would be dead weight for a tool with no pre-v81 consumers. Recorded as a gap rather than dismissed because it is a real difference in what a user can ask VEP for.

desc: use_ok VariationTabix: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::Cache::VariationTabix module compiles and loads
rationale: A module-load probe: `use_ok` asserts only that Perl found and compiled the .pm at run time. Rust answers the same question at link time -- `tests/port_cache_layout.rs` cannot build unless `datafusion_bio_function_vep::parquet_cache::detect::PartitionedParquetCache` resolves at the pin -- so a run-time assertion here would restate the linker. docs/ledger-contract.md names `use_ok`/`can_ok` existence probes as the legitimate not-applicable case. This row says nothing about whether vepyr has a tabix-backed variation source; that question is rows 4, 5, 7 and 41-43, and the answer there is no-feature.

desc: use_ok Config: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config module compiles and loads

desc: get new config object: Config->new(base_testing_cfg) returns a defined object

Perl can hand back undef; Rust cannot -- `AnnotateVcfConfig::default()` (`vcf_sink.rs` @ dfbf 391f94bd) yields a value of the struct type by construction -- so asserting definedness would assert a property of Rust rather than of vepyr. The defaults the object carries are the substance, and they belong to ledger/Config.ledger.toml. Same reading as ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=7.

desc: new is defined: Cache::VariationTabix->new({config, dir, cols}) constructs a tabix-backed variation source over the cache directory
rationale: Read as Perl plumbing this is a definedness probe, and ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=2 takes exactly that reading for the abstract base class. Here the object is the feature: constructing `Cache::VariationTabix` selects one of VEP's two variation-cache backends -- a single tabix-indexed bgzip per chromosome (`VariationTabix.pm:51`: `Variants are stored in one file per chromosome, named [chr]/all_vars.gz`), as against `Cache::Variation`'s per-1-Mb storable dumps. vepyr has one shape, per-chrom parquet resolved by `PartitionedParquetCache::context_path`, and no tabix-backed cache reader at all: `grep -ro tabix src/` over datafusion-bio-function-vep 0.15.0 @ dfbf 391f94bd returns 6 hits and every one is about the INPUT VCF's index (`vcf_sink.rs:1041`/`1049`/`1050` the workers>1 requirement, `lookup_provider.rs:224` filter-pushdown seeks, `annotate_provider.rs:12911` the count pass, `golden_benchmark.rs:92` index copying); none is a cache reader. Missing feature: a tabix-indexed variation-cache backend. docs/ledger-contract.md's tie-break -- when two readings are both defensible, take the one that keeps the row in the denominator -- picks no-feature over not-applicable.

desc: get_dump_file_name: the tabix backend resolves (chr 1, region '1-100') to <dir>/1/all_vars.gz -- one file per chromosome, with the region argument accepted and discarded
rationale: Same property, different channel. The Perl pins that the tabix subclass's dump-file resolver is a function of the chromosome alone: `get_dump_file_name` takes a region argument, and `VariationTabix.pm:315-322` formats `%s/%s/all_vars.gz` from `$dir` and `$chr` without it -- unlike `Cache::Variation`, whose name carries the 1-Mb block (`Variation.t:186` expects `1-100_var.gz`). vepyr's resolver is `PartitionedParquetCache::context_path(context_type, chrom)`, which has no region parameter at all and returns `<base>/variation/<chrom>.parquet`; the named test asserts that exact path for chr21 against a tempdir fixture, so the asserted value is a path, not merely a boolean. The literal `all_vars.gz` is a storage-shape detail with no counterpart (parquet, not bgzipped TSV) -- region-independence is the portable half, and it is what makes the tabix backend different from its sibling. `PartitionedParquetCache` has no `get_dump_file_name`: a probe naming it fails to build with `error[E0599]: no method named `get_dump_file_name` found for reference `&PartitionedParquetCache``, while `context_path(`variation`, `chr21`)` in the same probe file compiles (positive control). Cross-ledger ruling, from this chain's review and recorded so issue #14 does not re-litigate it: this test may NOT be dual-claimed. Its sibling assertion `Variation.t:186` is that file's row 19 (the enumerator's numbering; `port_cache_layout.rs` labelled it #18 from the detailed_plan's table and has been corrected in this PR), and it pins region-DEPENDENCE -- the 1-Mb block appears IN the filename -- which `context_path(context_type, chrom)` can never witness, because that parameter is absent from its signature. That row is `no-feature` when #14 is worked, not a second claimant here. This row is the one the test can carry, because region-INDEPENDENCE is exactly what the signature does witness.

desc: get_dump_file_name no chromosome: calling the resolver with no chromosome dies with /No chromosome/
rationale: Same property -- the variation dump-file resolver refuses a request that names no chromosome -- observed through a different channel. Perl throws: `VariationTabix.pm:319` is `throw(`No chromosome given`) unless $chr`. vepyr returns `Option::None`; there is no fallible-result variant on this path, so `None` is the whole of the refusal. The named test asserts `cache.context_path(`variation`, ``).is_none()` and, as a second case, that a chromosome absent from the manifest also yields None. The difference in channel (exception versus Option) is why this is analog-port rather than unit-port. Cross-ledger ruling, same review: unlike n=5, this test MAY be dual-claimed. `Variation.t:189` is that file's row 21 (labelled #20 from the detailed_plan's table before this PR) and asserts the identical property at the identical boundary -- a resolver call naming no chromosome is refused -- so both ledgers may name it and the shared-`rust_test` norm is satisfied exactly.

desc: delimiter: the tabix backend parses its cache rows as tab-delimited text
rationale: A text-shape accessor. VEP's two variation-cache shapes differ in field separator and `delimiter` (`VariationTabix.pm:298`, `Caller: parse_variation()`) is what switches the line parser between them. vepyr never parses variation-cache text: the cache is parquet read through DataFusion, so columns are binary-typed and there is no separator to configure. Probed: `error[E0599]: no method named `delimiter` found for reference `&PartitionedParquetCache``, with `context_path(`variation`, `chr21`)` compiling in the same probe file as the positive control. The crate does carry a `delimiter` -- 14 occurrences at dfbf 391f94bd, all in `plugin_cache` (`source_manifest.rs:51` `pub delimiter: String`, consumed at `provider.rs:82`), i.e. for user-supplied TSV plugin sources. That is a different feature; the missing one is a delimited-text variation-cache reader.

desc: use_ok Parser::VCF: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF module compiles and loads
rationale: The third module-load probe in this file (n=1, n=2). vepyr reads VCF through `datafusion-bio-format-vcf`, linked at build time, so the availability question is settled by the compiler. VCF parsing behaviour belongs to ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml.

desc: get parser object: Parser::VCF->new({config, file, valid_chromosomes => [21]}) returns a defined parser
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. The type that stands in is `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`: vepyr never hands a caller a parser object, so the nearest thing an external crate can construct is the provider `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` registers internally (`vcf_sink.rs:1074` and `:1079` @ dfbf 391f94bd, both `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` — the five arguments the named test passes), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The probe is load-bearing rather than plumbing because that constructor is genuinely fallible: it `block_on`s `determine_schema_from_header` and propagates with `?` (`table_provider.rs:869-879` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8), i.e. it reads and parses the VCF header before it can return — exactly the ruling's defined/undef -> `Ok`/`Err` case. The named test asserts both limbs: `Ok` over a one-row VCF written to a tempdir, and over a missing path a typed error that is classified `NotFound` and names the path — because an `is_ok()` on its own would also pass against a constructor that never fails. Dual-claimed with the fourteen sibling rows the sweep moved together; all fifteen are the same statement at the same boundary, and the roster is kept in one place, the table at the top of tests/port_parser_vcf_construct.rs. The `valid_chromosomes` argument this call adds is not a boundary difference: `ok($p)` inspects no argument, so the assertion holds for any defined return and would still hold if the file were empty. What that argument does is ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml's subject.

desc: use_ok InputBuffer: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer module compiles and loads
rationale: The fourth and last module-load probe in this file. Compile-time in Rust, as for n=1, n=2 and n=8. What the buffer does belongs to ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml.

desc: check class: ref($ib) is exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer
rationale: A blessing probe -- docs/ledger-contract.md's named not-applicable case. It asserts the constructor returned an InputBuffer rather than, say, a bare hashref. In Rust the binding's type is that assertion and the compiler checks it. Same reading as ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=34.

desc: check buffer next: the first ib->next() call yields an array of variants
rationale: A reference-type probe on `next()`'s return value: `ref(...) eq 'ARRAY'` is true of an empty arrayref too, so it does not even assert the buffer filled. In vepyr the unit handed to the annotator is a typed Arrow `RecordBatch`, so the container's shape is static; whether it holds the expected variants is what n=13 onward assert. Same reading as ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=35.

desc: _annotate_cl: annotating 21:25585733 C/T through the tabix command-line backend attaches rs142513484's full existing-variant record -- allele_string C/T, the 1000 Genomes and gnomADe per-population frequencies, minor_allele T at 0.0010, and matched_alleles a_index 0 T/T
rationale: Ported against the committed micro-cache (#96) through the CSQ channel this row's previous rationale named. Perl observes `$vf->{existing}`, a per-variant array of cache-record hashes; vepyr never materialises one, so the same values are read out of the CSQ subfields of the VCF `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` writes -- `Existing_variation`, the six 1000-Genomes `*_AF` columns, the ten `gnomADe_*_AF` columns, `CLIN_SIG`, `SOMATIC`, `PHENO`, `PUBMED`. That difference of observation point is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. Re-derived rather than transcribed, as detailed_plans/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.md and #101 both require, and the split is measurable: the six 1000-Genomes values (`AF 0.0010`, `AFR 0.003`, `AMR 0.0014`, `EAS/EUR/SAS 0`) come back from the v115 fixture IDENTICAL to the Perl's v84 literals, while all ten gnomADe values moved (`gnomADe` v84 `0.0003478` -> v115 `9.481e-05`, `gnomADe_AFR` `0.004643` -> `0.003061`, and so on). Two of the Perl's keys have no vepyr column at all and are recorded as unported rather than quietly dropped: the ESP `AA`/`EA` frequencies (the pin's 80-field CSQ layout carries no ESP columns) and `strand` (the parquet variation shard has no strand column; its rows are `+1` by construction). `matched_alleles` likewise has no CSQ column -- it is n=36-39's subject and is ported there. The four rows n=13, n=16, n=44 and n=47 assert ONE record through what VEP treats as four entry points: `_annotate_cl` (:129), `_annotate_pm` (:538) and `annotate_InputBuffer` twice (:172, and :584 with `$CAN_USE_TABIX_PM = 0`). vepyr has a single code path and no per-variant call at all -- `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` annotates whole batches -- so the backend-equivalence half of each Perl assertion has no counterpart and the four collapse onto the same property at the same boundary, which is exactly the condition docs/ledger-contract.md puts on a shared `rust_test`. Ask its test: could this test fail if only another row's behaviour regressed? For these four the answer is that there is no other behaviour to regress. The named test also asserts `CLIN_SIG`, `SOMATIC`, `PHENO` and `PUBMED` are EMPTY, which is Perl's `clin_sig => undef` (t/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.t:86), `pubmed => undef` (:95), `somatic => 0` (:74) and `phenotype_or_disease => 0` (:67): a plain dbSNP record with no clinical annotation is part of the assertion, not an omission from it. The `undef` spelling is this file's; the twin row ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.ledger.toml n=46 asserts the same two fields as `''` (t/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.t:302, :311). Both collapse onto one unset CSQ subfield, so the shared test is right, but the two are not the same Perl literal and this rationale previously attributed the wrong one to this file. Mutation-checked: flipping the asserted rsID to `rs142513485` and `AMR_AF` to `0.0015` each turn the test red, transcripts in the test's module header.

desc: chr synonym: with chr_synonyms loaded and the variant's chromosome set to NC_000021.9, the tabix backend still resolves chromosome 21 and attaches rs142513484
rationale: What is pinned is file-driven chromosome aliasing: VEP loads a two-column synonyms file (`BaseVEP.pm:637` into `{canonical => {synonym => 1}}`) and can therefore map an arbitrary spelling such as the RefSeq accession NC_000021.9 onto the cache's `21`. vepyr has no such loader -- probed: `error[E0433]: failed to resolve: could not find `chromosome_synonyms` in `datafusion_bio_function_vep``, with `cache::manifest::contig_alias_set` resolving in the same probe file as the positive control. What it has instead is a stateless derivation from the name itself. Measured out-of-tree (`cargo test --test probe -- --nocapture` on a probe calling the public fn, run in this worktree and then deleted): `contig_alias_set(`21`) = [`21`, `chr21`]`. NC_000021.9 is not derivable from `21` by any rule, only by a table nobody loads, so no fixture would unblock this. Missing feature: a user-supplied chromosome-synonyms file. Same finding as ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=28.

desc: miss by coord - _annotate_cl: moving the variant one base past rs142513484, to 21:25585734, leaves existing unset
rationale: The negative half of n=13, ported through the same CSQ channel: the row at 21:25585734 comes back with an EMPTY `Existing_variation` cell. The observation point differs from Perl's `undef` only in that Rust has no undef -- an unset CSQ subfield is the empty string -- which is what makes this analog-port rather than unit-port. The port is STRONGER than the Perl here, and the test says why with a positive control: the committed v115 shard DOES carry a record at 21:25585734, `rs754901467` with `allele_string T/C` (measured through `SinglePathParquetVariationLookup::resolve_and_take`, which returns `matched_positions = 1` there), so the empty cell is allele checking rather than an empty window. A lookup keyed on the region instead of the coordinate, and a matcher that skipped allele comparison, both fail this test; against a cache that simply had nothing at 25585734 neither would. The complementary control is in the same test: one base back, 21:25585733 still reads `rs142513484`. Mutation-checked -- asserting `rs754901467` instead of the empty string turns it red.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer: the buffer-level entry point attaches the same rs142513484 record as the direct _annotate_cl call of n=13
rationale: The buffer-level entry point, and the one of the four whose Perl shape matches vepyr's: `annotate_InputBuffer` annotates a whole buffer, which is what `annotate_to_vcf` does. Same record, same CSQ channel and same re-derived values as n=13, whose rationale carries the v84-vs-v115 table. The four rows n=13, n=16, n=44 and n=47 assert ONE record through what VEP treats as four entry points: `_annotate_cl` (:129), `_annotate_pm` (:538) and `annotate_InputBuffer` twice (:172, and :584 with `$CAN_USE_TABIX_PM = 0`). vepyr has a single code path and no per-variant call at all -- `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` annotates whole batches -- so the backend-equivalence half of each Perl assertion has no counterpart and the four collapse onto the same property at the same boundary, which is exactly the condition docs/ledger-contract.md puts on a shared `rust_test`. Ask its test: could this test fail if only another row's behaviour regressed? For these four the answer is that there is no other behaviour to regress. What this row alone would have added over n=13 -- that the public entry point dispatches to the same backend result as the private one (`VariationTabix.pm:120` on `$CAN_USE_TABIX_PM`) -- is the half with no vepyr counterpart, so nothing is lost by the shared test.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer count annotated: 132 of the buffer's variants come back carrying an existing-variant record
rationale: The blocker this row carried was two-part and its first part was FALSE at the pin: it said `$test_cfg->{test_vcf}` is not vendored here. It is -- `tests/data/vep116_runner_input/test.vcf.gz`, whose plaintext is byte-identical to upstream's t/testdata/input/test.vcf (sha256 a7ecda18970e4546e0e3850648f55682c96f884a89f2c1e2ec153d76dc2d4bf3, 132 records, all chr21); the search behind the claim was `find -name '*.vcf'`, which cannot match a `.vcf.gz`. The second part -- that the committed shard was too narrow -- was true, and is closed by recipe R1 in tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/PROVENANCE.md: +-100 bp around each of the 132 vendored positions. The condition R1 rests on was verified on the NATIVE v115 cache before the rebuild, so that the number 132 survives the change of release rather than being produced by it: 132/132 positions have an exact-start v115 record with a matching REF/ALT, 0 mismatches, 0 missing. Positive control for the method: the same pass counts 160516 records in 25585733..25982445, matching the campaign unlock map's independent figure (position is field 5 of all_vars.gz). Negative controls: positions +7 gives 7/132, ALT rotated A->C->G->T gives 16/132. Channel, named, and deliberately NOT the one ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.ledger.toml n=47 uses. `VariationTabix::annotate_InputBuffer` (VariationTabix.pm:112-128) branches on $CAN_USE_TABIX_PM; this row runs `_annotate_pm`, the in-process INDEXED reader, where n=47's source class reads a whole 1-Mb region dump. vepyr has one cache format and no tabix, but it has the same two read paths over that format, and this row takes the indexed one: `SinglePathParquetVariationLookup::resolve_and_take` -- footer PageDir row-group pruning, then a start-only pass for exact offsets, then a projected take -- driven over the 132 input coordinates as one probe set. Candidates are then paired with the inputs by `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles`, the pin's public `compare_existing`, so a coordinate hit alone is not counted; the in-test negative control shifts every probe by 7 bases and the census collapses. The two tests are not one claim twice: n=47's never opens the point-lookup path, so a PageDir that pruned a live row group leaves it green, and this one never scans, so a lost scan batch leaves it green.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - phenotype_or_disease: 21:25891796 C/T carries two existing records -- CM930033 with allele_string HGMD_MUTATION and no frequencies, and rs63750066 with clin_sig not_provided,pathogenic -- both flagged phenotype_or_disease 1
rationale: Ported through the CSQ channel plus a direct read of the shard, because one half of the Perl assertion does not survive the CSQ flattening and saying so is the point of the rationale. What CSQ carries: `Existing_variation` accumulates both matched names joined with `&` (`rs63750066&CM930033`), `PHENO` carries one flag per record (`1&1`), and `CLIN_SIG`/`PUBMED` carry the clinical terms. What it cannot carry is Perl's per-record structure -- `is_deeply` over an array of two hashes -- so the named test recovers it from the cache underneath with `SinglePathParquetVariationLookup`, which returns exactly two rows at 21:25891796: `CM930033` with `allele_string HGMD_MUTATION` and `rs63750066` with `C/T`, both `phenotype_or_disease = true`. That is where the row's real content is visible: an allele string with no `/` in it does not break matching, because the unknown-allele branch falls back to coordinate equality. Re-derived, and the v115 caveat this row's previous rationale predicted is confirmed: `clin_sig` reads `pathogenic&likely_pathogenic` where v84 read `not_provided,pathogenic`, and `pubmed` carries eight ids where v84 carried none on this backend. Record ORDER also differs by channel and is recorded rather than asserted as equivalent: the shard returns `[CM930033, rs63750066]`, which is the Perl's order here, while the CSQ cell reads `rs63750066&CM930033`. Mutation-checked on the `CLIN_SIG` term order.

desc: check_frequency_filter: with the default freq_pop, the frequency filter's configuration validates and returns true
rationale: VEP's `--check_frequency` family (`--freq_pop`, `--freq_freq`, `--freq_gt_lt`, `--freq_filter`) drops variants, or single alleles of a variant, by population allele frequency; `check_frequency_filter` is its configuration validator, called from `frequency_check_buffer` (`VariationTabix.pm:126`). vepyr does not filter: its public entry point takes an `AnnotateVcfConfig` carrying some forty VEP flags (`everything`, `pick`, `failed`, `distance`, ...) and not one of them is a frequency knob. Probed: `error[E0609]: no field `freq_pop` on type `AnnotateVcfConfig``, and the same for `freq_freq`, `freq_gt_lt`, `freq_filter` and `check_frequency`; the positive control `cfg.everything` compiles in the same probe file. `grep -ro 'filter_common|check_frequency|freq_pop' src/` at dfbf 391f94bd returns 0 (positive control: `frequency` returns 72, all of it the AF-column projection that feeds CSQ). Missing feature: frequency-based variant and allele filtering. vepyr annotates and emits the AF columns; deciding what to drop is left to the consumer's SQL over the resulting table, which is a different product, not a different observation point.

desc: check_frequency_filter - fails on missing pop: setting freq_pop to 'foo' makes the validator die with /Invalid population/
rationale: Validation of a filter option vepyr does not have (n=19). There is nothing here to reject, because there is no field to reject it in: `error[E0609]: no field `freq_pop` on type `AnnotateVcfConfig``. vepyr does carry a population catalogue -- the `AF_COLUMNS` table at `annotate_provider.rs:947` @ dfbf 391f94bd -- but it enumerates OUTPUT columns: every population in it is emitted, none is selected, so no name can be invalid. Missing feature is the same one as n=19: a population selector to validate.

desc: check_frequency_filter - fails on pop with AF added: 'gnomADe_AFR_AF' is rejected because the _AF suffix names the CSQ field, not the population
rationale: The Perl pins a naming rule -- the population is `gnomADe_AFR` and `gnomADe_AFR_AF` is the field that reports it, so passing the field name where a population is expected must fail. vepyr keeps both spellings and keeps them apart: `AF_COLUMNS` carries `cache_col: `gnomADe_AFR`` with `max_af_pop: Some(`gnomADe_AFR`)` while the emitted CSQ field is `gnomADe_AFR_AF` (`annotate_provider.rs:947` onward @ dfbf 391f94bd). What is missing is the selector that could be handed either spelling, and with it the rule that distinguishes them at the input boundary -- the same absent feature as n=19 and n=20, not a different one.

desc: check_frequency_filter - fails on pop for incorrect grouping: 'ExAC_AFR' is rejected as a population from a retired dataset
rationale: The Perl pins that the validator knows which dataset groupings exist. vepyr has no such validator (n=19), and it also has no ExAC at all: `grep -ro ExAC src/` at dfbf 391f94bd returns 0, with the positive control `gnomADe_AFR` returning 14. Its AF catalogue is 1000 Genomes plus gnomAD exomes and genomes (`AF_COLUMNS`, `annotate_provider.rs:947`). With neither a selector nor an ExAC population there is no input to reject and no grouping to reject it against.

desc: get_frequency_data - _freq_check_freqs: the per-population lookup finds the 1000 Genomes global frequency 0.0002 for the T allele of rs63750066, the synthetic 21:25891796 C/T variant built at :177 (NOT rs142513484, whose global AF is 0.0010)
rationale: The split this row's previous rationale drew is now executable. The filter accumulator `_freq_check_freqs` is machinery vepyr does not have (n=19, no-feature); the VALUE is emitted unconditionally, because where VEP selects one population vepyr writes them all as separate CSQ columns and `1KG_ALL` is the `AF` column (`AfColumn { cache_col: `AF`, format_4f: true }`, annotate_provider.rs:951 @ dfbf 391f94bd). That is the different observation point, hence analog-port. The value ports as the Perl's OWN v84 literal: `0.0002` comes back unchanged from the v115 fixture. CORRECTION carried by this row, and the reason its `desc` is rewritten in the same PR as the test: the previous `desc` attributed `0.0002` to rs142513484. It is rs63750066's. `$vf` at t/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.t:285 is `$ib->buffer->[0]` of the buffer built at :177 -- the synthetic `21 25891796 . C T` row -- not the test-VCF buffer of :165. rs142513484's global AF is `0.0010` (asserted at n=13), so the two numbers are not interchangeable and the mix-up would have made this row a duplicate of a value it does not assert. The named test carries that contrast as its positive control.

desc: get_frequency_data - _freq_check_pass: with the default threshold and direction, rs142513484's T allele is recorded as failing the filter
rationale: A filter verdict, not a frequency. `_freq_check_pass` is the per-allele pass/fail map `get_frequency_data` writes for `frequency_check_buffer` to consume; vepyr computes no such verdict because it has no frequency filter at all (n=19). Probed: `error[E0609]: no field `freq_pop` on type `AnnotateVcfConfig``, and the same for `freq_freq`, `freq_gt_lt`, `freq_filter` and `check_frequency`; the positive control `cfg.everything` compiles in the same probe file. `grep -ro 'filter_common|check_frequency|freq_pop' src/` at dfbf 391f94bd returns 0 (positive control: `frequency` returns 72, all of it the AF-column projection that feeds CSQ). The frequency this verdict is computed from is a separate row, n=23, and that one stays in `deferred` because vepyr does emit it.

desc: get_frequency_data - _freq_check_all_failed: with one allele and that allele failing, the whole-variant aggregate flag is set
rationale: The aggregate over n=24's per-allele map: VEP records both `_freq_check_all_failed` and `_freq_check_all_passed` so `frequency_check_buffer` can drop or keep a whole variant in one test. Both are internals of the filter vepyr does not have (n=19); with no per-allele verdicts there is nothing to aggregate. Probed: `error[E0609]: no field `freq_pop` on type `AnnotateVcfConfig``, and the same for `freq_freq`, `freq_gt_lt`, `freq_filter` and `check_frequency`; the positive control `cfg.everything` compiles in the same probe file. `grep -ro 'filter_common|check_frequency|freq_pop' src/` at dfbf 391f94bd returns 0 (positive control: `frequency` returns 72, all of it the AF-column projection that feeds CSQ).

desc: get_frequency_data - gt_lt: flipping freq_gt_lt to 'lt' reverses the verdict, so the same T allele now passes
rationale: Pins the direction knob of the filter: at a fixed threshold the same frequency must pass under `lt` and fail under `gt`. Both halves belong to the absent filter (n=19) -- `error[E0609]: no field `freq_gt_lt` on type `AnnotateVcfConfig``. Nothing about the underlying frequency changes between this row and n=24; only the comparison does, and the comparison is what is missing.

desc: get_frequency_data - gt_lt - _freq_check_all_passed: after the direction flip, the whole-variant aggregate records a pass
rationale: The `lt` counterpart of n=25: the same aggregate flags, now on the passing side. Absent for the same reason -- there is no filter to aggregate over (n=19), and no `freq_gt_lt` field to flip (`error[E0609]: no field `freq_gt_lt` on type `AnnotateVcfConfig``).

desc: get_frequency_data - freq: lowering freq_freq to 0.0001 makes the same T allele pass at the unchanged 'gt' direction
rationale: The threshold knob, tested independently of the direction knob of n=26: the pair of rows establishes that the verdict is a function of both. vepyr has neither -- `error[E0609]: no field `freq_freq` on type `AnnotateVcfConfig`` -- because it has no filter (n=19).

desc: get_frequency_data - freq - _freq_check_all_passed: after the threshold change, the whole-variant aggregate records a pass

desc: get_frequency_data - rev strand: a variant carrying strand -1 and allele_string G/A finds the same 1000 Genomes frequency, reported against the reverse-complemented allele A
rationale: No input format vepyr accepts carries a strand, so the operation this row asserts is never performed -- that is the absence, and it is a product statement, not a visibility problem. vepyr's public annotation entry point is `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf(input_vcf, ...)` (`vcf_sink.rs` @ dfbf 391f94bd) and VCF is defined on the forward strand; no input format, config field or API can present a minus-strand variant, so nothing ever requests a strand-aware frequency lookup and no code computes one. Flagged in this chain's announcement on #15 as a claim a reviewer might argue down to blocked-api; the review ruled absent-over-private, and this ordering reflects that.

desc: nastiness 1: 21:8987005 A/AGCG matches the cache row through an insertion trim -- matched_alleles a_index 0, a_allele GCG against b_allele GCG
rationale: Channel: NOT the CSQ string. `matched_alleles` has no CSQ column at all, so the observation point the record rows (n=13 etc.) use cannot reach it. The public `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles` (src/allele.rs:203 @ dfbf 391f94bd) computes exactly this structure -- same four fields in, same four out -- and its doc names VEP's `compare_existing()` and Ensembl Variation's `get_matched_variant_alleles()` as anchors; tests/port_compare_existing.rs already unit-ports five rows of ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_Variation.ledger.toml n=9-14 against it. #173 named the gap exactly: what was missing was never the observation point, it was the SECOND INPUT -- the cache record's allele_string/start/strand, which the Perl never writes down because it comes out of the cache at run time. tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache (#96) supplies it, and the test reads it rather than inventing it. What does NOT survive v84 -> v115 is the b-side, and this row's assertion is split accordingly: a_index and a_allele are the Perl's OWN literals, b_allele and b_index are re-derived. The v84 cache carried an insertion record at this locus whose alleles were `GCG` and `GTG`; the committed v115 record is rs372061766, `GCGGCGGCGG/GCGG/GCGGCGG/GCGGCGGCGGCGG/GCGGCGGCGGCGGCGG` at 21:8987006-8987015. That is the re-derivation #101 and detailed_plans/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.md ask for, not a weakening: the halves that are the Perl's are asserted as the Perl's. The test is exhaustive rather than locus-picked: it runs the matcher over ALL 16666 rows of the committed shard and asserts the complete match set, so a second matching record could not hide. Two positive controls, because `it matched` is worth nothing alone: four committed records carry an allele token that is LITERALLY `GCG` (rs1601202819, rs1988347167, rs1419902987, rs1168016116) and none of them is the match, so the pairing is coordinate-plus-minimisation and not string equality; and the neighbouring insertion at the same start, rs1555836472 `G/GTGG`, does not match either, so it is not `any insertion at 8987006`. One behaviour is recorded rather than asserted as equivalence: handed the RAW VCF spelling `A/AGCG` at 8987005 the matcher STILL finds rs372061766, because it minimises its own a-side too -- what the parser-level derivation fixes is the reported a_allele, which dfbf reports as the pre-trim input allele (src/allele.rs:261, `orig_a_alt`): `AGCG` from the raw spelling, `GCG` -- the Perl's value -- from the VF. Mutation-checked on a_index and on the match count.

desc: get_frequency_data - matched alleles: at 21:25005812 CA/CAAA,CAAA the frequency is looked up under the trimmed allele AAA, giving 1KG_AMR 0.4107 -- not under the raw ALT
rationale: Ported, and `0.4107` ports as the Perl's OWN v84 literal. The row joins n=36-39 to n=23: the frequency must key on the allele the MATCHER produced, not on the input's ALT text. Both halves are measurable against tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache (#96). (1) With the a-side derived as at n=36, the VF for `21 25005812 . CA CAAA,CAAA` is `A/AAA/AAA` at 25005813, and over ALL 16666 committed records exactly one matches: rs34989270 at 25005813-25005820, `a_allele AAA` (the TRIMMED allele, never the VCF's `CAAA`) at `a_index 0`, paired with the record's own spelling of the same insertion, `AAAAAAAAAA`, at `b_index 2` of six ALTs. (2) The 1000-Genomes AMR frequency the shard carries for that record is attached to exactly that allele: `AMR = AAAAAAAAAA:0.4107`, read back through the pin's own point-lookup reader, which reconstructs the `allele:freq` spelling VEP's cache uses. Observation point, and what this row does NOT claim. VEP reports the frequency under the INPUT's matched allele (`AAA`); vepyr's cache stores it under the RECORD's allele (`AAAAAAAAAA`); `frequency_match_output_allele()` (annotate_provider.rs:1854 @ dfbf 391f94bd, whose doc cites VEP's `add_colocated_frequency_data()`) is the function that would map one onto the other -- and THE NAMED TEST NEVER RUNS IT. What is ported is the matcher's property (the a-side allele is the trimmed `AAA`, and the b-side it pairs with is the record whose frequency row this is) plus the cache's stored value; the pipeline step between them is not observed here, so an earlier draft of this rationale claiming `the value ... are the same` overstated it and is corrected. LIMITATION, measured on these very fixtures rather than argued: end to end the engine does not currently reproduce this row at all. `annotate_to_vcf` over `21 25005812 . CA CAAA` emits `Allele=AA` -- the engine minimises past VEP's one-anchor-base parser rule, which would give `-/AAA` at 25005813 -- with `Existing_variation` and `AMR_AF` both EMPTY; and feeding the already-normalised spelling `21 25005813 . A AAAA` gives `Allele=AAA` and still an EMPTY `Existing_variation`, so the miss is the colocation itself and not only the allele spelling. Positive control in the same run: `21 25585733 . C T` colocates normally, `Existing_variation=rs142513484`, `AF=0.0010`, `AMR_AF=0.0014`. That divergence candidate is tracked as old-repo issue #331 (single-ALT insertion normalisation); if it is confirmed as a divergence this row is a candidate to become `failed` with an end-to-end pin, which this sweep was not authorised to create. Deliberately NOT through CSQ: this input is multi-ALT, and measured on this fixture `annotate_to_vcf` emits a field-shifted CSQ group for multi-ALT rows (see n=37), so the emitted VCF cannot be read for this row at the pin. Positive control that the allele qualifier is a selection rather than decoration: the record offers six ALTs and every 1000-Genomes column names the same one of them. The filter accumulator `_freq_check_freqs` the Perl reads the value out of is still absent (n=19, no-feature) -- the same split as n=23 and n=30. Mutation-checked on the AMR value and on the a-side allele.

desc: _get_tabix_obj - ref: asking the source for chromosome 21's handle returns a Bio::DB::HTS::Tabix object
rationale: A concrete adapter-class identity on a per-chromosome file handle. `_get_tabix_obj` (`VariationTabix.pm:260`) opens `Bio::DB::HTS::Tabix->new(filename => $file)` for one chromosome's `all_vars.gz`. vepyr has no per-chromosome handle to return: parquet shards are read through DataFusion's `TableProvider::scan`, which yields an `ExecutionPlan`, and `PartitionedParquetCache` resolves paths only -- probed, `error[E0599]: no method named `tabix_obj` found for reference `&PartitionedParquetCache``, with `context_path` compiling as the positive control in the same file. This sits inside the SKIP block guarding `CAN_USE_TABIX_PM`, whose whole purpose is the tabix backend vepyr lacks, so docs/ledger-contract.md's SKIP convention keeps it at no-feature rather than letting the class-identity reading pull it out of the denominator. Missing feature: a tabix-indexed variation-cache reader and its handles (n=4).

Missing feature: a per-chromosome cache-file handle, and with it the bounded pool that this row and n=43 pin.

rationale: The invalidation half of n=42: the cache is a plain hashref slot, and clearing it must be observable as a different object coming back. Both halves need a public per-chromosome handle, which vepyr does not have (n=41, n=42). The nearest vepyr concept, session-level metadata caching, is neither per-chromosome nor clearable through a documented call, so it is not a different observation point for this property but a different property.

The fixture now exists (tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache, #96) and the test is written. Values re-derived as at n=13.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer count annotated: with the Perl tabix module disabled, 132 of the buffer's variants still come back annotated
rationale: The blocker this row carried was two-part and its first part was FALSE at the pin: it said `$test_cfg->{test_vcf}` is not vendored here. It is -- `tests/data/vep116_runner_input/test.vcf.gz`, whose plaintext is byte-identical to upstream's t/testdata/input/test.vcf (sha256 a7ecda18970e4546e0e3850648f55682c96f884a89f2c1e2ec153d76dc2d4bf3, 132 records, all chr21); the search behind the claim was `find -name '*.vcf'`, which cannot match a `.vcf.gz`. The second part -- that the committed shard was too narrow -- was true, and is closed by recipe R1 in tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/PROVENANCE.md: +-100 bp around each of the 132 vendored positions. The condition R1 rests on was verified on the NATIVE v115 cache before the rebuild, so that the number 132 survives the change of release rather than being produced by it: 132/132 positions have an exact-start v115 record with a matching REF/ALT, 0 mismatches, 0 missing. Positive control for the method: the same pass counts 160516 records in 25585733..25982445, matching the campaign unlock map's independent figure (position is field 5 of all_vars.gz). Negative controls: positions +7 gives 7/132, ALT rotated A->C->G->T gives 16/132. This row sits in the file's last SKIP block, which sets $CAN_USE_TABIX_PM = 0 to force `_annotate_cl`, the batched command-line reader, in place of n=17's in-process one. So the row is not a duplicate of n=17: what it exists to say is that the census does NOT depend on which reader produced the candidates. vepyr has no second backend to force, and inventing one would be fiction -- what it has is a second READ PATH over the same shard, the full projected scan `parquet_cache::scan::read_context_parquet`, and the invariant carries across unchanged. The test therefore asserts SET equality between the indexed path's annotated inputs and the scanned path's, keyed on the 132 distinct input rsIDs, not merely that both count 132: two readers that each drop a different input agree on the count and disagree on the set, and it is the set VEP's two backends are required to share. Recorded rather than claimed: the Perl-ecosystem machinery that does the forcing has no vepyr counterpart, so what is ported is the invariant, not the switch.

desc: nastiness 3 - _annotate_cl: with the Perl tabix module disabled, 21:8987004 TAT/TAGCGT still trims shared prefix and suffix to GCG
rationale: This row sits in the file's last SKIP block, which forces the command-line backend by setting `$CAN_USE_TABIX_PM = 0`; the forcing is Perl-ecosystem machinery with no vepyr counterpart, so the row inherits its twin's disposition exactly. Twin of n=38. STILL BLOCKED, and now measured rather than asserted. The blocker is no longer `the missing chr21 variation cache` -- that is closed (#96) and its siblings n=36/37/49/50 are ported against it through the public `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles`. What is missing is narrower: a cache record at 21:8987004-8987006 carrying the v84 INSERTION ALLELES the Perl's expected value spells. Measured with the a-side derived exactly as for n=36 (`allele::vcf_to_vep_input_allele` plus VEP's first-alt anchor rule): the VF is `AT/AGCGT` at 8987005, and over ALL 16666 committed records the single match is rs372061766 with `a_allele AGCGT`, `a_index 0`, `b_allele GCGGCGGCGGCGG`, `b_index 2`. The Perl expects `a_allele GCG` -- the TRIMMED spelling -- and that is this row's whole distinctive content over n=36, which already ports `a_index 0` with `a_allele GCG`. The committed v115 records at the locus are `C/T`, `C/CCGC/CGGC` and `CTGC/C` at 8987004, `T/A/C/G` at 8987005 and rs372061766 at 8987006-8987015; positive control that the search for the v84 alleles was real, four OTHER records in the shard do carry an allele token that is literally `GCG` (rs1601202819, rs1988347167, rs1419902987, rs1168016116) and none of them sits at this locus. RECORDED FOR WHOEVER GETS THE RECORD: the `a_allele` difference may be a real divergence in reporting rather than a fixture artefact -- VEP reports the pass-current allele of whichever trim direction matched, while dfbf always reports the pre-trim input allele (`orig_a_alt`, src/allele.rs:261 @ 391f94bd). It is not adjudicable here, because with a different b-side the two implementations are not being asked the same question.

desc: nastiness 4 - _annotate_cl: with the Perl tabix module disabled, 21:8987004 TAT/TAGCGT,TAGTGT still matches both ALTs to two cache rows, GCG and GTG
rationale: This row sits in the file's last SKIP block, which forces the command-line backend by setting `$CAN_USE_TABIX_PM = 0`; the forcing is Perl-ecosystem machinery with no vepyr counterpart, so the row inherits its twin's disposition exactly. Twin of n=39, and the last assertion in the file. STILL BLOCKED, for a sharper reason than n=38's and one that no re-derivation closes. This row's content is that ONE cache record accumulates TWO matches with paired a/b indices -- Perl asserts `$existing->[0]{matched_alleles}` has two entries, `(0, AGCGT, GCG, 0)` and `(1, AGTGT, GTG, 1)`. Measured over all 16666 committed records with the a-side derived as at n=36: the VF `AT/AGCGT/AGTGT` at 8987005 matches TWO DIFFERENT records, one per ALT -- rs372061766 gives `(a_index 0, AGCGT, b_allele GCGGCGGCGGCGG, b_index 2)` and rs1555836472 (`G/GTGG`) gives `(a_index 1, AGTGT, b_allele GTGG, b_index 0)`. Perl's per-record array therefore has one entry per record here, and the accumulate-rather-than-short-circuit property has no input at all. Measured: 0 of the 16666 records carry both a `GCG` and a `GTG` alt token (positive control: 4 carry a literal `GCG`, 2 carry a literal `GCGG`). What is missing is a single cache record at the locus whose allele_string offers two alts each matching a different input ALT. A RE-SITED analogue is available if the owner wants one -- rs1402623917 at 21:8987004 (`C/CCGC/CGGC`) and rs1555836714 at 21:8987929 (`-/A/GC/GGC/T`) both offer two candidate alts -- but it would change the Perl's input, which is why it is not taken unilaterally. Note that vepyr's side of the property is present: `get_matched_variant_alleles` accumulates into a Vec with a HashSet guard against exact duplicates (src/allele.rs:250, :266-269 @ 391f94bd); it is the second input that is absent. Its SKIP block declares `skip ..., 2` while containing six assertions (n=47-52) -- an upstream counting slip, one of the 14 collected at old-repo issue #172 and tabulated at docs/upstream-findings.md:50, and inert because every file ends in `done_testing()`. desc: BASIC TESTS: the database regulatory-feature annotation-source module loads
rationale: The file's only top-level assertion, and a module-load probe: it asserts Perl's `require` found AnnotationSource/Database/RegFeat.pm, compiled it and ran its import. docs/ledger-contract.md ruling R2 makes that not-applicable unconditionally — no Rust design performs a module load at runtime that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart whatever the class denotes. desc: DATABASE TESTS: Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config loads inside the database SKIP block, so a config can be built from the live-DB credentials
rationale: A module-load probe on VEP's config class. Not-applicable under ruling R2 for the same reason as n=1, and R2 is explicit that position inside a SKIP block does not change the answer: the subject is Perl's loader, not the database feature the block guards. desc: get new config object: Config->new accepts the live-DB credential hash together with database => 1, offline => 0, species => homo_vepiens and regulatory => 1
rationale: A constructor probe, decided by denotation under docs/ledger-contract.md's ok($obj) ruling, and two absent options meet in it. `database => 1` with `offline => 0` selects the MySQL backend: `grep -rniI '"database"' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `options_json` -> 95, the probe ledger/Config.ledger.toml n=19 and n=30 already record. `regulatory => 1` is the request flag ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=30 classifies no-feature for the same reason — the pin's option vocabulary does not contain it, regulatory annotation being decided by what the cache holds rather than by a flag. The credential keys of `%$db_cfg` (host, port, user, password) appear in neither the 31-key DataFusion option vocabulary nor AnnotateVcfConfig's 34 public fields.

desc: new is defined: AnnotationSource::Database::RegFeat->new({config}) returns a defined source, built from nothing but the database-mode config
rationale: The load-bearing constructor probe of the file, and the row that accounts for the construction n=5 reads back. Decided by denotation under the ok($obj) ruling: the class denotes a regulatory-feature source backed by an Ensembl Funcgen database, reached through the adaptor factory. Neither half exists at the pin — `grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 and `grep -rniI 'Funcgen' src/` -> 2 lines, both //! doc comments in motif_matrix.rs, against the positive control `regulatory` -> 243. vepyr reads regulatory features from parquet written ahead of time; there is no source object that could be constructed from credentials. ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=43-50 classify the sibling database block the same way.

desc: check class: ref($as) reads back exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::Database::RegFeat for the object n=4 just constructed
rationale: A blessing readback two lines after its constructor, and ruling R1 takes it on the first bullet: the construction already carries its own row at n=4, so all this line adds is Perl object identity, which is on docs/ledger-contract.md's explicit not-applicable list. R1's worked case states the counterfactual — Parser_SPDI n=4 and Parser_CAID n=4 stay no-feature only because neither file contains an `ok($p = ...->new)` row, and had either opened with a constructor probe the readback would have been not-applicable. Counting it again here would count n=4's absence twice, the double-counting R2 rules out one paragraph later.

desc: info: the source's info hash is exactly { regbuild => 13.0 } — one key, the Ensembl regulatory-build version, read from the funcgen database rather than from a file
rationale: What the row pins is where the regulatory-build version comes from: VEP asks the funcgen database, through the adaptor layer, which build produced the features it is about to fetch. The tempting shortcut is to say vepyr has no regbuild at all — `grep -rniI 'regbuild'` -> 0 lines over both pinned workspaces — and that reading is wrong, which is why it is written out here. `SourceDescriptor::from_info_source` (bio-format-ensembl-cache 0d9730c8 info.rs:26-45) turns every `source_<name>` line of info.txt into a `source_<name>` Arrow column at runtime, so a cache declaring `source_regbuild 13.0` does surface the value on every entity schema (schema.rs:440-455) even though the token appears nowhere in the code. That cache-mode channel already has its row, as an analog-port, at ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=24. What is absent is this row's own boundary: an `info` method on a database-backed source that queries the funcgen meta tables — no adaptor (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `regulatory` -> 243) and no database client. So the row is no-feature about the database origin, and it does not restate n=24.

desc: get_available_cell_types - empty: with no cell type requested the source lists all 38 cell types the funcgen database offers, sorted, from A549 to neutrophil:VenousBlood:hist
rationale: The row pins that the source can enumerate its own cell-type dimension before anything is fetched — the list a user picks `--cell_type` from and the list n=8 and n=9 validate against. vepyr has no such dimension in the annotation path: `grep -rniI 'cell_type' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, against the positive controls `regulatory` -> 243 and `motif` -> 417. The measurement worth recording is that the data is not missing, the feature is: the cache writer emits a `cell_types` column into both the regulatory and motif schemas (bio-format-ensembl-cache 0d9730c8 schema.rs:269 and :300, populated at regulatory.rs:487 and :527), and the annotation crate never reads it. Nothing enumerates it, nothing filters on it, and no option selects it.

desc: check_cell_types: with cell_type set to the available HUVEC, the validation passes
rationale: The positive arm of a validation step that exists only because cell types are a user-supplied restriction: check_cell_types intersects the request against n=7's list and lets the run proceed. With no cell-type dimension read anywhere in the annotation crate (`grep -rniI 'cell_type' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `regulatory` -> 243) there is no request to validate and no set to intersect. The missing feature is cell-type-restricted regulatory annotation, not the check.

desc: check_cell_types - fail: with cell_type set to the non-existent JUVEC the source dies with /Cell type .* unavailable/, i.e. an unusable request is refused up front rather than silently annotating nothing
rationale: The sharper half of n=8 and the one with real content: a typo in a cell-type name must fail loudly, because the alternative — annotating with an empty cell-type set — looks like a clean run with no regulatory hits. vepyr cannot exhibit either behaviour, correct or incorrect, because it never reads a cell type (n=7's measurement). This is an absent operation rather than a private one, so the contract's absent-operation test returns no-feature: what is missing is the restriction feature, not a `pub`.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached ref 1: the single-region database fetch for [21, 511] returns an arrayref
rationale: A container-kind probe whose subject IS the absent thing, which is the distinction R2's corollary draws: `get_features_by_regions_uncached` issues the funcgen query for one 50 kb region and blesses the rows into Funcgen objects (AnnotationSource/Database/RegFeat.pm:144-213 @ release/116.0, where `get_adaptor('funcgen', 'RegulatoryFeature')->fetch_all_by_Slice` at :185 and the MotifFeature arm at :213 are the two queries). vepyr has no adaptor to query — `grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `regulatory` -> 243 — so there is no call whose return shape could be checked. Contrast ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=37, where the same probe is not-applicable because the pull it describes is a real cache-mode operation.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached count: exactly 12 regulatory-family features come back for the single region [21, 511]
rationale: A census over one 50 kb window, and the row that would catch a fetch window off by a base or a join that duplicated rows. It is the uncached arm specifically, so it also pins what the memo n=15-17 later replays. Nothing in vepyr issues this query, and the number is a property of the homo_vepiens MultiTestDB fixture, so even with a database source built the value would have to be re-derived rather than carried across.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached ref 2: the first element of the single-region fetch is a Bio::EnsEMBL::Funcgen::RegulatoryFeature, so the fetch is ordered regulatory-before-motif
rationale: A blessing probe of the absent thing, and more than a type check: taken with n=14 it says the mixed result is ordered so that a RegulatoryFeature comes first. vepyr has no Funcgen object model at all — `grep -rniI 'Funcgen' src/` -> 2 lines, both //! doc comments in motif_matrix.rs — and no database fetch to order. Its own regulatory-before-motif ordering is a separate, cache-mode property already accounted for at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=20/n=21 through the `FeatureType::rank` constant, so nothing is lost by classifying this row by its own source.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached stable_id: the first fetched regulatory feature is ENSR00001963185
rationale: Identity rather than shape: the row pins which feature the query returns first, so it catches an ORDER BY change or a window shifted by one region as n=11's count alone would not. vepyr produces no ENSR identifier from a database — its regulatory stable ids come from the parquet cache, a different source with a different fixture — and there is no query here to reorder. The absent product is the funcgen fetch measured at n=10.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached feature types: the distinct blessed classes in the single-region result are exactly MotifFeature and RegulatoryFeature — two families in one fetch, and no third
rationale: The row that makes n=12 more than a type check: one call to the database source returns two different Funcgen classes, and the assertion pins that set exactly, so a fetch that silently dropped motifs or gained a third class would fail here. vepyr keeps the two families in separate parquet datasets read by separate providers rather than in one mixed fetch, and has no Funcgen class to name in either case (`grep -rniI 'Funcgen' src/` -> 2 prose lines). What is missing is the mixed database fetch, so the row is no-feature rather than a differently-shaped analogue.

desc: get_features_by_regions_cached ref 1: after the uncached fetch, the CACHED accessor for the same region [21, 511] returns an arrayref without going back to the database
rationale: The first of three rows about the per-source region memo, which exists because each miss costs a SQL round trip: upstream's own comment at perl/AnnotationSource_Database_RegFeat.t:151 says `now we should be able to retrieve the same from memory`. vepyr has no such memo for regulatory features and no query to avoid; its only pruning analogue, `prune_persisted_buffer_transcripts` (dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:11523), is transcript-only and private. So the row's subject — the cached arm of a database fetch — has no counterpart to call.

desc: get_features_by_regions_cached ref 2: the memo replays a Bio::EnsEMBL::Funcgen::RegulatoryFeature first, i.e. the cached path preserves the uncached path's class and ordering
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=12: the point is agreement between two paths, so a memo that stored a flattened or re-ordered copy would fail here while the uncached assertions still passed. Both paths are absent from vepyr for the reason measured at n=10 and n=15, and there is no second path whose agreement with a first could be asserted.

desc: get_features_by_regions_cached stable_id: the memo replays ENSR00001963185 first, identical to the uncached fetch of n=13
rationale: The identity half of n=16 and the strongest statement of the memo's contract: the cached path must return the same features, in the same order, as the database path it replaces. vepyr has neither path (n=10, n=15), so there is nothing to compare; the absent feature is the database-backed regulatory source together with the per-region memo layered over it.

desc: clean_cache: after clean_cache() the source's entire region memo is the empty hash, so memory does not grow without bound as the input walks the genome
rationale: The lifecycle end of n=15-17, and the row where a near-analogue has to be refused explicitly. vepyr does mirror VEP's clean_cache — `prune_persisted_buffer_transcripts` (dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:11523) carries a doc comment citing `AnnotationSource::clean_cache()` by URL — but it prunes persisted TRANSCRIPT objects against the still-active transcript cache regions, and it is a private free fn with no `pub`. This row's subject is a regulatory source's own `cache` hash going empty; vepyr holds no regulatory memo at all, so the analogue is a different entity as well as an unnameable item. Naming it would be a false analogue, so the row is no-feature rather than deferred / blocked-api.

desc: TESTS WITH AN INPUT BUFFER: Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF loads, so the test VCF can be read into a buffer
rationale: A module-load probe on the VCF parser. Not-applicable under ruling R2, and here the class does not even denote something absent: vepyr reads VCF (`grep -rniI 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, and `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` at vcf_sink.rs:1018 is the public entry point). What the assertion checks is Perl's loader, which has no runtime counterpart in Rust.

desc: get parser object: Parser::VCF->new({config, file => the test VCF}) returns a defined parser
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. The type that stands in is `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`: vepyr never hands a caller a parser object, so the nearest thing an external crate can construct is the provider `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` registers internally (`vcf_sink.rs:1074` and `:1079` @ dfbf 391f94bd, both `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` — the five arguments the named test passes), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The probe is load-bearing rather than plumbing because that constructor is genuinely fallible: it `block_on`s `determine_schema_from_header` and propagates with `?` (`table_provider.rs:869-879` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8), i.e. it reads and parses the VCF header before it can return — exactly the ruling's defined/undef -> `Ok`/`Err` case. The named test asserts both limbs: `Ok` over a one-row VCF written to a tempdir, and over a missing path a typed error that is classified `NotFound` and names the path — because an `is_ok()` on its own would also pass against a constructor that never fails. Dual-claimed with the fourteen sibling rows the sweep moved together; all fifteen are the same statement at the same boundary, and the roster is kept in one place, the table at the top of tests/port_parser_vcf_construct.rs. R2's corollary still contributes its negative half here — the SKIP block guarding the absent database does not carry this row to no-feature, because the probe's subject is the VCF parser and not the database. What the sweep adds is the positive half: that subject is a capability vepyr does have, so the row is a port rather than plumbing.

desc: TESTS WITH AN INPUT BUFFER: Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer loads
rationale: The last of this file's four module-load probes. Not-applicable under ruling R2; as with n=19 the class denotes something vepyr has — `InputBufferAccumulator` (dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:9521) is the buffer VEP's InputBuffer corresponds to — so the only thing the line could add is the runtime `require`, which Rust never performs.

rationale: A blessing probe on a class vepyr has: ruling R1's second bullet, since InputBuffer denotes buffering and `InputBufferAccumulator` (annotate_provider.rs:9521) is its counterpart, so the readback restates a compile-time fact — a Rust constructor's return type is its class and cannot disagree with itself at runtime. R2's corollary contributes only the negative half — it blocks the SKIP block from carrying the row to no-feature, the subject being the buffer and not the database — and R1 is what delivers not-applicable. Four merged ledgers read the identical line the same way: ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=9, ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=34, ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=11, ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=9.

rationale: A reftype probe on a method's return value, and only that: an empty arrayref satisfies it, so the line says nothing about how many variants were read or which. In Rust the shape of a return is a compile-time fact carried by the signature, and vepyr's counterpart hands back Arrow RecordBatch values whose type no runtime check could contradict. What delivers the category is the contract's own not-applicable list, on which a reference-type probe sits alongside the blessing probes; R2's corollary does no more than block the SKIP block from carrying the row to no-feature, the subject being the buffer and not the database. The same line is already not-applicable at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=10, ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=10 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=12.

desc: get_all_regions_by_InputBuffer: the chr21 test buffer reduces to exactly eight 50 kb fetch regions — [21,511] through [21,519] with 516 absent, because no variant falls in it
rationale: Read carelessly this looks like the blocked-api rows at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=11 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=36, which pin the same method name. It is not the same property. Those assert [[21, 25]] — the 1 Mb cache block whose index vepyr really does compute, privately, at annotate_provider.rs:11410. This row asserts a 50 kb granularity, set for every database source by `$self->{cache_region_size} ||= 50000` (modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/AnnotationSource/Database.pm:84 @ release/116.0), whose only consumer is the SQL fetch window built at AnnotationSource/Database/RegFeat.pm:165-166 and handed to `fetch_all_by_Slice` at :185. vepyr's region size is not a database-fetch parameter at all: it is read from the cache's own info.txt into `CacheInfo::cache_region_size` (bio-format-ensembl-cache 0d9730c8 info.rs:48, key matched at info.rs:108-110). No fetch, no 50 kb, no `pub` to add — an absent operation, so no-feature.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 1: the buffer-wide pull across all eight regions returns an arrayref
rationale: The buffer-wide counterpart of n=10, and no-feature for the same reason and by the same measurement: the pull concatenates one database fetch per region of n=24, and vepyr has no adaptor to fetch from (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `regulatory` -> 243). Its subject is the absent call, not a container shape vepyr could disagree about, which is what keeps it out of the not-applicable column that ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=37 occupies for the cache-mode pull.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 2: the buffer-wide pull OPENS with a Bio::EnsEMBL::Funcgen::RegulatoryFeature
rationale: A blessing probe of the absent thing, and it is about the concatenation rather than the single fetch: n=12 pins the ordering inside one region, this pins that the ordering survives the join of eight. vepyr has no Funcgen object model (`grep -rniI 'Funcgen' src/` -> 2 //! doc lines in motif_matrix.rs) and no per-region fetch to concatenate. The cache-mode statement of the same concatenation property is separately accounted for at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=38, deferred / blocked-data, so this row does not double-count it.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 3: the buffer-wide pull also CLOSES with a RegulatoryFeature — unlike the cache source, whose same pull ends on a MotifFeature
rationale: Worth its own row twice over. First, checking only the head would miss a later region contributing a differently-blessed row or an undef, so the `[-1]` index is what makes n=26's claim cover the join. Second, the expected class differs from the cache source's: t/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.t:144 asserts a MotifFeature last for the same buffer, so the two backends are pinned to produce differently-ordered concatenations and this row is not the cache row restated. vepyr performs neither concatenation, having no database fetch (n=25) and, in cache mode, a separately-accounted ordering claim at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=39.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer stable_id: the first feature of the buffer-wide pull is ENSR00001963192 — a different feature from the single-region fetch's ENSR00001963185, because the buffer spans more than region 511
rationale: The row pins that the concatenation is ordered by position across regions rather than by the order the regions were fetched: if it were the latter, region 511's ENSR00001963185 would still be first. That is a real failure mode of a per-region fetch loop, which is why the row is not n=13 repeated. vepyr issues no database fetch to order (n=25), and its cache-mode counterpart is ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=40, deferred / blocked-data.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer count: exactly 90 regulatory-family features overlap the whole chr21 test buffer, against 12 for the single region of n=11
rationale: The census closest to production: it counts what an annotation run would actually consider for this buffer, so a boundary or filter regression moves it, and it is the row that would catch a region silently dropped from the eight of n=24. Nothing in vepyr issues the query, and the value is a property of the homo_vepiens MultiTestDB fixture rather than of the algorithm, so it could not be carried across even if the source were built.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer again: a SECOND buffer-wide pull over the same unchanged buffer returns ENSR00001963192 first again, so the per-region memo is hit rather than the database re-queried
rationale: Idempotency across a warm memo, one level up from n=15-17 — upstream's own comment at perl/AnnotationSource_Database_RegFeat.t:234 says `do it again to get them from memory`. It earns its row because a stateful reader that consumed its input on the first pass would fail here and nowhere else. vepyr has neither the query to avoid nor the memo to hit (n=15), and its cache-mode counterpart is ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=42, deferred / blocked-data.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - display_consequence: after _finish_annotation the first buffered variant reports regulatory_region_variant, i.e. the database overlap wins the most-severe-consequence ranking and reaches the user

Reading it as portable would claim coverage of a backend that does not exist.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the database structural-variation annotation-source module loads
rationale: The file's only top-level assertion, and a module-load probe: it asserts Perl's `require` found AnnotationSource/Database/StructuralVariation.pm, compiled it and ran its import. docs/ledger-contract.md ruling R2 makes that not-applicable unconditionally — no Rust design performs a module load at runtime that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart whatever the class denotes. The missing feature is database-backed annotation; until it exists there is no configuration to accept or refuse.

desc: new is defined: AnnotationSource::Database::StructuralVariation->new({config}) returns a defined source, built from nothing but the database-mode config
rationale: The load-bearing constructor probe of the file and the row that accounts for the construction n=5 reads back. Under the ok($obj) ruling it is decided by denotation, and the class denotes two capabilities vepyr lacks at once: a database-backed annotation source (no adaptor layer, `grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd) and an existing-structural-variant catalogue (`grep -rniI 'StructuralVariationFeature|overlapping_svs' src/` -> 0, positive control `transcript` -> 3040). desc: check class: ref($as) reads back exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::Database::StructuralVariation for the object n=4 just constructed
rationale: A blessing readback two lines after its constructor, and docs/ledger-contract.md ruling R1 takes it on the first bullet: the construction already carries its own row at n=4, so all this line adds is Perl object identity, which is on the contract's explicit not-applicable list. R1's own worked case states the counterfactual — Parser_SPDI n=4 and Parser_CAID n=4 stay no-feature only because neither file contains an `ok($p = ...->new)` row, and had either opened with a constructor probe the readback would have been not-applicable. This file opens with one at n=4, which is where the gap is counted; counting it again here would count the same absence twice, the double-counting R2 rules out one paragraph later.
