desc: TESTS WITH AN INPUT BUFFER: Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF loads, so the test VCF can be read into a buffer
rationale: The third module-load probe, on the VCF parser. Not-applicable under ruling R2, and here the class does not even denote something absent: vepyr reads VCF (`grep -rniI 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, and `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` at vcf_sink.rs:1018 is the public entry point). What the assertion checks is Perl's loader, which has no runtime counterpart in Rust.

desc: get parser object: Parser::VCF->new({config, file => the test VCF}) returns a defined parser
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. The type that stands in is `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`: vepyr never hands a caller a parser object, so the nearest thing an external crate can construct is the provider `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` registers internally (`vcf_sink.rs:1074` and `:1079` @ dfbf 391f94bd, both `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` — the five arguments the named test passes), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The probe is load-bearing rather than plumbing because that constructor is genuinely fallible: it `block_on`s `determine_schema_from_header` and propagates with `?` (`table_provider.rs:869-879` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8), i.e. it reads and parses the VCF header before it can return — exactly the ruling's defined/undef -> `Ok`/`Err` case. The named test asserts both limbs: `Ok` over a one-row VCF written to a tempdir, and over a missing path a typed error that is classified `NotFound` and names the path — because an `is_ok()` on its own would also pass against a constructor that never fails. Dual-claimed with the fourteen sibling rows the sweep moved together; all fifteen are the same statement at the same boundary, and the roster is kept in one place, the table at the top of tests/port_parser_vcf_construct.rs. R2's corollary still contributes its negative half here — the SKIP block guarding the absent database does not carry this row to no-feature, because the probe's subject is the VCF parser and not the database. What the sweep adds is the positive half: that subject is a capability vepyr does have, so the row is a port rather than plumbing.

desc: TESTS WITH AN INPUT BUFFER: Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer loads
rationale: The fourth and last module-load probe. Not-applicable under ruling R2; as with n=6 the class denotes something vepyr has — `InputBufferAccumulator` (dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:9521) is the buffer VEP's InputBuffer corresponds to — so the only thing the line could add is the runtime `require`, which Rust never performs.

desc: check class: ref($ib) is exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer, not a subclass and not a plain hashref
rationale: A blessing probe on a class vepyr has: docs/ledger-contract.md ruling R1's second bullet, since InputBuffer denotes buffering and `InputBufferAccumulator` (annotate_provider.rs:9521) is its counterpart, so the readback restates a compile-time fact — a Rust constructor's return type is its class and cannot disagree with itself at runtime. R2's corollary contributes only the negative half — it blocks the SKIP block from carrying the row to no-feature, the subject being the buffer and not the database — and R1 is what delivers not-applicable. Four merged ledgers read the identical line the same way: ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=9, ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=34, ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=11, ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=9.

desc: check buffer next: InputBuffer::next returns an arrayref — a list-shaped batch rather than a scalar, hashref or object
rationale: A reftype probe on a method's return value, and only that: an empty arrayref satisfies it, so the line says nothing about how many variants were read or which. In Rust the shape of a return is a compile-time fact carried by the signature, and vepyr's counterpart hands back Arrow RecordBatch values whose type no runtime check could contradict. What delivers the category is the contract's own not-applicable list, on which a reference-type probe sits alongside the blessing probes; R2's corollary does no more than block the SKIP block from carrying the row to no-feature, the subject being the buffer and not the database. The same line is already not-applicable at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=10, ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=10 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=12.

desc: get_all_regions_by_InputBuffer: the chr21 test buffer reduces to exactly eight 50 kb fetch regions — [21,511], [21,512], [21,513], [21,514], [21,515], [21,517], [21,518], [21,519] — with 516 absent because no variant falls in it
rationale: Read carelessly this looks like the blocked-api rows at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=11 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=36, which pin the same method. It is not the same property. Those assert [[21, 25]] — the 1 Mb transcript-cache block whose index vepyr really does compute, privately, at annotate_provider.rs:11410. This row asserts a 50 kb granularity, set for every database source by `$self->{cache_region_size} ||= 50000` (modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/AnnotationSource/Database.pm:84 @ release/116.0), whose only consumer is the SQL fetch window built at StructuralVariation.pm:132-133. vepyr performs no fetch that would need it and has no constant of that size, so what is missing is an operation, not a `pub`: the contract's absent-operation test returns no-feature. The gap the row also pins — that empty blocks are dropped rather than fetched — belongs to the same absent operation.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 1: the buffer-wide structural-variant pull returns an arrayref
rationale: A container-kind probe, which would be not-applicable if its subject were present — as it is at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=37, where the pull is a real cache-mode operation. Here the subject IS the absent thing, which is exactly the distinction R2's corollary draws: `get_all_features_by_InputBuffer` on a database structural-variation source fetches known SVs through a StructuralVariationFeature adaptor, and neither the adaptor layer nor an existing-SV catalogue exists at the pin (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0, `grep -rniI 'StructuralVariationFeature' src/` -> 0, positive control `transcript` -> 3040). There is no call whose return shape could be checked.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 2: the first element of the pull is a Bio::EnsEMBL::Variation::StructuralVariationFeature
rationale: A blessing probe whose subject is the absent product: the element type is the Ensembl Variation SV feature, the object a StructuralVariationFeatureAdaptor returns. vepyr has no such type — `grep -rniI 'StructuralVariationFeature' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `transcript` -> 3040 — and its only structural type, `StructuralFeature` (transcript_consequence.rs:603), is a consequence-side record carrying feature_id, chrom, start, end, feature_kind and event_kind, with none of the catalogue identity this row is about. R2's corollary keeps such a probe in the denominator; ledger/Parser_ID.ledger.toml n=7 records the same refusal to name vepyr's SV table as the analogue.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 3: the LAST element of the pull is also a StructuralVariationFeature, so the concatenation of the eight region fetches is homogeneous end to end
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=13. The pull concatenates one fetch per region (StructuralVariation.pm:117-140 loops over the regions n=11 enumerates), so checking only the head would miss a later region contributing a differently-blessed row or an undef; the `[-1]` index is what makes the claim cover the join. The absent product is the same as n=13's and measured the same way, and the concatenation boundary has no vepyr counterpart either, there being no per-region fetch to concatenate.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer variation_name: the first fetched structural variant is the dbVar accession nsv1061577
rationale: The first row whose content is catalogue identity rather than shape: it pins that the fetch is ordered so that nsv1061577 comes first, and that the accession survives the adaptor round trip. vepyr produces no accession of this kind. Its structural record has no variation_name, study or source field (`StructuralFeature`, transcript_consequence.rs:603-610), and there is no CSQ column for it: `grep -rniI 'SV_OVERLAP' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, against the positive control `regulatory` -> 243. detailed_plans/AnnotationSource_Database_StructuralVariation.md sizes the missing cache-mode prerequisite at M and the database source on top of it at a further M.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer count: exactly 750 known structural variants overlap the buffer's eight 50 kb regions
rationale: A census, and the row that would catch a fetch window off by a region or a de-duplication that dropped SVs spanning two regions — 750 is what the whole loop of n=11's regions yields after the per-source cache merges them. Nothing in vepyr counts anything comparable, there being no existing-SV catalogue to count from; the same absence measured at n=13 and n=15. Note also that the number is a property of the homo_vepiens MultiTestDB fixture, so even with the feature built the value would have to be re-derived rather than carried across.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer again: a SECOND pull over the same unchanged buffer returns nsv1061577 first again, i.e. the per-source memo cache is hit rather than the database re-queried
rationale: The row's distinct content is idempotency across a warm memo — upstream's own comment at perl/AnnotationSource_Database_StructuralVariation.t:133 says `do it again to get them from memory`. The memo is `$self->cache` in get_features_by_regions_uncached (StructuralVariation.pm:113), a per-source structure that only exists because each miss costs a SQL round trip. vepyr has neither the query to avoid nor the memo to hit: the absent feature is the database fetch itself, so the caching layered over it cannot be observed either.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer on empty buffer: after ib->next() advances past the data, the pull returns an empty list rather than the previous buffer's 750 features
rationale: The exhaustion case, and the sharp end of n=17: the memo that made the second pull cheap must not make an empty buffer look populated. It is a real failure mode of exactly this design — a per-source cache keyed by region rather than by buffer would return stale rows here — which is why it earns its own row. vepyr has no per-source SV memo and no SV pull, so there is neither a stale answer to guard against nor an empty one to assert.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer: the first buffered variant ends up carrying exactly nine overlapping known SVs, keyed by dbVar accession — nsv1055407, nsv1061577, nsv1189327, nsv531521, nsv544385, nsv544386, nsv544410, nsv916276 and nsv996057, each mapped to 1
rationale: The end-to-end payload row, and the only one that pins the shape of the annotation VEP hands the user: a set keyed by accession, so an SV overlapping twice contributes one key, not two. annotate_InputBuffer (StructuralVariation.pm:83-92) walks the fetched SVs and, for each, every buffered variant returned by get_overlapping_vfs, writing `$vf->{overlapping_svs}->{$svf->variation_name} = 1`. Both halves are absent from vepyr: the fetched SVs (n=13, n=15) and the interval join that attaches them. Its structural table is joined against transcripts to produce SO consequence terms (annotate_provider.rs:7341-7348), never against input variants to produce a colocated-SV list, and there is no CSQ column that could carry one.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer count annotated: 132 of the buffer's variants come back with an overlapping_svs key, i.e. the annotation reaches a defined fraction of the buffer rather than only the variant n=19 inspects
rationale: A whole-buffer census, and a distinct property from n=19: it catches an overlap test that works for one variant and silently misses the rest, which a single-variant assertion cannot. vepyr emits no per-variant SV overlap to count — there is no CSQ field for it (`grep -rniI 'SV_OVERLAP' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `motif` -> 417) — so the count has no channel, not merely no value. The same 132 appears at ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=17 for a different annotation, which is a fact about the shared test VCF and not evidence that the two rows share a property.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the database transcript annotation-source module loads
rationale: The file's only top-level assertion, and a module-load probe: it asserts Perl's `require` found AnnotationSource/Database/Transcript.pm, compiled it and ran its import. docs/ledger-contract.md ruling R2 makes that not-applicable unconditionally — no Rust design performs a module load at runtime that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart whatever the class denotes. The absence the class names stays in the denominator through the eighty-nine rows that exercise the source rather than load it.

desc: DATABASE TESTS: Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config loads inside the database SKIP block, so a config can be built from the live-DB credentials
rationale: A module-load probe on VEP's config class. Not-applicable under ruling R2 for the same reason as n=1, and R2 is explicit that position inside a SKIP block does not change the answer: the subject is Perl's loader, not the database feature the block guards. The 28 classified `use_ok Config`-style rows already in the corpus read it the same way.

desc: get new config object: Config->new accepts the live-DB credential hash together with database => 1, offline => 0, species => homo_vepiens, everything => 1 and xref_refseq => 1
rationale: A constructor probe, decided by denotation under docs/ledger-contract.md's ok($obj) ruling: the configuration the line asserts is accepted cannot be expressed in vepyr. `database => 1` with `offline => 0` selects the MySQL backend — `grep -rniI '"database"' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `options_json` -> 95, the probe ledger/Config.ledger.toml n=19 and n=30 already record. `xref_refseq` is likewise absent from the pin's 31-key option vocabulary (`grep -oh 'parse("[a-z_0-9]*")' src/*.rs | sort -u | wc -l` -> 31, and the list contains all_refseq but neither refseq nor xref_refseq). `everything` is the one key vepyr does have (vcf_sink.rs:383), which is why the row is classified on the two that it does not.

desc: new is defined: AnnotationSource::Database::Transcript->new({config}) returns a defined source, built from nothing but the database-mode config
rationale: The load-bearing constructor probe of the file, and the row that accounts for the construction n=5 reads back. Decided by denotation under the ok($obj) ruling: the class denotes a transcript source backed by an Ensembl core database and reached through the adaptor factory. Neither half exists at the pin — `grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 and `grep -rniI 'mysql' src/` -> 0, against the positive control `parquet` -> 913. vepyr's transcripts come from parquet written ahead of time and reached through `TranscriptTableProvider`; there is no source object constructible from credentials. ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=43-50 classify the sibling database block the same way.

desc: check class: ref($as) reads back exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::Database::Transcript for the object n=4 just constructed
rationale: A blessing readback two lines after its constructor, and ruling R1 takes it on the first bullet: the construction already carries its own row at n=4, so all this line adds is Perl object identity, which is on docs/ledger-contract.md's explicit not-applicable list. R1's worked case states the counterfactual — Parser_SPDI n=4 and Parser_CAID n=4 stay no-feature only because neither file contains an `ok($p = ...->new)` row, and had either opened with a constructor probe the readback would have been not-applicable. Counting it again here would count n=4's absence twice, the double-counting R2 rules out one paragraph later.

desc: valid_chromosomes: the source reports [21, LRG_485] — the chromosome names it will accept, derived from the core database's seq_region table rather than from any file
rationale: The naive claim, that vepyr has no valid-chromosome list, is false and is not made here: `chromosomes()` returns exactly that list in vepyr, extracted from discovered cache file paths (bio-format-ensembl-cache discovery.rs:244-259), and ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=23 already claims it as part of an analog-port (tests/port_cache_dir.rs::info_txt_facts_surface_in_the_provider_schema). What this row adds is the ORIGIN: a database source builds the list by querying the core schema through the adaptor layer, which vepyr has no client for (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `parquet` -> 913). The two lists even differ by fixture — the database returns [21, LRG_485] where the cache directory returns [21, 22, LRG_485] — so this is not n=23 restated.

desc: chr lengths: the source reports each accepted chromosome's full length — 21 => 46709983 and LRG_485 => 9429 — so coordinates can be range-checked before any fetch
rationale: Sequence lengths are what let VEP reject an out-of-range coordinate and clamp a fetch window to the end of a chromosome (the `$e = $slice->length if $e > $slice->length` guard the database sources share). vepyr keeps no such number: `grep -rniI 'chr_lengths' src/`, `... 'chr_length' src/` and `... 'contig_len' src/` -> 0 lines each at dfbf 391f94bd, and `seq_region` -> 4 lines, none of them a length; the positive control is `chromosomes()` in the cache reader (discovery.rs:244-259), which yields names only. Nothing downstream needs one, because a parquet scan is bounded by the data it finds rather than by a declared extent. The missing feature is the seq-region metadata a database source reads at startup.

desc: info: the source reports the five provenance facts it will stamp on its output — genebuild 2014-07, gencode GENCODE 24, assembly GRCh38.p5, polyphen 2.2.2, sift sift5.2.2 — read from the core and variation databases
rationale: As with n=6, the tempting claim that vepyr keeps none of this is wrong. Four of these five survive in vepyr as provenance columns: `SourceDescriptor::from_info_source` (bio-format-ensembl-cache 0d9730c8 info.rs:26-45) turns every `source_<name>` info.txt line into a `source_<name>` Arrow column on every entity schema (schema.rs:440-455), and ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=24 enumerates thirteen such lines including sift, polyphen, gencode and genebuild; `assembly` is a `CacheInfo` field in its own right (info.rs:48) claimed at CacheDir n=23. The absent thing is the boundary: a database source assembles the hash from live meta-table queries (Transcript.pm's `info`), and vepyr has no adaptor to query. No-feature about the database origin, and not a second claim on n=23 or n=24.

desc: check_sift_polyphen - not specified: with neither --sift nor --polyphen requested the availability check passes trivially
rationale: The baseline arm of a three-row family (n=9, n=10, n=11) whose subject is a capability negotiation against a live database: VEP asks the variation database whether protein-function prediction data exists for this species and refuses, or silently disables, accordingly. vepyr negotiates nothing. It has SIFT and PolyPhen — `grep -rniI 'sift' src/` -> 409 and `... 'polyphen' src/` -> 126, including a whole `sift_decode` module — but reads them as cache columns, and neither `sift` nor `polyphen` is a request option: the pin's option vocabulary is closed at 31 keys (`grep -oh 'parse("[a-z_0-9]*")' src/*.rs | sort -u | wc -l` -> 31) and contains neither. With no request and no server, there is nothing to check.

desc: check_sift_polyphen - SIFT: with sift set on the source the check still passes, because the homo_vepiens variation database does carry SIFT data
rationale: The positive arm of n=9 for SIFT specifically, and it earns its own row because it is the arm that actually consults the database: the trivial pass of n=9 would survive a broken lookup, this one would not. vepyr performs no lookup — SIFT availability is decided by whether the cache's translation entity carries the column, fixed when the cache was built rather than negotiated at run time — and `sift` is not among the 31 option keys, so the flag this row sets has no counterpart to set.

desc: check_sift_polyphen - PolyPhen: with polyphen set on the source the check likewise passes against the homo_vepiens variation database
rationale: The PolyPhen half of n=10, and not a duplicate: SIFT and PolyPhen are stored and versioned separately in the variation schema (n=8 reports two different version strings for them), so a species can have one and not the other — which is exactly what n=97 exercises for mus_muscuvep. vepyr has PolyPhen (`grep -rniI 'polyphen' src/` -> 126) but as cache data, with no per-species availability question to ask and no `polyphen` option key to ask it about.

desc: get transcript adaptor: the test database hands back a Bio::EnsEMBL::DBSQL::TranscriptAdaptor, the object every prefetch row below is driven through
rationale: The adaptor layer itself, asserted directly rather than through the source — this is the object n=13 through n=41 all depend on. vepyr has no adaptor factory and no DBSQL layer: `grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 and `grep -rniI 'adaptor' src/` -> exactly 1 line, a prose comment at annotate_provider.rs:2478, against the positive control `parquet` -> 913. ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=44 classifies the identical assertion for the Slice adaptor as no-feature; this is the transcript half of the same absence.

desc: get transcript: fetch_by_stable_id('ENST00000307301') on that adaptor returns a fully-formed Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript
rationale: A blessing probe whose subject is the absent thing, which is the distinction R2's corollary draws: what it pins is that a stable id resolves, through a SQL query, to a lazily-loaded Ensembl Transcript object carrying its exons, translation and attributes. vepyr's transcripts are `TranscriptFeature` values decoded from a parquet row group, with no stable-id-to-object resolver and no database to resolve against (n=12's measurement). The object model is not what is missing — vepyr has transcripts — the fetch is.

desc: prefetch_transcript_ids (gene arm): prefetch_gene_ids returns true for ENST00000307301, i.e. the gene-level cross-reference queries ran
rationale: The gate row for n=15, n=16 and n=17: `prefetch_gene_ids` (Transcript.pm) issues the xref queries that attach a gene symbol, its source and its HGNC id to the transcript before annotation, so that the per-variant path never touches the database. vepyr has no prefetch phase at all — the equivalent values are columns already present in the transcript parquet, read in the same scan as the coordinates — so there is no operation whose success this row could report. The absent feature is database-backed cross-reference resolution.

desc: prefetch_transcript_ids - gene symbol: after the gene prefetch the transcript carries _gene_symbol = MRPL39
rationale: The value itself is not what vepyr lacks: the symbol reaches the user as the `SYMBOL` CSQ field and `grep -rniI 'gene_symbol' src/` -> 50 at dfbf 391f94bd. What this row pins is where it came from — an xref join executed at prefetch time against the core database — and that join has no counterpart, the symbol being a column of the transcript cache written when the cache was built (n=12's measurement of the missing adaptor layer). Classified on the origin, so that the cache-mode statement of the same field is not counted twice.

desc: prefetch_transcript_ids - gene symbol source: the transcript also carries _gene_symbol_source = HGNC, i.e. which nomenclature authority the symbol of n=15 came from
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=15: a symbol without its authority is ambiguous, and VEP emits the two as separate CSQ fields precisely because a gene can be named by HGNC, by Clone_based_ensembl_gene or by others. vepyr emits `SYMBOL_SOURCE` too, from a cache column, so again the absence is the prefetch query rather than the datum — the same missing adaptor layer measured at n=12.

desc: prefetch_transcript_ids - gene HGNC ID: the third product of the gene prefetch is _gene_hgnc_id = HGNC:14027, the stable accession behind the symbol
rationale: The third and most stable of the three gene-level identifiers, and the one downstream tools key on when a symbol is renamed. vepyr carries it — `grep -rniI 'hgnc' src/` -> 194 and `HGNC_ID` is one of the 80 fields of `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (golden_benchmark.rs:556) — as a transcript-cache column. Absent is the prefetch that fills it from the core database's xref tables, for the reason measured at n=12.

desc: prefetch_transcript_ids: the transcript-level cross-reference prefetch returns true for ENST00000307301
rationale: The gate row for n=19 and n=20, and a different query set from n=14's: gene-level xrefs come from the gene the transcript belongs to, transcript-level ones from the transcript itself, so the two prefetches can fail independently. Neither exists in vepyr, which has no prefetch phase and no database to prefetch from (n=12). The missing feature is the same: database-backed cross-reference resolution.

desc: prefetch_transcript_ids - CCDS: the transcript-level prefetch attaches _ccds = CCDS33522.1, the Consensus CDS accession
rationale: vepyr reports CCDS as a CSQ field and carries it in the transcript cache (`grep -rniI 'ccds' src/` -> 43 at dfbf 391f94bd), so the datum is present; what this row pins is that it is resolved by an xref query at prefetch time, against a database vepyr cannot reach (n=12). Classified on the origin, which is also why it does not restate whatever cache-mode row covers the field.

desc: prefetch_transcript_ids - RefSeq: with xref_refseq set the same prefetch attaches _refseq = NM_080794.3, the RefSeq transcript this Ensembl transcript is cross-referenced to
rationale: Two absences stack. The datum has a vepyr counterpart in the RefSeq-flavoured cache (`refseq` -> 946 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, and `CacheSource::Refseq`, cache_source.rs:87), but the request flag does not: `xref_refseq` is absent from the pin's closed 31-key option vocabulary, which contains `all_refseq` and neither `refseq` nor `xref_refseq`. And the resolution route — an xref query at prefetch time — is the missing adaptor layer of n=12. Either alone makes the row no-feature.

desc: prefetch_translation_ids: the translation-level cross-reference prefetch returns true for ENST00000307301's translation
rationale: The third prefetch family and the gate row for n=22, n=23 and n=24. It takes the translation as a second argument, so it can only run for coding transcripts, and its queries hit the protein xref tables rather than the transcript ones. vepyr has no prefetch phase and no database (n=12); protein-level identifiers are transcript-cache columns filled at build time.

desc: prefetch_translation_ids - SWISSPROT: the translation prefetch attaches _swissprot = Q9NYK5
rationale: vepyr emits `SWISSPROT` as one of the 80 `--everything` CSQ fields and carries it in the cache (`grep -rniI 'swissprot' src/` -> 29 at dfbf 391f94bd), so the datum is present. The row is about the prefetch query that fills it from the core database's protein xrefs, which has no counterpart for the reason measured at n=12.

desc: prefetch_translation_ids - UniParc: the same prefetch attaches _uniparc = UPI00001AEAC0, the sequence-identity accession
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=22: UniParc keys on the protein sequence itself while SwissProt keys on the curated entry, so the two come from different xref sets and one can be present without the other. vepyr carries UniParc as a cache column (`grep -rniI 'uniparc' src/` -> 26) and emits it in CSQ; absent is the prefetch query, per n=12.

desc: prefetch_translation_ids - Ensembl protein: the third product is _protein = ENSP00000305682, the Ensembl protein stable id
rationale: The internal identifier of the three, and the one that needs no xref table at all — it is read off the translation object the adaptor already returned, which is why it is asserted alongside the two external accessions rather than separately. vepyr emits it as the `ENSP` CSQ field from a cache column. What is absent is the translation object and the adaptor that produced it (n=12, n=13).

desc: prefetch_translation_data: the heavyweight translation prefetch returns true, having loaded the peptide sequence, the protein features and the prediction matrices in one pass
rationale: The gate row for n=26 through n=30, and the most expensive operation in the file: it pulls the translated sequence, every protein domain and the SIFT/PolyPhen matrices out of two databases and hangs them on the transcript's `_variation_effect_feature_cache`. vepyr has no such per-transcript side-cache and no prefetch phase; the same data, where it exists, is read column-wise from parquet during the annotation scan. Absent operation, so no-feature rather than a missing export.

desc: prefetch_translation_data - peptide: the prefetched cache holds the full 349-residue MRPL39 peptide, MEALAMGSRALRLWLVAP... compared character for character
rationale: The peptide is what every amino-acid-level consequence is computed against, so the row is a correctness anchor rather than a plumbing check: a wrong translation start or an unapplied selenocysteine edit would show here and nowhere else in this file. vepyr does translate — `translateable_seq` -> 134 lines at dfbf 391f94bd — but from cached CDS sequence, and the row's subject is the database prefetch that produced this string (n=25). No adaptor, no fetch, no row to port.

desc: prefetch_translation_data - protein features: the prefetched cache holds exactly seven Bio::EnsEMBL::ProteinFeature objects sorted by start — PTHR11451 38-324 (hmmpanther), 3.10.20.30 85-132 (Gene3D), SSF81271 86-130 and SSF55186 136-313 (Superfamily), 1tkeA02 138-225 and 1tkeA03 226-267 (Gene3D), seg 329-341 (Low complexity) — each with its analysis display label
rationale: The domain set behind the `DOMAINS` CSQ field, asserted as blessed objects with their analysis labels, so the row covers both the fetch and the analysis-name join. vepyr does carry protein features: `protein_features` is a transcript-cache column read at annotate_provider.rs:4201 and :4241-4271, and the pin's own tests use labels of the same family (annotate_provider.rs:15584 constructs `Gene3D db`). The row is classified on the boundary — a prefetch against the core database's protein_feature and analysis tables (n=25) — not on the datum, and on the object shape, which a typed decode cannot exhibit.

desc: prefetch_translation_data - sift matrix: with sift set, the prefetched cache holds a Bio::EnsEMBL::Variation::ProteinFunctionPredictionMatrix under protein_function_predictions->{sift}
rationale: Not the SIFT score but the matrix object: VEP fetches one compressed per-protein matrix covering every possible substitution, so a per-variant score is a lookup rather than a query. vepyr has no such object — `grep -rniI 'ProteinFunctionPrediction' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, against the positive control `sift` -> 409 — because it stores the same information as decoded per-position cache data (`sift_decode`). The row's subject, the prefetched matrix hanging off the transcript, is the absent thing.

desc: prefetch_translation_data - polyphen_humvar matrix: the same prefetch also holds a prediction matrix under polyphen_humvar
rationale: The HumVar-trained PolyPhen matrix, keyed separately from SIFT because it is fetched and versioned separately. Same absence and same measurement as n=28: `ProteinFunctionPrediction` -> 0 at the pin against `polyphen` -> 126, vepyr keeping predictions as cache columns rather than as fetched matrix objects.

desc: prefetch_translation_data - polyphen_humdiv matrix: a THIRD matrix is held under polyphen_humdiv, so both PolyPhen training sets are prefetched even though VEP reports only one by default
rationale: The row that makes n=29 more than a duplicate: HumDiv and HumVar are different models over the same protein, and the prefetch loads both, which is a real cost decision worth pinning. vepyr has one PolyPhen value per substitution and no notion of a second training set to choose between, and no matrix object at all (`ProteinFunctionPrediction` -> 0). Absent feature, not an unnameable item.

desc: prefetch_transcript_data: the structural prefetch returns true, having loaded introns, sorted exons, the coordinate mapper, the codon table, both UTRs and the translateable sequence onto ENST00000307301
rationale: The gate row for n=32 through n=38, and the last of the four prefetch families. Everything it loads is derived from the transcript's exons and translation, so in vepyr it is either computed on the fly during consequence calling or stored as cache columns — there is no phase in which a transcript is decorated before annotation begins. The prefetch is the absent operation; the individual products are handled row by row below.

desc: prefetch_transcript_data - introns: the prefetched cache's introns list holds Bio::EnsEMBL::Intron objects, i.e. the gaps were materialised as first-class features rather than left implicit between exons
rationale: A blessing probe whose subject is the absent prefetch (n=31). The property has substance — VEP needs intron objects because splice-region consequences are computed against intron boundaries — and vepyr computes the same consequences from exon coordinates directly, with no intron type to bless. So this is not merely a Perl object-identity line: what it pins is a materialisation step that vepyr's design does not have and a database fetch it cannot make (n=12).

desc: prefetch_transcript_data - sorted_exons 1: the prefetched cache's sorted_exons list holds Bio::EnsEMBL::Exon objects
rationale: The exon half of n=32, and the input to the mapper of n=35: VEP sorts the exons once at prefetch time so that every later cDNA coordinate conversion is a binary search rather than a re-sort. vepyr holds exon coordinates as cache columns and orders them when it builds its cDNA mapper segments (transcript_consequence.rs:244 documents them as TranscriptMapper exon-to-cDNA segments in genomic order), so the ordering exists but the prefetched blessed list does not, and neither does the fetch that would produce it (n=12, n=31).

desc: prefetch_transcript_data - sorted_exons 2: the first entry of the sorted exon list is ENSE00003528074, so the sort is by genomic start and the exons carry their stable ids
rationale: Two claims in one line, and the second is why it is not n=33 restated: the list is ordered, and the objects in it are identified. vepyr carries exon stable ids — they reach the user as the `EXON` CSQ field, and exons are their own cache entity — but as decoded columns rather than as a prefetched blessed list, and the fetch that would produce this one needs the adaptor layer measured at n=12 (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `parquet` -> 913).

desc: prefetch_transcript_data - mapper: the prefetched cache holds a Bio::EnsEMBL::TranscriptMapper, the object that converts genomic coordinates to cDNA, CDS and peptide positions
rationale: The single most reused product of the prefetch: every cDNA_position, CDS_position and Protein_position in the output comes out of this object, which is why VEP builds it once per transcript and caches it. vepyr computes the same conversions, and its own source says so — `transcript_consequence.rs:244` documents its segment list as TranscriptMapper exon-to-cDNA segments in genomic order, and `:1844-1852` reproduces VEP's frameshift-intron rule by citation. So the mapping is present; what is absent is a mapper OBJECT hung on a prefetched transcript by a database source, and the fetch behind it (n=12, n=31). Classified on that boundary rather than on the arithmetic.

desc: prefetch_transcript_data - codon_table: the prefetched cache records codon table 1, the standard genetic code, read from the transcript's codon_table attribute
rationale: The row pins that the translation table is a per-transcript fact fetched from the database, not a constant — which is what lets VEP translate a mitochondrial transcript with table 2 in the same run. vepyr has no such per-transcript value: `grep -rniI 'codon_table' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control `codon` -> 1009, and the mitochondrial case is handled by chromosome name instead (`is_mitochondrial_chrom`, annotate_provider.rs:7484, consulted at :7497). So the mechanism differs and the attribute fetch that this row asserts has no counterpart; the absent feature is the per-transcript codon-table attribute, on top of the absent fetch.

desc: prefetch_transcript_data - five_prime_utr: the prefetched cache holds the 42-base 5' UTR sequence AGGGCGGAGAAGGACTTGCGCGCGACGGTTCTCACCGCTGCT as a sequence object
rationale: NOT `no-feature`: the earlier reading took the MECHANISM for the PROPERTY. What the `is()` pins down is a literal 42-base sequence for ENST00000307301, and vepyr holds exactly that string, for exactly that transcript, in the committed fixture -- measured, not inferred: `tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/transcript/chr21.parquet` column `five_prime_utr_seq` on the ENST00000307301 row is byte-equal to Perl's literal. Channel, named: Perl reads `$tr->{_variation_effect_feature_cache}->{five_prime_utr}`, the slot `prefetch_transcript_data` fills; vepyr's counterpart is the `pub` field `TranscriptFeature.five_prime_utr_seq` (transcript_consequence.rs:283 @ dfbf 391f94bd), whose doc comment names the Perl slot verbatim -- `Raw 5' UTR cached on the VEP transcript object` -- and which is loaded from that parquet column. The test reads the column through `parquet_cache::scan::read_context_parquet`, the same public reader every other cache-transcript port here uses. What genuinely does not cross is only the FILLING of the slot -- vepyr fills it from a cache, not from a Bio::EnsEMBL::DBSQL adaptor -- and that absence is already counted by n=31 (the prefetch) and n=12 (the adaptor), which stay `no-feature`. Two controls in the test: 124 of the shard's 228 transcripts carry a non-empty `five_prime_utr_seq`, so the column is a real per-transcript value rather than a constant; and ENST00000352957, which starts at the same coordinate 25585656 on the same strand, carries a different, 6-base 5' UTR, so a read keyed on the locus rather than on the stable id would fail.

desc: prefetch_transcript_data - three_prime_utr: the prefetched cache likewise holds the 95-base 3' UTR sequence, CTGAAGATCAAAGT...AAATATAA
rationale: The 3' half of n=37, same channel (`TranscriptFeature.three_prime_utr_seq`, transcript_consequence.rs:285, from the `three_prime_utr_seq` column) and same verdict: the committed shard's value for ENST00000307301 is byte-equal to Perl's literal. Not a duplicate of n=37 -- the two UTRs are cut from opposite ends of a MINUS-strand transcript (`strand = -1`, 25585656-25607517 in the shard), which is exactly the case where an implementation that forgot to reverse-complement produces a plausible wrong answer at one end and a correct one at the other. Correction carried in the same PR as the port: this desc read `94-base` for a sequence that is 95 bases long; counted from the vendored Perl literal at perl/AnnotationSource_Database_Transcript.t:245 and re-counted off the parquet value, both give 95, and the test asserts the length so the number cannot drift again. Same two controls as n=37: 125 of 228 transcripts carry a non-empty `three_prime_utr_seq`, and the sibling ENST00000352957 carries a different, 51-base one.

desc: same utr - prefetch_transcript_data: running the structural prefetch on a SECOND transcript, ENST00000352957, also succeeds
rationale: The setup row for n=40 and a real assertion in its own right: it shows the prefetch is re-entrant across transcripts sharing a locus, where a naive implementation could collide on a shared cache key. vepyr has no prefetch phase to re-enter (n=31) and no per-transcript side-cache, so there is neither a second run nor a collision to rule out. Absent operation, so no-feature rather than a missing export.

desc: same utr - same ref: the two transcripts' five_prime_utr entries are the SAME object, not merely equal strings — the prefetch shares one sequence between transcripts whose UTRs coincide
rationale: STAYS `no-feature`, but the reason is replaced: the old one is FALSIFIED BY n=37 AND n=38 IN THIS SAME FILE. It said `vepyr never materialises a UTR sequence object per transcript at all (n=37)`. It does -- `TranscriptFeature.five_prime_utr_seq` and `.three_prime_utr_seq` are `pub` fields (transcript_consequence.rs:283, :285 @ dfbf 391f94bd) carrying the sequence per transcript, and n=37/n=38 now assert the exact Perl strings against them. What is genuinely absent is not the MATERIALISATION but the SHARING. `_fetch_utr` (AnnotationSource/Database/Transcript.pm:393-414) keys a 50-entry LRU on `md5_hex($this_utr->seq)` (:403) in `$self->{_utr_cache}` (:406) and hands the SAME `Bio::Seq` to every transcript whose UTR sequence matches; this line compares those references with `eq`, so what it pins is the interning, not the value. vepyr stores each transcript`s UTR as an owned `Option<String>` read from that transcript`s own parquet row: there is no interning step, no shared handle, and no identity for a test to compare -- two transcripts with equal UTRs simply carry two equal Strings. The optimisation exists because each Perl fetch costs a database round trip and a Bio::Seq allocation; a column read has neither cost, so the mechanism was never built. That missing capability belongs to the absent database prefetch, which is why the row keeps `database-mode` and stays `no-feature` rather than becoming not-applicable: its subject IS the absent thing.

desc: prefetch_transcript_data - translateable_seq: the prefetched cache holds the full 1050-base coding sequence, ATGGAGGCGCTGGCC...GAGTAA, compared character for character
rationale: The CDS the peptide of n=26 is translated from, and the last product of the structural prefetch. Getting it right means having stitched the coding exons in the correct order, trimmed both UTRs and applied the transcript's strand — so this single string is the strongest correctness anchor in the prefetch family. vepyr builds a translateable sequence too (`grep -rniI 'translateable_seq' src/` -> 134 at dfbf 391f94bd), from cached exon coordinates and reference FASTA rather than from a database fetch. Classified on the boundary (n=31, n=12), not on the sequence.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached ref 1: the single-region database fetch for [21, 511] returns an arrayref
rationale: A container-kind probe whose subject IS the absent thing, which is the distinction R2's corollary draws: `get_features_by_regions_uncached` issues the core-database query for one 50 kb region and blesses the rows into Transcript objects (AnnotationSource/Database/Transcript.pm:204-218 @ release/116.0 builds the window from `$self->{cache_region_size}`). vepyr has no adaptor to query (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0, positive control `parquet` -> 913), so there is no call whose return shape could be checked. Contrast ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=37, where the same probe is not-applicable because the pull it describes is a real cache-mode operation.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached count: exactly 6 transcripts overlap the single 50 kb region [21, 511] under the default Ensembl configuration
rationale: A census over one region, and the baseline the RefSeq run of n=61 is compared against — 6 Ensembl transcripts against 8 RefSeq ones over the identical window, which is what makes the pair meaningful. It would catch a fetch window off by a base or a filter that dropped a transcript. vepyr issues no such query, and 6 is a property of the homo_vepiens MultiTestDB fixture rather than of the algorithm, so the number could not be carried across even if the source were built.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached ref 2: the first element of the single-region fetch is a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript
rationale: A blessing probe of the absent thing: the elements are lazily-loaded Ensembl Transcript objects, each able to fetch its own exons and translation on demand — the property that makes the prefetch rows above necessary in the first place. vepyr decodes `TranscriptFeature` values from a parquet row group, a typed struct whose class cannot vary at runtime, and there is no database fetch to produce anything else (n=42).

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached stable_id: the first transcript of the single-region fetch is ENST00000456917
rationale: Identity rather than shape: the row pins which transcript the query returns first, so it catches an ORDER BY change or a window shifted by one region as the count of n=43 alone would not. It is also the value n=48 asserts the memo replays unchanged. vepyr carries transcript stable ids everywhere (`grep -rniI 'stable_id' src/` -> 157 at dfbf 391f94bd) but reads them from parquet; there is no query here whose ordering could be asserted.

desc: get_features_by_regions_cached ref 1: after the uncached fetch, the CACHED accessor for the same region [21, 511] returns an arrayref without going back to the database
rationale: The first of three rows about the per-source region memo, which exists because each miss costs a SQL round trip — upstream's own comment at perl/AnnotationSource_Database_Transcript.t:266 says `now we should be able to retrieve the same from memory`. vepyr has no per-source transcript memo of this kind and no query to avoid; its only related machinery is `prune_persisted_buffer_transcripts` (annotate_provider.rs:11523), a private free fn that evicts persisted transcripts between buffers rather than serving a cached region read. So the row's subject, the cached arm of a database fetch, has no counterpart to call.

desc: get_features_by_regions_cached ref 2: the memo replays a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript first, i.e. the cached path preserves the uncached path's class
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=44: the point is agreement between two paths, so a memo that stored a flattened or re-blessed copy would fail here while the uncached assertions still passed. Both paths are absent from vepyr for the reasons measured at n=42 and n=46, and there is no second path whose agreement with a first could be asserted.

desc: get_features_by_regions_cached stable_id: the memo replays ENST00000456917 first, identical to the uncached fetch of n=45
rationale: The identity half of n=47 and the strongest statement of the memo's contract: the cached path must return the same transcripts, in the same order, as the database path it replaces. vepyr has neither path (n=42, n=46), so there is nothing to compare; the absent feature is the database-backed transcript source together with the per-region memo layered over it.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached - merged sets _source_cache: with the source's merged flag on, every fetched transcript is stamped _source_cache = 'Ensembl', so a merged run can tell which of the two catalogues each transcript came from
rationale: The datum survives in vepyr and the flag does not, which is exactly the split this file keeps producing. `source_cache` is a transcript-cache column, read at annotate_provider.rs:3716 and :3800-3944 and consumed at :2515 (`tx.source_cache.as_deref().or(tx.source.as_deref())`) to fill the `SOURCE` CSQ field; the merged flavour itself is real, as `CacheSourceType::Merged` (cache_source.rs:16, parsed at :87). But the flavour is read from cache schema metadata (`bio.vep.cache_source_type`, cache_source.rs:10), never from a request flag — `merged` is absent from the pin's closed 31-key option vocabulary — and the stamping this row asserts happens during a database fetch vepyr cannot make (n=42). Absent boundary, present datum.

desc: clean_cache: after clean_cache() the source's entire region memo is the empty hash, so memory does not grow without bound as the input walks the genome
rationale: The lifecycle end of n=46-48, and the row where a near-analogue has to be refused explicitly. vepyr does mirror VEP's clean_cache — `prune_persisted_buffer_transcripts` (annotate_provider.rs:11523) carries a doc comment citing `AnnotationSource::clean_cache()` by URL — but it prunes persisted transcripts against the still-active cache regions rather than emptying a source's own memo, and it is a private free fn with no `pub`. This row's subject is a database source's `cache` hash going empty, and that source does not exist (n=42). ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=30 classifies the identical assertion for the cache source as no-feature on the same reasoning.

desc: count transcripts of biotype 'artifact' in test database: the core test database really does contain 3 artifact-biotype transcripts, so the discard of n=52 is not passing vacuously
rationale: A precondition assertion, and load-bearing: without it n=52's `0 artifact transcripts survived` would be satisfied by a database that never had any. It is made through the adaptor's own `count_all_by_biotype`, which is the point — vepyr can neither count by biotype across a whole catalogue nor reach one: `grep -rniI 'count_all_by_biotype' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control `biotype` -> 122, and there is no adaptor at all (n=12). The absent feature is the database-wide query, not the biotype concept.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached - discard transcripts of biotype 'artifact': fetching region [21, 137], which spans the 3 artifact transcripts of n=51, yields none of them
rationale: One of the two content filters this source applies on the way out of the database, and the reason n=51 exists. vepyr applies no such filter: `grep -rniI 'artifact' src/` -> 3 lines at dfbf 391f94bd and none is a biotype filter — build.rs:854 and parquet_cache/write.rs:66 are prose about build artifacts, transcript_consequence.rs:278 is about poly-A tails — against the positive control `biotype` -> 122. The biotype filtering vepyr does have is different and flag-driven (`gencode_basic`, vcf_sink.rs:426, and `exclude_predicted`, annotate_provider.rs:1431-1445), so naming it here would be a false analogue. Absent feature: the unconditional artifact discard, on top of the absent fetch.

desc: count readthrough transcripts in test database: the core test database really does contain 3 transcripts carrying the readthrough_tra attribute, so the discard of n=54 is not passing vacuously
rationale: The readthrough twin of n=51, and it reaches the fact a different way: `$ta->fetch_all()` over the whole database followed by `get_all_Attributes('readthrough_tra')` per transcript. Both halves are absent from vepyr — no adaptor to fetch_all from (n=12) and no transcript attribute model: `grep -rniI 'readthrough' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control `biotype` -> 122. The absent feature is the attribute layer, not just the query.

desc: get_features_by_regions_uncached - discard readthrough transcripts: fetching region [21, 787], which spans the 3 readthrough transcripts of n=53, yields none of them
rationale: The second content filter, and not a duplicate of n=52: artifact is a biotype while readthrough is an attribute, so they are stored differently, filtered by different code and can regress independently. vepyr has neither concept — `readthrough` -> 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `biotype` -> 122 — and no fetch to filter (n=42). Absent feature: the unconditional readthrough discard.

desc: clean_cache: the region memo is emptied a second time, after the filter tests, so the RefSeq block that follows starts from a cold source
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=50: the first call empties a memo filled by the Ensembl-flavoured fetches, this one empties a memo filled by the filter-test fetches of n=52 and n=54, and it is what makes the RefSeq counts of n=61 and n=63 attributable to the RefSeq configuration rather than to leftovers. The absence is the same as n=50's — a source-owned memo vepyr does not have, and a database source it cannot construct — and the test-isolation property has no counterpart because there is no state to isolate.

desc: refseq - get new config object: a second Config is accepted with refseq => 1 replacing the everything/xref_refseq pair, selecting the otherfeatures database instead of core
rationale: A constructor probe decided by denotation under docs/ledger-contract.md's ok($obj) ruling, and both of its halves are absent. `database => 1` is the measurement of n=3. `refseq => 1` is the RefSeq FLAVOUR SELECTOR, and vepyr does not have it as a request: the pin's option vocabulary is closed at 31 keys (`grep -oh 'parse("[a-z_0-9]*")' src/*.rs | sort -u | wc -l` -> 31) and contains `all_refseq` but neither `refseq` nor `xref_refseq`. vepyr does support RefSeq caches — `CacheSourceType::RefSeq` (cache_source.rs:17) — but the flavour comes from cache schema metadata, not from a flag, so what this line asserts is accepted cannot be expressed.

desc: refseq - get transcript adaptor: the OTHERFEATURES database, not core, hands back the TranscriptAdaptor for the RefSeq block
rationale: Not n=12 repeated: the point is which database the adaptor comes from. VEP keeps RefSeq transcripts in a separate `otherfeatures` schema alongside core, and switching flavour means switching database, which is the whole mechanism this block exercises. vepyr has no adaptor layer and no schema to switch between (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `parquet` -> 913); its RefSeq flavour is a different cache directory, resolved from schema metadata rather than from a second connection.

desc: refseq - get transcript: fetch_by_stable_id('NM_201413.2') against otherfeatures returns a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript — a RefSeq accession resolving through the same object model as an ENST
rationale: A blessing probe whose subject is the absent fetch, and its content is that both catalogues share one object model: a RefSeq transcript is a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript, so every downstream consequence path is flavour-agnostic. vepyr reaches the same end differently — one `TranscriptFeature` type for all three cache flavours (cache_source.rs:13-18) — but has no stable-id resolver and no database to resolve against (n=57, n=12).

desc: refseq - prefetch_transcript_ids - gene symbol: after the gene and transcript prefetches run against otherfeatures, NM_201413.2 carries _gene_symbol = APP
rationale: The RefSeq counterpart of n=15, and it earns its own row because the xref route differs: in otherfeatures the symbol comes from the RefSeq annotation itself rather than from an Ensembl HGNC xref, so a prefetch correct for core can be wrong here. vepyr emits `SYMBOL` for RefSeq caches too, from a cache column, but runs no prefetch and reaches no database (n=14, n=12). Classified on the boundary.

desc: refseq - get_features_by_regions_uncached ref 1: the single-region fetch for [21, 511] against the RefSeq source returns an arrayref
rationale: The RefSeq arm of n=42, and its absence is measured the same way: no adaptor, hence no fetch whose return shape could be checked (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `parquet` -> 913). It is not redundant with n=42 because the source is configured against a different database (n=57), which is precisely what the RefSeq block is testing.

desc: refseq - get_features_by_regions_uncached count: 8 RefSeq transcripts overlap the same 50 kb region [21, 511] that yielded 6 Ensembl transcripts at n=43
rationale: The row that makes the flavour switch observable: same region, same code path, different catalogue and therefore a different count, so a source that silently kept querying core would fail here and nowhere else in the block. vepyr issues no query, and both numbers are properties of the homo_vepiens MultiTestDB fixtures rather than of any algorithm, so neither could be carried across even if the database source were built.

desc: refseq - get_features_by_regions_uncached ref 2: the first element of the RefSeq fetch is a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript, the same class the Ensembl fetch returns
rationale: The class-agreement claim across flavours, and the region-fetch counterpart of n=58: whichever database the source is pointed at, the objects it returns are indistinguishable by class, which is why the annotation path below needs no flavour switch. vepyr also uses one transcript type for all flavours, but the assertion is about the return of a database fetch it cannot make (n=60).

desc: refseq - get_features_by_regions_uncached stable_id: the first RefSeq transcript of region [21, 511] is NR_001458.3 — an NR_ non-coding accession, not the NM_ one the prefetch rows used
rationale: Identity rather than shape, and the RefSeq counterpart of n=45. That the first entry is an NR_ accession is itself informative: the fetch is ordered by position and does not privilege coding transcripts, so a filter that dropped non-coding RefSeq entries would show here. vepyr carries RefSeq accessions in its RefSeq-flavoured cache (`grep -rniI 'refseq' src/` -> 946 at dfbf 391f94bd) but reads them from parquet; there is no query whose ordering could be asserted.

desc: refseq - get_features_by_regions_cached ref 1: the RefSeq source's memo returns an arrayref for the same region without re-querying otherfeatures
rationale: The RefSeq arm of n=46: the per-region memo is a property of the source object, so it has to be shown to work for a source pointed at a second database as well. vepyr has no per-source memo and no query to avoid (n=46's measurement), and its nearest machinery, `prune_persisted_buffer_transcripts` (annotate_provider.rs:11523), is private and evicts rather than serves.

desc: refseq - get_features_by_regions_cached ref 2: the RefSeq memo replays a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript first, so the cached and uncached paths agree on class for this flavour too
rationale: The RefSeq arm of n=47, and the same reason it is not a duplicate: the claim is agreement between two paths, which a memo storing a re-shaped copy would break while every uncached assertion still passed. Neither path exists in vepyr (n=60, n=64).

desc: refseq - get_features_by_regions_cached stable_id: the RefSeq memo replays NR_001458.3 first, identical to the uncached fetch of n=63
rationale: The identity half of n=65 and the closing statement of the RefSeq memo contract: the cached path must return the same transcripts in the same order as the otherfeatures query it replaces. vepyr has neither the query nor the memo (n=60, n=64), so there is nothing to compare; the absent feature is the database-backed RefSeq source together with its per-region memo.

desc: TESTS WITH AN INPUT BUFFER: Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF loads, so the test VCF can be read into a buffer
rationale: A module-load probe on the VCF parser. Not-applicable under ruling R2, and here the class does not even denote something absent: vepyr reads VCF (`grep -rniI 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, and `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` at vcf_sink.rs:1018 is the public entry point). What the assertion checks is Perl's loader, which has no runtime counterpart in Rust.

desc: get parser object: Parser::VCF->new({config, file => the test VCF}) returns a defined parser
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. The type that stands in is `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`: vepyr never hands a caller a parser object, so the nearest thing an external crate can construct is the provider `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` registers internally (`vcf_sink.rs:1074` and `:1079` @ dfbf 391f94bd, both `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` — the five arguments the named test passes), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The probe is load-bearing rather than plumbing because that constructor is genuinely fallible: it `block_on`s `determine_schema_from_header` and propagates with `?` (`table_provider.rs:869-879` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8), i.e. it reads and parses the VCF header before it can return — exactly the ruling's defined/undef -> `Ok`/`Err` case. The named test asserts both limbs: `Ok` over a one-row VCF written to a tempdir, and over a missing path a typed error that is classified `NotFound` and names the path — because an `is_ok()` on its own would also pass against a constructor that never fails. Dual-claimed with the fourteen sibling rows the sweep moved together; all fifteen are the same statement at the same boundary, and the roster is kept in one place, the table at the top of tests/port_parser_vcf_construct.rs. R2's corollary still contributes its negative half here — the SKIP block guarding the absent database does not carry this row to no-feature, because the probe's subject is the VCF parser and not the database. What the sweep adds is the positive half: that subject is a capability vepyr does have, so the row is a port rather than plumbing.

desc: TESTS WITH AN INPUT BUFFER: Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer loads
rationale: The last of this file's four module-load probes. Not-applicable under ruling R2; as with n=67 the class denotes something vepyr has — `InputBufferAccumulator` (dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:9521) is the buffer VEP's InputBuffer corresponds to — so the only thing the line could add is the runtime `require`, which Rust never performs.

desc: check class: ref($ib) is exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer, not a subclass and not a plain hashref
rationale: A blessing probe on a class vepyr has: ruling R1's second bullet, since InputBuffer denotes buffering and `InputBufferAccumulator` (annotate_provider.rs:9521) is its counterpart, so the readback restates a compile-time fact — a Rust constructor's return type is its class and cannot disagree with itself at runtime. R2's corollary contributes only the negative half — it blocks the SKIP block from carrying the row to no-feature, the subject being the buffer and not the database — and R1 is what delivers not-applicable. Four merged ledgers read the identical line the same way: ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=9, ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=34, ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=11, ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=9.

desc: check buffer next: InputBuffer::next returns an arrayref — a list-shaped batch rather than a scalar, hashref or object
rationale: A reftype probe on a method's return value, and only that: an empty arrayref satisfies it, so the line says nothing about how many variants were read or which. In Rust the shape of a return is a compile-time fact carried by the signature, and vepyr's counterpart hands back Arrow RecordBatch values whose type no runtime check could contradict. What delivers the category is the contract's own not-applicable list, on which a reference-type probe sits alongside the blessing probes; R2's corollary does no more than block the SKIP block from carrying the row to no-feature, the subject being the buffer and not the database. The same line is already not-applicable at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=10, ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=10 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=12.

desc: get_all_regions_by_InputBuffer: the chr21 test buffer reduces to exactly eight 50 kb fetch regions — [21,511] through [21,519] with 516 absent, because no variant falls in it
rationale: Read carelessly this looks like the blocked-api rows at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=11 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=36, which pin the same method name. It is not the same property. Those assert [[21, 25]] — the 1 Mb block whose index vepyr really does compute, privately, from `VEP_TRANSCRIPT_CACHE_REGION_SIZE_BP = 1_000_000` (annotate_provider.rs:8826, divided at :11411). This row asserts a 50 kb granularity, set for every database source by `$self->{cache_region_size} ||= 50000` (modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/AnnotationSource/Database.pm:84 @ release/116.0), whose only consumer is the SQL fetch window built at AnnotationSource/Database/Transcript.pm:217-218. vepyr has no fetch that would need it and no constant of that size; an absent operation, not a missing `pub`.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 1: the buffer-wide pull across all eight regions returns an arrayref
rationale: The buffer-wide counterpart of n=42, and no-feature by the same measurement: the pull concatenates one core-database query per region of n=72, and vepyr has no adaptor to query (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `parquet` -> 913). Its subject is the absent call, not a container shape vepyr could disagree about, which is what keeps it out of the not-applicable column that ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=37 occupies for the cache-mode pull.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 2: the buffer-wide pull OPENS with a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript
rationale: A blessing probe of the absent thing, about the concatenation rather than a single fetch: n=44 pins the class inside one region, this pins that the class survives the join of eight. vepyr decodes one `TranscriptFeature` type from parquet, whose class cannot vary at runtime, and performs no per-region database fetch to concatenate (n=73).

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 3: the buffer-wide pull also CLOSES with a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript, so the concatenation is homogeneous end to end
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=74: checking only the head would miss a later region contributing a differently-blessed row or an undef, so the `[-1]` index is what makes the claim cover the join. Same absent fetch, same measurement. Note the contrast with the sibling regulatory source, whose equivalent pull is asserted to END on a different class (t/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.t:144 pins a MotifFeature last) — here the catalogue is homogeneous, and that is the content.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer stable_id: the first transcript of the buffer-wide pull is ENST00000567517 — a different transcript from the single-region fetch's ENST00000456917, because the buffer spans more than region 511
rationale: The row pins that the concatenation is ordered by position across regions rather than by the order the regions were fetched: if it were the latter, region 511's ENST00000456917 (n=45) would still be first. That is a real failure mode of a per-region fetch loop, which is why the row is not n=45 repeated. vepyr issues no database fetch to order (n=73).

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer count: exactly 44 Ensembl transcripts overlap the whole chr21 test buffer, against 6 for the single region of n=43
rationale: The census closest to production: it counts what an annotation run would actually consider for this buffer, so a boundary or filter regression moves it, and it is the row that would catch a region silently dropped from the eight of n=72. It is also the baseline the RefSeq count of n=90 (35) and the all_refseq count of n=91 (51) are read against. Nothing in vepyr issues the query, and 44 is a property of the homo_vepiens MultiTestDB fixture.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer again: a SECOND buffer-wide pull over the same unchanged buffer returns ENST00000567517 first again, so the per-region memo is hit rather than the database re-queried
rationale: Idempotency across a warm memo, one level up from n=46-48 — upstream's own comment at perl/AnnotationSource_Database_Transcript.t:421 says `do it again to get them from memory`. It earns its row because a stateful reader that consumed its input on the first pass would fail here and nowhere else. vepyr has neither the query to avoid nor a per-source region memo to hit; its nearest machinery, `prune_persisted_buffer_transcripts` (annotate_provider.rs:11523), is private and evicts rather than serves.

desc: get_all_features_by_InputBuffer on empty buffer: after ib->next() advances past the data, the pull returns an empty list rather than the previous buffer's 44 transcripts
rationale: The exhaustion case and the sharp end of n=78: the memo that made the second pull cheap must not make an empty buffer look populated. That is a real failure mode of a memo keyed by region rather than by buffer, which is why it earns its own row. vepyr holds no such memo and performs no database pull, so there is neither a stale answer to guard against nor an empty one to assert.

desc: get_all_regions_by_InputBuffer - include upstream: a single variant at 21:13002936 resolves to TWO regions, [21,259] and [21,260], because the up/downstream annotation distance widens the window back across the 13.0 Mb boundary
rationale: The one region row in the family whose content is the expansion rather than the reduction, and vepyr genuinely implements the expansion: `cache_regions_for_coords(chrom, start, end, upstream_distance, downstream_distance)` (annotate_provider.rs:11429) carries a doc comment citing VEP's `AnnotationType::Transcript::up_down_size()` by URL and applies max(upstream, downstream) symmetrically, exactly as the Perl does. It still cannot witness this assertion, and the reason is arithmetic rather than access: vepyr's region size is 1 Mb (`VEP_TRANSCRIPT_CACHE_REGION_SIZE_BP`, annotate_provider.rs:8826), so this variant plus 5 kb falls inside ONE region and the two-region answer cannot arise. The 50 kb granularity that makes the boundary crossing observable belongs to the database source (Database.pm:84), which does not exist. A `pub` on the free function would not produce the asserted value, so the row is no-feature rather than deferred / blocked-api.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - get_all_TranscriptVariations count: after the database source annotates the buffer, the first variant carries exactly 3 TranscriptVariations — three overlapping transcripts, not two and not duplicated
rationale: The load-bearing end-to-end row of the file: it runs the whole database annotation path and checks the cardinality of the result, so it catches both a missed transcript and a double-counted one. vepyr computes transcript consequences in quantity (`grep -rniI 'TranscriptVariation' src/` -> 288 at dfbf 391f94bd, in doc comments tracing VEP's own classes) and would express the same claim as the number of CSQ rows for the variant. What it cannot do is produce them from a core-database fetch: `get_adaptor` -> 0, `mysql` -> 0, positive control `parquet` -> 913. Classified on the backend, which is what keeps it from restating whatever cache-mode row covers per-variant consequence counts.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - display_consequence: after _finish_annotation the first buffered variant reports missense_variant, i.e. the most-severe of the three consequences of n=81 wins and reaches the user
rationale: The other end-to-end row, and the one that would catch consequences computed but never ranked. vepyr emits this exact term — `missense_variant` appears 37 times at dfbf 391f94bd, and the SO vocabulary lives in so_terms.rs — which is precisely why the row must be classified by its backend rather than by its expected value: the annotation it ranks came from a database fetch vepyr has no client for (n=81). Reading it as portable would claim coverage of a backend that does not exist.

desc: with filter - filtered transcript absent: constructing the source with filter => 'stable_id ne ENST00000352957' leaves zero TranscriptVariations on that transcript, so the expression is parsed and applied at fetch time
rationale: VEP's `--transcript_filter` is a small expression language over transcript fields, evaluated per fetched transcript, and this row pins that a `ne` predicate on stable_id actually removes a transcript that would otherwise be annotated. vepyr has nothing of the kind: `grep -rniI 'transcript_filter' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control `biotype` -> 122, and the pin's option vocabulary is closed at 31 keys and contains no filter key at all. The filtering it does have is fixed and flag-shaped (`gencode_basic`, vcf_sink.rs:426; `exclude_predicted`, annotate_provider.rs:1431-1445), not an expression, so naming it here would be a false analogue. Absent feature: the transcript filter language.

desc: with filter - display_consequence: with ENST00000352957 filtered out the same variant now reports 3_prime_UTR_variant instead of the missense_variant of n=82 — the filter changes the answer, not just the transcript list
rationale: The row that makes n=83 more than bookkeeping: removing one transcript demotes the most-severe consequence, which is the user-visible effect a filter is for. Both halves are absent — the filter language (n=83) and the database annotation path that produced the baseline (n=82) — so vepyr can exhibit neither the before nor the after. Note the term itself is one vepyr emits, which is why the row is classified on the filter and the backend rather than on the value.

desc: refseq - info: with refseq => 1 the source's provenance hash gains a refseq key naming the GFF it was built from (2015-10-26 11:20:17 - GCF_000001405.31_GRCh38.p5_genomic.gff) and LOSES the sift and polyphen keys of n=8, because otherfeatures carries no prediction data
rationale: The most informative of the three info rows, because the key SET changes with the flavour: RefSeq gains a build-provenance string and drops the two prediction versions, so a source that kept querying the variation database would fail here. As at n=8, the cache-mode channel for such versions exists and is already claimed — `SourceDescriptor::from_info_source` (bio-format-ensembl-cache 0d9730c8 info.rs:26-45) makes a `source_refseq` column out of exactly this kind of info.txt line, and ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=24 claims that as an analog-port. What is absent is the boundary and the flavour switch: `refseq` is not among the pin's 31 option keys, and there is no meta-table query to make.

desc: refseq - get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 1: the buffer-wide pull against the RefSeq-configured source returns an arrayref
rationale: The RefSeq arm of n=73, absent for the same measured reason — no adaptor, hence no fetch whose return shape could be checked (`grep -rniI 'get_adaptor' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `parquet` -> 913). It is not redundant with n=73 because the source is pointed at the otherfeatures database (n=57), which is what this block exists to exercise.

desc: refseq - get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 2: the RefSeq buffer-wide pull OPENS with a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript, the same class the Ensembl pull returns
rationale: The class-agreement claim across flavours at the buffer level, matching n=62 at the region level: whichever database the source is pointed at, the objects reaching the annotation path are indistinguishable by class. vepyr also uses one transcript type for all three cache flavours (cache_source.rs:13-18), but the assertion is about the return of a database fetch it cannot make (n=86).

desc: refseq - get_all_features_by_InputBuffer ref 3: the RefSeq pull also CLOSES with a Bio::EnsEMBL::Transcript, so the RefSeq concatenation is homogeneous end to end too
rationale: The RefSeq mirror of n=75, and not a duplicate of n=87 for the same reason n=75 is not a duplicate of n=74: an end-of-list check catches a later region contributing a differently-shaped row that a head check cannot. Same absent fetch (n=86).

desc: refseq - get_all_features_by_InputBuffer stable_id: the first transcript of the RefSeq buffer-wide pull is NR_024092.1 — a non-coding RefSeq accession, and a different one from the single-region fetch's NR_001458.3
rationale: Identity rather than shape, and it carries the same ordering claim as n=76: the buffer spans more regions than the single fetch of n=63, so a different accession must come first if the concatenation is ordered by position. vepyr carries RefSeq accessions in its RefSeq-flavoured cache (`grep -rniI 'refseq' src/` -> 946 at dfbf 391f94bd) but reads them from parquet; there is no query whose ordering could be asserted.

desc: refseq - get_all_features_by_InputBuffer count: 35 RefSeq transcripts overlap the whole chr21 test buffer, against 44 Ensembl ones at n=77 over the identical buffer
rationale: The buffer-level statement of the flavour switch, and the baseline for n=91: same buffer, same code path, a different catalogue and therefore a different count, so a source that silently kept querying core would fail here. vepyr issues no query, and both numbers belong to the homo_vepiens MultiTestDB fixtures rather than to any algorithm.

desc: refseq - get_all_features_by_InputBuffer count - all_refseq: setting all_refseq on the source raises the same buffer's RefSeq transcript count from 35 to 51, i.e. the predicted XM_/XR_ models are no longer filtered out
rationale: This is the row where vepyr comes closest: `all_refseq` really is a request option at the pin — `pub all_refseq: bool` (vcf_sink.rs:430), emitted into options_json at :582 and read at annotate_provider.rs:1413 — one of only 31 keys, and its effect is the same widening of the RefSeq transcript set. It is still no-feature, and the reason is the whole file's reason rather than a special case: what this row asserts is the flag's effect on a DATABASE FETCH from otherfeatures, counted before annotation, and vepyr applies it while scanning a RefSeq parquet cache with no fetch to widen. The 35 and the 51 are counts of rows returned by a SQL query that cannot be issued (n=86). The flag is present; the boundary it acts on is not.

desc: get new config object (other species): a Config is accepted for species => mus_muscuvep with everything => 1 and quiet => 1, i.e. the whole run can be re-pointed at a second species' databases
rationale: A constructor probe decided by denotation under docs/ledger-contract.md's ok($obj) ruling, and the species dimension is what it denotes. vepyr has none: `grep -rniI 'species' src/` -> 0 at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control `assembly` -> 8 in the same tree and `species` -> 31 in the cache reader, where it survives only as a provenance column.
