desc: get parser object: Parser::VCF->new({config, a generated one-line VCF holding 21 25585733 rs142513484 C T, valid_chromosomes [21]}) returns a defined parser
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. The type that stands in is `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`: vepyr never hands a caller a parser object, so the nearest thing an external crate can construct is the provider `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` registers internally (`vcf_sink.rs:1074` and `:1079` @ dfbf 391f94bd, both `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` — the five arguments the named test passes), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The probe is load-bearing rather than plumbing because that constructor is genuinely fallible: it `block_on`s `determine_schema_from_header` and propagates with `?` (`table_provider.rs:869-879` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8), i.e. it reads and parses the VCF header before it can return — exactly the ruling's defined/undef -> `Ok`/`Err` case. The named test asserts both limbs: `Ok` over a one-row VCF written to a tempdir, and over a missing path a typed error that is classified `NotFound` and names the path — because an `is_ok()` on its own would also pass against a constructor that never fails. Dual-claimed with the fourteen sibling rows the sweep moved together; all fifteen are the same statement at the same boundary, and the roster is kept in one place, the table at the top of tests/port_parser_vcf_construct.rs. The `valid_chromosomes` argument this call adds is not a boundary difference: `ok($p)` inspects no argument, so the assertion holds for any defined return and would still hold if the file were empty. What that argument does is ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml's subject.

desc: TESTS WITH INPUT BUFFER: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer module compiles and loads, so parsed variants can be batched for annotation
rationale: Fifth and last module-load probe in the file, not-applicable under docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 - the ruling that also reclassified ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=1. What the buffer does with variants is asserted in t/InputBuffer.t; here it is only the fixture n=12 to n=21 annotate through.

desc: check class: InputBuffer->new({config, parser}) returns an object blessed into exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer, not a subclass and not a plain hashref
rationale: A blessing readback, decided on the second limb of docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R1. The first limb does not apply - this file has no ok($ib = InputBuffer->new(...)) row - but the second does: InputBuffer denotes a capability vepyr HAS under a different type, accumulating parsed variants into a batch before annotation, namely `struct InputBufferAccumulator` over `VecDeque<RecordBatch>` plus two counters at dfbf 391f94bd, annotate_provider.rs:9522, with pending_rows() at :9529. A Rust constructor's return type is its class and cannot disagree with itself at run time. What is NOT claimed: that struct is private, which is why InputBuffer.t's rows about the buffer's own state are deferred/blocked-api there rather than covered here. Same assertion and reading at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_VCF.ledger.toml n=9, ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=9 and ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=9.

desc: check buffer next: the first InputBuffer::next() call returns an arrayref - a list-shaped batch rather than a scalar, hashref or object
rationale: A reftype probe on a method's return value, and only that: an empty arrayref satisfies it, so the line says nothing about how many variants were read or which. In Rust the shape of a return is a compile-time fact carried by the signature, and vepyr's counterpart hands back Arrow RecordBatch values whose type no run-time check could contradict. Nothing is dropped: what this buffer's annotation produces is n=12 onwards, all no-feature. Same reading at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_VCF.ledger.toml n=10 and ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=10.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - overlap: annotating the 21:25585733 C/T buffer under the default overlap type attaches _custom_annotations keyed 'test.bw' - the source's default short_name, its own basename - holding one record whose NAME IS THE SCORE, { name => 10 }, with no score key because summary_stats had not been set when this annotate call ran
rationale: The core bigWig contract and the one place this format differs from every other custom source: a bigWig has no ID column, so _get_record_name returns the interval's VALUE (AnnotationSource/File/BigWig.pm:149-161 @ release/116.0) where the VCF and BED sources return an ID. The row also pins the same in-place annotation and short_name keying the sibling formats have (AnnotationSource/File.pm:437), and - by the absent score key - that a value is reported twice, as name and as score, only when statistics are requested. The feature is absent at the pin on the measurement n=5 quotes in full: bigwig, bigbed and bigfile match nothing anywhere in dfbf 391f94bd or in vepyr 346b9173, against controls that do match. The bio-formats BigWig reader n=5 names (datafusion-bio-format-bbi, in neither Cargo.lock) does not rescue it: it scans intervals and has no annotation step.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - no summary statistics: for that same variant _custom_annotations_stats is an EMPTY hash, because summary_stats was assigned on line 74 AFTER the annotate call on line 73 - statistics are accumulated during annotation, never derived afterwards from the stored records
rationale: The row looks like a triviality and is not: it fixes WHEN statistics are computed. annotate_VariationFeature reads $self->{summary_stats} at the moment of annotation (AnnotationSource/File.pm:398-400, :422-434 @ release/116.0), so a source configured afterwards leaves the hash untouched - an implementation that aggregated lazily over _custom_annotations at output time would produce a populated hash here and fail. vepyr has neither the accumulator nor the records to aggregate: summary_stats scores 0 lines in datafusion/bio-function-vep src/ at dfbf 391f94bd (control parquet 913), and the plugin-cache track's only multi-record rule is build-time keep-first dedup (plugin_cache/dedup.rs:1-15), which selects a row rather than reducing over rows.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - exact, additive: after type('exact') and short_name('foo'), a SECOND annotate pass over the same buffer adds a 'foo' key holding { name => 10, score => 10 } - the value now appearing as BOTH name and score, since statistics are requested - while the earlier 'test.bw' entry survives untouched
rationale: Two properties in one assertion. (a) Annotation is additive per short_name, so the same source annotated twice under two names leaves both keys standing - what makes several --custom sources composable in one run. (b) For a bigWig, exact and overlap agree on this single-base variant, so what the pass actually adds is the score field, attached only because $get_scores is true (AnnotationSource/File.pm:399, and the base-class _create_records at :465-467 which BigWig inherits). vepyr has no per-source annotation map to accumulate into and no match modes at all - short_name 0, overlap_cutoff 0, reciprocal 0 lines in datafusion/bio-function-vep src/ at dfbf 391f94bd, controls plugin_cache_root 25 and ProviderKind 7.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - single score, summary statistics: with summary_stats ['min','mean','max','sum','count'], the stats hash under 'foo' is min 10, max 10, mean 10, sum 10, count 1 - every requested statistic present, including mean and count derived from a single observation
rationale: The degenerate case of the aggregator, and it pins two things a one-value input can still distinguish: that count is 1 rather than absent, and that mean is emitted at all. Neither is accumulated: AnnotationSource/File.pm:432 @ release/116.0 adds to sum for BOTH sum and mean, then after the record loop :346 sets count from $record_count, :347-348 derives mean as sum / $record_count, and :350 DELETES sum unless the caller asked for it. So the exact-hash comparison here pins three separate decisions - count is a record count and not a base count, mean is derived rather than tracked, and the internal accumulator does not leak into the output. vepyr has no numeric aggregator over annotation records: summary_stats 0 lines at the pin (control parquet 913), and detailed_plans/AnnotationSource_File_BigWig.md records the same conclusion from the design side - the conservation-score use case is served by pre-baked cache columns, not by a runtime track reader plus aggregator.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - overlap, multiple scores: a symbolic <DEL> spanning 21:25585733-25592852 under type overlap collects FOUR records under 'foo' - names/scores 20, 30, 11, 21 - one per bigWig interval intersecting the span, in file order, neither sorted nor deduplicated
rationale: The multi-interval arm: one variant, many track intervals, each contributing its own record with the value as name and as score. The order in the expected list is the reader's walk order, not a ranking, so it pins that no re-ordering or best-hit selection happens - the opposite of what a cache lookup does. vepyr performs no such walk. The feature is absent at the pin on the measurement n=5 quotes in full: bigwig, bigbed and bigfile match nothing anywhere in dfbf 391f94bd or in vepyr 346b9173, against controls that do match. The bio-formats BigWig reader n=5 names (datafusion-bio-format-bbi, in neither Cargo.lock) does not rescue it: it scans intervals and has no annotation step.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - multiple scores, summary statistics: over those same four intervals the stats hash under 'foo' is min 11, max 30, mean 20.5, sum 82, count 4 - the mean exact rather than rounded, and computed over records, not bases
rationale: The real content of the aggregator, and the row that n=15 cannot stand in for: min and max here select different records, and mean 20.5 is 82/4 to full precision. Note what is being averaged - one value per intersecting INTERVAL, each counted once regardless of how many bases it covers - which is a modelling decision a port would have to reproduce rather than an obvious consequence: the denominator is $record_count, incremented once per successful annotate_VariationFeature call (AnnotationSource/File.pm:332-341), and mean is sum / $record_count at :347-348. A per-base weighting would give a different 'mean' over the same four intervals. No such aggregation exists at the pin (summary_stats 0 lines, control parquet 913).

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - out by 1 (5'): a variant at 21:25585732, one base 5' of the first interval, leaves the VariationFeature with NO _custom_annotations key at all - not an empty one and not a 0 score
rationale: A negative assertion, and the one that protects the coordinate conversion: bigWig intervals are 0-based half-open and Ensembl coordinates are 1-based inclusive, so an off-by-one in the conversion would silently produce a false hit with a real-looking score. Note the shape - ok(!...) passes both when the key is absent and when it is false - so what it pins is that nothing was recorded, the early return at AnnotationSource/File.pm:396. Absent from vepyr for the reason n=12 measures; and there is no boundary convention at the pin to compare with, because nothing there opens a bigWig at all. The reader named in n=5's rationale (datafusion-bio-format-bbi) does carry a coordinate_system_zero_based flag (bigwig.rs:42), but it is not in the dependency graph and there is no annotation step behind it.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - out by 1 (3'): a variant at 21:25585735, one base 3' of the interval, likewise leaves the VariationFeature with no _custom_annotations key
rationale: The 3' mirror of n=18 and not a duplicate of it: an interval-boundary error can be present at one end and not the other - a half-open end is exactly where the two conventions differ - so a single 5' test could pass while the 3' arm was wrong. Same absent product and same measurement as n=18.

desc: overlap fixedStep: a variant at 21:25592821 falls in a fixedStep section of the same bigWig and is annotated as { name => '11', score => '11' } - the second of the format's two section encodings, read through the same code path as the variableStep hits above
rationale: bigWig stores runs as either variableStep or fixedStep sections, and this row is the only one that exercises the second: everything n=12 to n=17 touched came from the variableStep part of test.bw. The property is that the section encoding is invisible above the reader - the record shape is identical - which is a statement about the reader family vepyr does not have. The feature is absent at the pin on the measurement n=5 quotes in full: bigwig, bigbed and bigfile match nothing anywhere in dfbf 391f94bd or in vepyr 346b9173, against controls that do match.

desc: get scores even when reporting coords: with report_coords(1) the same 21:25592821 hit is named '21:25592820-25592822' AND keeps score '11' - switching the NAME to coordinates does not suppress the score
rationale: The row exists because for a bigWig the two are the same datum: the name IS the value (n=12), so a naive implementation of report_coords would lose the number entirely. AnnotationSource/File/BigWig.pm:416-428 replaces only the name, while the score is attached separately in _create_records, and the expected hash carries both. Note also the coordinates: '21:25592820-25592822' is the interval's own span, not the variant's. vepyr has no per-source rendering mode - report_coords 0 lines in datafusion/bio-function-vep src/ at dfbf 391f94bd, controls plugin_cache_root 25 and ProviderKind 7 - and the caller-side twin of the flag is already classified no-feature as ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=18.

desc: use test: the AnnotationSource::File custom-source base class compiles and loads -- deliberately OUTSIDE the SKIP block, because the guard on line 36 reads that package's $CAN_USE_TABIX_PM variable and cannot until the package is compiled
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (in flight as old-repo issue #142 at the time of writing, whose diff this follows): a use_ok row is not-applicable UNCONDITIONALLY. The reason is not the usual compile-time one -- it is that no Rust design contains a run-time module-load assertion at all, so the statement has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. Nothing is hidden by keeping it out of the denominator: every row that asserts what a GFF source DOES stays in, and all 51 of them are no-feature. The byte-identical statement is n=1 of ledger/AnnotationSource_File.ledger.toml and n=1 of ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml, read the same way.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the AnnotationSource::File::GFF reader subclass compiles and loads -- the first assertion inside the tabix-guarded SKIP block, and the only one that names the GFF reader class itself
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (in flight as old-repo issue #142 at the time of writing, whose diff this follows): a use_ok row is not-applicable UNCONDITIONALLY. The reason is not the usual compile-time one -- it is that no Rust design contains a run-time module-load assertion at all, so the statement has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. It sits inside a SKIP block whose whole purpose is a feature vepyr lacks, where docs/ledger-contract.md's older SKIP-block convention would keep a probe in the denominator; R2 narrows that convention to its general statement -- a probe is carried to no-feature when the probe's SUBJECT is the absent feature, and a use_ok's subject is Perl's loader, not the GFF reader. ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=2 is this same statement one format across and reads it the same way. Recorded rather than hidden: 10 use_ok rows in four Haplo_* ledgers are still no-feature under the pre-R2 reading, tracked at old-repo issue #141.

desc: need to get a config object: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Runner module compiles and loads, so lines 47-50 can build the config object every source, parser and buffer below is handed
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (in flight as old-repo issue #142 at the time of writing, whose diff this follows): a use_ok row is not-applicable UNCONDITIONALLY. The reason is not the usual compile-time one -- it is that no Rust design contains a run-time module-load assertion at all, so the statement has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. Pure scaffolding here: the Runner is borrowed only for its config. What a Runner actually resolves is the subject of t/Runner.t and belongs to ledger/Runner.ledger.toml (M2 issue #51), so keeping this load probe out of the denominator loses nothing.
