desc: get new runner object: Runner->new({base_testing_cfg, input_file => test.vcf}) returns a defined object -- the config carrier the GFF source, the VCF parser and the input buffer are all built against
rationale: A constructor-truthiness probe, and the plumbing arm of docs/ledger-contract.md's RULING on ok($obj). BaseRunner::new is two statements -- bless {}, $class (BaseRunner.pm:89) and $self->{_config} = Config->new(@_) (:92) -- so the return is a blessed empty hashref and is ALWAYS true; the line cannot fail except by Config->new dying first, which would be an exception rather than a false. vepyr's counterpart to the option hash is vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig, a plain struct built by infallible literal initialisation, so there is no run-time definedness left to observe. Identical reading at ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=3 and ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=5. Worth noting what this line does NOT assert: $runner->init() on the next line carries no assertion, so nothing here proves a cache opened.

desc: new is defined: GFF->new({file => t/testdata/custom/test.gff.gz, config}) returns an object -- a GFF custom annotation source built from a bgzipped, tabix-indexed GFF3 and the runner's config, with no format token needed because the class is named directly
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md's RULING on ok($obj) decides by what the class denotes, and Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::File::GFF denotes a capability vepyr does not have: a user's GFF registered as an annotation source. Unlike n=4 the constructor is load-bearing -- BaseGXF::new refuses the source unless sequence is reachable (BaseGXF.pm:105-106), refuses the exact type (:109), warns about --nearest (:113-115) and fixes cache_region_size at 1e6 (:117) -- and it produces the object rows 6-29 and 35-43 all work through. ledger/AnnotationSource_File.ledger.toml n=17 is the anchor: NONE of BED, GFF, GTF or VCF becomes a reader at the pin, and the only format vocabulary that exists, plugin_cache::source_manifest::ProviderKind {Vcf, Csv, Tsv, Parquet, Bed} (source_manifest.rs:23-29), names neither gff nor gtf and returns NotImplemented for both arms it does name (provider.rs:111; provider.rs:3 says VCF/BED (bio-formats) are not wired in the prototype). Measured here at dfbf 391f94bd, per-pattern hit counts in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/: gff 0, gtf 0, annotate_InputBuffer 0; positive controls same command shape: ProviderKind 7, plugin_cache_root 25, parquet 913. no-feature and not deferred/blocked-api because nothing here is one pub away: the operation does not exist.

desc: setup fasta_db: the GFF source has a FASTA handle -- a GXF file carries no sequence of its own, so BaseGXF::new refuses to construct without one and every translation row below spends it
rationale: What the line pins is that a custom GXF source ACQUIRES sequence access, the precondition BaseGXF.pm:105-106 enforces (--fasta, or a non-offline cache, or a database). The near-miss is real and is named here so a reviewer can weigh it rather than rediscover it: vepyr does open an indexed reference FASTA -- reference_fasta_path (vcf_sink.rs:406) feeds the reader built at annotate_provider.rs:3654 -- and ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=25 reads BaseVEP's own fasta_db through exactly that channel. It cannot be borrowed for this row, because the subject is not that a FASTA opens but that a custom GXF SOURCE owns one, and there is no such source: fasta_db scores 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control fasta 63. Missing feature: the GXF source, not an accessor on it.

desc: cant use exact type: GFF->new({..., type => 'exact'}) dies naming GXF annotation sources cannot be used as exact custom annotation type -- of VEP's two --custom match modes, a transcript-model source accepts only overlap
rationale: The refusal is BaseGXF.pm:109, and its content is a per-format restriction on the match vocabulary: coordinate equality between a variant and a gene model is meaningless, so the constructor rejects the combination up front instead of producing a source that never matches. vepyr has no match modes to restrict -- overlap_cutoff and reciprocal each score 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd (the measurement ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml records for the same family), and type 0. A product statement, not an export: the missing feature is custom annotation match types together with the per-format rules over them.

desc: _get_records_by_coords - count: the single-base query 21:25585733 yields 75 records, far more than literally overlap it, because the fetch re-scans outward whenever a returned feature overhangs the window
rationale: The count is a property of the algorithm, not of the fixture: _get_records_by_coords seeks (chr, start-1, end+1), tracks the min start and max end of the included records, and then recurses with $no_rescan set to 1 or 2 so the expansion runs once in each direction (BaseGXF.pm:207-260, the two recursions at :252-257). Nothing at the pin reads a tabix-indexed annotation file: the pinned crate's AnnotationBackend declares one variant, Parquet (annotation_store.rs:11-14), and gff/gtf score 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd against controls parquet 913 and transcript 3040. Missing feature: file-backed record retrieval.

desc: _get_records_by_coords - first content: the first record is the whole hash BaseGXF::_record_to_hash builds -- source, chr, start, end, strand, phase, type, an md5 of the raw GFF block, and every GFF3 attribute (exon_id, rank, ensembl_phase, Parent transcript:ENST00000307301, ...) parsed into a sub-hash
rationale: Pins the record shape the whole class is built on, including the deduplication key: _record_to_hash sets md5 => md5_hex($parser->{current_block}) alongside the parsed fields (BaseGXF.pm:276-291), and phase is carried as undef rather than dropped. vepyr has neither the shape nor the digest -- md5, blake3 and xxhash each score 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd (the only hashing at the pin is cache key encoding in cache/key_encoding.rs), against control parquet 913. The same absence, measured the same way, is recorded at ledger/Haplo_AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml n=13. Missing feature: a parsed GFF3 record.

desc: _get_records_by_coords - non-overlapping sub-features count: 57 of those 75 records do NOT overlap the queried base -- the direct evidence that the outward rescan dragged in sibling exons of a parent that overhangs the window
rationale: This row, not n=9, is what pins the rescan: a fetch returning only literal overlaps would answer 0 here and n=9 alone could not tell the difference between 75 overlapping records and 18 overlapping plus 57 pulled in. The comment at BaseGXF.pm:248-251 states the intent -- sub-features such as exons do not come back even when their parent does -- and :252-257 is the mechanism. Nothing at the pin has a parent/child record model whose siblings must be completed: lazy_load_transcript and annotate_InputBuffer each score 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd, control transcript 3040; vepyr's window planner reads whole cache partitions and never a tabix index. Missing feature: the sub-feature-completing rescan.

desc: _create_transcripts - count: the 75 records at 21:25585733 compile into exactly 4 transcripts -- the parent/child tree is built, gene records are unwrapped into their children, and every surviving transcript record becomes one transcript
rationale: _create_transcripts walks the top level of _get_parent_child_structure, replaces each gene record by its _children and keeps non-gene records as themselves (BaseGXF.pm:311-341, the tree at :363). The count is the join working: 75 flat records, one gene, four transcripts. vepyr never builds transcripts from records -- transcripts arrive as rows of the parquet cache and are hydrated into TranscriptFeature, with AnnotationBackend declaring Parquet as the only backend (annotation_store.rs:11-14). Measured at dfbf 391f94bd: lazy_load_transcript 0, gff 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/, controls transcript 3040 and parquet 913. Missing feature: compiling a transcript model out of GFF records.

desc: stable_id: the first compiled transcript is ENST00000307301 -- the GFF3 ID attribute with its transcript: prefix stripped, not the record's md5 fallback
rationale: _record_get_id takes ID, then Name, then id, then name, and falls back to the record's md5 when none of them holds a word character (GFF.pm:272-283); the prefix strip is BaseGXF.pm:657. So the line pins a four-deep precedence plus a fallback, on a naming convention that is GFF3's and not GTF's -- ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GTF.ledger.toml n=11 is the same assertion where the id comes from transcript_id instead, which is why the two files each need the row. vepyr reads transcript_id as a cache column; it has no id-resolution precedence because it never sees an attribute list. Missing feature: identifier resolution from GFF attributes.

desc: _gene_stable_id: the transcript carries ENSG00000154719, taken from its own gene_id attribute -- the FIRST of the three fallbacks in _add_identifiers, and the one n=22 removes to reach the third
rationale: BaseGXF.pm:638 reads $tr_record->{attributes}->{gene_id} directly; :642-648 falls back to a GeneID pair inside Dbxref (which is how the RefSeq half reaches n=50); :651-658 falls back to the parent gene record. This row pins the first branch and n=22 pins the third, so neither covers the other. vepyr carries a Gene column in the cache and never derives one: gene_symbol scores 50 hits at dfbf 391f94bd but every one reads a cache-hydrated field, and gff scores 0. Missing feature: gene identity derived from a GFF record's attributes.

desc: _gene_symbol: the transcript carries MRPL39 -- resolved from a gene_name or gene attribute on the transcript record, or failing that from Name/name on the parent gene record
rationale: Two attribute names on the transcript record are tried in order, then two more on the gene record (BaseGXF.pm:662-671). The four-way spelling tolerance is the content: an Ensembl GFF3 spells it gene_name, a RefSeq GFF spells it gene (which is what n=51 exercises), and neither is the GTF spelling. vepyr's SYMBOL is a cache column, populated by the cache builder rather than resolved at annotate time. Same measurement as n=14. Missing feature: symbol resolution from a user file's attribute vocabulary.

desc: _protein: the transcript carries ENSP00000305682 -- the protein accession read off the CDS child record rather than off the transcript record itself
rationale: BaseGXF.pm:726 sets _protein from the protein id found while walking the CDS children, so this row pins that the transcript/protein link survives the flattening of a three-level GFF3 hierarchy into a transcript object. vepyr has an ENSP column in the cache (protein_id 7 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd) and no code that derives one, because there is no CDS record to walk: gff 0 hits, control transcript 3040. Missing feature: protein identity assembled from GFF child records.

desc: attributes: get_all_Attributes returns exactly ONE Bio::EnsEMBL::Attribute, {code TSL, value tsl5} -- the GFF's transcript_support_level promoted into the Ensembl attribute list, and nothing else promoted alongside it
rationale: The shape is the assertion: is_deeply pins a one-element list, so a source that also promoted the record's other attributes would fail it. BaseGXF.pm:673-679 promotes transcript_support_level (or tsl) and prefixes the literal tsl, and :688-690 promotes MANE_Select, MANE_Plus_Clinical, gencode_primary and gencode_basic from the tag attribute -- absent from this fixture, which is why the list is one long. The near-miss is worth naming: vepyr does carry TSL, but as a CSQ field read from the parquet cache (tsl 40 hits at dfbf 391f94bd, and the literal token TSL, in quotes, 3 under the case-SENSITIVE `git grep -c` that quoted form needs), never as an attribute list assembled from a user's GFF. Kept in the denominator although the expected value is a blessed object: docs/ledger-contract.md's ruling on two defensible readings is to keep the row in, and the subject here is the promotion, not the blessing. Missing feature: attribute promotion out of a GFF record.

desc: count exons: the compiled transcript has 11 exons -- every exon child of the mRNA record, which is only possible because the rescan of n=11 fetched the ones outside the query window
rationale: The row that closes the loop on n=11: the queried base sits in one exon, and the other ten are reachable only through the outward rescan, so this count is the end-to-end witness that record completion and transcript assembly agree. Exons are added under an eval whose failure is n=27/n=28 (BaseGXF.pm:576). vepyr's exon structure comes from cache columns (exon_number 121 hits at dfbf 391f94bd) and is never assembled from records: gff 0. Missing feature: exon assembly from GFF child records.

desc: translateable_seq: the CDS of ENST00000307301 spliced out of the reference FASTA -- 1062 bases pinned literally, and the proof that the fasta_db of n=6 was actually spent, since the GFF supplies coordinates only
rationale: A GFF has no sequence, so every base of this string came from the FASTA through coordinates the GFF supplied; the assertion therefore pins the JOIN of the two, including strand handling (the transcript is on -1) and exon order. vepyr does splice a CDS and does hold a reference FASTA, but the exon and CDS coordinates come from the parquet cache, never from a user file. It cannot be claimed as an analogue under docs/ledger-contract.md's dual-claim rule: a cache-driven splice test could not fail if GFF-driven model building regressed, because there is no GFF-driven model building (gff 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd, control transcript 3040). Missing feature: transcript sequence assembled from a user's GFF plus a FASTA.

desc: translate: that CDS translates to the 353-residue MRPL39 protein -- the full round trip GFF coordinates -> FASTA sequence -> peptide, on chr21 and therefore on the standard genetic code
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=19: n=19 pins the nucleotide splice and this pins the translation on top of it, and the same peptide is reasserted at n=54 from the RefSeq model, which is why the file stores it in $prot_seq rather than pasting it twice. Absent for n=19's reason -- no GFF-driven model to translate. Recorded here because it is the measurement the sibling GTF ledger leans on: the pinned crate's only two codon tables both map ATA to I (transcript_consequence.rs:9493 in translate_codon_bytes and :9806 in translate_codon), i.e. the standard table 1, and codon_table, translation_table and genetic_code each score 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd against control codon 1009. That is harmless for this row (chr21 is table 1 anyway) and is the whole of ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GTF.ledger.toml n=28/n=29.

desc: _create_transcripts - big fetch check biotypes: a 500 kb fetch (21:25.5-26 Mb) compiles into 58 named transcripts with their biotypes -- including ENST00000419219_1, which upstream's own comment at :158 calls a fake transcript to test exons having 2 parents
rationale: The scale-and-fan-out row. Two things it pins that no single-locus row can: the parent/child tree survives a window three orders of magnitude larger than n=9's, and an exon whose Parent attribute is a comma-separated list becomes a child of EVERY named parent rather than of the first (_record_get_parent_ids splits on comma, GFF.pm:242-256), which is what makes ENST00000419219_1 appear at all. It also pins the biotype vocabulary that comes straight from the attribute (biotype / transcript_type / transcript_biotype, GFF.pm:310-312) rather than from the guesswork the RefSeq half of n=55 needs. Absent for n=12's reason and by the same measurement. Missing feature: the record tree, including multi-parent children.

desc: gene_stable_id from gene object ID not gene_id: with gene_id deleted from two records the transcript still reports ENSG00000154719 -- the THIRD fallback, the parent gene record's own ID with its gene: prefix stripped
rationale: The failsafe n=14's first branch hides. With the attribute removed, _add_identifiers falls past the Dbxref branch (:642-648, empty for an Ensembl GFF) to the gene record (:651-658), takes _record_get_id and strips a leading gene: or transcript: with s/^(gene|transcript)\://i at :657. A test of the happy path cannot witness a fallback, so this row is not covered by n=14 however similar the expected value looks. Absent for n=14's reason. Missing feature: the gene-identity fallback chain.

desc: _get_parent_child_structure - parent not found: a record naming Parent foo when no such ID exists warns Parent entries with the following IDs were not found or skipped due to invalid types on STDERR, rather than dying or dropping the record in silence
rationale: The first of the file's five failsafe rows, and the one that fixes the policy: a malformed user GFF is REPORTED and survived, not fatal (BaseGXF.pm:425). The test reaches it by redirecting STDERR into a scalar at :205-209 and pattern-matching the buffer, which is why the row is an ok() on a regex rather than a throws_ok. vepyr has no user-file ingestion to be tolerant about: gff 0 and annotate_InputBuffer 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd, controls ProviderKind 7 and plugin_cache_root 25. ledger/AnnotationSource_File.ledger.toml n=17 is the anchor: NONE of BED, GFF, GTF or VCF becomes a reader at the pin, and the only format vocabulary that exists, plugin_cache::source_manifest::ProviderKind {Vcf, Csv, Tsv, Parquet, Bed} (source_manifest.rs:23-29), names neither gff nor gtf and returns NotImplemented for both arms it does name (provider.rs:111; provider.rs:3 says VCF/BED (bio-formats) are not wired in the prototype). Missing feature: the parent/child compiler, together with its tolerance policy.

desc: _create_transcripts - unexpected type of child: retyping the first record to foo makes lazy_load_transcript throw Transcript has unexpected type of child record -- the ONE malformation in this file that is fatal instead of a warning
rationale: This row is where the failsafe policy has an edge. Rows 23, 25-29 warn and continue; BaseGXF.pm:517 throws, because an unknown child type means the record tree is structurally uninterpretable rather than merely incomplete. A ledger that classified only the warning rows would lose the distinction, which is why the row stands on its own. Absent for n=23's reason and by the same measurement. Missing feature: the child-type contract, and the decision about which violations are fatal.

desc: no biotype skips transcript: deleting the biotype attribute from one of the four transcript records leaves 3 defined transcripts -- the unusable one is dropped and the other three still load, so one bad record does not poison the batch
rationale: Isolation, not rejection: lazy_load_transcript returns undef for the record it cannot type (BaseGXF.pm:471 area) and the map keeps the rest, so the count 3 is the assertion rather than a die. Note this depends on GFF.pm:304-320 having already failed to GUESS a biotype from the record type, which is the same guesser the RefSeq half of n=55 depends on succeeding -- the two rows read opposite ends of one function. Absent for n=23's reason. Missing feature: per-record failure isolation in a GFF compiler.

desc: no biotype warning message: that drop is announced as Unable to determine biotype of <id> on STDERR -- the diagnostic half of n=25
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=25 and not redundant with it: n=25 would still pass if the transcript were dropped in complete silence, which is the failure mode that makes a user's custom annotation quietly incomplete. BaseGXF.pm:471. Absent for n=23's reason. Missing feature: the diagnostic, which is a product commitment separate from the behaviour it describes.

desc: overlapping exons skips transcript: extending the first exon by 100 kb and deleting its rank makes its transcript unbuildable, again leaving 3 of 4 -- the same drop-one, keep-the-rest failsafe as n=25 reached through a different malformation
rationale: The malformation is geometric rather than missing metadata, and it enters through a different code path: the Ensembl API's add_Exon raises, BaseGXF.pm:576 catches it under eval and abandons that transcript. A test of the missing-biotype path (n=25) could not fail if the eval around exon addition were removed, so the two rows are not interchangeable. Absent for n=23's reason. Missing feature: exon-assembly failure isolation.

desc: overlapping exons warning message: Failed to add exon to transcript <stable_id> on STDERR, carrying the Ensembl API exception the eval caught -- the diagnostic half of n=27
rationale: Same relationship to n=27 that n=26 has to n=25, and the same argument for keeping it as its own row: the count would pass if the transcript vanished silently. Note the message at BaseGXF.pm:576 interpolates $@, so what is pinned is that the underlying exception is surfaced rather than swallowed. Absent for n=23's reason. Missing feature: the diagnostic, and the decision to propagate the inner error text.

desc: no exons warning message: a hand-built protein_coding mRNA record whose only children are two CDS features and no exon warns No exons found for protein_coding transcript -- the one failsafe driven by a literal record hash rather than by damaging a parsed one
rationale: Two things at once, which is why it is the longest fixture in the file (:237-285). First the behaviour: a coding transcript with CDS but no exon is a real RefSeq-style malformation, and BaseGXF.pm:523 reports it. Second, and only here, the row pins the INPUT CONTRACT of lazy_load_transcript -- the _children / _gene_record / _parent_id / _id / attributes shape that _get_parent_child_structure is expected to produce -- because the hash is written out by hand rather than parsed. Absent for n=23's reason. Missing feature: the record-tree data structure itself, of which this is the only written-down specification in the corpus.

desc: TESTS WITH INPUT BUFFER: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF module compiles and loads, so a one-variant VCF can be read into a buffer for the annotation rows
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (in flight as old-repo issue #142 at the time of writing, whose diff this follows): a use_ok row is not-applicable UNCONDITIONALLY. The reason is not the usual compile-time one -- it is that no Rust design contains a run-time module-load assertion at all, so the statement has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. VCF parsing behaviour itself is the subject of t/Parser_VCF.t and ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml (M2 issue #49); this line asserts none of it. Same treatment at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=6 and ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml.

desc: get parser object: Parser::VCF->new({config, a generated one-line VCF holding 21 25585733 rs142513484 C T, valid_chromosomes [21]}) returns a defined parser
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. The type that stands in is `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`: vepyr never hands a caller a parser object, so the nearest thing an external crate can construct is the provider `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` registers internally (`vcf_sink.rs:1074` and `:1079` @ dfbf 391f94bd, both `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` — the five arguments the named test passes), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The probe is load-bearing rather than plumbing because that constructor is genuinely fallible: it `block_on`s `determine_schema_from_header` and propagates with `?` (`table_provider.rs:869-879` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8), i.e. it reads and parses the VCF header before it can return — exactly the ruling's defined/undef -> `Ok`/`Err` case. The named test asserts both limbs: `Ok` over a one-row VCF written to a tempdir, and over a missing path a typed error that is classified `NotFound` and names the path — because an `is_ok()` on its own would also pass against a constructor that never fails. Dual-claimed with the fourteen sibling rows the sweep moved together; all fifteen are the same statement at the same boundary, and the roster is kept in one place, the table at the top of tests/port_parser_vcf_construct.rs. The `valid_chromosomes` argument this call adds is not a boundary difference: `ok($p)` inspects no argument, so the assertion holds for any defined return and would still hold if the file were empty. What that argument does is ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml's subject.

desc: TESTS WITH INPUT BUFFER: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer module compiles and loads, so parsed variants can be batched for annotation
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (in flight as old-repo issue #142 at the time of writing, whose diff this follows): a use_ok row is not-applicable UNCONDITIONALLY. The reason is not the usual compile-time one -- it is that no Rust design contains a run-time module-load assertion at all, so the statement has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. The buffer it loads is the fixture n=33-38 annotate through; what the buffer itself does with variants is asserted in t/InputBuffer.t and belongs to ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml (M2 issue #37). Same treatment at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=8.

desc: check class: InputBuffer->new({config, parser}) returns an object blessed into exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer -- not a subclass and not a plain hashref
rationale: A blessing readback, decided by docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R1 (in flight as old-repo issue #142, whose diff this follows). R1's second arm applies: the class denotes a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type -- InputBufferAccumulator, dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs -- so the readback restates a compile-time fact, because a Rust constructor's return type is its class and cannot disagree with itself at run time. R1's fallback (a readback that is the ledger's only accounting for the construction) does not bite: nothing else in this file needs the InputBuffer construction accounted for, since what the buffer DOES here is n=35's annotation. Byte-identical assertion and identical verdict at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=9 and ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=9.

desc: check buffer next: the first InputBuffer::next() call returns an arrayref -- a list-shaped batch rather than a scalar, hashref or object
rationale: A reftype probe on a return value, and only that: an EMPTY arrayref satisfies it, so the line says nothing about how many variants were read or which. In Rust the shape of a return is carried by the signature and checked by the compiler, and vepyr's counterpart hands back Arrow RecordBatch values whose type no run-time check could contradict. The content of this buffer is not lost by keeping the shape probe out of the denominator: n=35 asserts what annotating it produces and is no-feature. Identical reading at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=10 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=35.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - display_consequence: annotating the 21:25585733 C>T buffer through the GFF source and finishing annotation gives display_consequence missense_variant -- the whole GFF pipeline, from tabix fetch to most-severe term, in one assertion
rationale: The end-to-end row for the Ensembl-GFF half, and the one place where the file asserts that a transcript model read from a USER'S FILE produces the same consequence machinery as the cache. vepyr does compute missense_variant for exactly this variant, so the temptation to call this an analog-port is real and is refused on docs/ledger-contract.md's dual-claim test: a cache-driven consequence test could not fail if GFF-driven annotation regressed, because there is no GFF-driven annotation to regress. GFF::annotate_InputBuffer dispatches on gff_type and routes the transcript case into AnnotationType::Transcript::annotate_InputBuffer (GFF.pm:154-164); measured at dfbf 391f94bd, annotate_InputBuffer 0, gff_type 0 and gff 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/, controls most_severe 58 and transcript 3040. ledger/AnnotationSource_File.ledger.toml n=17 is the anchor: NONE of BED, GFF, GTF or VCF becomes a reader at the pin, and the only format vocabulary that exists, plugin_cache::source_manifest::ProviderKind {Vcf, Csv, Tsv, Parquet, Bed} (source_manifest.rs:23-29), names neither gff nor gtf and returns NotImplemented for both arms it does name (provider.rs:111; provider.rs:3 says VCF/BED (bio-formats) are not wired in the prototype).

desc: with filter - filtered transcript absent: of the variant's TranscriptVariations, exactly 0 are on ENST00000352957 -- the named transcript was removed from the source's output rather than merely deprioritised
rationale: The substance of n=36's warning. Note the shape: a count of 0 over get_all_TranscriptVariations, so it also pins that filtering happens BEFORE consequence calculation rather than as a display filter afterwards. vepyr's nearest behaviour (TranscriptSelectionFlags, see n=36) likewise excludes before annotation, but over a fixed flag vocabulary and over the parquet cache, so it cannot witness a stable_id predicate over a GFF-derived transcript set. Missing feature: as n=36.

desc: with filter - display_consequence: with ENST00000352957 filtered out, the most-severe term for the same variant falls from missense_variant (n=35) to 3_prime_UTR_variant -- the filter changes the ANSWER, not just the transcript list
rationale: Not covered by n=37: that row would still pass if the filter had removed EVERY transcript, and this one pins that the survivors still annotate and still re-rank, so the reported consequence is recomputed over the filtered set. It is also the only place in the file where the same variant is shown to have two different answers, which is what makes the filter a correctness feature rather than a cosmetic one. Missing feature: as n=36; and the ranking it feeds is over a transcript set vepyr cannot obtain from a file at all (n=35's measurement).

desc: load synonyms: chromosome_synonyms(t/testdata/chr_synonyms.txt) loads onto the GFF source and returns a truthy alias map -- the precondition n=42 spends
rationale: BaseVEP.pm:637 reads a two-column file into {canonical => {synonym => 1}}, and the assertion is that the loader ran and produced something. There is no such loader at the pin, and the measurement needs care because of a substring trap worth recording: synonym scores 78 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd and EVERY one is synonymous_variant or the cache column var_synonyms (cache/schema.rs:67) -- not one is a chromosome alias; chr_synonym and chromosome_synonym each score 0. At the vepyr reference pin 346b9173 the option-name probe git grep -cniE for custom|gff|gtf|bigwig|dont_skip|chr_synonyms|synonyms over src/ returns no files, against the positive control plugin_cache_root|fasta|regulatory which returns 3. Same finding as ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=19 and ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=28. Missing feature: a user-supplied chromosome-synonyms file.

desc: get_source_chr_name - exists, same: a query name already present in the GFF source's valid_chromosomes comes back unchanged, and is memoised into _chr_name_map so the resolution runs once per name
rationale: The identity arm of BaseVEP.pm:689-738, and it is not trivial: the method returns the name unchanged only after CONSULTING the source's own valid_chromosomes (:700-706), the contig set read out of the custom file's tabix index. That set is the thing vepyr does not have -- name resolution at the pin is the fixed rule normalize_chrom with no state a caller can override, as ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=10 records -- that row is the one whose subject is the writable valid_chromosomes setter, and it is no-feature for exactly this reason. Not shareable with that ledger's analog-port rows n=21 (tests/port_transcript_tree.rs::fetch_strips_a_chr_prefix_from_the_query) and n=22 (::fetch_matches_when_only_the_stored_name_carries_chr) under docs/ledger-contract.md's dual-claim rule: their tests observe the transcript tree, and neither could fail if a GFF source's name resolution regressed, because there is no GFF source. Measured: get_source_chr_name 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd, control transcript 3040. Missing feature: name resolution against a custom file's own contig set.

desc: get_source_chr_name - strip chr: a chr21 query resolves to 21 -- but CONDITIONALLY, because BaseVEP.pm:722-727 accepts the stripped name only when 21 is in valid_chromosomes
rationale: The conditionality is the content, and it is what stops the row being an analogue. vepyr's nearest behaviour is real: normalize_chrom is chrom.strip_prefix(chr).unwrap_or(chrom) (private original transcript_consequence.rs:3803, public twin golden_benchmark.rs:237), and ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=21 already claims that observable as an analog-port at the tree boundary. It cannot be claimed twice, on both halves of the dual-claim test: vepyr strips UNCONDITIONALLY and on both sides, so it has no valid_chromosomes to consult and cannot exhibit the conditional acceptance this line pins, and the test named there could not fail if a GFF source's resolution regressed. Missing feature: as n=40.

desc: get_source_chr_name - synonyms: the RefSeq accession NC_000021.9 resolves to 21 through the map loaded at n=39 -- the alias arm, which BaseVEP.pm:708-716 tries BEFORE the add/strip-chr arm
rationale: The substance of the synonyms feature, and the ordering matters: an alias table beats a textual transform, so a spelling that is not derivable from the canonical name still resolves. The negative control is already committed in this repository -- tests/port_transcript_tree.rs::fetch_strips_a_chr_prefix_from_the_query shows NC_000021.9 returning zero hits over a tree keyed 21 while chr21 and 21 both return one, because prefix-stripping is not an alias lookup. no-feature rather than failed: vepyr never claims the table, so it does not resolve accessions wrongly, it has nowhere to resolve them. Same finding as ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=20, ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=29 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix.ledger.toml n=14. Missing feature: as n=39.

desc: get_source_chr_name - add chr: after pushing chrFoo onto the source's valid_chromosomes, a bare Foo query resolves to chrFoo -- the ADD-prefix arm at BaseVEP.pm:728-730, the mirror of n=41 and the only place in this file where valid_chromosomes is written
rationale: An off-by-direction in name resolution can be present in one arm and absent in the other, so n=41 cannot stand for this row: stripping a prefix and adding one are separate branches of the same if/elsif. vepyr never adds a prefix in any code path -- normalize_chrom only strips (transcript_consequence.rs:3803), and canonical_contig_str only strips and folds the mitochondrial aliases to MT (plugin_cache/normalize.rs:22-35). ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=22 reaches the same OBSERVABLE (the query hits) by keying both sides through normalize_chrom and says so in its rationale; it cannot stand for this row, whose asserted value is the returned NAME rather than a hit. Missing feature: as n=40.

desc: REFSEQ FILE - load synonyms: the same alias file loaded onto a SECOND source, built from the RefSeq GFF whose contigs are spelled NC_000021.9 -- here the load is a precondition rather than a probe, since without it n=45-58 cannot address the file at all
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=39 in role even though it is the same statement: at n=39 the synonyms are optional decoration on an Ensembl-spelled file, and here they are the only way the RefSeq file can be reached, which is why upstream repeats the call and comments it requires synonyms (:353). The absence is n=39's, measured the same way. Missing feature: as n=39.

desc: _get_records_by_coords - refseq - count: 104 records at the same locus, against 75 from the Ensembl GFF at n=9 -- the same outward rescan over a denser annotation set
rationale: The count differs from n=9 by more than the fixtures differ in size: RefSeq annotates this locus with more transcripts and more sub-features, so the row pins that the rescan termination condition (min/max tracked per direction, BaseGXF.pm:228-235) does not depend on the density of the file. Absent for n=9's reason and by the same measurement.

desc: _get_records_by_coords - check first: the first RefSeq record's full hash -- source BestRefSeq, chr NC_000021.9 kept in the FILE's own spelling rather than mapped to 21, and RefSeq-flavoured attributes including a Dbxref list, gbkey, exception, transcript_id NM_017446.3 and a product value whose comma survives as the GFF3 escape %2C
rationale: Three things a reader would otherwise assume. First, _record_to_hash is format-agnostic: the same eight keys as n=10, whatever the attribute vocabulary (BaseGXF.pm:276-291). Second, the chr field keeps NC_000021.9 -- the synonyms map of n=44 resolves the QUERY, not the stored record, so nothing rewrites the file's own names. Third, GFF3 percent-escaping is preserved verbatim in the attribute value rather than decoded. Absent for n=10's reason (md5 0, gff 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd; controls parquet 913, transcript 3040). Missing feature: a parsed GFF3 record.

desc: _create_transcripts - count: the 104 RefSeq records also compile into exactly 4 transcripts -- the same tree walk over a file that names its parents differently
rationale: Not n=12 repeated: an Ensembl GFF3 links children through Parent => transcript:ENSTxxx and RefSeq through Parent => rna144911, so this row pins that _get_parent_child_structure keys on the raw ID string and never on an Ensembl-shaped one. Absent for n=12's reason and by the same measurement.

desc: stable_id: the fourth compiled transcript is NM_080794.3 -- a RefSeq accession as the stable id, taken from the record's ID/Name chain rather than from an Ensembl-prefixed ID
rationale: The RefSeq counterpart of n=13, and it exercises a different branch of the same precedence: GFF.pm:272-283 tries ID, Name, id, name and falls back to the record's md5, and there is no gene:/transcript: prefix to strip here. Note the index moved to 3: the four transcripts come back in a different order than the Ensembl file's, which is itself part of what the row pins. Absent for n=13's reason.

desc: _gene_stable_id: the gene id is the bare NCBI GeneID 54148, dug out of the record's Dbxref list -- the SECOND fallback in _add_identifiers, which no Ensembl-GFF row reaches
rationale: RefSeq GFFs carry no gene_id attribute, so BaseGXF.pm:638 yields nothing and :642-648 splits Dbxref on commas, splits each pair on a colon and keeps the value of the first GeneID key -- from Dbxref => GeneID:54148,Genbank:NM_017446.3,HGNC:HGNC:14027,... , where a naive split would have produced HGNC:14027 for the HGNC pair. That is the branch this row and only this row witnesses: n=14 takes the first fallback and n=22 the third. Absent for n=14's reason. Missing feature: gene identity derived from a cross-reference list.

desc: _gene_symbol: MRPL39 again, here from the RefSeq gene attribute rather than from the Ensembl gene_name of n=15
rationale: The second spelling in the two-name loop at BaseGXF.pm:662-667, so the row witnesses the fallback that n=15 skips over on its first iteration. It also pins that the two annotation sets agree on the symbol for this gene, which is the cross-annotation theme n=54 completes. Absent for n=15's reason.

desc: _protein: the RefSeq protein accession NP_542984.2, read off the CDS child of NM_080794.3
rationale: The RefSeq counterpart of n=16 (BaseGXF.pm:726). Worth its own row because RefSeq spells the CDS protein reference differently from Ensembl and the resolution has to reach it either way; a test on the Ensembl file alone would not show that. Absent for n=16's reason.

desc: count exons: the RefSeq transcript has 11 exons -- the same count the Ensembl model gives for the same locus at n=18
rationale: Two annotation sets, independently parsed, agreeing on the exon structure: the row is a cross-check on the compiler rather than on either file, since an assembly bug specific to one attribute vocabulary would show up as a disagreement here. Absent for n=18's reason.

desc: translate: the RefSeq transcript translates to the SAME 353-residue protein as the Ensembl one at n=20 -- which is why the file stores the peptide in $prot_seq at :124 and reuses it rather than pasting it twice
rationale: The strongest cross-annotation row in the file: identical peptide from two files that share nothing but the reference FASTA and the locus, so it pins the whole chain -- record parse, parent/child tree, exon assembly, CDS splice, translation -- as being independent of the input vocabulary. Absent for n=19/n=20's reason: there is no GFF-driven model to translate (gff 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd, control transcript 3040). Missing feature: as n=19.

desc: _create_transcripts - big fetch check biotype: the 500 kb RefSeq fetch yields 49 transcripts with RefSeq-vocabulary biotypes -- lncRNA and misc_RNA where the Ensembl fetch of n=21 says antisense, lincRNA, retained_intron and processed_transcript -- plus two rna144907/rna144908 ids for miRNAs that carry no accession
rationale: The row that exercises the biotype GUESSER, which n=21 never touches: a RefSeq GFF has no biotype/transcript_type/transcript_biotype attribute, so GFF.pm:304-320 onwards works one out from the record type and other attributes, and this 49-entry map is the specification of what it produces. The two rna##### stable ids also pin the _record_get_id fallback of n=13 firing for real. Absent for n=12/n=21's reason. Missing feature: biotype inference from a non-Ensembl GFF.

desc: check buffer next: the first next() on the buffer built for the RefSeq annotation returns an arrayref
rationale: The same reftype probe as n=34, re-run because a fresh parser and buffer were built at :454-459 for the RefSeq source. An empty arrayref satisfies it, so it says nothing about what was read; the content is n=57, which is no-feature. Identical reading at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=10.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - display_consequence: the same 21:25585733 C>T variant annotated through the RefSeq GFF source also reports missense_variant -- the end-to-end row for the RefSeq half, and the twin of n=35
rationale: Not n=35 repeated: the two sources disagree about transcript ids, biotype vocabulary and gene identifiers (n=49-55), and this row pins that they nevertheless agree about the CONSEQUENCE, which is the property a user swapping --gff files cares about. Refused as an analogue for n=35's reason and by the same measurement (annotate_InputBuffer 0, gff 0 at dfbf 391f94bd; controls most_severe 58, transcript 3040). Missing feature: GFF-driven annotation.

desc: dont_skip variants which are not in GFF file: a full Runner->run with gff and dont_skip writes exactly ONE output line matching SEQ_21 -- a variant on a contig the GFF does not contain is reported rather than dropped
rationale: The only assertion in the file that drives a whole Runner rather than a source object, and it pins an output-COMPLETENESS policy: without --dont_skip the second input line would vanish from the output entirely, so the row is about what happens to input that cannot be annotated. Two absent things, measured separately. --gff as a run option: gff scores 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd and 0 in vepyr src/ at 346b9173. --dont_skip: 0 at both pins. The vepyr option-name probe git grep -cniE for custom|gff|gtf|bigwig|dont_skip over src/ at 346b9173 returns no files, against the positive control plugin_cache_root|fasta|regulatory which returns 3 (src/annotate.rs, src/lib.rs, src/vepyr/__init__.py). Missing features: the --gff run mode, and a switch for unannotatable-input policy.

desc: REFSEQ miRNA - load synonyms: the alias file loaded onto a THIRD source, built from the RefSeq GFF v2 fixture under offline => 0 with an explicit --fasta -- the precondition for n=60 and n=61
rationale: The third and last chromosome_synonyms row, and the only one whose source is configured for the miRNA-carrying v2 fixture: the runner at :490-496 sets offline => 0 and passes fasta explicitly, which is a different sequence-access route through BaseGXF.pm:105-106 than the other two sources take. Absent for n=39's reason and by the same measurement. Missing feature: as n=39.

desc: check buffer RefSeq: the first next() on the buffer built against the RefSeq GFF v2 runner returns an arrayref
rationale: The third instance of the reftype probe of n=34/n=56, on the buffer built at :514. Same argument: an empty arrayref satisfies it, the shape of a return is a compile-time fact in Rust, and the content is n=61. Identical reading at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=10 and ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=10.

desc: RefSeq GFF annotation: after annotating through the RefSeq GFF v2 source, the buffer's first entry is still there and true -- the smoke test for the miRNA-carrying v2 fixture, which the earlier RefSeq source (n=45-57) never touches
rationale: Read as a bare truthiness probe this would be plumbing, and docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2's corollary is what decides otherwise: a probe belongs to no-feature when the probe's SUBJECT is the absent feature, and the subject here is the RefSeq-v2 GFF annotation itself -- the line runs after $gff_refseq->annotate_InputBuffer and finish_annotation, so what it checks is that annotation left the variant in place rather than that a constructor returned something. Weak as an assertion (it would pass on an unannotated variant) but not empty: the v2 fixture exists to cover a RefSeq miRNA layout the v1 fixture lacks, and this is the file's only row over it. Absent for n=35's reason. Missing feature: GFF-driven annotation.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - gff_type gencode_promoter: a source built with gff_type => gencode_promoter takes the OTHER branch of GFF::annotate_InputBuffer and writes _custom_annotations GENCODE_PROMOTER => a single record named 21:25584733-25595733 with fields feature_id ENSR1_234, associated_gene ENSG00000123456 and type promoter_window -- custom-annotation output, not transcript consequences
rationale: The file's only assertion on the second gff_type, and it pins a dispatch rather than a value: GFF.pm:154-164 routes gff_type transcript into AnnotationType::Transcript::annotate_InputBuffer and gff_type gencode_promoter into AnnotationSource::File::annotate_InputBuffer -- the same custom-annotation path BED and VCF take -- with include_feature_types switched to a different set at GFF.pm:218-227. So ONE class serves two products depending on a construction parameter, and this is the only row that shows it. Three absences at dfbf 391f94bd, each 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/: gff_type, custom_annotations, annotate_InputBuffer; controls ProviderKind 7, plugin_cache_root 25. The per-source _custom_annotations map is the same structure ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=11 pins for BED. One near-miss deserves naming because the word matches: promoter scores 7 hits at the pin, and all of them are a regulatory-feature BIOTYPE read from the Ensembl regulatory build (transcript_consequence.rs:547, :13518) -- an annotation vepyr's own cache supplies, not a promoter-window GFF a user hands it. Missing feature: gff_type, and the custom-annotation output channel.

desc: use test: the AnnotationSource::File custom-source base class compiles and loads -- deliberately OUTSIDE the SKIP block, because the guard on line 36 reads that package's $CAN_USE_TABIX_PM variable and cannot until the package is compiled
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (in flight as old-repo issue #142 at the time of writing, whose diff this follows): a use_ok row is not-applicable UNCONDITIONALLY. The reason is not the usual compile-time one -- it is that no Rust design contains a run-time module-load assertion at all, so the statement has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. Nothing is hidden by keeping it out of the denominator: every row that asserts what a GTF source DOES stays in, and all 19 of them are no-feature. The byte-identical statement is n=1 of ledger/AnnotationSource_File.ledger.toml, ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml and ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml, read the same way.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the AnnotationSource::File::GTF reader subclass compiles and loads -- the first assertion inside the tabix-guarded SKIP block, and the only one that names the GTF reader class itself
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (in flight as old-repo issue #142 at the time of writing, whose diff this follows): a use_ok row is not-applicable UNCONDITIONALLY. The reason is not the usual compile-time one -- it is that no Rust design contains a run-time module-load assertion at all, so the statement has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. This is also the row R2's corollary covers. It sits inside a SKIP block whose whole purpose is a feature vepyr lacks, where docs/ledger-contract.md's older SKIP-block convention would keep a probe in the denominator; R2 narrows that convention to its general statement -- a probe is carried to no-feature when the probe's SUBJECT is the absent feature, and a use_ok's subject is Perl's loader, not the GTF reader. The sibling ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml (M2 issue #23) carries the same reading for the same statement over the GFF reader. Recorded rather than hidden: 10 use_ok rows in four Haplo_* ledgers are still no-feature under the pre-R2 reading, tracked at old-repo issue #141 -- two of them (n=2, n=3 of ledger/Haplo_AnnotationSource_File_GTF.ledger.toml) name this very class hierarchy.

desc: need to get a config object: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Runner module compiles and loads, so lines 47-50 can build the config object every source, parser and buffer below is handed
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (in flight as old-repo issue #142 at the time of writing, whose diff this follows): a use_ok row is not-applicable UNCONDITIONALLY. The reason is not the usual compile-time one -- it is that no Rust design contains a run-time module-load assertion at all, so the statement has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. Pure scaffolding: the Runner is borrowed only for its config, twice -- once at :47 for the chr21 half and once at :214 for the MT half. What a Runner actually resolves is the subject of t/Runner.t and belongs to ledger/Runner.ledger.toml (M2 issue #51). Same treatment at ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=24 (t/BaseVEP.t:113, the corpus's other classified use_ok on this same Runner class).

desc: get new runner object: Runner->new({base_testing_cfg, input_file => test.vcf}) returns a defined object -- the config carrier the GTF source, the VCF parser and the input buffer are all built against
rationale: A constructor-truthiness probe, and the plumbing arm of docs/ledger-contract.md's RULING on ok($obj). BaseRunner::new is two statements -- bless {}, $class (BaseRunner.pm:89) and $self->{_config} = Config->new(@_) (:92) -- so the return is a blessed empty hashref and is ALWAYS true; the line cannot fail except by Config->new dying first, which would be an exception rather than a false. vepyr's counterpart to the option hash is vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig, a plain struct built by infallible literal initialisation. Identical reading at ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=3 and ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=5. Note the SECOND runner at :214-215, built for the MT half, carries no assertion at all -- only this one does.

desc: new is defined: GTF->new({file => t/testdata/custom/test.gtf.gz, config}) returns an object -- a GTF custom annotation source built from a bgzipped, tabix-indexed GTF and the runner's config
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md's RULING on ok($obj) decides by what the class denotes, and Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::File::GTF denotes a capability vepyr does not have: a user's GTF registered as an annotation source, reached through --gtf or --custom. The constructor is load-bearing, not decoration -- BaseGXF::new refuses the source unless sequence is reachable (BaseGXF.pm:105-106), refuses the exact type (:109) and fixes cache_region_size at 1e6 (:117) -- and it produces the object rows 6-19 and 25-29 all work through. Note the GTF class is the SIMPLER of the two GXF readers: unlike GFF it has no gff_type parameter, so include_feature_types is unconditional (GTF.pm:116-118) and there is no gencode_promoter mode to construct. ledger/AnnotationSource_File.ledger.toml n=17 is the anchor: NONE of BED, GFF, GTF or VCF becomes a reader at the pin, and the only closed format vocabulary that exists, plugin_cache::source_manifest::ProviderKind {Vcf, Csv, Tsv, Parquet, Bed} (source_manifest.rs:23-29), names neither gff nor gtf and returns NotImplemented for both arms it does name (provider.rs:111; provider.rs:3 says VCF/BED (bio-formats) are not wired in the prototype). Measured at dfbf 391f94bd, per-pattern hit counts in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/: gtf 0, gff 0, annotate_InputBuffer 0; positive controls, same command shape: ProviderKind 7, plugin_cache_root 25, parquet 913. no-feature and not deferred/blocked-api: nothing here is one pub away, because the operation does not exist.

desc: setup fasta_db: the GTF source has a FASTA handle -- a GTF carries no sequence of its own, so BaseGXF::new refuses to construct without one and the translation rows below spend it
rationale: What the line pins is that a custom GXF source ACQUIRES sequence access, the precondition BaseGXF.pm:105-106 enforces (--fasta, or a non-offline cache, or a database). The near-miss is named here rather than left to be rediscovered: vepyr does open an indexed reference FASTA -- reference_fasta_path (vcf_sink.rs:406) feeds the reader built at annotate_provider.rs:3654 -- and ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=25 reads BaseVEP's own fasta_db through exactly that channel. It cannot be borrowed here: the subject is not that a FASTA opens but that a custom GXF SOURCE owns one, and there is no such source. Measured: fasta_db 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control fasta 63. Missing feature: the GXF source, not an accessor on it.

desc: _get_records_by_coords - count: the single-base query 21:25585733 yields 77 records, far more than literally overlap it, because the fetch re-scans outward whenever a returned feature overhangs the window
rationale: The count is a property of the algorithm, not of the fixture: _get_records_by_coords seeks (chr, start-1, end+1), tracks the min start and max end of the included records, then recurses with $no_rescan set to 1 or 2 so the expansion runs once in each direction (BaseGXF.pm:207-260, the two recursions at :252-257). It is also a cross-format check worth keeping distinct from the GFF twin: 77 here against 75 at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml n=9, over the same locus, because the two fixtures do not carry identical record sets. Nothing at the pin reads a tabix-indexed annotation file -- AnnotationBackend declares one variant, Parquet (annotation_store.rs:11-14) -- and gtf/gff score 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd against controls parquet 913 and transcript 3040. Missing feature: file-backed record retrieval.

desc: _get_records_by_coords - first content: the first record is the whole hash BaseGXF::_record_to_hash builds, in GTF's attribute vocabulary -- gene_id, transcript_id, exon_number, transcript_biotype, ccds_id, havana_* and a tag that is an ARRAYREF ['CCDS', 'basic'] rather than the comma-separated string a GFF3 would carry
rationale: Two things at once. First, _record_to_hash is format-agnostic: the same eight keys as the GFF twin (BaseGXF.pm:276-291), with phase carried as undef rather than dropped, and an md5 over the raw block (:281) that differs from the GFF record's for the same feature precisely because it hashes the FILE TEXT, not the biology. Second, the tag arrayref is the one shape difference the downstream code has to know about -- BaseGXF.pm:681-686 branches on ref($tr_record->{attributes}->{tag}) eq ARRAY exactly because gff tags are a comma-separated string and gtf tags are an arrayref -- so this row is the fixture-side witness for that branch. vepyr has neither the record shape nor the digest: md5, blake3 and xxhash each score 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd (the only hashing at the pin is cache key encoding in cache/key_encoding.rs), against control parquet 913. Missing feature: a parsed GTF record.

desc: _get_records_by_coords - non-overlapping sub-features count: 59 of those 77 records do NOT overlap the queried base -- the direct evidence that the outward rescan dragged in sibling exons of a parent that overhangs the window
rationale: This row, not n=8, is what pins the rescan: a fetch returning only literal overlaps would answer 0 here, and n=8 alone could not tell 77 overlapping records from 18 overlapping plus 59 pulled in. The comment at BaseGXF.pm:248-251 states the intent and :252-257 is the mechanism. Nothing at the pin has a parent/child record model whose siblings must be completed: lazy_load_transcript and annotate_InputBuffer each score 0 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd, control transcript 3040; vepyr's window planner reads whole cache partitions and never a tabix index. Missing feature: the sub-feature-completing rescan.

desc: _create_transcripts - count: the 77 records at 21:25585733 compile into exactly 4 transcripts -- the parent/child tree is built from GTF's TYPED id attributes, with no Parent attribute anywhere in the file
rationale: The structural difference from the GFF twin, and the reason the row is not redundant with it: GFF3 links a child to its parent through an explicit Parent attribute (GFF.pm:242-256), while GTF has none -- GTF::_record_get_parent_ids looks the record's type up in %PARENTS and reads the attribute that TYPE implies, $record->{attributes}->{$PARENTS{$type}.'_id'} (GTF.pm:133-141), so an exon's parent is its transcript_id and a transcript's is its gene_id. Same count, entirely different linkage. vepyr never builds transcripts from records: they arrive as parquet-cache rows hydrated into TranscriptFeature, with AnnotationBackend declaring Parquet as the only backend (annotation_store.rs:11-14). Measured at dfbf 391f94bd: lazy_load_transcript 0, gtf 0 hits, controls transcript 3040 and parquet 913. Missing feature: compiling a transcript model out of GTF records.

desc: stable_id: the first compiled transcript is ENST00000307301 -- from the transcript_id attribute, selected by the record's own type rather than by a fixed key name
rationale: GTF::_record_get_id is one line and it is type-keyed: $record->{attributes}->{$record->{type}.'_id'} || $record->{md5} (GTF.pm:156-159), so an exon record resolves through exon_id and a transcript record through transcript_id, with the record's md5 as the last resort. That is a different mechanism from the GFF twin's four-deep ID/Name/id/name precedence (GFF.pm:272-283), which is why ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml n=13 does not cover this row. vepyr reads transcript_id as a cache column and has no id-resolution rule, because it never sees an attribute list. Missing feature: identifier resolution from GTF attributes.

desc: _gene_stable_id: the transcript carries ENSG00000154719, taken from its own gene_id attribute -- the FIRST branch of _add_identifiers, which a GTF always satisfies
rationale: BaseGXF.pm:638 reads $tr_record->{attributes}->{gene_id} directly, and a GTF record always carries gene_id because that is how GTF encodes parentage at all (n=11). So this row pins that the GTF path never needs the Dbxref fallback (:642-648) or the parent-gene fallback (:651-658) that the RefSeq and Ensembl GFF halves of ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml n=50 and n=22 exercise. vepyr carries a Gene column in the cache and never derives one: gene_symbol scores 50 hits at dfbf 391f94bd and every one reads a cache-hydrated field, while gtf scores 0. Missing feature: gene identity derived from a GTF record's attributes.

desc: _gene_symbol: the transcript carries MRPL39, resolved from the GTF gene_name attribute -- the first of the two names tried on the transcript record
rationale: BaseGXF.pm:662-667 tries gene_name then gene on the transcript record, then Name/name on the gene record (:669-671). GTF spells it gene_name and so takes the first iteration, where a RefSeq GFF spells it gene and takes the second (ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml n=51): the loop exists because the three annotation vocabularies disagree, and this row is the GTF witness for it. vepyr's SYMBOL is a cache column populated by the cache builder, not resolved at annotate time. Same measurement as n=13. Missing feature: symbol resolution from a user file's attribute vocabulary.

desc: _protein: the transcript carries ENSP00000305682 -- the protein accession read off the CDS child record rather than off the transcript record itself
rationale: BaseGXF.pm:726 sets _protein from the protein id found while walking the CDS children, so the row pins that the transcript/protein link survives flattening a gene/transcript/exon/CDS record set into one transcript object -- and in GTF that walk depends on the typed parentage of n=11, since a CDS record names its transcript only through transcript_id. vepyr has an ENSP column in the cache (protein_id 7 hits in datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/ at dfbf 391f94bd) and no code that derives one, because there is no CDS record to walk: gtf 0 hits, control transcript 3040. Missing feature: protein identity assembled from GTF child records.

desc: count exons: the compiled transcript has 11 exons -- every exon child of the transcript record, which is only possible because the rescan of n=10 fetched the ten that lie outside the query window
rationale: The row that closes the loop on n=10: the queried base sits in one exon and the other ten are reachable only through the outward rescan, so this count is the end-to-end witness that record completion and transcript assembly agree. Exons are added under an eval (BaseGXF.pm:576) whose failure path this file, unlike its GFF sibling, never exercises. vepyr's exon structure comes from cache columns (exon_number 121 hits at dfbf 391f94bd) and is never assembled from records: gtf 0. Missing feature: exon assembly from GTF child records.

desc: translateable_seq: the CDS of ENST00000307301 spliced out of the reference FASTA -- 1062 bases pinned literally, and the proof that the fasta_db of n=6 was actually spent, since the GTF supplies coordinates only
rationale: A GTF has no sequence, so every base of this string came from the FASTA through coordinates the GTF supplied; the assertion therefore pins the JOIN of the two, including strand handling (the transcript is on -1) and exon order. The expected value is byte-identical to ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml n=19's, which is the cross-format check: two files with different linkage conventions must yield the same CDS. vepyr does splice a CDS and does hold a reference FASTA, but the coordinates come from the parquet cache, never from a user file, and the analogue cannot be claimed under docs/ledger-contract.md's dual-claim rule: a cache-driven splice test could not fail if GTF-driven model building regressed, because there is none (gtf 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd, control transcript 3040). Missing feature: transcript sequence assembled from a user's GTF plus a FASTA.

desc: translate: that CDS translates to the 353-residue MRPL39 protein -- the full round trip GTF coordinates -> FASTA sequence -> peptide, on chr21 and therefore on codon table 1
rationale: Not a duplicate of n=17: n=17 pins the nucleotide splice and this pins the translation on top of it. It is also the baseline n=28 and n=29 are the counterexample to -- here the chromosome is 21, so BaseGXF.pm:765 leaves codon_table at 1 and vepyr's own hard-coded standard table would agree; on MT it does not. Absent for n=17's reason: no GTF-driven model to translate. Missing feature: as n=17.

desc: _create_transcripts - big fetch check biotypes: a 500 kb fetch (21:25.5-26 Mb) compiles into 58 named transcripts with their biotypes -- including ENST00000419219_1, which upstream's own comment at :154 calls a fake transcript to test exons having 2 parents
rationale: The scale-and-fan-out row, and a cross-format identity: the 58-entry map is BYTE-IDENTICAL to ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml n=21's (verified by extracting both literals and comparing: 58 keys each, no key-only-in-one and no value difference), so what it pins is that the GTF and GFF3 readers agree on the entire window despite resolving parentage, ids and biotypes through different attributes. Biotype in GTF is transcript_biotype, then transcript_type, then biotype, then -- uniquely to this reader -- the record's SOURCE column (GTF.pm:176-182), a fallback the GFF reader does not have. And ENST00000419219_1 appears here too, so GTF's typed linkage (n=11) reaches a two-parent exon just as GFF3's comma-separated Parent list does, by splitting transcript_id on commas (GTF.pm:137). Absent for n=11's reason and by the same measurement. Missing feature: the record tree, including multi-parent children.

desc: TESTS WITH INPUT BUFFER: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF module compiles and loads, so a one-variant VCF can be read into a buffer for the annotation rows
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (in flight as old-repo issue #142 at the time of writing, whose diff this follows): a use_ok row is not-applicable UNCONDITIONALLY. The reason is not the usual compile-time one -- it is that no Rust design contains a run-time module-load assertion at all, so the statement has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, which is the contract's definition of not-applicable. VCF parsing behaviour itself is the subject of t/Parser_VCF.t and ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml (M2 issue #49); this line asserts none of it. Same treatment at ledger/AnnotationSource_File_BED.ledger.toml n=6.

desc: get parser object: Parser::VCF->new({config, a generated one-line VCF holding 21 25585733 rs142513484 C T, valid_chromosomes [21]}) returns a defined parser
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. An implementation that compared the raw start and end would report no hit here, so the insertion case needs its own witness. A reader that passed '.' through would satisfy n=13 and fail here, which is why the pair is two rows. Absent from vepyr on both counts: there is no custom source (n=11's measurement) and no score-collecting path whose missing-value handling could be compared - the plugin-cache track's only value handling is a strict cast of manifest-declared columns.

rationale: Pins run-time reconfiguration: VEP's Config stays mutable for the life of a run and param(key, value) both stores and returns (BaseVEP.pm:149). Read as `pick a different species', the property is one vepyr has -- but only where its Python surface carries a species: build_cache(..., species: str = "homo_sapiens") and _download_cache(species=...) (vepyr 346b9173, src/vepyr/__init__.py:384, :288) resolve and fetch the Ensembl tarball for whichever species is asked for. The observation point differs (vepyr picks the species when the cache is built, rather than mutating a live config), which would make this an analog-port -- but not from here: `grep -ric species src/` over datafusion-bio-function-vep 0.15.0 at dfbf 391f94bd is 0 (positive control: `chrom` = 1067) and vepyr is crate-type = ["cdylib"], so it is not linkable as a Rust dependency. Same blocker as rows 10 and 13; tracked in #77.

desc: param without key: calling $bv->param() with no key dies with /No param/
rationale: The error exists only because param dispatches on a string key supplied at run time (BaseVEP.pm:149). Rust configuration is field access -- cfg.buffer_size names the field at compile time -- and `no key given` is not expressible, so there is no run-time arity error for a test to observe.

desc: species get: the named $bv->species accessor returns 'homo_sapiens' by default
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay on the FORMATS crate, and the half that does not survive is named rather than dropped. datafusion-bio-function-vep has no species concept at all -- 0 occurrences across its src/ at the pin, positive control chrom = 1088 -- so the counterpart is one crate over: CacheInfo.species (datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache info.rs:51), parsed from the cache's own info.txt at :102. It was doubly unreachable, a pub(crate) struct inside a private mod info; re-measured in this checkout as error[E0603]: module `info` is private pointing at lib.rs:15, against four resolving positive controls in the same probe file. PINS.toml formats_test_overlay (8fd75f30) adds an opaque test_internals::CacheInfo whose species() is one field read. WHAT SURVIVES: asking vepyr for the species of the cache this corpus runs against returns exactly homo_sapiens, measured over the committed tests/data/vep115_native_slice/homo_sapiens/115_GRCh38/info.txt. WHAT DOES NOT: Perl pins a CONFIGURATION default -- Config->new() is built with no arguments at BaseVEP.t:51 -- and vepyr's Rust surface has no species option to default; that default exists only in vepyr's Python surface, build_cache(species = "homo_sapiens") at src/vepyr/__init__.py:384, and vepyr is crate-type = ["cdylib"] so no Rust test here can reach it. That is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. A separate rust_test from n=10 under the one-test-per-boundary rule: n=10 is the generic string-keyed lookup and carries the defaulting question, this row is the NAMED accessor and carries the accessor-is-a-reader question -- a second cache declaring mus_musculus must come back as mus_musculus. Third assertion is a disclosure, not a claimed match: Perl's named accessor lower-cases and normalises (BaseVEP.pm:222) and vepyr returns the declared string verbatim, so a cache declaring Homo_Sapiens comes back as Homo_Sapiens. No row asserts the normalisation (n=14, the setter that would show it, has no counterpart at any visibility). Mutation-checked: expecting homo_sapiens from the mus_musculus cache fails with left: "mus_musculus" / right: "homo_sapiens".

desc: species set: $bv->species('human') sets the species and returns the new value
rationale: The named-accessor form of row 11 (BaseVEP.pm:222), which also normalises the value. vepyr does select a species -- vepyr.build_cache(species=...) at src/vepyr/__init__.py:384 -- so this is not a feature vepyr lacks; it is a feature no Rust item in the pinned dependency exposes, because the choice is made at cache-build time from Python and the annotation crate has no species at all (0 occurrences at dfbf 391f94bd; positive control `chrom` = 1067). A behaviour only vepyr's Python surface can reach is blocked-api by docs/ledger-contract.md; tracked in #77.

desc: stats: $bv->stats lazily builds a Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Stats holding empty counters, no_stats => undef and a back-reference to the Config
rationale: VEP's per-run statistics subsystem (Stats.pm; the --stats_file / --no_stats summary) does not exist in vepyr: `grep -ric stats_file` over dfbf 0.15.0's datafusion/bio-function-vep/src is 0 (positive control: `chrom` = 1067) and nothing accumulates per-run counters. The Stats port is tracked separately as issue #52. Until the feature is built there is no lazily-constructed object, no counter map and no config back-reference to compare against.

desc: get_adaptor - offline: with offline=1 and database=0, get_adaptor('variation','VariationFeature') still returns a VariationFeatureAdaptor built by new_fake
rationale: The Perl-API adaptor factory (BaseVEP.pm:340) plus its offline fallback _get_fake_adaptor (BaseVEP.pm:379), which fabricates a Bio::EnsEMBL::Variation::DBSQL::VariationFeatureAdaptor via new_fake so downstream code still has an object to call. vepyr has no adaptor layer: cache access is a DataFusion TableProvider registered on a SessionContext (annotate_provider.rs @ 391f94bd), selected by cache path, never by a (group, type) string pair. The absent feature is the Ensembl object-adaptor API, and vepyr is cache-only by design.

desc: get_adaptor no group: calling get_adaptor() with no adaptor group dies with /No adaptor group specified/
rationale: An argument guard inside the adaptor factory that row 16 shows vepyr does not have (BaseVEP.pm:340). With no get_adaptor there is no call to make and no error to raise. Recording this as not-applicable would quietly drop the fact that a whole VEP subsystem is missing, so it stays in the denominator as an absent feature.

desc: get_adaptor no type: calling get_adaptor('core') without an adaptor type dies with /No adaptor type specified/
rationale: The second arity guard of the same absent factory (BaseVEP.pm:340). See row 16: vepyr resolves cache readers by path through DataFusion table providers, so neither the group nor the type argument exists to be omitted.

desc: add_shortcuts: add_shortcuts('test') copies the Config value for 'test' into $bv->{test}
rationale: add_shortcuts (BaseVEP.pm:755) is a Perl-runtime speed hack: it caches selected config values in the object's own hash so later reads skip the param -> Config -> AUTOLOAD chain. A Rust struct field read is already a compile-time offset; there is no dispatch chain to short-circuit and no per-object hash to populate, so the construct has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design.

desc: add_shortcuts arrayref: add_shortcuts(['test']) accepts the arrayref calling form and copies the same value
rationale: The same Perl-runtime cache as row 19, exercised through its scalar-or-arrayref argument idiom (BaseVEP.pm:755). What it pins is Perl's calling convention, not VEP's behaviour; Rust's equivalent overloads are resolved by the type system at compile time.

desc: add_shortcuts overwrite: a second add_shortcuts('test') on the same object dies with /add_shortcuts would overwrite value/
rationale: The invariant belongs to the shortcut cache itself -- a key already present must not be silently replaced (BaseVEP.pm:755). With no shortcut cache in vepyr (row 19) the invariant has nothing to protect. Perl-runtime plumbing, not a VEP behaviour.

desc: fasta_db - no file: $bv->fasta_db returns undef when no FASTA is configured
rationale: The negative branch of the FASTA accessor (BaseVEP.pm:488). vepyr has no accessor to return undef from -- the alias `FastaReader` is private (dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_provider.rs:8901`) and the reader never leaves the provider -- so the analogue reads the same state off the run, which is why this is analog and not unit. The sharp form of `undef` here is that nothing is opened at all: `validate_hgvs_reference_fasta` returns Ok before it touches the path when no HGVS flag is set (`:3641-3643`), so three runs of the same record -- `reference_fasta_path` None, a path that does not exist, and the real committed slice -- produce the SAME BYTES. A configured-but-unopened FASTA is indistinguishable from an absent one downstream, which is what `fasta_db` being undef means; and the middle arm is what makes the equality load-bearing, since an eagerly built reader would fail there. The test also asserts the record really was annotated (`missense_variant` on ENST00000352957) and that HGVSc is empty, so the equality is not an equality of nothing. Was `deferred`/`blocked-data` under issue 77 -- which said in as many words that the analogue was writable in API terms and blocked only by the absent Parquet cache -- until `tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/` and `tests/data/vep115_reference_slice/` landed (issue 96). It does not claim the refusal a missing path produces when HGVS IS on: that is Config.ledger.toml n=32, a different property at a different boundary.

desc: get_slice - no fasta_db or database: get_slice('1') returns undef when there is neither a slice adaptor nor a FASTA
rationale: RE-MEASURED AT THE OVERLAY PIN; still deferred, with a corrected reason. The test-internals overlay exposes read_reference_sequence (annotate_provider.rs:8149, delegated at :17648), which docs/campaigns/2026-08-28-final-deferred-v3/unlock-map.md section 2 named as this row's unblock while already noting the arm has no counterpart. Confirmed by reading the exposed signature, not inferred: it takes reader: &mut fasta::io::indexed_reader::IndexedReader<R> -- NON-OPTIONAL, at both the base :8150 and the overlay :17649 -- so no argument of it can express 'there is no source'. Nothing else returns a slice or a reader either: over the whole pinned vep crate src/, `grep 'pub fn' | grep -i slice` = 0 hits and `grep 'pub fn' | grep -i fasta` = 0 hits, against the positive controls of 276 pub fn in that tree and 39 mentions of fasta across five files (vcf_sink.rs, colocated.rs, annotate_provider.rs, transcript_consequence.rs, hgvs.rs). So the blocker is not a missing pub and blocked-api was the wrong label after the overlay: vepyr has no get_slice abstraction at all, which is deferred/blocked-engine. no-feature is the defensible alternative and this row does NOT claim to settle it -- it is left to the reviewer, because moving it would also require choosing a feature_area and changing the missing-feature map. n=23 specifically: the BOTH-ARMS-FAIL branch of get_slice (BaseVEP.pm:409) -- no Slice adaptor and no fasta_db, so no Slice is built and undef is cached and returned. vepyr's nearest observable for 'no FASTA configured' is not an undef slice but a refusal, and that refusal is already pinned elsewhere and must not be double-claimed here: tests/port_base_vep_reference_fasta.rs covers n=22 (nothing is opened at all when no HGVS flag is set) and ledger/Runner.ledger.toml n=71 covers the named error. What is still missing is an operation that can be ASKED for a slice and answer 'none'.

desc: use_ok Runner: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Runner module compiles and loads
