rationale: A third module-load probe, needed here only because the next assertions borrow a Runner to build a fully-populated config with a real FASTA. Module resolution is a compile-time fact in Rust (rows 1 and 6), so nothing about VEP behaviour is pinned.

desc: fasta_db: with a FASTA configured, $bv->fasta_db is a Bio::DB::HTS::Faidx or Bio::DB::Fasta handle
rationale: The positive branch, and the Perl `ok(A || B)` shows what it pins: either backend is acceptable, so the assertion is about the FACT of the open, not the class. vepyr has one backend and does not hand the handle back, so the open is read off the run -- with HGVS requested and the committed indexed slice configured, `annotate_to_vcf` gets past `fasta::io::indexed_reader::Builder::default().build_from_path` (dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_provider.rs:3654`) and writes `ENST00000352957.9:c.991G>A`. The discriminator that makes this an assertion about the open rather than about the path is the other arm: a structurally valid FASTA with no `.fai` is a real file at a real path, so it clears the existence check at `:3648-3652` and fails at the builder with `annotate_vep(): failed to open indexed reference FASTA '<path>'`. Deliberately NOT claimed: that the reference was read. Issue 96's chain measured that HGVSc for a SNV is spelled from the transcript shard's cached cdna_seq and that an all-N reference gives the same answer; only a shifted indel reads bases, and `tests/annotate_end_to_end_smoke.rs` is where that is exercised. The Perl assertion is about the handle, so the open is the right boundary. Was `deferred`/`blocked-data` under issue 77 until the micro-cache and reference slice landed (issue 96).

desc: chr lengths: $bv->chr_lengths derives {21 => 46709983, MT => 16569} from the FASTA index
rationale: RECLASSIFIED 2026-08-30, `deferred`/`blocked-api` -> `no-feature`, and CORRECTED IN REVIEW the same day. The verdict stands; the argument for it did not, and the correction is recorded rather than quietly swapped. THE ABSOLUTE WAS FALSE: an earlier draft of this rationale said the id->length map has no counterpart at ANY visibility and that dfbf never holds one. It does hold one. `AnnotationWorkerState` (annotate_provider.rs:9374) carries `hgvs_reader: Option<FastaReader>` (:9381), `FastaReader` is `fasta::io::indexed_reader::IndexedReader<fasta::io::BufReader<File>>` (:8901), and noodles-fasta 0.49.0 makes the index readable from any reader one holds -- `pub fn index(&self) -> &fai::Index` (io/indexed_reader.rs:58). So a `fai::Index`, carrying exactly the id->length records this row asserts, is live inside the pin at annotation time. THE VERDICT SURVIVES THAT COUNTEREXAMPLE for two measured reasons, both about the OPERATION rather than the visibility. FIRST, THE CRATE NEVER ASKS: `grep -rn '\.index()' src/` returns 0 across all 58 files of the ANNOTATOR CRATE -- nothing in datafusion/bio-function-vep reads the index's records, ever. That scope is the measurement's, and the sentence below is now held to it. Every use of a reader is the same single operation, fetching the bases of one named region: `read_reference_sequence` at annotate_provider.rs:8149, colocated.rs:206 and hgvs.rs:1180, each calling `reader.query(&region)` at :8180, :216 and :1190. Enumerating the sequences, or asking any one of them its length, is not an operation `bio-function-vep` performs. NARROWED 2026-08-31: that sentence read "anywhere" until the partition-3 feature re-audit, and "anywhere" was wider than the probe -- the same negation-wider-than-the-measurement defect corrected in #403 and #404. One crate away a contig->length map DOES exist: `VcfTableProvider` carries `contig_names: Vec<String>` and `contig_lengths: Vec<u64>` -- the latter commented `Contig lengths from the file header (for balanced partitioning)` -- at datafusion-bio-format-vcf table_provider.rs:512-515 @ tag v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8, built at :888 and read at :1333 and :1340 by `estimate_region_sizes` / `estimate_sizes_from_tbi` to feed `balance_partitions`. It leaves the verdict untouched on three counts. Its SOURCE is the input VCF's own `##contig` lines, not the reference FASTA index this row asserts -- lengths absent from the header default to 0. Its PURPOSE is splitting a scan, not describing a reference. And it is a private field of another crate, so nothing hands it back. The FASTA-index measurement itself is unchanged and was re-derived independently: `.index()` = 0 over the same 58 files, with positive controls issued in the same invocation -- `.query(` 5, `IndexedReader` 11, `noodles_fasta` 8, `read_reference_sequence` 14. At dfbf master 3a3fca3 (the rev vepyr 0.4.0 ships) the count is 1 and it is still not the fai: `plugin_cache/provider.rs:57` calls `.index()` on a TABIX index and asks it for `reference_sequence_names()` -- contig names, not lengths. SECOND, A `pub` WOULD HAND AN EXTERNAL CRATE NOTHING: `struct AnnotationWorkerState` (:9374) carries no `pub`; `hgvs_reader` appears 8 times in the crate and 0 of those is a public accessor or a return (`grep -rn 'pub .*hgvs_reader\|fn hgvs_reader' src/` -> 0); and no public function anywhere returns such a reader (`grep -rnE 'pub (fn|async fn).*->.*(FastaReader|IndexedReader)' src/` -> 0). The struct is constructed only inside the per-partition execute path -- `spawn_annotation_from_lookup_sharded` (:10574, inside a `tokio::spawn`), `annotate_window_owned` (:12040), and `Stream::poll_next` (:12317) -- so an outside caller never holds one to call `.index()` on, and publishing the field would expose state nobody can reach. What is missing is therefore the OPERATION `name and expose a contig->length map`, not the visibility of state vepyr already computes, which is the line docs/ledger-contract.md draws in `Absent operation vs present-but-private state`: an operation vepyr does not perform is `no-feature` however easy it would be to add, while state it holds behind an item an external crate cannot name is `blocked-api`. WHY THIS DIFFERS FROM n=23 AND n=27, the rows of this same file that stay `blocked-api`: there dfbf PERFORMS the operation the Perl asserts -- `read_reference_sequence` exists and runs at the three call sites above, which is get_slice's work -- so a thin `pub` accessor over work the crate already does would let a test drive it, and #77 can deliver exactly that. Here there is no operation to put an accessor on: a wrapper would have to read the index for the first time, which is new code and not a widening. THE VOCABULARY PROBE STANDS, now read as the record that the crate NAMES no such map rather than that the data is unreachable: `grep -ric chr_length` = 0 (the same form and the same 0 the earlier rationale reported), `grep -rn 'fasta::fai'` = 0, `grep -rnE '\bfai\b'` = 0, `grep -rnE 'fai::(Index|Record|read)'` = 0, and chr_lengths / chrom_length / contig_length / seq_region_length / reference_length / chromosome_length = 0 each. The one near-miss is `sequence_length` = 3, and it is not one: all three are a local variable for a MOTIF's own sequence length (motif_matrix.rs:190, :197, :198). `grep -rn '\.fai'` returns 3 and all three are the substring inside `failed` (vcf_sink.rs:587, cache/lookup_exec.rs:1159, :1218). POSITIVE CONTROLS that the greps discriminate rather than failing for a path or build reason, over the same 58 files: `chrom` (grep -ric) = 1067, `pub fn` = 237, `noodles_fasta` = 8, `IndexedReader` = 10 -- which is precisely why the counterexample above had to be answered rather than ignored. The nearest chromosome-keyed public structure is `cache::manifest::ChromDatasetEntry { chrom, dataset, rows }` (cache/manifest.rs:11), and it carries cache ROW COUNTS, not reference lengths. `feature_area` `cache-and-reference-discovery`, whose inclusion rule is `The assertion resolves, scans for, or reads the declared contents of a cache directory or a reference directory`: the FAI is the reference directory's declared inventory of what sequences exist and how long they are, and reading it is discovery rather than sequence access. Consistent with n=31 and n=32, this file's other two reference-directory rows, which already carry that area. Off #77 accordingly: that issue collects the exports this file waits on, and this row is no longer one of them.

desc: get_slice - fasta_db: a contig absent from the FASTA yields a fake Bio::EnsEMBL::Slice (is_fake => 1, start/end/seq_region_length = 1) inside a rank-1 chromosome CoordSystem
rationale: RE-MEASURED AT THE OVERLAY PIN; still deferred, with a corrected reason. The test-internals overlay exposes read_reference_sequence (annotate_provider.rs:8149, delegated at :17648), which docs/campaigns/2026-08-28-final-deferred-v3/unlock-map.md section 2 named as this row's unblock while already noting the arm has no counterpart. Confirmed by reading the exposed signature, not inferred: it takes reader: &mut fasta::io::indexed_reader::IndexedReader<R> -- NON-OPTIONAL, at both the base :8150 and the overlay :17649 -- so no argument of it can express 'there is no source'. Nothing else returns a slice or a reader either: over the whole pinned vep crate src/, `grep 'pub fn' | grep -i slice` = 0 hits and `grep 'pub fn' | grep -i fasta` = 0 hits, against the positive controls of 276 pub fn in that tree and 39 mentions of fasta across five files (vcf_sink.rs, colocated.rs, annotate_provider.rs, transcript_consequence.rs, hgvs.rs). So the blocker is not a missing pub and blocked-api was the wrong label after the overlay: vepyr has no get_slice abstraction at all, which is deferred/blocked-engine. no-feature is the defensible alternative and this row does NOT claim to settle it -- it is left to the reviewer, because moving it would also require choosing a feature_area and changing the missing-feature map. n=27 specifically, and this row now carries a MEASURED DIVERGENCE that a reviewer must adjudicate before it can move again. With a fasta_db present but the contig missing from it, Perl does not return undef: $fasta_db->length('1') is false, the length falls back to 1, and a Bio::EnsEMBL::Slice with is_fake => 1 and seq_region_length => 1 is fabricated so downstream defined($slice) checks still pass (BaseVEP.pm:409-441). vepyr, asked the same question through the now-exposed reader over the committed tests/data/vep115_reference_slice/21.fa.gz, ERRORS instead: read_reference_sequence(reader, "1", 1, 1) returns Err(Execution("annotate_vep(): failed querying FASTA for 1:1-1: invalid reference sequence name: 1")), and the same for "chr1". Positive control in the same run: read_reference_sequence(reader, "21", 25585733, 25585735) returns Ok("CTT"), so the reader is open and working and the Err is about the contig. This row's previous rationale PREDICTED exactly this outcome and called for `failed'. It is deliberately NOT set to failed here: `failed' requires an issue naming the discrepancy, no open issue covers it (#77 is an extraction request, not a divergence tracker), and unlock-map section 7 records that filing a divergence tracker is a decision for a human rather than something a porting worker settles. The measurement is recorded so that decision can be taken on evidence.

desc: chromosome_syonyms - empty: with no synonyms file loaded, $bv->chromosome_synonyms is an empty hash
rationale: VEP's user-supplied chromosome-synonyms file (--synonyms, loaded by BaseVEP.pm:637 into {canonical => {synonym => 1}}) has no counterpart in vepyr. What dfbf 0.15.0 has instead is a stateless pure function: pub fn contig_alias_set(chrom) -> HashSet<String> (cache/manifest.rs:121), reachable from this crate as datafusion_bio_function_vep::cache::manifest::contig_alias_set -- the same path tests/_quarantine/port_cache_layout.rs:37 already compiles against -- and asserted upstream by contig_alias_set_covers_mito_and_chr_prefix (cache/manifest.rs:251). It derives the chr-prefix add/strip pair plus the M/MT/chrM/chrMT set from the name itself, so there is no map to load and `empty before a file is read' has no counterpart: the function is never empty, always containing at least the spelling it was given. The absent feature is file-driven aliasing. The single non-`synonymous' match for `synonym' in the crate is the cache column var_synonyms (cache/schema.rs:67), which holds variant, not chromosome, synonyms.

desc: chromosome_syonyms - ref: passing a synonyms file to chromosome_synonyms() returns the loaded map
rationale: Pins that the loader is also the getter: called with a path it parses the file and returns the resulting map (BaseVEP.pm:637, reading it via _fetch_chr_synonyms at :596). vepyr has no synonyms loader to call (row 28), so there is no return value to probe. Kept as a feature gap rather than a Perl artefact because what is absent is the --synonyms capability, not the ref() idiom the assertion happens to use.

desc: chromosome_syonyms - content check: the loaded map records CM000683.2, NC_000021.9 and chr21 as synonyms of chromosome 21
rationale: The substance of the synonyms feature: an INSDC accession (CM000683.2), a RefSeq accession (NC_000021.9) and a UCSC-style name (chr21) must all resolve to Ensembl's `21', so a VCF written against any of them can be annotated. Exactly one of the three is covered in vepyr, and by a public function: contig_alias_set("chr21") contains "21" (cache/manifest.rs:121, asserted upstream at :251 as assert!(contig_alias_set("chr1").contains("1"))). The other two thirds are unreachable at dfbf 391f94bd -- an accession cannot be derived from the name, only read from a file, and there is no loader (row 28). VEP reaches that same third without the file too, via the add/remove-chr transform in get_source_chr_name (BaseVEP.pm:689), so the accession aliases are the whole of the gap. Porting this needs the loader named in row 28 to be built first.

desc: fasta_dir - fasta_db OK: pointing the run at a directory (fasta_dir) is enough for fasta_db to open a handle
rationale: VEP's --fasta_dir auto-detection: the Runner scans the directory and sets fasta to the single FASTA it finds, so the user never names the file. `fasta_dir` occurs 0 times in dfbf 0.15.0's vep crate (positive control: `fasta` 63) and 0 times in vepyr 346b9173; vepyr's Python surface takes reference_fasta: str | None -- an explicit file path (src/vepyr/__init__.py:707). The missing feature is directory auto-detection, not a hidden accessor.

desc: fasta_dir - fasta param set: auto-detection writes the resolved path back into the config as param('fasta') = <fasta_dir>/Homo_sapiens.GRCh38.toplevel.test.fa
rationale: The side effect of row 31's feature: the resolved file name is stored back on the Config so every later reader sees a path rather than a directory. With no fasta_dir option in vepyr there is nothing to resolve and nothing to write back -- and AnnotateVcfConfig is construct-once (vcf_sink.rs:381), so even the write-back half has no counterpart.

desc: status_msg: $bv->status_msg('Hello') writes the message to STDOUT
rationale: VEP's per-run progress channel: status_msg (BaseVEP.pm:780) prints to STDOUT unless --quiet is set. dfbf 0.15.0 has neither the channel nor the switch -- `grep -ric quiet` over its vep crate src is 0 -- and its 6 info!(...) call sites go through the `log` facade, whose sink belongs to the embedding process rather than to a config option. The missing feature is a configurable run-status output; capturing a log record in a test would observe the caller's subscriber, not vepyr.

desc: warning_fh: configuring warning_file opens a FileHandle that every warning is written through
rationale: VEP's --warning_file sidecar: warning_fh (BaseVEP.pm:878) opens the configured file once and hands the same handle to every warning. `warning_file` occurs 0 times in dfbf 0.15.0's vep crate and 0 times in vepyr 346b9173 (positive controls: `fasta` 63 and 15 respectively). vepyr emits a single warn!(...) through `log`, with no per-run destination to open. The absent feature is the warnings sidecar file itself.

desc: warning_msg: $bv->warning_msg('test warning message') writes through warning_fh and returns true
rationale: The write half of the sidecar feature (BaseVEP.pm:802). vepyr has no warnings destination to write to (row 34) and no per-message return contract -- log::warn! evaluates to (). Until a warnings sidecar exists there is no code path here that can succeed or fail.

desc: warning_msg in file: the first line of the warning file is exactly 'WARNING: test warning message'
rationale: This is the sidecar's file format -- the literal `WARNING: ` prefix, one message per line -- which downstream tooling and VEP's own tests parse. dfbf produces no such file at all (rows 34, 35); a `log` record carries a level rather than a prefix, and its layout is chosen by whoever installs the logger. The gap is the product decision to write a machine-readable warnings file, which vepyr has not made.

desc: warning_msg to STDERR: with warning_file => 'STDERR' the same call writes to STDERR instead of a file
rationale: The routing half of the feature: warning_file accepts the literal string STDERR to send warnings to the terminal (BaseVEP.pm:878). vepyr has no warning_file option to give either value to. That a logger installed by the caller usually defaults to stderr is a property of the embedding process, not a vepyr behaviour, so it is not the same property observed through another channel.

desc: get_database_assembly - no DB: with no database connection, get_database_assembly returns undef
rationale: get_database_assembly (BaseVEP.pm:457) reads the assembly out of a core database's meta table. vepyr is cache-only -- docs/ledger-contract.md's standing no-feature example -- with no DBI dependency and no registry, so the accessor has no counterpart; asserting `undef because there is no database` would assert vepyr's permanent state rather than a behaviour it computes.

desc: skipped_variant_msg - warning about invalid variant: skipped_variant_msg('Invalid variant', 3) sends the description through the warning channel
rationale: skipped_variant_msg (BaseVEP.pm:840) formats `WARNING: line 3 skipped Invalid variant` through warning_fh and pushes a record onto the run's skipped-variants list. vepyr has neither: its invalid-input path logs and continues, and `grep -rn skipped` over dfbf 0.15.0's vep crate finds only unrelated uses (cache_builder.rs:139, `skipped (no source files)`, plus comments). The missing feature is VEP's skipped-variants reporting, which 116.0 also writes to --skipped_variants_file.

desc: skipped_variant_msg - description: the recorded entry keeps the caller's description text
rationale: Pins the first field of the {line, line_number, description} record that skipped_variants accumulates (BaseVEP.pm:193, :840). With no accumulator in vepyr (row 39) there is no entry to read back; the gap is the record itself, not the regex the Perl matches it with.

desc: skipped_variant_msg - line number: the recorded entry keeps the input line number (3) it was called with
rationale: The provenance field of the same absent record: which input line was dropped, so a user can find it in the source VCF. vepyr's skip path emits no structured record and keeps no line index once a record has been parsed, so nothing carries the number.

desc: skipped_variant_msg - line content: the entry's 'line' field is undef when no parser is attached, so no input text is captured
rationale: Pins the conditional third field: line is filled from $self->{parser}->{current_block} only when a parser is attached, and here there is none (BaseVEP.pm:840). The whole record is absent from vepyr (rows 39-41), so its optional field is absent with it.

desc: db - registry: with database => 1 and DB credentials, $bv->registry returns a loaded Bio::EnsEMBL::Registry (SKIP block: runs only with a local test database)
rationale: The first of the 8 assertions VEP skips unless a local Ensembl test database is configured (`skip 'No local database configured', 8`, t/BaseVEP.t:277). registry (BaseVEP.pm:250) loads the Ensembl registry from credentials. vepyr is cache-only: no DBI, no registry, no live server -- docs/ledger-contract.md's standing example of a feature that must be built before it can be ported.

desc: get_adaptor slice: in database mode get_adaptor('core','slice') returns a Bio::EnsEMBL::DBSQL::SliceAdaptor (SKIP block)
rationale: The database arm of row 16's adaptor factory, returning a real DB-backed adaptor instead of a fake one (BaseVEP.pm:340). Both halves -- the factory and the database connection -- are absent from vepyr, which reaches cache data through DataFusion table providers over Parquet.

desc: db - registry from registry file: a registry file path given as `registry` also produces a loaded registry (SKIP block)
rationale: The second way VEP can be pointed at databases: an Ensembl registry configuration file instead of inline credentials (BaseVEP.pm:250). vepyr has no registry loader of either kind; its only data-source argument is a cache directory (vepyr.annotate(vcf, cache_dir, ...), src/vepyr/__init__.py:694).

desc: get_adaptor slice - registry file: adaptors resolved through the registry-file route are the same SliceAdaptor class (SKIP block)
rationale: Pins that the two registry-loading routes converge on the same adaptor class. With neither route and no adaptor layer in vepyr (rows 44, 45), there is nothing to converge and no class to compare.

desc: get_slice - database: with a database connection get_slice('21') returns a real Bio::EnsEMBL::Slice from the slice adaptor (SKIP block)
rationale: The first arm of get_slice (BaseVEP.pm:409), which prefers a DB slice adaptor and only falls back to the FASTA when there is none. vepyr has no database mode, so this arm cannot exist; the FASTA arm is what rows 23 and 27 account for.

desc: get_database_assembly: connected to a homo_vepiens core database, get_database_assembly returns 'GRCh38' (SKIP block)
rationale: The positive branch of row 38's accessor: the assembly name is read from the core database's meta table so VEP can refuse a mismatched cache. vepyr takes its assembly from the cache it was handed (build_cache(..., assembly = "GRCh38"), src/vepyr/__init__.py:385) and has no database to interrogate.

desc: get_adaptor - species with no var db gets fake: for mus_muscuvep, get_adaptor('variation','VariationFeature') falls back to a fake VariationFeatureAdaptor carrying only species => 'mus_muscuvep' (SKIP block)
rationale: A multi-species policy: when the requested species has no variation database, VEP fabricates a fake VariationFeature adaptor so downstream calls degrade to no-ops instead of dying (BaseVEP.pm:340, :379). vepyr has neither the species dimension (rows 11, 14) nor the adaptor layer (row 16), so there is no policy to exercise and no blessed fake to compare against.

desc: get_adaptor - species with no var db no fake available: get_adaptor('variation','Variation') returns undef, because only VariationFeature has a fake implementation (SKIP block)
rationale: Pins the limit of row 49's policy: _get_fake_adaptor (BaseVEP.pm:379) knows how to fabricate a VariationFeature adaptor and nothing else, so every other variation type is undef even in the same run. The distinction lives entirely inside the adaptor factory vepyr does not have.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the CacheDir class loads under `use`
rationale: A module-load probe: `use_ok` asserts only that Perl found and compiled `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::CacheDir` at runtime. Rust answers the same question at link time — `tests/port_cache_dir.rs` cannot build unless `datafusion_bio_format_ensembl_cache::{EnsemblCacheOptions, TranscriptTableProvider}` exist at the pin — so a runtime assertion here would restate the linker. Same family as the `can_ok`/`isa_ok` existence probes docs/ledger-contract.md names as legitimately not-applicable.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config class loads under `use` before a config object is built
rationale: The second module-load probe, for `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config`. vepyr splits that one class in two — `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` for run options and `EnsemblCacheOptions` for cache identity — and the test crate proves both exist by compiling against them. There is no runtime load step that could fail. See n=1.

desc: BASIC TESTS: Config->new returns a defined object for the base testing config
rationale: A constructor-truthiness probe: it asserts `Config->new` returned something other than `undef`. `EnsemblCacheOptions::new` (table_provider.rs:86) and `AnnotateVcfConfig::default()` are infallible struct constructors that cannot yield a null, so the Rust type system carries at compile time exactly what this line checks at runtime. Perl-runtime plumbing, per docs/ledger-contract.md's not-applicable list; the same reading was accepted for AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.t n=3.

desc: BASIC TESTS: CacheDir->new({config, root_dir}) resolves and accepts the v84 test cache
rationale: Not a bare truthiness probe: `new` calls `init` (CacheDir.pm:113) whose first statement is `my $dir = $self->dir` (CacheDir.pm:221), so this line asserts that directory resolution succeeded for the base testing config. vepyr has no CacheDir object; the constructor that consumes a cache directory is `TranscriptTableProvider::new(EnsemblCacheOptions{..})`, and the defined/undef distinction becomes `Ok`/`Err` — a different channel, hence analog-port. The named test rebuilds ensembl-vep's own `homo_sapiens/84_GRCh38` layout in a tempdir, constructs the provider and asserts it resolved the three chromosome directories. It is also the positive control for n=12, n=13 and n=14, whose negative arms use the same fixture.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the constructed object is blessed into Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::CacheDir
rationale: A blessing probe — `ref()` on a Perl object returns the package it was blessed into. Rust has no runtime class tag to read: `TranscriptTableProvider::new` returns `Result<TranscriptTableProvider>` and a value of any other type would not compile. docs/ledger-contract.md names assertions about blessing and Perl object identity as the not-applicable case.

desc: auto-detection: a chr_synonyms.txt sitting in the cache directory becomes the `synonyms` param
rationale: vepyr has no chromosome-synonyms feature to auto-detect into. Measured at the pin: `grep -rniE 'chr_synonym|chromosome_synonym|chromosome synonym|synonym_file' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src datafusion/bio-format-ensembl-cache/src` returns 0 lines; the positive control is `grep -rni synonym` over the same two trees, which returns 101 lines, every one of them a `synonymous`-family consequence term or `var_synonyms` — the variation column holding dbSNP/COSMIC identifiers, nothing to do with contig naming. Absent feature: VEP's `--synonyms` contig-alias mapping, which CacheDir.pm:243 auto-populates from the cache directory.

desc: auto-detection: a *.fa in the cache directory becomes the `fasta` param (matches test.fa)
rationale: The other half of `CacheDir::init` (CacheDir.pm:224-240): it `readdir`s the cache directory and adopts the first `.fa`/`.fa.gz` it finds. vepyr takes the reference only as an explicit path, `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig.reference_fasta_path: Option<String>` (vcf_sink.rs:406), and nothing scans a cache directory for one: at the pin the only `.fa"` literals in either crate's `src/` are hard-coded absolute benchmark paths inside `transcript_consequence.rs` test bodies, against 63 lines matching `fasta` overall as the positive control. Absent feature: cache-directory FASTA auto-detection.

desc: auto-detection precedence: a config-supplied `synonyms` value survives the cache-directory scan
rationale: This row is only meaningful once auto-detection exists: it pins the precedence rule that a user-provided value wins over a detected one. With no chromosome-synonyms feature at all (n=6) there is nothing to lose a race against, so there is no precedence to observe. Absent feature: the same one n=6 names.

desc: auto-detection precedence: a config-supplied `fasta` value survives the cache-directory scan
rationale: The FASTA half of n=8. `AnnotateVcfConfig.reference_fasta_path` is the only way vepyr learns about a reference, so an explicit value cannot be overwritten by a scan that never runs. Contingent on n=7's absent feature.

desc: auto-detection: --no_fasta suppresses the cache-directory FASTA scan entirely
rationale: An off switch for a scan vepyr does not perform. Measured at the pin: `grep -rni no_fasta datafusion/bio-function-vep/src datafusion/bio-format-ensembl-cache/src` returns 0 lines against 63 for `fasta` as the positive control, and the option vocabulary `AnnotateProvider` parses out of `options_json` is 25 keys (af, af_1kg, af_gnomade, af_gnomadg, all_refseq, check_existing, everything, exclude_predicted, flag_pick, flag_pick_allele, flag_pick_allele_gene, gencode_basic, gencode_primary, hgvs, hgvsc, hgvsp, hgvsp_use_prediction, max_af, no_escape, per_gene, pick, pick_allele, pick_allele_gene, pubmed, remove_hgvsp_version) — `no_fasta` is not among them. Absent feature: the scan of n=7 and its switch.

desc: path resolution: with only cache_version given, species falls back to the default and the assembly is found by scanning root_dir
rationale: vepyr has no root_dir concept: `EnsemblCacheOptions.cache_root` is documented as the 'Root directory of a single Ensembl VEP cache' (table_provider.rs:36-37) — the already-resolved leaf, Perl's `dir`, not Perl's `root_dir`. Measured at the pin, `grep -rn root_dir datafusion/bio-format-ensembl-cache/src` returns 0 lines against 49 for `cache_root`. Nothing searches `<root>/<species>/` for a version prefix or enumerates assemblies, so there are no defaults to fall back to. The one surviving fragment is release recovery from the leaf basename (info.rs:190-207), which n=20 exercises. Absent feature: the whole root_dir to species/version/assembly search of CacheDir.pm:287-360.

desc: path resolution: passing the full cache path as `dir` bypasses the root_dir search
rationale: Perl offers two entry points and this line asserts the second one works; vepyr offers only the second, so the property survives as a requirement rather than an option. The named test states it in the sharpest available form: the leaf `homo_sapiens/84_GRCh38` is accepted, and its parent `homo_sapiens/` — a directory that exists and contains caches — is refused for want of an `info.txt`. That negative arm is what distinguishes this row from n=14, where the path does not exist at all.

desc: path resolution: constructing with neither `dir` nor `root_dir` dies before any filesystem access
rationale: Perl offers two ways to name a cache — the leaf `dir` or the coarser `root_dir` it searches — and this line asserts the check that neither was supplied (CacheDir.pm:108). vepyr has no second channel: `EnsemblCacheOptions::new(cache_root)` takes one mandatory path (table_provider.rs:86) and `grep -rn root_dir datafusion/bio-format-ensembl-cache/src` returns 0 lines against 49 for `cache_root`, so there is no pair of parameters and therefore no 'neither supplied' state to detect. Absent feature: the two-channel location API, the same one n=11, n=18, n=19, n=21 and n=22 name. This row was pre-registered as the ledger's weakest claim on issue #27 and the review upheld the doubt: it was briefly an analog-port asserting `cache_root: ""`, but an empty string is a *specified* location that merely does not exist, which is n=14's property, not this one. That empty-path case now lives as a second arm of n=14's test rather than as a claim of its own.

desc: path resolution: a species directory that does not exist dies with the path in the message
rationale: The property is that the error names the directory it looked in, so a user can see the path that was composed (CacheDir.pm:307). vepyr composes nothing, but it does keep the path: `CacheInfo::from_root` formats `Missing required VEP cache metadata file: {info_path}` (info.rs:64-70), and the named test asserts the absent directory's own `info.txt` path appears verbatim in the message. Worth recording against issue #95, which reports 13 dfbf sites where `io_err` drops the path VEP reports: this is not one of them.

desc: path resolution: --species homo_sapiens_refseq is refused with the advice to use --refseq/--merged instead
rationale: The Perl pins a design rule, not just an error string: refseq-ness is a mode, never a species name, even though the cache directory is called `homo_sapiens_refseq` (CacheDir.pm:299). dfbf states the same rule from the other side, in `EnsemblCacheOptions.cache_source_type`'s own documentation — 'This must be set by callers. The provider does not infer source mode from directory names such as homo_sapiens_refseq' (table_provider.rs:38-44) — and enforces it before touching the disk (table_provider.rs:134-138). The named test puts the fixture under a literal `homo_sapiens_refseq/84_GRCh38`, shows construction refused with `cache_source_type is required; provide one of ensembl, merged, or refseq`, then shows it accepted once the mode is passed as an option, with `bio.vep.cache_source_type = refseq` in the schema metadata. Perl's `--refseq`/`--merged` flags survive as `AnnotateVcfConfig.refseq` and `.merged` (vcf_sink.rs:421-424).

desc: path resolution: a cache_version the installation does not carry dies with that version in the message
rationale: Perl scans `<root>/<species>/` for directories prefixed with the requested version and throws `No cache found for <species>, version 20` when none match (CacheDir.pm:325). vepyr asks the same question by comparison rather than by search: `EnsemblCacheOptions::with_expected_cache_version(20)` against a cache that recovers release 84 yields `VEP cache version mismatch for '<root>': raw cache declares '84' but expected cache release is '20'` (info.rs:145-150). Same property — a requested release the cache cannot supply is refused and the request is echoed back — through a different observation point.

desc: path resolution: a config assembly that differs from the one in the resolved directory name is refused
rationale: `EnsemblCacheOptions` carries an `expected_cache_version` assertion but no assembly assertion: its eight fields are cache_root, cache_source_type, expected_cache_version, coordinate_system_zero_based, target_partitions, batch_size_hint, max_storable_partitions and preserve_sort_order (table_provider.rs:35-77). The assembly is read from info.txt into `CacheInfo.assembly` and published as a provenance column (schema.rs:440-448), but nothing ever compares it with a caller expectation, and `cache_version_from_raw_root_name` deliberately requires the assembly token to be non-empty without using its value (info.rs:190-207). Absent feature: an assembly assertion on the cache options. The release-token analogue of this check does exist and is n=20.

desc: path resolution: several assemblies installed for one version and none requested is an ambiguity error naming the candidates
rationale: An ambiguity only a root-directory search can produce (CacheDir.pm:350-353). vepyr never enumerates sibling caches — `cache_root` is one already-chosen leaf (n=11) — so two assemblies of one release are two unrelated roots the caller picks between, and there is no moment at which the code could notice that a choice was left open. Absent feature: the same root_dir search n=11 names.

desc: path resolution: an explicitly requested species+assembly whose composed directory does not exist is refused
rationale: What this row adds over n=14 is the composition: Perl builds `<root>/foo/84_tar` out of three config values and only then tests for existence (CacheDir.pm:356-358). vepyr composes no path from species, version and assembly — the caller supplies the leaf — so the failure mode this row pins cannot arise. Absent feature: path composition from the identity triple, the second half of CacheDir.pm:287-360.

desc: info(): the assembly recorded in the cache directory and the one in its own info.txt may not disagree
rationale: The fixture makes this a two-records-disagree check rather than a config check: `t/testdata/cache/foo/84_bar/info.txt` declares `assembly GRCh38` while the directory it sits in is named `84_bar`, and the config assembly `bar` is chosen to match the directory (CacheDir.pm:397). dfbf runs exactly that check on the other identity token: `CacheInfo::from_root` refuses when info.txt and the root basename declare different releases — `VEP cache version conflict for '<root>': info.txt declares 'X' but raw cache root basename declares 'Y'` (info.rs:124-133). Same property (a cache whose two identity records contradict each other is refused before use), different token, hence analog-port. The assembly token specifically has no assertion at all — that is n=17. Pre-registered on issue #27 as one of the three claims to argue with.

desc: METHOD CALLS: root_dir() returns the installation root the object was constructed with
rationale: The accessor exists in Perl because CacheDir holds two paths at once and derives one from the other (CacheDir.pm:262-266). vepyr holds one: `EnsemblCacheOptions.cache_root` is the leaf, there is no installation root anywhere in the type, and `grep -rn root_dir datafusion/bio-format-ensembl-cache/src` returns 0 lines at the pin against 49 for `cache_root` as the positive control. Absent feature: the root_dir/dir pair itself, and with it the accessor. See n=11 and n=22.

desc: METHOD CALLS: dir() returns the fully resolved species/version_assembly cache path
rationale: In Perl `dir()` is the output of the resolution n=11 and n=19 describe, which is what makes it worth asserting. In vepyr the same string is the input: `EnsemblCacheOptions.cache_root` is handed in already resolved and nothing derives it, so asserting that it round-trips would test the caller's own variable rather than any vepyr behaviour. Absent feature: the derivation. What the provider does with that path — reading `<cache_root>/info.txt` and discovering region files beneath it — is asserted by n=14 and n=23.

desc: METHOD CALLS: info() is the whole parsed info.txt — species, assembly, version_data, build, regulatory, cell_types, valid_chromosomes [21, 22, LRG_485] and the variation_cols list, of whose 31 entries only 18 are load-bearing on the vepyr side (the other 13 are unconditional core columns)
rationale: vepyr parses the same info.txt — the upstream file is tab-separated `key<TAB>value` and `CacheInfo::from_root` accepts that as well as `key = value` (info.rs:63-116) — but has no hash to hand back: what it keeps is published as Arrow schema fields and metadata on each table provider. The named test asserts, from a tempdir carrying ensembl-vep's own v84 info.txt, that species, assembly, cache_version and serializer_type are provenance columns, that `bio.vep.cache_version` metadata equals 84, that every `variation_cols` entry becomes a variation-schema column (schema.rs:154-159) and — the load-bearing half of that claim — that exactly 18 of the 31 disappear when info.txt stops declaring them. The other 13 are unconditional core fields that `variation_schema` emits whether or not info.txt lists them (schema.rs:120-137), so asserting their presence measures the hard-coded field list, not the parse, and that `chromosomes()` returns exactly [21, 22, LRG_485] — Perl's `valid_chromosomes`, which it reads by `readdir`ing the cache directory (CacheDir.pm:420) where vepyr extracts it from discovered file paths (discovery.rs:244-259). Five keys of the Perl hash are dropped by the pinned parser and are deliberately not claimed here: polyphen, sift, build, regulatory and cell_types have no match arm in info.rs:100-114. cell_types is n=34; the other four have no row of their own.

desc: METHOD CALLS: version_data() is the 13 source_* lines of info.txt (sift, polyphen, 1000genomes, COSMIC, ESP, gnomADe, gencode, genebuild, HGMD-PUBLIC, regbuild, dbSNP, ClinVar, assembly)
rationale: Perl builds this sub-hash by stripping the `source_` prefix from every matching info.txt line (CacheDir.pm:457). dfbf builds one `SourceDescriptor` per identical line and turns each into one Arrow provenance field (info.rs:26-43, schema.rs:440-455), so the same 13 facts survive as 13 columns instead of 13 hash keys. The named test asserts all 13 are present under the names the normaliser produces — lower-cased, non-alphanumerics collapsed to `_`, and a `src_` guard when the key starts with a digit, so VEP's `1000genomes` arrives as `source_src_1000genomes` and `HGMD-PUBLIC` as `source_hgmd_public` — and asserts that the unguarded `source_1000genomes` is absent, so the renaming is pinned in both directions. What does not survive is the values: the columns carry the version strings per row at scan time, and no public API returns them without reading the cache.

desc: get_all_AnnotationSources: the default config yields a non-empty list of annotation sources
rationale: vepyr has no source-list object; which sources fire is decided inside the annotation run and is observable only in the emitted CSQ. Both public entry points were always there — what blocked this was the fixture, and `tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/` (#96) supplies it. The ported channel is the `annotate_vep` UDTF, which takes the options_json string directly, so the rows of this block can each set exactly the flag they are about; `annotate_to_vcf` cannot, having no `check_existing` field. Non-emptiness is asserted as at least one CSQ group carrying a `Feature_type`, with a cache stripped of every feature entity as the control: that run still succeeds and still emits CSQ, but no group carries a `Feature_type` at all, so the claim is about the cache's sources rather than about the pipeline always saying something. Filed under old-repo issue #104.

desc: get_all_AnnotationSources: the return value is an array reference rather than a single object
rationale: A Perl reference-type probe. Perl subroutines are typeless, so a caller has to ask at runtime whether it received an arrayref; in Rust the shape is fixed by the signature and a wrong one fails to compile. Same family as the `ref()` blessing probe at n=5.

desc: get_all_AnnotationSources: the default config activates exactly one source
rationale: The count is a statement about which cache entities the default configuration reads: with no --regulatory and no --check_existing, only transcripts. **Ported, run, and vepyr differs.** Over the committed micro-cache, which carries regulatory data exactly as VEP's own test cache does, a default vepyr run emits `regulatory_region_variant` rows beside the transcript ones — two sources where `perl/CacheDir.t:250` asserts one. Its positive control is that the variation source stays inactive in the same run, as in VEP, so the divergence is specific rather than vepyr ignoring its options. Which side has to move, stated as the reading the issue exists to settle rather than as a finding: **vepyr's**. VEP's two-arm behaviour is asserted deliberately by the vendored file itself — one source at `perl/CacheDir.t:250` and two at `:259`, the only difference being `regulatory => 1` — so the gate is a requested capability, not an accident; vepyr's answer follows from an option it does not implement (n=30, `no-feature`) rather than from a decision to annotate regulatory features unasked. The user-visible cost is that any comparison against real VEP over a regulatory-bearing cache differs in CSQ row count unless VEP is also given --regulatory. Filed as old-repo issue #333, which is where that reading is contested. Fails at the current pin; the test's `issue:` line names the tracker.

desc: get_all_AnnotationSources: the first activated source is the transcript cache
rationale: Perl reads the blessed class off `$as->[0]`; vepyr's counterpart is which source's rows the run emits first, and the CSQ `Feature_type` value for a transcript row is the tail of Perl's own class name. n=4's tempdir construction proves the transcript entity is *readable*, which is not what this row asserts; a run over the committed cache shows it is the entity the run leads with. The test asserts on the first group of the first annotated row and separately that a second source is present in the same run, so being first is a choice the run made rather than the only option it had.

desc: get_all_AnnotationSources: the cache's version_data is copied onto every annotation source it hands out
rationale: The property is propagation: cache-level provenance is not kept in the CacheDir object, it is attached to each source so that whatever consumes a source can report where its data came from (CacheDir.pm:150, :162, :194). dfbf does the same thing structurally — `provenance_fields(cache_info)` is appended to every entity schema (schema.rs:440-455, called from the variation, transcript, regulatory, motif, exon and translation builders), so the identical `source_*` set rides on each provider. The named test builds the transcript, regulatory and variation providers from one cache root and asserts all 13 provenance columns appear on all three. Perl asserts the sub-hash is equal; vepyr can only assert the field set is shared, because the values are per-row scan output (n=24).

desc: regulatory: constructing a CacheDir with --regulatory enabled succeeds
rationale: There is no --regulatory in vepyr to enable. The option vocabulary `AnnotateProvider` parses out of options_json is the 25 keys listed at n=10 and `regulatory` is not among them; `AnnotateVcfConfig` has no such field either — its only textual `regulatory` is a doc comment at vcf_sink.rs:397. Regulatory annotation in vepyr is driven by what the cache contains, not by a request flag, which is n=33. Absent feature: the request flag.

desc: regulatory: get_all_AnnotationSources still returns a non-empty list once --regulatory is on
rationale: The flag half of the Perl assertion has no vepyr counterpart and is separately booked at n=30 (`no-feature`), so what this row ports is what its own earlier rationale predicted it would: a cache carrying regulatory data does produce regulatory annotation, named and typed. The test asserts the `Feature_type`, the feature `ENSR21_B6Z6N`, its `enhancer` biotype and the `regulatory_region_variant` consequence all reach the CSQ of one run over the committed micro-cache (#96), which is the fixture that unblocked it.

desc: regulatory: --regulatory raises the activated source count from one to two
rationale: A count over the source list, which vepyr does not expose (n=25); the observable equivalent is that one run emits two kinds of output row. In vepyr the *trigger* is the cache rather than a request flag, so the two arms are two caches: with the `regulatory` entity the run activates transcript and regulatory sources, without it exactly the transcript source, and both runs succeed. That the trigger moved is booked once, as the divergence at n=27; that a second source exists at all and is the regulatory one is this row. The negative arm additionally asserts no regulatory feature identifier survives the entity being absent, so it cannot pass by the run having failed.

desc: regulatory: the second activated source is the RegFeat cache
rationale: Perl gates the RegFeat source on two things at once: the --regulatory flag and the `regulatory 1` line in info.txt (CacheDir.pm:165). vepyr has neither — `CacheInfo::from_root` has no `regulatory` match arm (info.rs:100-114) and there is no request flag (n=30). What survives is the same conclusion reached from the files themselves: `RegulatoryFeatureTableProvider::new` succeeds exactly when the cache carries regulatory region files and otherwise refuses with `No source files discovered for RegulatoryFeature under <root>` (discovery.rs:105, table_provider.rs:208-214). The named test asserts both arms, against the v84 fixture and against a transcript-only cache built from the same info.txt. The flag half is genuinely uncovered; pre-registered on issue #27 as one of the three claims to argue with.

desc: regulatory: the RegFeat source is handed the 39 cell types listed in info.txt's cell_types line
rationale: The `cell_types` key of info.txt is never parsed at the pin: `CacheInfo::from_root`'s match covers species, assembly, cache_version/version, the serialiser aliases, var_type, cache_region_size, variation_cols and `source_*`, and nothing else (info.rs:100-114), so the cache-level inventory this row asserts is dropped while reading. A per-feature `cell_types` column does exist in the regulatory and motif schemas (schema.rs:269, :300; decoded per record at regulatory.rs:49) — a different datum, the activity of one regulatory feature rather than the list of cell types the cache offers — and the annotation engine ignores it entirely: `grep -rniE 'cell_type|celltype' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 0 lines at the pin, against 13 in datafusion/bio-format-ensembl-cache/src as the positive control. Absent feature: the cache-level cell-type inventory and the --cell_type selection it feeds.

desc: variation: constructing a CacheDir with --check_existing enabled succeeds
rationale: Unlike --regulatory (n=30), `check_existing` does exist at the pin: `VepFlags::from_options_json` parses it and every AF flag implies it (annotate_provider.rs:1181-1182). `VepFlags` itself is private — a probe under tests/ calling `VepFlags::from_options_json(None)` fails with error[E0603] and error[E0624] — but that was never the blocker for this row, because the flag reaches vepyr inside the options_json string of an annotation run and the `annotate_vep` UDTF takes that string as an argument. What blocked it was the cache, and #96 supplies one. Acceptance is not vacuous: the same call refuses an options key it does not support, by name and at planning time (`options_json key 'merged' is unsupported`), which the test asserts as its control.

desc: variation: get_all_AnnotationSources still returns a non-empty list once --check_existing is on
rationale: Same list, same channel and same fixture as n=31; here the observable is a CSQ carrying the colocated variant's identifier, which only the variation source can put there. The test runs with `check_existing` as the single non-default option and asserts `rs142513484` — the record the committed variation shard holds at 21:25585733 — appears as an exact CSQ field.

desc: variation: --check_existing raises the activated source count from one to two
rationale: The count over the source list again (n=25), and the *raise* is the content: two runs over one cache differing in that flag alone. The colocated identifier is absent from the default run and present in the check_existing one, while the feature sources the two runs activate are identical — so what the flag added is exactly one source and nothing else. A single run could not show this, which is why this test is not n=36's.

desc: variation: the second activated source is the Variation cache
rationale: Perl's gate for the variation source is `$self->param('check_existing') && $info->{variation_cols}` (CacheDir.pm:168) — the request flag and the info.txt column declaration. dfbf keeps the second half exactly: `variation_schema` refuses with `Malformed info.txt: variation_cols must be present for variation entity` when the key is absent (schema.rs:114-118), so `VariationTableProvider::new` succeeds precisely when the cache declares variation columns. The named test asserts both arms from one tempdir, dropping only the `variation_cols` line between them. The flag half is n=35. A neighbouring defect found while writing this test is filed as issue #108 (variation discovery claims transcript region files when a cache has no `_var` files); it does not affect this row, whose fixture keeps both file families.

desc: gnomAD/ExAC: --af_gnomad against a cache whose variation_cols include gnomADe activates the sources without error
rationale: The positive arm of the capability check whose negative arm is n=40. vepyr's equivalent flag is `af_gnomade` (annotate_provider.rs:1176), reachable through an annotation run's options_json, so the successful case is observable as a CSQ carrying gnomAD allele frequencies. The precondition — Perl's `a cache whose variation_cols include gnomADe` — is asserted rather than assumed: the committed variation shard's scanned batch carries `af_gnomade_freqs`, with a column name the shard lacks as the control, because `read_context_parquet` silently drops unknown columns and a scan that merely succeeded would prove nothing. Then the flag's own observable: 9.481e-05 reaches the CSQ with it and does not without it.

desc: gnomAD/ExAC: --af_gnomad against an ExAC-only cache dies with `gnomAD data is not available in this cache`
rationale: VEP performs a capability check before annotating: it compares the requested AF source against the cache's declared variation_cols and refuses when the cache cannot serve it (CacheDir.pm:179-186, deliberately skipped under --everything). vepyr does not perform that comparison FOR AF SOURCES: AF columns are built from `cache_info.variation_cols` (schema.rs:154-159) and a requested source the cache lacks simply yields an empty CSQ field, so a user asking for gnomAD against an ExAC-only cache gets silence instead of an error. Absent feature: the pre-flight cache-capability check for requested AF sources. CORRECTION (2026-08-31, batch-2 feature-area re-audit): the sentence that used to stand here -- `vepyr has no such check anywhere` -- is the same over-broad negative PR #403/#404 removed from ledger/Runner.ledger.toml, and it is false at the pin. vepyr HAS the mechanism, keyed on the cache's own schema metadata rather than on a mutable config hash: `TranscriptSelectionFlags::from_options_json(cache_source_type, options_json)` (annotate_provider.rs:1418-1450) refuses a requested option the chosen cache cannot serve, with upstream's own tests at :16350-16372; the crate carries 77 distinct `annotate_vep()` / `annotate_to_vcf()` refusal messages in all. Measured by an EXECUTED run over the committed micro-cache at dfbf aa2be930, whose schema metadata declares `ensembl`: `--all_refseq` -> REFUSED at plan time with `annotate_vep(): --all_refseq requires cache schema metadata bio.vep.cache_source_type=refseq or merged`; `--exclude_predicted` -> the same; `expected_cache_version=999` -> `unsupported VEP cache version 999; supported cache versions: 115, 116`; positive control `--gencode_basic` alone -> ACCEPTED, 1 row. The verdict survives because what is absent is this comparison for the AF-SOURCE family specifically, which is this row's subject. A reviewer might prefer deferred/blocked-engine here; it is filed as no-feature because nothing in the engine is half-built — the comparison is simply not part of the design.

desc: both: constructing a CacheDir with --check_existing and --regulatory together succeeds
rationale: The composite carries --regulatory, which has no counterpart at the pin (n=30), so the configuration this line asserts is accepted cannot be expressed at all. The check_existing half exists but only inside an annotation run's options JSON (n=35). Absent feature: the regulatory request flag, as in n=30.

desc: both: get_all_AnnotationSources returns a non-empty list with regulatory and variation both on
rationale: Same list and same fixture as n=31 and n=36, over a cache that carries transcript, regulatory and variation data at once; what it adds over those two is that the three coexist — serving one source does not stop the cache serving the others. The test asserts a transcript identifier, a regulatory feature identifier and the colocated variant in the CSQ of a single `check_existing` run.

desc: both: the activated sources come back in the fixed order Transcript, RegFeat, Variation
rationale: An ordering claim over the source list, and the one row of this block the micro-cache does not unblock, so its reason changes rather than its category. Two thirds of it are now observable — a run over the committed cache emits the transcript groups before the regulatory one — but `Variation` is not a row in vepyr's output at all: the variation source's contribution arrives as columns on the feature rows (`Existing_variation` and the frequencies, n=36 and n=39), so nothing can show it arriving *third*. Asserting the observable two thirds and calling the row covered would be the mistake this ledger already rejected at n=36 of AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml, where a test that dropped the asserted block index was refused as `a coverage claim for something the test never observes`. The remaining blocker is the **engine**, and it is not an export: nothing here waits on a `pub`. The ordering vepyr does perform is already nameable from this crate — `pub enum FeatureType` at `transcript_consequence.rs:849` with `pub fn rank` at `:870` (dfbf 391f94bd), and `pub enum EnsemblEntityKind` at `bio-format-ensembl-cache/src/entity.rs:3`, re-exported at that crate's `lib.rs:27` (tag v1.10.0#0d9730c8) — and `FeatureType`'s variants are `Transcript`, `RegulatoryFeature`, `MotifFeature`, `None`, with **no `Variation`**: the vocabulary that orders CSQ rows cannot express the third element Perl asserts, so exporting something would not settle this row. Measured on the annotation rather than argued, out of tree with a temporary `#[tokio::test]` built from `tests/port_cache_dir_variation.rs`'s own helpers — `annotate(&micro_cache(), CHECK_EXISTING_OPTIONS)`, then `Row::kind` and field membership over every emitted group: the run returns 17 CSQ groups whose `Feature_type` values are exactly {`Transcript`, `RegulatoryFeature`}, and the colocated identifier `rs142513484` rides as a field on 14 of those 17 while forming none of its own. Perl's third list element gets a counterpart when the engine emits the variation source's contribution as a row rather than as columns — an annotation-engine behaviour, which is what `blocked-engine` names, and not an item somebody could `pub` this afternoon. This row stays tracked on old-repo issue #104, which the other ten rows of the block now leave.

desc: tabix: setting info's var_type to `tabix` switches the variation source to the VariationTabix class
rationale: RE-MEASURED AT THE OVERLAY PIN; still deferred, with a corrected reason and a new measurement. The old blocker was that nothing public reported the cache's declared var_type: CacheInfo is pub(crate) inside a private mod info, and a probe writing use datafusion_bio_format_ensembl_cache::info::CacheInfo failed with error[E0603]: module `info` is private pointing at lib.rs:15. That half is now closed -- PINS.toml formats_test_overlay (8fd75f30) exposes test_internals::CacheInfo::var_type(), and over the committed tests/data/vep115_native_slice/homo_sapiens/115_GRCh38 it returns Some("tabix"), alongside species "homo_sapiens", assembly "GRCh38" and cache_version "115" as the positive control that the whole file parsed. Measured, so the fixture question is settled: this row needs no new artefact. But exposure demonstrates the divergence rather than closing the row, which is the case docs/ledger-contract.md warns about. Perl asserts a CLASS SWITCH -- setting info's var_type to tabix makes get_all_AnnotationSources->[1] a ...AnnotationSource::Cache::VariationTabix -- and vepyr does not select on var_type at all: the field is still carried as #[allow(dead_code)] // Parsed from info.txt; will be used for tabix index support. (info.rs:55-56), and the backend is chosen by file discovery instead, discover_variation_files preferring all_vars* when present (discovery.rs:9-29) as table_provider.rs:150-151 says in as many words. So a var_type=tabix cache and an all_vars.gz cache still present the same public surface, and no public item reports which layout was chosen. The reason is therefore blocked-engine, not blocked-api: the mechanism the row asserts does not exist, and one more pub would not create it. Deliberately not ported as a weaker claim -- asserting only that var_type reads back as tabix would be a coverage claim for a switch the test never observes, the same defect #75 removed from AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat n=36. Tracked in issue #106; the extraction umbrella is #93.

desc: use_ok Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config: the config module compiles and loads
rationale: A module-load probe. In Rust the equivalent is a compile-time fact: `tests/port_config.rs` opens with `use datafusion_bio_function_vep::vcf_sink::{AnnotateVcfConfig, VEP_DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE};`, so if the module or either item disappeared from the pinned dependency the test crate would not build and every row in this ledger would fail with it. A runtime assertion would restate the compiler.

desc: new is defined: the no-argument constructor returns an object rather than undef
rationale: Perl asserts the constructor returned a defined blessed reference instead of `undef`. vepyr's nearest constructor is `AnnotateVcfConfig::default()` (dfbf 391f94bd `vcf_sink.rs:458`), whose return type is `Self` — `Default::default()` cannot yield the absence of a value — so "the constructor returned something" is enforced by the type system, which is the contract's Perl-object-identity case. What the constructor puts *into* the object is a separate assertion, row 17, and that one is ported.

desc: check class: ref($cfg) is the string 'Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config'
rationale: A runtime class-name probe — `ref()` on a blessed hashref. Rust has no runtime class name to compare a string against: the binding's type is fixed at compile time and `AnnotateVcfConfig` is a plain struct, not a blessed reference. docs/ledger-contract.md lists class-existence and blessing probes as the not-applicable case.

desc: new with invalid arg: a non-hashref first argument is refused with /First argument/
rationale: What this pins down is that the configuration entry point refuses a first argument of the wrong type and names the argument in doing so. vepyr's configuration entry point is not a constructor taking a hashref but the `annotate_vep()` table function; its first-argument check is `extract_string_arg` (dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_table_function.rs:68`, body at `:125-138`), which refuses anything that is not a string literal with "annotate_vep() vcf_table must be a string literal, got: Int64(1)". Different channel — a SQL literal's type instead of Perl's `ref()` — and the named test drives it through `ctx.sql(...)` with no table and no cache registered, because the check runs before the planner reaches either.

desc: param get: a key written at construction reads back through the dynamic param() accessor
rationale: Perl's Config is a dynamic key-value store: `new({testing => 'hello'})` accepts a key the module knows nothing about and `param('testing')` reads it back. vepyr has no such store to port. `AnnotateVcfConfig` (dfbf 391f94bd `vcf_sink.rs:381-456`) is a plain struct whose field names are compile-time, and options crossing the UDTF boundary travel as an `options_json` string read by per-key private parsers (`parse_json_bool_option`, `annotate_provider.rs:3523`), so an unrecognised key is ignored rather than stored — there is nothing to read back. The missing feature is a generic get-by-arbitrary-key configuration accessor.

desc: param set: param('testing', 'goodbye') writes the key and returns the value just written
rationale: The same absent store as row 5, plus mutability: `AnnotateVcfConfig` is built once by struct literal and handed to `annotate_to_vcf` by shared reference (`vcf_sink.rs:1018-1024`), so there is no write-through-the-accessor path and no accessor to echo the written value back. The missing feature is a mutable, dynamically-keyed config object.

desc: param without key: calling the accessor with its mandatory key omitted dies with /No param/
rationale: Rows 5 and 6 are `no-feature` because vepyr has no dynamic `param()` store; this row is different, because what it pins is not the store but the enforcement — the configuration entry point refuses a call that omits a mandatory argument instead of silently defaulting it. vepyr exhibits that in `AnnotateFunction::call`'s arity check (dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_table_function.rs:61-66`), which refuses `annotate_vep('vcf', 'cache')` with "requires at least 3 arguments: vcf_table, cache_source, backend", naming the missing argument as Perl's /No param/ names the missing key. Different channel: UDTF arity instead of an accessor's argument list.

desc: read_config_from_file no file given: the INI reader dies with /Could not open config file/
rationale: vepyr has no configuration-file reader of any kind. Measured at the pin: `grep -rniE '\.ini\b|read_config_from_file|config_file' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 0 hits at 391f94bd, against a positive control of 95 hits for `options_json` in the same tree — options reach the engine as a JSON string assembled in-process, never from a file. The missing feature is an INI/config-file loader, and rows 8-16, 24 and 25 are all that same gap seen from different angles.

desc: read_config_from_file invalid file given: a named path that does not exist dies with the same /Could not open config file/
rationale: The same absent config-file loader as row 8 (0 hits at 391f94bd for any config-file reader; positive control `options_json`, 95 hits). What this row adds on its own — that a file which was *named but is missing* is refused rather than quietly skipped — still has no code path to exercise, because vepyr never opens a config file to begin with.

desc: read_config_from_file ok: reading the test INI returns a populated hashref
rationale: The same absent config-file loader, seen from its positive arm: rows 8 and 9 pin the refusals, this one pins that a well-formed INI parses into a config hash at all. vepyr's corresponding step consumes a JSON object built from Python `annotate()` kwargs (audit/vepyr-master/vepyr-python.md §3) rather than a file, and it lives in the Python wrapper, which is `cdylib`-only and unreachable from any Rust test in this crate.

desc: read_config_from_file basic: a plain `format ensembl` INI line becomes the scalar param 'ensembl'
rationale: The same absent config-file loader. Beyond the file itself, this row pins the INI lexer's simplest rule — `key value` on one line yields a scalar. vepyr has no key/value config text format at all (0 config-file hits at 391f94bd), so there is no lexer whose scalar rule could regress; JSON carries scalar-ness in the encoding.

desc: quoted string with spaces: an INI value quoted across spaces keeps them, giving dir = '/this/is/a path with spaces'
rationale: The same absent config-file loader, this time pinning its quoting rule specifically. vepyr has no config text format to quote in — values arrive already delimited inside a JSON string, so whitespace is preserved by the encoding rather than by a hand-written quote-stripper that could get it wrong.

desc: read_config_from_file flag not allowed multiple: a scalar-arity key such as `terms` keeps one value instead of becoming a list
rationale: The missing feature here is not only the INI loader but Config.pm's per-key arity table, which decides whether repeating a key overwrites or appends. vepyr has no such table: each option is read from `options_json` by a key-specific private parser typed at its own call site (`parse_json_bool_option` / `parse_json_string_option` / `parse_json_i64_option`, `annotate_provider.rs:3523-3548`), so arity is a property of the reader's Rust type, not configurable data that could be misdeclared.

desc: read_config_from_file flag list preserved comma-separated: `fields` stays the single string 'Allele,Consequence,Feature_type,Feature' rather than being split
rationale: Two absences at once: the config-file loader, and `--fields`. vepyr emits a CSQ field list driven by `everything` plus per-feature options and has no output-column whitelist to project onto (`grep -rn '"fields"' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` = 0 at 391f94bd; positive control `options_json`, 95). Note what the Perl actually pins — the value is *preserved* as one comma-joined scalar here, in deliberate contrast to row 26's list conversion — so even a generic comma-splitter would be the wrong analogue for it.

desc: read_config_from_file flag allowed multiple: a repeated `plugin` key accumulates into a two-element arrayref
rationale: vepyr does have a plugin mechanism at the pin — `pub mod plugin_cache` with thirteen public submodules under the default `parquet-cache` feature (audit/vepyr-master/vepyr-python.md §3) — but it is a TOML source manifest plus a built cache directory, selected by the single field `plugin_cache_root: Option<PathBuf>` (`vcf_sink.rs:452-455`). There is no repeatable `--plugin` config key, so the append-on-repeat semantics this row pins has nothing to attach to. The missing feature is the multi-valued config key, not plugins.

desc: read_config_from_file flag multiples added not overwritten: re-reading the same INI into an existing hash grows `plugin` from 2 entries to 4
rationale: The strongest form of row 15's gap: it pins that a second `read_config_from_file` call accumulates *into* the hash it is handed rather than replacing it. vepyr has neither the loader nor a config object that is filled incrementally — `AnnotateVcfConfig` is constructed once by struct literal, and `AnnotateVcfConfig::to_options_json` (`vcf_sink.rs:514`) serialises it once per call — so there is no second read for entries to accumulate across.

desc: defaults applied: the no-argument constructor fills in the defaults table, here species = 'homo_sapiens'
rationale: The property is that constructing a config with no arguments applies the library's documented defaults rather than leaving fields unset. vepyr exhibits it through `impl Default for AnnotateVcfConfig` (dfbf 391f94bd `vcf_sink.rs:458-497`), which the named test pins field by field. Different channel, and a different key: vepyr has no `species` option at all — single species and assembly by design, `grep -rn '"species"' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` = 0 at the pin — so the one default this Perl line reads cannot be observed. What can be, and what the test asserts, is that the same kind of default is applied, including `buffer_size == VEP_DEFAULT_BUFFER_SIZE`, documented at `vcf_sink.rs:29-30` as Ensembl VEP's own `--buffer_size` default of 5000, i.e. a VEP default carried across rather than a Rust one.

desc: empty array ref (cell_type) does not trigger option set: a key present but empty leaves `regulatory` undef
rationale: This pins a rule of the option-set table itself — a key that is present but empty must not fire its expansion. vepyr has no option-set table: the only flag fan-out at the pin is a hard-coded boolean expression over a fixed key list in `VepFlags::from_options_json` (`annotate_provider.rs:1166-1191`), with no data-driven table, no `cell_type` key and therefore no emptiness rule that could be got wrong. The missing feature is Config.pm's `%OPTION_SETS` indirection.

desc: option sets, one in multiple out: --genomes sets host to mysql-eg-publicsql.ebi.ac.uk and port to 4157
rationale: The Ensembl Genomes database mode. vepyr is offline and cache-only: it has no DBI layer, no MySQL client and no host or port to set — `grep -rnE '"database"|"genomes"' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 0 at 391f94bd (positive control: `options_json`, 95 hits). The missing feature is database-backed annotation; until it exists there is no one-in-multiple-out expansion to observe.

desc: option sets, multiple in same out 1: --af turns on --check_existing
rationale: vepyr implements the rule -- `check_existing = parse("check_existing") || af || af_1kg || af_gnomade || af_gnomadg || max_af || pubmed` at dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_provider.rs:1180-1182`, under a doc comment at `:1148-1151` citing the very Config.pm#L346-L374 this Perl line exercises -- and the resolver is private, so the analogue reads the resolved value off a run rather than off a config object: `Existing_variation` in the emitted CSQ is populated exactly when `check_existing` came out true. That is a different observation point from Perl's `param('check_existing')`, hence analog rather than unit. The row was `blocked-data` under issue 76 for the reason issue 76 gives -- the run needs a VEP parquet cache -- and `tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/` (issue 96) is one. Three configurations, because two would not separate the implication from the flag: `{}` leaves Existing_variation empty (with `Consequence` still `3_prime_UTR_variant`, so the empty field is a real observation and not an empty run), `{"check_existing": true}` reports `rs142513484`, and `{"af": true}` -- which never asked for it -- reports it too. The channel is the `annotate_vep` UDTF and not `annotate_to_vcf`, because `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-456`) carries neither `af` nor `check_existing`: `options_json` is the only public way in.

desc: option sets, multiple in same out 2: --check_frequency also turns on --check_existing
rationale: Unlike row 20, this row's input does not exist in vepyr at all: `grep -rn 'check_frequency' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 0 at 391f94bd against a positive control of 10 hits for `check_existing` in the same tree, and the Python `annotate()` keyword surface does not offer it either — audit/vepyr-master/vepyr-python.md §3 enumerates the ten VEP options it accepts beyond the config struct, and `check_frequency` is not among them. The missing feature is frequency filtering (VEP's `--check_frequency` with its `--freq_*` companions), so the second input this row adds to row 20's rule has nothing to be supplied to.

desc: option sets, substitution: --gff test expands to custom = ['file=test,format=gff']
rationale: Custom annotation. vepyr's only annotation sources are the partitioned parquet cache and the plugin cache; `grep -rnE '"custom"|"gff"|"gtf"|"bigwig"' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 0 at 391f94bd (positive control: `options_json`, 95 hits). Both halves of the assertion are therefore absent — the `--gff` input and the `--custom` output the option set substitutes it into. The missing feature is user-supplied custom annotation files.

desc: option sets, multiple substitution: --ucsc_assembly hg38 with --phyloP 7,100 expands to two templated hgdownload bigwig custom entries
rationale: Row 22's gap plus two more of its own: URL templating inside an option set, and BigWig as a custom-annotation format. None of `ucsc_assembly`, `phyloP` or `bigwig` appears at 391f94bd (0 hits each; positive control `options_json`, 95). BigWig is one of the standing `no-feature` examples in docs/ledger-contract.md, and vepyr never fetches annotation over HTTP, so there is no remote URL for a template to build.

desc: config file: --config <ini> makes the file's `format ensembl` line win, giving param('format') = 'ensembl'
rationale: The same absent config-file loader as rows 8-16 (0 hits at 391f94bd; positive control `options_json`, 95). What this row adds beyond them is the `--config` flag itself — the explicit request to merge a named file into the resolved config — which vepyr also lacks, because the only channel into the engine is the `options_json` string built in-process by the caller.

desc: ini file: with only --dir given, VEP auto-detects and reads $dir/vep.ini
rationale: The implicit half of row 24: a config file found by convention rather than named. vepyr has no config-file loader to discover one with, and its nearest equivalent to `--dir`, the `cache_source` argument (`annotate_table_function.rs:69`), is read only for the parquet cache's manifest and shards — `CacheSourceType::from_partitioned_parquet_cache_source` (`cache_source.rs:42-59`) looks for `variation/chrom_manifest.json` and nothing else beside it.

desc: list conversion: individual => 'dave,barry,keith' becomes the three-element list [dave, barry, keith]
rationale: Per-sample selection. vepyr annotates every record of the input VCF and has no `--individual` option whose value could be converted: `grep -rn '"individual"' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 0 at 391f94bd (positive control: `options_json`, 95 hits). A generic comma-list splitter does exist and is public — `schema_contract::parse_column_list` (`schema_contract.rs:70`) — but it splits cache *column* names for projection, so naming it in `rust_test` would claim coverage of VEP option handling that vepyr does not perform. The missing feature is sample selection, not string splitting.

desc: individual_zyg - list conversion: individual_zyg => 'dave,barry,keith' converts the same way --individual does
rationale: The same absent per-sample selection as row 26, one option further along: `--individual_zyg` additionally asks VEP to report each named sample's zygosity. vepyr emits no per-sample output at all — `annotate_to_vcf` (`vcf_sink.rs:1018-1024`) writes one CSQ INFO field per record and never reads the sample columns — so neither the key nor the reporting behind it exists for a value to be converted for.

desc: deprecated no replacement: --convert is rejected outright with /deprecated/
rationale: vepyr has no deprecated-flag rejection mechanism. Apart from two deliberately refused source selectors (`merged` and `refseq`, `annotate_table_function.rs:258-266`), an unrecognised key in `options_json` is ignored, because every reader is a per-key lookup falling back to a default when the key is absent (`parse_json_bool_option`, `annotate_provider.rs:3523`, used as `.unwrap_or(false)` at `:1167-1170`). The one deprecated alias the pin does carry shows the direction of the design: `AnnotationBackend::parse` *accepts* "lance" as "a deprecated alias for the same Parquet backend" (`annotation_store.rs:17-25`) rather than refusing it. The missing feature is a deprecation list with a rejecting resolver.

desc: invalid value for key: --format gobbledegook is rejected with /not a valid value/
rationale: What this pins is closed-set validation of an enum-valued option: a spelling outside the allowed set must be refused with a message rather than accepted and mishandled downstream. vepyr has no `--format` option, its input always being a VCF, but it does validate one enum-valued option against a closed set and does so in `pub fn AnnotationBackend::parse` on a `pub enum` in `pub mod annotation_store` (`annotation_store.rs:19-26`) — reachable directly from an external crate with no session, cache or fixture. Different key, same property; the named test also keeps a positive control on the two accepted spellings, so it cannot pass by rejecting everything.

desc: incompatible params: --database together with --cache is refused with /Can't use.+together/
rationale: The mutually exclusive pair this row pins cannot be formed in vepyr, because one half of it does not exist: `grep -rn '"database"' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 0 at 391f94bd (positive control: `options_json`, 95 hits), vepyr being cache-only, so `--cache` is not a mode selected against an alternative. The pin does carry one entry-point conflict check, `reject_options_json_source_selectors` (`annotate_table_function.rs:258-266`), but it guards something else — the cache's source type must come from schema metadata rather than from `options_json` — so it is not this assertion's analogue. The missing feature is database mode.

desc: incompatible pass with safe: --safe lets an otherwise-conflicting --most_severe plus --symbol construct succeed
rationale: Two absences compound here. vepyr has no `--safe` (`grep -rn '"safe"' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` = 0 at 391f94bd; positive control `options_json`, 95), and, as row 30 records, it has no incompatibility table for `--safe` to downgrade: the entry-point checks it does perform (`annotate_table_function.rs:61-94`, `annotation_store.rs:19-26`) are unconditional and offer no bypass.
