rationale: The "_"-prefix arm (FilterSet.pm:562-565), and the one with a concrete purpose: VEP's internal per-consequence hashes carry private fields under an underscore, and this arm lets a filter reach them without the user knowing which are private. It is also the arm whose absence would be least noticeable in testing and most annoying in use. Anchor n=144.

desc: evaluate - value is field - pass: `FOO > #BAR` compares two fields of the same record — FOO => 2 against BAR => 1 — and evaluates to 1
rationale: The #-sigil branch (FilterSet.pm:475-479): when the parsed value begins with #, evaluate resolves the rest of it through get_input against the same record and uses the result as the comparison operand. That turns the filter language from constant-comparison into record-relative comparison — `--filter "gnomADe_AF > #gnomADg_AF"` — which is a qualitatively different capability from anything a fixed set of CLI flags could express, and worth naming separately when sizing the absent feature. Anchor n=144.

desc: evaluate - value is field - pass synonym: `FOO > #bar` also resolves against BAR, so the #-operand goes through the same synonym search as the field
rationale: The composition claim: the second get_input call at FilterSet.pm:476 is the ordinary one, so every arm of n=144-146 applies to the right-hand side too. An implementation that resolved the #-operand with a plain hash lookup would satisfy n=147 and fail here. Anchor n=144.

desc: evaluate - value is field - fail: `FOO < #BAR` with FOO => 2 and BAR => 1 evaluates to 0
rationale: The negative direction, and it also fixes the operand *order*: the #-value is the right-hand side of the comparison, so reversing the two fields reverses the answer. With n=147 it rules out an implementation that compared the pair symmetrically. Anchor n=144.

desc: evaluate - value is field - fail missing: `FOO = #BAR` against a record carrying only FOO evaluates to 0, by an early return rather than by a comparison
rationale: The unresolvable-operand case, and it has its own code path: `return 0 unless defined($value)` (FilterSet.pm:477) fires inside the #-branch, before the ordinary input guard at :481 and before any predicate. So a record-relative comparison against a field the record lacks is false, never an error and never a comparison against undef — the same product decision n=55 and n=124 record for the left-hand side. Anchor n=144.

desc: empty synonyms without limit_synonym_search: after an evaluate whose field lookup failed, the synonyms hash is still {} — a failed lookup is not memoised, so it is repeated for every record
rationale: The default half of the memoisation knob. synonyms (FilterSet.pm:630-634) auto-vivifies `{}` on read, so this row asserts two things at once: the slot exists and nothing was cached in it. Every arm of the search at :546-583 writes to the hash only on a hit, and the fall-through at :582-583 writes undef only when limit_synonym_search is set — so by default a filter naming a field the data does not have re-runs the whole search, including the O(keys) prefix grep, once per record. Anchor n=144.

desc: undef synonym with limit_synonym_search: after limit_synonym_search(1), the same failed lookup memoises {foo => undef}, so it is not retried
rationale: The knob's other position (FilterSet.pm:582-583, read back through :652-656), and the pair's real subject: this is a performance control on a hot loop, not a semantic one — the answer to n=141 is the same either way, but filter_vep over a whole-genome VCF calls get_input once per field per consequence. The undef sentinel is what lets the memo distinguish `known to be absent` from `not yet looked up`, since :546 tests `exists` rather than truth. vepyr has no such loop to tune because it resolves no user-supplied field names; limit_synonym_search is one of the nine names in the header's engine grep. Anchor n=144.

desc: is_child - no adaptor: with the filter `foo is_child gene_variant`, evaluating foo => 1 dies with /No ontology adaptor set/ because the term hierarchy needs a database handle that has not been supplied
rationale: FAMILY ANCHOR for n=153-160, and the file's only SKIP block: `skip 'No local database configured', 8 unless $can_use_db` (t/FilterSet.t:514) declares exactly eight assertions, which is exactly this range, so n=153-160 is precisely the database-backed part of the file. filter_is_child (FilterSet.pm:722-748) first tries filter_re($child, $parent) as a short-circuit, and only on a miss asks an OntologyTermAdaptor for the parent term's descendants — which is why this row's input is 1 rather than a term name: it has to miss the regex to reach the throw. Two vepyr absences meet here, and each has its own measurement. (i) No database client at all: `grep -rqi 'mysql\|dbi:\|db_adaptor' src/` exits 1 at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control `grep -rqi 'parquet' src/` exit 0 — vepyr is cache-only, the contract's standing no-feature example. (ii) No SO hierarchy even offline: so_terms.rs carries a flat enum of 41 terms (`ALL_SO_TERMS: [SoTerm; 41]`, so_terms.rs:58) with rank() and impact() and no parent/child relation — `grep -cE 'parent|child|is_a|descend' src/so_terms.rs` -> 0 against `grep -c 'pub fn' src/so_terms.rs` -> 6. So this is no-feature twice over, and detailed_plans/FilterSet.md's sizing ("an OBO parser is small, ~100 LOC") is optimistic: the hierarchy is fetched from a live Ensembl ontology database, not read from a packaged file. File anchor n=2.

desc: is_child - set adaptor: ontology_adaptor() accepts and returns the OntologyTermAdaptor obtained from the MultiTestDB `multi` database, so the setter is usable as a truth test
rationale: A setter probe whose subject is the absent feature, which is what keeps it no-feature rather than not-applicable. Two readings are defensible and the contract settles the tie. Against not-applicable: the assertion exercises a database handle, and the contract lists mock database handles among the legitimate not-applicable cases. Against that: MultiTestDB is a real Ensembl test database, not a mock, and the SKIP-block corollary in docs/ledger-contract.md carries a probe to no-feature when the probe's *subject* is the absent thing — here the subject is the ontology adaptor itself, the second half of what n=153 measures missing. The contract's tie-break is explicit — when both readings are defensible, take the one that keeps the row in the denominator — so no-feature. Anchor n=153.

desc: is_child - no ontology_name: with the adaptor set but no ontology name, the same evaluation dies with /No ontology_name set/
rationale: The second of the two configuration guards (FilterSet.pm:737), and a separate product statement from n=153: the lookup needs not only a connection but a namespace, because fetch_all_by_name is asked for a term *within* an ontology and Ensembl's ontology database holds several. A Rust reimplementation shipping only SO would have no counterpart to this row at all — which is an argument about how the absent feature would be built, not evidence it exists. Anchor n=153.

desc: is_child - set ontology_name: ontology_name('SO') is accepted and returns a true value, selecting the Sequence Ontology namespace
rationale: The second setter probe, same reading as n=154 and the same tie-break: its subject is the ontology namespace selector, which is part of the missing capability rather than Perl plumbing. It also fixes 'SO' as the namespace the operator is exercised against, so n=158-160's expectations are about Sequence Ontology terms specifically. Anchor n=153.

desc: is_child - fail: with the adaptor and namespace set, foo => 1 evaluates to 0 — 1 is neither the term `gene_variant` nor one of its descendants
rationale: The first row that actually reaches the database path to completion: the regex short-circuit misses, the adaptor fetches gene_variant, its descendants are cached on the FilterSet (FilterSet.pm:740-744), and the final `grep {lc($_) eq lc($child)}` finds nothing, returning 0 in scalar context. So the row pins both the negative answer and the fact that the descendant comparison is case-insensitive equality over names rather than another regex. Anchor n=153.

desc: is_child - pass exact: foo => 'gene_variant' evaluates to 1 — the term matches its own filter value, and does so without touching the database
rationale: The short-circuit row, and it is subtler than `a term is its own descendant`: the fast path is `return 1 if filter_re($child, $parent)` (FilterSet.pm:726), an unanchored case-insensitive *regex* match, not equality. So `Consequence is_child variant` would also short-circuit on `intron_variant` for the wrong reason, and any term whose name contains the parent's name as a substring passes without a hierarchy lookup. desc: is_child - pass child 1: foo => 'missense_variant' evaluates to 1, because it is a descendant of gene_variant in the Sequence Ontology

rationale: Not a bare constructor probe: TranscriptTree::new asserts the source does AnnotationType::Transcript, refuses it unless it can('populate_tree'), and then calls `$as->populate_tree($self)` (TranscriptTree.pm:94-111, the call at :106), so this one line performs the entire tabix scan the next three rows observe. The channel is the one every analog-port row of ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml uses -- TranscriptEngineProfile::tx_candidates, counted per node the COITree returns -- and the test carries its own positive control, so the zero is not merely a query that never ran. desc: fetch after populated: populate_tree seeks every contig of the GTF and inserts each included feature's range, so the same 21:25585733 query that returned nothing at n=8 now returns [25585656, 25607517]
rationale: Three absent things stand between n=8 and this line. First the scan: populate_tree is this class's own override -- for every seqname in the tabix index it seeks (chr, 1, 1e10) and walks every record, inserting the ones whose type survives deleting exon, CDS and stop_codon from include_feature_types (Haplo/AnnotationSource/File/GTF.pm:84-85), then throws the parser away. Second the insert: `$tree->insert($chr, $start, $end)` passes no payload object, which selects the merging branch of TranscriptTree::insert (TranscriptTree.pm:169-184) -- fetch the overlaps, remove them, re-insert one expanded range. ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=17 and n=18 already establish that this branch's only production callers are the four haplosaurus sources and that vepyr has no mutating insert at all. Third, the file itself: vepyr reads transcripts only from the parquet cache (see n=2). Whether [25585656, 25607517] is one feature's span or the union the merge leaves behind cannot be read off the .t and does not change the verdict. Missing features: the file scan, and tree population by merge-on-insert.

desc: input buffer next count: the first next() on the haplosaurus buffer yields 34 variants -- as many as reach the far end of the transcripts overlapping the first variant, not a fixed buffer_size
rationale: 34 is not a configured size, it is a consequence of the fill rule, and the rule is haplosaurus's. Haplo::InputBuffer overrides next (modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:119 onwards) to keep reading until a variant starts past a `$max` from get_max_from_tree($chr, $start, $end) at :134 -- the right-hand edge of the transcripts the tree returns for the first variant -- which is why the class doc at :54-57 describes the buffer as filled by transcript overlap rather than by count. Measured: `git grep -n get_max_from_tree release/116.0 -- modules` returns lines only in Haplo/InputBuffer.pm (call site :134, definition :169), so transcript-bounded buffering exists nowhere else in VEP. vepyr buffers by count: InputBufferAccumulator drains `while self.pending_input_units >= input_unit_limit` (dfbf 391f94bd src/annotate_provider.rs:9587), and the pinned crate's own design note says per-transcript grouping is what haplotype features need and what the window-based pipeline does not do (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-17-within-contig-parallel-annotation-design.md:218). That is why this is no-feature and not the deferred/blocked-api that ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=13 gives the mainline buffer_size fill: there the behaviour exists and is merely private, here the fill rule itself does not exist.

desc: annotate_InputBuffer - ref: the source's annotate_InputBuffer returns Bio::EnsEMBL::Variation::TranscriptHaplotypeContainer objects, not consequences
rationale: The return type is what separates haplosaurus from the annotator. Haplo::AnnotationType::Transcript::annotate_InputBuffer (module :76-111) walks the protein-coding transcripts overlapping the buffer, collects per-sample SampleGenotypeFeature objects through get_genotypes (:163-195, which re-injects the raw VCF record into the parser to lazy-read GT and marks every genotype phased => 1 at :183) and hands them to create_container (:212-220). vepyr's output unit is a CSQ row per variant and transcript written into a VCF, and it never reads per-sample genotypes at all: measured, `grep -rniE 'genotype' --include=*.rs` over the pinned crate returns exactly one line, a ##FORMAT=<ID=GT,...> header string inside tests/vcf_output_roundtrip.rs:24 -- a fixture, not a consumer. Missing feature: the haplotype container, and the phased-genotype layer that would feed it.

Neither is expressible in vepyr, and not because the values would differ: vepyr emits a CSQ row for every overlapping transcript and reports the biotype as a field (BIOTYPE is a CSQ header entry at dfbf 391f94bd src/annotate_provider.rs:296) rather than using it to include or exclude, it has no per-transcript output object whose presence or absence could be compared, and it cannot read a transcript set out of a GTF in the first place. desc: BASIC TESTS: the AnnotationType::Transcript role loads, so its CAN_USE_INTERVAL_TREE flag can gate everything below

The reason the load happens at all is Perl-only: line 35 reads `$Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationType::Transcript::CAN_USE_INTERVAL_TREE` to decide whether to skip, i.e. whether the optional CPAN module Set::IntervalTree is installed. vepyr's interval tree is `coitrees`, a hard cargo dependency of `datafusion-bio-function-vep`, so there is no build in which it is absent and no runtime probe to port. desc: transcript_tree: the buffer's accessor gives back the same tree the runner built, so buffer and annotation source share one index
rationale: The getter/setter round trip at `Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:205-209`, asserted structurally against `$runner->get_TranscriptTree`. Its content is a sharing claim: the buffer windows variants with the same tree the annotation source later fetches transcripts from, so a variant can never be buffered into a window no transcript backs. vepyr has no object pair to share anything between — `PreparedContext::tx_trees` (dfbf 391f94bd `transcript_consequence.rs:890`) is built once inside the consequence engine and consumed there (`:1035`, queried at `:1240-1245`); nothing upstream of it batches by transcript, because the batching is by contig and row count (`InputBufferAccumulator::push_window_and_drain_ready`, `annotate_provider.rs:9552`).
