desc: get_max_from_tree: a 1 bp query at 25585733 returns 25607517, the far end of the whole overlapping transcript block, not of the transcript hit first
rationale: This is the file's substantive algorithm and the row a reviewer should push hardest on, because the ingredient looks present. `get_max_from_tree` (`Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:169-189`) is a fixpoint walk, not a query: it calls `$tree->fetch($c, $s - 1, $e)`, extends `$e` to the largest end among the hits, and repeats until `$e` stops moving — VEP's own comment calls the result `the beginning of the next intergenic region` (`:159-161`). The single overlap query underneath it IS reachable in vepyr and is already ported: ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=12-14 observe exactly that through `tests/port_transcript_tree.rs`, counting hits via `TranscriptEngineProfile::tx_candidates`. What is absent is the iteration. No vepyr code path re-queries the tree with a widened window: `evaluate_variant_prepared` issues one query per variant over `[start - max_dist, end + max_dist]` (dfbf 391f94bd `transcript_consequence.rs:1240-1245`) and stops. And the closure result is not observable even in principle through the public surface, because `tx_candidates` (`:678`) is a `usize` counter of nodes returned, not the coordinates that would let a caller compute a maximum. Missing feature: the transcript-block closure that defines a haplotype window.

desc: get_max_from_tree missed: a position 2 bp past the block returns 0, the sentinel that means `no window here`
rationale: The negative control for n=7, and not covered by it: n=7 shows the walk converging, this one shows it never starting, `$prev_max` staying 0 because the first `fetch` came back empty (`Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:174-178`). The sentinel is load-bearing rather than cosmetic — `next()` loops on `while(!$max && ...)` to skip intergenic variants entirely (`:133-136`) and returns an empty buffer on `return $buffer unless $max` (`:138`), so 0-vs-coordinate is what separates `skip this variant` from `open a window`. vepyr has no such decision to make: every input row is annotated, and a variant with no overlapping transcript yields an intergenic consequence rather than being passed over (`intergenic_outputs` in the engine profile, `transcript_consequence.rs:759`). Missing feature: the same one as n=7; this row pins its empty case.

desc: next - count: the first window over the shared test VCF holds exactly 34 variants
rationale: The size of a haplotype window is a derived quantity — the number of input variants whose start falls at or below the `get_max_from_tree` maximum on the same chromosome (`Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:141-144`) — so 34 is a joint assertion about the fixture, the transcript block and the loop bound. vepyr's batching is not derived from any of those. `InputBufferAccumulator::push_window_and_drain_ready` (dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_provider.rs:9552-9594`) drains on an accumulated input-unit count and never reads a coordinate, so there is no vepyr number that could be 34 for the same reason. Missing feature: variant batching whose boundary is a transcript block; vepyr's is a row budget.

desc: next - first element: a buffered variant is a plain hash of chr/start/end/ids/record/alleles carrying the untouched VCF columns, including the phased genotype `0|0`
rationale: The shape assertion, and it is about payload rather than plumbing, so it stays in the denominator. `Haplo::Parser::VCF::create_VariationFeatures` (`Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:181-194`, the hash literal at `:186-193`) returns a hash, not a VariationFeature, and keeps `record => \@{$parser->{record}}` — the whole VCF line including FORMAT and the per-sample column — because haplotype reconstruction downstream has to read each sample's phased GT. That is the field vepyr never materialises, and the scope of the measurement matters here more than anywhere else in this ledger. `grep -rlI --include='*.rs' -i genotype $DFBF/datafusion` returns exactly 1 file, and the hit is a `##FORMAT=<ID=GT...>` header string in `datafusion/bio-function-vep/tests/vcf_output_roundtrip.rs:24` — test data, not a decoder. `grep -rlI --include='*.rs' --include='*.py' -i genotype $VEPYR` returns 0. The unfiltered form does NOT: `grep -rlI -i genotype $VEPYR` returns 7, every one of them a golden or input VCF fixture under `tests/data/` whose FORMAT column carries the string. So the claim is precisely that no vepyr or dfbf *code* reads a genotype, and the fixtures are what a passthrough looks like: vepyr copies sample columns to the output VCF (`vcf_sink.rs:1105-1116`) and never parses them. Missing feature: per-sample phased-genotype input, without which the record hash has no purpose.

desc: next - last element: the window ends at rs141666402 / 25607474, inside the 25607517 bound n=7 computed and before the next block starts
rationale: Not subsumed by n=10: that row pins the shape of a buffered element, this one pins the window's right edge, and only this one would fail if the loop bound at `Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:141` used the first transcript's end instead of the closure maximum. Read together with n=7 it is the arithmetic of the whole design — 25607474 is under 25607517, so the buffer stopped because the parser handed it a variant past the bound (parked in `pre_buffer`, `:146`) and not because the file ran out. vepyr has no window and therefore no right edge; its drain boundary falls wherever the input-unit budget lands (`annotate_provider.rs:9552-9594`), which is a property of batch sizes rather than of the genome. Missing feature: as n=7.

desc: next again - first element: the second call opens a fresh window at the next transcript block (rs8132639 / 25639842) rather than continuing the first
rationale: The hand-off between calls, which is three cooperating pieces: `next()` clears the buffer with `reset_buffer()` first (`Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:122`), then re-reads the variant the previous call parked in `pre_buffer` before touching the parser (`:124`, `:133`), then re-runs the closure to get a new maximum. 25639842 is roughly 32 kb past where the first window ended, i.e. the intervening intergenic variants were skipped by the `while(!$max)` loop rather than buffered. vepyr's accumulator does the opposite by construction: it keeps the remainder of a partially drained batch on `pending_batches` and continues from it (`annotate_provider.rs:9622`), because a DataFusion stream is consumed once and nothing may be skipped. Missing feature: window-at-a-time iteration with skipped intergenic input.

desc: next again 2: a third call still returns a non-empty window, so windowing is not a two-shot special case
rationale: A deliberately weak assertion whose value is positional: it separates n=12 (the second window is correct) from n=14 (the fourth is empty), and without it an implementation that opened exactly two windows and then stopped would satisfy every other row in this file. That is worth keeping in the denominator even though the assertion itself only checks `> 0`. vepyr has nothing to call repeatedly — annotation is a single plan execution driven by DataFusion, with no caller-visible `next()` on any buffer; `InputBufferAccumulator` is private and reached only from `AnnotationWorkerState` (dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_provider.rs:10757`). Missing feature: an iterator surface over haplotype windows.

desc: next again 3 empty: once the parser is exhausted next() returns an empty arrayref, not undef
rationale: The termination contract, and the distinction is real in Perl: `next()` returns `$buffer` — an arrayref that `reset_buffer` has just emptied — on the `return $buffer unless $max` path (`Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:138`), so the caller loop in Haplo::Runner tests emptiness with `scalar @$vfs` and never has to guard for undef. vepyr expresses end-of-stream as `Poll::Ready(None)` from a DataFusion `RecordBatchStream`, a type-level distinction the compiler enforces rather than a value a test could observe, and there is no haplo buffer to observe it on in any case. Missing feature: the haplo buffer's iteration protocol; the empty-not-undef convention is the part of it this row pins.

desc: The 3 entries from chromosome 21 are in the same buffer: with fixture test_vcf3, the first window holds all three chr21 variants and stops at the chromosome change
rationale: The chromosome-boundary flush, asserted on a second fixture built for it. The buffer loop carries `&& $vf->{chr} eq $current_chr` alongside the coordinate bound (`Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:141`), so a variant on a new chromosome ends the window even when its start is numerically below the previous chromosome's maximum — which is the whole point, since haplotypes cannot span chromosomes. vepyr never faces the case: `ContigAnnotationExec` partitions the plan by contig before any buffering (`contig_partitions: Vec<Vec<String>>`, dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_provider.rs:8671-8700`) and both `LookupProvider::new` sites immediately restrict the scan — `provider.set_vcf_filter(Some(col(chrom).eq(lit(&*chrom))))` at `:13425` and the range-sliced form at `:13538`, the only two such sites in the crate. So the invariant holds in vepyr but is enforced three layers upstream and is not observable as a buffer flush. Missing feature: a buffer that decides its own chromosome boundary.

desc: The entry from chromosome 22 is in a different buffer: the next call yields exactly the one chr22 variant test_vcf3 holds
rationale: The other half of n=15 and not covered by it: n=15 shows the window closing at the boundary, this one shows the parked variant coming back. The mechanism is `pre_buffer` — the variant that failed the `eq` test was pushed there (`Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:146`) and is shifted off before the parser is touched again (`:133`), so it is buffered rather than dropped. An implementation that closed the window correctly and lost the straddling variant would pass n=15 and fail this row, which is why both exist. vepyr has no counterpart to `pre_buffer` at any visibility, and for the reason ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=8 sets out for the non-haplo buffer: the scan is already restricted to one contig, so no variant is ever read past a boundary and there is nothing to park. Missing feature: the lookahead slot that makes a self-flushing buffer lossless.

desc: The 3 entries from chr21 are in the same buffer: the same grouping holds when fixture test_vcf4 names its chromosomes `chr21`/`chr22`
rationale: Deliberately not a duplicate of n=15: the fixture changed from numeric `21` to prefixed `chr21`, and the assertion changed from `==` to `eq` to match. What it pins is that the boundary test at `Haplo/InputBuffer.pm:141` is a string comparison, so a non-numeric or prefixed chromosome name groups exactly as a numeric one does — and that the transcript tree was keyed with whatever name the input used, since a window can only open if `get_max_from_tree` found the chromosome. vepyr answers the naming half and not the grouping half: `normalize_chrom` strips a `chr` prefix when the tree is keyed (dfbf 391f94bd `transcript_consequence.rs:1029`, definition at `:3803`) and is private to that module. Missing feature: the grouping this row is really about; the naming half is present but is a different assertion, so this is not an analog-port.

desc: The entry from chr22 is in a different buffer: the prefixed-name fixture also flushes and re-emits the straddling variant
rationale: n=16 under the prefixed-name fixture, and it earns a separate row for the same reason n=16 does: it is the only assertion that would fail if the `chr22` variant were parked in `pre_buffer` and then dropped, or if `eq` had been left as the numeric `==` that would make `chr21 == chr22` compare 0 to 0 and silently merge the two windows into one. That second failure mode is the sharpest argument for keeping all four of n=15..n=18 in the denominator rather than collapsing them: numeric and string comparison agree on the first fixture and disagree on this one. vepyr has neither the flush nor the slot — see n=15 and n=16. Missing feature: as n=16.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the haplosaurus VCF parser class Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Haplo::Parser::VCF loads
rationale: A module-load probe, and therefore `not-applicable` under docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (`use_ok` is `not-applicable` unconditionally): Rust performs no runtime module load that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart whatever the class denotes -- and the reading below, that there is no symbol whose existence a compiler could check, is precisely the criterion R2 supersedes. The haplosaurus subsystem's absence is counted by the 10 rows of this ledger that exercise it, every one still `no-feature`; counting the module-load line as well counts one gap twice. The original rationale is kept below unchanged, for its account of what the subclass overrides. Not the same probe as n=2, and the difference decides the category: n=2 loads a class vepyr has a counterpart for, so its Rust answer is a link-time fact; this one loads haplosaurus, and there is no symbol whose existence a compiler could check. The class is a subclass of the ordinary VCF parser (`Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:68`) that overrides three things — `parser` eagerly builds the sample table (`:88-94`), `create_VariationFeatures` returns a raw hash instead of a VariationFeature (`:181-193`), and `validate_chr` warns instead of filtering (`:207-225`) — and all three exist only to feed haplotype reconstruction. Missing feature: haplosaurus, the protein-haplotype tool VEP ships as the separate `haplo` executable; its VCF front end is what this file tests. Same reading as ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=5 gives the sibling Haplo::Runner load.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config class loads under `use` before a config object is built
rationale: A module-load probe on ordinary VEP plumbing, not on anything haplo-specific: `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config` is loaded only so line 35 can build the config that line 71 hands the parser. Rust answers the same question at link time, and vepyr splits that one class in two — `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` for run options and `EnsemblCacheOptions` for cache identity — both of which this test crate already compiles against. Identical wording and identical treatment in ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=2 and ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=2.

desc: BASIC TESTS: Config->new returns a defined object for the base testing config
rationale: A constructor-truthiness probe: all it asserts is that `Config->new` returned something other than undef. By the ok($obj) ruling in docs/ledger-contract.md the category follows from what the class denotes, and Config denotes generic plumbing whose Rust analogue is an infallible struct — `EnsemblCacheOptions::new` (dfbf 391f94bd `bio-format-ensembl-cache` table_provider.rs:86) and `AnnotateVcfConfig::default()` cannot yield a null, so the type system already carries at compile time what this line checks at run time. The same reading was accepted for ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=3 and ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml n=3.

desc: new: the haplo VCF parser constructs over the shared test VCF
rationale: The ok($obj) ruling again, landing on the other arm: this class denotes a capability vepyr does not have, so the row stays in the denominator instead of leaving it with n=3. It is worth saying what makes the two differ, because the shape is identical. Config is a hash carrier; `Haplo::Parser::VCF` is the front end of a tool whose defining requirement is per-sample phased genotypes — its `parser` accessor calls `samples()` eagerly (`Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:88-94`) and `samples()` throws on a VCF that carries none (`:119`). vepyr accepts exactly that VCF as its normal input: when no FORMAT-derived sample names are found, `vcf_sink` falls back to schema metadata and then to a synthetic `SAMPLE` label, and errors in neither branch (`vcf_sink.rs:1120-1129`). Missing feature: a VCF reader for which sample data is mandatory. Distinguish from ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=4, which is an analog-port because Perl's `new` did directory resolution there and vepyr has a constructor consuming the same input; here `new` opens no file at all (the parse is lazy, `:88-98`) and vepyr has no haplo parser to construct.

desc: ref: the object new() returned is blessed into Haplo::Parser::VCF itself, i.e. no format dispatch happened
rationale: A blessing check, which docs/ledger-contract.md names as a legitimate not-applicable case: Rust has no run-time class tag, so `ref($p)` has no counterpart in any Rust design however the surrounding feature is built. The reason the line exists in Perl is real but does not survive translation — `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::new` is a factory that re-blesses into a format-specific subclass and returns a *different* object when a `format` key is present (Parser.pm:141-160) — and this call passes no `format`, so what is asserted is that the factory branch was not taken. In Rust the constructor's return type is the declaration; a function cannot return a different type depending on a hash key. Same treatment, same shape, as ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=11 (`ref(...) eq 'Set::IntervalTree'`). This is the row of this ledger a reviewer should push on first: the class it names is haplo-specific, so keeping it out of the denominator is the least conservative call here.

desc: no file: constructing the haplo VCF parser with no arguments at all dies with `No input file`
rationale: The message comes from the shared base — `die(ERROR: No input file given) unless $hashref->{file}` (Parser.pm:132) — but what the row pins is that *this* class carries that construction contract, and vepyr has no constructor here to carry one. The competing reading is not-applicable, on the grounds that vepyr's equivalent input path is a positional typed parameter (`annotate_to_vcf(input_vcf: &str, ...)`, dfbf 391f94bd `vcf_sink.rs:1018-1024`) so the state `no file was supplied` cannot be constructed and the compiler already refuses it. That reading loses on the contract's tie-break: it would take a row whose subject class is absent out of the denominator, and an over-counted gap is visible and arguable where an under-counted one is not. Same disposition as ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=13, the other throws_ok-on-a-missing-constructor-argument in the corpus. Missing feature: as n=4.

desc: samples: the VCF header's one sample column becomes a Sample entity wrapping an outbred Individual, both with negative synthetic dbIDs and display UNDISPLAYABLE
rationale: The whole structure is built by `Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:113-133`: for each name in the VCF header it mints a `Bio::EnsEMBL::Variation::Sample` (`:121`) wrapping a `Bio::EnsEMBL::Variation::Individual` (`:125`), numbering both with decreasing negative dbIDs so they are distinguishable from database-backed rows. Haplosaurus needs the entities because it reports haplotypes per individual. Be precise about what vepyr lacks here, because it is not sample awareness as such: `vcf_sink` does recover sample names, by splitting FORMAT column names of the form `<sample>_<FORMAT_ID>` (`vcf_sink.rs:1105-1116`) and falling back to the `bio.vcf.samples` schema metadata (`:1122-1127`), so it can rebuild the per-sample columns on output. What is absent is any entity behind the name, and any reading of the value: `grep -rlI --include='*.rs' -i genotype $DFBF/datafusion` returns 1 file, whose hit is a `##FORMAT=<ID=GT...>` header string in `tests/vcf_output_roundtrip.rs:24`, and the same command for `phased` returns 0; on the vepyr side the code-scoped form (`--include='*.rs' --include='*.py'`) returns 0 for both, while the unfiltered form returns 7 for `genotype`, all of them VCF fixtures under `tests/data/` — see this ledger's header for why the scope is part of the claim. Missing feature: sample and individual entities, the objects haplotype output is keyed by.

desc: no samples: a VCF whose header stops at INFO — eight columns, no FORMAT, no sample — is rejected with `no sample/individual entries`
rationale: The sharpest row in this file, because vepyr does not merely lack the check: it takes the opposite position. `samples()` throws on an empty sample list (`Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:119`) and `parser()` calls it eagerly (`:94`), so for haplosaurus a sample-less VCF is unusable by definition — there are no haplotypes without genotypes. A plain 8-column VCF is vepyr's ordinary input: `vcf_sink` leaves `sample_names` empty, tries the schema metadata, and only invents a `SAMPLE` label when FORMAT columns exist without one (`vcf_sink.rs:1120-1129`); no branch errors. So this is not a check waiting to be added but a requirement that would contradict the current product. Missing feature: the mandatory-genotype input contract that haplosaurus is built on. Not covered by n=7: that row asserts the shape of the sample table that *is* built, this one asserts refusal when it cannot be.

desc: parser ref: the lazily built reader is an ensembl-io VCF4 parser
rationale: A blessing check on the delegate, the same shape and the same disposition as ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=11. The accessor around it does real work — `parser()` memoises the reader and, on the first call only, runs `headers()` and `samples()` (`Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:88-98`) — but this line calls no method on what comes back, so once the class name is removed nothing portable is left. vepyr's delegate is `noodles-vcf` through `datafusion-bio-format-vcf`, and that substitution is exactly the `vepyr does it differently` the contract refuses as a not-applicable ground; it is admitted here only because the assertion's content is the Perl class tag itself, which no Rust design carries. The eager-samples side effect is what n=7 and n=8 pin.

desc: next - accounts for header fetch: the first record returned is the file's first data line, not the one the header read consumed, and it carries the raw VCF columns including the phased GT `0|0`
rationale: Two things at once, and the test name names the subtler one. Reading the header has to consume the first data line — `headers()` calls `$parser->next` and records that with `_have_read_next` (Parser/VCF.pm:154-156) — and the haplo `next()` consumes that flag instead of advancing again (`Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:155-156`), so no variant is lost to header parsing. The payload half is the hash `create_VariationFeatures` returns (`:186-193`): chr/start/end/ids/alleles plus `record => \@{$parser->{record}}`, the untouched VCF line, FORMAT and sample column included, because haplotype reconstruction reads each sample's GT from it. vepyr has neither half. It reads a VCF through a DataFusion table provider, where the header is schema and cannot consume a row, and it never parses the GT it copies through (see this ledger's header). Missing feature: a record hash that carries the genotype forward; the off-by-one the test name is about cannot arise in a schema-driven reader.

desc: next again: the second call advances to the next data line (rs187353664), so the reader is a cursor and not a re-read
rationale: Deliberately weaker than n=10 and not covered by it: n=10 would pass on a reader that returned its first record forever, and only this row rules that out. The cursor it pins is the ensembl-io parser's, driven one line at a time from `Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:148-167`. vepyr has no per-record cursor on any public surface — input arrives as `RecordBatch`es pulled by a DataFusion plan, and the accumulator that holds them is private (`InputBufferAccumulator`, dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_provider.rs:9521`, constructed only inside `AnnotationWorkerState` at `:10757`). Missing feature: the record-at-a-time reader interface haplosaurus drives; note this is the surface, not the data — the same variants do reach vepyr, in batches.

desc: validate chr - chromosome not in valid list: a record on chromosome 211 against valid_chromosomes [21] scores 0
rationale: `validate_chr` exists only in the haplo subclass (`Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:207-225`; the base class has no sub of that name, only the shared helper `_have_chr` at Parser.pm:770, which it calls at `:219`). Its contract is warn-and-report, and the report is the return value this row reads. vepyr has no equivalent judgement: a contig the cache does not carry is not diagnosed against a valid list — the only contig check in the crate is `validate_contig_identity` (`annotate_provider.rs:8656`), which compares a cache partition against its own identity metadata, a different question asked of a different object. Missing feature: input-record validation against the annotation source's chromosome list. Worth recording as an upstream oddity while the row is being argued: `Haplo::Parser::VCF::next` calls `validate_chr($vf)` in void context (`:163`) and returns the record anyway, so in the haplo pipeline this boolean is only ever a warning trigger.

desc: validate chr message - chromosome not in valid list: the warning reaching STDERR reads `Chromosome 211 not found in annotation sources`
rationale: The message text, captured by redirecting STDERR into a scalar (t/Haplo_Parser_VCF.t:95-99), which makes it a contract and not an implementation detail: it names the offending chromosome so a user can grep for it. vepyr has no warnings channel to carry such a line — the same absence ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=35-37 records for `warning_msg` and its `warning_file` sidecar, where dfbf offers only `log::warn!` whose destination is chosen by whoever installs the logger. Missing feature: a per-record diagnostic stream with a stable message format. Not covered by n=12: an implementation that returned 0 silently would pass that row and fail this one.

desc: validate chr - genomic position not valid: a record whose start is the literal `x` scores 0, before the chromosome is even looked at
rationale: The first guard in `validate_chr`, ordered ahead of the chromosome check: `looks_like_number($vf->{start}) && looks_like_number($vf->{end})` (`Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:214`). The property is tolerance — a malformed coordinate is reported and the run continues. vepyr cannot reach this state and cannot express that policy: `start` and `end` are non-nullable `UInt32` Arrow fields (datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0, `bio-format-vcf/src/header_builder.rs:365-366`), so a non-numeric POS fails during VCF decoding and takes the scan with it rather than being skipped. Missing feature: per-record fault tolerance on the input path. This row and n=12 are two different guards with two different messages, so neither subsumes the other.

desc: validate chr message - genomic position invalid: the warning reads `WARNING: Start x or end 25585733 coordinate invalid`, echoing both coordinates
rationale: The message half of n=14, and the pair is the same split as n=12/n=13: the score says a record was rejected, the text says which field made it invalid — here both coordinates are echoed, so a user can see that the end was fine and the start was not. The `WARNING: ` prefix is VEP's sidecar format, whose absence from vepyr ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=36 records in detail (a `log` record carries a level, and its layout belongs to the embedding process). Missing feature: as n=13. Note the two messages differ in prefix — `WARNING: ` here (`Haplo/Parser/VCF.pm:215`), none at `:220` — which is upstream inconsistency the ledger records rather than repairs.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the AnnotationType::Transcript role loads, so its CAN_USE_INTERVAL_TREE flag can gate the first SKIP block
rationale: A module-load probe, and one of only two assertions in this file outside a haplo-gated region (the other is n=24). What it asserts is that Perl found and compiled Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/AnnotationType/Transcript.pm at run time; Rust answers that at compile time, so a runtime assertion would restate the compiler. The reason for the load is Perl-only: line 39 reads `$Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationType::Transcript::CAN_USE_INTERVAL_TREE` to decide whether to skip, i.e. whether the optional CPAN module Set::IntervalTree is installed, whereas vepyr's interval tree is `coitrees`, a hard cargo dependency of `datafusion-bio-function-vep`, present in every build. Identical line and identical treatment in ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=1 and ledger/Haplo_InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=1.

desc: the haplosaurus driver class Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Haplo::Runner loads
rationale: A module-load probe, and therefore `not-applicable` under docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (`use_ok` is `not-applicable` unconditionally): Rust performs no runtime module load that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart whatever the class denotes -- and the reading below, that there is no symbol whose existence a compiler could check, is precisely the criterion R2 supersedes. The absence of a haplosaurus driver is counted by the 22 rows of this ledger that exercise it, every one still `no-feature`; counting the module-load line as well counts one gap twice. The original rationale is kept below unchanged, because n=3 and n=24 cite this ordinal for its `_core` pymodule measurement. Not the same probe as n=1: that one loads a class vepyr has a counterpart for, so its Rust answer is a link-time fact; this one loads haplosaurus, and there is no symbol whose existence a compiler could check. `Haplo::Runner` is what upstream's separate `haplo` executable is a wrapper around (`use Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Haplo::Runner` at haplo:20, plus haplo-only options such as `haplotype_frequencies`). vepyr exposes no such entry point: its `_core` pymodule registers one class (`StreamingAnnotator`) and seven functions — `build_cache`, `build_cache_entity`, `build_plugin_cache`, `create_annotator`, `annotate_vcf`, `supported_vep_targets_json`, `cache_contig_identity_json` (vepyr 346b9173 `src/lib.rs:372-382`) — the annotator and its cache, and nothing else. Missing feature: the haplosaurus driver. Same reading as ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=5, the same `use_ok` on the same class. Distinct from n=24, which repeats the load inside the JSON block.

desc: new is defined: the haplosaurus runner constructs from the offline test config with test.vcf as input
rationale: By the ok($obj) ruling in docs/ledger-contract.md the category follows from what the class denotes, and this class denotes a whole tool vepyr does not ship — so `no-feature`, not the `not-applicable` an infallible struct literal would earn. The line is load-bearing rather than decoration: `new` runs `BaseRunner::new` and then rewrites two parameters, `haplo` (n=5) and a default `output_file` of `haplo_output.txt` (Haplo/Runner.pm:102-103), so construction is where the run mode is decided. Missing feature: as n=2.

desc: check class: the object new() returned is blessed into Haplo::Runner itself
rationale: A blessing check, which docs/ledger-contract.md names as a legitimate not-applicable case: Rust has no run-time class tag, so `ref($runner)` has no counterpart in any Rust design however the surrounding feature is built. It is weaker here than the same idiom in ledger/Haplo_Parser_VCF.ledger.toml n=5, where `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::new` really can re-bless into a format-specific subclass (Parser.pm:141-160) and the assertion therefore rules something out; `BaseRunner::new` has no such factory branch, so this line can only ever agree with the class it was called on. Same shape and disposition as ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=11.

desc: haplo param set by new: constructing the runner sets the `haplo` flag to 1, i.e. the mode is chosen by which class you build
rationale: `$self->param('haplo', 1)` (Haplo/Runner.pm:102) is how the rest of VEP learns it is running haplosaurus rather than the annotator: shared code reads that flag rather than checking the runner's class. vepyr has no such mode and no option that could carry one — `AnnotateVcfConfig` declares 34 public fields (dfbf 391f94bd `vcf_sink.rs:381-456`) covering pick order, HGVS, cache flavour, distances, workers and plugins, and none of them is haplotype-related; measured, `grep -ci haplo` over that struct definition returns 0. Missing feature: a haplotype run mode. This row is not covered by n=3: a constructor could return a defined object and set no parameter at all.

desc: get_all_AnnotationSources: exactly one source, a Haplo::AnnotationSource::Cache::Transcript, with its whole attribute hash — dir, cache_region_size 1000000, the parsed info.txt (GRCh38.p5, GENCODE 24, dbSNP 149, ...) and valid_chromosomes [21, 22, LRG_485]
rationale: Be precise about which half is missing, because half of this hash is already ported. The info.txt parse and the chromosome list have vepyr counterparts and are claimed in ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=23 through `tests/port_cache_dir.rs::info_txt_facts_surface_in_the_provider_schema`, which asserts the same v84 fixture's species, assembly, cache_version and variation columns. What has no counterpart is the subject of the assertion: the *haplo* subclass of the transcript cache source, whose reason for existing is that its `annotate_InputBuffer` returns TranscriptHaplotypeContainer objects instead of consequences. That class is issue #30's file (t/Haplo_AnnotationSource_Cache_Transcript.t) and is not claimed here. Missing feature: a haplotype-producing annotation source; the cache underneath it is present.

desc: setup_db_connection: in offline mode the call returns silently rather than opening a registry connection
rationale: The assertion is that a database connection was *not* attempted: `setup_db_connection` returns immediately when `offline` is set (BaseRunner.pm:113-116) and only otherwise inits the Ensembl registry (`:124-125`). vepyr is cache-only — docs/ledger-contract.md's standing no-feature example — with no DBI dependency, no registry and no connection code, so there is no operation that could be skipped and no offline switch to skip it. Asserting `nothing happened because there is no database` would assert vepyr's permanent state rather than a behaviour it computes; that is exactly the reading ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=38 gives the sibling `get_database_assembly - no DB` row. Missing feature: the database-backed annotation path, and with it the offline/online distinction.

desc: valid_chromosomes: the runner republishes its annotation source's chromosome list, [21, 22, LRG_485], as its own
rationale: It would be easy to hand this row to `tests/port_transcript_tree.rs::chromosome_set_is_derived_from_the_source_transcripts`, which ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml n=9 names for the same three chromosomes, and it would be wrong. The contract's dual-claim rule asks whether the shared test could fail if only this row's behaviour regressed. It could not: that test observes the chromosome set derived from the transcripts themselves (`normalize_chrom` over `PreparedContext::tx_trees`, dfbf 391f94bd `transcript_consequence.rs:1029-1041`), while this row pins a *delegation* — `BaseRunner::valid_chromosomes` (`:444`) asking its annotation source and caching the answer on the runner. A runner that returned the wrong list would leave the tree's key set untouched. vepyr has no runner object at all: annotation is a DataFusion plan, so there is no second surface that could republish the list correctly or incorrectly. Missing feature: the runner-level chromosome list.

desc: get_Parser: the runner wires a Haplo::Parser::VCF with the input file, the source's valid_chromosomes as a lookup hash and a tab delimiter, leaving individual / individual_zyg / phased unset
rationale: The wiring itself is the assertion: `get_Parser` passes exactly config, file and valid_chromosomes (Haplo/Runner.pm:348-352) and everything else in the expected hash is a default inherited from `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser`. The three that matter are `individual`, `individual_zyg` and `phased`, all undef — VEP's per-sample options are *not* how haplosaurus reaches genotypes; the haplo parser reads them from the raw record instead (ledger/Haplo_Parser_VCF.ledger.toml n=10). vepyr has neither end of this: no runner to do the wiring, and no per-sample options to leave unset — `AnnotateVcfConfig`'s 34 fields (`vcf_sink.rs:381-456`) contain no individual, no zygosity and no phase. Missing feature: the haplo parser and the object that configures it.

desc: get_TranscriptTree: the runner builds a TranscriptTree over its annotation source, and the tree carries the same chromosome list — asserted with the built trees deleted first
rationale: Note the fixture surgery two lines above: `delete $t->{trees}` (t/Haplo_Runner.t:124) removes the Set::IntervalTree objects so that what remains to compare is the wiring, not the index. So this row is about construction — `TranscriptTree->new({config, annotation_source => $self->get_AnnotationSource})` (Haplo/Runner.pm:400-403) — and the tree's own behaviour belongs to ledger/TranscriptTree.ledger.toml, which ports it as analog-port rows through `tests/port_transcript_tree.rs`. vepyr builds the equivalent index (`PreparedContext::tx_trees`, dfbf 391f94bd `transcript_consequence.rs:1035`) inside the consequence engine, from the transcripts, with no runner and no annotation-source object in between. Missing feature: the runner-level assembly step; the index it assembles exists.

desc: get_InputBuffer: the runner hands the haplo buffer its parser and its transcript tree, plus buffer_size and the two out-of-order tolerances
rationale: The row that closes the wiring chain n=9 and n=10 open: `get_InputBuffer` passes config, the memoised parser and the memoised tree (Haplo/Runner.pm:374-378), which is what makes the buffer window variants against the same index the annotation source will use — the sharing ledger/Haplo_InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=6 asserts from the buffer's side. vepyr has no such triple to assemble. Recorded while reading, and reported on the PR rather than repaired: the expected value is blessed into `Bio::EnsEMBL::Haplo::VEP::InputBuffer` (t/Haplo_Runner.t:143), a package that does not exist upstream — `git ls-tree -r --name-only release/116.0 | grep -c modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/Haplo/` returns 0 against 8 for `modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/Haplo/` — and the assertion passes anyway because `is_deeply` compares structure and ignores the blessed package (probed locally with a two-line Test::More script). Missing feature: as n=9 and n=10.

desc: haplotype_frequencies - no hex header found: a frequency file whose header line declares no `hex` column is refused
rationale: The frequency table is keyed by the md5 hex of a haplotype's sequence, so a header without a `hex` column cannot be joined to anything and is rejected up front (Haplo/Runner.pm:451). The fixture is deliberately absurd — the gzipped test VCF — which is what makes the check observable at all. vepyr has no frequency table: haplotype frequencies are population statistics about haplotypes, and there are no haplotypes to have statistics about (see this ledger's header measurement). Missing feature: the haplotype-frequency side input, which n=12 through n=18 collectively describe. Not covered by n=13: that row is the headerless path, which never reaches this check.

desc: haplotype_frequencies - no hex column found: with no header line at all, a first column that is not a 32-character md5sum is refused
rationale: The headerless fallback's entry condition: with no `#` line the loader inspects the first data row and accepts it only if column 0 matches `/^[a-fA-F0-9]{32}$/`, otherwise throwing `first column should be an md5sum` (Haplo/Runner.pm:460-465). The fixture is the chromosome-synonyms file, whose first column is a chromosome name. This is a different failure mode from n=12 — that one has a header and no hex, this one has no header and no hex — and an implementation could plausibly get one right and the other wrong. Missing feature: as n=12.

desc: haplotype_frequencies: a well-formed frequency file loads and the accessor returns a true hash
rationale: The positive control for n=12 and n=13, and the precondition for n=15, n=16 and n=21. `haplotype_frequencies` is a getter/setter that parses on write and memoises on `{_haplotype_frequencies}` (Haplo/Runner.pm:427-490), so this line pins that the happy path returns the populated table rather than dying or returning empty. vepyr has no side input of any kind that is keyed by a sequence hash; the nearest thing in the crate, the plugin cache (`plugin_cache_root` in `AnnotateVcfConfig`, `vcf_sink.rs:381-456`), is keyed by genomic position. Missing feature: as n=12.

desc: haplotype_frequencies - check data 1: hex 79d615f3... maps to a single row carrying a transcript id and six population frequencies (ALL 0.889, AFR 0.708, AMR, EAS, EUR, SAS)
rationale: The parsed shape: a hex maps to an *arrayref* of rows even when there is only one, each row a hash of header name to value with the `hex` column deleted after it becomes the key (Haplo/Runner.pm:480-483). The populations are 1000 Genomes super-populations, and the values are the frequencies haplosaurus prints in column 6 of its output (n=21). vepyr has no table and no column to print it in. Missing feature: as n=12. Not covered by n=14, which only asserts the table is non-empty.

desc: haplotype_frequencies - check data 2: hex 91212e92... maps to TWO rows, the same frequencies under two different transcript ids
rationale: The multi-row case, and the reason the value is an arrayref at all: one protein haplotype hash can be reached from several transcripts, so the table has to keep them apart by transcript id — which is what the `transcript` column is for, and what the output path then selects on (`grep {$_->{transcript} eq $tr_stable_id}`, Haplo/Runner.pm:271-273). An implementation that overwrote instead of pushing would pass n=15 and fail this row. vepyr has neither the table nor the many-transcripts-one-haplotype relation, because it has no haplotypes. Missing feature: as n=12.

desc: haplotype_frequencies - no header: the same data with its header line stripped loads on a freshly built runner
rationale: The headerless happy path, deliberately run on a new runner (t/Haplo_Runner.t:192) because the loader memoises and merges into `{_haplotype_frequencies}` — a second load onto the old object would not have been a clean test. It is the positive counterpart of n=13: same absent header, but a first column that *is* an md5sum, so the column-name guesser runs instead of the throw. vepyr has no frequency loader in either shape. Missing feature: as n=12.

desc: haplotype_frequencies - no header - check data: with no header the columns are named by inspection — unknown1 for the transcript id, freq1..freq6 for the six values in [0,1]
rationale: The guesser itself, and it is a real piece of behaviour rather than a fallback stub: every column after the hex is called `freq<N>` when it looks like a number in [0, 1] and `unknown<N>` otherwise, numbered independently, and the whole file is rejected if not one column looked like a frequency (Haplo/Runner.pm:468-475). So a transcript id becomes `unknown1` and the six frequencies become `freq1`..`freq6` in file order, and those invented names reach the output verbatim (n=22). vepyr has no schema-inference step on any side input. Missing feature: as n=12; this row is the part of it that would be easiest to get subtly wrong.

desc: init: the whole setup sequence — post_setup_checks, DB, synonyms, annotation source, FASTA, frequencies, input buffer, stats — runs and reports success
rationale: `init` is the runner's one-shot setup: it memoises on `{_initialized}` so `run()` can call it unconditionally (Haplo/Runner.pm:128-159), and its eight steps are exactly the objects n=6 through n=14 test individually — this row is what pins that they compose. vepyr has no initialisation phase to assert: the equivalent work is done lazily by DataFusion when the plan executes, and `annotate_to_vcf` (dfbf 391f94bd `vcf_sink.rs:1018-1024`) builds and runs the plan in one call with no separately observable setup. Missing feature: the runner lifecycle. Note `post_setup_checks` inside it is haplo-specific — it refuses `--json` when the JSON module is missing (`:174-178`), the gate the second SKIP block of this file reads.

desc: run - check output: the whole tab-delimited haplosaurus report for test.vcf — six lines, transcript / CDS-haplotype name / protein-haplotype name / contributing rsIDs / per-sample counts, across three transcripts
rationale: The product itself, and the row that makes the rest of this file matter. `dump_TranscriptHaplotypeContainer` builds each line from eight fields — transcript id, CDS haplotype name, its flags, protein haplotype name, its flags, frequencies, contributing variation names, per-sample counts — sorted by count then name and with reference haplotypes dropped (Haplo/Runner.pm:256-300). Every column is a haplotype concept: `ENST00000352957:91T>C,612A>G` names a CDS haplotype by its accumulated differences, `ENSP00000284967:31S>P` the protein one, `HG00096:1` the count for one sample. vepyr emits VCF rows with a CSQ string, one record per variant per transcript; there is no representation in which two variants on one transcript become one output line. Missing feature: haplotype reconstruction and its report format — the whole tool.

desc: run with haplotype_frequencies: for the ENST00000307301:612 haplotype, column 6 of the report carries the six population=frequency pairs from the loaded table, with the transcript column dropped
rationale: This is where n=15's table meets n=20's report: the writer looks the protein haplotype's hex up in the frequency table, picks the row whose transcript matches, and joins the remaining columns as `NAME=VALUE` pairs — dropping the `transcript` key itself, which is why the expected hash has six entries and not seven (Haplo/Runner.pm:267-288). Not covered by n=15: that row asserts what was parsed, this one asserts that the right row was selected and re-serialised into the output. vepyr has neither end. Missing feature: as n=20, with the frequency join of n=12.

desc: run with haplotype_frequencies - no header: the same report column carries the guessed names — unknown1=ENST00000307301 plus freq1..freq6 — so invented column names reach the output verbatim
rationale: The consequence of n=18 observed at the far end of the pipeline, and the reason both rows exist: because the header was guessed, the `transcript` column was never identified as such, so the drop-the-transcript-key step of n=21 does not fire and `unknown1=ENST00000307301` is printed as if it were a population. That is upstream's actual behaviour, asserted deliberately — the expected hash has seven entries where n=21's has six. vepyr has no output column that could carry either. Missing feature: as n=21.

desc: run - use input_data: feeding the same VCF as an in-memory string instead of a file path produces byte-identical output to n=20
rationale: Two claims in one line. The input channel: `get_Parser` opens a filehandle onto a scalar when `input_data` is set and hands that to the parser in place of a path (Haplo/Runner.pm:343-346) — vepyr has no such channel, since `annotate_to_vcf(input_vcf: &str, ...)` takes a path and nothing else (dfbf 391f94bd `vcf_sink.rs:1018-1024`), and `StreamingAnnotator` on the Python side is likewise path-driven. The equality claim: the two channels must agree byte for byte, which is why the expected block is n=20's repeated verbatim rather than abbreviated. Missing feature: in-memory input, on top of the haplotype report of n=20. Not a duplicate of n=20 — that row would still pass if `input_data` were ignored and the file read instead.

desc: test JSON output: the Haplo::Runner class is loaded again at the top of the JSON block, before that block's own skip is evaluated
rationale: A module-load probe, and therefore `not-applicable` under docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (`use_ok` is `not-applicable` unconditionally): Rust performs no runtime module load that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart whatever the class denotes -- and the reading below, that there is no symbol whose existence a compiler could check, is precisely the criterion R2 supersedes. The absence of a haplosaurus driver is counted by the same 22 rows; counting the module-load line as well counts one gap twice. The original rationale is kept below unchanged, because n=1 and n=2 cite this ordinal. Its distinct content -- that this load sits above the block's own `skip`, so it runs even where n=2 does not -- is unaffected by the reclassification: R2 applies to a `use_ok` wherever it sits. The same module as n=2, and its distinct content is where it sits: it is placed *above* `skip 'Set::IntervalTree or JSON not installed', 1` (t/Haplo_Runner.t:334 vs :338), so unlike n=2 it runs even on a machine with neither optional module. Whether that is deliberate or an accident of editing, the effect is that this is the one haplo assertion in the file that always executes. It is still a load probe for a class vepyr does not have, so it is `no-feature` for n=2's reason and not `not-applicable` for n=1's: there is no symbol whose existence a compiler could check. Missing feature: as n=2.

desc: JSON output: the first emitted record decodes to a whole TranscriptHaplotypeContainer — total counts, two protein haplotypes and two CDS haplotypes with hex, name, count, sample map, population frequencies, contributing variants, diffs and SIFT/PolyPhen predictions
rationale: The richest assertion in the three Haplo ledgers, and it is one object rather than a report: with `--json` the writer serialises the container itself through `JSON->new->convert_blessed`, honouring `dont_export` to drop the sequence fields (Haplo/Runner.pm:240-250). Every key is a haplotype concept with no vepyr counterpart — `hex` is the md5 that n=15's table is keyed by, `other_hexes` links a protein haplotype to the CDS haplotypes that produce it, `diffs` carries per-difference SIFT and PolyPhen predictions, `population_frequencies` is `count / total`. vepyr does emit JSON-adjacent metadata (`supported_vep_targets_json`, `cache_contig_identity_json`, vepyr 346b9173 `src/lib.rs:381-382`) but nothing that serialises an annotation result as an object graph; its output is VCF with a CSQ string. Missing feature: the container and its JSON form. Not covered by n=20: that is the tab format of the same objects, and the JSON carries fields the tab format never prints.

desc: warning message because of empty output: a VCF whose variants overlap no transcript makes run() warn `Haplosaurus can't find transcripts...`, rather than exit quietly on an empty report
rationale: The empty-result diagnostic: `run` counts the lines it emitted and warns when the count is zero or unset (Haplo/Runner.pm:213-215), so a user whose input simply misses every transcript is told rather than left with a zero-byte file. It is worth noting how the assertion is written, because the enumerator's numbering depends on it: line 496 is `my $warning = warning { $runner->run() };`, a *capture* rather than an assertion, deliberately excluded by the statement-boundary rule (docs/enumerator-rules.md names this exact line as the one excluded `warning` call in the corpus), and the row is the `like` on the next line. vepyr has no counterpart at either end: no haplotype report to be empty, and no warnings channel to carry the message — the same absence ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=35-37 records for `warning_msg`. Missing feature: as n=20, plus the empty-output diagnostic on top of it.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the InputBuffer module loads under `use`
rationale: A module-load probe, and therefore `not-applicable` under docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (`use_ok` is `not-applicable` unconditionally), which supersedes this row's earlier reading. That reading's substance survives as a fact: vepyr exposes no InputBuffer type on any surface, and the nearest thing — `InputBufferAccumulator` (dfbf 391f94bd, `annotate_provider.rs:9522`), a private struct over `VecDeque<RecordBatch>` and two counters — is not one, because the annotate pipeline reaches the same end through a DataFusion plan rather than an object. What changes is that the fact belongs to the rows that exercise the buffer, not to the line that loads its module: this ledger's remaining 44 `no-feature` rows are collectively about exactly that absence. R2 also makes the file's three `use_ok` rows consistent — n=2 (Config) and n=3 (Parser::VCF) were already `not-applicable`.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config module loads under `use` before a config object is built
rationale: The second module-load probe, for `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config`. vepyr's configuration is the `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` struct (dfbf 391f94bd `vcf_sink.rs:381`), whose existence this crate proves by compiling against it; there is no runtime load step that could fail and therefore nothing to assert. See n=1.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the VCF parser module loads under `use`
rationale: The third module-load probe. vepyr reads VCF through `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`, a compile-time dependency of this crate declared in Cargo.toml; nothing is loaded at runtime and nothing can fail to load. See n=1.

desc: BASIC TESTS: Config->new returns a defined object for base_testing_cfg plus buffer_size => 10
rationale: A constructor-truthiness probe — it asserts `Config->new` returned something other than `undef`. The vepyr analogue is `AnnotateVcfConfig { buffer_size: 10, ..Default::default() }`, a plain struct built by literal initialisation (`vcf_sink.rs:381-456`): infallible, and it cannot yield a null. The Rust type system carries at compile time the guarantee this line checks at runtime — Perl-runtime plumbing, per docs/ledger-contract.md's not-applicable list. The value 10 is not asserted here; rows 13/15/16 carry the buffer_size claim.

desc: BASIC TESTS: Parser::VCF->new returns a defined object for the chr21 test VCF
rationale: Reclassified by the corpus-wide constructor-probe sweep (old-repo issue #120), which supersedes the provisional not-applicable this row carried. docs/ledger-contract.md's `ok($obj)` ruling decides such a row by what the class denotes, and `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` denotes reading a VCF input file — a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, which is the ruling's third line. The type that stands in is `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`: vepyr never hands a caller a parser object, so the nearest thing an external crate can construct is the provider `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` registers internally (`vcf_sink.rs:1074` and `:1079` @ dfbf 391f94bd, both `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` — the five arguments the named test passes), which is why this is analog-port and not unit-port. The probe is load-bearing rather than plumbing because that constructor is genuinely fallible: it `block_on`s `determine_schema_from_header` and propagates with `?` (`table_provider.rs:869-879` @ datafusion-bio-formats v1.10.0 = 0d9730c8), i.e. it reads and parses the VCF header before it can return — exactly the ruling's defined/undef -> `Ok`/`Err` case. The named test asserts both limbs: `Ok` over a one-row VCF written to a tempdir, and over a missing path a typed error that is classified `NotFound` and names the path — because an `is_ok()` on its own would also pass against a constructor that never fails. Dual-claimed with the fourteen sibling rows the sweep moved together; all fifteen are the same statement at the same boundary, and the roster is kept in one place, the table at the top of tests/port_parser_vcf_construct.rs. The `valid_chromosomes` argument this call adds is not a boundary difference: `ok($p)` inspects no argument, so the assertion holds for any defined return and would still hold if the file were empty. What that argument does is ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml's subject.

desc: BASIC TESTS: InputBuffer->new blesses into Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer
rationale: `is(ref($ib), 'Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::InputBuffer')` is a blessing probe: it asserts which package the reference was blessed into. docs/ledger-contract.md names assertions about blessing and Perl object identity as legitimately not-applicable — Rust has no blessing, and the type of the analogous value is fixed at compile time. That vepyr has no InputBuffer type at all is the claim of n=7..11, which stay in the denominator as gaps.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: a freshly constructed InputBuffer exposes an empty `buffer` accessor
rationale: Ported through the `test-internals` overlay, which is what retired the `blocked-api` reason this row carried as docs/ledger-contract.md's worked example of present-but-private state. Probed, not assumed. At the BASE pin 391f94bd the item is declared without `pub` (`struct InputBufferAccumulator` `annotate_provider.rs:9522`), and a `use` of a sibling private item of the same module still answers `error[E0603]: function `alt_input_units` is private … note: … defined here … annotate_provider.rs:9681:1` — run 2026-08-31 in this crate, with five known-public controls (`cache_lookup_column_names`, `AnnotateProvider`, `TranscriptConsequenceEngine`, `vcf_to_vep_allele`, `VcfTableProvider`) resolving in the same compilation, so the refusal is the item's and not the crate path's. The accessor the test calls is `annotate_provider::test_internals::InputBufferAccumulator` (overlay `dfbf_test_overlay`, sha aa2be930), a newtype whose `new()` is `super::InputBufferAccumulator::default()` and whose methods delegate to `:9529` / `:9552` / `:9566`; no base item is widened, deleted or changed, so parity is still measured against the base. CHANNEL: Perl asserts an empty ARRAY (`$ib->buffer`); vepyr has no `VariationFeature` list to take `scalar @` of, so emptiness is read off the row counter `pending_rows()` (`:9529`) together with the drain returning no ready buffer when asked with nothing to give. Measured: `pending_rows()` 0 before and after an empty window, and 0 ready buffers. That the value the test builds is the value the engine builds is not assumed either: `AnnotationWorkerState::new` sets `input_buffer_accumulator: InputBufferAccumulator::default()` (`:10757`), the same `#[derive(Default)]` (`:9521`) the newtype's `new()` calls.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: a freshly constructed InputBuffer exposes an empty `pre_buffer`
rationale: `pre_buffer` is VEP's lookahead staging area — an ARRAY ref, not a single slot (`sub pre_buffer` is `return $_[0]->{pre_buffer} ||= [];`, InputBuffer.pm:588-590), though in the flow this file exercises exactly one variant is ever parked in it. `next()` cannot push a variant back onto the parser, so a variant read past a chromosome boundary goes there instead (`:223-233`). vepyr has no counterpart, and the reason is not that its accumulator ignores contigs — an earlier draft of this ledger said that and it was wrong. vepyr does keep one buffer to one contig, but enforces it three layers upstream rather than in the buffer: `ContigAnnotationExec` (dfbf 391f94bd `annotate_provider.rs:8671`) partitions the plan by contig (`contig_partitions: Vec<Vec<String>>`, built by `partition_contigs_for_execution`), and both `LookupProvider::new` sites immediately restrict the scan to the contig being processed — `provider.set_vcf_filter(Some(col("chrom").eq(lit(&*chrom))))` at `:13425`, and the range-sliced form at `:13538`. Measured: `grep -n 'LookupProvider::new' src/*.rs` returns exactly 2 hits (`:13415`, `:13517`) and `grep -n 'set_vcf_filter' src/*.rs` returns 3 (those two call sites plus the definition at `lookup_provider.rs:225`). So `InputBufferAccumulator::push_window_and_drain_ready` (`:9552-9594`) can drain purely on an input-unit count, never reading `chrom`, and still never span a contig — the invariant is real but IMPLICIT, enforced upstream and asserted nowhere near the code that relies on it. Because the scan is already restricted to one contig, no variant is ever read past a boundary and there is nothing to stage. The accumulator does keep a remainder — `drain_input_units` slices a batch and pushes the tail back onto `pending_batches` (`:9622`) — but that is a partial-batch remainder within one contig, not a boundary artefact. Missing feature: the lookahead staging area.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: rejoin_required is 0 on a buffer that has not read anything yet
rationale: `rejoin_required` (InputBuffer.pm:607) is the flag half of VEP's two-phase minimal pipeline: `split_variants` decomposes a multi-ALT VF into one VF per ALT and sets the flag (`:717`) so a later rejoin can merge the per-allele consequences back onto one output line. vepyr has no rejoin phase — a multi-ALT VCF row is counted as one input unit per ALT from the start (`batch_input_units`, `annotate_provider.rs:9692`, over `alt_input_units`, `:9681`) and each ALT is annotated and emitted independently — so there is no state that could be false before the first read. Missing feature: the split/rejoin round trip. The trimming primitive it wraps is present in the pinned crate but is reached from vepyr's colocated-allele path, not its input path — which is why n=70 and n=71 are no-feature too, and why the tests that exercise it are booked as vepyr-only rather than as a port of this file.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: reset_buffer empties a buffer that had an element pushed onto it
rationale: A lifecycle assertion on a reusable buffer object: push, reset, observe empty (InputBuffer.pm:535). vepyr's accumulator is drained, never reset — `push_window_and_drain_ready` returns whole buffers and leaves the remainder pending (`annotate_provider.rs:9552-9594`); there is no operation that discards buffered rows, and no caller that would want one, because a DataFusion stream is consumed exactly once. Missing feature: the reset lifecycle. Note VEP's `reset_buffer` also drops the memoised interval and hash trees, which is the n=21/22 feature.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: reset_pre_buffer empties a pre_buffer that had an element pushed onto it
rationale: The same lifecycle assertion for the lookahead staging area n=8 describes (InputBuffer.pm:551). Both the array and the operation that clears it are absent, and for the reason n=8 gives: vepyr's plan is partitioned per contig upstream of the buffer, so nothing is ever read past a boundary and staged. Note this row and n=8 assert different things about the same array — n=8 that it starts empty, this one that an explicit reset empties it again — so neither subsumes the other.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: next() returns an ARRAY reference
rationale: A Perl reference-type probe. The container type of the vepyr counterpart is a compile-time fact — `push_window_and_drain_ready` returns `Vec<Vec<RecordBatch>>` (`annotate_provider.rs:9552-9557`) and the public surface returns a typed DataFusion stream — so a runtime assertion would restate the type checker. Same family as the `isa_ok`-on-a-reference probes docs/ledger-contract.md excludes. What next() returns INSIDE that array is the claim of n=13 and n=14.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: the first next() fills the buffer to exactly buffer_size (10) variants
rationale: Same input file, not the same shape on other data: Perl drives the buffer from `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF` over `$test_cfg->{test_vcf}` = upstream `t/testdata/input/test.vcf`, and that file is vendored here as `tests/data/vep116_runner_input/test.vcf.gz` (132 records, all contig 21). The port reads it through `VcfTableProvider` and hands the batches to the accumulator. CHANNEL: one `next()` is `push_window_and_drain_ready_limited(batches, 10, false, 1)` — the `max_ready_buffers` cap turns the engine's window-at-a-time drain (`:11944`, `config.input_buffer_size`) into a call-at-a-time one — and the drained buffer's `RecordBatch` row count replaces `scalar @$vfs`. Measured: 1 buffer, 10 rows, `pending_rows()` 122, opening at 21:25585733 rs142513484, which is where Perl's first buffer opens. The second half is the UNIT: VEP's buffer_size counts post-`split_variants` features, vepyr's counts ALT alleles (`batch_input_units` / `alt_input_units` `:9681`, still private and deliberately not exposed). Over this file every row is bi-allelic so 10 units are 10 rows; the test's second arm feeds a hand-built window carrying one two-ALT row and measures the 10-unit buffer closing after 9 ROWS, so the port claims the allele-major reading rather than a row count that would coincide with it here. Probed, not assumed. At the BASE pin 391f94bd the item is declared without `pub` (`struct InputBufferAccumulator` `annotate_provider.rs:9522`), and a `use` of a sibling private item of the same module still answers `error[E0603]: function `alt_input_units` is private … note: … defined here … annotate_provider.rs:9681:1` — run 2026-08-31 in this crate, with five known-public controls (`cache_lookup_column_names`, `AnnotateProvider`, `TranscriptConsequenceEngine`, `vcf_to_vep_allele`, `VcfTableProvider`) resolving in the same compilation, so the refusal is the item's and not the crate path's. The accessor the test calls is `annotate_provider::test_internals::InputBufferAccumulator` (overlay `dfbf_test_overlay`, sha aa2be930), a newtype whose `new()` is `super::InputBufferAccumulator::default()` and whose methods delegate to `:9529` / `:9552` / `:9566`; no base item is widened, deleted or changed, so parity is still measured against the base.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: the first buffered variant is rs142513484 at 21:25585733, allele_string C/T, start == end == 25585733
rationale: Observable on the public surface, and now runnable: the emitted VCF carries the variant's identity, coordinates and allele, and #96 committed the cache #107 was blocked on. The analogue runs over the SAME INPUT AND THE SAME BUFFER SIZE as the Perl — perl/InputBuffer.t:38 sets buffer_size => 10 and :41 points a Parser::VCF at t/testdata/input/test.vcf, which is committed unmodified at release/116.0 as tests/data/vep116_runner_input/ — so the assertion is on emitted row 1 of that very file. The row is not the input echoed back: SYMBOL/Gene come off the transcript shard (MRPL39 / ENSG00000154719) and Existing_variation — the direct analogue of VEP's `variation_name` — off the variation shard, so a cache that had lost either record would fail while CHROM/POS/ID/REF/ALT still matched. Reaching the colocated record needs `--everything`, because AnnotateVcfConfig has no standalone check_existing field (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) and base_testing_cfg does not set one either, so it is asserted in a second run. `start == end` is the one-base REF. NOT covered even now, and not claimed: the blessed hash's `map_weight` and `nontrimmed_allele_string`, which have no CSQ column. tests/_quarantine/port_input_buffer.rs stays quarantined and is not named — its eleven tests return early on the absent vep-benchmark path and would report ok while asserting nothing.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: the second next() again fills the buffer to buffer_size (10) — first of two byte-identical assertions, see n=16
rationale: The steady-state half of n=13: the fill size is a property of the buffer, not an artefact of the first call. CHANNEL as n=13, one `next()` later — the same accumulator asked again with an empty window, which drains from what is already pending because the loop at `annotate_provider.rs:9587` is a `while` and not an `if`. Measured: 1 buffer, 10 rows, `pending_rows()` 112, opening at 21:25592911 rs148490508 — where Perl's second buffer opens (`perl/InputBuffer.t:88-100`), so this is the second window and not the first re-measured. The test is shared with n=16 under the one condition docs/ledger-contract.md allows it: `:84` and `:85` are byte-identical statements, so the property and the boundary are the same and neither row could regress without the other. Probed, not assumed. At the BASE pin 391f94bd the item is declared without `pub` (`struct InputBufferAccumulator` `annotate_provider.rs:9522`), and a `use` of a sibling private item of the same module still answers `error[E0603]: function `alt_input_units` is private … note: … defined here … annotate_provider.rs:9681:1` — run 2026-08-31 in this crate, with five known-public controls (`cache_lookup_column_names`, `AnnotateProvider`, `TranscriptConsequenceEngine`, `vcf_to_vep_allele`, `VcfTableProvider`) resolving in the same compilation, so the refusal is the item's and not the crate path's. The accessor the test calls is `annotate_provider::test_internals::InputBufferAccumulator` (overlay `dfbf_test_overlay`, sha aa2be930), a newtype whose `new()` is `super::InputBufferAccumulator::default()` and whose methods delegate to `:9529` / `:9552` / `:9566`; no base item is widened, deleted or changed, so parity is still measured against the base.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: the second next() again fills the buffer to buffer_size (10) — second of the two byte-identical assertions, see n=15
rationale: Byte-identical to n=15, one line later, under a different name; it adds no independent claim and recording the duplication is why it is a row rather than a silently merged one. It therefore names n=15's test, which is the one case docs/ledger-contract.md permits a shared `rust_test`: identical statements are the same property at the same boundary, and the question the contract asks — could this test fail if only the other row's behaviour regressed? — has no content when the two rows are the same behaviour. See InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=15 for the measurement and the probe.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: the second batch's first variant is rs148490508 at 21:25592911, allele_string A/G — i.e. input order survives a buffer drain
rationale: The n=14 claim on the second buffer, and the only assertion in this file that pins cross-buffer continuity of input order at the variant level: an implementation that re-ordered or dropped across a drain boundary would fail here and nowhere else. The port is exact rather than analogous in its inputs — with perl/InputBuffer.t:38's own buffer_size = 10 over the committed t/testdata/input/test.vcf, record 11 IS the first variant of batch 2, and it is `21 25592911 rs148490508 A G`, exactly what the Perl asserts — so the assertion is on emitted row 11, with its 14 consequence groups checked so the drain is shown not to have handed on a bare row. `AnnotateVcfConfig::buffer_size` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:437) is the analogue of --buffer_size. The control is also the honest statement of what a drain boundary does here: at buffer_size = 5000 the whole file is ONE buffer and the output is byte-identical, so the boundary leaves no trace in the fields this row asserts. That is #107's own Correction 2 made executable — buffer scope is observable in general (HGNC_ID is where it shows), just not in identity, coordinates or allele. Same not-covered caveat as n=14: map_weight and nontrimmed_allele_string.

desc: METHOD_TESTS: min_max returns a hash reference
rationale: A Perl reference-type probe on the return of `min_max` (InputBuffer.pm:463-497). The container type of the vepyr counterpart is a compile-time fact — `buffer_variant_bounds` returns `Result<Option<(String, i64, i64)>>` (`annotate_provider.rs:11362`) — so asserting it at runtime would restate the type checker.
