Measured, not argued: `the_contig_invariant_is_enforced_upstream_of_the_buffer` in the ported file hands ONE accumulator all three records and gets ONE buffer spanning contigs 1, 2 and 3 — so the single-contig property is not the buffer's, and a test that only drove the accumulator would assert nothing. What makes a vepyr buffer single-contig is (1) the scan being restricted to one contig, `provider.set_vcf_filter(Some(col("chrom").eq(lit(&*chrom))))` (`:13425`, and the range-sliced form at `:13538`; those are the only two `LookupProvider::new` sites), and (2) each contig getting its own accumulator — `ContigAnnotationStream` pops contigs one at a time and builds a fresh `AnnotationWorkerState` per contig (`:12523`) whose `input_buffer_accumulator` is `InputBufferAccumulator::default()` (`:10757`), with the partial buffer flushed when that contig's lookup ends (`flush_partial = worker.lookup_done && worker.window_buffer.is_empty()`, `:11942`, passed at `:11944`). The port applies that same `Expr` to the same `VcfTableProvider` scan of Perl's own three-record input and drains a fresh accumulator at buffer_size 5 with `flush_partial = true`. LIMIT OF THE PORT, stated rather than hidden: `AnnotationWorkerState` is not in the overlay, so the wiring between (1) and (2) is supplied by the test from the two lines above rather than obtained from the engine; the anchor test is what keeps the assertion non-vacuous. CORRECTION: this row previously said vepyr runs "3 separate `ContigAnnotationExec` partitions", and unlock-map.md §2 named `partition_contigs_for_execution` (`:8806`) as these rows' witness. Both are false at the pin — the function returns `vec![contigs]`, ONE partition holding all three, and `ContigAnnotationExec::execute` hands that whole list to a single `ContigAnnotationStream` (`:8760-8783`). The anchor test asserts the one-partition answer so the corrected prose cannot rot back. The surviving finding is unchanged and is #121: the invariant is real but IMPLICIT, enforced layers above `buffer_variant_bounds` (`:11362-11402`), which takes the first row's `chrom` and would mis-window a mixed buffer; 116.1 moved VEP the other way, turning the analogous implicit assumption into an explicit guard (`_chr_matches_for_vf_overlap`, InputBuffer.pm:348-357). Probed and unblocked as InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=13: private at the BASE pin 391f94bd (`annotate_provider.rs:9522`, `error[E0603]` on the module's sibling `alt_input_units` with five public controls resolving in the same compilation), reached through the overlay newtype `annotate_provider::test_internals::InputBufferAccumulator`.

desc: split buffer at chromosome change: the variant in buffer 3 is the chr-3 one — emitted order follows the input's contig order
rationale: Distinct from n=66: that row pins how many variants the buffer holds, this pins WHICH contig they are on and in what order — here that the THIRD drained buffer holds the chr-3 variant. Ported 2026-08-27 with n=61 (whose row carries the full account of the port and its two controls): the exact ordered (CHROM, POS) list's THIRD element is (3, 123). The reversed-input control leans hardest on this row: under a contig sort the chr-3 variant is the one that could not be last when fed first.

desc: split buffer at chromosome change: after the last contig the pre_buffer is empty — nothing was read past the end
rationale: The negative of n=62 and n=65, and the one that makes them meaningful: at end of input nothing is parked, so the staging area is a boundary artefact rather than a permanent one-behind lag. Same missing feature — vepyr has no staging area to be empty, for the reason n=62 gives — and the same reason it is `no-feature` while its neighbours are `deferred`.

desc: split buffer at chromosome change: the fourth next() returns 0 variants after the three single-contig buffers have been drained
rationale: Termination on the multi-contig path: after the third contig is drained a further call yields nothing. The publicly observable half — the emitted VCF holds exactly the three input variants and no fourth — is what the port asserts, exactly as this row's deferred rationale said it would: the exact ordered (CHROM, POS) list has LENGTH THREE, in both the ascending and the reversed arm, so a phantom fourth buffer fails on the list however it is ordered (mutation-checked: appending an expected fourth row turns the test red). Distinct from n=58: that one drains a single-contig buffer (tests/port_input_buffer_annotate.rs::once_the_input_is_exhausted_no_further_rows_are_emitted), this one drains a plan whose CONTIG PARTITIONS were exhausted one after another (`ContigAnnotationExec`, dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:8671-8700), which is the case where a partition-exhaustion off-by-one would survive n=58. Ported 2026-08-27 with n=61/64/67 once #96's fixture grew the variation-only chr1/chr2/chr3 shards; n=61 carries the full account of the port and its controls.

desc: minimal - split_variants: 1:1 CAGAAGAAAG>TAGAAGAAAG,C decomposes into C/T at 1-1 and AGAAGAAAG/- at 2-10
rationale: The pinned crate does carry a source-equivalent port of the Ensembl `trim_sequences` that `InputBuffer.pm:665` calls — `allele::trim_sequences_ensembl_with_end` (dfbf 391f94bd `allele.rs:32`), same `(ref, alt, start, end, changed)` 5-tuple — and fed this row's inputs it reproduces VEP's expected values exactly. That is not enough to make the row a port, because vepyr never runs it on the input path: its only two production call sites are inside `get_matched_variant_alleles` (`allele.rs:237`, `:253`), i.e. colocated-allele matching against cache allele strings. What vepyr's input path runs is `vcf_to_vep_allele` (`allele.rs:296`, feeding the CSQ Allele field at `annotate_provider.rs:5719`), and that function deliberately does NOT suffix-trim equal-length alleles — `if ref_bytes.len() != alt_bytes.len()` guards the suffix loop at `allele.rs:311`, with the doc comment stating "VEP only suffix-trims indels (different-length alleles), not MNVs". So on the input path this row's MNV stays `CAGAAGAAAG/TAGAAGAAAG`, untrimmed, by design. Missing feature: the `--minimal` decomposition itself. The two tests that exercise the trimming primitive are kept and booked where they belong, as `input-buffer-02` in ledger/vepyr-only.ledger.toml — vepyr runs this algorithm, VEP's corpus never asserts that use of it. Beyond the trimming, the row also pins buffer bookkeeping vepyr has no equivalent of at all — that one entry became two, the `merge_with` / `_base_allele_number` linkage, and the `original_allele_string` / `original_start` / `original_end` / `minimised` / `first` fields — which is n=9's missing feature, the split/rejoin round trip.

desc: minimal - rejoin_required: after splitting the 2-ALT row the buffer flags that a rejoin is required
rationale: The flag half of what n=70 pins. `split_variants` publishes its per-ALT list only `if($changed)` (InputBuffer.pm:704-705) and then sets `rejoin_required` to `scalar @split_list != $original_vf_count` (`:717`). Both halves are absent for the same reason: vepyr has no rejoin phase (n=9), and the trimming primitive whose `changed` flag would stand in for the predicate is not on vepyr's input path — see n=70. Reclassified from `analog-port` in review: asserting `changed == true` from `trim_sequences_ensembl_with_end` would have claimed coverage of a decision vepyr never makes.

desc: minimal - doesnt affect non-minimisable: 1:1 CAG>TAG,T keeps the untrimmed joined allele_string CAG/TAG/T over 1-3
rationale: The one row of this block that IS about vepyr's production input path, which is why it survives review as the ledger's only port. Perl keeps this site as ONE VariationFeature with the joined, untrimmed `allele_string` CAG/TAG/T over 1-3, because `minimise_alleles` exempts any site with more than one ALT — the `/.+\/.+\/.+/` branch at Parser.pm:978-984 records `original_allele_string` and pushes the VF through unchanged. (It is reached at all because `post_process_vfs` flags the site as a non-minimised indel: ALT `T` differs in length from REF `CAG`, Parser.pm:864-882.) vepyr has no joined representation and converts each ALT on its own through `vcf_to_vep_allele` (`allele.rs:296`) — the function that actually feeds the CSQ Allele field (`annotate_provider.rs:5719`) — so the same fact, this site is NOT minimised, is read off the per-ALT conversion: the full `CAG` survives for both ALTs and `vep_norm_start` / `vep_norm_end` (`allele.rs:764`, `:778`) return 1 and 3. Reassembled that is exactly CAG/TAG/T over 1-3. NOT covered: that the three alleles ride on ONE record, and the `original_allele_string` bookkeeping. The row is not vacuous — `trim_sequences_ensembl_with_end('CAG', 'TAG', 1, 3, false, 1)` DOES minimise to C/T at 1-1, so the two functions disagree here and what the test pins is that the input path takes the non-minimising one.

desc: unsorted input: next() dies once more than max_not_ordered_variants (5) backwards steps within max_not_ordered_variants_distance (5 bp) have been seen
rationale: VEP defends against unsorted input: `next()` counts variants whose start goes backwards within the distance window (InputBuffer.pm:247) and dies with 'The input file appears to be unsorted. Please sort by chromosome and by location and re-submit.' once the count passes the limit (`:215-221`, again at `:258-261`). vepyr has no such guard. Measured at the pin: `grep -rniE 'no_check_variants_order|max_not_ordered|appears to be unsorted|input file appears' src/` returns nothing and exits 1; positive control, `grep -c 'opts.insert' src/vcf_sink.rs` returns 25, so VEP-style options ARE recognised in general and it is this family that is absent. `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-456`) declares no field for either knob. Missing feature: input sort-order validation — and vepyr's position is stronger than "accepts any order", which is how an earlier draft put it. At `workers > 1` it REQUIRES a tabix index precisely so the scan yields "contiguous, position-ordered partitions", and refuses to run without one (`vcf_sink.rs:1040-1052`). At `workers = 1` there is no such check and no validation anywhere, so sortedness is assumed rather than either enforced or verified. That is the shape of the gap: not indifference to order, but reliance on it without a guard.

desc: unsorted input: the no_check_variants_order flag suppresses the n=73 death
rationale: The off switch for the n=73 guard. An option that disables a feature vepyr does not have cannot be ported: `no_check_variants_order` has zero occurrences at the pin (same measurement and positive control as n=73). Two missing features stacked — the guard, and therefore its escape hatch. Worth its own row rather than folding into n=73 because it is the only assertion that pins the guard as OPTIONAL: a vepyr that later added sort checking without an opt-out would satisfy n=73 and still break callers this line protects.

desc: unsorted input: format => 'hgvs' also suppresses the n=73 death, via the unsorted_formats config list
rationale: The second exemption: VEP skips the sort check for input formats that have no meaningful genomic order until resolved, consulting `config->{_params}{unsorted_formats}` (InputBuffer.pm:209, applied at `:240`). vepyr has no input format other than VCF — `grep -rniE '"hgvs_input"|input_format|parse_hgvs_input|format *== *"hgvs"' src/` returns nothing and exits 1, while src/hgvs.rs carries HGVS OUTPUT formatters (`format_hgvsc`, `:172`) as the positive control that the string 'hgvs' is otherwise well represented in the tree. Two missing features stacked: the guard, and non-VCF input.

desc: unsorted input: raising max_not_ordered_variants_distance to 100 lets the same unsorted file through — the check is distance-gated, not count-only
rationale: The window half of the guard: a backwards step only counts as disorder when it falls within `max_not_ordered_variants_distance`, so widening the window to 100 nt makes the same file legal that n=73 rejects at 5 nt. The window has no counterpart for the same reason the guard does not — see n=73 for the measurement. This is the fourth and last row of the block; together the four pin a whole subsystem vepyr chose not to build, which is why they are no-feature rather than deferred: there is nothing to unblock, only something to build.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the OutputFactory base module compiles and loads under `use`
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 makes `use_ok` not-applicable unconditionally, and R2's reason applies literally: the line asserts that Perl's `require` found modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/OutputFactory.pm, compiled it and ran its `import`, and no Rust design contains a runtime module-load assertion that could succeed or fail. Unlike the same line in ledger/OutputFactory_JSON.ledger.toml n=3 or ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=1, the class named here is the writer-independent BASE, whose capability -- turning one annotated variant into one record per (allele x feature) -- vepyr does have; so even the no-feature reading R2 supersedes would not have applied. Nothing is hidden by the classification: the 138 rows that exercise what the base class does are classified on their own merits below.

desc: WE NEED A RUNNER: the Runner module loads under `use`, so the `get_annotated_buffer` helper at lines 2089-2111 can build the annotated buffers most of this file's rows are driven from
rationale: The second module-load probe, and pure scaffolding: Runner is loaded only so lines 41-46 and the two helper subs at the foot of the file (t/OutputFactory.t:2089, :2113) can produce annotated InputBuffers. Same R2 argument as n=1. vepyr's counterpart to the whole runner is the free function `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:1018), whose existence a test crate proves by compiling against it; there is no run-time load step that could fail. What the runner does end to end is t/Runner.t's subject and belongs to ledger/Runner.ledger.toml.

desc: WE NEED A RUNNER: `Runner->new({base_testing_cfg, input_file => test.vcf, check_existing => 1, dir => cache_root})` returns a defined object -- the config carrier every fixture in this file is built from
rationale: The `ok($obj)` constructor probe of docs/ledger-contract.md, on the denotation table's FIRST row: an object whose Rust analogue is an infallible struct literal. Runner.pm declares no `new` of its own, so it inherits BaseRunner.pm's, whose entire body is `my $self = bless {}, $class` (BaseRunner.pm:89) and `$self->{_config} = Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config->new(@_)` (:92) -- a blessed empty hashref that is ALWAYS true, so the line cannot fail except by Config->new dying first, which would be an exception rather than a false. vepyr's counterpart to the option hash is `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig`, a pub struct of pub fields with a derived Default (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:381), which cannot fail to construct. Identical reading, on the identical Perl line, at ledger/bam_edit.ledger.toml n=4 and ledger/AnnotationSource_File_GFF.ledger.toml n=4. The alternative reading -- Runner denotes the annotation driver, which vepyr has, hence analog-port -- is rejected here for the same reason it was rejected there: this line asserts only that construction returned something defined. What the driver does is asserted one line later, at n=5.

desc: WE NEED A RUNNER: check class -- `ref($runner)` is exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Runner, not a subclass and not a plain hashref
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R1, first condition: the construction already carries its own row (n=3, two lines up), so all this line adds is Perl object identity -- which the contract lists among the legitimate not-applicable cases, and which n=3 has already accounted for. R1's second condition holds independently: a Rust constructor's return type is its class and cannot disagree with itself at run time, so there is no `ref()` to call. Same assertion, same reading, at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=9 and ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=3.

desc: WE NEED A RUNNER: `$runner->init` returns true -- the one-shot setup that builds the plugins, the annotation sources, the chromosome synonyms, the FASTA accessor and the InputBuffer, memoised so later calls are no-ops
rationale: RECLASSIFIED 2026-08-31, `no-feature` / `feature_area = runner-lifecycle` -> `analog-port`, on an INTEGRITY defect rather than on a new measurement: the identical Perl statement is already ported elsewhere in this corpus. `ok($runner->init, 'init')` at perl/OutputFactory.t:51 is the same call on the same class as `ok($runner->init, 'init')` at perl/Runner.t:242. THE OLD RATIONALE MADE A PRODUCT CLAIM -- "vepyr has no such phase to assert" -- and that claim is false: the setup phase is observable at a boundary of its own, because it produces the writer and its HEADER before any variant is annotated. Two rows cannot hold contradictory readings of one Perl line, so this one follows the ported one; see ledger/Runner.ledger.toml n=15, an analog-port against the same test, whose rationale states that boundary in full. WHAT THE ANALOGUE ASSERTS: the run completes over the committed chr21 micro-cache, and the header written before the first data row is the input's two meta-lines plus exactly one `##INFO=<ID=CSQ...>` carrying the pin's default 74-slot layout in the pinned field order -- setup having succeeded is read off what setup PRODUCED. THE ABSENCE THE OLD ROW POINTED AT IS REAL AND IS NOT THIS ROW'S SUBJECT: there is no callable `init` a test could drive, measured rather than asserted -- `cargo check` on a probe naming `vcf_sink::init`, `vcf_sink::reset` and `vcf_sink::get_all_annotation_sources` returns three E0425s while `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` in the same file resolves, and the module's whole top-level public surface is `pub struct AnnotateVcfConfig` plus that one `pub async fn` (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:381 and :1018). What that absence blocks is an assertion ON the phase object; this line asserts only that setup succeeded, which the emitted header witnesses. WHY THE TWO SIBLING ROWS KEEP THE OLD READING: at ledger/Haplo_Runner.ledger.toml n=19 the row stays no-feature because the whole haplotype product is absent, so there is no run whose setup boundary could be observed at all, and `haplotypes` is the gap it waits on; the same holds at ledger/VariantRecoder.ledger.toml n=5, no-feature on `variant-recoder`. This row's `$runner` is an ordinary annotation run, which vepyr performs. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE MAP: `runner-lifecycle` was a one-row area and now carries none, so it leaves the Missing-feature map (35 areas -> 34). Its declaration stays in ledger/feature-areas.toml, with a comment recording why it is unused, so re-adopting it is not a fresh decision.

desc: BASIC TESTS: `OutputFactory->new({config => $runner->config})` returns a defined object -- the base factory 138 of this file's assertions are then driven through
rationale: The constructor probe again, and it lands on the same first row of the denotation table as n=3. OutputFactory::new (OutputFactory.pm:137) is `$class->SUPER::new(@_)` followed by `add_shortcuts` over a long qw() list of option names (:144), so the return is the blessed hash BaseVEP::new produced and the line records only that the bless happened. This is NOT the reading ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=4 and ledger/OutputFactory_JSON.ledger.toml n=6 give their sibling lines, and the difference is the denotation, exactly as the ruling says: those classes denote the per-format writer that `--tab` or `--json` selects, a capability vepyr does not have, so they are no-feature; the base class denotes per-consequence record assembly, which vepyr does perform, so nothing is absent and what is left is an infallible construction. The rows that assert what the assembly produces are n=48, n=60, n=77 and their neighbours, and they are ports.

desc: BASIC TESTS: check class -- `ref($of)` is exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::OutputFactory, the base class rather than one of the four format subclasses
rationale: RULING R1, first condition, as at n=4: the construction has its own row one line up (n=6), so this line adds only Perl object identity. R1's denotation branch is not reached, and would not change the answer if it were -- the class denotes a capability vepyr has (n=6), which is R1's second not-applicable condition. Contrast ledger/OutputFactory_JSON.ledger.toml n=6, where neither condition held: that file contains no `ok($of = ...->new)` at all, so its readback was the only accounting for the construction and inherited the denotation table, which returned no-feature for the JSON writer.

desc: add_colocated_variant_info: a variant that matches a known rsID gains Existing_variation => ['rs142513484'] beside the allele it was called for
rationale: FAMILY ANCHOR for n=8, n=10, n=11 and n=12, the colocated-variation block. The method folds the variation cache's record for a locus into the per-allele output hash, and the four rows walk its four output groups. vepyr does the same fold: the colocated join is what populates the CSQ Existing_variation column, field 17 of CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING (dfbf 391f94bd, golden_benchmark.rs:556). Measured on the committed shard, 21:25585733 C>T comes back with Existing_variation = rs142513484 on every one of the record's CSQ groups -- Perl's literal exactly. The named test asserts the DISTINCT set of that subfield across the whole record, so a value on only some groups fails, and it carries a positive control in the same run: 21:25586000 T>C sits in the same 1 Mb transcript block, annotates normally, and has no variation row in the shard (PROVENANCE.md's fourth exclusion category), so its Existing_variation is empty -- which is what makes the first assertion evidence rather than a constant. Mutating the expectation to rs142513483 fails it. CHANNEL, stated once for n=8, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 and referred to by each: Perl inspects the hash `add_colocated_variant_info` / `VariationFeature_to_output_hash` returns; vepyr has no output-hash object, so the only observation point is the CSQ string of the VCF `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` writes (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:1018) over the committed micro-cache tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/ and reference slice tests/data/vep115_reference_slice/ (#96). That is docs/ledger-contract.md's 'same property, different observation point', so these are analog-port and not unit-port even where the expected literal is byte-identical to Perl's. The test reads the subfield index out of the emitted ##INFO=<ID=CSQ...Format:...> header, so it cannot silently read a neighbouring column, and it never contradicts the CSQ pins in tests/port_output_factory_vcf_csq.rs (#201), which are about the field VOCABULARY while every assertion here is about a VALUE. The blocker recorded on this row before the reclassification -- 'a pin-conformant parquet cache carrying chr21 variation data' -- is exactly what #96 delivered.

desc: add_colocated_variant_info - _freq_check_freqs: a variant carrying --check_frequency results gains FREQS => ['1KG_ALL:A:0.1'], the population:allele:frequency triples the frequency filter computed
rationale: The odd one out of the colocated block: unlike n=8 and n=10-12 this row does not read the variation cache at all. `_freq_check_freqs` is a slot the --check_frequency FILTER writes on the VariationFeature (OutputFactory.pm:711-721 folds it into FREQS), so the row asserts the output half of a feature whose input half is a filter vepyr does not have. Over dfbf 391f94bd, `grep -rc --include='*.rs' check_frequency src/` and the same grep for `FREQS` both return 0 (positive control on the same tree: `vcf_sink` returns 19), and `FREQS` is absent from both CSQ layouts in golden_benchmark.rs (:464, :556). Missing feature: --check_frequency, the frequency-based variant filter, and the FREQS field that reports what it measured. Porting it means building the filter first, not finding a fixture.

desc: add_colocated_variant_info - pheno, clin_sig, multiple: 21:25891796 C>T collects TWO colocated records (rs63750066 and CM930033) and merges their PHENO flags and three CLIN_SIG terms into parallel arrays
rationale: Two properties beyond n=8's: a locus with more than one colocated record contributes all of them rather than the first, and the per-record flags stay positionally aligned with the identifiers. Measured at 21:25891796 C>T over the committed shard: Existing_variation = rs63750066&CM930033 and PHENO = 1&1 -- Perl's identifiers, Perl's order, Perl's flag pair, in the &-joined multi-value convention CSQ uses for a Perl arrayref. The third expectation is re-derived: Perl's v84 CLIN_SIG is ['uncertain_significance','not_provided','pathogenic'] and the v115 answer is pathogenic&likely_pathogenic, because the shard's clin_sig_allele column at that locus reads 'T:pathogenic;T:likely_pathogenic' and AnnotateProvider prefers that allele-scoped column over the locus-wide clin_sig (annotate_provider.rs:1982-1984) -- so vepyr's terms are the ones scoped to the ALT actually called, in the column's order, which is a sharper reading than the Perl's and not a divergence. The named test additionally asserts that Existing_variation and PHENO have equal element counts, which is the parallel-arrays half; shortening PHENO to '1' fails it. Perl's fixture is homo_sapiens_vep_84_GRCh38 and the committed cache is VEP 115, so every expectation was re-derived rather than transcribed, per tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/PROVENANCE.md.

desc: add_colocated_variant_info - pubmed: with $of->{pubmed} set, 21:25272769 C>T gains PUBMED => ['20708005'] alongside its rsID and PHENO flag
rationale: The third arm of the colocated fold. Measured at 21:25272769 C>T over the committed shard, all three of Perl's literals come back unchanged: Existing_variation rs9977253, PHENO 1, PUBMED 20708005. What does NOT carry across is the gating: Perl sets and unsets $of->{pubmed} around the call (t/OutputFactory.t:137, :154), while AnnotateVcfConfig (vcf_sink.rs:381-455) has no pubmed member and emits the field whenever the variation shard carries citations, so the vepyr observation is of the value only. That is recorded rather than hidden: the analogue covers the row's expected hash, not the option's on/off behaviour, for which the pin has no switch to toggle. CHANNEL, stated once for n=8, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 and referred to by each: Perl inspects the hash `add_colocated_variant_info` / `VariationFeature_to_output_hash` returns; vepyr has no output-hash object, so the only observation point is the CSQ string of the VCF `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` writes (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:1018) over the committed micro-cache tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/ and reference slice tests/data/vep115_reference_slice/ (#96). That is docs/ledger-contract.md's 'same property, different observation point', so these are analog-port and not unit-port even where the expected literal is byte-identical to Perl's. The test reads the subfield index out of the emitted ##INFO=<ID=CSQ...Format:...> header, so it cannot silently read a neighbouring column, and it never contradicts the CSQ pins in tests/port_output_factory_vcf_csq.rs (#201), which are about the field VOCABULARY while every assertion here is about a VALUE. The blocker recorded on this row before the reclassification -- 'a pin-conformant parquet cache carrying chr21 variation data' -- is exactly what #96 delivered.

desc: add_colocated_variant_info - somatic: 21:25891785 G>A collects rs145564988 and COSM1029633, and the SOMATIC and PHENO arrays are [0, 1] -- per-record flags in the identifiers' order, not a single flag for the locus
rationale: The sharpest row of the colocated block: the wrong reading -- one somatic flag per variant -- would still produce a well-formed hash, and only the positional list catches it. Measured at 21:25891785 G>A over the committed shard: Existing_variation = rs145564988&CM160073&COSV60998056, SOMATIC = 0&0&1 and PHENO = 1&1&1. Three records where v84 had two, because the v115 cache adds the HGMD record CM160073, and COSMIC re-accessioned Perl's COSM1029633 as COSV60998056 -- both visible in the shard (variation_name/allele_string COSMIC_MUTATION, somatic = true). The row's content is untouched by that: the named test asserts the flag list has exactly one entry per identifier, that the entry at the COSMIC identifier's index is 1, and that the entry at the dbSNP identifier's index is 0 -- written on the RELATION, so it fails for any implementation that emits a single locus-wide flag, and mutating the list to 0&1&1 fails it. The desc names PHENO as well, so the test pins it too: measured 1&1&1, NOT the 0&0&1 that symmetry with SOMATIC would suggest -- all three v115 records carry a phenotype association, where v84 had 0 on the dbSNP record. Asserting the expected-by-analogy 0&0&1 fails with left [1&1&1] (5 passed; 1 failed), which is the measurement. Consequence: no row in the corpus pins a 0 inside a PHENO list, because at this locus the shard has none to pin. Perl's fixture is homo_sapiens_vep_84_GRCh38 and the committed cache is VEP 115, so every expectation was re-derived rather than transcribed, per tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/PROVENANCE.md.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash: the per-VF base hash is exactly two keys -- Uploaded_variation => 'rs142513484' and Location => '21:25585733' -- before any per-allele or per-feature work
rationale: The row pins the base hash's whole content, and the is_deeply makes the absence of every other key part of the assertion. vepyr exhibits the same two facts through the record itself: its only sink writes a VCF (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:1018), so Perl's Location is the CHROM and POS columns and its Uploaded_variation is the ID column. 'Exactly two keys' becomes 'the record level gains nothing per-feature': the named test asserts the annotated record at 21:25585733 carries ID rs142513484, POS 25585733, more than one CSQ group, and an INFO field whose key list is exactly [CSQ] -- so a per-feature key leaking to record level fails it. Positive control in the same run: the same locus spelled with '.' for ID keeps '.', while its Existing_variation is still rs142513484, proving the ID column is the input's identity and not the colocated record's. The synthesised Uploaded_variation for an ID-less variant (21_25741665_CAGAAGAAAG/..., t/OutputFactory.t:1703) has no vepyr counterpart at all, but that belongs to n=118, not here.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - variant_class: with $of->{variant_class} on, the base hash gains VARIANT_CLASS => 'SNV', the SO class of the variant itself rather than of its consequence
rationale: The one option in this group vepyr implements under the same name: VARIANT_CLASS is index 21 of CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING (dfbf 391f94bd, golden_benchmark.rs:556). The classifier itself is a private free function in annotate_provider.rs (:7326-7333) and stays unreachable -- 'grep -cE '^\\s*pub (fn|struct|enum|const|type)' src/annotate_provider.rs' returns 2 against 56 for transcript_consequence.rs as the positive control -- so the observation point is the emitted column, which the committed micro-cache now makes reachable. Measured: 21:25585733 C>T gives VARIANT_CLASS = SNV, Perl's literal. The row's distinct content is that the class is the VARIANT's and not the consequence's, so the named test asserts the DISTINCT set of VARIANT_CLASS over the record is a single value while the distinct set of Consequence over the same groups has more than one member, and adds a second input row -- the deletion at 21:25592910 -- which comes back as 'deletion', so the field is read from the variant rather than being a constant.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - overlapping_svs: a variant that falls inside known structural variants gains SV => ['sv1', 'sv2'], the co-located SVs' identifiers sorted by name
rationale: vepyr reads co-located structural variants and does something else with them. `AnnotateProvider::load_structural_features` (dfbf 391f94bd, annotate_provider.rs:5044) pulls `feature_id`, `feature_kind` and `event_type` from a cache table into `StructuralFeature`s, and the engine turns each overlap into a consequence TERM -- `TranscriptAblation`, `TranscriptAmplification`, `FeatureElongation`, `FeatureTruncation`, via `parse_sv_event_kind` (:7343) -- rather than into a list of identifiers. There is no column to put the names in: `grep -rc --include='*.rs' OverlapBP src/` and the same grep for a standalone `SV` field return 0, and no `SV` entry appears in either CSQ layout (golden_benchmark.rs:464, :556); positive control, `vcf_sink` -> 19. Missing feature: reporting WHICH co-located structural variants a variant falls in, as distinct from what they do to it.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - individual: with --individual dave, the base hash gains IND => 'dave' and ZYG => 'HET', so one input record becomes one output record per selected sample
rationale: FAMILY ANCHOR for n=16, n=44, n=45 and n=140-143 -- everything per-sample in this file. VEP's --individual re-keys the output by sample and re-derives each sample's genotype from the FORMAT column; vepyr annotates the record, once, and never looks at the genotype columns. Over dfbf 391f94bd the three names this needs return nothing: `grep -rc --include='*.rs' individual_zyg src/` -> 0, `process_ref_homs` -> 0, and the two hits for `individual` are both prose (annotate_provider.rs:939 and :9258, the word inside a sentence). Positive control on the same tree: `vcf_sink` -> 19. `AnnotateVcfConfig` has no sample field either (vcf_sink.rs:381-456). Missing feature: per-sample expansion, and with it the IND and ZYG output fields. Same reading as the already-classified per-sample row cited in ledger/Config.ledger.toml, which found the same zero and refused to point it at the generic comma-list splitter.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - custom annotations: an annotation entry WITHOUT an allele key is attached at variant level (custom1 => ['foo'], custom2 => ['bar', 'car']) and one WITH an allele key is skipped, because that one belongs to the per-allele hash instead
rationale: FAMILY ANCHOR for n=17, n=52 and n=127-129, the --custom block. The row's content is the variant-level half of a two-level split: allele-less entries land here, allele-scoped ones land on the VFOA hash (n=52 asserts the complement). vepyr has no --custom mechanism to split. Over dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rc --include='*.rs' short_name src/` returns 0 (positive control: `vcf_sink` -> 19), and `AnnotateVcfConfig` has no field for an annotation-file list (vcf_sink.rs:381-456). What it does have is a different mechanism with a superficially similar effect -- `plugin_cache_root` (:455) points at pre-BUILT parquet plugin caches whose manifests declare extra CSQ fields (plugin_cache/registry.rs:100) -- and it is not this feature: it reads no user-supplied VCF, BED or BigWig at run time, has no per-file short name to key on, and has no variant-versus-allele scoping at all. Missing feature: --custom file annotation. Its header half is n=127-129; its plugin cousin, which DOES have an analogue, is n=130.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - nearest: with the nearest slot filled, the base hash gains NEAREST => ['foo', 'bar'], the identifiers of the closest features to a variant that may overlap none
rationale: VEP's --nearest answers a question vepyr never asks: which feature is closest to a variant that overlaps nothing. vepyr's engine manufactures an `intergenic_variant` consequence for exactly that case (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:1664-1674, witnessed by tests/port_output_factory_hashes.rs::a_variant_overlapping_no_feature_still_yields_exactly_one_consequence) and reports no neighbour with it. `grep -rc --include='*.rs' nearest src/` returns 0 over the whole crate (positive control: `vcf_sink` -> 19) and NEAREST appears in neither CSQ layout (golden_benchmark.rs:464, :556). Missing feature: nearest-feature search, which needs a distance query over the transcript tree that the pin does not perform.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - ambiguity: with $of->{ambiguity} on, the base hash gains AMBIGUITY => 'R', the single IUPAC code standing for the variant's whole A/G allele string
rationale: The assertion is that VEP can COLLAPSE an allele string into one ambiguity symbol. vepyr can read such a symbol and never writes one: `allele::reverse_complement_allele` (dfbf 391f94bd, allele.rs:138-160) complements R, Y, M, K, S and the rest when it meets them in a cache record, which is the positive control that the crate knows the alphabet -- but `grep -rc --include='*.rs' AMBIGUITY src/` returns 0, there is no encoder to pair with that decoder, and no AMBIGUITY column exists in either CSQ layout (golden_benchmark.rs:464, :556). Missing feature: --ambiguity, the IUPAC rendering of the allele string.

desc: pick_worst_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele - empty list: handed no candidates the picker returns undef rather than dying or inventing a winner
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay; what would close it was one pub, and the overlay is that pub. At the base pin every picker function is private: over dfbf 391f94bd, grep -nE '^(pub )?fn .*pick' src/annotate_provider.rs lists fifteen and not one carries pub, the module exporting two items in total; positive control on the same search shape, transcript_consequence.rs exports 56. Re-measured in this checkout: a throwaway probe naming the pre-overlay paths emitted error[E0603] five times against annotate_provider::cache_lookup_column_names resolving in the same file as the control. PINS.toml dfbf_test_overlay (aa2be930) delegates the entry point; the private PickCriterion never crosses the boundary because the overlay takes the order from an opaque PickFlags wrapper. The end-to-end channel still cannot express either row, which is why they were filed under #213 and not #212: an empty candidate list is not an input a VCF can carry, because the engine manufactures an intergenic consequence when nothing overlaps (transcript_consequence.rs:1664-1674, witnessed by tests/port_output_factory_hashes.rs::a_variant_overlapping_no_feature_still_yields_exactly_one_consequence). unit-port and not analog-port: same input (an empty candidate list), same answer (nothing), at the same boundary -- pick_worst_assignment (annotate_provider.rs:2553) is the function VEP's own line calls, and its if candidates.is_empty() { return None; } at :2575-2577 runs before any criterion. Perl's undef is Option::None; no channel is substituted. The assertion is repeated across all eight pick_order spellings from_options_json can produce, because the order is the argument the overlay had to route around and a picker that read it before checking for emptiness would be order-sensitive here. Not a vacuous pass: the same call handed two real candidates returns Some(idx) with idx in range, and PickFlags::defaults() is checked to carry VEP's eleven criteria (Config.pm:300-307), so `every mode' is not one mode eight times over. Mutation-checked: is_none() flipped to is_some() fails with an empty candidate list must not produce a winner (pick_order length 11).

desc: pick_worst_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele - default: with the shipped pick_order, the winner among the VFOAs of rs142513484 is ENST00000307301
rationale: FAMILY ANCHOR for n=21-27, n=29-40 and n=50, the whole --pick block. Nothing here is missing from vepyr: AnnotateVcfConfig carries a public field for every mode the block exercises -- pick (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:385), pick_allele (:387), per_gene (:389), pick_allele_gene (:391), flag_pick (:393), flag_pick_allele (:395), flag_pick_allele_gene (:398) and pick_order (:400) -- and the winner is observable in two CSQ columns: Feature, which says which transcript survived, and the standalone PICK column that csq_field_names_for_mode_with_pick inserts after FLAGS (golden_benchmark.rs:661-677). The implementation is a private block of annotate_provider.rs -- pick_worst_assignment (:2553), retain_best_pick_candidates (:2529), sort_pick_candidates_by_vep_order (:2630) -- which is why the two empty-input rows n=20 and n=28 stay blocked-api under #213 while these rows only ever needed a cache. #96 committed one (tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/), so the family is ported through vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf (vcf_sink.rs:1018) over it. CHANNEL: analog-port, not unit-port -- Perl reads ->feature->stable_id off a returned VFOA object and vepyr has no VFOA, so the surviving consequences are observable only as CSQ groups. FIXTURE MOVE: Perl's v84 block puts 3 candidates over 21:25585733 and the committed v115 shard puts 14, and MRPL39's canonical/MANE-Select transcript moved from ENST00000307301 to ENST00000352957 -- so this row's expected winner is re-derived while n=22, n=23 and n=27 reproduce Perl's literals unchanged. This row pins the SHIPPED default order, which PickFlags::default (annotate_provider.rs:1275-1294) declares as mane_select, mane_plus_clinical, canonical, appris, tsl, biotype, ccds, rank, length, ensembl, refseq against VEP 115 Config.pm:300-307; the named test asserts the winner is the ONLY candidate carrying MANE_SELECT (so the first criterion decides alone), and that it is not the first candidate in output order (so --pick ranks rather than truncates). The multi-allelic arm of the family, n=34-39, is blocked on something else entirely and is argued on its own rows.

desc: pick_worst_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele - rank: with pick_order reduced to ['rank'], the winner changes to ENST00000352957 -- consequence severity alone picks a different transcript from the default order
rationale: The row's content is the CHANGE: the same candidate set under a one-criterion order yields a different winner from n=21's shipped order, which is what proves the order is consulted rather than hard-wired. vepyr's severity criterion is SoTerm::rank (dfbf 391f94bd, so_terms.rs:197), VEP's own consequence order, and pick_order is a public config field (vcf_sink.rs:400) parsed into the same criterion vocabulary. Measured over the committed micro-cache, pick_order='rank' returns ENST00000352957 -- Perl's literal, unchanged by the v84 -> v115 move. The named test adds the mechanism as its control: the winner's Consequence is missense_variant and the first candidate's is 3_prime_UTR_variant, so severity is demonstrably what separated them rather than candidate order. Mutating the order to 'length' returns ENST00000307301 instead and fails the test. See the family anchor at n=21 for the public-field inventory, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move.

desc: pick_worst_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele - appris: with pick_order ['appris'], the APPRIS principal-isoform annotation alone picks ENST00000352957
rationale: APPRIS is the criterion most likely to be silently unimplemented, because a picker that ignored it would still return a plausible transcript. vepyr does implement it: parse_appris_pick_rank (dfbf 391f94bd, annotate_provider.rs:2317) turns the cache's APPRIS string into a rank, and APPRIS is index 29 of CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING (golden_benchmark.rs:556), so the annotation reaches the output as well as the picker. Measured, pick_order='appris' returns ENST00000352957 -- Perl's literal, unchanged. The named test guards exactly the silent-unimplemented failure mode: it asserts the winner's APPRIS is P3 (principal) AND that at least one other candidate in the pool carries A1 (alternative), so the criterion is shown to RANK rather than to select the only annotated candidate. Mutating the order to 'ccds' moves the answer to ENST00000307301 and fails it. See the family anchor at n=21 for the public-field inventory, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move.

desc: pick_worst_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele - canonical,biotype: a TWO-criterion order picks ENST00000307301 -- the second criterion is consulted only where the first ties
rationale: The only row of the family that pins the tie-break COMPOSITION rather than a single criterion, and the reason vepyr's pick_order is a comma-separated string rather than one enum value (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:400). The mechanism is retain_best_pick_candidates (annotate_provider.rs:2529-2551): it returns a winner only when exactly one candidate is best, otherwise it truncates to the tied set and pick_worst_assignment moves to the next criterion (:2580). Perl's own order ['canonical','biotype'] returns ENST00000352957 on the committed shard rather than v84's ENST00000307301, because v115 moved CANONICAL=YES; the row is about composition, not about that id, so the named test exhibits the composition directly and does not rest on the moved literal. It asserts four measurements: canonical,biotype == canonical (a decisive first criterion makes the second inert), biotype alone -> ENST00000307301 (thirteen of fourteen candidates are protein_coding, so the criterion ties and falls through), biotype,canonical -> ENST00000352957 (the tie IS broken by the second), and biotype,length -> ENST00000307301 (the SAME answer biotype alone gives). The evidence that the second criterion is read is the contrast between the last two, not either on its own: biotype,length would hold unchanged if length were ignored entirely, so it is biotype,canonical vs biotype,length -- two second criteria, two winners -- that discriminates. Replacing biotype,canonical with biotype alone fails it. See the family anchor at n=21 for the public-field inventory, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move.

desc: pick_worst_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele - canonical bail out: with pick_order ['canonical'] alone the winner is still ENST00000307301, so exhausting the order without a decision falls back to the first candidate instead of returning undef
rationale: The complement of n=20: n=20 is the empty INPUT, this is the exhausted ORDER, and they are different code paths in OutputFactory.pm's pick loop -- which is why n=20 stays blocked-api under #213 and this one did not. vepyr's fallback is explicit: when every criterion of pick_order has run without narrowing to one, pick_worst_assignment returns candidates.first() (dfbf 391f94bd, annotate_provider.rs:2623) over a pool pre-sorted into CSQ output order by sort_pick_candidates_by_vep_order (:2630), whose own comment calls the fallback 'a deterministic representative choice'. Perl's expected id moved with the cache (v84 ENST00000307301, v115 ENST00000352957) and is not what the row is about, so the named test asserts Perl's call ('canonical' alone, one winner, never empty) AND exhibits the bail-out from a criterion that genuinely ties on the committed shard: pick_order='biotype' returns exactly the FIRST entry of the unfiltered CSQ list, asserted by reading that list rather than by naming an id. A picker that returned nothing on an exhausted order would give an empty consequence list and fail. See the family anchor at n=21 for the public-field inventory, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move.

desc: pick_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele_per_gene: --per_gene keeps one winner PER GENE -- two transcripts survive (ENST00000307301, ENST00000567517) where --pick kept one
rationale: The row pins the GROUPING, not the ranking: the same picker runs, but once per gene key. vepyr's per_gene is a public config field (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:389) and the grouping function is pick_assignment_gene_key (annotate_provider.rs:2472). Measured over the committed micro-cache, per_gene keeps ENST00000352957 (ENSG00000154719) and ENST00000567517 (ENSG00000260583) -- Perl's second transcript verbatim, its first re-derived from ENST00000307301 for the v115 canonical move. The named test does not assert the bare number 2: it first collects the DISTINCT Gene values of the fourteen unfiltered candidates, finds two, and requires the survivor count to equal that -- so the assertion is literally 'one per gene' and would fail on a shard with a third gene. It also asserts --pick over the same pool keeps one, which is the contrast the Perl row draws. Forcing the expected count to genes.len() - 1 fails it (left 2, right 1). See the family anchor at n=21 for the public-field inventory, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move.

desc: pick_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele_per_gene - change pick_order: under pick_order ['rank'] the per-gene winners become ENST00000352957 and ENST00000567517 -- the gene grouping is unchanged and only the within-group choice moves
rationale: The row is n=26 crossed with n=22, and its content is the independence of the two: changing the order changes one winner and leaves the other, which a per-gene implementation that re-picked globally would not reproduce. Perl's expected pair under ['rank'] -- ENST00000352957 and ENST00000567517 -- comes back VERBATIM from the committed v115 shard, and the named test asserts it first. But under v115 'rank' happens to agree with the default order, so that assertion alone cannot witness the 'moves' half; the test therefore also runs per_gene under 'length', which returns ENST00000307301 + ENST00000567517, and then asserts the three facts the row is made of: the gene sequence is identical between the two runs, the first gene's winner differs, and the second gene's winner does not. Changing the expected 'length' winner to ENST00000352957 fails it. See the family anchor at n=21 for the public-field inventory, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move.

desc: filter_VariationFeatureOverlapAlleles - empty arrayref: the mode dispatcher handed an empty candidate list returns an empty list, whatever mode is set
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay. The dispatcher's empty-input arm and n=20's twin one level up: n=20 is the picker refusing to choose from nothing, this is the dispatcher refusing to fail on nothing. At the base pin every picker function is private: over dfbf 391f94bd, grep -nE '^(pub )?fn .*pick' src/annotate_provider.rs lists fifteen and not one carries pub, the module exporting two items in total; positive control on the same search shape, transcript_consequence.rs exports 56. Re-measured in this checkout: a throwaway probe naming the pre-overlay paths emitted error[E0603] five times against annotate_provider::cache_lookup_column_names resolving in the same file as the control. PINS.toml dfbf_test_overlay (aa2be930) delegates the entry point; the private PickCriterion never crosses the boundary because the overlay takes the order from an opaque PickFlags wrapper. The end-to-end channel still cannot express either row, which is why they were filed under #213 and not #212: an empty candidate list is not an input a VCF can carry, because the engine manufactures an intergenic consequence when nothing overlaps (transcript_consequence.rs:1664-1674, witnessed by tests/port_output_factory_hashes.rs::a_variant_overlapping_no_feature_still_yields_exactly_one_consequence). The counterpart is apply_pick_mode (annotate_provider.rs:2754). unit-port: Perl's [] is an empty Vec and the call is the same one. Perl's label says WHATEVER MODE IS SET and demonstrates it with one mode; the test runs all eight modes from_options_json can produce, because apply_pick_mode returns early for a disabled mode (:2760-2762) and takes a different branch for a flag mode (:2766-2776), so a single mode would leave two of the three routes unvisited -- and each mode's spelling is separately asserted to be RECOGNISED (mode_is_enabled matches the expected flag), so a typo'd options key could not pass as a disabled mode. Not a vacuous pass: handed two real candidates, a disabled mode returns both and a flag mode returns both (it marks rather than filters), so `empty out' is the input's doing. Still deliberately not folded into n=20's accounting: a picker and a mode dispatcher are different call sites, and a pub on one would not expose the other -- the overlay had to delegate both. Mutation-checked: expecting length 1 fails with mode None must return an empty list, left: 0 / right: 1.

desc: filter_VariationFeatureOverlapAlleles - no filter: with no mode set the dispatcher is the identity -- the candidate count out equals the count in
rationale: The default arm, and the row that makes every other filter row meaningful: without it a dispatcher that dropped candidates unconditionally would still satisfy n=30's single-winner assertion. vepyr's counterpart is AnnotateVcfConfig with every pick flag false, its derived Default (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:381-401), under which each overlapping feature contributes one CSQ group. The named test asserts the sharp form, which no other row in the file covers: a POPULATED pick_order with no mode set filters nothing and reorders nothing -- the Feature sequence is identical to the default run's -- while the same pick_order under `pick` collapses the run to one group. An implementation that read a populated pick_order as a request to pick would fail here and pass every other row. Mutating the identity comparison to a length of 13 fails it (left 14, right 13). See the family anchor at n=21 for the public config fields, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move (3 candidates over 21:25585733 became 14, and MRPL39's canonical/MANE-Select transcript moved to ENST00000352957).

desc: filter_VariationFeatureOverlapAlleles - pick: with $of->{pick} on, the dispatcher routes to the picker and the candidate list collapses to the single winner ENST00000307301
rationale: The dispatch half of n=21: n=21 calls the picker directly, this asserts that setting the `pick` option is what makes the dispatcher call it. vepyr's `pick` is a public config field (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:385) read by apply_pick_mode (annotate_provider.rs:2754). The row's distinct content is the COLLAPSE, so the named test asserts the count relation -- 14 candidates in, exactly one out -- plus the survivor's membership in the unfiltered pool, and deliberately leaves WHICH transcript wins and why to n=21, whose test could not fail if the collapse regressed and vice versa. Perl's ENST00000307301 is the v84 canonical transcript; the committed shard answers ENST00000352957, and mutating the expectation back to 307301 fails the test. See the family anchor at n=21 for the public config fields, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move (3 candidates over 21:25585733 became 14, and MRPL39's canonical/MANE-Select transcript moved to ENST00000352957).

desc: filter_VariationFeatureOverlapAlleles - per_gene: routing through the per_gene option keeps one winner per gene, so ENST00000307301 and ENST00000567517 both survive where --pick kept one
rationale: The dispatch half of n=26, as n=30 is the dispatch half of n=21: the option, not a direct call, is what selects the per-gene picker. vepyr's per_gene is a public config field (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:389). The row's distinct content is the ROUTING -- that the mode chooses between reductions -- so the named test asserts all three counts against each other in one place, (14, 2, 1) for none / per_gene / pick, and additionally that the two per_gene survivors sit in DIFFERENT Gene values, which is what makes 2 the per-gene answer rather than an arbitrary pair. n=26 covers 'one per gene' against the distinct-gene count; neither test could stand in for the other. Perl's second transcript ENST00000567517 comes back verbatim. Mutating the triple to (14, 1, 1) fails it. See the family anchor at n=21 for the public config fields, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move (3 candidates over 21:25585733 became 14, and MRPL39's canonical/MANE-Select transcript moved to ENST00000352957).

desc: filter_VariationFeatureOverlapAlleles - flag_pick count: --flag_pick keeps EVERY candidate, so the output count equals the input count -- flagging is not filtering
rationale: The row that separates the flag modes from the pick modes, and the half a naive implementation gets wrong by filtering anyway. vepyr keeps the same split: flag_pick is its own config field (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:393) and csq_field_names_for_mode_with_pick inserts a standalone PICK column after FLAGS (golden_benchmark.rs:661-677) precisely so every candidate can be emitted with the winner marked. Measured over the committed micro-cache, flag_pick returns the same 14 Feature ids in the same order as the unfiltered run. The named test asserts that equality rather than a bare count, and pairs it with pick -> 1 and per_gene -> 2 in the same test, so 'the count was preserved' cannot be satisfied by an annotator that never filters at all. Comparing flag_pick's output against pick's instead fails it (14 ids vs 1). See the family anchor at n=21 for the public config fields, the observation channel and the v84 -> v115 fixture move (3 candidates over 21:25585733 became 14, and MRPL39's canonical/MANE-Select transcript moved to ENST00000352957).

desc: filter_VariationFeatureOverlapAlleles - flag_pick check: of the candidates --flag_pick returned, exactly one carries PICK, and it is the same ENST00000307301 --pick would have kept
rationale: The complement of n=32 and the pair's real content: the count assertion alone would pass for an implementation that flagged nothing. vepyr stores the flag on the consequence itself -- TranscriptConsequence.picked (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:641) -- and emits it as the PICK column. The field is public but nothing public sets it: the setter is apply_pick_mode (annotate_provider.rs:2754), which is not pub, so the only observation is end to end, which the committed micro-cache now permits. The named test asserts exactly one of the fourteen groups carries PICK=1, that the remaining thirteen carry an empty PICK, and that the flagged Feature equals the one a second run under `pick` keeps -- compared run against run rather than against a hard-coded id, so the two cannot drift apart silently. Mutating the expected bearer to ENST00000307301 fails it. desc: filter_VariationFeatureOverlapAlleles - pick_allele: on a multi-allelic site (C>G,T) the picker runs once PER ALLELE, so both G:ENST00000307301 and T:ENST00000307301 survive

desc: add_colocated_frequency_data - af: with --af the per-allele hash gains AF => ['0.0010'], the 1000 Genomes global frequency of the allele that was called
rationale: FAMILY ANCHOR for n=53-59, the frequency block. The method looks up a colocated record's per-allele frequencies and attaches the ones the options asked for; the seven rows walk the allele-matching rule, the population sets and the maximum. vepyr computes the same quantities: AF and the five 1000G super-populations are indices 42-47 of CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING (dfbf 391f94bd, golden_benchmark.rs:556), the ten gnomADe_* fields follow at 48-57, the eleven gnomADg_* at 58-68, and MAX_AF/MAX_AF_POPS at 69-70. The only public entry point that produces any of them is vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf (vcf_sink.rs:1018), and #96 committed the pin-conformant chr21 cache it needs. CHANNEL: analog-port, not unit-port -- Perl reads the returned hash, vepyr has none, and the frequencies are observable only as CSQ subfields. WHAT DOES NOT CARRY ACROSS: unlike VEP there is no per-population option to set -- AnnotateVcfConfig (vcf_sink.rs:381-455) has no af, af_1kg, af_gnomade or max_af member and `everything` is the only switch -- so each row's gating half ('with --af the hash GAINS AF') is not expressible and the value half is what is asserted; the gating is pinned once, generically, by tests/port_output_factory_vcf_csq.rs::row9_sift_column_appears_only_when_everything_is_on. THIS ROW: measured at 21:25585733 allele T, AF comes back 0.0010 -- Perl's literal, to the digit, four decimal places produced by AF_COLUMNS' format_4f flag on the AF entry (annotate_provider.rs:952) where a plain float render would spell 0.001; mutating the expectation to 0.001 fails the test. Two controls: a second locus in the same run gives 0.8458, and the field is asserted constant across all fourteen CSQ groups of the record, which is what makes it a variant-level rather than a per-transcript value. n=55 and n=57 of this block stay deferred and say on their own rows what is missing.

desc: add_colocated_frequency_data - af absent allele: asked for allele G at a C/T locus the hash comes back with Allele => 'G' and NO AF key -- a frequency is attached only for an allele the colocated record actually carries

Measured: the shard's record at 21:25585733 is C/T, and annotating the same position as C>G returns an empty AF while C>T returns 0.0010. The named test runs both and additionally asserts the G row IS annotated (it has consequence groups), so the empty AF is the lookup's answer rather than a row that failed to annotate -- the silent-empty reading this row exists to exclude. One measurement is stronger than the Perl: the whole colocated record drops out on an allele mismatch, not merely its frequency, so Existing_variation is empty too; that is asserted and noted rather than assumed. See the family anchor at n=53 for the CSQ indices and the observation channel.

desc: add_colocated_frequency_data - af other allele: asked for the REFERENCE allele C the hash gains AF => ['0.999'] -- the complement frequency, so the lookup is by allele rather than by alt-ness
rationale: Between n=53 and n=54 this completes the three-way case analysis: the called allele, an allele the record does not carry, and the other allele it does. The third is the one that shows the frequency is keyed by SEQUENCE and not by the record's notion of which allele is alternate. BLOCKER RE-BASELINED: the cache arrived with #96 and n=53, n=54, n=56, n=58 and n=59 are ported against it; this row is not, because the query it makes cannot be expressed. MISSING ARTEFACT: a public entry point that returns a colocated record's frequency for an ARBITRARY allele. Measured at the pin, the only public route to a frequency is vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf, and its lookup is keyed on the allele the input matched -- `freq_data.get(matched_allele.b_allele.as_str())` (annotate_provider.rs:2068), where b_allele comes from the record's ALT -- so the REFERENCE allele can never be the query. Confirmed end to end over the committed micro-cache: 21:25585733 C>T gives AF 0.0010, and the same locus spelled T>C, the only way a VCF can put C in the ALT column, matches no colocated record at all and gives an empty AF and an empty Existing_variation. WHAT IS NOT REACHABLE, PROBED PER docs/ledger-contract.md section "'Inaccessible' is a claim, and claims are probed": an earlier draft of this rationale offered ColocatedCacheEntry, its af_value(col) accessor and AF_COL_NAMES as evidence that the frequency DATA is reachable and only the allele-selection step is not. That control was FALSE, and the correction makes blocked-api more right rather than less. All three items are indeed `pub` (colocated.rs:105, :124, :136) but they sit inside a module that is not: lib.rs:53 reads `pub(crate) mod colocated;`, so nothing outside the crate can name them. Probed from an integration test in this repository at the pinned rev -- `use datafusion_bio_function_vep::colocated::{AF_COL_NAMES, ColocatedCacheEntry};` -- gives error[E0603]: module `colocated` is private, with the note pointing at lib.rs:53. desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash: an upstream VFOA's hash carries DISTANCE => 2407 beside STRAND, Feature_type => 'Transcript', Feature and Gene -- the distance being the one key the method computes rather than copies
rationale: The transcript-level base method, and the row is deliberately read for its computed half. Four of its keys (STRAND, Feature, Gene, Feature_type) are transcript metadata that VEP copies off `$tr` and vepyr reads through the transcript the consequence points at, and the Consequence key is passed IN by the caller (t/OutputFactory.t:842), not computed. DISTANCE is the exception: VEP measures the gap from the variant to the transcript bound, and so does vepyr -- `TranscriptConsequence.distance` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:637). The named test puts a variant 100 bp before a transcript starting at 1000 and requires `distance == Some(100)` together with the `upstream_gene_variant` term and `feature_type == Transcript`, and additionally requires `cdna_position == None`, which is what distinguishes an upstream overlap from an internal one. The metadata keys are not asserted, because reading back a field the test itself wrote would assert the fixture rather than vepyr; the rows whose whole content IS that metadata are n=66-69, and they are deferred. CHANNEL, stated once for n=42, 48, 60, 62, 63 and 64 and referred to by each: vepyr has no output-hash object and no writer hierarchy, but it builds the same per-(variant x feature) record one layer down. At dfbf 391f94bd `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::evaluate_variant_with_context` (transcript_consequence.rs:1154) returns one `TranscriptConsequence` (:613) per overlapping feature, and it takes its transcripts, exons and translations as plain slices -- so the channel needs no cache and the fixture is built in the test. That is also why these rows are analog-port and not unit-port: the property is the same, the inputs are not. Perl's are chr21 identifiers from the v115 block; the Rust fixture is a three-exon transcript whose CDS is ATG GCA GAT TGC AAA CCC GGG TTT AAA CCC GGG TGA, chosen so every expected value is derived by hand from the sequence.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - domains: with --domains a coding variant's hash gains DOMAINS => ['Low_complexity_(Seg):seg'] -- the analysis name and the domain identifier, joined by a colon, for every protein feature the variant's residue falls in
rationale: FAMILY ANCHOR for n=65-76: the transcript-metadata block of BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash. What these rows assert is that a fact recorded against the TRANSCRIPT in the cache reaches the per-consequence output record. vepyr carries every one of them as a CSQ column of the --everything layout (dfbf 391f94bd, golden_benchmark.rs:556) and copies them from TranscriptFeature the same way, but the copying happens inside annotate_provider.rs, whose entire public surface is two items (`grep -cE '^\s*pub (fn|struct|enum|const|type)' src/annotate_provider.rs` -> 2; positive control on transcript_consequence.rs -> 56). The only public observation point is the emitted CSQ, and #96 committed the chr21 cache it needs. These rows are deliberately NOT claimed against tests/port_output_factory_hashes.rs: the engine-level channel that carries n=60-64 does not carry them, because they are transcript metadata the test itself would have written, and reading back a field the fixture set asserts the fixture rather than vepyr -- running them over a real cache is the whole point. STILL DEFERRED in this block: n=69 (no RefSeq CSQ column at the pin) and n=73-76 (no RefSeq or merged cache), each with its own reason. THIS ROW is the strongest of the block because the value is COMPUTED rather than copied: VEP intersects the variant's protein position with the translation's domain features and gates the whole thing on the consequence being coding (OutputFactory.pm:1434, `if($self->{domains} && $pre->{coding})`). vepyr reproduces both halves -- lookup_domains(transcript_id, protein_position, amino_acids, ctx) behind an is_coding guard derived from cds_position (annotate_provider.rs:6269-6290, whose comment cites that exact Perl line) -- and emits DOMAINS at index 39. RE-SITED, and this is the disclosure: Perl drives rs116645811 and greps ENST00000307301 (:898-899); the analogue drives 21:25585733 and asserts on ENST00000352957. The move is forced by the coding gate above -- this variant is a 3_prime_UTR_variant on ENST00000307301, which is exactly why that transcript serves as the empty-DOMAINS control rather than as the subject. Measured over the committed shard: at 21:25585733 the missense consequence on ENST00000352957 sits at Protein_position 331, and the translation_core shard's ENSP00000284967 carries 75 protein features of which 67 span that residue, so DOMAINS has 67 &-separated entries against Perl's single v84 Low_complexity_(Seg):seg. The count is re-derived; the SHAPE is Perl's and is what the named test asserts -- every entry exactly analysis:identifier with both halves non-empty, the three distinct analyses being AFDB-ENSP_mappings, PANTHER and PDB-ENSP_mappings, and PANTHER:PTHR42753 present by name. The coding gate is the control: the same variant on ENST00000307301 is a 3_prime_UTR_variant with no protein position, and its DOMAINS must be empty. One escaping note: the shard spells the analyses with a space (`PDB-ENSP mappings`) and the CSQ with an underscore. That is the NON-divergent half of the escaper -- the pinned divergence tests/port_output_factory_vcf_csq.rs::rows20_and_28_whitespace_runs_do_not_collapse_the_way_vep_collapses_them (#200) is about RUNS of whitespace, and its own positive control asserts that a single space escapes exactly as VEP escapes it. Mutating the entry count to 66 fails the test.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - symbol: with --symbol an is_deeply over the WHOLE seven-key hash -- STRAND => -1, HGNC_ID => 'HGNC:14027', SYMBOL => 'MRPL39', Feature_type => 'Transcript', SYMBOL_SOURCE => 'HGNC', Gene => 'ENSG00000154719', Feature => 'ENST00000307301' -- three of which are coupled, so the display name always arrives with the authority that issued it
rationale: The COUPLING is the row's content: an implementation that emitted SYMBOL without SYMBOL_SOURCE would still look right in isolation. vepyr keeps the same triple as CSQ columns -- SYMBOL at index 3, SYMBOL_SOURCE at 22 and HGNC_ID at 23 (dfbf 391f94bd, golden_benchmark.rs:556) -- fed from TranscriptFeature.gene_symbol, gene_symbol_source and gene_hgnc_id (transcript_consequence.rs:250, :251, :258). Measured over the committed micro-cache at 21:25585733, all three of Perl's literals come back unchanged: MRPL39, HGNC, HGNC:14027. Perl's is_deeply is over the WHOLE hash -- SEVEN keys, not three (:909-921) -- so the named test pins six of them: SYMBOL, SYMBOL_SOURCE, HGNC_ID, STRAND = -1 and Feature_type = Transcript explicitly, Feature by the lookup that selects the group; the seventh, Gene = ENSG00000154719, is the control's discriminator below rather than a second pin. STRAND matters beyond this row, because n=60's rationale forwards the metadata keys to n=66-69 explicitly and n=66 is no longer deferred: before this assertion, `git grep -n '"STRAND"' -- 'tests/port_output_factory*.rs'` reached exactly ONE hit and it was the vocabulary list at port_output_factory_vcf_csq.rs:68, not a value (two hits after). Positive control that the grep is not silently empty and that the scoping is honest: the corpus does pin one strand value elsewhere, motif_strand = Some(1) at port_output_factory_regmotif.rs:218 -- a MOTIF's own orientation, on a field vepyr names motif_strand, not a transcript's CSQ STRAND. RE-SITED, disclosed: Perl reads buffer->[0]'s FIRST overlap, ENST00000307301 (:908); the analogue asserts on ENST00000352957 at the same variant. Only Feature differs -- STRAND -1, Feature_type Transcript, SYMBOL MRPL39, SYMBOL_SOURCE HGNC, HGNC_ID HGNC:14027 and Gene ENSG00000154719 were probed on ENST00000307301 and measure identically. The named test asserts the coupling rather than the values alone, using the second gene over the same locus as its control: ENST00000567517 belongs to an unnamed gene and its SYMBOL, SYMBOL_SOURCE and HGNC_ID are asserted empty TOGETHER, so the trio is shown to travel as a unit. Truncating the expected HGNC_ID fails it; so does STRAND -1 -> 1 (left "-1") and Feature_type -> RegulatoryFeature (left "Transcript"), both mutation-checked at 6 passed; 1 failed. See the family anchor at n=65 for the channel, the reason these rows are not claimed against tests/port_output_factory_hashes.rs, and the v84 -> v115 fixture move.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - gene_phenotype: with --gene_phenotype a variant in a gene with a recorded phenotype association gains GENE_PHENO => 1 -- a flag on the GENE, not on the variant
rationale: vepyr's field is TranscriptFeature.gene_phenotype (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:306), emitted as GENE_PHENO at CSQ index 36 (golden_benchmark.rs:556). That is Perl's single-overlap check WIDENED, not narrowed -- one overlap becomes fourteen, and the per-gene split below is only visible because of it. Measured, 21:25585733 gives GENE_PHENO = 1 -- Perl's literal. The row's distinct content is that the flag is on the GENE and not on the variant, and the committed shard can show that directly because one variant overlaps two genes: the named test walks EVERY CSQ group of the record and requires GENE_PHENO to be 1 on each of the thirteen MRPL39 transcripts and empty on the one ENSG00000260583 transcript -- same variant, same record, different answer per gene. It also asserts a second gene is present at all, so the loop cannot pass vacuously. Making the expectation unconditional fails it (left "", right "1"). See the family anchor at n=65 for the channel, the reason these rows are not claimed against tests/port_output_factory_hashes.rs, and the v84 -> v115 fixture move.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - en-masse scalar flags: one statement inside a foreach, standing for FIVE cases -- --ccds gives CCDS => 'CCDS33522.1', --protein gives ENSP => 'ENSP00000305682', --canonical gives CANONICAL => 'YES', --biotype gives BIOTYPE => 'protein_coding' and --tsl gives TSL => 5

The fifth, CANONICAL => YES, is on ENST00000352957 here because v115 moved MRPL39's canonical transcript; Perl's rendering -- the string YES rather than 1 -- is reproduced exactly. The named test asserts all five on ENST00000307301 (with CANONICAL required EMPTY there) and all five again on ENST00000352957 with different CCDS, ENSP and TSL values, so the scalars are shown to be per-transcript rather than five constants; and it requires exactly two CANONICAL=YES groups over the record, one per gene. desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - en-masse arrayref flags: the same loop for THREE cases whose values are lists rather than scalars -- --xref_refseq gives RefSeq => ['NM_080794.3'], and --uniprot gives both SWISSPROT => ['Q9NYK5'] and UNIPARC => ['UPI00001AEAC0'] from one option
rationale: Three cases in one statement (t/OutputFactory.t:952-964), and two properties beyond n=68: the values are LISTS because a transcript can carry several cross-references, and ONE option (--uniprot) populates TWO columns. vepyr keeps the list shape as &-joined CSQ values and the same two-from-one expansion -- SWISSPROT at index 32, TREMBL at 33, UNIPARC at 34 and UNIPROT_ISOFORM at 35 (dfbf 391f94bd, golden_benchmark.rs:556), from TranscriptFeature.swissprot, trembl, uniparc and uniprot_isoform.
