Measured: `grep -c '"RefSeq"' src/golden_benchmark.rs` returns 0 and `grep -rc xref_refseq src/` returns 0 for every file; positive controls on the same file, `"SWISSPROT"` 2, `"UNIPARC"` 2, `"REFSEQ_MATCH"` 8. The data is present and unread: the committed transcript shard's refseq_id column is non-null on 24 of its 228 rows. TWO OF THE THREE CASES DO COME BACK, recorded here rather than silently lost -- measured at 21:25585733 on ENST00000307301, SWISSPROT is Q9NYK5.193 (Perl's Q9NYK5, now version-suffixed) and UNIPARC is UPI00001AEAC0, which is Perl's literal exactly. The row is ONE is_deeply standing for three (option, column) cases, so claiming coverage for two of them would be a coverage claim the gate cannot police (docs/ledger-contract.md, 'What the gate does not check'); it stays deferred until the third column exists. See the family anchor at n=65.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - miRNA stem: for a SNV inside a miRNA transcript's stem, the hash gains miRNA => ['miRNA_stem'] -- the secondary-structure element the variant sits in, read off the ncRNA structure string
rationale: FAMILY SUB-ANCHOR for n=70-72. Unlike the rest of the n=65-76 block this value is computed from a STRING GEOMETRY: VEP indexes the transcript's ncRNA structure annotation at the variant's cDNA position and reports stem or loop. vepyr does exactly that, with the same output vocabulary: mirna_structure_field (dfbf 391f94bd, annotate_provider.rs:2813) gates on biotype != "miRNA" (:2819), expands the run-length structure string, indexes it with cdna_pos - struct_start, and maps `(` and `)` to miRNA_stem and `.` to miRNA_loop (:2809, :2905-2911); the result is the miRNA column at CSQ index 40. NOT RE-SITED, and the earlier wording of this rationale was wrong to say it was: the committed shard holds exactly one miRNA transcript and it is ENST00000385060 (MIR155) -- exactly the stable id Perl greps for at :978, :986 and :994. What moved for n=70-72 is the LOCI, not the transcript: n=71 25573987 -> 25573985 and n=72 25573994 -> 25574012, plus n=70's alleles C>T -> A>G because 25573985 reads A in the v115 reference slice where Perl's synthetic input file claimed C. n=70 itself sits at Perl's own position. The transcript spans 21:25573980-25574044, strand +1, one exon, so cDNA p is genomic 25573979 + p. Its ncrna_structure is `(14.(3.(8.(3.4)3.2)25`, which expands to the 65 characters of the transcript, and the module header of the named test writes the expansion out with its cDNA ranges. So 21:25573985 is cDNA 6, a `(`. Measured: miRNA = miRNA_stem, Perl's literal verbatim. The test asserts the cDNA position alongside the term, because that position is the index the structure lookup uses and a test checking only the term could pass while reading the wrong character. Mutating the expected term to miRNA_loop fails it.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - miRNA stem insertion: an INSERTION at the same miRNA transcript also reports miRNA => ['miRNA_stem'], and reports it once rather than twice for the two structure positions an insertion sits between
rationale: The row that separates a correct implementation from a plausible one: an insertion spans a boundary, so a naive index lookup emits the element twice. vepyr's comment records the same hazard in the same words -- mirna_structure_field warns against reporting miRNA_stem twice for a single overlapped region (dfbf 391f94bd, annotate_provider.rs:2812) -- and its implementation collapses the two by setting a boolean per structure character rather than pushing a term per position (:2885-2900). Perl's own transcript; the locus moved, 25573987 (:972) -> 25573985, to sit the insertion between two stem positions of the v115 structure string -- see n=70 for the full list of what moved and what did not. Measured: the insertion 21:25573985 A>AGG on ENST00000385060 comes back with cDNA_position 6-7, VARIANT_CLASS insertion, and miRNA = miRNA_stem -- Perl's literal, reported once. The named test asserts the ONCE directly (the value must carry no `&` separator, where a per-position implementation would write miRNA_stem&miRNA_stem) and asserts the 6-7 span, without which 'once' would be indistinguishable from 'the insertion only touched one position'. Mutating the expectation to the doubled term fails it. See the sub-anchor at n=70.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - miRNA loop: a SNV at a different position of the same transcript reports miRNA => ['miRNA_loop'] instead, so the field names WHICH element rather than merely that the transcript is a miRNA
rationale: The complement of n=70 and the pair's real content: two positions in one transcript give two different answers, which a field derived from the biotype alone could not produce. vepyr's mapping is per-character over the structure string (dfbf 391f94bd, annotate_provider.rs:2905-2911). Measured on Perl's OWN transcript at a moved locus (25573994 at :973 -> 25574012, to reach a loop character; the transcript is not re-sited -- see n=70): 21:25574012 is cDNA 33 of ENST00000385060, inside the four-character terminal loop the structure string spells `.4` (expanded positions 32-35), and miRNA comes back miRNA_loop -- Perl's literal verbatim, against n=70's miRNA_stem on the same transcript with the same BIOTYPE. The named test asserts the cDNA position too, for the reason given at n=70. Mutating the expected term to miRNA_stem fails it. See the sub-anchor at n=70.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - REFSEQ_MATCH: against a RefSeq cache the hash gains REFSEQ_MATCH => ['rseq_mrna_nonmatch', 'rseq_cds_mismatch'] -- the list of ways the RefSeq transcript disagrees with the genome it was aligned to
rationale: FAMILY SUB-ANCHOR for n=73-74. STAYS DEFERRED, but the blocker has CHANGED IN KIND and the old wording is now false. Until #197's fixture landed (PRs #497-#499) the reason was "no RefSeq or merged cache exists in this repository"; that cache now exists — tests/data/vep116_parquet_micro_cache/{refseq,merged}/, release 116, footers declaring bio.vep.cache_source_type — and it unblocked the nine sibling rows of this family: n=75 and n=76 of this file, AnnotationSource_Cache_Transcript.ledger.toml n=32-37 and OutputFactory_VCF.ledger.toml n=57. THE NEW BLOCKER, measured rather than assumed: `refseq_match` is NULL in EVERY release-116 transcript row measured: 0 non-null over 41,684 RefSeq rows and 165,022 merged rows, across chr1, chr17, chr21, chrX and chrMT. POSITIVE CONTROL on the same read of the same files, because an all-zero count is what a broken read also produces: `refseq_id` non-null = 9,920 and `source_cache` non-null = 154,178 on the merged side. The same control holds in miniature inside the committed fixture — `merged/transcript/chr21.parquet` has `refseq_id` non-null on 2 of its 45 rows and `refseq_match` on 0. The layer is missing UPSTREAM OF THE PARQUET BUILD: the builder does populate the column when the source carries the attributes, collecting every transcript attribute whose `code` starts with `rseq` and joining them with `&` (datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache/src/transcript.rs:781, :816, :894), and the column is present in the release-116 schema — it is simply empty. So the accurate statement is no longer "the release gate refuses v84" but "the supported release does not carry this layer": release 84's RefSeq cache does carry it (rseq_cds_mismatch 15, rseq_mrna_nonmatch 13; merged v84 adds rseq_ens_match_cds 24, per docs/campaigns/2026-08-28-final-deferred-v3/unlock-map.md) and release 84 fails the release gate, SUPPORTED_VEP_TARGETS holding 115 and 116 only (vep_semantics.rs:44-61). POSITIVE CONTROLS that vepyr's side is not what is missing: csq_field_names_for_mode_with_pick splices REFSEQ_MATCH into the RefSeq layout (golden_benchmark.rs:661-706 @ dfbf aa2be930), the value comes from TranscriptFeature.refseq_match (transcript_consequence.rs:267), and the field IS declared in the CSQ header emitted over the committed refseq fixture and empty in every group — asserted in CI by tests/port_output_factory_refseq_merged_csq.rs::refseq_match_is_the_one_field_the_release_116_build_cannot_fill, which goes red the day a populated layer arrives. THIS ROW needs the refseq arm: its expected list, ['rseq_mrna_nonmatch', 'rseq_cds_mismatch'], is what a RefSeq-only cache records about a transcript that disagrees with the genome it was aligned to, and no synthetic fixture can invent that vocabulary without inventing the alignment comparison behind it. Tracked in #529.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - REFSEQ_MATCH merged: against a MERGED cache the same field carries a longer list -- ['rseq_ens_match_cds', 'rseq_mrna_nonmatch', 'rseq_cds_mismatch'] -- including the Ensembl-versus-RefSeq comparison term a RefSeq-only cache cannot produce
rationale: The row's content is the difference from n=73: a merged cache knows both annotations, so it can record agreement between them, and the extra term rseq_ens_match_cds is the evidence. STAYS DEFERRED on the same measured blocker as n=73, and NOT on the one it used to carry — the merged cache this row named is now committed (tests/data/vep116_parquet_micro_cache/merged/) and its merged arm is demonstrably reachable: n=75 and n=76 of this file are ported against it. What is missing is only the content of one column: refseq_match non-null = 0 over 165,022 merged transcript rows, with source_cache non-null = 154,178 on the same read as the positive control. A refseq slice still does not satisfy n=73 and a merged one does not satisfy this row — they remain two artefacts, not one, and now for a reason about the cache BUILD rather than about which caches this repository happens to hold. See the sub-anchor at n=73 for the full measurement and the controls. Tracked in #529.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - merged source 1: on a merged cache a RefSeq transcript's hash carries SOURCE => 'RefSeq', a column that exists only in merged mode
rationale: UNBLOCKED by #197's merged micro-cache (PRs #497-#499). The blocker was never the field and never the mode — it was that the committed v115 shard's `source` column took only havana_tagene / havana / ensembl_havana / ensembl / mirbase over its 228 rows, none of which normalize_source_label maps to RefSeq, so the value this row asserts could not occur. The release-116 merged chr21 shard carries `source_cache` on all 45 rows, RefSeq on 8 and Ensembl on 37. ANALOG on channel: Perl reads SOURCE off BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash; vepyr has no per-VFOA hash, so the observation is the CSQ group the same value lands in (annotate_provider.rs:3944-3951, from TranscriptFeature.source). The field name and the expected value are Perl's, unchanged. MEASURED at 21:25585733 over the merged root: `NM_017446.4` comes back with SOURCE `RefSeq`, Gene `54148`, SYMBOL_SOURCE `EntrezGene`, `missense_variant`. CONTROL that SOURCE is a merged-mode column rather than one the layout always carries — which is what would make "SOURCE == RefSeq" vacuous: the same annotation over the REFSEQ root emits a header with no SOURCE field at all, and the two layouts are otherwise the identical list (csq_field_names_for_mode_with_pick splices SOURCE for merged alone, golden_benchmark.rs:661-706). That control is its own test, tests/port_output_factory_refseq_merged_csq.rs::the_source_column_is_a_merged_mode_column, because it is a property of the layout and not of either value.

desc: BaseTranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - merged source 2: the sibling transcript in the SAME merged run carries SOURCE => 'Ensembl', so the column varies per row rather than reporting the run's mode
rationale: The complement of n=75 and the pair's whole point: one run, two values, which an implementation that filled SOURCE from the configured mode would fail. That is why these are two rows with two tests and not one shared claim — n=76 can go red while n=75 stays green, and the dual-claim question ("could this test fail if only the other row's behaviour regressed?") answers yes in both directions. vepyr's value is per transcript (TranscriptFeature.source, transcript_consequence.rs:263 @ dfbf aa2be930), not per run. UNBLOCKED by the same fixture as n=75: the v115 shard already showed per-transcript variation over five distinct source values, but none of them was RefSeq, so the RefSeq-versus-Ensembl split this row is about could not be shown. MEASURED at 21:25585733 over the merged root, in ONE annotation: `ENST00000352957` carries SOURCE `Ensembl`, Gene `ENSG00000154719`, SYMBOL_SOURCE `HGNC`, while `NM_017446.4` in the same output carries `RefSeq`. The assertion is over the run's whole SOURCE set — exactly {Ensembl, RefSeq} — so a third spelling fails rather than passing unnoticed.

desc: TranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash: the full coding hash for the missense VFOA of rs142513484 -- Consequence, IMPACT => 'MODERATE', Feature_type, Feature, Gene, STRAND, and the five coding keys CDS_position 991, cDNA_position 1033, Protein_position 331, Amino_acids 'A/T' and Codons 'Gca/Aca'
rationale: The widest transcript-level hash in the file, and the one whose keys are all computed rather than copied. vepyr computes every one of them into the same record: `cdna_position`, `cds_position`, `protein_position`, `amino_acids` and `codons` are fields of `TranscriptConsequence` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:627-635), and IMPACT follows from the term through `SoTerm::impact` (so_terms.rs:243). The named test drives a G>A at codon 2 of the fixture's CDS and requires the whole set -- terms missense_variant, IMPACT MODERATE, the position triple 4/4/2, and crucially `Amino_acids == \"A/T\"` with `Codons == \"Gca/Aca\"`, which are the SAME TWO VALUES Perl asserts, because the fixture's codon 2 is GCA exactly so they would be. The positions differ (4/4/2 against 991/1033/331) because the transcript does; that difference is the whole of what separates this from a unit-port. CHANNEL, as at n=48: `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::evaluate_variant_with_context` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:1154) returns one `TranscriptConsequence` (:613) per overlapping feature, taking transcripts, exons and translations as plain slices, so the fixture is built in the test and no cache is involved. That the inputs are a synthetic three-exon transcript rather than chr21 is what makes this analog-port and not unit-port.

desc: TranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - total_length: with --total_length the three position keys change SHAPE, from 991 to '991/1017', 1033 to '1033/1110' and 331 to '331/338' -- each position rendered over the length of the sequence it indexes
rationale: A rendering switch on three columns at once, and the denominators are facts the row asserts as much as the positions: 1017 CDS bases, 1110 cDNA bases, 338 residues. vepyr never renders the pair. Over dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rc --include='*.rs' total_length src/` returns 0 (positive control on the same tree: `vcf_sink` -> 19), there is no config field (vcf_sink.rs:381-456), and `TranscriptConsequence`'s three position fields are single values with no length beside them (transcript_consequence.rs:627-631) -- as tests/port_output_factory_hashes.rs::coding_output_hash_carries_the_position_triple_amino_acids_and_codons shows by asserting bare `4`, `4` and `2`. Missing feature: --total_length.

desc: TranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - HGVSc: with --hgvsc the hash gains HGVSc => 'ENST00000352957.8:c.991G>A' -- the VERSIONED transcript accession, the c. prefix, the CDS-relative position and the substitution, in one string
rationale: The row pins a formatted string rather than a field, so the analogue has to produce the same grammar. vepyr does: `hgvs::format_hgvsc` (dfbf 391f94bd, hgvs.rs:172) builds it and the engine stores the result on `TranscriptConsequence.hgvsc` (transcript_consequence.rs:645), emitted as HGVSc at CSQ index 10 (golden_benchmark.rs:556). The named test requires `<accession>:c.4G>A` for the fixture's codon-2 substitution -- same four components in the same order as Perl's, with 4 where Perl has 991 because the CDS is 36 bases rather than 1017. The version suffix Perl shows (`.8`) is absent here only because the fixture's transcript carries `version: None`; that the accession is versioned when the cache supplies one is `TranscriptFeature.version` (transcript_consequence.rs:293), and is the same fact n=61 finds the Feature column does NOT have. CHANNEL, as at n=48: `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::evaluate_variant_with_context` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:1154) returns one `TranscriptConsequence` (:613) per overlapping feature, taking transcripts, exons and translations as plain slices, so the fixture is built in the test and no cache is involved. That the inputs are a synthetic three-exon transcript rather than chr21 is what makes this analog-port and not unit-port.

desc: TranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - HGVSp: with --hgvsp the hash gains HGVSp => 'ENSP00000284967.6:p.Ala331Thr' -- built on the TRANSLATION's accession, not the transcript's, and spelling both residues in three-letter form
rationale: Two properties beyond n=79, and both are easy to get wrong: the accession changes namespace (ENSP, not ENST) and the residues change alphabet (Ala/Thr, not A/T -- the same substitution n=77 reports as `A/T`). vepyr keeps both: `hgvs::format_hgvsp` (dfbf 391f94bd, hgvs.rs:1966) renders the notation, `hgvs::aa_one_to_three` (:99) is the alphabet conversion, and the result lands on `TranscriptConsequence.hgvsp` (transcript_consequence.rs:647), emitted as HGVSp at CSQ index 11 (golden_benchmark.rs:556). The named test requires `<protein accession>:p.Ala2Thr` against the fixture's own translation stable id, so a notation built on the transcript accession or in one-letter codes fails. CHANNEL, as at n=48: `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::evaluate_variant_with_context` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:1154) returns one `TranscriptConsequence` (:613) per overlapping feature, taking transcripts, exons and translations as plain slices, so the fixture is built in the test and no cache is involved. That the inputs are a synthetic three-exon transcript rather than chr21 is what makes this analog-port and not unit-port.

desc: TranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - non-coding: the same method on the 3' UTR VFOA reports cDNA_position 1122 and NO CDS_position, Protein_position, Amino_acids or Codons -- the absence being as much of the assertion as the presence
rationale: The complement of n=77, and the reason the pair exists: an implementation that emitted zeros or empty strings for the coding keys would satisfy neither `is_deeply`. vepyr keeps all five as `Option` fields of one struct (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:627-635), so absence is representable rather than a sentinel. The named test drives a variant 45 bases into the fixture's cDNA -- past the stop codon at cDNA 34-36 -- and requires `cdna_position == Some(\"45\")` together with `None` on each of cds_position, protein_position, amino_acids and codons. CHANNEL, as at n=48: `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::evaluate_variant_with_context` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:1154) returns one `TranscriptConsequence` (:613) per overlapping feature, taking transcripts, exons and translations as plain slices, so the fixture is built in the test and no cache is involved. That the inputs are a synthetic three-exon transcript rather than chr21 is what makes this analog-port and not unit-port.

desc: TranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - shift_length: with --shift_hgvs and --shift_length the hash gains SHIFT_LENGTH => 0 -- how far 3' the variant was moved before HGVS was computed, reported even when the answer is no movement at all
rationale: The row is about reporting the shift, not performing it, and the zero is the point: the field appears whenever the option is on, so a reader can distinguish an unshifted variant from one the annotator never considered. vepyr performs the shift and never reports its size. Over dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rc --include='*.rs' SHIFT_LENGTH src/` returns 0 (positive control on the same tree: `vcf_sink` -> 19), where `shift_hgvs` IS a public config field (vcf_sink.rs:414) and `hgvs::build_hgvs_genomic_shift` (hgvs.rs:849) computes the shifted coordinates. The nearest column is HGVS_OFFSET at CSQ index 41 (golden_benchmark.rs:556), which is VEP's own separate field with its own semantics and is not this one. Missing feature: the SHIFT_LENGTH output field.

desc: TranscriptVariationAllele_to_output_hash - sift and polyphen renderings: one statement inside a foreach standing for SIX cases -- --sift p gives 'tolerated_low_confidence', --sift s gives '0.17', --sift b gives 'tolerated_low_confidence(0.17)', and --polyphen p/s/b the same three shapes for 'benign' and 0.001
rationale: Six cases in one row (t/OutputFactory.t:1187-1203), and what they assert is a RENDERING CHOICE: the same stored prediction is written as a word, a number, or both, depending on the option's value. vepyr implements one of the three and offers no choice: its lookup helper's own doc says `Output uses --sift b / --polyphen b` (dfbf 391f94bd, annotate_provider.rs:2949, in the comment block over `lookup_sift_polyphen` at :2955, which cites Ensembl VEP `OutputFactory::add_sift_polyphen()` at :2943). So four of the six cases have no counterpart at all and two are merely unrunnable, which is why this row is no-feature and not blocked-data: a fixture would not make the p and s renderings appear. The prediction data itself is present and public -- `CachedPredictions::lookup_sift` and `lookup_polyphen` (transcript_consequence.rs:435, :439) return a (term, score) pair, and the crate ships a `sift_decode` module (lib.rs:68) -- so what is missing is the option, not the numbers. Missing feature: the --sift / --polyphen p and s output modes.

desc: RegulatoryFeatureVariationAllele_to_output_hash: the regulatory hash is six keys -- IMPACT => 'MODIFIER', Consequence => ['regulatory_region_variant'], Feature_type => 'RegulatoryFeature', Feature => 'ENSR00000140763', BIOTYPE => 'promoter' and Allele => 'T' -- with BIOTYPE carrying the FEATURE's type, not a transcript biotype
rationale: The first of the two non-transcript feature classes, and its distinguishing key is BIOTYPE: on a transcript hash that column holds `protein_coding`, here it holds the regulatory feature's own type. vepyr builds the same record in the same place -- the engine pushes a `TranscriptConsequence` with `feature_type: FeatureType::RegulatoryFeature`, `terms` containing `SoTerm::RegulatoryRegionVariant` and `biotype_override: r.feature_type` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:2044-2053), under a traceability comment that names `OutputFactory::RegulatoryFeatureVariationAllele_to_output_hash()` outright (:2073). IMPACT follows from the term through `SoTerm::impact` (so_terms.rs:243). The named test builds one RegulatoryFeature in memory -- the engine takes them as a plain slice (:1154) -- and asserts the term, MODIFIER, the feature type, the ENSR id in the Feature slot and `biotype_override == Some(\"promoter\")`. analog-port and not unit-port because the feature is synthetic: Perl's comes from the chr21 v115 regulatory cache, which this repository does not have (#212, #96).

desc: RegulatoryFeatureVariationAllele_to_output_hash - cell_type: with --cell_type HUVEC the regulatory hash gains CELL_TYPE => ['HUVEC:INACTIVE'] -- the feature's activity state in the named cell line, one entry per cell type requested
rationale: FAMILY ANCHOR for n=85 and n=111. VEP's regulatory build records a per-cell-type activity for each regulatory feature, and --cell_type selects which of them to report. vepyr's cache has no such axis: `RegulatoryFeature` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:542-549) is feature_id, chrom, start, end and a single `feature_type` used as BIOTYPE -- no activity, no cell line -- and `grep -rc --include='*.rs' cell_type src/` returns 0 over the whole crate (positive control on the same tree: `vcf_sink` -> 19), with no CELL_TYPE column in either CSQ layout (golden_benchmark.rs:464, :556). Missing feature: per-cell-type regulatory activity, which is a cache-build capability before it is an output field.

desc: MotifFeatureVariationAllele_to_output_hash: the widest single hash in the file -- eleven keys, five of them motif-specific: MOTIF_NAME => 'ENSPFM0042', MOTIF_POS => 7, HIGH_INF_POS => 'N', MOTIF_SCORE_CHANGE => '-0.026' and TRANSCRIPTION_FACTORS => ['CTCF'], plus STRAND taken from the MOTIF because there is no transcript to take it from
rationale: vepyr carries all five motif fields on the same record -- `motif_name`, `motif_transcription_factors`, `motif_strand`, `motif_pos`, `high_inf_pos` and `motif_score_change` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:652-670) -- emitted as CSQ indices 75-79 (golden_benchmark.rs:556), and the engine manufactures them from a `MotifFeature` slice with no transcript involved (:1154, :2341-2361). Two of Perl's expected values are reproduced EXACTLY by the named test, and both are derived rather than observed: MOTIF_POS 7, because the test's variant is the 7th base of its motif; and HIGH_INF_POS N, because the fixture's 7th matrix column is uniform, so its information content is 2 - H = 0 bits, far under the 1.5-bit threshold of `MotifMatrix::is_position_informative` (motif_matrix.rs:100-119). The same uniformity fixes MOTIF_SCORE_CHANGE at exactly 0.000 -- with (25 + 0.1) / (100 + 0.4) = 0.25 every weight in that column is log2(0.25/0.25) = 0, so substituting the base cannot move the relative similarity score -- where Perl's chr21 motif reports -0.026. The number differs because the matrix does, which is the whole of what makes this analog-port and not unit-port. The file's second test is the negative control: a non-uniform column yields an informative position and a negative, non-zero delta, so neither assertion above passes for want of a matrix.

desc: IntergenicVariationAllele_to_output_hash: the intergenic hash is three keys -- IMPACT => 'MODIFIER', Consequence => ['intergenic_variant'] and Allele => 'A' -- with no Feature, no Feature_type and no Gene, because there is no feature to name
rationale: The narrowest to_output_hash in the class, and its content is as much the three ABSENT keys as the three present ones: an intergenic allele must not be given a Feature. vepyr builds the same record -- `evaluate_variant_prepared_inner` pushes a consequence with `terms: vec![SoTerm::IntergenicVariant]` and `..Default::default()` when no transcript was hit (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:1664-1674), so `feature_type` defaults to `FeatureType::None` (:849-855) and `transcript_id` to None. The named test requires exactly that: the term, MODIFIER from `SoTerm::impact`, `feature_type == FeatureType::None` and `transcript_id == None`. Distinct from n=42, which asserts the same manufactured row EXISTS and would not fail if its contents were wrong. CHANNEL, as at n=48: `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::evaluate_variant_with_context` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:1154) returns one `TranscriptConsequence` (:613) per overlapping feature, taking transcripts, exons and translations as plain slices, so the fixture is built in the test and no cache is involved. That the inputs are a synthetic three-exon transcript rather than chr21 is what makes this analog-port and not unit-port.

desc: SV - VariationFeature_to_output_hash: a `21 25606614 sv_dup T . . . SVTYPE=DUP;END=25606616` record produces Location => '21:25606615-25606616' -- a SPAN derived from the INFO END field, where every non-SV row in this file reports a single coordinate
rationale: The SV block's first row, and the one that shows the input path is different before any output work happens: the span comes from INFO, not from the ALT column, and the start is shifted by one because a symbolic ALT means the anchor base is not part of the event. FAMILY ANCHOR for n=88-113, the whole STRUCTURAL VARIATION half of this file. Every one of those rows begins with an input record whose ALT is absent and whose span comes from `SVTYPE=DUP;END=...` in INFO, and vepyr has no such input path. Over dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rc --include='*.rs' SVTYPE src/` returns 0 (positive control on the same tree: `vcf_sink` -> 19); `VariantInput::from_vcf` (transcript_consequence.rs:34) takes a REF/ALT pair of plain sequences and trims them, with no symbolic-allele branch; and the variant classifier recognises only `SNV`, `substitution` and `indel` (annotate_provider.rs:7326-7333). What vepyr DOES have is the mirror image, and it must not be mistaken for this: `StructuralFeature` (transcript_consequence.rs:603) is a structural variant read FROM THE CACHE by `load_structural_features` (annotate_provider.rs:5044) and overlapped against an ordinary input variant, producing `transcript_ablation` / `transcript_amplification` / `feature_elongation` / `feature_truncation` terms (parse_sv_event_kind, :7343). That is VEP's co-located-SV annotation, the subject of n=15 -- not the StructuralVariationOverlapAllele hierarchy these rows exercise. Missing feature: annotating a structural variant given as input.

desc: SV - pick_worst_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele: the picker runs unchanged over StructuralVariationOverlapAlleles and returns ENST00000307301
rationale: The row asserts that the SV hierarchy reuses the variant-level picker rather than a parallel one -- the same method name, a different allele class. See the family anchor at n=88 for the measured absence of the SV input path, and for what vepyr's cache-side StructuralFeature is instead.

desc: SV - pick_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele_per_gene: per-gene selection over SV alleles keeps ENSR00000140751 and ENST00000307301, so a regulatory feature counts as its own gene group
rationale: Beyond n=89 this pins the grouping key's behaviour for a feature that has no gene: the regulatory feature forms a group of its own instead of being dropped. See the family anchor at n=88 for the measured absence of the SV input path, and for what vepyr's cache-side StructuralFeature is instead.

desc: SV - filter_StructuralVariationOverlapAlleles - no filter: the SV-specific dispatcher is the identity when no mode is set, returning as many alleles as it was given
rationale: The default arm of a SECOND dispatcher: VEP has one for variant alleles (n=29) and one for structural ones, and this row is what shows they behave alike unfiltered. See the family anchor at n=88 for the measured absence of the SV input path, and for what vepyr's cache-side StructuralFeature is instead.

desc: SV - filter_StructuralVariationOverlapAlleles - pick: --pick collapses the SV alleles to ENST00000307301 alone
rationale: The dispatch half for the SV hierarchy, as n=30 is for the variant hierarchy. See the family anchor at n=88 for the measured absence of the SV input path, and for what vepyr's cache-side StructuralFeature is instead.

desc: SV - filter_StructuralVariationOverlapAlleles - pick_allele: --pick_allele over a single-allele structural variant also yields ENST00000307301, so per-allele keying degenerates to per-variant when there is one allele

desc: get_multiple_custom_headers - different short_name: two --custom sources with DIFFERENT short names produce two header entries in declaration order, ['test', ...] then ['sample', ...]
rationale: The row's content beyond n=127 is the ordering and the one-entry-per-source rule. See the family anchor at n=17 for the measured absence of --custom, and for why vepyr's plugin-cache mechanism is a different feature rather than this one.

desc: get_multiple_custom_headers - same short_name: two --custom sources sharing ONE short name collapse to a single header entry whose second element is both paths joined by a comma -- merged, not duplicated and not silently dropped
rationale: The sharpest row of the custom-header trio: a name collision is resolved by merging the sources under the shared name, which neither a first-wins nor a last-wins implementation reproduces. See the family anchor at n=17 for the measured absence of --custom, and for why vepyr's plugin-cache mechanism is a different feature rather than this one.

desc: get_plugin_headers: every configured plugin contributes its declared output fields to the header -- one plugin declaring one field yields exactly one entry, ['test', 'header'], the field name beside its description
rationale: The one assertion of this file's plugin block with a vepyr counterpart. `OutputFactory::get_plugin_headers` (OutputFactory.pm:2399-2413) asks every configured plugin for `get_header_info` and returns one [field, description] pair per declared output field, in plugin order; those pairs are what lets a reader name the extra columns. vepyr's plugins are built parquet caches rather than Perl modules, and each carries a manifest.json declaring its `value_columns` and the CSQ field each contributes (dfbf 391f94bd, plugin_cache/cache_manifest.rs:25-33, :42-51). `PluginRegistry::field_names` (plugin_cache/registry.rs:100-109) reads those manifests -- opening no shard -- and returns exactly that list, and `vcf_sink.rs:671-677` is its only caller: it appends the names to the `##INFO=<ID=CSQ ... Format:` list. Same property, different channel, which is analog-port. WHAT THE CHANNEL DOES NOT CARRY, recorded rather than dropped: VEP's pair has a description and vepyr's manifest records none, so the CSQ Format list is names only. The row's substance is the field-name half -- it is what a reader needs to decode the trailing CSQ columns -- which is why the description's absence does not move the row to no-feature. The named test writes one manifest into a tempdir with `CacheManifest::write` (the same call the builder makes, :95-104) and asserts the single field comes back; the file's other two tests are its controls -- an empty root contributes nothing, and two plugins' fields arrive grouped by plugin and ordered by plugin name, the guarantee `discover_plugins` sorts for (:128).

desc: run_plugins: the dispatcher calls the configured plugin once per VFOA and merges what it returns into the output hash -- a plugin returning {test => 'Hello'} puts that key there
rationale: FAMILY ANCHOR for n=131-136. VEP's plugin system loads a Perl module per --plugin and calls `$plugin->run($vfoa, $line_hash)` once per consequence, taking whatever hashref comes back and merging it into the output; the six rows walk that call's contract -- a normal return, a skip, a non-hashref return, and the two warning paths. vepyr has no run-time plugin call at all. Its plugins are BUILT caches: a TOML source manifest is compiled into `<root>/plugin/<name>/*.parquet` plus a manifest.json, and at annotation time the values are joined in, not computed by a callback (dfbf 391f94bd, plugin_cache/mod.rs:1-8, plugin_cache/lookup.rs:279 `PluginLookup::probe`). So there is no `run` to dispatch, no skip protocol to honour, and no plugin-error path to warn from: `grep -rc --include='*.rs' run_plugins src/` returns 0 (positive control on the same tree: `vcf_sink` -> 19). Missing feature: a per-consequence plugin callback. What vepyr DOES have an analogue for is the header half -- n=130 -- because a built plugin still declares its output field names.

desc: run_plugins - skip: when the caller passes the 'skip' sentinel instead of a hash, the dispatcher returns undef and the plugin is not run at all
rationale: The skip protocol: a caller can suppress plugin evaluation per consequence without unconfiguring the plugin. See the family anchor at n=131.

desc: run_plugins - return is not hash: a plugin returning something that is not a hashref has its return value passed straight through rather than merged, so a misbehaving plugin cannot corrupt the output hash
rationale: The defensive arm: the dispatcher validates what came back before merging. See the family anchor at n=131.

desc: run_plugins - return is not hash message: the same misbehaving plugin makes the run warn 'did not return a hashref' on STDERR, so the silent passthrough of n=133 is not actually silent
rationale: The row pairs with n=133 and asserts on captured STDERR -- the Perl reopens STDERR onto a scalar for the purpose (t/OutputFactory.t:1904-1909). Both halves are absent for the same reason. See the family anchor at n=131.

desc: run_plugins - new fails: a plugin whose constructor throws leaves the dispatcher returning an empty hash rather than dying, so one broken plugin does not abort the run
rationale: The isolation guarantee: plugin failures are contained. See the family anchor at n=131.

desc: run_plugins - new fails message: the same failure warns 'went wrong' on STDERR, so a contained plugin failure is still reported
rationale: The pair to n=135, as n=134 is to n=133. See the family anchor at n=131.

desc: HGVS 3prime shifting - ON: with --shift_hgvs 1 an insertion at 21:25592985 A>ATAAA reports HGVSg => '21:g.25592986_25592989dup' beside Consequence => ['intron_variant'] and Allele => 'TAAA'
rationale: FAMILY SUB-ANCHOR for n=137 and n=138. The subject of the pair is --shift_hgvs, and vepyr has that: `shift_hgvs` is a public config field (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:414), the engine takes it through `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::new_with_hgvs_shift` (transcript_consequence.rs:1114) and `hgvs::build_hgvs_genomic_shift` (hgvs.rs:849) computes the shifted genomic coordinates. What makes the rows unsatisfiable is the OBSERVATION POINT: the only key in either expected hash that the shift can move is HGVSg, and that field does not exist. See the family anchor at n=51: `grep -rniwc --include='*.rs' hgvsg src/` returns 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, with `hgvsp` returning 63 on the same tree as the positive control. Missing feature: the HGVSg output field, not the shifting.

desc: HGVS 3prime shifting - OFF: with --shift_hgvs 0 the SAME insertion reports the SAME HGVSg => '21:g.25592986_25592989dup', because the 5'-most placement of a duplication in a homopolymer run coincides with the 3'-most one here
rationale: The pair's real content is that the two settings agree on this input -- an assertion that cannot be made at all without the field both sides report. See the sub-anchor at n=137.

desc: reset_shifted_positions: after `_return_3prime` has shifted a variant and the transcript variation's cds_start has been set, `reset_shifted_positions` clears it -- the memoised coordinate is invalidated so the next read recomputes
rationale: The row is about CACHE INVALIDATION on a mutable object graph: VEP memoises shifted coordinates on the TranscriptVariation and needs an explicit step to drop them when the shift no longer applies (`reset_shifted_positions`, OutputFactory.pm:306). vepyr performs no such operation, and could not: its consequence records are values built per variant by `evaluate_variant_with_context` (dfbf 391f94bd, transcript_consequence.rs:1154) and discarded, with no memoised coordinate to invalidate -- `grep -rc --include='*.rs' reset_shifted src/` returns 0 (positive control on the same tree: `vcf_sink` -> 19). This is not the not-applicable case: the assertion is not about Perl object identity or plumbing but about an operation the class performs, and an operation vepyr does not perform is no-feature (docs/ledger-contract.md, 'Absent operation vs present-but-private state'). Missing feature: coordinate memoisation with an explicit invalidation step -- which vepyr does not need, but which is nonetheless what this row pins.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - individual_zyg: with --individual_zyg all, ONE output row carries every sample's zygosity as a sorted list, 'barry:HOM,dave:HET,jeff:HOMREF' -- including the reference-homozygous sample
rationale: The zygosity variant of the per-sample family, and it differs from --individual (n=16) in shape: --individual emits one row PER sample, --individual_zyg emits one row carrying ALL samples. Both are absent. See the family anchor at n=16: vepyr annotates the record once and never reads the genotype columns, and `individual_zyg` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - individual_zyg wrong sample name: --individual_zyg john against a VCF whose samples are dave, barry and jeff makes the run DIE rather than silently annotating nothing
rationale: The only dies_ok in this file, and its content is that an unknown sample name is a configuration error rather than an empty selection. vepyr has no sample selection to validate, so there is no name to be wrong. See the family anchor at n=16: vepyr annotates the record once and never reads the genotype columns, and `individual_zyg` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - individual_zyg correct sample name: --individual_zyg dave,barry reports 'barry:HOM,dave:HET' -- the requested SUBSET, sorted, with jeff absent
rationale: The complement of n=140: the option selects rather than merely enabling, and the omission of jeff is as much of the assertion as the presence of the other two. See the family anchor at n=16: vepyr annotates the record once and never reads the genotype columns, and `individual_zyg` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd.

desc: VariationFeature_to_output_hash - individual_zyg alt = '.': a record with NO alternate allele still reports 'dave:HOMREF', so a sample is described even where there is no variant to describe
rationale: The edge case that makes the feature coherent: zygosity is a property of the genotype call, not of the variant, so an ALT-less record still has one. See the family anchor at n=16: vepyr annotates the record once and never reads the genotype columns, and `individual_zyg` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd.

desc: VariationFeatureOverlapAllele_to_output_hash - hgvsg for multi-allelic (first alt): for `21 25769083 . CT C,CTT` the FIRST alt's HGVSg is '21:g.25769085del'
rationale: FAMILY SUB-ANCHOR for n=144 and n=145. The pair's content is that HGVSg is computed PER ALLELE from a shared record: two alts of one site produce two different notations, and a deletion and a duplication at that. See the family anchor at n=51: `grep -rniwc --include='*.rs' hgvsg src/` returns 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, with `hgvsp` returning 63 on the same tree as the positive control. Missing feature: the HGVSg output field.

desc: VariationFeatureOverlapAllele_to_output_hash - hgvsg for multi-allelic (second alt): the SECOND alt of the same record is '21:g.25769085dup' -- a different HGVS type from the first, not merely a different position
rationale: The half that makes the pair load-bearing: an implementation that computed one notation for the site would fail here and pass at n=144. See the sub-anchor at n=144.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the OutputFactory parent module loads under `use` — which is also what makes its $CAN_USE_JSON package variable readable by the SKIP guard on line 37
rationale: A module-load probe, and the only assertion in the file outside the SKIP block. docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 makes `use_ok` not-applicable unconditionally: the line asserts that Perl's `require` found modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/OutputFactory.pm, compiled it and ran its `import`, and Rust performs no run-time module load that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design. It also does double duty, exactly as ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=14 does: perl/OutputFactory_JSON.t:37 skips the remaining assertions unless $Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::OutputFactory::CAN_USE_JSON is true, which presupposes the package compiled — and its hard-coded skip count, 24, is exactly rows 2-25 of this ledger. Both halves are Perl run-time plumbing. Nothing is hidden by the reading: the 19 rows that assert what the JSON writer does are all no-feature and stay in the denominator.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the CPAN JSON module loads under `use`, so `JSON->new` on line 229 can decode the writer's output for every comparison after it
rationale: The second module-load probe, and the only one in the file naming a third-party CPAN distribution rather than a VEP class. R2 applies unchanged: the line asserts Perl's loader found JSON.pm at run time, and Rust resolves its dependencies at build time. The nearest Rust fact is that `serde_json = "1"` is already declared in datafusion-bio-function-vep's Cargo.toml (line 26) and links today — a Cargo resolution, not an assertion. Worth stating because it locates the gap precisely: what vepyr lacks is the JSON *writer* (n=6), not a JSON serialiser to build it with.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the OutputFactory::JSON subclass loads under `use`, so line 50 can construct the writer object every later assertion is driven from
rationale: The third module-load probe, and the one that names the absent feature's own class. R2 says the classification does not change for that reason, and its corollary says why: a probe is carried to no-feature when the probe's *subject* is the absent feature, and `use_ok`'s subject is Perl's loader, not the class it names. The JSON writer's absence is carried instead by n=6, which reads the class back off a constructed object, and by the 18 rows that assert what the writer emits. Same call as ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=1 on the sibling Tab writer.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config module loads under `use`, so `Config->new()` on line 48 can build the config handed to the writer on line 50
rationale: Pure scaffolding, and the same compile-time-versus-run-time argument as n=1 (R2). vepyr's configuration object is the `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` struct (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:381), whose existence a test crate proves by compiling against it; there is no run-time load step that could fail. What Config actually resolves is t/Config.t's subject and is classified in ledger/Config.ledger.toml.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Runner module loads under `use`, so the `get_annotated_buffer` helper at lines 719-736 can build the annotated buffers 17 later rows are driven from
rationale: The fourth module-load probe. Runner is loaded only for `get_annotated_buffer` (perl/OutputFactory_JSON.t:719-736), which runs a full annotation pass and hands back an InputBuffer; rows 8-22, 24 and 25 use it as their fixture. Same R2 argument as n=1; what the runner does end to end is t/Runner.t's subject and belongs to ledger/Runner.ledger.toml.

desc: check class: `OutputFactory::JSON->new({config})` returns an object blessed into the JSON subclass — the writer `--json` selects, not its OutputFactory parent
rationale: docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R1 decides this row, and it lands on the denotation branch rather than the not-applicable one. Neither of R1's two not-applicable conditions holds. The construction on line 50 has no row of its own: `grep -c 'ok(' perl/OutputFactory_JSON.t` returns 6 and every one of the six is a `use_ok` line (31, 43, 44, 46, 47, 650), so this readback is the ledger's only accounting for the `new`. And the class does not denote a capability vepyr has. R1 therefore sends the row to the `ok($obj)` constructor table, where a class denoting a capability vepyr does not have is `no-feature`. The capability is per-format output dispatch: at dfbf 391f94bd the vep crate has no output-writer type family at all — the only public sink is the free function `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` (vcf_sink.rs:1018, the single hit of `grep -rnE 'pub (async )?fn annotate_to' src/`) — and `grep -rniE 'json_sink|annotate_to_json|output_format|JsonOutput' src/` returns no hits at all (positive control on the same tree: 19 hits for `vcf_sink`). There is no type whose identity could be read back, because there is no second writer to choose between. Same call as ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=4.

desc: headers - empty: the JSON writer contributes no header lines at all — `$of->headers` is the empty list, where every other OutputFactory subclass returns a preamble
rationale: The assertion's content is a difference *between* writers: JSON-Lines carries no preamble, so the inherited method returns nothing, while Tab and VEP_output return several blocks (ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=6). vepyr can exhibit neither side. Its one sink writes a VCF header — three `write_header` call sites at vcf_sink.rs:1301, :1322 and :1385, whose CSQ INFO description is assembled by the private `csq_header_description` (vcf_sink.rs:660) — so asserting `headers == []` against vepyr would invert the property rather than port it. This is no-feature rather than deferred/blocked-api: making `csq_header_description` public would still not produce a writer that emits no header, so the blocker is the absent writer (n=6), not a missing `pub`.

desc: add_VariationFeatureOverlapAllele_info: the per-VFOA half of the JSON document for rs142513484 — three snake_case objects under `transcript_consequences` (3_prime_UTR on ENST00000307301, missense on ENST00000352957, upstream on ENST00000567517) plus the sibling top-level `most_severe_consequence`
rationale: The JSON writer's document-building method, and the row pins both the nesting and the key spelling: cdna_start/cdna_end, cds_start/cds_end, protein_start/protein_end, amino_acids, codons and impact as snake_case JSON keys inside an array, with `most_severe_consequence` hoisted to the top level beside it. Every value in it is a quantity vepyr computes — cDNA_position, CDS_position, Protein_position, Amino_acids, Codons and IMPACT are entries 13-17 and 3 of `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (golden_benchmark.rs:464), and `most_severe_consequence` is a real output column of the annotate provider (annotate_provider.rs:3432, derived by `most_severe_term` at :5983) — so what is absent is the document, not the data. There is no per-VFOA JSON serialiser to call: `grep -rniE 'json_sink|annotate_to_json|JsonOutput' src/` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control 19 for `vcf_sink`. The same values are asserted through the CSQ channel in ledger/OutputFactory.ledger.toml and ledger/OutputFactory_VCF.ledger.toml, which own that observation point.

desc: add_colocated_variant_info_JSON: the `colocated_variants[]` object for rs142513484 — id, start/end/strand/allele_string, a per-allele `frequencies` map with 16 populations under key T, minor_allele and minor_allele_freq, var_synonyms, and pubmed and clin_sig split out of comma strings into JSON arrays
rationale: Two properties, and vepyr has nowhere to put either. The first is the nesting: an array of colocated-variant objects, each carrying a `frequencies` map keyed by the matched allele. vepyr emits colocated data as flat CSQ subfields — Existing_variation, AF, AFR_AF..SAS_AF, the gnomADe_* block, MAX_AF, CLIN_SIG and PUBMED, all in `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (golden_benchmark.rs:464) — one pipe-separated value per field per annotation record, never a nested per-allele object. The second is type coercion: `pubmed => '10,20,30'` becomes the numeric array [10, 20, 30] and `clin_sig => 'pathogenic,benign'` a two-element string array, which in VEP is the JSON writer's own `numberify` stage — `OutputFactory/JSON.pm:288` is its only caller — the same absence ledger/Utils.ledger.toml rows 10-15 book while pointing at this ledger. Missing feature: the JSON writer (n=6).

desc: add_colocated_variant_info_JSON_multi: for the tri-allelic co-located variant rs145564988 (G/A/T) only the input allele A gets a `frequencies` entry — the 1000G frequency carried by the variant's other allele T is deliberately not reported
rationale: A different property from n=9, and a sharper one: allele-scoped selection inside a multi-allelic colocated record, where the wrong reading — report every allele's frequencies — would still produce a well-formed document. The expected hash contains only gnomADe populations under key A, and the *absence* of the af/amr/afr block is the whole assertion. vepyr does perform allele scoping: `allele::get_matched_variant_alleles` (allele.rs:237, :253) matches an input variant against a cache allele_string. But the object this row inspects is built by the JSON writer, which does not exist (n=6), and vepyr's frequency output is one flat CSQ subfield per population with no per-allele grouping to select within. So the row is no-feature for the writer, not deferred on the matching.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - count: the JSON writer emits exactly one line per buffered VariationFeature — the per-VFOA fan-out is folded into the nested arrays rather than into extra lines
rationale: The row pins the writer's cardinality, and it is the one property in this file where JSON differs from every other VEP writer: Tab and VEP_output emit one line per variant x feature x allele (744 lines for a comparable buffer, ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=11), JSON emits one per variant. vepyr has neither cardinality to observe, because it has no line-emitting writer other than the VCF sink, whose unit is the VCF record and whose per-VFOA fan-out is packed into a single CSQ INFO value. Nothing is hidden behind a missing `pub`: the operation — rendering an annotated buffer as JSON lines — is absent (n=6). What vepyr's record count is worth asserting against belongs to ledger/OutputFactory_VCF.ledger.toml.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - check first: the whole first JSON object for rs142513484 after decoding — `input` echoing the raw VCF line including its GT column, assembly_name GRCh38, seq_region_name/start/end/strand/allele_string/id, most_severe_consequence, and the three transcript_consequences
rationale: The file's top-level schema assertion: which keys exist at the root of the document, and that the raw input line is echoed back verbatim under `input`. vepyr has no JSON document (n=6) and no counterpart to the `input` echo in any channel — its VCF output rewrites the record rather than quoting it — while assembly_name and seq_region_name have no CSQ subfield at all: `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (golden_benchmark.rs:464) starts Allele|Consequence|IMPACT|SYMBOL and contains neither name. The annotation values nested underneath are the ones n=8 covers and are observable through CSQ; what this row adds on top of them is the root schema, and that is the missing feature.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - regulatory information: under `--everything`, line 29 of the output carries a `regulatory_feature_consequences[]` array with regulatory_feature_id ENSR00000140751, biotype promoter, impact MODIFIER and consequence regulatory_region_variant
rationale: A third nested array, parallel to transcript_consequences and colocated_variants, holding regulatory-feature hits under their own key. vepyr does annotate regulatory features and motifs — `FeatureType::RegulatoryFeature` renders the Feature_type value "RegulatoryFeature" (transcript_consequence.rs:861), and MOTIF_NAME, MOTIF_POS, HIGH_INF_POS, MOTIF_SCORE_CHANGE and TRANSCRIPTION_FACTORS are entries 24-28 of `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (golden_benchmark.rs:464) — but it renders them as further CSQ records inside the same INFO value, distinguished by a column, never as a separate array under a key of their own. The missing feature is the JSON document's partitioning by feature class (n=6); what the regulatory annotations themselves should contain is ledger/AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat.ledger.toml's subject.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - everything: under `--everything` the first JSON object expands to the full document — variant_class SNV, the colocated_variants block, and per-transcript hgvsc/hgvsp, hgnc_id, gene_symbol, exon, canonical, protein_id, swissprot/uniparc, ccds, tsl, appris and the split sift_score/sift_prediction and polyphen_score/polyphen_prediction pairs
rationale: The widest document assertion in the file, and the one whose *content* vepyr already implements: `AnnotateVcfConfig::everything` (vcf_sink.rs:383) selects the 80-field vocabulary `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (golden_benchmark.rs:556), which carries HGVSc, HGVSp, HGNC_ID, SYMBOL, EXON, CANONICAL, ENSP, SWISSPROT, UNIPARC, CCDS, TSL, APPRIS, SIFT, PolyPhen and VARIANT_CLASS. What is absent is the channel and its typing — nested snake_case JSON keys, with each predictor split into a numeric score and a string prediction, instead of one pipe-separated `tolerated_low_confidence(0.17)` string per field — and the writer that would produce it (n=6). VEP's chr21 test cache, which this repository does not carry, is a second blocker behind the first, not the primary one.

desc: minimal - expanded count: under `--minimal`, the two-ALT row 21:25741665 CAGAAGAAAG>TAGAAGAAAG,C is decomposed into 2 buffer entries before any output is written
rationale: The row asserts InputBuffer state rather than JSON, but it asserts the state `--minimal` produces, and vepyr has no `--minimal`: `grep -rniE '\bminimal\b' src/` returns 5 hits at dfbf 391f94bd and every one is a doc comment or a test-helper name (allele.rs:283, annotate_provider.rs:15621, transcript_consequence.rs:13628 and :18755, plugin_cache/build.rs:238) — no option, no field, no function. vepyr counts a multi-ALT row as one input unit per ALT from the start (`batch_input_units`, annotate_provider.rs:9692, over `alt_input_units`, :9681) and annotates each independently, so there is no decomposition step whose result could be counted. Missing feature: the `--minimal` split, exactly as ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=70 books it.

desc: minimal - expanded first allele string: the first decomposed entry has allele_string C/T — the shared 9 bp suffix AGAAGAAAG is trimmed off an equal-length MNV
rationale: The trimming half of what n=15 pins, and the reason it cannot be claimed as a port is precise. The pinned crate does carry a source-equivalent port of the Ensembl `trim_sequences` that InputBuffer.pm:665 calls — `allele::trim_sequences_ensembl_with_end` (allele.rs:32) — and fed these inputs it returns C/T. But vepyr never runs it on the input path: its only production callers are inside `get_matched_variant_alleles` (allele.rs:237, :253), the colocated-allele matcher. What vepyr's input path runs is `vcf_to_vep_allele` (allele.rs:296), whose suffix loop is guarded by `if ref_bytes.len() != alt_bytes.len()` (:311) with the doc comment stating that VEP only suffix-trims indels, not MNVs — so on vepyr's input path this allele stays CAGAAGAAAG/TAGAAGAAAG by design. Naming the colocated function would claim coverage of a code path vepyr never takes; ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=70 records that correction and ledger/vepyr-only.ledger.toml `input-buffer-02` books the tests that do belong to it.

desc: minimal - rejoined count: `rejoin_variants_in_InputBuffer` merges the 2 decomposed entries back into 1 before the writer runs
rationale: The rejoin phase — the second half of VEP's two-phase minimal pipeline, where per-allele consequences are merged back onto a single output record. vepyr has no rejoin at all: `grep -rniE 'rejoin' src/` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd (positive control on the same tree: 19 hits for `vcf_sink`), because nothing was ever split (n=15). ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=9 books the same missing feature from the flag side, `rejoin_required`. The method is defined on the OutputFactory parent, so the gap sits in the writer layer here as well as in the input layer there.

desc: minimal - rejoined allele string: after the rejoin the single entry is restored to the original untrimmed VCF allele string CAGAAGAAAG/TAGAAGAAAG/C, not to a re-joined minimal one
rationale: A property n=17 cannot reach: that one only counts entries, while this one pins that the rejoin restores the *original* allele string, i.e. that VEP carried `original_allele_string` alongside the minimised form for the whole round trip and put it back. vepyr keeps no such pair — there is no split (n=15), no rejoin (n=17), and `grep -rn 'original_allele_string' src/` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd (positive control on the same tree: 19 hits for `vcf_sink`), so there is nothing to restore from. The bookkeeping fields it depends on are part of the missing feature ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=70 names.

desc: minimal - get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer: after the rejoin the one JSON object carries one transcript_consequences entry per original ALT — keyed here by variant_allele, `-` (inframe_deletion + splice_region_variant) and T (missense) — each tagged with the allele_num that maps it back to its VCF ALT column, 2 and 1
rationale: The output side of the minimal round trip, and the only row in the file that asserts `allele_num`. vepyr emits nothing of the kind: `grep -rniE 'allele_num' src/` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd (positive control on the same tree: 19 hits for `vcf_sink`), and ALLELE_NUM appears in neither `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (74 entries, golden_benchmark.rs:464) nor `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (80, :556). Without the split there is nothing to number, and without the JSON writer (n=6) there is no object to key by variant_allele. Two missing features stacked on one line, which is why the row stays separate from n=15-n=18 rather than folding into them.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - refseq used_ref: under `--refseq --uploaded_allele` the first transcript_consequences entry of a G>GA insertion on NM_000484.3 carries given_ref and used_ref both `-`, refseq_match [rseq_mrna_match], uploaded_allele G/GA, and a frameshift_variant with amino_acids I/IX
rationale: Worth recording precisely, because two of the three things this row pins are within vepyr's reach and one is not. GIVEN_REF and USED_REF exist as vepyr output columns and CSQ subfields — annotate_provider.rs:825 and :831 declare the names, transcript_consequence.rs:648-651 documents their meaning, and they are formatted into the refseq CSQ tail at annotate_provider.rs:6350 and :6355 — and `AnnotateVcfConfig::refseq` is `pub` (vcf_sink.rs:422). `uploaded_allele` does not exist: `grep -rn 'uploaded_allele' src/` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd (positive control on the same tree: `pub refseq` 4 hits, `pub everything` 1). And the row's channel — snake_case keys inside a per-VFOA JSON object — is absent regardless (n=6). The primary blocker is the writer, hence no-feature rather than deferred; when a JSON sink is built, this row ports with only the `--uploaded_allele` option still to add.

desc: use total_length 1: under `--total_length` the cDNA, CDS and protein coordinates render as position/length pairs — cdna_start 1122/1199, cds_start 991/1017, protein_start 331/338 — instead of bare integers, across all three transcript_consequences entries
rationale: A rendering option, and vepyr has neither the option nor the totals it needs: `grep -rn 'total_length' src/` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd (positive control on the same tree: 19 hits for `vcf_sink`), and no field of `AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) corresponds to it. vepyr emits bare positions in CSQ subfields 13-15, cDNA_position/CDS_position/Protein_position (`golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES`, golden_benchmark.rs:464). The row additionally pins that the pairs come out as JSON *strings* rather than numbers — '1122/1199' is not numberifiable — which is a property of the JSON writer's typing stage and has no counterpart anywhere in vepyr. Missing features: `--total_length`, and the writer.

desc: check coordinates when variant is outside of feature: for a 45 bp symbolic <DEL> at 21:25585652-25585700 the two overlapping transcripts get cdna_start but NO cdna_end key at all, alongside bp_overlap 45, percentage_overlap 0.21 and a feature_truncation term — the assertion 116.0 added to this file
rationale: This file's only `new` row (audit/vep-116/OutputFactory_JSON.md), and it lands on three separate gaps, each measured at dfbf 391f94bd with the same positive control, 19 hits for `vcf_sink` on the same tree. (1) Structural input: `grep -rn 'SVTYPE' src/` returns 0 hits, so a symbolic <DEL> carrying END= is not a record vepyr's input path recognises. (2) Overlap statistics: `grep -rniE 'bp_overlap|percentage_overlap' src/` returns 0 hits, and neither name appears in `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (74, golden_benchmark.rs:464) or `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (80, :556). (3) The consequence: `feature_truncation` exists in vepyr only as SO vocabulary — `SoTerm::FeatureTruncation` occurs at so_terms.rs:24, :68, :114, :160, :208 and :254 (declaration, term list, to_string, from_str, rank, impact) and nowhere else, so no code path assigns it. On top of the three sits the assertion's actual content, which the audit isolates: an undefined coordinate is rendered as an ABSENT KEY, not as null and not as a copy of the start — 116.x changed JSON.pm's two `delete $vfoa_hash->{...}` guards to fire on `defined($s)`/`defined($e)`, and to stop overwriting an HGVS-style `?`. Absent-key semantics need a writer that can omit a key; vepyr's CSQ is positional, where an unset subfield is the empty string between two pipes, so even a built JSON sink would have to make this choice deliberately. Recording that is the point of this row.

desc: custom: the AnnotationSource::File module loads under `use` — which is also what makes its $CAN_USE_TABIX_PM package variable readable by the inner SKIP guard on line 656
rationale: The sixth and last module-load probe, doing the same double duty as ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=14 and ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=15 on the identical module: perl/OutputFactory_JSON.t:656 skips the two assertions that follow unless $Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::File::CAN_USE_TABIX_PM is true, which presupposes the package compiled. Both halves — that Perl found the file, and that a package variable is now visible — are Perl run-time plumbing with no Rust counterpart, and R2 makes the call unconditional. That the feature the module implements is absent from vepyr does not change the reading and hides nothing: the two assertions the guard protects (n=24, n=25) are no-feature and stay in the denominator.

desc: custom_annotations: with a --custom VCF declared short_name=test,type=exact,fields=FOO, the JSON object gains a custom_annotations map whose `test` array holds one record — name test1, allele T, and a nested fields object carrying FOO=BAR and FILTER=[PASS]
rationale: A double gap, both halves measured. The JSON writer is absent (n=6), and so is the --custom annotation source that would fill the map: `grep -rniE 'custom_annotation|pub custom|CustomAnnotation|short_name' src/` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd (positive control on the same tree: `pub plugin_cache_root` at vcf_sink.rs:455). vepyr annotates from its parquet cache and, optionally, a pre-built plugin cache; there is no mechanism for attaching an arbitrary tabix-indexed VCF and projecting its INFO fields — nor for the FILTER column this record carries beside them. Sitting inside a SKIP block does not soften the classification: docs/ledger-contract.md keeps such rows in the denominator as no-feature, and R2's corollary confirms the reading, because here the assertion's subject really is the absent feature rather than Perl's loader.

desc: custom_annotations overlap: with type=overlap instead of type=exact, a 4 bp CATG>TACG input matches three custom records (test1, del1, del2) by position alone, and each is reported with its name only — no allele and no fields
rationale: A distinct property from n=24, and the reason the two rows stay apart: type=overlap changes both the matching rule — positional overlap rather than exact allele match — and the record shape, because an overlap match has no matched allele to report and this source declares no fields. Same two absences as n=24, no JSON writer (n=6) and no custom annotation source at all (`grep -rniE 'custom_annotation|pub custom|CustomAnnotation|short_name' src/` = 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `pub plugin_cache_root` at vcf_sink.rs:455), so a built writer on its own would not make this row portable: the source has to exist first, and with both match modes.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the OutputFactory::Tab module compiles and loads under `use`
rationale: A module-load probe: `use_ok` asserts only that Perl found and compiled modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/OutputFactory/Tab.pm at run time, and nothing about what the class does. Rust answers the same question at link time — an item named by a `use` that does not resolve is E0432/E0433 and there is no binary to run — so a run-time assertion would restate the compiler. docs/ledger-contract.md names use_ok/can_ok/isa_ok existence probes as the legitimate not-applicable case. That the module's *feature* is absent from vepyr does not change the reading, and hides nothing: the 13 rows that assert what the Tab factory does (n=4-13, 15-17) are all no-feature and stay in the denominator. Same treatment, same argument, at ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=15.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config module loads under `use`, so line 37 can build the config every later object is handed
rationale: The second of this file's four module-load probes, pure scaffolding: Config is loaded only so `Config->new()` on line 37 can produce the config passed to the Tab factory on line 39. Same compile-time-versus-run-time argument as n=1. vepyr's configuration object is the `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` struct (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:381), whose existence a test crate proves by compiling against it; there is no run-time load step that could fail. What Config actually resolves is t/Config.t's subject and is classified in ledger/Config.ledger.toml.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Runner module loads under `use`, so the two helper subs at lines 283 and 302 can build annotated buffers
rationale: Third module-load probe. Runner is loaded only for `get_annotated_buffer`/`get_annotated_buffer_runner` (perl/OutputFactory_Tab.t:283-319), which rows 8, 11-13 and 15-17 use as a fixture. Same compile-time argument as n=1; what the runner does end to end is t/Runner.t's subject and belongs to ledger/Runner.ledger.toml.

desc: check class: `OutputFactory::Tab->new({config, header_info})` returns an object blessed into the Tab subclass — the writer `--tab` selects, not its OutputFactory parent
rationale: Read as a bare blessing probe this would be not-applicable, but what is blessed is the per-format output factory, and format dispatch is exactly the feature vepyr lacks. At dfbf 391f94bd the vep crate has no output-writer type family at all: the only public sink is the free function `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` (vcf_sink.rs:1018 — the one hit of `grep -rnE 'pub (async )?fn annotate_to' src/`), and `grep -rniE 'tab_sink|flat_?tab|to_tsv|output_format|field_selector' src/` returns no hits at all (positive control: 19 hits for `vcf_sink` on the same tree). There is no type whose identity could be read back, because there is no second writer to choose between. docs/ledger-contract.md's RULING on the `ok($obj)` constructor probe settles it: decide by what the class denotes, not by the shape of the assertion, and a class denoting a capability vepyr does not have is `no-feature` — the same call the ruling makes for CacheDir.t n=30. (The SKIP-block convention is not what governs here: this row is not inside a SKIP block.)

desc: fields: the --tab writer's default column vocabulary is exactly these 18 names in this order, Uploaded_variation .. FLAGS plus the fixture's custom_test column
rationale: The row pins a column vocabulary *and* its order for a writer vepyr does not have (n=4), including a `custom_test` column that only exists because the fixture's header_info declares a --custom annotation. vepyr's own output vocabulary is a different list in a different channel: the VCF CSQ subfield names, `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (74 entries, golden_benchmark.rs:464) and `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (80, :556), both public at the pin. That list starts Allele|Consequence|IMPACT|SYMBOL and contains neither Uploaded_variation nor Location, so naming it here would claim the Perl's expected value against a list that does not match it. What vepyr's CSQ vocabulary is worth asserting against belongs to ledger/OutputFactory.ledger.toml and ledger/OutputFactory_VCF.ledger.toml; the missing feature here is the flat-tab column layout.

desc: headers: the --tab preamble is 3 provenance lines, a `## Column descriptions:` block with one human-readable line per column, a `## VEP command-line: vep ...` line, and finally the `#`-prefixed tab-joined column header
rationale: Four distinct header blocks, and vepyr writes none of them. What it writes instead is a VCF header (`write_header`, vcf_sink.rs:1301/:1322/:1385) whose CSQ INFO description is assembled by the private `csq_header_description` (vcf_sink.rs:660) as `Consequence annotations from annotate_vep. Format: <field names joined by |>`. So the per-column descriptions and the recorded command line have no counterpart in any vepyr output at all, and the fourth block — the column header — survives only as a pipe-joined Format list inside one INFO line, a different channel for a different format. This is no-feature rather than deferred/blocked-api: making `csq_header_description` public would still not produce a tab preamble, so the blocker is the absent writer, not the missing `pub` (docs/ledger-contract.md §"Absent operation vs present-but-private state"). The VCF header vepyr does write is ledger/OutputFactory_VCF.ledger.toml's subject.

desc: --merged and --custom dont duplicate SOURCE header: with both options on, `grep {$_ eq 'SOURCE'} @{$of->fields}` counts exactly 1
rationale: What the row pins is a *collision* between two independent SOURCE-adding options, and vepyr has only one of the two. `AnnotateVcfConfig::merged` exists (vcf_sink.rs:424) and its merged vocabulary carries SOURCE exactly once — dfbf's own in-src test asserts `merged[29] == "SOURCE"` (golden_benchmark.rs:1352), which no external crate can index. A --custom annotation source does not exist at the pin: `grep -rniE 'custom_annotation|pub custom|CustomAnnotation|short_name' src/` returns 0 hits, positive control `pub plugin_cache_root` at vcf_sink.rs:455. With a single contributor the duplication this assertion guards against cannot arise, so there is nothing to observe and the missing feature is the custom-annotation source. Note what is deliberately NOT claimed: `golden_benchmark::csq_field_names_for_mode(false, false, true)` is public (:653) and a cheap test could assert one SOURCE in merged mode, but that pins a strictly weaker property than the Perl — one adder instead of two — so claiming it as an analogue would overstate coverage.

desc: headers - plugin: the last two header lines, concatenated, record the `--plugin TestPlugin` command line and end with the plugin-declared column `test`
rationale: Two properties, both belonging to the tab header block: that the invoking command line is written into the output, and that a loaded plugin's declared column is appended to the column header. vepyr records no command line in any output at the pin, and has no tab header at all (n=4). Its plugin mechanism does exist and does append plugin field names to the output vocabulary — `AnnotateVcfConfig::plugin_cache_root` (vcf_sink.rs:455) and the `PluginRegistry::field_names(root)` loop in `csq_header_description` (vcf_sink.rs:672-678) — but that appends to the VCF CSQ Format list, and it consumes a pre-built plugin cache rather than loading a Perl plugin module named on `--plugin`. So neither half of this assertion has a vepyr observation point: the missing feature is the tab header, and behind it the plugin *loader*.

desc: output_hash_to_line - empty: an empty output hash renders as 18 columns, every one of them the `-` sentinel
rationale: The assertion pins the row formatter and its empty-value sentinel. vepyr has no row formatter for any tab format (n=4), and no `-` sentinel either: an unset CSQ subfield is the empty string between two pipes, which dfbf's own test states for SOURCE and REFSEQ_MATCH (`assert_eq!(merged_values[merged_index("SOURCE")], "")`, annotate_provider.rs:16487). Nothing here is private: the 13 textual matches for `output_hash|hash_to_line|format_row` in the crate are all doc-comment traceability pointers to VEP's Perl methods — `output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk()` at annotate_provider.rs:2258 and transcript_consequence.rs:4010, the VCF renderer, never Tab's `output_hash_to_line` — and not one is a Rust fn — so this is an absent operation, i.e. no-feature and not deferred/blocked-api.

desc: output_hash_to_line - test 0: the falsy id 0 survives into column 1 as `0` rather than collapsing to the `-` sentinel, while the other 17 columns stay `-`
rationale: A boundary the empty-hash row (n=9) cannot reach: it pins that the formatter tests *definedness*, not truthiness, which in Perl is a real hazard because `0` is false. Same absent formatter as n=9, so the same product statement — but the row is kept separate rather than folded into it, because a writer could pass n=9 and still fail this one. It is not not-applicable: what it pins is an output-rendering rule of a writer, not Perl object plumbing. When a tab writer is built for vepyr, Rust's `Option<String>` carries the same distinction in the type, so the row will become portable rather than moot.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - count: the annotated test_vcf buffer renders 744 tab lines, one per variant x feature x allele, under show_ref_allele + uploaded_allele
rationale: The per-VFOA fan-out is a property vepyr does have — it emits one CSQ record per variant/feature/allele — but this assertion counts *lines emitted by the tab writer*, and that writer does not exist (n=4); the CSQ-record count is observed in ledger/OutputFactory.ledger.toml and ledger/OutputFactory_VCF.ledger.toml, which own that channel. Two of the three inputs are missing as well, which is why no wording here promises a quick port: `show_ref_allele` and `uploaded_allele` return 0 hits over the whole crate (positive control: `pub everything`/`pub refseq`/`pub merged` at vcf_sink.rs:383/:422/:424), and the fixture is VEP's chr21 test cache, which this repository does not carry (audit/vepyr-master/per-port.md §"the three notes": 13 call sites of `workspace_path("vep-benchmark/data/port/_cache115/...")`). The primary blocker is the absent writer, so the row is no-feature rather than deferred/blocked-data.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - check first: the first tab line byte for byte — rs142513484 at 21:25585733, a 3_prime_UTR_variant on ENST00000307301, with the reference allele C and the uploaded allele C/T occupying two extra columns before IMPACT
rationale: The row pins the writer's whole per-row rendering at once: column order, the `-` sentinel in every unfilled column, and the two extra columns that --show_ref_allele and --uploaded_allele insert after Existing_variation. vepyr has neither the writer (n=4) nor those two options (`grep -rn 'show_ref_allele\|uploaded_allele' src/` = 0 hits at the pin; positive control as in n=11). The annotation values the line carries — the consequence term, cDNA position 1122, IMPACT, STRAND -1 — are quantities vepyr does compute and are asserted through the CSQ channel in ledger/OutputFactory.ledger.toml; what this row would add on top of those is the tab rendering, which is the missing feature.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - check last: the last tab line byte for byte — a missense on ENST00000448850 carrying Amino_acids V/I, Codons Gtt/Att and the FLAGS value cds_start_NF
rationale: The same absent writer and the same two absent options as n=12, on the other end of the buffer; the row is distinct because it is the only one in the file that exercises a filled FLAGS column and the coding-position columns (CDS 832, protein 278).
