Worth recording precisely because the *values* are within vepyr's reach: FLAGS is CSQ field 20 of `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (golden_benchmark.rs:464; the crate's own test pins the neighbours, STRAND at 19 on :1299 and SOURCE at 28 on :1300), so what is missing is only the rendering — which is why this is no-feature and not blocked-engine.

desc: custom: the AnnotationSource::File module loads under `use` — which is also what makes its $CAN_USE_TABIX_PM package variable readable by the SKIP guard on line 209
rationale: The fourth module-load probe, doing the same double duty as ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=15 on the identical module: line 209 skips the assertion that follows unless $Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::File::CAN_USE_TABIX_PM is true, which presupposes the package compiled. Both halves — that Perl found the file, and that a package variable is now visible — are Perl run-time plumbing with no Rust counterpart. The feature the module implements is absent from vepyr, but classifying the load probe not-applicable hides nothing: the assertion it guards (n=15) is no-feature and stays in the denominator.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - custom: with a --custom VCF source declared as short_name=test, the first tab line gains the trailing columns test1 and BAR (inside the Bio::DB::HTS::Tabix SKIP block)
rationale: A double gap. The tab writer is absent (n=4), and so is the --custom annotation source that contributes the two trailing columns: `grep -rniE 'custom_annotation|pub custom|CustomAnnotation|short_name' src/` returns 0 hits at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control `pub plugin_cache_root` at vcf_sink.rs:455. vepyr annotates from its parquet cache and, optionally, a pre-built plugin cache; there is no mechanism for attaching an arbitrary tabix-indexed VCF and projecting its INFO fields into output columns. Being inside a SKIP block does not soften the classification — docs/ledger-contract.md keeps such rows in the denominator as no-feature.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - everything: under --everything the first tab line expands to roughly 80 columns byte for byte — HGVSc, CCDS/ENSP/UniProt identifiers, the 1000G and gnomADe frequency block, MAX_AF and MAX_AF_POPS
rationale: The widest rendering assertion in the file, and the only one whose *content* vepyr already implements: `AnnotateVcfConfig::everything` (vcf_sink.rs:383) selects the 80-field vocabulary `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (:556), whose doc comment traces the order to VEP's own Constants.pm L66-138. What is absent is the channel — one tab column per field instead of one pipe-separated CSQ subfield — and the writer that would produce it (n=4). The v115 chr21 cache the line's expected values were derived from is also not in this repository (see n=11), so even a built writer would need a re-derived expectation; the primary blocker remains the missing feature.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - configure fields: `--fields Location,HGVSc` projects the output down to exactly those two columns, in that order
rationale: The row pins output field projection: the caller narrows and orders the column set, and the writer honours it. At dfbf 391f94bd there is no field-selection API of any kind — the sole occurrence of `--fields` in the crate is the doc comment at golden_benchmark.rs:463 describing the *fixed* CSQ order, and `field_selector`/`output_format` return no hits at all (positive control: 19 `vcf_sink` hits). vepyr's CSQ vocabulary is chosen by mode (74 fields, or 80 under --everything) and cannot be narrowed or reordered by a caller, so the projection this row asserts has no observation point. The missing feature is output field selection, which the quarantined port names as `FieldSelector::from_csv` in the commented-out stub at tests/_quarantine/port_output_factory_tab.rs:244.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the VCF output-factory module loads -- require found OutputFactory/VCF.pm, compiled it and ran its import
rationale: RULING R2 (docs/ledger-contract.md) makes every classified `use_ok` row `not-applicable`, unconditionally: `use_ok` asserts that Perl's own loader found the file, compiled it and ran its `import`, and no Rust design performs a module load at runtime that could succeed or fail. The class this one names happens to denote a capability vepyr does have -- VCF with a CSQ INFO field is vepyr's only output format, written by `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` (`vcf_sink.rs:1018` at dfbf 391f94bd) -- but R2 does not turn on what the class denotes, and the writer's behaviour is carried by the 52 rows of this file that exercise it.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config module loads, so the config hash the factory is constructed with can be built
rationale: RULING R2 (docs/ledger-contract.md) makes every classified `use_ok` row `not-applicable`, unconditionally: `use_ok` asserts that Perl's own loader found the file, compiled it and ran its `import`, and no Rust design performs a module load at runtime that could succeed or fail. The subject is Perl's loader, not configuration: vepyr's counterpart config is the plain `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` struct (`vcf_sink.rs:381` at dfbf 391f94bd), whose existence the Rust compiler settles before anything runs.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Runner module loads, so get_runner() below can build a real annotation run
rationale: RULING R2 (docs/ledger-contract.md) makes every classified `use_ok` row `not-applicable`, unconditionally: `use_ok` asserts that Perl's own loader found the file, compiled it and ran its `import`, and no Rust design performs a module load at runtime that could succeed or fail. `Runner` is the wiring `get_runner()` (perl/OutputFactory_VCF.t:736-754) uses to produce a populated InputBuffer for two dozen later rows; what vepyr can and cannot do with that wiring is what those rows say, and this line only says the file parsed.

desc: BASIC TESTS - check class: the object OutputFactory::VCF->new returned is blessed into that class, not into a parent or a factory-chosen sibling
rationale: RULING R1 (docs/ledger-contract.md), second bullet. This file contains no `ok($of = ...->new)` row for R1's first bullet to point at -- `grep -c 'ok('` over the vendored file returns 8, which is the four `use_ok` lines plus the four `ok($x =~ ...)` regex probes at :525, :546, :573 and :590 -- so the readback is decided by denotation. What the class denotes is VCF output with the consequences in a CSQ INFO field, and that is not merely a capability vepyr has, it is vepyr's only output format: `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` (`vcf_sink.rs:1018` at dfbf 391f94bd). Under R1 a readback of a class vepyr has restates a compile-time fact, because a Rust constructor's return type is its class and cannot disagree with itself at runtime. Nothing is dropped from the denominator by this: the construction is not load-bearing here (`OutputFactory::VCF->new` stores a config and a header_info hash; unlike `CacheDir::new` it resolves nothing), and the writer it produces is what the rest of the file asserts.

desc: headers: the complete 6-line default preamble -- ##fileformat, the ##VEP= provenance line, the CSQ INFO line, an ##INFO line for the --custom source, the ##VEP-command-line= record, and the #CHROM column header
rationale: Three of the six elements name capabilities vepyr does not have. (a) `##VEP="v1" API="v1" time="test"` and (b) the `##VEP-command-line='vep ...'` record are provenance headers: at dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rn '##VEP' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/` returns nothing, and `grep -rn 'push_str("##' src/` returns nothing outside a test assertion -- vepyr's output header is whatever noodles carries over from the input plus the single `##INFO=<ID=CSQ,...>` record `vcf_sink.rs:660-679` adds. (c) The `##INFO=<ID=custom_test,...>` line and the `custom_test` name in the Format list come from `--custom file=...,short_name=test`, a tabix-indexed source read during the run; `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455`) has no `custom` member, and vepyr's nearest mechanism, `plugin_cache_root`, is a set of Parquet shards built ahead of the run, not a file queried inside it. Missing features: a provenance header line (n=43 carries it alone) and run-time custom annotation sources (n=31, n=32). The CSQ description divergence this line also carries is counted once, at n=42 and n=52, and not again here.

desc: headers - plugin: loading TestPlugin appends its `test` field to the CSQ Format list and injects a free-form `##test=header` line, while the #CHROM line keeps FORMAT and the HG00096 sample column
rationale: Half of this exists and half does not, and the half that does not is what decides the row. vepyr does append plugin field names to the Format list: `vcf_sink.rs:673-677` walks `plugin_cache::registry::PluginRegistry::field_names(root)` and pushes each name on. What has no counterpart is the other assertion on the same line -- a plugin injecting an arbitrary VCF header record (`##test=header`). At dfbf 391f94bd nothing in the crate emits a `##` line of its own (same grep as n=5), and a vepyr plugin is a Parquet shard plus a manifest (`plugin_cache/registry.rs`) with no hook that could write one. Missing feature: plugin-supplied VCF header records.

desc: headers - BAM_EDIT: --refseq extends the CSQ Format list with REFSEQ_MATCH, REFSEQ_OFFSET, GIVEN_REF, USED_REF and BAM_EDIT, in that order, and drops SOURCE
rationale: vepyr splices exactly those five names, in exactly VEP's order, over the `SOURCE` slot -- `golden_benchmark.rs:721-729` at dfbf 391f94bd, an inclusive `splice(source_idx..=source_idx, ...)`, which is why SOURCE disappears in refseq mode just as it does from VEP's header at perl/OutputFactory_VCF.t:78. Same property, different channel: Perl reads the assembled `##INFO` string off a blessed OutputFactory, and the named test reads the ordered vocabulary off the public `csq_field_names_for_mode(false, true, false)`, because the header string is built by the private `csq_header_description` (`vcf_sink.rs:660`) and only `annotate_to_vcf` can be made to emit it. The test also asserts the five are absent before refseq is on, which is the positive control for the claim. The whole-line equality Perl asserts does not hold -- description prefix and list length both differ -- and that failure is recorded once, at n=42 and n=52, under issue 201.

desc: fields - default: the default CSQ vocabulary is the 21 core field names in a fixed order, plus whatever a --custom source contributes
rationale: vepyr has no `--fields` selector, so the vocabulary is not an accessor on a configured object but a `pub const`: `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (`golden_benchmark.rs:464` at dfbf 391f94bd), 74 names. The named test asserts its first 21 are byte-identical to the 21 Perl lists at :85-105, in the same order. Different channel, same property -- the ordered vocabulary is what fixes the meaning of each `|`-separated position in a CSQ entry, which is the whole reason the Perl pins the list rather than the set. The two lists are not equal: vepyr's carries no `custom_test` (no `--custom`, see n=5) and keeps going for 53 more names. Those two facts are carried by n=11 (no `--fields`) and by n=42/n=52 (issue 201), so this row claims only the prefix it can prove.

desc: fields - flag on: asking for SIFT (sift => 'b') adds a SIFT column to the CSQ vocabulary, appended after the 21 core names
rationale: vepyr has no per-predictor request flag -- `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) carries no `sift`. The same column is switched on by `everything`: `SIFT` is in `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (80 names, `golden_benchmark.rs:556`) and absent from the 74-name default, and the named test asserts both halves, so the property Perl pins -- a SIFT request puts a SIFT column in CSQ, and nothing else does -- is observed through the mode switch rather than the flag. The mode switch is coarser than VEP's knob, which is itself part of the finding: vepyr cannot add SIFT alone, because the everything list differs from the default in more names than that one.

desc: fields - --merged and --custom dont duplicate SOURCE: a merged cache contributes REFSEQ_MATCH, SOURCE and REFSEQ_OFFSET contiguously, and SOURCE appears exactly once even though two features both want it
rationale: vepyr reaches the same no-duplicate result by construction rather than by a guard: `golden_benchmark.rs:711-720` at dfbf 391f94bd splices the merged block over the inclusive range `source_idx..=source_idx`, overwriting the one existing `SOURCE` slot with [REFSEQ_MATCH, SOURCE, REFSEQ_OFFSET, GIVEN_REF, USED_REF, BAM_EDIT], so a duplicate is not possible. The first three of those are VEP's three in VEP's order (perl/OutputFactory_VCF.t:170-172). The named test asserts the count is exactly one and the triple is contiguous. Channel differs: the public vocabulary function instead of the OutputFactory accessor.

desc: fields - user-defined: --fields Allele,Consequence replaces the whole CSQ vocabulary with the two named columns, in the user's order
rationale: `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) has no field-selection member of any kind. The vocabulary at the pin is one of two `pub const` lists chosen by `everything`, with fixed splices for refseq, merged and pick (`golden_benchmark.rs:661-737`); no code path lets a caller narrow it, so there is nothing to port rather than something not yet ported. Missing feature: a user-selected CSQ field subset. This is also the reason n=8 can claim only a prefix.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - empty: an empty field hash still renders one empty field per vocabulary entry (20 bare pipes for 21 fields), so a consumer can index CSQ by position
rationale: What the line pins is fixed record width, and vepyr honours it -- `plugin_cache/csq.rs:50-55` renders n empty fields as `"|".repeat(n)` and `:39-48` states the width invariant in prose -- but the engine's own record is assembled inside `annotate_provider.rs` with no public entry that renders a record from a field map, and nothing public accepts an empty map. The width contract that is public, `csq_field_names_for_mode`, is asserted by tests/port_output_factory_vcf_csq.rs::row8_default_csq_vocabulary_opens_with_veps_21_default_fields; the padding around it is not reachable from this crate. `blocked-api` and not `blocked-data`: an end-to-end run would not produce an empty-hash record either. See issue 203.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk: one populated field renders in its own position and the remaining 20 stay empty, so a value never shifts into a neighbour's slot
rationale: The per-value half is reachable and trivial (`format_scalar(Str("A"))` is `"A"`, `plugin_cache/csq.rs:30-37` at dfbf 391f94bd); the positional half is not, for the same reason as n=12. Naming a test on the escape alone would claim the wrong thing, because what this assertion pins is the padding around the value rather than the value. See issue 203.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - allele revcomped: a negative strand argument reverse-complements the Allele field only, turning A into T while every other field is left alone
rationale: vepyr's CSQ `Allele` is always the forward-strand VCF ALT, and no output path takes a strand argument: neither `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) nor the escaper (`annotate_provider.rs:2274`) carries one. `reverse_complement_allele` does exist at the pin (imported at `annotate_provider.rs:181`, used at `:1929`) but for matching an ALT against a minus-strand cache entry, which is a different job from rendering a column. Missing feature: strand-relative rendering of the CSQ Allele. Kept in the denominator deliberately, even though VEP's own VCF writer never passes a negative strand -- `OutputFactory/VCF.pm:379-382` defaults it to 1 -- because the contract prefers the reading that keeps a row countable.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - "-" erased: a lone hyphen in a non-Allele field is VEP's null sentinel and is written as an empty field, not as a literal -
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay, and the row could NOT have been satisfied by the public mirror the rest of tests/port_output_factory_vcf_csq.rs uses -- which is the whole point of it. vepyr has the same rewrite as the opening statement of csq_escape (if val == "-" { return Cow::Borrowed("") }, annotate_provider.rs:2275-2277), asserted upstream by the in-src test test_csq_escape_dash_becomes_empty (:17234) which an external crate cannot index. Private at the base pin and still private there: re-measured in this checkout as error[E0603]: function `csq_escape` is private, against annotate_provider::cache_lookup_column_names resolving in the same probe file as the positive control. PINS.toml dfbf_test_overlay (aa2be930) delegates it as test_internals::csq_escape. THE MIRROR IS NOT A STAND-IN: plugin_cache/csq.rs:13-14 says the built-in `-'-to-empty convention is deliberately NOT applied to plugin values, so a legitimate `-' is preserved -- a test written on format_scalar would have failed this row while the engine was right, and the test now asserts that divergence (escape("-") == "-" while engine_escape("-") == "") instead of assuming it. analog-port and not unit-port: Perl asserts the whole 21-field chunk and assembling that chunk is inline in annotate_provider.rs with no named renderer to call, which is why n=12 and n=13 stay deferred; what is asserted here is the per-value rule the chunk is made of. The test also pins that only a LONE hyphen is erased ("--" and "A-B" survive) and that the neighbouring rules still fire ("," -> "&", ";" -> "%3B"), so the erasure is one branch of a working escape rather than the function collapsing. SCOPE: csq_escape takes no column argument, so it cannot express the Allele exemption of OutputFactory/VCF.pm:392; that is n=16, which stays deferred and is not claimed here. Mutation-checked: expecting "-" fails with left: "" / right: "-". See issue 203.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - "-" intact for Allele: the Allele column is exempt from the hyphen-is-null rule, because there a - is a real allele (a deletion)
rationale: VEP puts the exemption in the `else` arm of `if($col eq 'Allele')` (`OutputFactory/VCF.pm:392-397`). vepyr's `csq_escape` takes no column argument and applies the rewrite unconditionally (`annotate_provider.rs:2275-2277` at dfbf 391f94bd), so the exemption cannot live there; whether the Allele column is routed through `csq_escape` at all is not decidable from outside the crate, and the public mirror does not apply the rule at all (`plugin_cache/csq.rs:13-14`). Recorded in issue 203 as a possible second output-side discrepancy and deliberately not filed as one: confirming it needs either a column-aware public escaper or an end-to-end run (issue 202).

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - ";" uri encoded: a semicolon inside a CSQ value is written %3B, because a raw one would end the INFO key and split the column
rationale: vepyr percent-encodes the same character: `plugin_cache/csq.rs:20` in the public formatter, `annotate_provider.rs:2287-2289` in the engine's private `csq_escape`, both at dfbf 391f94bd. The channel is the formatter, because `csq_escape` is private and `plugin_cache/csq.rs:10-14` documents `escape_csq_value` as a deliberate mirror of it; the two were compared character class by character class while writing the test and are identical for `,`, `|`, `;` and whitespace, differing only in the `-` rule that n=15 and n=16 carry. Analog and not unit because the function and its call site differ from Perl's `output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk`, whose expected value also carries the 20 trailing pipes of a full record (n=12); the expected value asserted, `%3B`, is Perl's own at :228.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - "|" converted: a pipe inside a CSQ value becomes &, because a raw one would open a new field and shift every later field by one
rationale: Same channel and same mirror argument as n=17: `plugin_cache/csq.rs:19` and the engine twin at `annotate_provider.rs:2283-2286`, both at dfbf 391f94bd. The expected value asserted, `&`, is Perl's own at :234. Of the four substitutions VEP applies (`OutputFactory/VCF.pm:401-404`) this is one of the three vepyr reproduces exactly; the fourth is the whitespace rule that n=20 records as failed.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - "," converted: a comma inside a CSQ value becomes &, because a raw one would end the whole consequence entry and split one transcript's annotation in two
rationale: Same channel and same mirror argument as n=17: `plugin_cache/csq.rs:19` at dfbf 391f94bd, sharing its match arm with the pipe of n=18, and the engine twin at `annotate_provider.rs:2283-2286`. The expected value asserted, `&`, is Perl's own at :240. This is the substitution vepyr's own comment at `annotate_provider.rs:2265-2270` calls out as load-bearing: the cache joins multi-valued sub-fields with `,`, which would otherwise split a CSQ entry.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - whitespace converted: a RUN of whitespace inside a CSQ value collapses to a single underscore, so 'A  G' (two spaces) is written A_G
rationale: vepyr writes `A__G`. VEP collapses the run -- `OutputFactory/VCF.pm:403` is `$data =~ s/\s+/\_/g;`, with a `+` quantifier -- while vepyr substitutes per character, in both the engine escaper (`annotate_provider.rs:2291-2293`) and its public mirror (`plugin_cache/csq.rs:21`), at dfbf 391f94bd. The two-space input was checked byte-wise in the vendored Perl rather than read off the page: `od -c` on :245 shows `A` SP SP `G`, and :246 expects one `_`. `blocked-engine` and not `blocked-data`: the fixture is a string literal, the divergence is in the code. Filed as issue 200. Fails at the current pin; the test's `issue:` line names the tracker.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - '0' kept: a field whose value is the string 0 is emitted as 0, not as an empty field
rationale: The Perl assertion exists because `if(my $data = $hash->{$col})` is false for the string `'0'`, so VEP needs the explicit `elsif` at `OutputFactory/VCF.pm:409-412` to rescue it. That much is Perl plumbing, but what the branch protects is a real output contract -- a zero-valued CSQ field must stay distinguishable from a missing one, which matters for every numeric column (SIFT scores, allele frequencies, distances) -- and vepyr exhibits it: `format_scalar(&PluginScalar::Str("0"))` returns `"0"` (`plugin_cache/csq.rs:30-37` at dfbf 391f94bd). Analog rather than unit because the observation point is the public plugin-value formatter rather than `output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk`, and because Rust has no falsy string to rescue the value from, so the mechanism differs even where the result does not. Kept in the denominator rather than called not-applicable because what is asserted is the output, not the language quirk.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - 0 kept: the numeric twin of the previous row -- a field whose value is the number 0 is emitted as 0
rationale: Same output contract as n=21, reached in Perl through the other half of one `elsif` -- `OutputFactory/VCF.pm:409-412` tests both `ne ''` and `== 0`, so the string and the number take different paths to the same result and upstream pins both. In vepyr they are two variants of one enum, `PluginScalar::Str` and `PluginScalar::I32` (`plugin_cache/lookup.rs:36-41` at dfbf 391f94bd), and `format_scalar` (`plugin_cache/csq.rs:30-37`) renders `I32(0)` as `"0"`. That collapse of two Perl paths into one Rust match is the different channel.

desc: output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk - empty string provided: an explicitly empty value renders as an empty field rather than being dropped, so a two-field record is |0 and not 0
rationale: The named test renders the same two values through vepyr's formatter and joins them with `|` the way a CSQ record is joined, reproducing Perl's expected `|0` (:268) byte for byte. Analog rather than unit because the join is the test's own: vepyr's record assembly is private (n=12, n=13, issue 203) and its public suffix helper `field_suffix` (`plugin_cache/csq.rs:41-48` at dfbf 391f94bd) prefixes each field instead of joining, so it would render `||0`. What the row claims is the property the Perl pins -- empty is a field, not an absence -- and not the record layout, which n=12 carries.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - count: the writer emits exactly one output line per buffered variant, never dropping or duplicating a record
rationale: Analog, not unit: vepyr has no `OutputFactory` and no per-line array to count, so the bijection Perl states between `@lines` and `@{$ib->buffer}` is observed one level down, between the records handed to `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` (`vcf_sink.rs:1018` at dfbf 391f94bd) and the data lines it writes -- and against an Ensembl 115 micro-cache rather than Perl's v84 fixture. The row was `deferred`/`blocked-data` under issue 202 until `tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/` and `tests/data/vep115_reference_slice/` landed (issue 96); the wall was the fixture and nothing else. What makes the count worth asserting is the never-duplicating half, so the test feeds three records whose consequence counts differ by an order of magnitude -- measured 1, 14 and 31 groups -- and asserts three lines: a writer emitting one line per consequence would produce 46. The group counts are asserted too, so the equality cannot pass vacuously on three single-consequence rows.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - check first: the whole first output line for chr21:25585733 C>T -- all eight VCF columns, the FORMAT and sample columns, and three CSQ groups in cache order
rationale: The line cannot be compared as a string, and the reason is already in this ledger: vepyr's CSQ vocabulary is 74 names against VEP's 21 (n=8), and the header those names are declared in is the divergence n=42 and n=52 pin as `failed` under issue 201. So the port asserts the same content through the same written file, per field: the seven fixed VCF columns and the `GT`/`0|0` pair verbatim from Perl's expected string, then each of Perl's three features looked up by `Feature` and checked on the fields the Perl literal carries. Nine of those values are the v84 literal and still hold on the Ensembl 115 micro-cache -- `3_prime_UTR_variant` with cDNA_position 1122, `missense_variant` with 991/331 `A/T` `Gca/Aca`, `upstream_gene_variant` with DISTANCE 2407, STRAND -1 throughout. Two moved with the assembly and are recorded in the test rather than asserted: cDNA_position 1033 -> 997 on ENST00000352957, and BIOTYPE `antisense` -> `lncRNA` on ENST00000567517. `in cache order` is asserted as the relative order of the three among the 14 groups v115 produces. Was `deferred`/`blocked-data` under issue 202 until the micro-cache landed (issue 96).

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - check last: the whole last output line for chr21:25982445 C>T, with ten CSQ groups, two of which carry cds_start_NF and cds_end_NF joined by & in FLAGS
rationale: Same channel and the same reason for analog as n=25, and the distinct content is what n=25 cannot reach: ten features on ONE line, in a fixed order, and a multi-valued FLAGS column spelled with `&`. Both are asserted against the Perl literal -- the ten transcript ids in Perl's order, each with the CDS_position, Protein_position, `V/I` and `Gtt/Att` the Perl expected value gives, `cds_start_NF&cds_end_NF` on ENST00000415997 and `cds_start_NF` on ENST00000448850, and FLAGS empty on the other eight so the two-of-ten claim is itself under test. All twenty position values survived v84 -> v115 unchanged; only ENST00000346798's cDNA_position moved (1157 -> 1273) and that is recorded in the test, not asserted. This is NOT a second claim on n=19's escape rule: n=19 pins a comma INSIDE a value becoming `&`, this pins how a column with several values is joined, and the two fail independently. Was `deferred`/`blocked-data` under issue 202 until the micro-cache landed (issue 96).

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - incomplete VCF entry filled out: a 5-column input record is written back as a complete 8-column VCF line, with . in QUAL and FILTER
rationale: No longer blocked by data: the micro-cache and reference slice are committed (issue 96) and n=24, n=25 and n=26 now run against them. What blocks this row is that vepyr cannot ingest the input the assertion is about. Perl hands VEP an `input_data` string of five fields with no header at all (:317-320) and VEP's own splitter pads it out. vepyr reads through `datafusion_bio_format_vcf`, which refuses every spelling of that record. Measured at the repo pin through `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` over the committed micro-cache, with `21 25585733 rs142513484 C T` as the record: a 5-column `#CHROM` header gives `IO error: invalid header: expected QUAL, got `; a well-formed 8-column header with a 5-field data line gives `Execution error: VCF read error: unexpected EOL`; no header at all gives `IO error: empty input`. Positive control in the same probe: the same record written with all eight columns annotates and writes one line, so the failure is the short record and not the fixture. `blocked-engine` and no longer `blocked-data`: what is missing is a tolerant record splitter in the read path. Not `no-feature` either -- vepyr does perform the operation the row is about, writing `.` into QUAL and FILTER for the eight-column form. One asymmetry with n=51 and with Parser_VCF.ledger.toml n=21, flagged in review and recorded rather than papered over: those two locate their mechanism to file:line, this row only to the crate (`datafusion_bio_format_vcf`). That is probably the floor rather than laziness -- all three messages are raised inside the noodles VCF reader the crate wraps (`invalid header: expected QUAL, got`, `VCF read error: unexpected EOL`, `empty input` are noodles strings, not dfbf ones), so pinning a line would mean pinning a line in a third-party crate that neither PINS.toml nor the ledger tracks. If a tolerant splitter is ever written, the decision point is the crate boundary anyway. Tracked in issue 202.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - invalid character conversion: a transcript id carrying a comma, two spaces, a pipe and a semicolon is escaped in place inside the CSQ payload, with the two spaces becoming ONE underscore
rationale: The record-level twin of n=20, and the same defect. Perl forces the stable_id to `ENST00,00  03|07;301` (:329, two spaces confirmed byte-wise with `od -c`) and expects `ENST00&00_03&07%3B301` (:334); vepyr's escaper produces `ENST00&00__03&07%3B301`. Three of the four substitutions match VEP exactly (n=17, n=18, n=19); the whitespace run does not, because `annotate_provider.rs:2291-2293` maps each whitespace character where `OutputFactory/VCF.pm:403` collapses the run. `blocked-engine`: the divergence is in vepyr's code, not in a fixture -- an end-to-end run would confirm it, not decide it. Filed as issue 200. Fails at the current pin; the test's `issue:` line names the tracker.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - everything: the whole --everything output line for chr21:25585733 across three transcripts, every CSQ field populated including HGVS, frequencies and the gnomADe_AFR max-AF pointer
rationale: The row's content is that `--everything` FILLS THE LINE OUT, so the port asserts both halves: the same record annotated with the flag and without it, populated columns under the flag and empty ones without, with `Consequence` still `missense_variant` in the default run so `empty` is a statement about those columns and not about a run that produced nothing. Analog and not unit for two reasons, one structural and one recorded: vepyr writes 80 `--everything` names against the Perl expected value's own layout (this ledger n=8), and the header those names are declared in is the divergence n=42 and n=52 pin as `failed` under issue 201 -- so the comparison is per field, exactly as this row's earlier rationale predicted it would have to be. Fifteen of the asserted values are the v84 literal and still hold on the Ensembl 115 micro-cache, `ENST00000307301.11:c.*18G>A` and the whole 1000 Genomes block `0.0010|0.003|0.0014|0|0|0` among them. Two moved by a version suffix only (ENST00000352957.8 -> .9, ENSP00000284967.6 -> .7) and are asserted at the v115 spelling. MAX_AF moved outright -- gnomAD v4.1 gives 0.004669 at gnomADg_AFR where v84 gave 0.004643 at gnomADe_AFR -- so it is asserted as the invariant the Perl literal encodes: MAX_AF equals the column MAX_AF_POPS names, and no frequency column exceeds it. Was `deferred`/`blocked-data` under issue 202 until the micro-cache and reference slice landed (issue 96).

desc: custom: the AnnotationSource::File module loads, which is also what makes its CAN_USE_TABIX_PM flag readable by the SKIP guard on the next line
rationale: RULING R2 (docs/ledger-contract.md) makes every classified `use_ok` row `not-applicable`, unconditionally: `use_ok` asserts that Perl's own loader found the file, compiled it and ran its `import`, and no Rust design performs a module load at runtime that could succeed or fail. Its position matters here and does not change the answer: the line sits immediately before the `SKIP` block at :368-406 and exists so `$Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::File::CAN_USE_TABIX_PM` can be read at :372. R2's corollary is explicit that what carries a probe to `no-feature` is the probe's subject being the absent feature, not its position inside a block that guards one; the subject here is Perl's loader. The `--custom` gap the block guards is carried by n=31 and n=32, the two assertions inside it.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - custom: a --custom VCF source with type=exact adds its short_name and its FOO field (test1|BAR) to every CSQ group of an overlapping variant
rationale: `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) has no `custom` member: vepyr cannot read an arbitrary tabix-indexed VCF, BED or GFF during annotation and fold its fields into CSQ. Its nearest mechanism, `plugin_cache_root`, is a set of Parquet shards with a manifest (`plugin_cache/registry.rs`) materialised ahead of the run. CORRECTED 2026-08-31 by a run: that cache IS queried inside the run, per variant and per transcript (`plugin_cache/lookup.rs`, `PluginBufferSlice::probe`), and a user's file really does reach the CSQ payload and the CSQ header — so the sentence that stood here, that it is 'materialised ahead of the run rather than queried inside it', understated what exists. The gap this row names survives the correction intact and is now stated in its measured form: the ingest accepts CSV/TSV/Parquet only (`provider Vcf not wired in prototype`, and the same for Bed, `plugin_cache/provider.rs:111`), and the lookup key is exact — `(start, allele_string[, discriminator])` — so there is no coordinate-matching mode at all, VEP's default `overlap` included. Missing feature: run-time custom annotation sources. Same gap as the `custom_test` half of n=5.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - custom overlap: type=overlap reports every record of the custom source that overlaps the variant (test1&del1&del2), not just an exact coordinate match
rationale: The same missing feature as n=31, plus the matching mode this row names on top of it. VEP's `type=exact` / `type=overlap` distinction decides whether a custom record must start and end on the variant or merely intersect it; at dfbf 391f94bd there is no custom source, so there is no mode to select. Missing feature: overlap-mode matching for run-time custom annotation sources.

desc: test uploaded_allele flag: --uploaded_allele echoes the input's original allele string (CT/CTT) into a CSQ column, beside the VCF-normalised T/TT the line was rewritten to
rationale: Neither the flag nor the column exists at the pin. `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) has no `uploaded_allele`, and enumerating both vocabularies (`golden_benchmark.rs:464` and `:556`) shows no uploaded-allele name in either the 74-field or the 80-field list. Missing feature: echoing the pre-normalisation allele into CSQ. The normalisation itself does happen in vepyr -- what is absent is the audit trail of what the user actually supplied.

desc: non-VCF input: an Ensembl default-format record (21 25585733 25585733 C/T 1) is converted to a VCF line with a synthesised 21_25585733_C/T identifier in the ID column
rationale: vepyr reads VCF and only VCF. Input arrives through `datafusion_bio_format_vcf::table_provider::VcfTableProvider`; there is no reader for VEP's default tab format and no `--format` selector on `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd), so there is no conversion for this row to assert. Missing feature: non-VCF input formats. The gathered port reached the same conclusion at port time and left it as a prose stub (tests/_quarantine/port_output_factory_vcf.rs:1250-1257).

desc: non-VCF input - deletion: an Ensembl-format deletion (C/-) becomes a VCF-legal left-anchored GC>G record, pulling the anchor base from the FASTA and shifting POS back by one

rationale: VEP's rule is two regexes over the INFO column (`OutputFactory/VCF.pm:329-330`). vepyr annotates by DataFusion projection, so an input `CSQ` column and vepyr's own are two columns with one name: the gathered port records that `annotate_to_vcf` returns a `DuplicateQualifiedField` error instead of a VCF (tests/_quarantine/port_output_factory_vcf.rs:613-618, with an observed-behaviour test at :628 asserting `result.is_err()`).
