The fix the port's own doc comment names is projection-time: detect the input `##INFO=<ID=CSQ,...>`, drop that column from the SELECT, then add vepyr's. Tracked in issue 204.

desc: trash existing CSQ 2: the same rule with CSQ first -- CSQ=foo;BAR=blah leaves BAR=blah followed by the new CSQ, so removal does not depend on the key's position
rationale: Same blocker as n=36. The three positional variants exist upstream to pin that the surviving keys keep input order and that the new CSQ is appended rather than substituted in place; vepyr does not reach the question, because the duplicate-column error fires before any INFO key is written. Stub at tests/_quarantine/port_output_factory_vcf.rs:687-700. Tracked in issue 204.

desc: trash existing CSQ 3: the same rule with CSQ last -- BAR=blah;CSQ=foo leaves BAR=blah followed by the new CSQ, which is where the third position closes the case
rationale: Same blocker as n=36 and n=37. Stub at tests/_quarantine/port_output_factory_vcf.rs:702-714. Tracked in issue 204.

desc: keep existing CSQ: with keep_csq set, the input's old CSQ=foo is kept alongside the new one, so the line carries two CSQ keys
rationale: `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) has no `keep_csq` member and vepyr offers no opt-out from replacing the CSQ column. Distinct from n=36 to n=38 on purpose: those are the default rule and are blocked on the engine (issue 204), while this is the knob that suppresses it and is simply absent. Missing feature: a keep-the-input-CSQ flag.

desc: dont trash BCSQ: BCSQ, the bcftools consequence key, is left alone -- only the literal CSQ key is replaced, not every key whose name ends in CSQ
rationale: Analog because the observation point is the written INFO column of `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` rather than an `OutputFactory` return value, and because the record is annotated against the Ensembl 115 micro-cache rather than Perl's v84 fixture -- the assertion itself is Perl's, and its expected INFO `BAR=blah;BCSQ=foo;CSQ=...` comes back in that same order and with those same two values. The test asserts exactly three `;` entries, `BAR=blah` first, `BCSQ=foo` second, vepyr's own `CSQ=` last, and exactly one entry beginning `CSQ=` -- so a suffix match that counted BCSQ as a CSQ key fails on the count as well as on the value. It stays silent about an input key actually named CSQ: that is n=36, n=37 and n=38, which remain deferred/blocked-engine because `annotate_to_vcf` refuses an input declaring its own `##INFO=<ID=CSQ...>`; this row's fixture declares no such header, which is why it is reachable and they are not. Was `deferred`/`blocked-data` under issue 202 until the micro-cache landed (issue 96).

desc: vcf_info_field: with vcf_info_field => 'EFF' the annotation is written under an EFF key and the line carries no CSQ at all
rationale: `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) has no `vcf_info_field` member; the key name is fixed wherever the column is named, including in the header description (`vcf_sink.rs:660-679`). Missing feature: a configurable INFO key for the consequence payload. FALSE FRIEND, recorded 2026-08-31: re-measured at dfbf aa2be930, `vcf_info_field` (SINGULAR, VEP's option) still matches 0 lines and is still not a field of the struct -- probed `error[E0609]: no field vcf_info_field on type AnnotateVcfConfig`, with `c.everything = true` compiling as the positive control in the same file -- but the PLURAL `vcf_info_fields` matches 15 lines. Those are the INFO keys carried over from the INPUT VCF, and `vcf_sink.rs:1213` hard-appends `CSQ` to that list. That line is the positive evidence for this row's claim that the key name is fixed; the near-collision is named here so the next auditor does not read the 15 hits as the option. Worth noting against issue 201: if that knob existed, the header-description question would become a per-run choice rather than a hard-coded string.

desc: headers (all but VEP) - from input test2: header elements 0, 2 and 4 are ##fileformat=VCFv4.1, the ##INFO=<ID=CSQ,...> line with VEP's description and 23-name Format list, and the #CHROM line with the sample column
rationale: The middle element diverged twice at dfbf 391f94bd: the description read `Consequence annotations from annotate_vep. Format: ...` (`vcf_sink.rs:679`) where VEP writes `Consequence annotations from Ensembl VEP. Format: ...` (:541) -- at the current pin (dfbf db54bed4, `vcf_sink.rs:930`) the description half already matches VEP, and `csq_header_description` stays private, so the test cites it and asserts the Format list. And vepyr's Format list is the 74-name `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (`golden_benchmark.rs:464`), whose first 23 names are byte-identical to VEP's and which then continues -- all at dfbf 391f94bd. The description literal itself sits behind the private `csq_header_description` (`vcf_sink.rs:660`), reachable only through `annotate_to_vcf`, so it is cited from source rather than asserted. `blocked-engine`: the divergence is in what vepyr writes, not in a fixture. Filed as issue 201. Fails at the current pin; the test's `issue:` line names the tracker.

desc: headers (VEP header) - from input test2: header element 1 is a ##VEP= provenance line, so a reader can tell which VEP version and which parameters produced the file
rationale: vepyr emits no `##VEP=` line and no provenance header of any kind. At dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rn '##VEP' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src/` returns nothing and `grep -rn 'push_str("##' src/` returns nothing outside a test assertion: the output header is the input's, carried over by noodles, plus the single `##INFO=<ID=CSQ,...>` record `vcf_sink.rs:660-679` adds. The gathered port reached the same conclusion at port time and disabled its own subtest with `#[cfg(any())]` (tests/_quarantine/port_output_factory_vcf.rs:829-841). Missing feature: a provenance header line. Worth recording against issue 201: this is where a tool's own identity belongs, which is precisely why VEP can afford to keep the CSQ description stable for parsers.

desc: no consequences added: a variant whose consequence set is empty is written with a bare . in INFO, not with an empty CSQ= key
rationale: Perl empties the set by hand -- `$ib->buffer->[0]->{transcript_variations} = {}` at :555 -- and vepyr offers no such lever: the set is whatever the engine computed. At a genuinely transcript-free locus vepyr emits an `intergenic_variant` sentinel group rather than an empty INFO, which the gathered port records and asserts (tests/_quarantine/port_output_factory_vcf.rs:864-925, itself fixture-gated). `blocked-engine` and not `blocked-api`: the observation point, the emitted line, is public; what is missing is an input that drives the engine to an empty consequence set. Same shape as issue 78 in Utils.t. Tracked in issue 204.

desc: SV converted to VCF retains END: a structural deletion given in Ensembl format keeps its END=25585735 in the output INFO, placed ahead of the CSQ key
rationale: Two absent features stack here. The input is the Ensembl default tab format vepyr cannot read (n=34), and the record is a structural variant: `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) has no SV handling, and enumerating both CSQ vocabularies (`golden_benchmark.rs:464`, `:556`) finds neither `SVLEN` nor `SVTYPE`. Missing feature: structural-variant input and the END/SVTYPE INFO round-trip that goes with it.

desc: SV overlap percent and length available: with --overlaps the CSQ of an SV carries the overlapped base count and percentage (3|0.01) for each feature it touches
rationale: `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) has no `overlaps` member, and enumerating both CSQ vocabularies (`golden_benchmark.rs:464`, `:556`) finds neither `OverlapBP` nor `OverlapPC`. On top of that the row needs the SV support n=45 already found absent. Missing feature: per-feature overlap statistics in CSQ.

desc: minimal - expanded count: --minimal splits a two-ALT record into two separate variation features before annotation, so the buffer holds 2 where the input held 1
rationale: `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) has no `minimal` member. vepyr annotates each ALT of a multi-allelic record in place and emits one CSQ group per allele; it never splits a record in two and never rejoins one (n=49, n=50). Missing feature: VEP's `--minimal` trim-and-split. Related but distinct is issue 178, which records that vepyr prefix-trims same-length MNVs in a way matching neither VEP's default nor `--minimal` -- that is a discrepancy in the trimming vepyr does do, not in the splitting it does not.

desc: minimal - expanded first allele string: after the split the first expanded record's allele string is the trimmed C/T, not the input's CAGAAGAAAG/TAGAAGAAAG
rationale: The same missing feature as n=47; where that row pins how many records the split yields, this one pins what each of them contains -- the minimal representation after common prefixes and suffixes are removed. Absent for the same reason: no `minimal` member on `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd). The trimming rule itself is where issue 178 sits.

desc: minimal - rejoined count: rejoin_variants_in_InputBuffer collapses the expanded records back to one before output, so the written VCF keeps the input's record count
rationale: There is no split, so there is nothing to rejoin. No member of `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) selects it and no function at the pin corresponds to `rejoin_variants_in_InputBuffer`. Missing feature: the `--minimal` rejoin step, which is what makes the split invisible to the output.

desc: minimal - rejoined allele string: after the rejoin the record carries the original multi-ALT allele string CAGAAGAAAG/TAGAAGAAAG/C, not the trimmed one
rationale: The same missing feature as n=49; this row is the one that shows the rejoin restores the input's own representation rather than leaving the trimmed alleles behind, which is the whole point of the round trip. Absent at the pin for the same reason.

desc: headers - from input 1: the first six output header lines are the input's own ##contig, ##ALT and ##INFO records, verbatim and in input order
rationale: RECLASSIFIED failed -> analog-port on 2026-09-01 by the vepyr 0.4.0 pin bump (issue 578), which is exactly the event the pin was built to detect and which its own assertion message named: `If assembly=GCF_000001405.26 is back, vepyr now round-trips contig attributes: close #367 and reclassify the row`. It is back. Measured, not inferred: the same standalone run the pin always made -- `annotate_to_vcf` over the committed fixtures (issue 96), input header exactly Perl's six records -- now returns all six byte-identical and in Perl's order, `##contig=<ID=21,assembly=GCF_000001405.26,length=46709983>` included, where at the previous pin it returned `##contig=<ID=21,length=46709983>`. The row's `expected` is `verbatim` and six of six is now verbatim. WHAT CHANGED, located: formats 9179628 (#242, `re-emit a source VCF header verbatim`), one of the five commits between formats_base v1.10.0#0d9730c8 and v1.11.0#80f3a6c0. `header_builder.rs:69-84` returns the source header unchanged when `VCF_HEADER_RAW_LINES_KEY` (`bio-format-core/src/metadata.rs:116`) is present and `table_provider.rs:343-359` populates it whenever the reader can capture the source header. The ID+length loop at `header_builder.rs:94-101` still stands behind that; it is simply no longer reached. The previous rationale recorded upstream as having shipped the MECHANISM while leaving UNMEASURED whether the raw-lines metadata survives vepyr's plan into `annotate_to_vcf`; bumping dfbf_master to v0.19.2#3a3fca3f, which pins formats at 80f3a6c0, carried it, and the run answers the question: it does. NOT A WEAKER ASSERTION. The two tests are inverted, not deleted -- what the pin required to be absent is now required to be present, in the same place, so a regression fails where it always did. The second test keeps the four-attribute contig (`assembly`, `md5`, `URL` and a PRIVATE `foo` key) and now requires all four back: the private key is the load-bearing one, because `ContigMetadata` (`bio-format-core/src/metadata.rs:209-218`) held the spec'd attributes unread all along, and only a verbatim re-emission can return a key the struct has no field for. The positive control is unchanged and still separate: the `##ALT` and both `##INFO` records in the same file survive byte-identically, as they did before the bump, so the contig assertions are not passing on a header that was copied wholesale by accident. `analog-port` and not `unit-port` for the same reason as n=53: Perl reads `$of->headers`, vepyr has no headers array, and the analogue is the `#`-prefixed lines of the file `annotate_to_vcf` writes. Issue 367 is closed by the PR that made this change; issue 202, the origin anchor, was already closed. The adjacent silent drop of records on cache-less contigs remains issue 368 and is still not part of this row -- Perl asserts nothing about it.

desc: headers - from input 2: the CSQ INFO header is the third-from-last header line and carries VEP's exact description text and its 23-name Format list
rationale: At dfbf 391f94bd vepyr wrote `Consequence annotations from annotate_vep. Format: ...` (`vcf_sink.rs:679`) where the Perl at :639 expects `Consequence annotations from Ensembl VEP. Format: ...` (matched at the current pin, `vcf_sink.rs:930` at db54bed4), and vepyr's Format list is the 74-name `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (`golden_benchmark.rs:464`) against VEP's 23 -- all at dfbf 391f94bd. Filed as issue 201. Fails at the current pin; the test's `issue:` line names the tracker.

desc: headers - from input 3: the last header line is the #CHROM row, and it keeps the input's FORMAT column and the HG00096 sample
rationale: Perl reads `$of->headers->[-1]`; vepyr has no headers array, so the analogue is the last `#`-prefixed line of the file `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` writes. The expected string needed no re-derivation -- the `#CHROM` line carries no version-dependent content -- and it comes back verbatim, sample column included, so this is the one row in the file whose Perl literal is asserted whole. `->[-1]` is meaningful only if something precedes it, so the test also requires vepyr's own CSQ INFO record to be in the header and NOT after `#CHROM`. The second half of the row, that the sample really survives, is asserted through the data line as well: without a `##FORMAT` record in the input the pin writes a `#CHROM` line still naming FORMAT and HG00096 while every data line stops at eight columns (measured -- deleting the declaration fails the data-line assertion while the header assertion still passes), so a header-only test would have called that a pass. This row does NOT claim the CSQ header line: that is n=52, which stays `failed` under issue 201. Was `deferred`/`blocked-data` under issue 202 until the micro-cache landed (issue 96).

desc: web_output - count lines: with --web_output the writer also emits a sidecar tab file, one line per variant-consequence pair, 132 of them for the test VCF
rationale: vepyr has one output, a VCF. `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-455` at dfbf 391f94bd) has no `web_output` member and there is no second writer at the pin -- `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` is the only public sink. Missing feature: the web sidecar summary file. The gathered port left it as a prose stub (tests/_quarantine/port_output_factory_vcf.rs:1261-1266).

desc: web_output - check last: the sidecar's last line is the 7-column summary for chr21:25982445 -- chrom, start, end, allele string, strand, identifier, most severe consequence
rationale: The same missing sidecar as n=54; where that row pins how many lines it has, this one pins its column layout, which is a second product decision with no counterpart at the pin. Missing feature: the web sidecar summary file and its per-variant column format.

desc: web_output - allele truncation: an over-long allele string is abbreviated in the sidecar to its length plus BP_SEQ (a 100-base T run becomes 100BP_SEQ), so the summary line stays short
rationale: The same missing sidecar as n=54, plus a truncation rule that has no counterpart anywhere at the pin: vepyr's VCF output never abbreviates an allele, because a VCF line has no length budget to protect. Missing feature: the web sidecar summary file and its allele truncation. Stub at tests/_quarantine/port_output_factory_vcf.rs:1267-1272.

desc: RefSeq MT transcripts are returned: MT RefSeq transcripts whose stable ids are bare numbers (4508 through 4576) are not filtered out, and all 19 appear in the CSQ
rationale: UNBLOCKED by #197 (PRs #497-#499), which supplies the ONE artefact with two properties this row's previous rationale named: an MT slice of a RefSeq cache. Both axes are closed — the committed refseq root carries chrMT (its transcript entity whole, 37 rows) and its footers declare bio.vep.cache_source_type = refseq, which is still the only way to set the mode (annotate_to_vcf refuses the config fields, vcf_sink.rs:1035-1039). The Perl INPUT is used verbatim: `MT 12848 rs267606899 C T`. ANALOG on ONE axis, and it is a measured release difference rather than a relaxation: release 84 named MT transcripts by their Entrez gene id, so Perl's expected CSQ reads `Gene=4508 Feature=4508`; release 116 keeps the number as gene_stable_id and names the transcript by gene symbol, so the same rows read `Gene=4508 Feature=ATP6`. The test therefore holds the NINETEEN Gene ids to Perl's own order, verbatim, and carries the 116 Feature beside each. EVERYTHING ELSE MATCHES THE PERL EXACTLY, which is why the assertion is field-by-field and not a count of nineteen: the same nineteen consequences, the same nineteen DISTANCE values (3641, 4276, 4579, 2858, 1899, 2444, 711, 2082, -, 1301, 1826, 2790, 642, 4484, 512, 3108, 2379, 583, 3040), the same three -1 strands, and at 4540 the same `512|512|171|A/V|gCa/gTa`. That last one also settles a doubt this row carried: issue #157 predicted the MT missense would diverge on the codon table, and at this locus it does not — the amino acids and codons are Perl's. ONE FIELD DOES DIVERGE and it is not this row's subject: Perl's groups carry REFSEQ_MATCH=rseq_mrna_nonmatch&rseq_no_comparison and vepyr's are empty, because refseq_match is NULL in every release-116 transcript row measured; that is n=73/74's blocker, tracked in #529 and pinned by tests/port_output_factory_refseq_merged_csq.rs::refseq_match_is_the_one_field_the_release_116_build_cannot_fill so it cannot be rediscovered as a surprise. The `is()` here asserts that the transcripts are RETURNED, and they are.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the OutputFactory::VEP_output module compiles and loads under `use`
rationale: A module-load probe: `use_ok` asserts only that Perl found and compiled modules/Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/OutputFactory/VEP_output.pm at run time, and nothing about what the class does. Rust answers the same question at link time — an item named by a `use` that does not resolve is E0432/E0433 and there is no binary to run — so a run-time assertion would restate the compiler. docs/ledger-contract.md names use_ok/can_ok/isa_ok existence probes as the legitimate not-applicable case. That the module's *feature* is absent from vepyr does not change the reading, and hides nothing: the 16 rows that assert what this factory does are all no-feature and stay in the denominator. Same treatment, same argument, at ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=15 and ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=1.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config module loads under `use`, so line 37 can build the config the factory is handed
rationale: The second of this file's four module-load probes, pure scaffolding: Config is loaded only so `Config->new()` on line 37 can produce the config passed to the VEP_output factory on line 39. Same compile-time-versus-run-time argument as n=1. vepyr's configuration object is the `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` struct (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:381), whose existence a test crate proves by compiling against it; there is no run-time load step that could fail. What Config actually resolves is t/Config.t's subject and is classified in ledger/Config.ledger.toml.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Runner module loads under `use`, so the helper subs at lines 263 and 282 can build annotated buffers
rationale: Third module-load probe. Runner is loaded only for `get_annotated_buffer`/`get_annotated_buffer_runner` (perl/OutputFactory_VEP_output.t:263-299), the fixture rows 10 and 15-18 and 20 depend on. Same compile-time argument as n=1; what the runner does end to end is t/Runner.t's subject and belongs to ledger/Runner.ledger.toml.

desc: check class: `OutputFactory::VEP_output->new({config, header_info})` returns an object blessed into the VEP_output subclass — the writer VEP's default output format selects, not its OutputFactory parent
rationale: Read as a bare blessing probe this would be not-applicable, but what is blessed is the per-format output factory, and format dispatch is exactly the feature vepyr lacks. At dfbf 391f94bd the vep crate has no output-writer type family at all: the only public sink is the free function `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` (vcf_sink.rs:1018 — the one hit of `grep -rnE 'pub (async )?fn annotate_to' src/`), and `grep -rniE 'tab_sink|flat_?tab|to_tsv|output_format|field_selector' src/` returns no hits at all (positive control: 19 hits for `vcf_sink` on the same tree). There is no type whose identity could be read back, because there is no second writer to choose between. docs/ledger-contract.md's RULING on the `ok($obj)` constructor probe settles it: decide by what the class denotes, not by the shape of the assertion, and a class denoting a capability vepyr does not have is `no-feature` — the same call the ruling makes for CacheDir.t n=30. (The SKIP-block convention is not what governs here: this row is not inside a SKIP block.) Identical reading at ledger/OutputFactory_Tab.ledger.toml n=4.

desc: fields: the default set of Extra-column keys is exactly IMPACT, DISTANCE, STRAND, FLAGS — the four VEP always packs into Extra before any option adds more
rationale: What the row pins is the *Extra column's* key set, and vepyr has no Extra column: its CSQ value is positional, declared once in the header as `Format: <names joined by |>` (`csq_header_description`, vcf_sink.rs:660/:679), so every field occupies a fixed slot and no subset is ever 'the keys that get packed'. All four names do exist in vepyr's vocabulary — IMPACT, DISTANCE, STRAND and FLAGS are entries 2, 18, 19 and 20 of the public `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (golden_benchmark.rs:464) — but they sit there unconditionally, alongside the other 70, which is a different structure making a different claim. The missing feature is the fixed-columns-plus-Extra layout.

desc: field_order: the same four keys carry an explicit rank map IMPACT=>0, DISTANCE=>1, STRAND=>2, FLAGS=>3, which is what sorts them inside the Extra column
rationale: Distinct from n=5 and kept as its own row: n=5 pins *which* keys exist, this one pins that each carries a rank, and it is the rank map that decides the order in which n=14 sees `IMPACT=HIGH;Foo=bar` come out. vepyr has no such map at any visibility. Its ordering is baked into the constant vocabularies themselves — `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (74 entries, golden_benchmark.rs:464) and `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (80, :556), selected by `csq_field_names_for_mode` (:653) — so position is a property of the list, not of a per-key integer a caller could read back. There is nothing to observe until a VEP-format writer exists; the missing feature is that writer's Extra-column ordering.

desc: field_order - test add flag: switching on --sift extends the rank map by one entry, SIFT=>4, appended after the four defaults
rationale: The property is incremental: one option is turned on, and the Extra key set grows by exactly one key at the next free rank. vepyr does not work that way and has no `--sift` knob to turn on: `grep -n sift src/vcf_sink.rs` returns 0 hits, so no field of `AnnotateVcfConfig` selects SIFT (positive control — the crate does implement SIFT: `sift` matches in cache_identity.rs, annotate_provider.rs, cache_common.rs and lib.rs, and `sift_decode.rs` is a module of its own). SIFT reaches vepyr's output only as part of the whole `--everything` vocabulary: it is absent from the 74-entry `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` and sits at index 37 of `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (golden_benchmark.rs:556) — a different list wholesale, not a base list plus one appended rank. So there is no incremental extension to observe; the missing feature is per-option Extra-key registration.

desc: --merged and --custom dont duplicate SOURCE header: with both options on, `grep {$_ eq 'SOURCE'} @{$of->fields}` counts exactly 1
rationale: Word for word the assertion at t/OutputFactory_Tab.t:110, and classified identically. What it pins is a *collision* between two independent SOURCE-adding options, and vepyr has only one of the two. `AnnotateVcfConfig::merged` exists (vcf_sink.rs:424) and its merged vocabulary carries SOURCE exactly once — dfbf's own in-src test asserts `merged[29] == "SOURCE"` (golden_benchmark.rs:1352), which no external crate can index. A --custom annotation source does not exist at the pin: `grep -rniE 'custom_annotation|pub custom|CustomAnnotation|short_name' src/` returns 0 hits, positive control `pub plugin_cache_root` at vcf_sink.rs:455. With a single contributor the duplication this assertion guards against cannot arise, so the missing feature is the custom-annotation source. Note what is deliberately NOT claimed: `golden_benchmark::csq_field_names_for_mode(false, false, true)` is public (:653) and a cheap test could assert one SOURCE in merged mode, but that pins a strictly weaker property than the Perl — one adder instead of two — so claiming it as an analogue would overstate coverage.

desc: headers: the default-format preamble is 3 provenance lines, a `## Column descriptions:` block, a separate `## Extra column keys:` block for the packed keys, the `## VEP command-line: vep ...` line, and a `#`-prefixed column header ending in the literal `Extra`
rationale: Five distinct header blocks, and vepyr writes none of them. What it writes instead is a VCF header (`write_header`, vcf_sink.rs:1301/:1322/:1385) whose CSQ INFO description is assembled by the private `csq_header_description` (vcf_sink.rs:660) as `Consequence annotations from annotate_vep. Format: <field names joined by |>`. The split this row pins — real columns described in one block, Extra keys in another — has no counterpart at all, because vepyr has no Extra column to describe, and neither the per-column prose nor a recorded command line appears in any vepyr output (`grep -rniE 'command.?line|cmdline|VEP command' src/` = 0 hits; positive control: the description string itself is found at vcf_sink.rs:679). This is no-feature rather than deferred/blocked-api: making `csq_header_description` public would still emit a VCF INFO line, not this preamble, so the blocker is the absent writer, not the missing `pub`.

desc: headers - plugin: the last two header lines, concatenated, record the `--plugin TestPlugin` command line and end with the literal `Extra` column name
rationale: Two properties, both belonging to the header block: that the invoking command line is written into the output, and that the column header still terminates in `Extra` once a plugin is loaded (the plugin's own key is packed inside Extra rather than given a column, which is what distinguishes this from t/OutputFactory_Tab.t:121, where the same regex ends in the plugin's column name). vepyr records no command line in any output at the pin, and has no header of this shape at all (n=9). Its plugin mechanism does exist and does append plugin field names to the output vocabulary — `AnnotateVcfConfig::plugin_cache_root` (vcf_sink.rs:455) and the `PluginRegistry::field_names(root)` loop in `csq_header_description` (vcf_sink.rs:672-678) — but it appends them to the pipe-joined CSQ Format list, and it consumes a pre-built plugin cache rather than loading a Perl plugin module named on `--plugin`. Neither half of the assertion has a vepyr observation point.

desc: output_hash_to_line - empty: an empty output hash renders as 14 columns — the `-` sentinel 13 times over the fixed columns and once more for an Extra column with nothing to pack
rationale: The assertion pins the row formatter and its empty-value sentinel. vepyr has no row formatter for this format, and no `-` sentinel either: an unset CSQ subfield is the empty string between two pipes, which dfbf's own test states for SOURCE and REFSEQ_MATCH (`assert_eq!(merged_values[merged_index("SOURCE")], "")`, annotate_provider.rs:16487). Nothing here is private: the 13 textual matches for `output_hash|hash_to_line|format_row` in the crate are all doc-comment traceability pointers to VEP's Perl methods — including `output_hash_to_vcf_info_chunk()` at annotate_provider.rs:2258, the *VCF* renderer, never this file's `output_hash_to_line` — and not one is a Rust fn. An absent operation is no-feature, not deferred/blocked-api.

desc: output_hash_to_line - test 0: the falsy id 0 survives into column 1 as `0` rather than collapsing to the `-` sentinel, while the other 13 columns stay `-`
rationale: A boundary the empty-hash row (n=11) cannot reach: it pins that the formatter tests *definedness*, not truthiness, which in Perl is a real hazard because `0` is false. Same absent formatter as n=11, so the same product statement — but the row is kept separate rather than folded in, because a writer could pass n=11 and still fail this one. It is not not-applicable: what it pins is an output-rendering rule of a writer, not Perl object plumbing. When a VEP-format writer is built for vepyr, Rust's `Option<String>` carries the same distinction in the type, so the row becomes portable rather than moot.

desc: output_hash_to_line - test extra 1: a key the writer never declared (Foo => 'bar') still reaches the output, packed into the Extra column as `Foo=bar`, while the declared Existing_variation fills its own fixed column
rationale: This is the Extra column's whole reason to exist: the format is open — any key in the output hash appears as `KEY=VALUE` — while the 13 fixed columns are closed. vepyr's CSQ is closed at both ends. Its value is positional against a vocabulary fixed at header time (`Format: <names joined by |>`, vcf_sink.rs:679), chosen from `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` / `CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` by `csq_field_names_for_mode` (golden_benchmark.rs:653), so a value with no declared field has nowhere to go and no key name to travel under. The only extension point is the plugin cache, whose fields are appended to the *declared* Format list before any row is written (vcf_sink.rs:672-678) — the opposite of an undeclared key surfacing per row. The missing feature is the open Extra column.

desc: output_hash_to_line - test extra 2: inside Extra, declared keys sort before undeclared ones by field_order rank and the pairs are joined with `;` — `IMPACT=HIGH;Foo=bar`, not `Foo=bar;IMPACT=HIGH`
rationale: The row that makes n=6's rank map observable, and the strongest ordering claim in the file: with one declared key and one unknown key present, the declared one comes first and `;` separates them. vepyr has neither half. Ordering there is positional and total — every field, declared or plugin-supplied, occupies its slot in the Format list — and the separator between the members of a CSQ value list is `,` at record level and `&` inside a subfield, never `;`, which VCF reserves for INFO keys; ledger/Utils.ledger.toml rows 7-9 pin those two separators through vepyr's own parser, `golden_benchmark::extract_csq_term_set` (golden_benchmark.rs:323). So neither the rank comparison nor the `;` join has an observation point until a VEP-format writer exists.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - count: the annotated test_vcf buffer renders 744 lines, one per variant x feature x allele, under show_ref_allele + uploaded_allele
rationale: Word for word the assertion at t/OutputFactory_Tab.t:151, and classified identically. The per-VFOA fan-out is a property vepyr does have — it emits one CSQ record per variant/feature/allele — but this assertion counts *lines emitted by the VEP-format writer*, which does not exist (n=4); the CSQ-record count is observed in ledger/OutputFactory.ledger.toml and ledger/OutputFactory_VCF.ledger.toml, which own that channel. Two of the three inputs are missing as well: `show_ref_allele` and `uploaded_allele` return 0 hits over the whole crate (positive control: `pub everything`/`pub refseq`/`pub merged` at vcf_sink.rs:383/:422/:424), and the fixture is VEP's chr21 test cache, which this repository does not carry (audit/vepyr-master/per-port.md §"the three notes": 13 call sites of `workspace_path("vep-benchmark/data/port/_cache115/...")`). The primary blocker is the absent writer, so the row is no-feature rather than deferred/blocked-data.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - check first: the first line byte for byte — 13 fixed columns for rs142513484 at 21:25585733 plus the Extra column REF_ALLELE=C;UPLOADED_ALLELE=C/T;IMPACT=MODIFIER;STRAND=-1
rationale: The row pins the writer's whole per-row rendering at once: the 13 fixed columns with `-` in every unfilled one, and an Extra column in which the two allele keys added by --show_ref_allele/--uploaded_allele precede the declared IMPACT and STRAND. vepyr has neither the writer (n=4) nor those two options (`grep -rn 'show_ref_allele\|uploaded_allele' src/` = 0 hits at the pin; positive control as in n=15) — and note that REF_ALLELE and UPLOADED_ALLELE are not in either public CSQ vocabulary, so they are absent as *fields*, not merely unrendered (`grep -rn 'REF_ALLELE\|UPLOADED_ALLELE' src/` = 0 hits; positive control `"MAX_AF_POPS"` at golden_benchmark.rs:536 and :628). The annotation values the line carries — the consequence term, cDNA position 1122, IMPACT, STRAND -1 — are quantities vepyr does compute and are asserted through the CSQ channel in ledger/OutputFactory.ledger.toml; what this row would add is the VEP-format rendering.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - check last: the last line byte for byte — a missense on ENST00000448850 with Amino_acids V/I and Codons Gtt/Att in fixed columns, and FLAGS=cds_start_NF appended last inside Extra
rationale: The same absent writer and the same two absent options as n=16, on the other end of the buffer; the row is distinct because it is the only one in the file where a fourth declared key (FLAGS) is populated and where the coding-position columns are filled (CDS 832, protein 278) — so it is what pins that FLAGS sorts last among the declared keys. Worth recording precisely because the *values* are within vepyr's reach: FLAGS is CSQ field 20 of `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES` (golden_benchmark.rs:464; the crate's own test pins the neighbours, STRAND at 19 on :1299 and SOURCE at 28 on :1300), so what is missing is only the rendering — which is why this is no-feature and not blocked-engine.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - everything: under --everything the Extra column alone expands to exactly 33 KEY=VALUE pairs byte for byte — VARIANT_CLASS through HGVSc, the 1000G and gnomADe frequency block, MAX_AF and MAX_AF_POPS=gnomADe_AFR
rationale: The widest rendering assertion in the file, and the one whose *content* vepyr already implements: `AnnotateVcfConfig::everything` (vcf_sink.rs:383) selects the 80-field vocabulary `golden_benchmark::CSQ_FIELD_NAMES_EVERYTHING` (:556), whose doc comment traces the order to VEP's own Constants.pm L66-138 and whose naming matches this very line — the Perl expects `gnomADe_AFR_AF=0.004643`, and the everything list spells that population `gnomADe_AFR_AF` where the 74-field list spells it `gnomADe_AFR` (measured over both constants). What is absent is the channel: `KEY=VALUE;` pairs in an Extra column instead of positional pipe-separated values, and the writer that would produce them (n=4). The v115 chr21 cache the expected values came from is not in this repository either (see n=15), so even a built writer would need a re-derived expectation; the primary blocker remains the missing feature.

desc: custom: the AnnotationSource::File module loads under `use` — which is also what makes its $CAN_USE_TABIX_PM package variable readable by the SKIP guard on line 232
rationale: The fourth module-load probe, doing the same double duty as ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=15 on the identical module: line 232 skips the assertion that follows unless $Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::AnnotationSource::File::CAN_USE_TABIX_PM is true, which presupposes the package compiled. Both halves — that Perl found the file, and that a package variable is now visible — are Perl run-time plumbing with no Rust counterpart. The feature the module implements is absent from vepyr, but classifying the load probe not-applicable hides nothing: the assertion it guards (n=20) is no-feature and stays in the denominator.

desc: get_all_lines_by_InputBuffer - custom: with a --custom VCF source declared as short_name=test, the Extra column gains three keys from it — test=test1, test_FILTER=PASS and test_FOO=BAR (inside the Bio::DB::HTS::Tabix SKIP block)
rationale: A double gap, and the row that shows why the Extra column and the custom source are separate features: the source contributes three keys whose names are derived at run time from the `short_name` (`test`, `test_FILTER`, `test_FOO`), which only an open key=value column can carry. vepyr has neither. The --custom source does not exist at dfbf 391f94bd — `grep -rniE 'custom_annotation|pub custom|CustomAnnotation|short_name' src/` returns 0 hits, positive control `pub plugin_cache_root` at vcf_sink.rs:455 — and the Format list is closed before the first row is written (n=13), so run-time-named fields have nowhere to appear. Being inside a SKIP block does not soften the classification: docs/ledger-contract.md keeps such rows in the denominator as no-feature.

desc: use test: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser base class loads under `use` -- the format dispatcher and per-variant validation pass this whole file is about
rationale: RULING R2 in docs/ledger-contract.md: a `use_ok` row is not-applicable unconditionally, whatever the class denotes. The reason is not the usual one, that the compiler already carries the fact -- for a format dispatcher vepyr does not have there is no symbol to carry -- but that no Rust design performs a runtime module load that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design. The absence is not lost: it is carried by the rows that EXERCISE the missing machinery, and this file has 95 of them, so counting the module-load line as well would count the same gap twice and inflate exactly the ledger where it is already most visible.

desc: new is defined: `Parser->new({file => test_vcf})` returns a defined object, so the base class resolved and opened the input path it was handed
rationale: Third arm of the `ok($obj)` constructor RULING in docs/ledger-contract.md: the class denotes a capability vepyr HAS, under a different type, so the row is an analog-port naming the test that constructs the vepyr equivalent and asserts Ok. The line is load-bearing rather than Perl plumbing, and the Perl says why: `Parser::new` calls `$self->file($hashref->{file})` (Parser.pm:133) and `sub file` throws `ERROR: File "$file" does not exist` unless `-e $file` (Parser.pm:239), so a defined `$p` is evidence that path resolution SUCCEEDED. That is the same shape as ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=4, where `CacheDir::new` resolves a directory through `init` and the row is an analog-port for the constructor that consumes it. vepyr counterpart: `VcfTableProvider::new` over a file that exists returns Ok, and the named test also reads the row back through SQL so the assertion is about THIS path and not about a constructor that accepts anything. An earlier draft booked the row not-applicable, arguing that n=7's test already carries the success arm as its positive control. That reading fails the contract's own test for a shared claim -- could this test fail if only the other row's behaviour regressed? `port_parser_subtest_07_nonexistent_path_errors` fails only if the MISSING path stops erroring, so it never witnessed the success arm as a claim; a positive control inside another row's test is a guard against vacuity, not coverage. The two-line sibling test is the fix. old-repo issue #120 remains the sweep that will settle the constructor-probe family corpus-wide.

desc: check class: the object `Parser->new` returned with no `format` and no config is blessed into the base class itself rather than into one of the seven format subclasses
rationale: RULING R1, first arm, in docs/ledger-contract.md: the construction already carries its own row -- n=2, two lines up -- so all this line adds is Perl object identity, which is on the not-applicable list. The first arm is only usable because n=2 is now an `analog-port` that names a test: R1 asks whether the construction is ACCOUNTED FOR, and while n=2 was itself not-applicable the pair removed a real construction from the denominator between them, which is the trap R1's closing paragraph warns about. With n=2 in the denominator the readback adds nothing but the blessing, and R1's second arm agrees independently -- the class denotes a capability vepyr has, so a Rust constructor's return TYPE cannot disagree with itself at runtime. Its content is the negative of rows n=97 and n=99, where a `format` IS supplied or sniffed and the factory does pick a subclass; that dispatch is the missing feature and both those rows are `no-feature`, so nothing about it rides on this row.

desc: need config object to use new with format: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config module loads under `use`, so a config carrying `fasta` and `offline => 1` can be built for the subtests below
rationale: RULING R2 (`use_ok` is not-applicable unconditionally, docs/ledger-contract.md), and not-applicable under the older denotation reading too, since vepyr's option containers do exist and the linker already resolves them -- `EnsemblCacheOptions` in datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache at v1.10.0 (0d9730c8) and `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` at dfbf 391f94bd. The corpus is consistent about this exact row: every already-classified `use_ok Config` row is not-applicable (AnnotationSource, AnnotationSourceAdaptor, AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat, AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix, BaseVEP, CacheDir, Config, InputBuffer, Parser_HGVS n=2, Parser_SPDI n=2, Parser_CAID n=2).

desc: file: the `file` accessor reads back the input path the parser was constructed with
rationale: Ported through the test-internals overlay on the FORMATS crate, and the row's own reason for staying deferred is what the overlay answered. VcfTableProvider has always stored the path it was opened with -- file_path: String at datafusion-bio-format-vcf v1.10.0 (0d9730c8) table_provider.rs:495 -- and handed it back through none of its eight public constructors. What was missing was a STABLE read-back, not every read-back: the struct is #[derive(Clone, Debug)] (:492), so format!("{provider:?}") really does print the path, and this row stayed deferred rather than claiming that channel because a derived Debug rendering is not an API contract -- a field rename or a hand-written Debug impl would silently empty a row that claimed coverage through it. PINS.toml formats_test_overlay (8fd75f30) adds the stable accessor instead, pub fn file_path(&self) -> &str at table_provider.rs:1782, one field read behind cfg(feature = "test-internals"). analog-port and not unit-port: Perl's $p is a parser object and vepyr's is a DataFusion TableProvider, so the property survives at a different boundary from the one the Perl names. Two independent providers are opened over two tempdir VCFs and each must report its own path, so the assertion cannot be satisfied by a constant or by an accessor returning whichever file was opened last. SCOPE unchanged: Perl's file() is dual-purpose -- it also OPENS the path, which is why n=7 can assert a die and n=2 the success arm -- and this row is the getter half only; neither of those is re-claimed. The row's twin n=10 (bcf_header) is deliberately NOT carried across: the overlay exposes that accessor too, but the field is populated only for VcfInputFormat::Bcf (:1092-1095) and is None for VCF input, so exposure demonstrates a divergence rather than closing the row -- measured beside n=5's own value in the same test, where bcf_header() is None. Mutation-checked: comparing the second provider against the first path fails with two providers must not report the same path. old-repo issue #175.

desc: file STDIN: the literal string `stdin` selects *main::STDIN as the input handle, so a VEP run can sit in the middle of a shell pipe
rationale: Absent feature: STDIN input. vepyr's inputs are paths, and only paths -- `annotate_to_vcf` opens `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, None, None, None, false)` (vcf_sink.rs:1074 at dfbf 391f94bd) and the Python surface's first positional parameter is a filename, `annotate(vcf: str, cache_dir: str, *, ...)` (vepyr 346b9173 src/vepyr/__init__.py:694). Measured: `grep -rni 'stdin' src/` over datafusion/bio-function-vep returns 0 lines, against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines as the positive control. This is not a small addition either: a DataFusion TableProvider is built around a path or object-store URI that the planner may re-open once per partition, and a non-seekable handle cannot be re-opened. Row n=96, where detecting a format from STDIN throws, is the same absence one level up.

desc: file not exists: `$p->file('foo')` dies with /File.+does not exist/, so a parser refuses a path it cannot open instead of quietly yielding an empty variant stream
rationale: vepyr has no `file()` accessor that opens as a side effect. The equivalent moment is `VcfTableProvider::new` (datafusion-bio-format-vcf v1.10.0 = `0d9730c8`, `table_provider.rs:752`), which resolves the path and probes its compression eagerly, so the same refusal happens at the same point in the pipeline; Perl's `die` becomes a typed `DataFusionError`. Measured at the pin: the call returns `Err` whose message is `IO error: NotFound (permanent) at  => cannot open <path> to detect its compression, source: No such file or directory (os error 2)`, and the named test asserts both `NotFound` and the filename, with a positive control constructing over a file that does exist. NOTE for reviewers: the gathered port asserted a PANIC here and wrapped the call in `catch_unwind` so it would pass either way, citing an unwrap at `object_storage.rs:183`. That comment is stale at this pin -- the parked-test finding on #120 is the same observation -- and the promoted test drops the `catch_unwind`.

desc: line_number get: a parser that has read nothing reports line 0
rationale: Absent feature: an input line counter. Perl keeps one so a rejection can say WHICH input line was rejected -- `Parser::VCF::create_VariationFeatures` increments it once per record and every `skipped_variant_msg` quotes it. vepyr has neither half. Measured at dfbf 391f94bd: `grep -rnE 'line_number|line_no' src/` returns 0 lines, against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines; and there is no warning sink for a number to be quoted to, which is the same absence rows n=43-56 are about. vepyr's unit of work is an Arrow RecordBatch handed over by DataFusion, which carries no source line at all, and a row dropped by a contig partition filter is never counted in the first place.

desc: headers: the base class's `headers` is a hard-coded empty arrayref -- `sub headers { return []; }` at Parser.pm:208-210, documented there as "Just a stub here" -- so the accessor every format subclass overrides answers [] on the base class itself
rationale: Reclassified from no-feature after the absence claim failed a probe one crate over. What the row pins is the getter shape -- a parser exposes its input's header lines as a list -- and vepyr's stack does build exactly that list: `pub fn build_vcf_header_lines(schema, info_fields, format_fields, sample_names) -> Result<Vec<String>>` at datafusion-bio-format-vcf v1.10.0 (0d9730c8) header_builder.rs:59, plus `pub async fn get_header(file_path, object_storage_options) -> Result<vcf::Header>` at storage.rs:278, which is what `VcfTableProvider` itself calls at construction (table_provider.rs:108). The earlier rationale measured `grep -rniE 'header_lines|raw_header|meta_lines' src/` -> 0 lines against `grep -rni 'header' src/` -> 51 inside dfbf's vep package and read that as absence; the measurement is correct and the inference was not, because the package it greps is not where a VCF data structure would live. What is genuinely unreachable is a read-back ON THE CONSTRUCTED PROVIDER: `VcfTableProvider` keeps only the derived pieces -- `schema`, `sample_names`, `source_sample_names`, `contig_names` (table_provider.rs:493-513) -- and exposes no accessor for the header it parsed, so the row waits on an export, not on a feature. Same shape and same issue as n=5. The two live pub functions are not a substitute: `get_header` re-reads the file from a path the caller must already have, and `build_vcf_header_lines` RECONSTRUCTS lines from an Arrow schema rather than returning what was read, so neither is the parser reading back its own state. old-repo issue #175.

desc: detect_format - VCF: sniffing a plain uncompressed VCF returns the format name `vcf`
rationale: Absent feature: input-format detection. vepyr has no detector because it has nothing to detect between -- VCF is the only input format it reads. Measured at dfbf 391f94bd: `grep -rnE 'detect_format|input_format' src/` returns 0 lines, against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines; and the DataFusion option vocabulary is closed at 31 keys (`grep -oh 'parse("[a-z_0-9]*")' src/*.rs | sort -u | wc -l` -> 31), none of which selects a format. This is one of 21 rows in this file that assert what `detect_format` returns (n=11, 13, 72-74, 76-92, 94). Contrast n=75, which also asserts `detect_format == vcf` and IS an analog-port: there the variable under test is the CRLF line ending and the detector is only the probe Perl has to hand, so the property survives a change of observation point. Here the detector itself is the subject.

desc: gzipped VCF: `$p->file($test_gzvcf)` returns a GLOB rather than a path, i.e. a gzip-compressed VCF is opened transparently instead of being rejected or read as bytes
rationale: Perl's evidence that gzip was handled is the SHAPE of the return value -- a filehandle GLOB instead of the path string that row n=5 gets back -- and a Perl filehandle has no counterpart in vepyr, whose reader hands out no handle to inspect. The property under test survives the translation: a gzip stream is decompressed transparently, with no flag and no separate API. desc: delimiter - set: assigning a tab makes it the field separator the parser splits input lines on, and the assignment returns it
rationale: Absent feature: a configurable input field separator. It exists in VEP because the base class serves formats with different column layouts -- `Parser::VEP_input` splits on runs of whitespace, which row n=81 asserts directly, while VCF splits on single tabs -- and vepyr has exactly one input format, whose separator the VCF specification fixes. Measured at dfbf 391f94bd: the only `delimiter` in the crate is `SourceManifest.delimiter` (plugin_cache/source_manifest.rs:51), consumed at plugin_cache/provider.rs:82-94 to configure a CSV reader for PLUGIN data files; it never touches variant input. `grep -rniE 'separator' src/` returns only CSQ-escaping and AF-bundle prose (annotate_provider.rs:2262, :3346, :6124; cache/af_bundle.rs:73-102).

desc: delimiter - get: the field separator reads back as the tab that was set

desc: valid_chromosomes empty: a parser built without a chromosome list has an empty valid set, so nothing has been ruled out yet
rationale: Absent feature: a parser-level, caller-supplied valid-contig slot that exists before it is populated. `Parser::new` sets `valid_chromosomes({map {$_ => 1} @{$hashref->{valid_chromosomes} || []}})` unconditionally (Parser.pm:139), so `{}` is the state of a real accessor on a real object when the caller passed nothing; the row pins that the slot exists and starts empty. vepyr has no such slot at any visibility. desc: minimal: `minimise_alleles` reduces GA/GT to a VariationFeature with allele_string A/T, start 2 (from 1), end 1, minimised 1 and original_allele_string GA/GT

desc: minimal - trim both ends: `minimise_alleles` reduces GAC/GTC to A/T, i.e. it trims the shared suffix as well as the shared prefix
rationale: vepyr's input path calls `vcf_to_vep_allele` (dfbf 391f94bd allele.rs:296) for every row (annotate_provider.rs:5719, under the comment `VEP-style allele minimization`) and its result becomes the CSQ Allele field at :6515, so this is production behaviour and publicly observable. The input path simply does not call it. rationale: Absent feature: identifier synthesis for unnamed input variants. rationale: Absent feature: the per-run chromosome allow-list (VEP's `--chr`). Perl's `validate_vf` tests `$self->{chr}` before anything else, so a run can be restricted without touching the input file. vepyr has no such option: the DataFusion option vocabulary is closed at 31 keys (`grep -oh 'parse("[a-z_0-9]*")' src/*.rs | sort -u | wc -l` -> 31 at dfbf 391f94bd) and none of them is `chr`. An ordinary SQL predicate a caller writes for themselves is not a property of the parser this row is about, and it is applied by the query, not by the validation pass.

rationale: Reclassified from no-feature in review, on measurement. rationale: Absent feature: the per-variant input-validation pass, and the per-variant warning sink it reports through. A malformed row either fails the whole DataFusion scan or is annotated as written; nothing is dropped WITH AN EXPLANATION. That silence is the gap these rows measure, which is why the message-matching rows are counted separately from the return-value rows rather than folded into them.

desc: use string fed to FH as input data: a filehandle over an in-memory scalar is accepted as the parser's input, so variants need not come from a file on disk
rationale: Absent feature: reading variants from an already-open handle rather than from a path. Perl opens a scalar as a filehandle and passes the glob straight to `file()`, which is the same mechanism row n=6 uses for STDIN. vepyr's inputs are paths only -- `annotate_to_vcf` calls `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, ...)` (vcf_sink.rs:1074 at dfbf 391f94bd) and `grep -rni 'stdin' src/` returns 0 lines, against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines. The obstacle is structural rather than an omission: a DataFusion TableProvider is built around a path or object-store URI the planner may re-open once per partition, and a handle cannot be re-opened.

desc: FH position reset: after detect_format has read the handle to sniff it, the read position is rewound, so the first data line is not consumed by the sniffing
rationale: Absent feature: reading variants from an already-open handle rather than from a path. Perl opens a scalar as a filehandle and passes the glob straight to `file()`, which is the same mechanism row n=6 uses for STDIN. vepyr's inputs are paths only -- `annotate_to_vcf` calls `VcfTableProvider::new(vcf_path, ...)` (vcf_sink.rs:1074 at dfbf 391f94bd) and `grep -rni 'stdin' src/` returns 0 lines, against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines. desc: fail detect format from STDIN: detecting a format from STDIN dies with /Cannot detect format from STDIN/, because a pipe cannot be rewound and sniffing would eat the first variant
rationale: The refusal that row n=95's rewind makes unnecessary for a seekable handle, and it is a precondition between two features vepyr has neither of: STDIN input (row n=6, `grep -rni 'stdin' src/` -> 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines) and format detection (rows n=11, 76-92). Compare ledger/Parser_HGVS.ledger.toml n=3, the same shape: a `dies` assertion about the interaction of two absent capabilities is `no-feature`, not `not-applicable`, because what is missing is the product, not the Perl artefact.

desc: new with explicit format: `Parser->new({format => 'vcf', ...})` returns an object blessed into Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF, so the factory turned the format STRING into a subclass and dispatched to it
rationale: Absent feature: factory dispatch on a caller-supplied input-format name. This row was `not-applicable` in an earlier draft, under RULING R1's second arm -- the class denotes a capability vepyr HAS, so the readback restates a compile-time fact. That reading swallows the row's content. What the line asserts is not that a VCF parser exists; it is that passing `format => 'vcf'` MADE the factory produce one, i.e. that the string was mapped through `%FORMAT_MAP` (Parser.pm:88-96) and dispatched at :158-159. R1's second arm also presupposes a Rust constructor whose return type could carry the fact, and there is none: `VcfTableProvider::new` takes no format argument, so nothing in vepyr expresses `format = vcf` at all. Read instead through docs/ledger-contract.md's corollary -- a probe is carried to `no-feature` when the probe's SUBJECT is the absent feature -- the class here is the factory's OUTPUT, exactly as it is in n=99, and the factory is the missing thing. The dispatch happy path is counted nowhere else, which is the concrete cost of the earlier verdict: n=98 asserts that an UNKNOWN format name is refused and n=99 that a format can be SNIFFED when none is given, and a factory that ignored its `format` argument entirely and always returned VCF would satisfy both of them. Only this row fails against such a factory. Measured at dfbf 391f94bd: `grep -rnE 'detect_format|input_format' src/` -> 0 lines against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines; the DataFusion option vocabulary is closed at 31 keys (`grep -oh 'parse("[a-z_0-9]*")' src/*.rs | sort -u | wc -l` -> 31) and names no input format; `AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) has 34 public fields and names none either. The row stays distinct from ledger/Parser_SPDI.ledger.toml n=4 and ledger/Parser_CAID.ledger.toml n=4, which are `no-feature` for the simpler reason that the class denotes a format vepyr cannot read; here the format IS readable and the DISPATCH is what is missing.

desc: new with unknown format: `Parser->new({format => 'foo'})` dies with /Unknown or unsupported input format/, so the factory has a closed vocabulary and refuses anything outside it
rationale: Absent feature: the input-format parameter, and with it any vocabulary to refuse a value outside. vepyr has no format selector to reject `foo` with: the DataFusion option vocabulary is closed at 31 keys (`grep -oh 'parse("[a-z_0-9]*")' src/*.rs | sort -u | wc -l` -> 31 at dfbf 391f94bd) and none of them is a format, while `AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) has 34 public fields and names no input format either. Worth keeping in the denominator rather than reading as Perl plumbing: a closed vocabulary that FAILS LOUDLY on an unknown value is a product property, and vepyr does have the shape elsewhere -- `AnnotationBackend::parse` refuses a backend outside its enum (ledger/vepyr-only.ledger.toml `lance-01`) -- so this is an absence in one place, not an idiom that cannot exist.

desc: new with format detection: `Parser->new({format => 'guess'})` sniffs the input and returns a Parser::VCF, so the factory can pick a subclass with no help from the user
rationale: Absent feature: format auto-detection wired into the factory -- the detector of rows n=11 and n=76-92, here at the moment it chooses a class. The blessing readback is not not-applicable here, and the reason is docs/ledger-contract.md's corollary: a probe is carried to `no-feature` when the probe's SUBJECT is the absent thing, and the class this line reads back is the OUTPUT of the detection rather than a restatement of anything the caller had in hand. An earlier draft used this row to contrast with n=97, arguing that there the class merely restates an argument the caller supplied; n=97 is now `no-feature` too, on the ground that turning the string `vcf` into a class is itself the dispatch and is itself absent. The two rows are still distinct, and the distinction is where the format name comes from: n=97 measures dispatch on a name the caller gave, this row measures dispatch on a name vepyr would have had to infer. Measured at dfbf 391f94bd: `grep -rnE 'detect_format|input_format' src/` returns 0 lines, against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516 lines.

desc: DB - validate_vf - successful transform insertion 1: an insertion on the contig AP000235.3 passes validation, because the database can place that contig on a chromosome
rationale: Absent feature: VEP's database mode. Every assertion from n=100 to n=113 sits inside `SKIP: { ... skip 'No local database configured', 11 unless $can_use_db }` (perl/Parser.t:351) and needs a live Ensembl core database through `Bio::EnsEMBL::Test::MultiTestDB`. vepyr is offline-cache-only by design: measured at dfbf 391f94bd, `grep -rniE 'mysql|dbi:|db_adaptor|slice_adaptor' src/` returns 0 lines against `grep -rn 'parquet' src/` -> 662 lines. docs/ledger-contract.md names cache-only as the standing `no-feature` example, and the SKIP-block convention keeps these rows in the denominator rather than letting a shape probe drop out of it. (Housekeeping: the declared skip count of 11 is short of the 14 assertions the block actually holds -- recorded upstream as old-repo issue #172, inert under `done_testing()`.) This row is about the contig-to-toplevel TRANSFORM specifically: the input names a sequence region (AP000235.3) that is not a chromosome, and the database maps it onto chromosome 21 with shifted coordinates. vepyr has no projection machinery of any kind -- a contig name is a string it matches against the cache's chrom set (`select_cache_backed_contigs`, annotate_provider.rs:8786) and never a coordinate system it can move a variant between.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Parser::CAID module loads under `use` — the class that supplies this file's entire subject
rationale: A module-load probe, and therefore `not-applicable` under docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (`use_ok` is `not-applicable` unconditionally): `use_ok` asserts that Perl's loader found, compiled and imported `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::CAID`, and Rust performs no runtime module load that could succeed or fail. The earlier reading — that there is no Rust symbol whose absence the linker could report — remains a true statement about the pin (`grep -rniE 'caid|clingen|allele.?registry' datafusion/` returns 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, against 308 matching `skip` and 72 matching `warn` as positive controls), but under R2 it is not the criterion. CAid's absence is carried by the nine rows that exercise the format, n=3 through n=11, every one of them `no-feature`; this line would be a tenth count of the same gap.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config module loads under `use` before a config object is built for the DB-backed subtests
rationale: A module-load probe on VEP's generic option container, not on anything CAid-specific: `use_ok` asserts only that Perl found and compiled `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config` at runtime. vepyr's counterparts exist and the linker already resolves them — `EnsemblCacheOptions` in datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache and `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:406) — so a runtime assertion here would restate the compiler. Same class-existence family docs/ledger-contract.md names as legitimately not-applicable, and the corpus is consistent: every already-classified `use_ok Config` row (AnnotationSource, AnnotationSourceAdaptor, AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat, AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix, BaseVEP, CacheDir, Config, InputBuffer) is `not-applicable`.

desc: throw without DB: `Parser::CAID->new` with `offline => 1` dies with /Cannot use CAid format in offline mode/ — CAid input is refused unless a database connection is available
rationale: The assertion pins a precondition between two features vepyr has neither of. CAid resolution is a database query by construction: Parser/CAID.pm:103 throws from `new` under `--offline`, :105 acquires the variation-DB `VariationFeature` adaptor, and :164 answers the lookup with `$ad->fetch_all_by_caid($caid)` after forcing `include_failed_variations(1)` (:162). vepyr has no CAid format (0 lines matching `caid|clingen|allele.?registry` over `datafusion/` at dfbf 391f94bd; positive controls 308 for `skip`, 72 for `warn`) and no database mode in which to refuse it: `grep -rniE 'mysql|DBI|ensembl_db|database_host' datafusion/` returns 0 lines against 2219 matching `cache` — the standing cache-only finding. Offline is vepyr's only mode, so there is no online/offline distinction for an error message to mark. Absent features: CAid identifier input, and the database adaptor layer the message is about.

desc: class ref: under a live-DB config the object returned by `Parser::CAID->new` is blessed into Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::CAID
rationale: A blessing probe, which read on its own would be `not-applicable` — Perl object identity is on docs/ledger-contract.md's explicit not-applicable list. It stays in the denominator under the same document's convention for probes inside a SKIP block guarding an absent feature: perl/Parser_CAID.t:56 skips this row and the seven after it unless a local Ensembl MySQL test database is configured (`MultiTestDB->new('homo_vepiens')`, :58), and the config the block then builds is explicitly `database => 1, offline => 0` (:60-65). The block's whole purpose is the DB-backed CAid path — two capabilities vepyr lacks, measured in n=1 and n=3 — so this is an absent feature, not Perl plumbing.

desc: basic input test: the CAid `CA9985736` resolves to a VariationFeature on chr 21 at start = end = 25585733 with allele_string 'C/T', class_SO_term 'SNV', ancestral_allele 'C', minor_allele 'T' at frequency 0.000998403, five evidence attributes and _source_name 'dbSNP' (whole blessed hash compared, after adaptor/variation/slice/variation_name/class_display_term are deleted at :107)
rationale: The payload of the file: an opaque ClinGen Allele Registry identifier is turned into a fully populated variation record, and the comparison is field-by-field rather than on one attribute. The gap must be stated precisely, because half of what the row displays does have a vepyr counterpart: colocated-variant annotation is read from the cache (`grep -rniE 'var_synonym|existing_variation|dbsnp' datafusion/bio-function-vep/src` returns 73 lines at dfbf 391f94bd), so fields like the allele string and the minor-allele frequency are not themselves unreachable. What has no counterpart is the *lookup* this row is about — `$ad->fetch_all_by_caid($caid)` (Parser/CAID.pm:164), a query against the Ensembl variation database keyed by CAid, with `include_failed_variations` toggled around it (:162, :180). vepyr has neither the identifier vocabulary (0 lines matching `caid|clingen|allele.?registry`) nor the database to query. Absent feature: CAid-to-variant resolution as an input format.

desc: missing ID: an unresolvable CAid (`CA123`) makes `next()` return undef rather than dying or emitting a partial record
rationale: The assertion pins the CAid parser's failure semantics: `create_VariationFeatures` warns and recurses when the registry lookup comes back empty (Parser/CAID.pm:166-169), so a file whose only line is unresolvable yields undef from `next()` at end of input rather than an exception or a half-built VariationFeature. There is no vepyr code path that can exhibit it, because the lookup whose failure is being characterised does not exist — 0 lines matching `caid|clingen|allele.?registry` over `datafusion/` at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control 308 for `skip`. The row is not about generic empty-input handling: what makes it non-trivial in the Perl is precisely that a *resolvable-looking* identifier resolved to nothing. Absent feature: CAid identifier input, hence also its not-found behaviour.

desc: missing CAid warning msg: the unresolvable identifier produces a /No variants found for CAid/ warning on the captured STDERR
rationale: The observable half of n=6: the parser does not fail silently — Parser/CAID.pm:167 emits `WARNING: No variants found for CAid '<id>'` through `warning_msg`, and the test captures it by rebinding STDERR to a scalar (perl/Parser_CAID.t:112-114). Two things would have to exist in vepyr for this to be portable, and neither does: the CAid lookup itself (0 lines matching `caid|clingen|allele.?registry` over `datafusion/` at dfbf 391f94bd) and a per-input-record diagnostic channel for a format that reports unresolved identifiers. The positive control is 72 lines matching `warn` in the same tree, so vepyr does emit diagnostics — it simply has no such class of event to report, because nothing resolves identifiers. Absent feature: CAid input and its not-found diagnostic.

desc: skip past missing ID: given `CA123 CA9985736`, the first (unresolvable) identifier is passed over and `next()` returns the VariationFeature named CA9985736
rationale: This is the row that pins *recovery*, not failure: the recursion at Parser/CAID.pm:168 (`return $self->create_VariationFeatures()`) is what makes one bad identifier cost one record instead of the rest of the file, and the assertion witnesses it by checking the returned VariationFeature's `variation_name` is the second line's identifier. It is a distinct property from n=6 — a parser could return undef for a lone bad ID (n=6) and still abandon the file (this row) — which is why it earns its own row rather than sharing n=6's judgement. vepyr cannot exhibit it for the same reason: no CAid lookup exists to fail and recover from (0 lines matching `caid|clingen|allele.?registry` over `datafusion/` at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control 308 for `skip`). Absent feature: CAid identifier input, hence also its per-record error recovery.

desc: missing ID warning msg: the skipped-over identifier from n=8 also produces a /No variants found for CAid/ warning, so recovery is not silent
rationale: The pair to n=8 as n=7 is to n=6, and the pairing is the point: the parser recovers *and* reports, so a user reading only the output cannot mistake a skipped identifier for one that matched nothing in the annotation. Same emitter (Parser/CAID.pm:167 via `warning_msg`), same STDERR capture (perl/Parser_CAID.t:112-114), with `$tmp` deliberately reset to '' at :126 so this assertion cannot pass on the warning left over from n=7. vepyr has no CAid lookup to report on (0 lines matching `caid|clingen|allele.?registry` at dfbf 391f94bd; 72 lines matching `warn` as the positive control that a diagnostic channel does exist). Absent feature: CAid input and its not-found diagnostic.

desc: parse input file with empty lines: leading blank and whitespace-only lines (a newline, a space-only line, then CA9985736) are tolerated and the file still yields n=5's exact VariationFeature
rationale: The assertion pins that blank-line tolerance does not disturb the parsed record — it re-compares the full expected hash from n=5, so a parser that skipped the lines but mis-set `line_number` or dropped a field would still fail here. The behaviour comes from the shared base class (`Parser.pm:266-291`, `skip_empty_lines`, which the docs note is 'not used by all parsers' and which only CAID.pm:147 and HGVS.pm:147 call), but it is only reachable in this file through the CAid parser. vepyr has no line-oriented identifier input at all: its input is a VCF *table* read through datafusion-bio-format-vcf, not a newline-delimited list, and at dfbf 391f94bd the only match for `skip_empty|empty line|blank line` anywhere under `datafusion/` is `bio-function-fastqc/src/overrepresented.rs:358` — an unrelated crate, which is the positive control that the grep reaches the workspace. Absent feature: CAid identifier input, and with it the line-list reader whose blank-line tolerance this row asserts.

desc: empty line warning: skipping those two lines emits /Skipped 2 empty lines/, so the tolerated lines are still accounted for to the user
rationale: The counting half of n=10: `Parser.pm:283-290` formats `Skipped %i empty line%s from line %i` from the running total, so the assertion pins both that the lines were skipped and that exactly two of them were — a parser that swallowed them silently, or miscounted, fails here while n=10 still passes. That is why it is a separate row and not a second claim on n=10's property. vepyr has nothing to count: there is no line-list reader (the sole `skip_empty|empty line|blank line` match under `datafusion/` at dfbf 391f94bd is in the unrelated `bio-function-fastqc` crate, `overrepresented.rs:358`) and no CAid format to read (0 lines matching `caid|clingen|allele.?registry`, positive controls 308 for `skip` and 72 for `warn`). Absent feature: the line-oriented identifier reader and its skipped-line accounting.

The one variant-input constructor is `VariantInput::from_vcf` (src/transcript_consequence.rs:34) and it has no `from_hgvs` sibling; the vepyr pin's public entry point is `annotate(vcf: str, cache_dir: str, ...)` (346b9173, src/vepyr/__init__.py:694), whose `hgvs`/`hgvsc`/`hgvsp` keywords are documented at :766-772 as output notation flags. desc: throw without DB: constructing Parser::ID with offline => 1 dies with /Cannot use ID format in offline mode/, because resolving an identifier needs a live variation database

So there is no code path that could raise this refusal and none that could bypass it. Classified no-feature rather than not-applicable although the assertion is about a die: what it pins is a product decision — which input formats need a server — and no-feature keeps that in the denominator.
