So the row is no-feature, and naming vepyr's SV table here would be a false analogue rather than a partial one; detailed_plans/Parser_ID.md reaches XL for exactly this half, since vepyr has no structural-variation cache to index.

desc: missing ID: `rs699` is absent from the test database, so next() returns undef rather than dying or emitting a placeholder feature
rationale: Pins the not-found contract of a lookup that vepyr does not perform: when neither the VariationAdaptor nor the StructuralVariationAdaptor knows the id, create_VariationFeatures warns and re-enters itself (Parser/ID.pm:174-176 @ release/116.0); with one line in the file the recursion immediately hits `return [] unless $parser->{record}` (:146), and next() propagates the empty list as undef. The failure mode has no counterpart because the lookup has none — a VCF record carries its own coordinates and alleles, so vepyr's reader can never be handed a variant it cannot locate; a record that simply matches nothing in the cache still produces an annotated row, which is a different outcome from `no variant at all`. Same missing feature as n=5, observed at its error edge.

desc: missing ID warning msg: the unresolvable `rs699` produces a /No variant found with ID/ line on the redirected STDERR rather than silent omission
rationale: The diagnostic half of n=8: warning_msg (Parser/ID.pm:175 @ release/116.0) reports the dropped identifier so a user can tell an empty result from an unrecognised input. vepyr emits no such per-record diagnostic and has nothing to report it about — `grep -rn 'max_sv_size\|dont_skip\|check_ref\|valid_chromosomes\|warning_file' src/` -> 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd (positive control `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516), and the 35 lines matching `skipped` in that tree are all cache-lookup and transcript-selection bookkeeping (lookup_exec.rs:646, :653, :731; annotate_provider.rs:12396), never input lines. Kept as its own row rather than folded into n=8 because a port could satisfy the undef and still lose the warning.

desc: skip past missing ID: given the two-line input `rs699` then `rs142513484`, the first next() skips the unresolvable identifier and returns the second variant, whose variation_name is rs142513484 — the parser advances instead of stopping at the first failure
rationale: A recovery property, and the reason n=8 alone would not cover the file: n=8 shows one bad identifier yields undef, this shows a bad identifier does not end the stream — the same tail call at Parser/ID.pm:176 @ release/116.0 produces both answers, and only the presence of a second line separates them. Both are behaviours of an identifier resolver vepyr does not have. The nearest-looking vepyr behaviour — a VCF record that finds no cache match still being emitted — is not the same property: nothing was skipped, because nothing failed to resolve. Claiming it here would put a coverage tick against a code path that cannot regress the way this line guards.

desc: missing ID warning msg (second occurrence): the skipped `rs699` in the two-line input also emits /No variant found with ID/, so recovering from a bad identifier is not silent
rationale: n=9's assertion re-made in the recovery scenario of n=10, and it earns its own row for the reason the pair exists upstream: a parser could plausibly warn when it returns nothing and stay quiet when it manages to return something, and this line forbids that. vepyr has no input-line diagnostic channel at all (probe and positive control at n=9), so the whole pair is absent rather than partially covered.

desc:
parse input file with empty lines: an input file of "
 
rs142513484 
" — a blank line, a whitespace-only line, then the identifier with a trailing space — still yields the complete VariationFeature of n=5, key-for-key
rationale: Two properties in one comparison: blank and whitespace-only lines are skipped (Parser.pm::skip_empty_lines, :266-292 @ release/116.0, whose test is `$parser->{record} !~ /\w+/` at :273), and the trailing space is stripped before the lookup (`$id =~ s/\s+//g`, Parser/ID.pm:153). Neither survives the crossing, because neither has a place to happen: vepyr's input is parsed by datafusion-bio-format-vcf's VcfTableProvider (vcf_sink.rs:17, :1074), a noodles-backed VCF reader in a different crate, and blank lines are not a VCF construct — there is no VEP-owned line reader to which an empty-line rule could belong. The expected value is n=5's database-fetched hash, so even the whitespace half cannot be checked without the absent lookup. no-feature rather than deferred: this is not an export waiting to happen.

desc: empty line warning: skipping those two blank lines emits /Skipped 2 empty lines/ on STDERR — the count, not merely the fact, is reported
rationale: skip_empty_lines counts what it drops and reports `Skipped %i empty line%s from line %i` (Parser.pm:279-289 @ release/116.0), so a user reading the log can reconcile input line numbers with output rows. vepyr has no line-number bookkeeping over its input and no warning channel to carry it: the 35 lines matching `skipped` at dfbf 391f94bd are cache and transcript bookkeeping (lookup_exec.rs:646/:653/:731, annotate_provider.rs:12396) and `grep -rn 'warning_file' src/` -> 0 lines, against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516. The missing feature is an input-line diagnostic log, not just this message.

desc: SV bigger than max_sv_size warning: resolving `nsv917902` produces a /nsv917902.* variant size .* is bigger than --max_sv_size/ line, so an oversized structural variant is reported by name and by size rather than annotated
rationale: The last assertion in the file and the one that needs three absent things at once: identifier resolution (n=5), structural variants as input (n=7), and the --max_sv_size ceiling that decides what counts as oversized (Parser.pm:491-497 @ release/116.0, where the option is read from the shortcut list added at :128). None exists at the pin: `grep -rn 'max_sv_size' src/` -> 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516, and the option is absent from both the 31-key DataFusion vocabulary and AnnotateVcfConfig's 34 fields (vcf_sink.rs:381-456). vepyr applies no size ceiling to an input record, so there is no threshold to cross and no message to emit.

desc: use_ok Parser::Region: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::Region module compiles and loads
rationale: A module-load probe: use_ok asserts that Perl found and compiled Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/Parser/Region.pm at run time, and nothing about what the parser does. Rust settles the same question at compile time — an absent item behind a `use` stops the test crate building — so a run-time assertion would only restate the compiler. docs/ledger-contract.md admits exactly this case; same reading as ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=1. The *feature* the module implements is absent from vepyr, but classifying the load probe not-applicable hides nothing: every row that asserts what the parser does (4-6, 8-17) is no-feature and stays in the denominator, which is the argument ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=15 makes for the same idiom.

desc: use_ok Config: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config module compiles and loads, so the fixture configs can be built
rationale: The second of this file's two module-load probes, and pure test scaffolding: Config is loaded only so t/Parser_Region.t:38, :48 and :55 can build the three config objects the constructors are handed. Same compile-time argument as row 1. What Config actually resolves is the subject of t/Config.t and is classified in ledger/Config.ledger.toml, so nothing is lost by keeping the load probe out of the denominator. Identical assertion and identical reading at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=2.

desc: get new config object: Config->new(base_testing_cfg + fasta) returns a defined, true config object
rationale: ok($cfg) pins the Perl idiom for `new did not die and did not return undef`, and nothing else — the option set is never inspected on this line. docs/ledger-contract.md's ok($obj) ruling puts a constructor probe in not-applicable when the class denotes generic plumbing whose Rust analogue is an infallible struct: AnnotateVcfConfig (dfbf vcf_sink.rs:381-456 @ 391f94bd) has a Default impl at :458, building one cannot fail and Rust has no undef, so the failure mode this line guards against does not exist. Same assertion, same reading, at ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=3 and ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=3. Note this row is *not* about the fasta key it passes: what the FASTA is for is asserted by rows 8-12, which are no-feature.

desc: new is defined: Parser::Region->new({config, file}) over the single region line 21:25587759-25587759/A returns a defined parser — the region input format is accepted when a FASTA is configured
rationale: The other arm of docs/ledger-contract.md's ok($obj) ruling, and the reason this row is not row 3's twin: what Parser::Region denotes is a capability, not plumbing. The line asserts that a region-format input file is an acceptable thing to hand VEP — the constructor is load-bearing, since Region::new (Parser/Region.pm:108-125 @ release/116.0) validates the mode and forces lookup_ref before returning. vepyr cannot express the configuration this line asserts is accepted: there is no `--format` in its vocabulary at all (31 closed option keys, and `AnnotateVcfConfig`'s 34 fields), and the input is a VCF path opened as VcfTableProvider (vcf_sink.rs:1074). Missing capability: region-string input. Worked precedent for this split is ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=30 (`ok($cd = ...->new({regulatory => 1}))` is no-feature because the flag cannot be expressed) against its n=3.

desc: new with --offline no --fasta fails: constructing Parser::Region offline and without a FASTA dies with /Cannot use Region format in offline mode/, because the reference allele can then be fetched from neither a FASTA nor a database
rationale: A precondition on a format vepyr does not offer. Region::new throws when `param('offline') && !param('fasta')` (Parser/Region.pm:115 @ release/116.0) precisely because the region string supplies only the ALT: the REF is a run of placeholder Ns (:189) that lookup_ref later replaces from the slice. vepyr never faces the choice — a VCF record carries its own REF, so the reference sequence is optional for it (`reference_fasta_path: Option<String>`, vcf_sink.rs:404, required only for HGVS) rather than mandatory for parsing. Distinct from n=6: this row is about the offline+no-FASTA combination, n=6 about --check_ref, and the two throws are separate statements in the same constructor. no-feature rather than not-applicable although the assertion is about a die: what it pins is which input formats need a reference, a product statement, and no-feature keeps it in the denominator.

desc: new with --check_ref fails: constructing Parser::Region with check_ref => 1 dies with /Region format is not compatible with --check_ref/, because the input supplies no reference allele to check
rationale: An incompatibility between two features vepyr has neither of. Region::new throws whenever check_ref is set (Parser/Region.pm:118 @ release/116.0); the comment on :117 gives the reason — 'no ref given' — which is exactly what makes the region format different from VCF. At the pin `grep -rn 'check_ref' src/` -> 0 lines against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516, and check_ref is absent from both the 31-key DataFusion vocabulary and AnnotateVcfConfig's 34 fields, so vepyr has no reference-verification mode that could be declared incompatible with anything. The missing feature named here is the pair, not just the region format: an option-compatibility matrix over input formats.

desc: check class: ref($p) is exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::Region — not a subclass and not a plain hashref
rationale: A blessing probe — ref() reads back the package a hashref was blessed into. docs/ledger-contract.md lists assertions about blessing and Perl object identity as the legitimate not-applicable case: a Rust value's type is fixed by its declaration and checked by the compiler, and there is no ref() to call at run time. Same assertion, same reading, at ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=3 and ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=2. The contract's SKIP convention, which keeps such a probe at no-feature, does not reach here: this line is at file top level, not inside any SKIP block — contrast ledger/Parser_ID.ledger.toml n=4 and n=6, where the same idiom stays no-feature because it sits inside the eleven-assertion database block. Nothing is hidden by the not-applicable reading: every row asserting what this parser produces (8-17) is no-feature and stays in the denominator.

desc: basic next test: `21:25587759-25587759:1/A` parses to a VariationFeature with chr 21, start=end=25587759, strand 1, map_weight 1, variation_name equal to the input string, _line the input string, and allele_string T/A — the T being read from the FASTA, since the region string supplies only the ALT
rationale: The row that shows why region input is a feature and not a notation: create_VariationFeatures writes a placeholder allele_string of `('N' x (($end - $start) + 1)) . '/' . $allele` (Parser/Region.pm:189-194 @ release/116.0), and the T only appears because Region::new forced lookup_ref (:121-122), so validate_vf replaces the Ns with the slice's real bases (Parser.pm:635-645). vepyr performs neither half. It has no region parser to produce the placeholder, and its FASTA is optional and used for HGVS rather than for supplying a missing REF (`reference_fasta_path: Option<String>`, vcf_sink.rs:404) — a VCF record's REF is given, never looked up. Building this means building the input format plus a reference-fill step; detailed_plans/Parser_Region.md sizes the whole parser at M and still records EXCLUDE-no-analogue.

desc: no strand: `21:25587759-25587759/A`, with the optional `:strand` field omitted, parses to the same feature as n=8 with strand defaulted to 1 — only variation_name and _line differ, because they echo the shorter input string
rationale: Pins the optionality of the strand field, which the regex expresses by capturing it in group 4 only when group 5 is also present (Parser/Region.pm:171-180); with no strand the default falls out of `($strand || '') =~ /\-/ ? -1 : 1` at :183. Nothing in vepyr can default a field it never reads: a variant carries no input strand at all — `VariantInput` (transcript_consequence.rs:15-27 @ dfbf 391f94bd) has 11 public fields and none is `strand`, and at the pin `strand` is a required *transcript-table* column (annotate_provider.rs:3782), i.e. a property of the annotation source. Kept as its own row rather than folded into n=8: a port could parse the four-field form and reject the three-field one, and only this line forbids that.

desc: negative strand (-1): `21:25587759-25587759:-1/G` parses to strand -1 and allele_string A/G — the A being the reverse complement of the forward-strand T, so the FASTA lookup is strand-aware, not merely positional
rationale: The strongest row in the strand group, and the reason n=9 does not cover it: the strand is not only recorded, it changes the reference base the parser reports, because _get_ref_allele fetches through a strand-carrying slice — `$vf->{slice}->sub_Slice($vf->{start}, $vf->{end}, $vf->{strand})`, Parser.pm:751 @ release/116.0 — and n=8's T at the same coordinate becomes A here. vepyr has no counterpart at either end. It reads no input strand (n=9's probe), and it never derives a reference allele — the VCF's REF is what it uses, always forward-strand, as hgvs.rs:1528 states outright ('VCF alleles are always reported on the forward genomic strand'). So this is not a differently-observed version of a vepyr behaviour; the behaviour is absent.

desc: insertion: `21:25587759-25587758:1/A` — end one *before* start — parses to a feature keeping start 25587759 and end 25587758, with allele_string -/A, so a zero-length reference span denotes an insertion
rationale: Two mechanisms meet: `('N' x (($end - $start) + 1)) || '-'` yields the empty string for end = start-1 and the `||` falls through to '-' (Parser/Region.pm:189), and validate_vf's `start > end + 1` guard (Parser.pm:483-488) admits exactly this one inverted case while rejecting n=16's. The *convention* — start = end+1 and a '-' reference for an insertion — is genuinely shared with vepyr: vep_norm_start / vep_norm_end (allele.rs:764, :778 @ dfbf 391f94bd, whose doc comment says 'For insertions this produces `start > end` (VEP convention)') and vcf_to_vep_allele (:296) produce it. It is deliberately NOT claimed here. Those functions derive the convention from a VCF REF/ALT pair; this row asserts that a *user-written region string* carrying an inverted range is accepted and read as an insertion, which no signature taking (pos, ref, alt) can witness — docs/ledger-contract.md's dual-claim rule, `could this test fail if only the other row's behaviour regressed?`, answers no. The convention is owned by ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml, where the input actually exists; claiming it here would double-count one Rust behaviour across two ledgers.

desc: deletion: `21:25587759-25587759:1/-` parses to allele_string T/- — a literal `-` as the ALT means delete the span, and the T is still filled from the FASTA
rationale: The mirror of n=11 and not covered by it: there the '-' is *produced* by a zero-length span, here it is *consumed* as an allele the caller wrote, and the regex must let it through — `$allele =~ /^[ACGTN-]+$/` (Parser/Region.pm:188) is what keeps a bare '-' on the VariationFeature branch instead of sending it to get_SO_term. vepyr never reads an allele token: `-` is an output spelling its VEP-minimisation produces (vcf_to_vep_allele, allele.rs:296-343), never an input it parses, because a VCF ALT is a sequence. Same reason as n=11 for not claiming the shared spelling — the boundary differs, so the claim would be unfalsifiable by this row's regression.

desc: SV dup: `21:25587759-25587769/DUP` parses to a StructuralVariationFeature — not a VariationFeature — with class_SO_term duplication, start 25587759, end 25587769, and no allele_string or map_weight at all
rationale: The first of three rows where the allele token is not a sequence, so `$allele =~ /^[ACGTN-]+$/` fails and the parser switches branch and *class*: get_SO_term (Parser.pm:663-728) resolves DUP through %SO_TERMS (imported at :71) to `duplication`, and the object built is a StructuralVariationFeature (Parser/Region.pm:208-216). vepyr does carry structural-variant machinery at the pin — StructuralFeature and SvEventKind (transcript_consequence.rs:594-610), populated from a separate `structural` DataFusion table read column-by-column (annotate_provider.rs:5060-5132) — and it is not an analogue: its event vocabulary is `ablation|deletion|del`, `amplification|duplication|dup|amp`, `elongation|elongate`, `truncation|truncate` (annotate_provider.rs:7341-7348), i.e. SO *consequence* kinds, and it is never derived from an input record. The classifier that does run on input is classify_variant (annotate_provider.rs:7321-7329), whose whole output vocabulary is insertion / deletion / SNV / substitution / indel. Naming either would be a false analogue, so the missing feature is structural variants as *input*.

desc: SV inv: `21:25587759-25587769/INV` parses to a StructuralVariationFeature with class_SO_term inversion over the same span as n=13
rationale: Same branch as n=13 with a different SO term, and it earns a separate row because the term is what the assertion pins: a parser could resolve DUP and drop INV, and only this line forbids that. `inversion` is the SV class with no vepyr representation whatever — `grep -rn 'inversion' src/` -> 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control `grep -rn 'duplication' src/` -> 45 — and it is absent from both closed vocabularies: classify_variant's five outputs (annotate_provider.rs:7321-7329) and parse_sv_event_kind's four event kinds (:7341-7348). An inversion is neither an allele-shape class nor an ablation/amplification consequence, so there is nothing in vepyr it could map onto even loosely.

desc: SV del: `21:25587759-25587769/DEL` parses to a StructuralVariationFeature with class_SO_term deletion — a *symbolic* deletion over an 11 bp span, carrying no allele_string, unlike n=12's sequence-level T/-
rationale: The row that makes the DEL/'-' distinction explicit and so is not a duplicate of n=12: the same word `deletion` appears in both, but n=12 produces a VariationFeature with an allele_string and this produces a StructuralVariationFeature with a class_SO_term and none. vepyr collapses that distinction because it has only one side of it: classify_variant returns the string `deletion` for a VEP-minimised (ref, '-') pair (annotate_provider.rs:7324), a sequence-level fact, and there is no symbolic-allele path to reach — `grep -rniE '<DEL>|<DUP>|SVTYPE|symbolic' src/` -> 0 lines against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516. Classifying this analog-port on the strength of the shared word would claim a boundary vepyr does not have.

desc: skip VF that fails validation: given `21:25587769-25587767:1/A` then `21:25587759-25587759:1/A`, the first next() drops the invalid region — start exceeds end+1 — and returns the second, whose start is 25587759
rationale: Pins the parser's default recovery policy, and it is the exact complement of n=11: validate_vf's `start > end + 1` test (Parser.pm:483-488 @ release/116.0) admits n=11's inverted-by-one insertion and rejects this inverted-by-two region, and the failure is skipped with a warning rather than aborting the run (Parser.pm:189). vepyr has no such policy because it has no such stage: a malformed coordinate cannot reach it — the VCF is read by datafusion-bio-format-vcf's VcfTableProvider (vcf_sink.rs:17, :1074), which yields typed Arrow columns, so an unparseable POS fails at read time in another crate rather than being weighed by a VEP-owned validator. The nearest-looking vepyr behaviour, a record that finds no cache match still being emitted, is a different property: nothing was rejected. Missing feature: a per-record input validator with a skip policy.

desc: dont skip VF that fails validation with dont_skip: with dont_skip => 1 the same invalid region 21:25587769-25587767 is returned rather than dropped, so its start 25587769 comes back from the first next()
rationale: The option half of n=16, and separately assertable: n=16 shows the validator rejects, this shows the rejection is overridable, and the switch is a real user-facing option — `unless($self->validate_vf($vf) || $self->{dont_skip})` (Parser.pm:189 @ release/116.0), read from the shortcut list added at :128. Neither the validator nor its override exists at the pin: `grep -rn 'dont_skip' src/` -> 0 lines against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516, and dont_skip is in neither the 31-key DataFusion vocabulary nor AnnotateVcfConfig's 34 fields (vcf_sink.rs:381-456). The missing feature is the pair — a validation stage *and* the flag that turns it off — so this is no-feature rather than blocked-api: there is no private switch waiting to be exported.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Parser::SPDI module loads under `use` — the class that supplies this file's entire subject
rationale: A module-load probe, and therefore `not-applicable` under docs/ledger-contract.md RULING R2 (`use_ok` is `not-applicable` unconditionally): `use_ok` asserts that Perl's loader found, compiled and imported `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::SPDI`, and no Rust design contains a runtime module-load assertion, whatever the class denotes. The measurement this row previously turned on is still true and is still worth having on the record — at dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rni 'spdi' datafusion/` returns 0 lines against 1541 matching `hgvs` as the positive control — but it is not what decides the category. SPDI's absence is already counted by the four rows that exercise the format: n=3 (the offline refusal), n=4 (the constructed parser), n=5 (the genomic parse) and n=6 (the LRG parse), all `no-feature`. Counting the load line as well would count one gap twice.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Config module loads under `use` before a config object is built for the DB-backed subtests
rationale: A module-load probe on VEP's generic option container, not on anything SPDI-specific: `use_ok` asserts only that Perl found and compiled `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config` at runtime. vepyr's counterparts do exist and the linker already resolves them — `EnsemblCacheOptions` in datafusion-bio-format-ensembl-cache and `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` (dfbf 391f94bd, vcf_sink.rs:406) — so a runtime assertion here would restate the compiler. Same class-existence family docs/ledger-contract.md names as legitimately not-applicable, and the corpus is consistent about it: every already-classified `use_ok Config` row (AnnotationSource, AnnotationSourceAdaptor, AnnotationSource_Cache_RegFeat, AnnotationSource_Cache_VariationTabix, BaseVEP, CacheDir, Config, InputBuffer) is `not-applicable`.

desc: throw without DB: `Parser::SPDI->new` with `offline => 1` dies with /Cannot use SPDI format in offline mode/ — SPDI input is refused unless a database connection is available
rationale: The assertion pins a precondition between two features vepyr has neither of. SPDI resolution in VEP is intrinsically database-backed: Parser/SPDI.pm:96 throws from `new` when `--offline` is set, because `create_VariationFeatures` resolves the notation through `$vfa->fetch_by_spdi_notation(-slice_adaptor => $sa, -transcript_adaptor => $ta, ...)` (SPDI.pm:163-168), i.e. through live core-DB adaptors. vepyr has no SPDI format (0 lines matching `spdi` over `datafusion/` at dfbf 391f94bd; 1541 matching `hgvs` as the positive control) and no database mode in which to refuse it: `grep -rniE 'mysql|DBI|ensembl_db|database_host' datafusion/` returns 0 lines against 2219 matching `cache` — the standing cache-only finding docs/ledger-contract.md already lists among its `no-feature` examples. Offline is the only mode vepyr has, so there is no online/offline distinction for an error message to mark. Absent features: SPDI input parsing, and the database adaptor layer the message is about.

desc: class ref: under a live-DB config the object returned by `Parser::SPDI->new` is blessed into Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::SPDI
rationale: A blessing probe, which read on its own would be `not-applicable` — Perl object identity is on docs/ledger-contract.md's explicit not-applicable list. It stays in the denominator under the same document's convention for probes inside a SKIP block guarding an absent feature: perl/Parser_SPDI.t:56 skips this row and the two after it unless a local Ensembl MySQL test database is configured (`MultiTestDB->new('homo_vepiens')`, :58), and the config the block then builds is explicitly `database => 1, offline => 0` (:60-66). The block's whole purpose is the DB-backed SPDI path — two capabilities vepyr lacks, with the measurements in rows n=1 and n=3 — so this is an absent feature, not Perl plumbing.

desc: spdi genomic: `21:25000869:G:T` parses to a VariationFeature on chr 21 with start = end = 25000870, allele_string 'G/T', strand 1, map_weight 1 and every other field undef (whole blessed hash compared, after adaptor/variation/slice/variation_name/_line are deleted at :104)
rationale: The payload of the file: SPDI's 0-based interbase position 25000869 becomes the 1-based VariationFeature coordinate 25000870, the deleted/inserted halves become the `G/T` allele string, and the result is compared field by field rather than on one attribute. vepyr can exhibit none of it — there is no SPDI parser to feed (0 lines matching `spdi` over `datafusion/` at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control 1541 for `hgvs`), and the Perl route to the answer runs through `fetch_by_spdi_notation` with a live Slice adaptor (SPDI.pm:163-168) and then `$vf->transfer($vf->slice->seq_region_Slice)` (SPDI.pm:190), the database layer that same pin has no trace of. Absent feature: SPDI input parsing together with its 0-based-to-1-based coordinate conversion — which detailed_plans/Parser_SPDI.md flags as load-bearing if the format is ever added, and this row is the assertion that would pin it.

desc: spdi genomic LRG: `LRG_485:6673:G:A` parses to a VariationFeature on the non-chromosomal sequence LRG_485 with start = end = 6674 and allele_string 'G/A' — n=5's shape on an LRG accession
rationale: What distinguishes this row from n=5 is the *sequence* half of the notation: the parser must accept a non-chromosomal accession (`LRG_485`, declared in `valid_chromosomes` at perl/Parser_SPDI.t:110) and resolve it through the core database's Slice adaptor. The gap must not be overstated as an LRG gap — vepyr can already carry an LRG contig: `cache/key_encoding.rs:334` registers `LRG_*` names through `register_non_canonical_contigs` (with a test pinning the FNV-1a collision between `LRG_1278` and `LRG_8`, :330-341), and `annotate_provider.rs:16598` builds a test transcript on `LRG_485` itself. The contig vocabulary is therefore present; what is absent is the SPDI input format (0 lines matching `spdi` over `datafusion/` at dfbf 391f94bd, positive control 1541 for `hgvs`) and the DB-backed accession resolution it uses (0 lines for `mysql|DBI|ensembl_db|database_host`, positive control 2219 for `cache`). Absent feature: `--format spdi` in its LRG-accession form.

desc: use_ok Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF: the VCF input parser module loads, compiles and imports
rationale: RULING R2 (docs/ledger-contract.md): `use_ok` asserts that Perl's `require` found the file, compiled it and ran its `import`. Rust performs no runtime module load that could succeed or fail, so the line has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design, whatever the class denotes. The VCF-parsing capability is not thereby dropped from the denominator: rows n=4 and n=7 to n=25 exercise it and are judged on their own merits.

desc: use_ok Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config: the config module loads so a config object can be handed to the parser
rationale: RULING R2, same reasoning as n=1. The configuration surface this line names is `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` (dfbf `391f94bd:vcf_sink.rs:381-456`) on the vepyr side, whose fields are the subject of `ledger/Config.ledger.toml`, not of this file.

desc: get new config object: Config->new over the base testing config returns a defined object
rationale: The constructor-probe ruling, first arm: generic Perl plumbing. The line asks only whether `Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config->new($base_testing_cfg)` returned something. Its vepyr counterpart, `AnnotateVcfConfig` (dfbf `391f94bd:vcf_sink.rs:381`), is a plain struct with public fields and a `Default` impl -- constructing it cannot return a null, so the compiler already carries at compile time what this line checks at run time. Same reading as `CacheDir.t` n=3, the ruling's worked case.

desc: new is defined: Parser::VCF->new({config, file, valid_chromosomes}) returns a usable parser over the test VCF
rationale: The constructor-probe ruling, third arm: the class denotes a capability vepyr has under a different type. `VcfTableProvider::new(path, info_fields, format_fields, object_storage_options, zero_based)` (`datafusion-bio-format-vcf` v1.10.0, `table_provider.rs:752`) is what consumes a VCF path in vepyr, and it is the constructor the annotation entry point drives. It is more load-bearing than the Perl line, not less: it reads and parses the header before returning, so `Ok` is a claim about the input file rather than about allocation. The named test asserts both arms -- a readable VCF constructs, a path that is not one does not -- because `Ok` alone would be satisfied by a constructor that never looked at its argument. NOT covered: `valid_chromosomes`, which has no counterpart; vepyr restricts each scan to one contig from the cache side instead (`ContigAnnotationExec`, `annotate_provider.rs:8671-8700`).

desc: check class: the object returned by Parser::VCF->new reads back as a Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VCF
rationale: RULING R1, first arm: the construction already carries its own row -- n=4, two lines earlier -- so all this line adds is Perl object identity, which is on the not-applicable list. In Rust a constructor's return type is its class and cannot disagree with itself at run time: `VcfTableProvider::new` returns `datafusion::common::Result<VcfTableProvider>` by signature.

desc: parser: the parser delegates tokenising to a Bio::EnsEMBL::IO::Parser::VCF4 instance
rationale: RULING R1, second arm: the class denotes a capability vepyr has under another type. `Bio::EnsEMBL::IO::Parser::VCF4` is the low-level tokeniser VEP's parser delegates to; vepyr's is `noodles_vcf`, held inside `VcfTableProvider`'s physical exec node (`datafusion-bio-format-vcf` v1.10.0, `physical_exec.rs`) with no public accessor. Which tokeniser is in use is fixed by the type at compile time, so the readback restates a compile-time fact. What the tokeniser produces is not lost: n=7 asserts the header it parsed and n=8 the first record.

desc: headers: the parser hands back all seven header lines of the test VCF, verbatim and in file order
rationale: The same property through a different channel. Perl keeps the header as a list of literal strings; vepyr parses it into typed Arrow schema metadata and columns, so the observation point is `VcfTableProvider::schema()`. Every one of the seven lines has a counterpart and the named test asserts each: `##fileformat` -> `bio.vcf.file_format`; the two `##contig` records -> `bio.vcf.contigs`, ids and lengths both; `##ALT=<ID=CNV,...>` -> `bio.vcf.alternative_alleles`; the two `##INFO` declarations -> real `SVLEN` and `SVTYPE` columns in the schema; the `#CHROM` line's trailing sample -> `bio.vcf.samples`. NOT covered: line order and the literal text, which vepyr does not retain. The test's ancestor asserted only that some metadata key contained the substring "contig", which no implementation could fail; it was strengthened on promotion.

desc: next: the first record of the test VCF is rs142513484 at 21:25585733 with allele_string C/T
rationale: Perl compares a whole blessed `VariationFeature` hash; vepyr builds no such object, so the same facts are read off the parsed row plus the allele conversion. The named test asserts chrom 21, start 25585733, id rs142513484, ref C and alt T, and `allele::vcf_to_vep_input_allele(25585733, "C", "T")` returns `("C", "T", 25585733)` -- Perl's `allele_string` and `start`. NOT covered: `strand`, `map_weight` and the `seq_region_*` mirrors, which are Ensembl-schema bookkeeping with no vepyr field, and `nontrimmed_allele_string`, whose content vepyr keeps as the untouched `ref`/`alt` columns rather than as a second field.

desc: next again: a second call to next() yields a second record, and it is a small variant rather than a structural one
rationale: Two halves, and only one carries over. The iteration half -- a second data line produces a second record -- is asserted directly: the named test's query returns 2 rows and pins the second at 21:25587759. The class half cannot be: vepyr has no VariationFeature/StructuralVariationFeature split because it has no structural-variant representation at all (`SoTerm`, dfbf `391f94bd:so_terms.rs:14`, carries 41 terms, none structural), so every record is the same row type and a readback could not distinguish them. Deliberately not R1 not-applicable: the row's load-bearing content is a run-time fact about the file -- that a second record exists -- not a compile-time fact about a type.

desc: no shorting out 1: with two ALT-less lines in the middle of the file, test1 is still the first record returned
rationale: Same property, different observation point, and the difference between the two is where the ALT-less line is dropped. Perl's `next()` skips a record whose ALT is '.' inside the parser, so the caller sees test1 first. vepyr's reader keeps it: the named test measures 4 rows out of this 4-line file, with `alt` an empty string (not NULL) for test2 and test3. test1 is still the first record, which is what this row asserts. The skip happens one layer later, at annotate time -- `annotate_provider.rs:5695-5702` emits a NULL CSQ for an ALT-less row and counts it as `engine_profile.null_alt_rows` before any classifier runs.

desc: no shorting out 2: test4, which sits after two ALT-less lines, is still reached rather than the stream ending at them
rationale: The sharper half of the pair, and the one that names the divergence. Perl asserts that the SECOND record returned is test4, the two ALT-less lines having been dropped inside the parser, so it pins both "the stream does not terminate at a non-variant line" and "non-variant lines are dropped". vepyr keeps only the first: test4 is present and correct (`alt` = A at 21:25587762) but it is the fourth row, not the second, because the reader drops nothing. The ordinal is therefore NOT covered; what is covered is that a non-variant line neither truncates the scan nor corrupts the record after it. Nothing is annotated for test2/test3 either way (`annotate_provider.rs:5695-5702`) -- n=21 is the row that pins exactly that, and it is `deferred`/`blocked-data` for want of a cache.

desc: deletion: 21:25587759 AC>A becomes allele_string C/- at start = end = 25587760
rationale: Same inputs, same expected values, through the function that is the port of the Perl sub under test: `allele::vcf_to_vep_input_allele` (dfbf `391f94bd:allele.rs:353`) cites `Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/Parser/VCF.pm#L321-L345` -- the very sub under test -- in its own doc comment, and `annotate_provider.rs:5739-5750` repeats that citation over its own call. It is on vepyr's production input path (`annotate_provider.rs:5472`, `:5750`, and `VariantInput::from_vcf` at `:5898`), with `vep_norm_end` (`allele.rs:778`) supplying the end coordinate the same path uses at `:5916`. Precision, because it decides the multi-ALT rows differently: each of those sites is handed the ALT COLUMN VALUE WHOLE -- `alt_allele` is bound once per row at `:5694` from `string_at(batch.column(alt_idx), row)` and nothing on that path splits it -- which for a biallelic record like this one IS the single ALT, so the claim is exact here. The genuine per-ALT loop lives one layer down, at `cache/lookup_exec.rs:2451-2452`. Measured at the pin: `vcf_to_vep_input_allele(25587759, "AC", "A")` = `("C", "-", 25587760)` and `vep_norm_end(25587759, "AC", "A")` = 25587760 -- Perl's `allele_string`, `start` and `end`, unchanged. The named test reads the record through `VcfTableProvider` first, so the REF/ALT it converts are the ones vepyr's own reader produced rather than string literals. NOT asserted: `minimised`, `original_allele_string`, `original_start`/`original_end`, `nontrimmed_allele_string` and the `seq_region_*` mirrors -- Perl's pre-trim bookkeeping, for which vepyr keeps the untouched VCF `ref`/`alt` columns and no second copy of the coordinates.

desc: insertion: 21:25587759 A>AC becomes allele_string -/C at start 25587760 and end 25587759, VEP's start-after-end insertion convention
rationale: The insertion mirror of n=12, and it carries one property n=12 cannot: an insertion's reported start is GREATER than its end, which is how VEP encodes a zero-width position. `allele::vcf_to_vep_input_allele` (dfbf `391f94bd:allele.rs:353`) cites `Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/Parser/VCF.pm#L321-L345` -- the very sub under test -- in its own doc comment, and `annotate_provider.rs:5739-5750` repeats that citation over its own call. It is on vepyr's production input path (`annotate_provider.rs:5472`, `:5750`, and `VariantInput::from_vcf` at `:5898`), with `vep_norm_end` (`allele.rs:778`) supplying the end coordinate the same path uses at `:5916`. Precision, because it decides the multi-ALT rows differently: each of those sites is handed the ALT COLUMN VALUE WHOLE -- `alt_allele` is bound once per row at `:5694` from `string_at(batch.column(alt_idx), row)` and nothing on that path splits it -- which for a biallelic record like this one IS the single ALT, so the claim is exact here. The genuine per-ALT loop lives one layer down, at `cache/lookup_exec.rs:2451-2452`. Measured: `vcf_to_vep_input_allele(25587759, "A", "AC")` = `("-", "C", 25587760)` and `vep_norm_end(25587759, "A", "AC")` = 25587759, so start > end holds and the named test asserts it explicitly -- an implementation that clamped the pair would pass the two equality assertions and fail that one. NOT asserted: `minimised`, `original_allele_string`, `original_start`/`original_end`, `nontrimmed_allele_string` and the `seq_region_*` mirrors -- Perl's pre-trim bookkeeping, for which vepyr keeps the untouched VCF `ref`/`alt` columns and no second copy of the coordinates.

desc: deletion ignore SVTYPE: SVTYPE=DEL in INFO does not promote the sequence-allele deletion AC>A to a StructuralVariationFeature
rationale: Same outcome, reached without the decision the Perl row protects, which is why this is an analogue and not a unit port. VEP inspects INFO/SVTYPE and decides the record is not structural because REF and ALT are sequence alleles; vepyr makes no such decision, because it reads no SV vocabulary at all -- `grep -rn 'SVTYPE' src/` over `datafusion-bio-function-vep` at `391f94bd` returns 0 against a positive control of 237 `pub fn`, and `vcf_to_vep_input_allele` takes REF and ALT and nothing else. No vepyr change could make this assertion fail for the reason the Perl row exists. What the named test does assert is the outcome: the parsed columns and the conversion are identical with and without the INFO key, and equal C/- at 25587760-25587760.

desc: insertion ignore SVLEN: SVLEN=1 in INFO does not promote the sequence-allele insertion A>AC to a StructuralVariationFeature
rationale: The SVLEN half of n=14's pair, and separable from it: an implementation could key its SV test on SVTYPE alone and pass n=14 while failing here, which is why upstream writes both. Same reading and same evidence: `grep -rn 'SVLEN' src/` over the pinned crate returns 0 against a positive control of 237 `pub fn`, so the key is not read rather than read and rejected, and the named test asserts the outcome -- -/C at 25587760-25587759 with and without `SVLEN=1`, byte-identical parsed columns either way.

desc: multiple alts: 21:25587759 A>C,G stays one record whose joined allele_string is A/C/G at 25587759
rationale: Perl keeps a multi-ALT site as ONE VariationFeature and joins its alleles into a single `allele_string`; vepyr has no joined representation -- the reader pipe-joins the raw ALTs (measured: `alt` = "C|G") and the conversion is applied per ALT at `cache/lookup_exec.rs:2451-2452`, the one site that splits the joined string (`for alt in vcf_alt.split(['|', ','])` feeding `vcf_to_vep_input_allele`). NOT `annotate_provider.rs:5719`, which an earlier draft of this rationale named: `alt_allele` is bound once per row at `:5694` from `string_at(batch.column(alt_idx), row)` and that path never splits it, so `:5719` receives the whole joined value and explodes nothing. Reassembling the per-ALT conversions reproduces Perl's string and coordinates exactly: (A, C) and (A, G), start = end = 25587759 for both. Same reading as `ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml` n=72, for the same reason. NOT covered: that the three alleles ride on one record.

desc: mixed types - different first base: A>C,GG shares no anchor base, so the joined allele_string stays A/C/GG and original_allele_string is recorded
rationale: What separates this from n=16 is the unequal ALT lengths: one ALT is a SNV and the other is longer than REF, so a site-level trimmer has to leave both alone. vepyr reaches the same result per ALT because `vcf_to_vep_allele` suffix-trims only different-length pairs (the `if ref_bytes.len() != alt_bytes.len()` guard at `allele.rs:315`) and here the last bases differ (A against G), so nothing is trimmed and GG survives whole at 25587759-25587759 (measured). NOT covered: `original_allele_string`, which Perl sets whenever it touches the site; vepyr records nothing because it never rewrites the site.

desc: mixed types - same first base: G>GC,GT shares an anchor base across BOTH ALTs, so the joined allele_string minimises to -/C/T at 25587760-25587759
rationale: The row that catches a trimmer which minimises one ALT and forgets the other: both ALTs share the leading G with REF, so each becomes an insertion and the site's start moves to 25587760 while its end stays at 25587759. vepyr reaches the same three slots and the same coordinate pair one ALT at a time -- measured `("-", "C", 25587760)` and `("-", "T", 25587760)`, `vep_norm_end` 25587759 for both -- so the reassembled site is -/C/T over 25587760-25587759, Perl's value. NOT covered: `original_allele_string` = G/GC/GT.

desc: stubby: a five-column data line with nothing after ALT parses as the SNV G/C at 21:25587759
rationale: Ported, run, divergent. The Perl input is exactly `21 25587759 test G C` -- five columns, no QUAL/FILTER/INFO -- and VEP returns a VariationFeature. Observed by `tests/port_parser_vcf.rs::pvcf_row19_a_stubby_five_column_row_parses_as_the_snv`, named in `rust_test`, which drives the Perl input unchanged and asserts vepyr's rejection. Its ancestor padded the input to eight columns to make it pass, which pinned a different assertion (docs/ledger-contract.md: "If you changed the inputs to make it pass, it is not a unit port"). Fails at the current pin; the test's `issue:` line names the tracker.

desc: non-variant: with allow_non_variant=1 the ALT-less record 21:25587759 G>. is returned as a VariationFeature carrying non_variant => 1 and allele_string G
rationale: Missing feature: the `--allow_non_variant` request flag and the `non_variant` marking it produces. `grep -rn 'allow_non_variant\|non_variant' src/` over `datafusion-bio-function-vep` at `391f94bd` returns 0 against a positive control of 237 `pub fn`, and `AnnotateVcfConfig` (`vcf_sink.rs:381-456`) declares no field for it, so there is no knob to set and no flag to read back. vepyr's reader does keep the record -- measured: one row, `alt` an empty string, `qual` NULL -- but that is a different fact: Perl admits the record to annotation BECAUSE it was asked to, while vepyr admits it to the batch and then denies it a consequence (`annotate_provider.rs:5695-5702`). n=21 is the other polarity of the same flag.

desc: non-variant without allow_non_variant: with the flag off, next() returns undef for the ALT-less record instead of a VariationFeature
rationale: The measurement below is unchanged; what changed is that it is now asserted. No longer `blocked-data`: `tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache/` and `tests/data/vep115_reference_slice/` are committed (issue 96), the run issue 179 asked for was made, and it falsifies the premise that issue was filed on. Issue 179 predicted the record would come back with a NULL CSQ via `engine_profile.null_alt_rows` (`annotate_provider.rs:5695-5702`). It does not. . . .`: the emitted line carries a full CSQ whose first group is `-|frameshift_variant|HIGH|MRPL39|ENSG00000154719|Transcript|ENST00000307301|...` with `VARIANT_CLASS` `deletion` -- vepyr annotates the ALT-less record as a one-base deletion where VEP drops it. Positive control in the same run: the well-formed `21 25585733 rs142513484 C T` record on the line above annotates as `3_prime_UTR_variant`, so the pipeline was working. The mechanism is located, not guessed: the `null_alt_rows` guard is `let Some(alt_allele) = string_at(...) else` and therefore fires only on a NULL alt column, while the reader hands `ALT=.` across as an EMPTY STRING (pinned by `tests/port_parser_vcf.rs::pvcf_18_non_variant_row_default_kept_with_null_alt`), and `vcf_to_vep_allele("G", "")` returns `("G", "-")` -- measured through that public fn (`allele.rs:296`), against `vcf_to_vep_allele("G", ".")` returning `("G", ".")` as the control that the empty string is what does it. So the row cannot be an analogue: the property Perl states -- an ALT-less record yields no VariationFeature -- does not hold. `blocked-engine`: vepyr performs the operation and returns a different answer, and what is missing is a non-variant policy in the engine, not a fixture. Which side is defective is issue 179's question, not this row's: the belief recorded here is that vepyr is, because an ALT of `.` is the VCF spelling of `no alternate allele` and reading it as a one-base deletion invents a variant the file does not state. RE-POINTED 2026-08-30, issue 179 -> issue 422: 179 was closed completed on 2026-08-27 and its closing comment marks its own body superseded while arguing the row should keep pointing there, so a live divergence was tracked only by a closed issue whose body is known to be false. Issue 422 is a fresh acceptance-criterion tracker on the pattern of issue 367 and issue 329; 179's body is deliberately left untouched as the record of what was believed and what falsified it. Re-checked before filing: `gh search issues --repo <old-repo> --state open "vcf_to_vep_allele"` returns only issue 242, the unrelated xref-resolver follow-up, with `"contig attributes"` returning issue 367 as the positive control that the search shape finds trackers. Fails at the current pin; the test's `issue:` line names the tracker.

desc: *-type 1: the GATK spanning-deletion placeholder in 21:25587759 G>C,* is kept verbatim in the joined allele_string G/C/*
rationale: The Perl row pins that `*` is neither dropped nor mistaken for a sequence allele. vepyr keeps it at the parser level for the same reason it keeps every ALT -- measured `alt` = "C|*". Correction to an earlier draft of this rationale: the star skip at `annotate_provider.rs:5706` / `:5891` (`if alt_allele == "*"`) does NOT fire on this input. `alt_allele` is bound once per row at `:5694` from `string_at(batch.column(alt_idx), row)` and nothing on that path splits it, so the comparison is against the joined "C|*" and the skip bites only when `*` is a record's sole ALT -- which makes the parser-level preservation this row asserts the whole of what vepyr does with the placeholder, not half of it. Reassembled per ALT the site is G/C/* at 25587759, Perl's value. The named test's assertion was tightened from `contains('C') && contains('*')` to the exact `"C|*"` when the file was promoted. NOT covered: the joined representation itself, and that VEP carries the placeholder through to output.

desc: *-type 2: the angle-bracketed placeholder <DEL:*> in G>C,<DEL:*> is kept verbatim and original_allele_string is recorded
rationale: The angle-bracketed spelling of n=22, and separable from it: an implementation that matched the literal `*` would pass n=22 and mangle this one. This file's own commented-out stanza asserted that vepyr "does not parse `<DEL:*>` ALT shapes"; measured, it does -- `alt` comes back as "C|<DEL:*>" and `vcf_to_vep_allele("G", "<DEL:*>")` returns the pair unchanged, because the trimmer is length-based and finds no shared prefix. That stanza was deleted when the file was promoted. NOT covered: `original_allele_string`, and the downstream fate of the placeholder -- `annotate_provider.rs:5706` / `:5891` matches the literal `"*"` against the WHOLE joined ALT column value, so neither this spelling nor n=22's bare `*` beside a sibling ALT is caught by the star skip.

desc: *-type with deletion: in 21:25587759 GC>G,* the deletion slot minimises to C/- at 25587760 while the * placeholder is kept
rationale: The row where the joint and the per-allele readings visibly part. Perl trims the SITE once, so its joined `allele_string` is C/-/* with a single REF slot; vepyr converts each ALT independently, so the placeholder keeps its own REF slot GC (measured: `vcf_to_vep_input_allele(25587759, "GC", "*")` returns "GC" as ref). The joint REF slot is therefore NOT covered -- vepyr has no site-level allele string to put it in. What IS covered, and is what the row exists to protect, is that the deletion half is unaffected by its placeholder sibling: `("C", "-", 25587760)`, Perl's value.

desc: *-type with insertion: in 21:25587759 G>GC,* the insertion slot minimises to -/C at 25587760-25587759 while the * placeholder is kept
rationale: The insertion mirror of n=24, and not a copy of it: an insertion beside a placeholder moves the site's start past its end, which is the case where a joint trimmer is most likely to mis-anchor. vepyr's per-ALT conversion gives `("-", "C", 25587760)` with `vep_norm_end` 25587759 (measured), Perl's coordinates. Same NOT-covered as n=24: the joint REF slot, which vepyr leaves as GC for the placeholder's own conversion.

desc: minimal: with --minimal the MNV 21:25587758 CAT>CCT is decomposed to allele_string A/C at 25587759
rationale: Missing feature: the `--minimal` decomposition. Binding precedent, `ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml` n=70 -- the pinned crate DOES carry Ensembl's `trim_sequences` as `allele::trim_sequences_ensembl_with_end` (`allele.rs:32`), but its only production call sites are inside `get_matched_variant_alleles` (`allele.rs:237`, `:253`), i.e. colocated-allele matching, not the input path. What the input path runs is `vcf_to_vep_allele` (`allele.rs:296`), which deliberately does not suffix-trim equal-length alleles: the `if ref_bytes.len() != alt_bytes.len()` guard at `allele.rs:315`, whose comment one line up (`:313`) states "VEP only suffix-trims indels (different-length alleles), not MNVs". Measured on this row's input: vepyr returns ("AT", "CT") over 25587759-25587760, not Perl's A/C at 25587759-25587759, and no flag would change it -- `grep -rn 'minimal' src/` finds only test-helper function names.

desc: minimal - multiple alts pass through here: --minimal exempts the multi-ALT site 21:25587758 C>T,CAA, leaving allele_string C/T/CAA untrimmed at 25587758
rationale: The exemption half of n=26's feature, and it has no counterpart for two reasons at once: there is no `--minimal` for a site to be exempt from, and there is no joined `allele_string` for the exemption to preserve. vepyr converts each ALT alone, so this site's second ALT becomes ("-", "AA") over 25587759-25587758 (measured) where Perl keeps CAA at 25587758. That is the OPPOSITE of `ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml` n=72, where the per-ALT conversions did reassemble to the Perl string and the row is therefore a port; the analogue holds there and fails here, which is what separates the two.

desc: StructuralVariationFeature 1: <DUP> with SVTYPE=DUP;END=25587769 becomes an SVF with class_SO_term duplication over 25587759-25587769, outer and inner bounds equal to the exact bounds
rationale: The block's anchor row: it pins the whole StructuralVariationFeature shape at once -- the SO term taken from SVTYPE, the 1-based start shifted past the VCF anchor base, the end taken from INFO/END, and the four fuzzy-bound fields defaulting to the exact bounds when no confidence interval is given. Missing feature: structural-variant parsing and the StructuralVariationFeature type itself. It does not reach even that far. With `END` in INFO and no `##INFO=<ID=END,...>` header declaration -- which is how Ensembl's harness writes every fixture in this file, `t/VEPTestingConfig.pm:208-231` writing no header at all -- the reader panics on an `unwrap` at `datafusion-bio-format-vcf` v1.10.0 `physical_exec.rs:665` ("invalid INFO END position value"), measured; declaring `END` in the header makes the same record parse. Filed as old-repo issue #176. vepyr has no structural-variant representation at the pin: `SoTerm` (dfbf `391f94bd:so_terms.rs:14`) enumerates 41 consequence terms and not one of them is structural, and `grep -rn` over the pinned crate's `src/` returns 0 for each of `SVTYPE`, `SVLEN`, `class_SO_term`, `breakend`, `tandem_repeat`, `copy_number_variation`, `CIPOS` and `CIEND`, against a positive control of 237 `pub fn`. Such a record reaches vepyr as an ordinary row whose ALT happens to be a string in angle brackets, and `vcf_to_vep_allele` (`allele.rs:296`) hands the pair straight back (measured: `("T", "<DUP>")`).

desc: StructuralVariationFeature 2: with ALT '.' and the same SVTYPE=DUP;END, the SVF is identical except allele_string, so the class comes from INFO and not from the ALT
rationale: Separable from n=28 by exactly one property, and it is the one that matters for a parser: with the ALT emptied to '.', every field of the expected object is unchanged except `allele_string`. The row therefore pins that `class_SO_term` is read from INFO/SVTYPE rather than inferred from the angle-bracket ALT -- an implementation that keyed only on the ALT would pass n=28 and fail here. Missing feature: any SVTYPE-driven classification at all. It does not reach even that far. desc: use_ok Parser::VEP_input: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VEP_input module compiles and loads
rationale: A module-load probe: use_ok asserts that Perl found and compiled Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/Parser/VEP_input.pm at run time, and nothing about what the parser does. Rust settles the same question at compile time — an absent item behind a `use` stops the test crate building — so a run-time assertion would only restate the compiler. docs/ledger-contract.md admits exactly this case; same reading as ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=1. The *feature* the module implements is absent from vepyr, but classifying the load probe not-applicable hides nothing: every row that asserts what the parser does (4, 6-18) is no-feature and stays in the denominator, which is the argument ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=15 makes for the same idiom.

desc: use_ok Config: the Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Config module compiles and loads, so the fixture config can be built
rationale: The second of this file's two module-load probes, and pure test scaffolding: Config is loaded only so t/Parser_VEP_input.t:38 can build the single config object every parser in the file is handed. Same compile-time argument as row 1. What Config actually resolves is the subject of t/Config.t and is classified in ledger/Config.ledger.toml, so nothing is lost by keeping the load probe out of the denominator. Identical assertion and identical reading at ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=2.

desc: get new config object: Config->new(base_testing_cfg) returns a defined, true config object
rationale: ok($cfg) pins the Perl idiom for `new did not die and did not return undef`, and nothing else — the option set it is handed (VEPTestingConfig::base_testing_cfg) is never inspected on this line. docs/ledger-contract.md's ok($obj) ruling puts a constructor probe in not-applicable when the class denotes generic plumbing whose Rust analogue is an infallible struct: AnnotateVcfConfig (dfbf vcf_sink.rs:381-456 @ 391f94bd) has a Default impl at :458, building one cannot fail and Rust has no undef, so the failure mode this line guards against does not exist. Same assertion, same reading, at ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=3 and ledger/AnnotationSource.ledger.toml n=3. Note this config carries no `fasta`, unlike t/Parser_Region.t's — the VEP-input format needs no reference lookup, which is what n=6 turns on.

desc: new is defined: Parser::VEP_input->new({config, file}) over the single tab line `21 25587759 25587759 C/A + test` returns a defined parser — the legacy VEP-input format is accepted
rationale: The other arm of docs/ledger-contract.md's ok($obj) ruling: decide by what the class denotes, and Parser::VEP_input denotes the `--format ensembl` capability, not plumbing. Be precise about how much this constructor does — Parser/VEP_input.pm defines no `new` of its own (it declares only `parser` at :85 and `create_VariationFeatures` at :109 @ release/116.0), so the call runs Parser::new, which is *itself* the format-dispatch site: it dies without a file (:132), sets the delimiter (:135) and selects or detects the subclass (:141). vepyr has no such site and no vocabulary in which this configuration could be stated: no `--format` among 31 closed option keys or AnnotateVcfConfig's 34 fields, and the input is a VCF path opened as VcfTableProvider (vcf_sink.rs:1074). Missing capability: tab-delimited VEP input. Worked precedent for the split against n=3 is ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=30 versus its n=3.

desc: check class: ref($p) is exactly Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VEP_input — not the Parser base class it inherits from and not a plain hashref
rationale: A blessing probe — ref() reads back the package a hashref was blessed into. docs/ledger-contract.md lists assertions about blessing and Perl object identity as the legitimate not-applicable case: a Rust value's type is fixed by its declaration and checked by the compiler, and there is no ref() to call at run time. Same assertion, same reading, at ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=3 and ledger/AnnotationSourceAdaptor.ledger.toml n=2. The contract's SKIP convention, which keeps such a probe at no-feature, does not reach here: this line is at file top level, not inside any SKIP block — contrast ledger/Parser_ID.ledger.toml n=4 and n=6. Nothing is hidden: every row asserting what this parser produces (6-18) is no-feature and stays in the denominator.

desc: basic next test: the six columns `21 25587759 25587759 C/A + test` parse to a VariationFeature with chr 21, start=end=25587759, strand 1, map_weight 1, allele_string C/A taken verbatim, variation_name `test` from the sixth column, and _line holding all six tokens
rationale: The row that fixes the format's whole contract: which column means what, that the allele column is stored without interpretation (Parser/VEP_input.pm:156 @ release/116.0), and that the optional sixth column becomes the variant's name (:160). Nothing in vepyr reads a positional column layout — its input is a VCF, whose fields are named by the specification and read by datafusion-bio-format-vcf's VcfTableProvider (vcf_sink.rs:17, :1074) into typed Arrow columns in a different crate. There is no VEP-owned tokeniser to which a six-column rule could belong, and no `--format` to select one. Unlike t/Parser_Region.t n=8 this row needs no FASTA: the REF is given in the allele column, so what is missing here is purely the input format, not a reference-fill step as well.

desc: negative strand (-): the same row with `-` in the fifth column yields strand -1 and, notably, allele_string still C/A — the alleles are NOT reverse-complemented, only the strand flag changes
rationale: The row that disproves the claim in detailed_plans/Parser_VEP_input.md that `-` strand inputs reverse-complement the ALT: `$strand = ($strand || '') =~ /\-/ ? -1 : 1` (Parser/VEP_input.pm:131 @ release/116.0) sets a flag and the allele_string is stored verbatim at :156, which is exactly what the expected hash at t/Parser_VEP_input.t:76-87 pins against the input written at :72. So the property is `the input may declare which strand its alleles are written on, and VEP carries that declaration forward untouched`. vepyr has no place to carry it: `VariantInput` (transcript_consequence.rs:15-27 @ dfbf 391f94bd) has 11 public fields and none is `strand`, and hgvs.rs:1528 states the standing invariant — 'VCF alleles are always reported on the forward genomic strand'. The missing feature is a per-variant input strand, not a transformation; vepyr's transcript-side `strand` (annotate_provider.rs:3782) is a different axis and claiming it would be a false analogue.

desc: negative strand (-1): the numeric spelling `-1` in the fifth column produces exactly n=7's feature, so the two accepted spellings of the reverse strand are interchangeable
rationale: A synonym rule, and separately assertable from n=7: the normalisation is a substring test rather than an equality test — `=~ /\-/` (Parser/VEP_input.pm:131 @ release/116.0) — so `-`, `-1` and anything else containing a hyphen all collapse to -1 while `+`, `1` and an absent column fall to 1. A port could honour one spelling and reject the other, and only this line forbids that. It is absent for the same reason as n=7 rather than a weaker one: with no input-strand field at all (`VariantInput`, transcript_consequence.rs:15-27), there is nothing whose spelling could be normalised.

desc: stubby: the four-column form `21 25587759 25587759 C/A`, with strand and id both omitted, parses to strand 1 and a *synthesised* variation_name `21_25587759_C/A` built from chromosome, start and allele string
rationale: Two defaults in one comparison, and the second is a real construction rather than a fallback constant: validate_vf synthesises the name with `sprintf('%s_%i_%s', $vf->{original_chr} || $vf->{chr}, $vf->{start}, $vf->{allele_string} || $vf->{class_SO_term})` (Parser.pm:462-467 @ release/116.0) whenever the input supplied none. vepyr never faces the question. A VCF row's ID column is read as data and surfaces as a CSQ field, never invented: there is no naming rule to compare against, and the nearest-sounding vepyr symbol, `variation_name_idx` (annotate_provider.rs:5728), reads an existing column rather than filling an empty one. Distinct from n=6, which supplies the id explicitly, so a port could pass n=6 and still have no synthesis rule.

desc: SV dup: `21 25587759 25587769 DUP + test` parses to a StructuralVariationFeature — not a VariationFeature — with class_SO_term duplication and no allele_string or map_weight, the class switch being triggered by the allele column containing no `/`
rationale: The first of seven rows on the structural branch, and the one that pins the trigger: `if($allele_string !~ /\//)` (Parser/VEP_input.pm:136 @ release/116.0) decides class by the *absence of a slash*, then get_SO_term (Parser.pm:663-728) resolves DUP through %SO_TERMS (imported at :71) to `duplication`. vepyr does carry structural-variant machinery — StructuralFeature and SvEventKind (transcript_consequence.rs:594-610), fed from a separate `structural` DataFusion table read column-by-column (annotate_provider.rs:5060-5132) — and it is not an analogue: its event vocabulary is `ablation|deletion|del`, `amplification|duplication|dup|amp`, `elongation|elongate`, `truncation|truncate` (annotate_provider.rs:7341-7348), i.e. SO *consequence* kinds, never derived from an input record. The input-side classifier is classify_variant (annotate_provider.rs:7321-7329), whose entire output vocabulary is insertion / deletion / SNV / substitution / indel. Missing feature: structural variants as input.

desc: SV inv: `21 25587759 25587769 INV + test` parses to a StructuralVariationFeature with class_SO_term inversion over the same span as n=10
rationale: Same branch as n=10 with a different SO term, and it earns a separate row because the term is what the assertion pins — a parser could resolve DUP and drop INV. `inversion` is the SV class with no vepyr representation whatever: `grep -rn 'inversion' src/` -> 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control `grep -rn 'duplication' src/` -> 45, and it is absent from both closed vocabularies, classify_variant's five outputs (annotate_provider.rs:7321-7329) and parse_sv_event_kind's four event kinds (:7341-7348). An inversion is neither an allele-shape class nor an ablation/amplification consequence, so there is nothing it could map onto even loosely.

desc: SV del 1: the bare token `DEL` in the allele column parses to class_SO_term deletion — a symbolic deletion over an 11 bp span carrying no allele_string, unlike a sequence-level REF/- pair
rationale: Makes the symbolic/sequence distinction explicit: the same English word `deletion` is what classify_variant returns for a VEP-minimised (ref, '-') pair (annotate_provider.rs:7324 @ dfbf 391f94bd), but that is a sequence-level fact about two allele strings, while this row asserts a *class assigned to a token that is not a sequence*. vepyr has only the first side — `grep -rniE '<DEL>|<DUP>|SVTYPE|symbolic' src/` -> 0 lines against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516 — so classifying this analog-port on the strength of the shared word would claim a boundary vepyr does not have. Paired with n=13, which asserts the same class through the angle-bracketed spelling.

desc: SV del 2: the VCF-style angle-bracketed spelling `<DEL>` yields exactly n=12's StructuralVariationFeature, so the brackets are stripped rather than treated as part of the type name
rationale: A normalisation rule, and the reason n=12 does not cover it: get_SO_term strips a leading `<` and trailing `>` and everything after a colon before the lookup (`$abbrev =~ s/\<|\>//g; $abbrev =~ s/\:.+//g`, Parser.pm:712-715 @ release/116.0), which is what lets VCF symbolic ALTs be pasted into VEP-input files unchanged. vepyr has no symbolic-allele vocabulary to normalise: the probe above returns 0 lines for `<DEL>` and `SVTYPE` alike, and its own ALT handling goes straight into vcf_to_vep_allele (allele.rs:296), which treats the string as a sequence and would trim `<DEL>` as if the angle brackets were bases. That is not a divergence to file as `failed` — vepyr is never handed such input, since it has no format in which this row's line could be written.

desc: SV CN0: the copy-number spelling `<CN0>` maps to class_SO_term deletion — zero copies is read as a loss, not as a generic copy-number event
rationale: The first of three rows on get_SO_term's copy-number branch, which is a small decision table rather than a lookup: `$type =~ /CN=?[0-9]/i` sets CNV, then `DEL if /^<?CN=?0>?$/` and `DUP if /^<?CN=?2>?$/` override it (Parser.pm:702-706 @ release/116.0), the diploid assumption being explicit in the comment on :703. So this row pins semantics — copy number zero *means* deletion — not merely a string mapping. vepyr has no copy-number concept at all: `grep -rn 'copy_number_variation' src/` -> 0 lines and `grep -rniE '<CN[0-9]>' src/` -> 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, against the positive control `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516, and neither closed vocabulary (classify_variant's five outputs, parse_sv_event_kind's four event kinds) has a slot for one.

desc: SV CN2: `<CN2>` maps to class_SO_term duplication — two copies above the diploid baseline is read as a gain
rationale: The second override in the same decision table (Parser.pm:706 @ release/116.0) and separately assertable from n=14: a port could implement the CN0 special case and let CN2 fall through to the generic CNV that n=16 asserts, and only this line forbids that. It is worth keeping in the denominator for a further reason — the mapping is a *modelling choice* a reimplementation could plausibly get wrong, since `<CN2>` is not self-evidently a duplication outside a diploid assumption. Absent at the pin for n=14's reason: no copy-number vocabulary exists, `grep -rniE '<CN[0-9]>' src/` -> 0 lines against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516.

desc: SV CN3: `<CN3>` falls past both overrides to class_SO_term copy_number_variation — the generic case, and the last assertion of the format block
rationale: Completes the copy-number table by pinning its default arm: any CN token that is neither 0 nor 2 keeps the CNV the first branch assigned (Parser.pm:702-706 @ release/116.0). Together n=14, n=15 and n=16 assert a three-way partition, which is why none of them is redundant. `copy_number_variation` is, with n=11's `inversion`, one of the two SO classes for which vepyr has no term anywhere: `grep -rn 'copy_number_variation' src/` -> 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd against the positive control `grep -rn 'duplication' src/` -> 45. Missing feature is the same as n=10's — structural variants as input — with the copy-number sub-vocabulary on top.

desc: skip VF that fails validation: given `21 foo bar C/A 1` then a well-formed row, the first next() drops the line whose start and end are not numbers and returns the second, whose start is 25587759
rationale: Pins the parser's default recovery policy at its coarsest edge: validate_vf's `looks_like_number` test (Parser.pm:475-480 @ release/116.0) rejects the row and next() recurses past it rather than aborting (Parser.pm:189). vepyr has no such stage because it has no such input: a VCF is read by datafusion-bio-format-vcf's VcfTableProvider (vcf_sink.rs:17, :1074) into typed Arrow columns, so a non-numeric POS fails at read time in another crate and never reaches a VEP-owned validator that could weigh it. The nearest-looking vepyr behaviour, a record that finds no cache match still being emitted, is a different property: nothing was rejected. Missing feature: a per-record input validator with a skip policy.

desc: dont skip VF that fails validation with dont_skip: with dont_skip => 1 the malformed row survives and its start comes back as the literal string `foo`, so the raw token is carried through unconverted rather than coerced or nulled
rationale: The option half of n=17, and the sharper of the two: n=17 shows the validator rejects, this shows the rejection is overridable *and* that overriding it hands downstream code an unvalidated string — `unless($self->validate_vf($vf) || $self->{dont_skip})` (Parser.pm:189 @ release/116.0), the flag read from the shortcut list added at :128. Neither half exists at the pin: `grep -rn 'dont_skip' src/` -> 0 lines against `grep -rn 'vcf' src/` -> 516, and dont_skip is in neither the 31-key DataFusion vocabulary nor AnnotateVcfConfig's 34 fields (vcf_sink.rs:381-456). It could not exist in the same shape either: vepyr's input start is an Arrow Int64 column — `batch.schema().index_of('start')` then `int64_at(start_col, row)` (annotate_provider.rs:10035-10041), and the declared input schema spells it `Field::new('start', DataType::Int64, false)` (:14173) — a type in which the string `foo` cannot be represented, so porting this would mean choosing a different behaviour rather than reproducing one. no-feature, not blocked-api: there is no private switch waiting to be exported.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the Runner module loads
rationale: RULING R2, docs/ledger-contract.md: a use_ok row is not-applicable unconditionally. It tests Perl's own loader — that require found Bio/EnsEMBL/VEP/Runner.pm, compiled it and ran its import. Rust performs no module load at runtime that could succeed or fail, so the assertion has no semantic counterpart in any Rust design. The absence it might be read as reporting is not lost: every row below that exercises an orchestrator behaviour vepyr lacks stays no-feature and counts the gap once.

desc: BASIC TESTS: Runner->new returns a defined object for base_testing_cfg plus input_data '21 25585733 25585733 C/T + rs142513484'
rationale: A constructor-truthiness probe, and what it constructs is a config, not the orchestrator.
