None of the orchestrator's work happens until init, which is n=15. Under the ok($obj) denotation table that is the first row: an object whose Rust analogue is an infallible struct literal. `AnnotateVcfConfig` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:381-456, Default at :457) is built by literal initialisation and cannot yield a null, so the compiler carries at compile time what this line checks at run time. Same line, same reasoning as ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=1 and ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=3.

desc: BASIC TESTS: the object new returned is blessed into Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Runner
rationale: RULING R1, first bullet: the construction already carries its own row — n=2, two lines above — so all this line adds is Perl object identity, which docs/ledger-contract.md lists as not-applicable and which n=2 has already accounted for. The R1 fallback (decide the readback by denotation, because it is the ledger's only accounting for the construction) does not apply here.

desc: METHOD TESTS: get_all_AnnotationSources returns exactly one source — a Cache::Transcript compared attribute by attribute (cache_region_size 1000000, source_type 'ensembl', the 13-key info registry, valid_chromosomes [21,22,LRG_485], and eleven undef mode flags)
rationale: VEP's runner owns an enumerable LIST of annotation sources, assembled from the mode flags by AnnotationSourceAdaptor, and this line compares the list and the whole object in it. vepyr has no such list to return. Its entire run-level public surface is one function: `grep -n '^pub fn \|^pub async fn ' vcf_sink.rs` at dfbf 391f94bd returns exactly one line, `vcf_sink.rs:1018 pub async fn annotate_to_vcf`, which takes `cache_source: &str` plus `backend: &str` and wires its providers internally; nothing hands back what it wired. Absent feature: an enumerable, inspectable annotation-source list. This is no-feature and not deferred/blocked-api under the contract's absent-vs-private test, which asks whether the OPERATION exists: 'return the configured sources' is an operation vepyr never performs, not state it holds behind a missing pub. Four of the compared attributes have no counterpart at any visibility either — `serializer_type`, `nearest`, `bam` and the `info` registry (see n=13).

desc: METHOD TESTS: setup_db_connection is a silent no-op returning false when the run is offline
rationale: The database adaptor layer, which docs/ledger-contract.md names as a standing no-feature for this corpus: vepyr is cache-only by design and has no DB mode for this line to observe being switched off. Measured over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at dfbf 391f94bd (`grep -rEn --include='*.rs' -c`): `mysql` 0, `DBI\b` 0, `ensembldb` 0, `db_host` 0, `species` 0 — positive controls over the identical tree: `plugin` 304, `hgvs` 1068. There is no connection to set up and no offline/online distinction to make, because every vepyr run is what VEP calls offline. Rows 102-106 are the same absence observed from the other side, inside the file's DATABASE TESTS SKIP block.

desc: METHOD TESTS: valid_chromosomes reports the three contigs the cache declares — 21, 22 and LRG_485
rationale: Same property, different observation point. VEP reads the contig set out of the cache's info.txt and re-exports it on the runner (`Runner::valid_chromosomes` delegates to the annotation source), where it gates input records — the same set produces the 'Chromosome chr402 not found in annotation sources or synonyms' rejection this file asserts at n=45. vepyr keeps the set on the cache rather than on the orchestrator, and exposes it publicly: `PartitionedParquetCache::available_chroms` (dfbf 391f94bd parquet_cache/detect.rs:50) returns the contigs of the variation `chrom_manifest.json`, and `variation_path` (:55) is the resolver that answers 'is this contig in the cache' with the chr-prefix and M/MT alias folding of `contig_alias_set` (cache/manifest.rs:121). The named test builds a three-entry manifest in a TempDir, asserts the same expected value [21, 22, LRG_485] in the same order, and adds the chr402 negative arm with a positive control so a broken resolver cannot pass by returning None for everything. Different fixture (a synthetic manifest, not upstream's t/testdata cache) and a different accessor, hence analog-port and not unit-port.

desc: METHOD TESTS: get_Parser returns a Parser::VEP_input wired from the config — 13 attributes including delimiter ' ', max_sv_size 10000000 and the valid_chromosomes lookup hash
rationale: Two absences at once, and either alone decides the row. First, the class: the object is a Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Parser::VEP_input, the reader for VEP's own space-delimited default format (`21 25585733 25585733 C/T + rs142513484`, perl/Runner.t:36). vepyr reads VCF and nothing else — its input path is `VcfTableProvider` over the file `annotate_to_vcf` is handed (vcf_sink.rs:1018), with no format dispatch to choose another reader; ledger/Parser_VEP_input.ledger.toml carries the format itself. Second, the shape: this is a whole-object comparison, and vepyr has no parser object with settable attributes to compare — `max_sv_size` and `dont_skip` have no counterpart in the 34 public fields of `AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:381-456). Absent feature: a pluggable input-format parser the orchestrator constructs and exposes.

desc: METHOD TESTS: get_InputBuffer returns an InputBuffer holding the same Parser object plus buffer_size, minimal and the two unsorted-input guards (max_not_ordered_variants 100, distance 100)
rationale: A whole-object comparison over an object graph — buffer wrapping parser — that vepyr does not build. One field of the five IS present and public: `AnnotateVcfConfig::buffer_size` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:438), and ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml n=13 defers on observing its EFFECT rather than on reaching the knob. The other four are absent at every visibility: `minimal` allele-trimming mode, and the unsorted-input guards `max_not_ordered_variants` / `max_not_ordered_variants_distance`, whose job — tolerating a mis-sorted input stream — vepyr's per-contig, position-ordered scan does not have (`workers > 1` even refuses an input that is not tabix-indexed, vcf_sink.rs:1042-1052). What makes the row a gap rather than a Perl artefact is that it compares a whole object, and there is no vepyr object to compare: the accumulator holds three fields (annotate_provider.rs:9522-9526) and the config holds thirty-four (vcf_sink.rs:381-456), and neither is the buffer this line inspects. Same reading as ledger/InputBuffer.ledger.toml's post-reset whole-object row.

desc: METHOD TESTS: get_output_header_info carries a `time` key — the run timestamp VEP stamps into the output header
rationale: First of the five rows (n=9-13) that observe VEP's output-header self-description, the hash BaseRunner.pm:395-430 assembles and OutputFactory formats into the `##VEP=` / `## Run on` header block. vepyr emits no such block: at dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rn '##VEP' src` and `grep -rn 'VEP=' src` each return 0 lines, against 171 lines matching `CSQ` as the positive control — the measurement ledger/version.ledger.toml n=2 records, reached independently there. The only header line vepyr writes about itself is the CSQ INFO description, `Consequence annotations from annotate_vep. Format: ...` (`csq_header_description`, vcf_sink.rs:660-681), which carries the field layout and no run metadata at all. Absent feature: run-provenance metadata in the output header.

desc: METHOD TESTS: get_output_header_info carries an integer `api_version` — the Ensembl Core API release the run linked against
rationale: The same absent header block as n=9, and additionally a version this stack does not have: `api_version` is `$self->registry->software_version` (BaseRunner.pm:405), the Ensembl Registry's own release number. vepyr has no Ensembl API to report — measured at dfbf 391f94bd, `mysql` 0, `DBI\b` 0, `ensembldb` 0 lines over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src (positive controls `plugin` 304, `hgvs` 1068) — because it reads a converted cache rather than talking to the Ensembl schema. Absent feature: the output header's record of which Ensembl API produced the run.

desc: METHOD TESTS: get_output_header_info carries a `vep_version` matching /^\d+(\.\d+)?$/ — the release of the VEP software doing the run
rationale: The self-description identity row, and the one where a near-miss has to be ruled out explicitly. vepyr's release identity is Cargo's (`datafusion-bio-function-vep 0.15.0` at the pin) and it never reaches the output. The tempting analogue, `SUPPORTED_VEP_TARGETS` (vep_semantics.rs:44-61) with its `vep_codebase_version = "115.2"` / `"116.0"`, was ALREADY ADJUDICATED and rejected for exactly this kind of row: ledger/version.ledger.toml n=2 and n=3 record that the matrix is keyed by CACHE version and declares which Ensembl releases the engine can CONSUME, never which release the engine IS, so it could not fail if vepyr's self-description regressed. This ledger follows that adjudication rather than reopening it. Absent feature: a self-reported software release in the output.

desc: METHOD TESTS: get_output_header_info carries `input_headers` as an ARRAY — the input file's own header lines, kept for echoing into the output
rationale: `input_headers` is `$self->get_Parser->headers` (BaseRunner.pm:406) — VEP collects the input's header lines into the runner's self-description hash so the output writer can replay them. Read narrowly this is a Perl reference-type probe, but what it pins down is the header-info structure's fourth slot, and that structure is what vepyr lacks (n=9). Note what is NOT the argument: vepyr does propagate the input's header, but by a different mechanism and without any hash to inspect — the output schema is built with the input's merged metadata (vcf_sink.rs:1215) and `write_header` is called from the writer (:1301, :1322, :1385), so there is no intermediate object holding a list of header lines for a test to observe the type of. Absent feature: the header-info structure itself; the pass-through it feeds survives, but not as state the orchestrator exposes.

desc: METHOD TESTS: get_output_header_info merges the cache's 13-key info registry into version_data — sift 5.2.2, polyphen 2.2.2, gencode GENCODE 24, dbSNP 149, assembly GRCh38.p5 and eight more
rationale: The payload of the header block: a component-keyed registry of the data versions the run used, merged from every annotation source's `info` (BaseRunner.pm:415-424) and formatted into the output header by OutputFactory. vepyr carries cache identity but not a registry, and not as anything a run reports: `ValidatedCacheIdentity` (cache_identity.rs:37-41) holds three fields — `cache_source_type`, `cache_version` and a `&SupportedVepTarget` — and exists to ACCEPT or REJECT a cache against `AnnotateVcfConfig::expected_cache_version` (vcf_sink.rs:403-404), not to describe it downstream. Nothing at the pin reads a cache info.txt into per-component versions: the assembly, the dbSNP build and the GENCODE release the cache was built from are not recoverable from any vepyr output. Absent feature: provenance of the annotation data in the emitted file. Same verdict and same reasoning as ledger/version.ledger.toml n=2.

desc: METHOD TESTS: get_OutputFactory returns a VEP_output factory whose complete default option hash matches, key for key
rationale: Unchanged between 115.2 and 116.0. This row carried `vep116_delta = "changed"` while the corpus was pinned to 116.1, where `@@ -193,6 +193,7 @@` of t/Runner.t inserts `'protein_version' => undef` into the expected hash — the only occurrence of that key anywhere in t/ at 116.1. The corpus now targets **116.0**, which does not carry the insertion: `grep -rn 'protein_version' perl/` returns nothing (positive control on the same tree and the same command shape: `grep -c 'pick_order' perl/Runner.t` prints 1, and `grep -c 'OutputFactory' perl/Runner.t` prints 3 -- so the empty result above is an absence and not a grep that read nothing), and the vendored file's sha256 is the 116.0 digest recorded in docs/campaigns/2026-08-31-vep-116-0-retarget/audit.md §2. The assertion count is unmoved either way — 107 at both releases — because the release edited a line inside one is_deeply rather than adding an assertion. WHAT THE ROW PINS is unaffected by any of that: VEP's runner BUILDS an OutputFactory and populates its option set from the config, so the assertion is that the derivation produced these values. vepyr has no derivation step — `AnnotateVcfConfig` is supplied by the caller and consumed directly by `annotate_to_vcf`, and there is no output-factory object between them. The option vocabularies are not comparable either: 34 public fields (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) against this hash's dozens of keys. Absent feature: a configured output-formatter object the orchestrator derives and exposes.

desc: init: the orchestrator's whole setup phase — DB connection, plugins, annotation sources, chromosome synonyms, FASTA db, input buffer, post_setup_checks, stats — completes and returns true
rationale: Ported against the committed chr21 micro-cache of #96, which is what #198 was waiting for. vepyr has no separable init and no `_initialized` flag: `annotate_to_vcf` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:1018) validates the config, resolves the cache source type from the cache's own schema metadata, builds the concurrency plan and constructs the providers inside the call (`:1019-1053`). The setup phase is still observable at a boundary of its own, because it produces the writer and its HEADER before any variant is annotated — measured independently by tests/annotate_end_to_end_smoke.rs::a_missing_reference_fasta_is_refused_by_name, where the header is written and the scan then fails. So the analogue asserts what setup produced: the emitted header is the input's two meta-lines plus exactly one added `##INFO=<ID=CSQ…>` whose `Format:` list is the pin's default 74-slot layout, head pinned at Allele|Consequence|IMPACT|SYMBOL|Gene|Feature_type|Feature|BIOTYPE|EXON|INTRON|HGVSc|HGVSp|cDNA_position|CDS_position|Protein_position|Amino_acids|Codons|Existing_variation|DISTANCE|STRAND — the twenty slots every output-line assertion in this file reads. The failing arm is the positive control: `expected_cache_version = "116"` against the 115 shards is refused with `cache version assertion failed for contig '21': embedded bio.vep.cache_version=115, expected 116` and annotates nothing, so `Ok` is not vacuous. Not a claim on the whole of init: `setup_db_connection` (n=5), the plugin list (n=59-70) and the stats handles (n=29-37) stay no-feature and are not exercised.

desc: _buffer_to_output: one buffered variant yields three VEP-tab lines — ENST00000307301 3_prime_UTR_variant at cDNA 1122, ENST00000352957 missense_variant A/T Gca/Aca at cDNA 1033 / CDS 991 / protein 331, and ENST00000567517 upstream_gene_variant at DISTANCE=2407
rationale: The annotation content itself, ported against #96's committed chr21 micro-cache — the fixture #198 named as the blocker. vepyr has no `_buffer_to_output` and no VEP-tab writer, but every field this line projects is a named slot of the CSQ string (`csq_field_names_for_mode_with_pick`, golden_benchmark.rs:661), and the Perl's first three columns (Uploaded_variation, Location, Allele) are the emitted row's own ID/CHROM+POS and the CSQ `Allele` field — all asserted. Two places the v115 fixture disagrees with VEP's v84-era test cache are named rather than papered over. (1) FOURTEEN consequence groups, not three: the Perl's three transcripts plus eleven MRPL39 models Ensembl added since, listed exactly in the test as EXTRA_V115_TRANSCRIPTS so the count is inventoried and not widened to `>= 3`. (2) ENST00000352957's cDNA position is 997, not the Perl's 1033; CDS 991, protein 331, A/T and Gca/Aca all match exactly. That single difference is proved to be the fixture's transcript model and not vepyr arithmetic by a second test in the same file, `cdna_position_follows_the_committed_shards_utr_length`, which reads `cdna_coding_start` out of the committed transcript shard (7) and checks 991 + 7 - 1 = 997; VEP's 1033 implies cdna_coding_start = 43. DISTANCE=2407 survives the cache change and is checked against the shard's own end coordinate for ENST00000567517 (25585733 - 25583326). Mutation-checked: restoring the Perl literal 1033 fails, as does poisoning the shard-derived control.

desc: next_output_line: a freshly constructed runner's first call returns the first of the three lines n=16 asserts — the per-line iterator, not the whole buffer
rationale: The same content as n=16 through the streaming accessor rather than the buffer-at-a-time one, so what it adds is the ORDER consequences leave the runner in: ENST00000307301 before ENST00000352957 before ENST00000567517. vepyr has no line-at-a-time public iterator — `annotate_to_vcf` writes a file and returns a row count — but the order survives into the CSQ string, whose groups are emitted in one deterministic sequence, so the analogue reads the FIRST group of the emitted row (Feature, Consequence, Allele, cDNA_position, IMPACT, STRAND) and then the whole emitted sequence. Measured against the committed micro-cache, that sequence is ascending stable_id, which is what makes the row falsifiable rather than incidental: it puts the MODIFIER 3-prime-UTR call BEFORE the MODERATE missense one, so a runner that ordered by consequence severity — the ordering VEP itself applies under --pick — would emit ENST00000352957 first and fail here. n=16 does not look at order at all, which is the boundary that separates the two rows. Mutation-checked: swapping the first two expected transcripts fails.

desc: output file: get_output_file_handle opens the configured output_file and returns a FileHandle
rationale: The assertion's subject is the CLASS of the Perl handle object, which docs/ledger-contract.md lists as not-applicable (blessing / Perl object identity). The behaviour the line accompanies is present in vepyr and is accounted for elsewhere: `annotate_to_vcf(input_vcf, cache_source, backend, output_vcf, config)` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:1018) creates and writes that path, and n=46/n=48 are the rows that observe it. What vepyr does not do is HAND BACK the stream — the path is the interface, so there is no object whose class a test could assert. Contrast n=19-21 and n=27-28, which are no-feature: there the subject is a behaviour of the handle (an overwrite guard, a stdout destination, an external compressor) that vepyr does not have at all, not the handle's Perl class.

desc: output file: a second get_output_file_handle on an existing output path throws 'Output file ... already exists', the guard --force_overwrite lifts
rationale: VEP refuses to clobber an existing output unless `--force_overwrite` is given. vepyr has no such guard and no such flag: `AnnotateVcfConfig`'s 34 public fields (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) contain neither, and the writer opens through `File::create`, which truncates — measured at dfbf 391f94bd, `grep -rEn --include='*.rs' -i 'already exists|force_overwrite|create_new'` over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src matches only cache/build.rs (`:112`, `:311`, `:364`, `:566-664`), the CACHE BUILDER's own overwrite handling, and never the output writer (positive control: `File::create` resolves at parquet_cache/scan.rs:55, plugin_cache/write.rs:54 and three more sites). Absent feature: destructive-write protection on the annotated output. Same shape as the sibling guards this file tests at n=31 (stats file) and n=40 (skipped-variants file).

desc: output file: output_file => 'stdout' resolves to the *main::STDOUT glob instead of opening a file
rationale: VEP treats the literal string `stdout` as a destination and writes the annotated output to standard output — the mode the REST and pipe use-cases depend on. vepyr has no stream destination: `annotate_to_vcf` takes `output_vcf: &str` and opens it as a path (vcf_sink.rs:1018), and measured over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rn --include='*.rs' -c 'stdout'` returns 0 while `plugin` returns 304 and `hgvs` 1068 over the identical tree. Absent feature: writing the annotated output to a stream rather than to a named file. Rows 27 and 28 are the same absence under `compress_output`.

desc: output file: an unknown compress_output value throws 'not found in path' — VEP resolves the compressor as an external binary before writing
rationale: What the line pins down is the DISPATCH: VEP's `compress_output` names a program (`gzip`, `bgzip`) that must exist on PATH, so an unknown value fails at handle-open time with a path lookup error. vepyr compresses in process and can express no such failure — its `AnnotateVcfConfig::compression` is a `VcfCompressionType` enum (vcf_sink.rs:445), so an unknown value is a compile error and there is no PATH to search; measured at dfbf 391f94bd, `compress_output` matches 0 lines over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src, and the crate spawns no subprocess (`std::process::Command` 0 lines, the measurement ledger/version.ledger.toml n=1 records) against 23 lines matching `gzip` as the positive control that compression itself is present. Absent feature: an external-compressor dispatch, and with it the whole class of errors it can raise.

desc: gzip block: the Utils module loads, so its CAN_USE_GZIP flag can gate the four compressed-output assertions
rationale: RULING R2, docs/ledger-contract.md: use_ok is not-applicable unconditionally, whatever the class denotes and whether or not it sits inside a SKIP block. Rust performs no runtime module load. The R2 corollary settles the SKIP question here too: the block below guards on `$Bio::EnsEMBL::VEP::Utils::CAN_USE_GZIP`, a Perl-environment condition (is gzip on PATH), not on a feature vepyr lacks — and this probe's subject is Perl's loader in any case, not compression.

desc: gzip block: get_output_file_handle with compress_output => 'gzip' returns a FileHandle for the .gz destination
rationale: The compressed sibling of n=18, and it is decided the same way: the subject is the class of the Perl handle object, which the contract lists as not-applicable, while the behaviour it accompanies — a compressed output file being opened for writing — is present in vepyr through `AnnotateVcfConfig::compression` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:445) and is accounted for by n=24-26, which assert what the handle produces rather than what it is. vepyr exposes no writer object at all: `VcfLocalWriter` is constructed inside `annotate_to_vcf` and never returned.

desc: gzip block: writing through the compressed handle actually creates the .out.gz file on disk
rationale: First of the three rows (n=24-26) that assert the compressed output is real. Nothing here needed a new pub — `AnnotateVcfConfig::compression` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:445) selects `VcfCompressionType::{Plain,Gzip,Bgzf}` from datafusion-bio-format-vcf, a dev-dependency of this crate — and the fixture #198 recorded as missing is now committed (#96). VEP takes the file HANDLE out of the runner and prints through it; vepyr exposes no handle (that is n=23, not-applicable) and puts the compressor at the end of the real writer, so the analogue's counterpart of `-e $compressed_file` is a completed run whose output path exists, is non-empty, reports the row it wrote, and begins with the gzip magic — an empty or truncated file would satisfy `-e` alone. The second half is the sharper half: the same compression into a destination named `annotated.vcf`, with no .gz on it, still yields a gzip stream, so what is under test is the config field and not the filename. Mutation-checked: flipping the run to `Plain` fails on the magic (left: [35, 35], i.e. `##`).

desc: gzip block: the file the compressed handle wrote is binary (-B), i.e. really compressed and not plain text with a .gz name
rationale: The assertion that distinguishes a working compressor from a misnamed plain file, and the one a naive port most easily drops: a writer that ignored compress_output entirely would still pass n=24. Ported against #96's committed cache through `AnnotateVcfConfig::compression` -> `VcfLocalWriter::with_compression` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:445, writer construction at :319 and :1300). Perl's `-B` is a heuristic; the analogue states it twice and mechanically — the first two bytes are the RFC 1952 gzip magic 1f 8b, and the bytes are not valid UTF-8, which is the closest exact form of `-B` for a writer whose uncompressed output is text. The POSITIVE CONTROL is what makes the word mean something: the identical run at `VcfCompressionType::Plain` IS valid UTF-8 and starts `##fileformat=`, so `is_err()` is a statement about compression and not about this crate's writer in general, and the two writers' leading bytes are asserted different. Mutation-checked: 0x8b -> 0x8c fails with left: [31, 139].

desc: gzip block: `gzip -dc` on the written file recovers exactly the line that was printed to the handle — the compressed stream round-trips
rationale: The round trip that makes n=24 and n=25 mean something. `gzip -dc` becomes an in-process `flate2::read::MultiGzDecoder` — flate2 is already a dev-dependency, so the test needs no external binary and stays standalone (docs/ledger-contract.md §8). The round-trip SUBJECT changes and the change strengthens the row: VEP prints `Hello world` through a handle that never met the annotator, whereas vepyr has no handle to print through, so the analogue round-trips the annotated output itself and compares it against the same run at `VcfCompressionType::Plain` — header, CSQ declaration, data row and all. `MultiGzDecoder` rather than `GzDecoder` is deliberate: a member-per-batch writer would produce a multi-member stream that GzDecoder silently truncates at the first member, and silent truncation is exactly the failure this row guards; the line-count equality asserted before the text equality is what would catch it. The recovered row is then checked to be the annotated variant (`21 25585733 rs142513484 C T` carrying CSQ=T|3_prime_UTR_variant|...|ENST00000307301|) so the comparison cannot be two empty files agreeing. The in-src `gunzip_to_string` test at vcf_sink.rs:1635 is still not claimable in rust_test (docs/ledger-contract.md) and is not claimed. Mutation-checked: dropping one recovered line fails with left: 4.

desc: gzip block: output_file => 'stdout' together with compress_output => 'gzip' still yields a FileHandle — a compressed stream to standard output
rationale: Not the handle-class row that n=23 is: what this line pins down is the COMBINATION, compressing straight into standard output, which is why it sits in its own Capture::Tiny block. vepyr has neither half of the destination — `grep -rn --include='*.rs' -c 'stdout'` over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at dfbf 391f94bd returns 0 (positive controls `plugin` 304, `hgvs` 1068), and `annotate_to_vcf` opens `output_vcf` as a path (vcf_sink.rs:1018) — so the configuration this line asserts is accepted cannot be expressed at all. Absent feature: a compressed output stream, as opposed to a compressed output file.

desc: gzip block: bytes actually reached standard output through the compressed stdout handle (the Capture::Tiny stdout buffer is non-empty)
rationale: The payload half of n=27: not just that a handle came back, but that writing to it put compressed bytes on standard output. vepyr has no stream destination to put them on — `annotate_to_vcf` opens `output_vcf` as a path (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:1018) and `grep -rn --include='*.rs' -c 'stdout'` over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src returns 0 (positive controls over the identical tree: `plugin` 304, `hgvs` 1068). Absent feature: writing the annotated output to standard output, compressed or not.

desc: stats file: get_stats_file_handle('txt') opens <output_file>_summary.txt and returns a FileHandle
rationale: First of the nine rows (n=29-37) on VEP's run-statistics subsystem: it counts variants, consequence types, per-chromosome distributions and timings during the run and dumps them to a text and an HTML summary beside the output. The whole subsystem is absent from vepyr, and the measurement is already committed in this repository: audit/ports-compile-status.md's Stats.t verdict records that at dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rniE '\bstats\b' src/` returns 2 hits over the whole crate, both unrelated (a cache-BUILD `EntityStats` at cache_builder.rs:135 and a doc comment at cache/lookup_exec.rs:751), while `grep -rniE 'no_stats|summary_html|stats_file|dump_html|dump_text|StatsReport|RunStats' src/` returns 0 — positive controls 19 for `vcf_sink` and 237 for `pub fn`. `annotate_to_vcf` returns a row count and nothing else. ledger/Stats.ledger.toml classifies all 29 of its own rows the same way, and its port stays quarantined for the same reason. Absent feature: run statistics.

desc: stats file: asking for the txt handle creates <output_file>.out_summary.txt on disk as a side effect
rationale: That the summary file is created eagerly, at handle-open time — VEP does this deliberately, in init (Runner.pm:145-149), so a run does not discover at the very end that it cannot write its summary. vepyr writes no summary at any time (measurement in n=29), so there is no file to create and no eager-open policy to observe. Absent feature: the statistics summary file.

desc: stats file: a second get_stats_file_handle('txt') over an existing summary throws 'Stats file ... already exists'
rationale: The overwrite guard on the summary file — the same policy n=19 asserts for the output and n=40 for the skipped-variants sidecar. Two absences compose here and either decides the row: vepyr has no summary file (n=29) and no destructive-write protection anywhere (n=19's measurement: the only `already exists` errors at dfbf 391f94bd are in cache/build.rs, the cache builder). Absent feature: the statistics summary file, and with it its overwrite guard.

desc: stats file: get_stats_file_handle('html') opens the HTML summary and returns a FileHandle — the same accessor dispatching on format
rationale: The HTML arm of n=29, and the one that shows the subsystem is a REPORT GENERATOR and not just a counter dump: VEP renders the same statistics as a standalone HTML page with embedded charts. vepyr produces neither format — `summary_html` and `dump_html` both match 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd (n=29's measurement). Absent feature: the HTML statistics report.

desc: stats file: asking for the html handle creates <output_file>.out_summary.html on disk
rationale: The HTML arm of n=30 — eager creation of the report file at handle-open time. Same absence: vepyr writes no summary in either format (n=29). Absent feature: the HTML statistics report file.

desc: stats file: extension handling 1 — stats_file '<user_file>.stats' plus format txt yields '<user_file>.stats.txt' (the format extension is appended)
rationale: First of four rows (n=34-37) pinning VEP's stats-filename rule, which is not a plain concatenation: an explicit --stats_file keeps its own stem and gains the format's extension unless it already ends in one. It is worth four assertions because getting it wrong silently writes the HTML report over the text one. vepyr has no --stats_file and no summary to name (n=29): `stats_file` matches 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd. Absent feature: the statistics summary file, and with it its naming rule.

desc: stats file: extension handling 2 — stats_file '<user_file>.txt' plus format txt keeps '<user_file>.txt' and does not become '.txt.txt'

desc: stats file: extension handling 3 — the same stats_file '<user_file>.txt' asked for html yields '<user_file>.html', i.e. the extension is replaced, not appended

desc: stats file: extension handling 4 — a stats_file with no extension at all, '<user_file>_stats', yields '<user_file>_stats.txt'

desc: skipped-variants sidecar: get_skipped_variants_file_handle opens the configured skipped_variants_file and returns a FileHandle
rationale: First of the eight rows (n=38-45) on VEP's skipped-variants sidecar: a second output file listing every input record the run could not annotate, with the line number, the record and the reason. It is the audit trail that makes a partial run trustworthy. vepyr has no such file — `skipped_variants` matches 0 lines over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at dfbf 391f94bd (positive controls `plugin` 304, `hgvs` 1068) — and, as n=42 measures, no record-skipping policy for it to record: a malformed record ends the scan. Absent feature: the skipped-variants sidecar.

desc: skipped-variants sidecar: asking for the handle creates <user_file>_skipped.txt on disk
rationale: Eager creation at handle-open time, the same policy as n=30 and for the same reason — a run should not discover at the end that its audit trail is unwritable. vepyr writes no sidecar at any time (n=38). Absent feature: the skipped-variants sidecar file.

desc: skipped-variants sidecar: a second get_skipped_variants_file_handle over an existing sidecar throws 'Skipped variants file ... already exists'
rationale: The third overwrite guard in this file (with n=19 for the output and n=31 for the summary), and it composes two absences: no sidecar (n=38) and no destructive-write protection anywhere in vepyr (n=19's measurement — at dfbf 391f94bd the only `already exists` errors are cache/build.rs's, in the cache builder). Absent feature: the skipped-variants sidecar, and with it its overwrite guard.

desc: skipped-variants sidecar: with force_overwrite => 1 the same path is reopened and the run proceeds instead of throwing
rationale: The lifting arm of n=40 — the guard is a policy the user can switch off, not a hard refusal. vepyr has neither the guard nor the flag: `force_overwrite` matches 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, and none of the 34 public fields of `AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) expresses it. Absent feature: the skipped-variants sidecar and its force-overwrite escape.

desc: skipped-variants sidecar: run() completes and returns true over a 13-record input of which three are malformed — a bad POS, an unknown contig and an invalid allele
rationale: vepyr cannot complete this run, and the failure is provable without the v115 cache the rest of this ledger is blocked on, because the input scan precedes annotation. VEP treats a bad data line as a RECORD-level problem — warn, drop, continue; vepyr's `VcfTableProvider` scan treats it as a QUERY-level one. An earlier, out-of-tree run of the same measurement on two-record subsets is kept below because it isolates each defect: `a_clean_only: OK rows=2` / `b_runner_t_pos123: COLLECT ERR: Execution error: VCF position error: invalid digit found in string` / `c_runner_t_bad_allele: OK rows=2` / `d_runner_t_unknown_contig: OK rows=2`. `a_clean_only` is the positive control — the identical harness over the same two well-formed records returns them — and in `b` those two records are lost along with `21 pos123` (perl/Runner.t:435). So the assertion is not merely unported: what it asserts is false of vepyr. Same divergence as ledger/Parser_VCF.ledger.toml n=19 and n=77, and the measurement above is recorded on that issue. Two further observations from the same run are NOT claimed as divergences, because what happens to them downstream needs the cache: vepyr's reader accepts both the `Z/Y` allele (VEP: 'Invalid allele string Z/Y or possible parsing error') and contig `chr402` (VEP: 'Chromosome chr402 not found in annotation sources or synonyms'). Fails at the current pin; the test's `issue:` line names the tracker.

desc: skipped-variants sidecar: the run writes at least one WARNING to the configured warning destination while skipping records
rationale: The live half of the audit trail: as VEP drops a record it warns on the warning stream, so a user watching a terminal sees the loss happen rather than discovering it in a sidecar afterwards. Two absences, and either decides the row. The destination: --warning_file has no counterpart — ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=34 measures `warning_file` at 0 occurrences in dfbf 0.15.0's vep crate and 0 in vepyr 346b9173 (positive controls `fasta` 63 and 15), and vepyr emits through `log` with no per-run destination to open. The content: there are no skipped records to warn about, because a malformed record ends the scan instead of being dropped (n=42, measured). Absent feature: per-record skip warnings.

desc: skipped-variants sidecar: the finished file has exactly 4 lines — one header plus one entry for each of the three records the run dropped
rationale: The count that pins WHICH records VEP considers unusable: three of thirteen, so the ten remaining — including the symbolic <DEL> at line 2 and the duplicate rs867018739 at lines 6 and 7 — were annotated. It is a statement about the skip POLICY, not just about a file. vepyr has neither the file (n=38) nor the policy: measured in n=42, the bad-POS record aborts the whole scan while the invalid allele and the unknown contig are accepted, so vepyr's set of unusable records is neither this one nor a subset of it. Absent feature: the skipped-variants sidecar and the record-level skip policy it reports.

desc: skipped-variants sidecar: the three entries name the input line, the record and the reason — 'Invalid start pos123 or end 0 coordinate' (line 3), 'Chromosome chr402 not found in annotation sources or synonyms' (line 5), 'Invalid allele string Z/Y' (line 6)
rationale: The most specific row of the sidecar block: not just that records were dropped but that each carries a machine-locatable line number and a human-readable cause. vepyr produces no such report and, measured in n=42, does not agree about the causes either — its reader accepts both `chr402` and `Z/Y` (`OK rows=2` in each case, against the `a_clean_only` positive control) and turns `pos123` into a scan-wide `Execution error: VCF position error: invalid digit found in string` with no line number and no surviving records. Absent feature: per-record diagnostics for input VEP cannot use. Note where the chr402 case IS accounted for on the vepyr side: n=6's analogue asserts that an undeclared contig does not resolve to a cache shard.

desc: run method: run() returns true for the default configuration — init, write the header, drain next_output_line into the output file, finish
rationale: The whole orchestrator in one assertion, now runnable: the fixture #198 named as its blocker is committed (tests/data/vep115_parquet_micro_cache, #96). vepyr's counterpart to `run` returning true is `annotate_to_vcf` returning `Ok(usize)` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:1018), and the analogue is more than an exit code — the reported count is compared against the rows that reached the file, the written row is checked to carry a real CSQ group (ENST00000307301) rather than an untouched INFO column, and an eight-record control run reports eight, so a constant cannot satisfy both. Distinct from n=15, which asserts what SETUP produced (the header and its CSQ layout) and whose second arm passes over a run that annotates nothing; this row fails if the drain writes the wrong number of rows or the return value disagrees with the file, neither of which n=15 observes. The input is `perl/Runner.t:36`'s own `21 25585733 C/T rs142513484` and is well formed in every column, so the scan-level abort pinned at n=42 (tests/port_runner_input_scan.rs) is not engaged. The quarantined tests/_quarantine/port_runner.rs is still not named: its file does not link (see this ledger's header).

desc: run method: the output file has exactly 41 lines — the 3 data lines n=48 asserts plus a 38-line VEP-tab header block
rationale: Read together with n=48, which greps out everything matching /^#/ and finds 3 lines, this row's unique content is the SIZE OF THE HEADER BLOCK: 41 - 3 = 38 lines of `##` metadata. That block is VEP-tab's, and vepyr writes none of it — no `##VEP=`, no `## Run on`, no per-column description list (`grep -rn '##VEP' src` returns 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd against 171 for `CSQ`; the only self-description vepyr emits is the single CSQ INFO line, `csq_header_description`, vcf_sink.rs:660-681). vepyr's output is a VCF, so its header is the input's plus one INFO line, and no count of it could be compared with 41. The annotation content is separately carried by n=48, which is deferred rather than absent. Absent feature: the VEP tab-delimited output format and its header block.

desc: run method: the three non-header output lines are the same three consequences as n=16 — 3_prime_UTR_variant, missense_variant with A/T Gca/Aca, and upstream_gene_variant at DISTANCE=2407 — now read back off disk
rationale: The row's content over n=16 is that NOTHING IS LOST OR REORDERED between the annotation buffer and the output; the Perl gets that by reading n=16's lines back off disk. vepyr has only one observation point — the emitted VCF — so restating n=16's content off the file would be the same assertion twice, which docs/ledger-contract.md forbids. The distinctive half is ported instead, through the knob that makes a buffer boundary visible from outside: `AnnotateVcfConfig::buffer_size` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:437, default 5000) is the analogue of VEP's --buffer_size, and if anything were dropped, duplicated or reordered on the drain path the number of drains would change the file. Measured over an eight-record chr21 input inside the committed cache's transcript window: buffer_size 1, 2, 3, 5 and 5000 — one variant per buffer up to all eight in one — give BYTE-IDENTICAL output, 24734 bytes each, and the test then re-reads perl/Runner.t:36's variant off that output so the invariance is over real consequences (ENST00000307301 3_prime_UTR_variant, ENST00000352957 missense_variant, ENST00000567517 upstream_gene_variant) and not over an empty file, plus the eight POS values in input order. The analogue's one liberty is varying a buffer size t/Runner.t leaves at VEP's default; nothing else can expose the boundary. Mutation-checked: doctoring the buffer_size=3 output in memory fails with the byte offset and both windows quoted.

desc: run method: with stats_text => 1 the run leaves the text summary on disk when it finishes — dump_stats really wrote it
rationale: The other end of n=29/n=30: the handle was opened at init, and finish() must have flushed a real report through it. vepyr has no statistics subsystem to dump (measurement in n=29: `no_stats|summary_html|stats_file|dump_html|dump_text|StatsReport|RunStats` all 0 at dfbf 391f94bd), so nothing is written at the end of a run but the annotated VCF itself. Absent feature: run statistics.

desc: run method: at the default up/downstream distance exactly 1 of the 3 output lines is a *stream_variant — the ENST00000567517 upstream call at DISTANCE=2407
rationale: The default arm of the distance block. `AnnotateVcfConfig::distance` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:436) is public, takes VEP's own textual up,down form and defaults to VEP's 5000, so the row ports directly against #96's committed cache; the blocker recorded in #198 was the fixture and it is gone. Not a bare count — against a 14-group answer a count would be weak — so the single *stream group is identified in full (ENST00000567517 / upstream_gene_variant / DISTANCE=2407) and the transcript that is JUST out of range is asserted absent: ENST00000419219 starts at 25592812, i.e. 7079 bases away, and enters only when the limit is raised. The positive control is a second run at `distance = "0"`: no up/downstream window at all, zero stream groups, and the answer drops from 14 groups to 13, so the default is load-bearing rather than incidental. The `distance => 10000` arm (n=51-53) is deliberately NOT asserted by this test and those rows stay blocked-api under #199. Mutation-checked: DISTANCE 2407 -> 2408 fails, and so does flipping the control's expected count.

desc: run method: at distance => 10000 the same input yields 2 *stream_variant lines instead of 1 — a second transcript comes into range
rationale: PORTED; the previous `blocked-api` reason was false at the pin and is corrected here. That reason turned entirely on one IN-SRC test having disappeared (`annotate_table_function.rs::test_annotate_vep_respects_options_json_distance_for_upstream_and_downstream`, present at 20497214a220, absent at 391f94bd) — which is true, and which is not the same thing as the API being unreachable. It never checked the second question. The option this row is about is a CONSTRUCTOR ARGUMENT on a public type: `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::new(upstream, downstream)` (dfbf 391f94bd src/transcript_consequence.rs:1100), defaulting to (5000, 5000) at :1095 exactly as VEP's --distance does, and `TranscriptFeature` / `VariantInput` are `pub struct`s with no private fields, so an external test builds the fixture by struct literal — `tests/port_transcript_tree.rs:153-157` already does. Probe, compiled clean in this crate with `HgvsFlags` in the same battery as the discriminating negative control (E0603): `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::new(10_000, 20_000)`, `TranscriptConsequence::distance`, `SoTerm::{UpstreamGeneVariant, DownstreamGeneVariant}` all resolve. Observation channel: Perl greps the written output file for the substring `stream`; the named test counts the consequences carrying `SoTerm::UpstreamGeneVariant` or `SoTerm::DownstreamGeneVariant`, and a fourth test in the same file asserts over `ALL_SO_TERMS` that those two are the ONLY terms in the pin whose spelling contains `stream`, so the substitution is measured rather than assumed. Both arms of the Perl pair are asserted — 1 at the default and 2 at 10000 — because the row's content is the change, not either count alone. Escalated by docs/campaigns/2026-08-28-final-deferred-v3/unlock-map.md §5.

desc: run method: at distance => 10000 exactly one output line carries DISTANCE=7079 — the actual distance is reported, not just the fact of being in range
rationale: PORTED, on the same correction as n=51: the vanished in-src test was never evidence about vepyr's public surface. The strongest of the three distance assertions — n=51 counts rows, this one pins the computed value, so it catches an off-by-one in the distance arithmetic that a count cannot see. Channel: `TranscriptConsequence.distance` is a `pub` field (dfbf 391f94bd src/transcript_consequence.rs:637, documented `Distance to transcript for upstream/downstream variants`) and is the DISTANCE CSQ slot Perl greps for; the named test asserts that exactly one emitted consequence carries the value, AND asserts the whole sorted multiset of reported distances, so a fixture in which every distance happened to equal it could not satisfy the count. Perl's own literal 7079 is kept: the fixture transcript is placed so the engine's +-strand upstream formula `tx.start - variant.end` (:3250) returns exactly it. Mutating the constant to 7080 turns the count to 0 — transcript in the test file's header.

desc: run method: at distance => '10000,20000' — separate upstream and downstream limits — 4 of the output lines are *stream_variant
rationale: PORTED behaviourally; the residual is smaller than the old rationale claimed and is measured here rather than inferred. What the Perl line ASSERTS is that the two limits are applied independently rather than the larger winning, and that is decided after the option is parsed, by `TranscriptConsequenceEngine::new(upstream, downstream)` (dfbf 391f94bd :1100) — public, and taking the parsed pair. The named test drives (10000, 20000) and asserts 4, with a (20000, 20000) control in the same run asserting 5: the count the assertion would have had if the pair had collapsed to its maximum. The excluded transcript is named, not merely counted. RESIDUAL, and it is not what the old rationale said: only the TEXTUAL pair parse `"10000,20000" -> (10000, 20000)` is unreachable, and the probe that says so is `error[E0624]: associated function `parse_json_distance_option` is private` (annotate_provider.rs:3564), with `AnnotateProvider` and `AnnotateVcfConfig` resolving in the same probe file as the positive controls — E0624 rather than the E0603 a module-path import would give, because it is an inherent associated fn. No row in Runner.t asserts that parse (VEP's own Config.pm does it before the Runner is built), so nothing in this ledger is waiting on it; it is tracked in #199 as an optional widening. A `pub` on `parse_json_distance_option`, or the pending test-internals overlay exporting the sibling `from_options_json` constructors, would make it directly assertable — but neither is needed by this row, which is why the row is a port and not a deferral. Escalated by docs/campaigns/2026-08-28-final-deferred-v3/unlock-map.md §5.

desc: run method: with stats_html => 1 the run leaves the HTML summary on disk when it finishes
rationale: The HTML arm of n=49, closing the statistics block: the report generator ran to completion and produced its page. vepyr has neither format (measurement in n=29; `summary_html` and `dump_html` are both 0 at dfbf 391f94bd), and ledger/Stats.ledger.toml reaches the same verdict for all 29 of its own rows. Absent feature: the HTML statistics report.

desc: Slice::seq restoration: after init the Bio::EnsEMBL::Slice::seq code ref lives in the FastaSequence package — VEP has replaced the core method with its FASTA-backed one
rationale: The assertion reads Perl's symbol table through the B compiler backend (`B::svref_2object(\&Bio::EnsEMBL::Slice::seq)->GV->STASH->NAME`, perl/Runner.t:588) to ask which package currently owns a method — method-resolution introspection, which docs/ledger-contract.md lists as Perl-runtime plumbing. It is available only because Perl's method table is mutable at run time, and Rust has no such table to inspect or swap. Note what is NOT absent: the capability the patch exists to provide — reading reference sequence from an indexed FASTA instead of from a database — IS in vepyr, as the ordinary config field `AnnotateVcfConfig::reference_fasta_path` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:405) consumed by ordinary code, so there is no product gap to name and this is not-applicable rather than no-feature. This departs deliberately from the inherited port's label ('#37 Slice::seq monkey-patch', filed under architectural-no-analogue, tests/_quarantine/port_runner.rs:33): that file used a three-class taxonomy which the contract replaced with six, and under the six the row has to be re-decided.

desc: Slice::seq restoration: after finish the code ref is back in Bio::EnsEMBL::Slice — the run leaves the caller's Ensembl API unpatched
rationale: The restore half of n=55, and the one that carries the real intent: a VEP run must not leave a long-lived Perl process with a globally patched Bio::EnsEMBL::Slice. Same reasoning and same category — the observation is of Perl's method table, and no Rust design has one. The invariant behind it is vacuous in vepyr rather than unimplemented: `annotate_to_vcf` mutates no global state, so there is nothing to restore and no post-run cleanup a test could observe. finish()'s other duties do have counterparts elsewhere in this ledger and are classified there: dumping stats (n=49/54) and the skipped-variants sidecar (n=38-45).

desc: empty-buffer continuation: with buffer_size 1 and filter_common/freq_freq 0.0012, the middle of three variants is filtered out and the run still yields rs142513484 and rs187353664 — an emptied buffer does not end the run
rationale: The row needs a filter that can empty a buffer, and vepyr has none: measured over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at dfbf 391f94bd, `filter_common` 0, `freq_freq` 0, `check_frequency` 0, `freq_pop` 0 (positive controls over the identical tree: `regulatory` 154, `hgvs` 1068). None of the 34 public fields of `AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) requests frequency-based exclusion, so no variant is ever dropped between the parser and the output and the situation this subtest constructs cannot arise. Absent feature: frequency-based variant filtering (--filter_common / --freq_freq and the --check_frequency family). The invariant it protects — an intermediate stage yielding nothing must not be read as end-of-stream — is real in vepyr too, but nothing in its pipeline can produce the empty batch that would exercise it.

desc: empty-buffer continuation: the identical filter scenario through the forked code path (fork => 2) yields the same two ids
rationale: The same absence as n=57 plus a second one: this row exists because VEP implements buffer draining twice, once in _buffer_to_output and once in _forked_buffer_to_output (Runner.pm:396 and :449), and the pair guards against the two copies diverging. vepyr has no second implementation to guard, because it has no fork model at all — its parallelism knob is `AnnotateVcfConfig::workers` (vcf_sink.rs:441-443), in-process async pipelines, and the crate rejects the vocabulary explicitly: `to_options_json` emits `workers` and the crate's own in-src test asserts `json.get("forks").is_none()` (vcf_sink.rs:1795-1803). Absent features: frequency-based filtering, and a forked execution path.

desc: plugins: get_all_Plugins returns a true value even after the plugins slot is explicitly undefined — it rebuilds rather than propagating undef
rationale: First of the twelve rows (n=59-70) on VEP's plugin loader, and the distinction this ledger has to keep straight: vepyr HAS plugins and does NOT have this. VEP's --plugin names a Perl module that is compiled at run time, instantiated with new(), checked for the methods it must implement, and then called per variant. vepyr's plugin mechanism is DATA: `AnnotateVcfConfig::plugin_cache_root` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:455) points at `<root>/plugin/*/manifest.json`, `PluginRegistry::field_names` (plugin_cache/registry.rs:100) reads the field names out of those manifests, and `csq_header_description` appends them to the CSQ layout (vcf_sink.rs:672-679). No code is loaded, so there is no plugin object to hold, to clear, or to rebuild. Measured: `get_header_info` 0 lines over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src (positive control `plugin` 304). Absent feature: a run-time code-loading plugin API.

desc: plugins: get_all_Plugins returns the loaded TestPlugin object with its params, version 2.3 and its declared variant_feature_types / feature_types (VariationFeature, Transcript)
rationale: The plugin CONTRACT, compared field by field: a VEP plugin declares which feature types it wants to be called for, carries a version, and receives the run's parameter hash. vepyr's manifests declare CSQ field names and a cache location, not dispatch criteria — nothing selects a plugin per feature type, because the plugin contributes precomputed columns rather than a callback (`PluginRegistry::field_names`, plugin_cache/registry.rs:100). `feature_types` matches 4 lines at dfbf 391f94bd, none of them a plugin concept (positive control `plugin` 304). Absent feature: the per-feature-type plugin callback contract.

desc: plugins: a plugin that fails to compile does not abort the run — get_all_Plugins still returns, having dropped it
rationale: First of the eight rows (n=61-68) on the loader's four failure modes, each asserted twice — once for the default tolerant behaviour and once for the fatal --safe behaviour. They all need something to compile at run time, and vepyr compiles nothing: its plugin data is read from `<root>/plugin/*/manifest.json` (plugin_cache/registry.rs:100), and a malformed manifest is a data error, not a compile error. Absent feature: run-time plugin compilation, and with it the whole failure taxonomy these eight rows enumerate.

desc: plugins: the dropped plugin is announced — a 'Failed to compile plugin' warning reaches the configured warning destination
rationale: The diagnostic half of n=61: tolerating a broken plugin is only acceptable if the user is told, so the run is not silently under-annotated. Two absences: nothing compiles plugins (n=61), and there is no configurable warning destination to write to — ledger/BaseVEP.ledger.toml n=34 measures `warning_file` at 0 occurrences in dfbf 0.15.0's vep crate and 0 in vepyr 346b9173 (positive controls `fasta` 63 and 15). Absent feature: plugin-load diagnostics on the warning stream.

desc: plugins: a plugin whose new() dies is dropped rather than aborting the run
rationale: The second failure mode: the module compiled, but constructing it threw. It is a separate assertion because it happens at a different point in the loader and is recovered from differently. vepyr instantiates no plugin object — a manifest is deserialized, not constructed (plugin_cache/registry.rs:100) — so there is no constructor that could throw. Absent feature: plugin instantiation, and its failure handling.

desc: plugins: the instantiation failure is announced — a 'Failed to instantiate plugin' warning reaches the warning destination
rationale: The diagnostic half of n=63, and distinct from n=62's message because a user has to be able to tell a broken module from a module that refused its arguments. Same two absences: no plugin instantiation (n=63) and no configurable warning destination (n=62). Absent feature: plugin-instantiation diagnostics.

desc: plugins: with --safe the same instantiation failure is fatal — get_all_Plugins throws 'Failed to instantiate plugin' instead of warning
rationale: The policy row: VEP lets the user choose between tolerating a broken plugin and refusing to run at all, because silently losing an annotation column is unacceptable in some pipelines. vepyr has neither the failure nor the switch — `AnnotateVcfConfig`'s 34 public fields (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) contain no --safe equivalent, and there is no plugin instantiation to make safe. The same shape appears elsewhere in the pinned stack and is already recorded as an upstream concern: old-repo issue #196 documents vepyr degrading silently where VEP aborts. Absent feature: a strict mode that turns plugin-load failures fatal.

desc: plugins: a plugin missing a method the interface requires is dropped rather than aborting the run
rationale: The third failure mode, and the one that shows VEP's plugin interface is a genuine duck-typed contract checked at load time (it can()-probes for the required methods). vepyr has no interface to satisfy: a plugin contributes named CSQ columns from a prebuilt cache, so there is no method set to be missing — `get_header_info` matches 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd against 304 for `plugin`. Absent feature: the plugin method contract and its load-time validation.

desc: plugins: the missing-method rejection is announced — a warning naming the 'required method' reaches the warning destination
rationale: The diagnostic half of n=66, the third of the three distinct messages this block pins down (compile, instantiate, required method) — the distinctions matter because they tell a plugin author which of three things to fix. vepyr validates no method set (n=66) and has no configurable warning destination (n=62). Absent feature: plugin-contract diagnostics.

desc: plugins: with --safe the missing-method case is fatal — get_all_Plugins throws on 'required method' instead of warning
rationale: The --safe arm of n=66, completing the tolerate/refuse pairing this block applies to each failure mode. Same absences as n=65: no plugin contract to violate, and no strict-mode switch among the 34 public fields of `AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:381-456). Absent feature: a strict mode over plugin-contract violations.

desc: plugins: before get_all_Plugins runs, param('regulatory') is undef — the baseline for the switch-on n=70 asserts
rationale: The before half of a two-row pair (n=69/70) pinning down that loading a plugin can MUTATE THE RUN'S CONFIGURATION: TestPluginRegFeat declares RegulatoryFeature among its feature_types, and the loader turns --regulatory on so the annotation sources will produce what the plugin asked for. Two things must be kept apart here. Regulatory annotation itself is present in vepyr — `regulatory` matches 154 lines and `RegulatoryFeature` 52 at dfbf 391f94bd. The REQUEST FLAG is not: none of the 34 public fields of `AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) is a --regulatory equivalent, the same finding ledger/CacheDir.ledger.toml n=30 records. And nothing can mutate a config mid-run, because `annotate_to_vcf` takes `&AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:1018) — a shared reference, so the type system forbids it. Absent feature: load-time option negotiation by a plugin.

desc: plugins: after get_all_Plugins runs, param('regulatory') is 1 — loading TestPluginRegFeat switched the flag on
rationale: The after half of n=69 and the row that carries the claim. Same absence, stated as the operation: vepyr never derives configuration from a plugin, because no plugin code runs and there is nothing to negotiate with (n=59-60), and `annotate_to_vcf`'s `&AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:1018) could not be rewritten if there were. Absent feature: a plugin turning on the annotation modes it depends on.

desc: post_setup_checks: --hgvs with --offline and no FASTA is refused before the run starts — 'Cannot generate HGVS coordinates'
rationale: PORTED; the previous `no-feature` rested on a measurement that is false at the pin, and the correction is arithmetic rather than interpretive. That rationale said `reference_fasta_path` occurs ONLY FOUR TIMES crate-wide at dfbf 391f94bd `with no comparison against config.hgvs anywhere`. `grep -rn reference_fasta_path` over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at that sha returns SIXTEEN lines, and one of them is the comparison it says is nowhere: annotate_provider.rs:5266, `Self::validate_hgvs_reference_fasta(hgvs_flags, reference_fasta_path.as_deref())?`, called from the scan before any cache is read. The guard itself is at :3637, under a doc-comment citing `Runner::post_setup_checks()` — this very Perl method — and its message is `annotate_vep(): Cannot generate HGVS coordinates (--hgvs/--hgvsc/--hgvsp) without reference_fasta_path (VEP --fasta)`, which CONTAINS Perl's own regex literal `Cannot generate HGVS coordinates` (perl/Runner.t:761) verbatim. The old rationale's positive control (`hgvs`, 1068 lines) passed, which is the trap docs/ledger-contract.md names: a positive control validates the method, not the search space. Observation channel: vepyr has no Runner object and no separable pre-flight method — `validate_hgvs_reference_fasta` is a private inherent associated fn — so the refusal is observed where a user meets it, through the public `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf` over the committed chr21 micro-cache, which carries no FASTA of its own. Measured, with Perl's two implicit controls in the same run: hgvs:true + fasta:None -> Err(Cannot generate HGVS coordinates...); hgvs:true + fasta:Some -> Ok(1); hgvs:false + fasta:None -> Ok(1). Zero annotated rows reach the output on the refused arm, which is `before the run starts` as far as this channel can see it. Escalated by docs/campaigns/2026-08-28-final-deferred-v3/unlock-map.md §5.

desc: post_setup_checks: --check_ref with --offline and no FASTA is refused — 'Cannot check reference sequences'
rationale: Cleaner than n=71, because here the option itself is missing as well as the guard: `check_ref` matches 0 lines over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at dfbf 391f94bd (positive controls `hgvs` 1068, `regulatory` 154), and none of the 34 public fields of `AnnotateVcfConfig` (vcf_sink.rs:381-456) requests it. VEP's --check_ref compares each input record's REF against the reference sequence and drops mismatches; vepyr performs no such comparison, so there is neither the operation nor a precondition on it to check. Absent feature: reference-allele verification against the reference sequence.

desc: post_setup_checks: --use_transcript_ref with --offline and no FASTA is refused — 'Cannot use transcript reference sequences'
rationale: The third of the three guards, and like n=72 the underlying option is absent too: `use_transcript_ref` matches 0 lines at dfbf 391f94bd (positive controls `hgvs` 1068, `regulatory` 154), and it is not among `AnnotateVcfConfig`'s 34 public fields (vcf_sink.rs:381-456). VEP's --use_transcript_ref substitutes the transcript's own reference allele for the input's when the two disagree, which is why it needs sequence; vepyr always uses the input REF. Absent feature: transcript-derived reference alleles.

desc: post_setup_checks: --everything has already turned --hgvs on before post_setup_checks runs — the before half of the auto-disable pair
rationale: RECATEGORISED from no-feature. The old rationale conceded that --everything fans out to sub-flags in vepyr but asserted that `hgvs is NOT in that expansion` and that the derivation `is not merely unreachable, it is not implemented`. It is implemented, in the same struct the rationale was reading: `HgvsFlags::from_options_json` (dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:1386-1389) computes `let hgvs = everything || parse("hgvs")` and fans it into hgvsc and hgvsp, under a doc-comment citing Config.pm#L346-L374 and `Runner::post_setup_checks()` — the method this row is about. The rationale was looking at the neighbouring `VepFlags::from_options_json` (:1166-1193), which handles the af_* family; the HGVS family has its own struct 200 lines further down. So what stands in the way is one `pub`, not a feature, which is exactly the boundary docs/ledger-contract.md §"Absent operation vs present-but-private state" draws. Probe, run from this crate with `AnnotateProvider` and `vcf_sink::AnnotateVcfConfig` resolving in the same file as the positive controls: `error[E0603]: struct `HgvsFlags` is private --> tests/zzz_probe2.rs:2:72 ... note: the struct `HgvsFlags` is defined here --> annotate_provider.rs:1369:1`. Exporting `HgvsFlags` and its constructor would make this a unit-port outright: build it from `{"everything":true}` and assert hgvsc and hgvsp, which is what Perl's `$runner->param(hgvs)` readback does. The AFTER half of the same pair (n=75) does not become portable with it — it diverges, and is filed as #401.

desc: post_setup_checks: --hgvs is silently turned back OFF when the run is offline with no FASTA — the flag --everything set is downgraded rather than honoured
rationale: The old rationale said vepyr `neither refuses nor demotes; it proceeds and the HGVS columns come out empty`, on n=71's four-occurrence miscount of `reference_fasta_path` (there are sixteen). Run here over the committed chr21 micro-cache through the public `vcf_sink::annotate_to_vcf`: `everything: true, reference_fasta_path: None` -> `Err(Execution error: annotate_vep(): Cannot generate HGVS coordinates (--hgvs/--hgvsc/--hgvsp) without reference_fasta_path (VEP --fasta))`, zero annotated rows emitted. VEP, at this exact line, sets hgvs back to 0, prints `Disabling --hgvs` (n=76) and CARRIES ON. So the two implementations answer one input differently: vepyr REFUSES where VEP DEMOTES. Mechanism: `HgvsFlags::from_options_json` folds everything into hgvs (annotate_provider.rs:1386-1389) before `validate_hgvs_reference_fasta` (:3637, called :5266) sees the flags, so an implied request is indistinguishable from an explicit one — and the explicit case, n=71, is where the two AGREE. The reading the issue argues is that vepyr is the side that must move: --everything is a convenience bundle, so refusing the whole run because one bundled sub-option is unsatisfiable is harsher than the request, and vepyr's own code cites the Config.pm passage that draws the distinction. That is a belief for #401 to settle, not a finding this ledger has made. Fails at the current pin; the test's `issue:` line names the tracker.

desc: post_setup_checks: the downgrade is announced on standard output — a 'Disabling --hgvs' status message
rationale: The row that makes n=75 acceptable: an option is only safe to demote silently-to-the-data if it is loud-to-the-user. vepyr emits no such notice, and this is the exact measurement old-repo issue #196 records from the other side — `disabling sift` 0 lines over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src at dfbf 391f94bd, against `gencode_basic` 32 as the positive control. CORRECTION (2026-08-30): the sentence that used to stand here — `there is no status stream either: stdout matches 0 lines, so vepyr has no channel for operator notices at all` — over-read n=20's measurement, which is about an output DESTINATION, into a claim about a diagnostic CHANNEL. The channel exists, on stderr: `eprintln!` occurs at 23 sites at dfbf 391f94bd (annotate_provider.rs 13, cache/lookup_exec.rs 5, vcf_sink.rs 3, transcript_consequence.rs 1, pipeline_trace.rs 1) against 0 bare `println!`. The conclusion survives on a better measurement: every one of the 23 is an env-gated `[VEP_PROFILE]`/`[VEP_PROGRESS]` trace (`profiling_enabled()`, `progress_trace`, `sink_profile`, `kv_profile_enabled()`, `pipeline_trace::enabled()`) or an in-src benchmark, so none is an operator notice. Absent feature: operator notices about options the run changed.

desc: post_setup_checks: with cache mode and database not disabled, each of the four flags lrg, check_sv, check_ref and hgvs produces its own 'Database will be accessed when using --<flag>' notice — one statement, four TAP results
rationale: A loop over qw(lrg check_sv check_ref hgvs) (perl/Runner.t:801-813), so the row stands for four cases, not one. What it pins down is that VEP tells the user when a requested option will silently pull the run out of pure-cache mode and onto the database — a cost and a network dependency the user did not ask for directly. Every element is absent: vepyr has no database mode at all (n=5's measurement: `mysql` 0, `DBI\b` 0, `ensembldb` 0 at dfbf 391f94bd, positive controls `plugin` 304 and `hgvs` 1068), so there is no cache-versus-database distinction to warn about; three of the four flags do not exist either (`check_ref` 0, `use_transcript_ref` 0, `check_sv` 0; `lrg` matches 4 lines, all of them an LRG_485 transcript-selection fixture in an in-src test at annotate_provider.rs:16598-16667); and the notice itself has no precedent — the stderr channel that does exist (23 `eprintln!` sites at dfbf 391f94bd, 0 bare `println!`) carries only env-gated `[VEP_PROFILE]`/`[VEP_PROGRESS]` traces, never an operator notice; see the correction on n=76, which replaces the `stdout` 0 reading this clause used to cite. Absent feature: operator notices about options that escalate a cache-only run to a database one.

desc: bam-edited transcripts: a GFF transcript set corrected against a BAM alignment still yields output for 21:10524654 C>A — the ref match passes through rather than being dropped
rationale: The configuration this line asserts is accepted cannot be expressed in vepyr: it needs a GFF annotation source, a BAM alignment and a chromosome-synonyms file, and none of the three is an option. ledger/bam_edit.ledger.toml settles the direction with measurements the reader can repeat — the pinned stack CONSUMES the result of a BAM edit (the transcript cache carries a `bam_edit_status` column, read by index at dfbf 391f94bd annotate_provider.rs:3723, :3807, :4528 and surfaced as the CSQ field BAM_EDIT) and never PERFORMS one: nothing in the stack can open a BAM (`grep -in 'bam|hts'` over the vep crate's Cargo.toml exits 1 against a non-empty dependency list), and `cigar`, `apply_edits`, `gff` and `gtf` all match 0 lines over datafusion/bio-function-vep/src. That ledger classifies 28 of its 32 rows no-feature on exactly this basis. Absent feature: building an annotation source from a GFF and correcting it against a BAM.

desc: fork: with no forking, four VCF records over three genes yield 12 output lines projected to (id, allele, transcript) — the reference result the three fork settings are compared against
rationale: The unforked baseline of the fork block, and on its own an ordinary annotation-content assertion. All three projected fields are named CSQ slots in vepyr (`csq_field_names_for_mode_with_pick`, golden_benchmark.rs:661). The fixture #198 recorded as missing is now committed twice over: #96's chr21 micro-cache, and tests/data/vep116_runner_input/ — VEP's OWN t/testdata/input/test.vcf at release/116.0 (sha256 a7ecda18...4bf3, unmodified), bgzipped and tabix-indexed. Measured on those bytes: 132 records, all on contig 21, 25585733-25982445, already position-sorted, and its FIRST FOUR RECORDS ARE EXACTLY the fork block's `$input` (perl/Runner.t:837-842) — so the baseline is that file's head at `workers = 1` and one fixture serves n=79 through n=84. The Perl's twelve triples are asserted in full and in order; the 44 the v115 shard adds are asserted too, because each record picks up its own three transcripts followed by the same eleven MRPL39 models (EXTRA_V115_TRANSCRIPTS), and the 56-entry expectation is built from those constants rather than read off the output. rs199510789 is the record that makes the list non-uniform — 5533 bases from ENST00000567517, past the default 5000, and 3953 from ENST00000419219 — and that is what the mutation check breaks.

desc: fork: with fork => 2 the output is identical to n=79's — parallelism changes throughput and not results, including the order lines come out in
rationale: Not a fork-model row: what it pins is DETERMINISM UNDER PARALLELISM, which survives the change of mechanism intact. vepyr does not fork — in-process async pipelines, and the crate's own option vocabulary excludes forks (`json.get("forks").is_none()`, vcf_sink.rs:1795) — but `AnnotateVcfConfig::workers` (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:441-443, '1 = serial. The single annotation-concurrency knob') is the counterpart, and preserving output order under it is designed for rather than hoped for: `annotate_to_vcf` refuses workers > 1 unless the input is tabix-indexed, precisely so the scan yields contiguous position-ordered partitions instead of a round-robin repartition (:1044-1052). The comparison is the WHOLE 3238-entry projection of the committed 132-record input, not just the fork block's head, because a merge that dropped or duplicated at a partition boundary need not show in the first four records. Positive control: the same .gz copied to a directory WITHOUT its .tbi is refused at workers = 2 by name (`workers>1 requires a tabix-indexed input`), so 'workers = 2 gave the same answer' is not equally true of an implementation that ignored the field. That refusal is also why the indexed pair had to be committed — noodles-tabix is not a dependency of this crate and datafusion-bio-format-vcf only reads a .tbi.

desc: fork: with fork => 4 the output is again identical to n=79's — the invariant holds at a second degree of parallelism, and 4 workers over 4 variants exercises the one-unit-per-worker edge
rationale: n=80 at a second setting, and a separate assertion for a reason: over 132 records four workers partition the contig differently from two, so this is the second sample that turns 'one lucky split' into a claim about the merge, and the head of the same file is still the one-unit-per-worker edge the Perl reaches with four records (the first 14 projection entries are asserted separately for that reason). vepyr's `workers` is an arbitrary positive integer, rejected only at 0 (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:1025-1029), so the pair of runs ports directly against the committed indexed input. Positive control: `workers = 0` IS refused with `annotate_to_vcf(): workers must be a positive integer`, which is what proves the field is read at all rather than silently downgraded to the serial path; the sibling control on n=80 proves the tabix guard is live. Same fixture as n=79/80 — tests/data/vep116_runner_input/, VEP's own test.vcf at release/116.0.

desc: fork: over the whole 132-record test VCF with --hgvs and a FASTA, fork => 2 reproduces the unforked output line for line — not a projection this time, the complete VEP-tab lines
rationale: n=80's determinism claim at full scale and full width, and now runnable because the input the Perl means is committed: tests/data/vep116_runner_input/ IS upstream's t/testdata/input/test.vcf at release/116.0 (sha256 a7ecda18...4bf3, unmodified), bgzipped and tabix-indexed. Same pair of `annotate_to_vcf` runs at workers = 1 and workers = 2 (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:441-443), compared BYTE FOR BYTE over the whole emitted file — header, CSQ declaration and every one of the 3238 consequence groups — so a difference in any field of any group fails here and could not fail in n=80, which projects to three. What --hgvs buys is stated honestly rather than assumed: all 132 records of that file are SNVs (`awk 'length($4)!=1 || length($5)!=1'` matches none), and #96's closing comment measured that for an SNV the pin spells HGVSc/HGVSp from the transcript shard's cached cdna_seq/translateable_seq and only OPENS the reference — a valid all-N FASTA passes byte-for-byte. So this row does not prove the reference's CONTENT is read (nothing over VEP's own fork input could; tests/annotate_end_to_end_smoke.rs covers that with a deletion in a poly-A run); it proves the HGVS path RUNS INSIDE THE WORKERS and spells the same values there, asserted as ENST00000352957.9:c.991G>A / ENSP00000284967.7:p.Ala331Thr / ENST00000307301.11:c.*18G>A rather than counted. The file's third test is the control: with HGVS set the PARALLEL run is refused by name when the reference is absent, so 'the outputs agreed' is not equally true of a build that dropped HGVS in the workers.

desc: fork: the run statistics counters after fork => 2 equal the unforked ones — the per-child counts were merged back, not lost or double-counted
rationale: Not a determinism row like n=82: what it pins down is that VEP's stats object survives the fork boundary, each child's counters being serialised back to the parent and summed. vepyr has no statistics subsystem to merge — audit/ports-compile-status.md's Stats.t verdict records that at dfbf 391f94bd `grep -rniE '\bstats\b' src/` returns 2 hits crate-wide, both unrelated, and `no_stats|summary_html|stats_file|dump_html|dump_text|StatsReport|RunStats` returns 0 (positive controls 19 for `vcf_sink`, 237 for `pub fn`) — and no fork boundary to carry anything across. `annotate_to_vcf` returns a single row count from the whole run. Absent feature: run statistics, and their aggregation across workers.

desc: fork: the same full-file check at fork => 4 — the output is again identical to the unforked run
rationale: n=82 at a second degree of parallelism, which is what makes the pair a test of the merge rather than of one lucky split: 132 records over 4 workers partition differently than over 2, so a boundary-dropping or boundary-duplicating merge shows in one and not the other. vepyr's `workers` takes any positive integer (dfbf 391f94bd vcf_sink.rs:441-443, rejected only at 0 at :1025-1029), so this is a third run compared against the first, again byte for byte over the whole emitted file, and the LAST record (21:25982445 rs141331202, the committed input's own final line) is asserted separately because the far end of the contig is where a dropped tail would show. Shares n=82's control — the parallel run is refused by name without the reference FASTA — and its fixture. Mutation-checked: flipping one missense_variant to synonymous_variant in the workers = 4 text fails at byte 1564 with both windows quoted.

desc: fork: the run statistics counters after fork => 4 also equal the unforked ones
rationale: The four-worker arm of n=83, separate because a merge that happens to be right for two children can be wrong for four. Same absence: no statistics subsystem (n=83's measurement) and no fork boundary. Absent feature: run statistics and their aggregation across workers.

desc: fork: after a forked run the TestPluginCache plugin's own {cache} hash is populated in the parent — plugin state accumulated in the children survived the fork
